By integrating type-2 fuzzy-logic and machine learning, the sensors can offer accurate glucose readings and monitor additional physiological markers, optimizing personalized interventions for type-1 diabetes. This innovation will aim to advance diabetes management with reliable, user-friendly health monitoring.

title: Autonomous Navigation of Robots on Roads using Vision-Based Techniques for Road Identification and Lane Detection
authors: Samadhan Manore; M Sasikumar; Abhijeet Suryawanshi
abstract: Autonomous robot navigation on Indian roads presents unique challenges, particularly within campuses limited by weak GPS signals due to surrounding buildings and trees. This paper proposes a cost-effective solution for navigating such environments using a DC-powered robot vehicle within the campus of CDAC Mumbai. The approach leverages computer vision for lane detection and road demarcation, eliminating reliance on GPS. The lane detection approach utilises binary mask generation, edge detection, and Hough transform, while road demarcation employs colour filtering, contouring, and moments from the OpenCV library. Experimental results demonstrate a 72% navigation accuracy with minimal false detections. This algorithm is applicable for real-time scenarios, and enables autonomous vehicle navigation using minimal and cost-effective sensors, making it suitable for environments with obstructed GPS signals.

title: Assembly Sequence Planning Algorithm Based on Topological Ordering and its Simulation System Development
authors: Junjuan Chen; Feng Li; Zhigang Xu; Runan Cao
abstract: Assembly sequence planning and its simulation are critical components in modern manufacturing. With the increase in the number of product components, the number of assembly sequences grows exponentially, presenting characteristics such as strong discreteness, large search spaces, and small feasible domains. The existing assembly sequence planning methods based on heuristic algorithms, such as particle swarms and genetic algorithms, are afflicted with shortcomings, including low solving efficiency and a proclivity to fall into local optimization during the solving process. To address these issues, this paper proposes a topology-ordered assembly sequence planning algorithm based on a greedy strategy. The algorithm employs a comprehensive evaluation index that considers both the part-level and the product-level in order to optimize the topological sorting process. It ensure that the output sequence are more compatible with the actual process. Additionally, a simulation system integrating interference checking, assembly sequence and path planning functions has been developed on the basis of the in-house Inte 3D software. The objective is to provide a set of intelligent assembly sequence planning tools for the manufacturing industry, with the aim of effectively shortening the product development cycle.

title: Fault Detection and Diagnosis Based on Ant Colony Algorithm
authors: Gula da; Jinxing Zhao
abstract: In this paper, the fault diagnosis problem is transformed into an optimization problem and solved by biological heuristic algorithm ant colony algorithm. Combined with the nearest neighbor function criterion in pattern recognition, this method optimizes the initial pheromone matrix and the value of nearest neighbor function, which greatly improves the speed of the algorithm. In the process of algorithm analysis, the errors in literature [1] are corrected. Finally, an empirical analysis is carried out to prove that our method can greatly improve the diagnosis efficiency.

title: Evoked Tactile Feedback for Fingertip Force Using Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation with Concurrent Frequency and Pulse Width Modulations
authors: Amir Khan; Ke Li
abstract: Fingertips are the most active portions of our fingers during interaction with our surroundings. The incorporation of tactile feedback to the fingertips may enhance perception and interaction with the real environment. Frequency., pulse width., and amplitude modulations of transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) are extensively studied to elicit sensory feedback in hand for sensorimotor function. However., in this study., a new approach to eliciting tactile feedback was investigated using TENS frequency., pulse width., and their novel concurrent modulations in linearly positive and negative correlations for fingertip forces. An instructor regulated the TENS parameters by fingertip force to invoke tactile sensation, and participants administered response fingertip force to a force sensor resistor to express the nature (strength) of the evoked tactile sensation. The ratio of response fingertip force to stimulation fingertip force, abbreviated as the fingertip force elicitation ratio (ER), was examined for each TENS modulation in terms of mean and maximal fingertip forces. The results exhibited that both conventional (frequency and pulse width) and novel concurrent modulations of frequency and pulse width TENS can evoke tactile feedback for fingertip force control. Furthermore, the results demonstrated that the fingertip forces resulting from tactile feedback induced by concurrent frequency and pulse width modulations were stronger., more stable, and more consistent compared to the forces produced by their independent modulations. Future applications of the innovative concurrent TENS modulations may include evoking tactile feedback responses for grasping tasks, touchpad gestures, fingertip force control, and intelligent prostheses.

title: Design of a Bioinspired Jumping Mechanism for Self-Takeoff of Flapping Robot
authors: Erzhen Pan; Wei Sun; Wenfu Xu
abstract: Most birds in nature rely on jumping for takeoff. Flapping-Wing Robots can flap and fly like birds but require an operator to take off, which are unable to generate sufficient lift to maintain flight at a low airspeed and must accelerate to take-off speed in a short time. It poses a challenge for the design of the jumping mechanism. This study is inspired by the jump-takeoff of birds and designs a simple and lightweight jumping leg, which is capable of storing and releasing energy with only one degree of freedom. In addition, a prototype was developed and tested, with a wingspan of 2 meters and a mass of 1.6 kilograms, accelerating to 4 m/s in 52 ms by jumping, achieving the jumping take-off from the ground.

title: Optimizing Path Planning and Human Detection Using YOLO and an RRT Algorithm in Autonomous Robots
authors: Ximena Herrera-Medina; Hector Arismendi-Valle
abstract: This research paper explores the integration of advanced technologies to improve the capabilities of autonomous robots. Specifically, the optimization of path planning and human detection using the RRT (Rapidly Exploring Random Tree) algorithm and the YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection model. By combining these powerful tools, robots can navigate controlled environments and interact with humans. The RRT algorithm generates collision-free paths for efficient robot navigation. This algorithm efficiently explores the search space and identifies optimal trajectories to achieve specific goals. YOLO, a state-of-the-art object detection model, is utilized to accurately detect and localize humans within the robot's field of view. This information is then fed into the RRT algorithm to dynamically adjust the robot's path and prioritize human interaction. To implement this system, the computational power of a Jetson Nano and a Raspberry Pi 4 is combined. The Jetson Nano handles the RRT path planning algorithm, while the Raspberry Pi 4 processes the camera feed and runs the YOLO model for human detection. Effective communication between the two devices is crucial for seamless integration and real-time response. Through rigorous testing, this research paper demonstrates the successful simulation of this integrated system. The robot is able to accurately detect humans, plan efficient paths, and simulate the navigation towards them while avoiding obstacles. This research contributes to the advancement of autonomous UGV (Unmanned Ground Vehicles) and has the potential to revolutionize various industries, including manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare.

title: Picking by Tilting: In-Hand Manipulation for Object Picking using Effector with Curved Form
authors: Yanshu Song; Abdullah Nazir; Darwin Lau; Yun–Hui Liu
abstract: This paper presents a robotic in-hand manipulation technique that can be applied to pick an object too large to grasp in a prehensile manner, by taking advantage of its contact interactions with a curved, passive end-effector, and two flat support surfaces. First, the object is tilted up while being held between the end-effector and the supports. Then, the end-effector is tucked into the gap underneath the object, which is formed by tilting, in order to obtain a grasp against gravity. In this paper, we first examine the mechanics of tilting to understand the different ways in which the object can be initially tilted. We then present a strategy to tilt up the object in a secure manner. Finally, we demonstrate successful picking of objects of various size and geometry using our technique through a set of experiments performed with a custom-made robotic device and a conventional robot arm. Our experiment results show that object picking can be performed reliably with our method using simple hardware and control, and when possible, with appropriate fixture design.

title: Development of a Reconfigurable Holonomic Mobile Manipulation Cobot for Smart Factory 5.0
authors: Thanatchai Wongjirad; Orapadee Joochim
abstract: This paper presents the design, experimentation, and evaluation of a reconfigurable holonomic mobile cobot equipped with a Mecanum wheel base and a coupling locking mechanism to support versatile manipulation tasks in smart factory 5.0 environments. The system, designed for omnidirectional movement and dynamic adaptability, aims to enhance flexibility and precision in human-robot collaborative manufacturing. Through a series of experiments, we assessed the accuracy of the mobile base in loaded and unloaded conditions and evaluated the alignment and coupling success of the cobot with a detachable manipulator arm module. Results indicate that the Mecanum wheel base achieves an impressive 80% alignment success rate using ArUco marker tracking, demonstrating reliable mobility and tracking in dynamic environments. However, the coupling locking mechanism achieved only a 20% success rate, revealing limitations in the locking system's tolerance to minor misalignments. These findings highlight the cobot's strengths in adaptive navigation and tracking accuracy while underscoring the need for further development of the coupling mechanism for consistent operation. For future work, we will focuses on refining the coupling system, enhancing alignment feedback through additional visual markers, and optimizing control algorithms for load-bearing accuracy. This study provides a foundational step toward implementing reliable, reconfigurable robotic systems that meet the complex demands of next-generation manufacturing environments.

title: Underwater Pipeline Defect Detection Method Based on Active Electric Field
authors: Minan Yang; Wenjie Yang; Jiaqi Wang; Jiegang Peng; Xu Lin
abstract: With the rapid development of marine exploration and the increase of submarine oil and gas transportation pipelines, the detection of underwater pipeline defects has become increasingly important. The existing defect detection technology has great advantages, but also has some limitations. Inspired by the active electrolocation system of weak electric fish, this paper proposes a new underwater pipeline defect detection technology based on frequency inflection points (FIP). In this method, the joint time-frequency spectrum (JTFS) is obtained by joint time-frequency analysis of the detection signal, and then the FIP corresponding to the characteristic defect is obtained by calculation and processing. The data show that there are obvious differences in FIP due to different materials and defect characteristics. In practical applications, the calculated FIP can be compared with the characteristic curve to obtain the defect information of the measured object. At the same time, this paper also carried out defect detection experiments on non-metallic objects. The experimental results show that the defect detection method proposed in this paper is convenient to use and has a wide range of applications. It has great potential in underwater pipeline defect detection and underwater robot applications.

title: An Improved Imperialist Competitive Algorithm For Solving Traveling Salesman Problems
authors: Guangqiang Li; Chen Xu; Yongjie Wang; Wenchao Dong; Daqing Zhu
abstract: In order to better solve traveling salesman problems, we proposed an improved imperialist competitive algorithm (IICA). Firstly, the original continuous algorithm is discretized to be suitable for solving combinatorial optimization problems. Then, four improvements are proposed to enhance the overall performances of the proposed algorithm: introducing immune fitness based on immune mechanism, employing parallel computation strategy, improving the strengthening link of imperialist countries according to the idea of simulated annealing, as well as adopting adaptive mechanism to accelerate algorithm convergence speed. Finally, comparing simulation results by proposed algorithm and other algorithms on typical traveling salesman problems selected from the classic test library demonstrate that IICA can solve these problems on different scales more effectively, and it has better convergence accuracy and speed.

title: Precision Cavity Length Control System Design for Ring Laser Gyroscope
authors: Shuying Li; Zhaoyang Xu; San Zhang
abstract: Laser gyroscope is a kind of high precision angular sensor which has been widely used in strapdown inertial navigation system. The cavity length of laser gyroscope varies with the external temperature changes, which have influence on the scale factor stability and bias stability. In this regard, to control cavity length of laser gyroscopes with higher precision and reliability, a precision cavity length control system with self-adaption temperature compensation method is designed. The main motivation of this contribution is to design the higher accurate cavity length control system with self-adaption temperature compensation algorithm embedded. Experimental tests show the significant performance and effectiveness of cavity length control system proposed.

title: Attitude Control of Airbag Isolation System Based on Adaptive Model Predictive Control
authors: Hanyan He; Wenxia Xu; Baocheng Yu; Zhiqiang Tang; Sanbao Zhu; Chen Cao
abstract: The air bag vibration isolation device has an important application in ship vibration and noise reduction. However, traditional fuzzy control has problems such as slow response and low accuracy when dealing with complex environments and multi-variable coupling. In this paper, a new method based on Adaptive Model Predictive Control (AMPC) is proposed to improve the attitude control performance of the airbag isolation system. Firstly, the system is modeled and a discrete-time state space model is established. By dynamically adjusting the model parameters, the future state of the system is accurately predicted. Then, a rolling optimization MPC controller was designed to select the optimal airbag for inflating and deflating operations by using the real-time collected pressure and displacement data, so as to realize the precise control of the attitude. Experimental results show that compared with the traditional fuzzy control method, the control algorithm based on AMPC shows significant advantages in control accuracy, response speed and pressure balance. This study provides a new technical approach for the efficient control of the air bag vibration isolation system, and lays a foundation for the application of more complex ship vibration and noise reduction system in the future.

title: A Hybrid CNN and Transformer Model for Chest X-Ray Classification: Toward Accurately Diagnosing COVID-19
authors: Xiaoqiang Shi; Kun Liu; Keyi Su; Gang Huang
abstract: Recent studies have employed computer vision and convolutional neural network based methods to automate and enhance the diagnosis based on chest X-ray. However, these approaches demand significant computational resources and other intricate techniques to produce results.In order to reduce the model parameters and improve the diagnostic accuracy of COVID-19, we proposed a framework based on lightweight CNN and vision transformer. This framework leverages two key components: the MBConvFusion module and the mobile inverted bottleneck convolution block. By introducing the MBConvFusion module, which connects three MBConv modules in parallel, our model achieves outstanding accuracy of 98.75% with only 1.4 million parameters.

title: The polynomial approach to accessibility of nonlinear fractional order difference system
authors: Ewa Pawluszewicz
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The focus of the paper are accessibility (in a finite number of steps) conditions for nonlinear control systems with the Grünwald-Letnikov fractional order h-difference operator. These conditions are presented in terms of the greatest left common divisors of shifted polynomials associated with the given system. The obtained results extend the polynomial approach to accessibility problem of nonlinear discrete-time control systems on fractional case.

title: Impact of Different Parameters on Symmetry and Size of Single Step Anodization Nanopores in Porous Alumina
authors: Nabeela Noor; Shah Haider; Zaki Uddin; Iqra Ashfaq
abstract: Nanoporous Alumina is used widespread as a template material for nano scaled objects since mid-20th century. These nano scaled objects are in the form of nanowires, nanotubes and nanodots etc. In order to synthesize nanoporous alumina, two step anodization techniques has been reported. We have prepared porous alumina with the distinction that arrays of pores in alumina were created by single step anodization. We fabricate nanoporous alumina in 0.3 M oxalic acid for various anodization times at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$23^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> under constant voltage of 40 v. EDX graphs revealed that oxide layer of aluminum was formed on the metal surface of aluminum. SEM micrographs however, depicted a good estimate of pore symmetry under low temperature and resulted in small pores as compared to room temperature. Longer anodization time deepens the pores' depth, whereas at room temperature the acid invaded pores' wall. SEM images made the evident that the sample anodized sporadically has lower degree of pore symmetry than continuously anodized sample. It was also observed that at voltage other than self-ordering i.e. at 60 V, hexagonal symmetry of pores decreases.

title: Nonconvex Extended Object Tracking Method Based on Set Inversion
authors: Yiguo Li; Tianli Ma; Kun Yan; Chaobo Chen
abstract: To address the problem of target tracking under nonlinear bounded measurements, this paper proposes a nonconvex extended object tracking method based on set inversion. The method first establishes a nonconvex extended object model using the adjacency matrix. A tree-structured constraint propagation algorithm then shrinks the node state prediction set and constructs the set inversion problem based on measurement equation constraints. The shrunk set serves as the initial interval for the set inversion algorithm, which is used to solve the set inversion problem to obtain the optimal state intervals of the extended object nodes. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in tracking nonconvex extended object.

title: Reproducible Fabrication of Liquid Metal Droplet with FIB Sputtering for Contact Angle Measurement in SEM
authors: Yuning Lei; Sergej Fatikow
publication_title: 2024 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: The wetting phenomenons of surfaces, such as surface tension, are a critical concern for various micro- and nanoelectromechanical systems (MEMS/NEMS) due to scaling effects. In recent years, a lot of efforts have been made in research and industry to study wetting phenomena at the micron and nanometer scales, among which, the liquid metal droplet-based contact angle measurement (CAM) method allows for the characterization of surface wetting properties in a scanning electron microscope (SEM), thus obtaining a resolution that goes beyond the limits of an optical microscope. However, reproducible fabrication of specific micrometer-scale droplets is a key challenge towards the automation of this technique. In this paper, we provide a reliable and reproducible method for the fabrication of specific-sized liquid metal droplets. This includes the generation of droplets at specific locations based on electromigration techniques and the use of focused ion beam (FIB) induced sputtering techniques to fabricate droplets of specific sizes. Using Galinstan as an example, this paper reports its sputtering yield of 0.866 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.nC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, along with the process of determining it. We also demonstrated the reproducibility of fabricating liquid metal droplets with a radius of 10 μm and 5 μm, the results show standard deviations of 0.168 μm and 0.63 μm, respectively.

title: Expert Recommendation System Based on Knowledge Graph
authors: Ziyang Zhang; Juan Zhang
abstract: This paper proposes an expert recommendation system based on knowledge graph and machine learning technologies, aiming to address the challenge of expert matching caused by equipment failures in the field of intelligent manufacturing. By introducing knowledge graph technology, the system effectively integrates a wide range of engineering knowledge, including expert experience and fault patterns. Combined with the high efficiency of machine learning in processing large-scale data, the system achieves precise matching between experts and fault issues. Compared with traditional manual allocation methods, the proposed system demonstrates significant advantages in automation, efficiency, and intelligence, while improving the accuracy and efficiency of the fault diagnosis process. Experiments show that the system's performance across multiple datasets validates its potential for applications in industrial manufacturing.

title: Motion Control of a Guide Dog Robot Adapted to the Intentions of Visually Impaired Individuals and Dynamic Environmental Conditions
authors: Yuhui Gao; Bin Zhang
abstract: To enhance the mobility and quality of life of visually impaired individuals, this paper proposed a guide dog robot by improving navigation and interaction capabilities under dynamic environments. Integrating with existing navigation technologies, two user-operated buttons are equipped to the robot to accelerate or decelerate the speed, temporarily stop or restart the robot, according to the will and operations of the user. The moving speed of the robot is finally calculated by combing the will of the user and the situation of the environment to ensure the safety of the user. Additionally, a voice interaction system is proposed to generate real-time environmental descriptions based on LSTM neural networks, conveyed through speech synthesis. Experiments demonstrate that the robot effectively responds to user commands, as well as ensuring safety, and interacts well with the user.

title: Limited Time Consensus Control of Multi-robot System Based on Sampled Data
authors: Xuan Cao; Wenxia Xu; Deng Chen; Baocheng Yu; Yanduo Zhang; Moutang Fan
abstract: In order to solve the consensus problem in the logistics multi-robot system, a logistics multi-robot system control protocol is designed. To Lyapunov theory and graph theory as the main research tool, trigger control strategy based on the use of sampling data limit event, the working mechanism of the policy more in line with the actual system. Based on the sampled data, a finite time self-trigger control strategy is further proposed. Based on this strategy, the event trigger function of periodic monitoring can be avoided, and the mechanism based on sampled data can fundamentally avoid the Zeno phenomenon. Finally, the validity of the theoretical results is verified by numerical simulation.

title: Cooperative Optimal Control of UAVs Based on Brain-Attention Mechanism Neural Network
authors: Ziyuan Ma; Huajun Gong; Xinhua Wang
abstract: With the increasing complexity and variety of mission environments, multiple-UAVs cooperative path optimization system is gradually becoming an important development direction in the future. Because the current intelligent level of UAV is difficult to meet the requirements of complex tasks, in order to improve the intelligence and collaborative ability of multiple-UAVs systems, this paper focuses on the intelligent decision-making and collaborative control of UAV in the collaborative path of multiple UAVs system. In this paper, an autonomous and innovative UAV Cooperative Path Optimization System Based on neural network of brain like attention mechanism is proposed. The experimental results show that this method has lower processing delay, can achieve positioning accuracy in a shorter time, and has higher reliability and accuracy than the traditional center controlled UAV cooperative positioning UAV method.

title: Research on Load Transfer Law of Artillery Equipment under Complex Boundary Conditions
authors: Can Ren; Hua Gao; Chunlai Shan; Jun Liu; Bin Gu; Yingchao Wu
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: This article focuses on the problem of load transfer during artillery firing under different soil boundary conditions, considering the complex boundary coupling effect and the law of system load transfer and boundary influence. On the basis of traditional dynamic simulation methods, a combination of spatial springs and damping friction is used to simulate the deformation behavior of soil. This system is used to establish equivalent displacement conditions for soil boundaries. Subsequently, efficient and high-precision dynamic modeling research was conducted on artillery. The parameter values of the boundary combination model are determined by solving the fitting test data through dynamic simulation, forming a soil boundary submodel. A large caliber self-propelled gun is tested and compared with the high-speed camera monitoring results of the vehicle displacement, parking hoe displacement, and hydraulic oil pressure monitoring results of the parking hoe during the shooting test. The simulation results meet the accuracy requirements. Compared with the traditional multi-body dynamics model, this method has higher simulation accuracy and does not increase the simulation complexity and computational scale, which can be applied to the development of the same type of artillery equipment to improve the simulation and design efficiency in the process of artillery equipment development.

title: Comparative Study of DQN and DDQN in Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Collision Avoidance Systems
authors: Siti Nurhafizza Maidin; Nurbaiti Wahid; Sarah Atifah Binti Saruchi; Sumiya Tamanna Fujita; Alvi Khan Chowdhury
abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of Deep Q-Network (DQN) and Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) agents for collision avoidance in autonomous vehicles using the CARLA simulator. By integrating a hybrid sensor system, comprising radar, collision, and lane invasion sensors and utilizing a prioritized experience replay (PER) buffer, both agents were able to achieve 100% accuracy within 1,000 training episodes. Experimental results demonstrate that DDQN outperforms DQN in terms of average reward, training stability, and responsiveness to dynamic traffic conditions. Its architecture mitigates common reinforcement learning challenges, such as value overestimation, leading to safer and more reliable autonomous driving behaviors. These findings offer valuable insights for enhancing autonomous driving safety and warrant further real-world validation.

title: Analysis of Power Supply Parameters for Indirect Process Control
authors: Sohyla M. Aboudeif; Alexey P. Ilyin
abstract: Most processes in chemical technologies are performed on non-transparent equipment (metal, opaque plastic, thermally insulated equipment). This prevents visual monitoring of the process in progress and, in certain cases, necessitates the installation of costly and sophisticated optical sensors in the machinery in order to enable the automation governing the process to make the required decisions. At the same time, most of these changes can be detected by indirect signs using sensors already installed in the system, which makes it possible to simplify and reduce the cost of parameter monitoring methods. One of these methods can be the use of data received from a monitor of electrical network parameters. In some cases, changes in the value of consumed currents, active and apparent power can be clearly associated with the processes occurring in the “black box”, and after proper calibration, serve as reliable criteria for making certain decisions.

title: Stable Wreckage Detection for AUVs Using YOLOv8 and Enhanced RRT Path Planning
authors: Harshith Kumar M B
abstract: Underwater robotics is rapidly emerging as a prominent research field globally. The underwater environment, characterized by a complex array of forces, necessitates the development of highly stable systems for effective operation. By exploring one of the least accessible terrains on Earth, underwater systems unveil a multitude of applications. This research paper presents a comprehensive system designed for Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) operations, targeting efficient underwater surveys and the detection of underwater wreckage. The system integrates several advanced technologies to achieve its objectives. A new mathematical model of the proposed AUV is designed and the stability of this system is achieved using the Proportional Integral and Derivative (PID) controller. Path planning is facilitated by the enhanced Smooth Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) algorithm, enabling the AUV to autonomously navigate complex underwater terrains. The AUV is also equipped with an onboard camera system that utilizes the YOLOv8 computer vision algorithm for classification, allowing it to differentiate between marine life, human divers, and wreckage. Furthermore, the system incorporates localization capabilities for identifying wreckage. This integrated approach aims to enhance the efficiency of underwater surveys, offering significant potential for applications in marine research, environmental monitoring, and search and rescue missions.

title: Adaptive Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control of a BLDC Motor Speed Control
authors: R. Achdad; A. Rabhi; S. Benzaouia; X. Pierre; H. Midavaine
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive super-twisting algorithm is introduced for controlling a Brushless DC motor (BLDC) drive system. The main focus of this study is the assumption that the bounds of uncertainties and perturbations are unknown. The proposed control strategy employs dynamically adapted control gains to ensure the controller's finite-time stability. A key aspect of the adaptation algorithm is its ability to avoid the overestimation of the control gain values. The controller's effectiveness is demonstrated through simulation and experiments on a test setup.

title: Optimizing Multi-Modal Transportation in Smart Cities: A Graph-Oriented Database Approach
authors: Mihai Hulea; Radu Miron; Andrei Rusu
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to enhancing urban transportation efficiency through the integration of multimodal transportation networks using graph databases, specifically OrientDB. Addressing the inefficiencies in traditional segregated passenger and freight movements, the study explores the potential of graph databases to effectively manage and optimize complex, interconnected urban transportation systems. Utilizing a practical implementation in Cluj-Napoca, Romania, the research demonstrates how this model can improve operational efficiency and resource allocation. The paper proposes a graph-oriented data model designed to store several types of transportation nodes and links effectively. Additionally, we explore a range of queries to demonstrate the practical usability and functionality of this data model.

title: Signal Representation with Optimal Subspace Graph Filtering
authors: Ying Chen; Jingjing Liu; Lin Zhou; Li Zhao
abstract: Signal representation is a prime problem in signal processing. In this paper, we propose a subspace graph filtering method for signal representation. We demonstrate an extended singular value decomposition (SVD) model of signal essentially is a subspace graph filtering, and build a bridge from SVD to graph filtering. A smoothing subspace graph filtering is sequentially learned in the space provided by SVD. In the experiments, we compare the signal restoration performance between the extended SVD and the proposed subspace graph filtering. It shows that clean signal can be better reconstructed from the noisy signal in our smoothing subspace than the SVD space, where the learned smoothed bases of graph filtering are more robust than the bases of SVD to cope with noise.

title: Analysis and Research on Technical Characteristics of Balance Type Twin-screw Compressor Based on Advantage Structure
authors: Ling Deng; Liwu Zhang
abstract: This paper introduces the methods of constructing the twin-screw compressor load characteristics which were in the background of the basic performance parameters of the exhaust pressure and the exhaust volume, and some relevant data and charts from them, on the basis of the definition of the load characteristics of twin-screw compressor, the principle of classical mechanics and mechanical work and the traditional theory of the compressor was applied, based on the advantage of balance type twin-screw compressor’ structure; then, the specific expression, the way of expression, the theoretical data and the conclusion analysis of the advantaged characteristics of the exploratory research on the excavation of the technical characteristics of the advantaged structure were given. They can provide a theoretical basis for the advantaged characteristics and value of balance type twin-screw compressor.

title: Force balance control method of adjustable parallel cable-driven platform
authors: Jia Longfei; Li Hao; Zheng Ranran; Song Hongzhou; Li Ke; Yu Zhiyuan
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the existing parallel cable-driven platform can not be balanced in many positions and orientations, this paper first proposes a new type of cable-driven platform with adjustable cable node positions. Then, by analyzing the relationship between the platform position and orientation, the size of the cable pulling force, and the relationship between the position and direction of the cable, a universal kinematic model is constructed. Finally, the experiment is verified by simulation. The simulation results show that, combined with the new platform and model designed in this paper, the force imbalance problem of the parallel cable-driven platform in any position and orientation can be solved.

title: UAV-Assisted Logo Inspection: Deep Learning Techniques for Real- Time Detection and Classification of Distorted Logos
authors: Mohammed Mohiuddin; Oussama Abdul Hay; Ahmad Abubakar; Mubarak Yakubu; Naoufel Werghi
abstract: Ensuring the integrity of safety logos on aircraft is crucial for aviation personnel and overall safety. Presently, human operators perform inspections, which are susceptible to human errors. To address this, we propose an autonomous approach using drone-acquired photographic imagery for detecting and inspecting safety logos on fighter aircraft. Our methodology involves multiple stages: logo detection, distortion assessment, text orientation computation, and checking for logo overlap. We also calculate placement constraints for accurate logo positioning. We rigorously tested our approach on a local dataset, achieving an impressive precision of 92.3 % and a recall of 91.1 % for logo detection. We estimated computed text orientation in degrees and determined the distance between logos in pixels. This research presents a significant advancement in automatic logo inspection for aircraft safety. By leveraging drones and comprehensive detection techniques, our approach reduces human errors and enhances inspection efficiency. The potential impact includes improved safety standards in aviation and the foundation for future advancements in autonomous inspection systems.

title: Robust State Feedback H-Infinity Controller Design for Bilateral Teleoperation System Having Saturated Actuators
authors: Bilal Gormus; Hakan Yazici
abstract: This paper considers a robust state-feedback H-infinity controller design for uncertain bilateral teleoperation system having norm bounded parametric uncertainties and saturated actuators. The proposed method utilizes nested attractive ellipsoids and employs linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) to obtain sufficient robust stability and H-infinity performance constraints under consideration of actuator saturation. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is illustrated through numerical simulations of responses a one-degree-of-freedom bilateral teleoperation system under exogenous input. Numerical simulation results show that in spite of the saturated actuators, the proposed LMIs based robust controller is very effective in reference tracking performance.

title: Accuracy analysis of the fractional order; positive; state space model of heat transfer process
authors: Krzysztof Oprzędkiewicz; Klaudia Dziedzic; Wojciech Mitkowski
publication_title: 2021 25th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: In the paper the accuracy estimation for fractional, positive state space model of heat transfer process is presented. The new criterion of the external positivity for this model is presented. Next the parameters of the model are estimated via numerical minimization of the Mean Square Error (MSE) and FIT cost functions. Finally the externally positive models are compared to non-positive. Results of simulations show that the positive model is more accurate in the sense of considered cost functions than non positive.

title: Design of a System for Near-Infrared Composite Spectral Image Acquisition and Information Processing
authors: Lin-mei Zhou; Peng Cao
abstract: The NIR camera is a device that captures images within the near-infrared spectral range, typically operating wavelengths from 700nm to 2500nm. The camera can possess exceptional penetrating capability and achieve multi-functions, making it a prominent subject of research and application in the industrial sector. The paper provides the system for near-infrared composite spectral image acquisition and information processing which is based on the Alvium 1800 U-130 VSWIR camera by Allied Vision. The system leverages QT Creator to establish an efficient and robust software platform with a user-friendly interface, facilitating NIR image acquisition and information processing across wavelengths ranging from 400 nm to 1700 nm. It is also equipped with narrow band filters for 940 nm, 1450 nm, and 1550 nm. The system effectively tackles challenges regarding the prevention of illegal copying, counterfeiting and infringement areas, detection of water content, differentiation of similar objects, and penetrability. Moreover, it offers practical applications in areas such as anti-counterfeiting measures, food safety assurance, and industrial processes.

title: Design of a Variable Stiffness Continuum Robot for Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection
authors: Heng Zhang; Xiaolong Zhu; Haiyan Hu; Zhenhao Chen; Haojie Tian
abstract: The incidence of gastrointestinal malignant tumors has been showing an upward trend, and endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has become the preferred surgical procedure for early-stage gastrointestinal cancers in recent years. However, there are numerous challenges in using traditional single-channel endoscopy for ESD. Addressing the issue of limited instrument flexibility and loading capacity due to the confined working environment in ESD, and considering the operational requirements of gastrointestinal endoscopic surgery, this paper proposes an innovative five-degree-of-freedom variable-stiffness continuum robot based on the principle of single-cord force locking. The robot’s base is designed similarly to a gimbal mechanism, allowing adjacent bases to rotate freely around the contact ball. By tensioning the pulling ropes, friction between the bases is increased, achieving the effect of variable stiffness. This paper establishes a kinematic model, and elucidates the working principle of variable stiffness. Experiments verify that the tip of the continuum robot can withstand a radial load of 2.5N and achieve trajectory tracking with small error, demonstrating significant potential for providing flexible operation and robust load capacity in ESD surgery.

title: Rural Sewage Automatic Monitoring System Based on the Internet of Things
authors: Yuan Shi
abstract: From the perspective of the world, the problem of water pollution and clean water shortage is increasingly increasing, among which rural water pollution has become a major source of river and lake pollution in the world. Due to the rural farmland runoff, farmland drainage and groundwater infiltration, the main cause of water pollution, which has had a great impact on the rural water environment and ecological environment. Therefore, the monitoring and treatment of rural sewage is a big difficult problem. In recent years, universities and scientific research institutions from all over the world have been committed to the treatment of agricultural sewage and intelligent system research, and have achieved effective results. Among them, the automatic control system with computing as the core has been widely used in the modern era. This paper mainly proposes a set of rural sewage automatic monitoring system based on the Internet of Things.

title: Global Information Attention Based Dual-Pathway Network for Oxidized Slag Segmentation of Metal Ingot Images
authors: Degang Xu; Ao Zhang; Xuming Liu; Jie Wu
abstract: The content of oxidized slag on the surface of metal ingot is the key to judge whether the metal ingot is qualified. However, it is still a challenge to determine the covering area of oxidized slag on the surface of metal ingot. In this paper, we proposed a novel Global Information Attention based dual-pathway Network (GANet) consists of context and edge pathways to segment oxidized slag on the metal ingot surface image. Specifically, to suppress the interference of background on oxidized slag segmentation, we propose novel Fusion Attention Module (FAM) and Global Position Attention Module (GPA), which can effectively aggregate global semantic information and improve segmentation performance. Meanwhile, we designed the edge pathway and Edge Perception Module (EPM) to extract the boundary information of the oxidized slag. The experimental results show that the performance of the GANet is better than the existing segmentation methods which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method and provides a research idea for the automation of metal casting process.

title: Collision-free Navigation of Flying Robots in Outdoor Environments with Dynamic Obstacles
authors: Yang Zhang
abstract: In this paper, a collision-free navigation algorithm for flying robots is proposed. The algorithm is applied to three-dimensional environments with dynamic obstacles. Shapes of moving obstacles may be non-convex, motion of the obstacles is variable. The algorithm is a sliding mode control law, switching between two modes, the target approaching mode and the obstacle avoidance mode. Mathematical analysis of the proposed algorithm is given. Simulation results are also provided in order to demonstrate its performance. Compared with other approaches, the algorithm is a really practical one as the constraints of the obstacles are not too hard to be satisfied. Moreover, the proposed algorithm is computationally efficient.

title: MPC-DCBF Based Motion Planning of Mobile Manipulator in Dynamic Environment
authors: Shihao Zhao; Xin Zhou; Jianliang Mao; Chuanlin Zhang
abstract: Traditional planning algorithms face many problems in trajectory planning for mobile robot arms, including long path planning time, long computation and data processing time, and limited ability to solve complex obstacle environments. To address these challenges and issues, this paper proposes a method that combines global path planning with local path safety planning. Using Rapidly exploring Random Trees Star (RRT*) for global planning of mobile chassis, combined with the tasks given by Model Predictive Control (MPC) at the end of the robotic arm, and using Dynamic Control Barrier Function (DCBF) method to provide overall safety assurance for the mobile robotic arm. This method can plan trajectories in environments with complex obstacles while considering external disturbances, ensuring system safety and achieving obstacle avoidance.

title: Integrated Design of Feedback Control and Fault Detection Based on Reduced-Order Observer
authors: Suichun Qu; Xue Li; Zhikang Fan; Bin Chen
abstract: This paper investigates an integrated design framework for feedback control and fault detection based on a reduced-order observer. Firstly, all stabilizing controllers can be described as a reduced-order observer, which is the joint form of state, output and residual feedback, based on well-known Youla parameterization of all stabilizing controllers. Furthermore, an integrated design framework for feedback control and fault detection is proposed, the advantages of which are low online computation, convenient fault detection, etc. Finally, the simulation of the Heating, Ventilation, and Air conditioning (HVAC) system is adopted to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed design framework.

title: Robotic Assisted Echocardiography: Enhancing Cardiac Imaging Through Teleoperation
authors: T. Sreelekha; J. Deepthi; S. Saranya
abstract: Echocardiography, which provides real-time viewing of the anatomy and function of the heart, is still a fundamental component of cardiac diagnosis. Nevertheless, traditional echocardiography techniques are constrained by their dependence on operator skill, requirement for close physical contact, and picture quality fluctuation. A revolutionary approach is robotic-assisted echocardiography, which combines sophisticated robotic equipment with tele-operational capabilities to capture high-quality heart pictures remotely. In addition to enhancing picture consistency and diagnostic accuracy, this method increases access to specialist treatment in underserved or rural areas by enabling skilled doctors to operate ultrasound probes from a distance. It allows geographically distributed healthcare professionals to deliver timely and expert cardiac assessments, bridging gaps in care delivery and improving patient outcomes. Clinical studies and pilot implementations have demonstrated the feasibility and effectiveness of such systems in intensive care units, mobile clinics, and even extreme environments like space missions. Despite challenges like system cost, network stability, and training needs, robotic-assisted echocardiography has excellent potential for the future of cardiovascular care, especially in space medicine, critical care settings, and international telehealth programs. Remote tele-mentored ultrasound echocardiography can be used to evaluate left and right ventricular and valvular function and to aid in the diagnosis of pathologies such as tamponade. This paper examines the current technologies, clinical applications, advantages, and disadvantages of robotic-assisted echocardiography and describes how it could change the cardiac imaging landscape.

title: Improving Popular Textbook Recursive Algorithms with Tail Recursion
authors: Sami Ullah
abstract: Iteration and recursion are two of the important programming techniques used to develop algorithms and software. Recursive programs are generally not considered as advantageous as iterative functions in the introductory curriculum of computer science. This is because the course books focuses primarily on branched top to bottom versions of recursion which is an inefficient way to create algorithms while iterations have low memory overhead. Recursive algorithms calculate values for the same perimeters repeatedly resulting in wastage of processor time and memory. However, different variants of recursions exist such as linear, tail and branched which are hardly mentioned in conventional studies and are more efficient than branched recursive. Like dynamic programming, tail recursion can provide remedy for such redundant processing. This paper will focus on alternative recursive solutions for some of the most popular known mathematical problems such as factorial, Fibonacci and binomial coefficient with same efficiency as iterative code that is widely discussed in the course books.

title: Gaussian and Non-Gaussian Information Based Hydraulic Component Internal Leakage Fault Diagnosis
authors: Zhiwei Qiu; Wanli Li; Daozhi Wang; Siwen Fan; Qiuping Wang
abstract: Internal leakage is primary fault mode of hydraulic components, typically caused by seal failure or damage. However, the fluid inside hydraulic components exhibits complex motion characteristics, and its external vibration signals often have intricate distributions, making fault diagnosis challenging. This paper focuses on the internal leakage of hydraulic directional valve and proposes a fault diagnosis method based on Gaussian and N on-Gaussian information. First, time and frequency domain features are extracted from the vibration signals of the hydraulic directional valve. Then, the correlation between internal leakage and signal features is analyzed. Finally, Gaussian and Non-Gaussian information is extracted based on the correlated signal features, and these are used to construct statistics for detecting the presence of internal leakage. In complex data distribution scenarios for fault diagnosis, this method offers a novel solution without requiring a large number of fault samples or complex parameter optimization. Experimental studies validate the performance of this method, demonstrating that it outperforms several classical fault diagnosis methods in terms of robustness and accuracy. This research provides an effective approach for detecting internal leakage faults in hydraulic directional valves.

title: An Ensemble Algorithm Combining Multi-models and Proposed Chaotic Harris Hawks Optimization for Fire Flame Recognition
authors: Jian Wang; Juan Nan; Zhiyan Han
abstract: Fire recognition and early prevention are of great significance to reduce the loss caused by fire. In this paper, an ensemble algorithm combining multi-models and proposed chaotic Harris hawks optimization (CHHO) is proposed for fire flame recognition. The combined multi-models include decision tree (DT), K-nearest neighbor (KNN), least squares support vector machine (LSSVM) and extreme learning machine (ELM). Aiming at the problem that improper parameter will seriously affect the classification performance of the combined models, a chaotic Harris hawks optimization (CHHO) is proposed to optimize the parameters of models. Tent mapping, improved exploration mode and improved exploitation mode are introduced into CHHO to improve the performance of Harris hawks optimization (HHO). Finally, the output of each optimized model are obtained, then the final output are obtained by weighted average method. Experiment on a set of flame images shows that the proposed model is effective and has good classification performance.

title: 3D Reconstruction of Astronomical Site Selection Based on Multi-Source Remote Sensing
authors: Xinhua Huang; Haocheng Liu; Qingkai Meng
abstract: The significance of astronomical site selection in site selection impacts the extent of utilization of astronomical science equipment and the accessibility of observation findings, which is related to both the progress of astronomical science and the expensive resource investment. In order to show the topography and important geographic factors of the Saishten Mountains and Xueshan Pastures potential areas. In this study, we undertake a 3D reconstruction of the astronomical site selection region using Chinese Gaofen satellite images, tailored high-resolution dem data, and a 3D platform, offering a precise visualization help for site planning. The study results show that (1) The 3D reconstruction is quite effective and useful for site selection, according to the results. (2) All candidate locations offer favorable topography, terrain, and elevation characteristics for the astronomical site selection, with the exception of the candidate site in the Saishten Mountains, which necessitates additional thought for the engineering and geological safety of the site selection. (3) Each candidate site's platform area is suitable for the deployment of astronomical research equipment, but the platform space at Snow Mountain Ranch is particularly well suited for the positioning of sizable astronomical scientific equipment.

title: Unmanned Boat Pollution Cleanup Based on Outpoint Penalty Functions
authors: Haosu Chen; Yuan Ge; Yujin Wang; Gang Ye; Qitao Lin; Jiqiang Zhao
abstract: This paper proposes an algorithm that combines an improved penalty function with a Hamiltonian optimization function to solve the trajectory planning problem of unmanned boat pollution cleaning in an ecological lake. In order to shorten the unmanned boat movement time and trajectory distance, this paper parameterizes and discretizes the time and constructs it as a nonlinear optimization problem over different time parameter segments. In addition, a simple and effective envelope modeling is used to transform the obstacles formed by artificial islands in the ecological lake into inequality constraints. The effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper is verified by experimental simulation. The results show that the algorithm in this paper can complete the contamination cleaning in a shorter movement time with a shorter movement distance and maintain a more stable speed.

title: A Study on the Classification of Subclasses of Glass Artifacts Based on Feature Selection
authors: Jiamei Jiang; Xuhan Li; Xingyu Hao; Tao Liu; Ruofeng Qiu; Qunfeng Miao
abstract: To explore the subclass types of ancient glass artifacts, first we combined the features provided in the dataset with the data on whether the artifacts were weathered or not, constructed a random forest model, and calculated the relative importance of each chemical component by the VIM (Variable Importance Measures) to give the important factors influencing the classification of major classes. Subsequently, we innovatively extracted the important components by improving the coefficient of variation to give the important factors influencing the classification of subclasses. Then, we construct a K-means clustering model for subclassification and give specific criteria for subclassification. Finally, we conducted the rationality analysis from two perspectives of chemical composition and heritage characteristics; we repeated the experiment to test the sensitivity of the large class division model for the random forest model normally distributed white noise sequence; we introduced Dunn index and contour coefficient for sensitivity analysis of the clustering model.

title: Attention Module in YOLO-Based Object Detection Method for Autonomous Smart Wheelchair Room Navigation System
authors: Ainandafiq Muhammad Alqadri; Fitri Utaminingrum; Muhammad Ali Fauzi; Rekyan Regasari Mardi Putri; Corina Karim; Femiana Gapsari
abstract: People with visual impairment have difficulty in navigating a room based on text in room nameplate. Recognizing room nameplate in real environments with computer vision approach is challenging, because the system has to detect the room nameplate objects. Detection result can be improved by adding attention module in deep learning architecture, however model complexity also need to be observed to prevent accident caused by slow response from the system. Based on that problem, we proposed to compare the effect of Coordinate Attention (CA), Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), and Shuffle Attention (SA) on YOLOv8 model. Based on our findings, CA module shows positive result on accuracy of 99,50%, precision of 1, and f1-score of 0,997. As for CBAM has reduced accuracy to 96,15% from original YOLOv8n that has 98,52% accuracy, this may occur because the placement of the CBAM module before detection head is not suitable in the case of room name plate detection. Meanwhile, SA module has the least number of parameters and model size increase of additional 73.896 parameters and 154 KB, respectively. Our findings enrich insight in improving object detection method for autonomous smart wheelchair room navigation system.

title: MPC Based Path-Tracking Algorithm Using Apriori Known Road Friction Condition for the Over-Actuated Subscale Vehicle Platform
authors: Jan Švancar; Tomáš Haniš
abstract: Recent advancements in vehicle technology and autonomous systems necessitate more sophisticated control algorithms, including path-tracking, which is critical for self-driving cars. This paper introduces a path-tracking solution that utilizes an over-actuated platform with steering redundancy, and leverages prior knowledge of road conditions. The prediction of road condition is assumed to be known and available through V2V communication or vision-based predictions. The paper compares the performance of the Stanley Control Law, serving as a benchmark solution, and the Model Predictive Control (MPC) algorithm under varying road friction conditions using a scaled-down vehicle platform. The results demonstrate that the MPC algorithm, with its adaptive capabilities and integrated use of front and rear steering controls, surpasses the Stanley Control Law in maintaining stable and accurate path-tracking under changing conditions.

title: AXLE: Computationally-efficient trajectory smoothing using factor graph chains
authors: Edwin Olson
abstract: Factor graph chains– the special case of a factor graph in which there are no potentials connecting non-adjacent nodes– arise naturally in many robotics problems. Importantly, they are often part of an inner loop in trajectory optimization and estimation problems, and so applications can be very sensitive to the performance of a solver.Of course, it is well-known that factor graph chains have an O(N) solution, but an actual solution is often left as "an exercise to the reader"… with the inevitable consequence that few (if any) efficient solutions are readily available.In this paper, we carefully derive the solution while keeping track of the specific block structure that arises, we work through a number of practical implementation challenges, and we highlight additional optimizations that are not at first apparent. An easy-to-use and self-contained solver is provided in C, which outperforms the AprilSAM general-purpose sparse matrix factorization library by a factor of 7.3x even without specialized block operations.The name AXLE reflects the names of the key matrices involved (the approach here solves the linear problem AX = E by factoring A as LL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sup>), while also reflecting its key application in kino-dynamic trajectory estimation of vehicles with axles.

title: Research on De-noising Method of Plant Electric Signal Based on EMD and Wavelet Threshold
authors: Zilu Liu; Zhigang Bing; Liguo Tian; Meng Li; Yu Sun; Yusong Wang
abstract: Plant electrical signal is a complex non-stationary signal, which can reflect the growth state of plants and the changes in the surrounding environment. There will be a lot of noise in the acquisition process. The Kalman filter and wavelet domain denoising used in the current research have certain limitations. In order to solve this problem, this article takes the Liliaceae herb Aloe as the research object and adopts self-built signal acquisition. The system extracts the electrical signal of aloe, and combines the empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and improved wavelet threshold function to denoise the collected signal. The results show that the method can effectively separate the interference signals in the aloe electrical signal, use the improved wavelet threshold method to remove the interference signals, and retain the effective information in the aloe electrical signals as much as possible, which has certainly practical significance for the analysis and feature extraction of the plant electrical signals, lay the foundation for the next step of exploring the relationship between plant electrical signals and growth status.

title: Flexible Circuits for Soft Robotics
authors: Li Wang; Yin Zhang; Peijin Li; Huangyu Zhou; Fanghao Ning; Tao Qin
abstract: In today's rapidly evolving industrial landscape, traditional rigid industrial robots are increasingly unable to meet the demands of complex and variable tasks due to their limited deformability, significant fatigue wear, and poor thermal management. This paper explores the flexible circuit technologies designed specifically for soft robots and their innovative manufacturing processes, highlighting how these technologies can significantly enhance the adaptability and flexibility of robots to address existing challenges. We propose a method combining liquid metal conductive pathways with an elastic substrate island structure to create stretchable circuit designs that meet the needs of soft robotics.

title: Developing a Digital Twin Framework for Monitoring the Trajectory of the UR10 Robot Using an Extended Kalman Filter
authors: Ramy Alham; Moncef Hammadi
abstract: In the era of modern robotics and Industry 4.0, integrating advanced state estimation techniques with digital twin technology is crucial for enhancing robotic system performance and safety. This study presents a pioneering Digital Twin framework to monitor the trajectory of Universal Robots' UR10 robotic arm. We address challenges such as system uncertainties, sensor noise, and environmental factors by combining a Kalman Filter-based state estimation with a Digital Twin approach. By creating a virtual replica that accurately mimics the UR10's physical properties and dynamics, our method enables realtime tracking and prediction of the robot's states, improving control and operational efficiency. The Digital Twin incorporates the robot's kinematics and dynamics to compute the Jacobian matrix for EKF estimation. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate a significant increase in accuracy in position (approximately 90.14%) and velocity (approximately 85.10%) estimations after introducing noise to the UR10 robot simulation. This approach paves the way for advanced control strategies, fault detection systems, and virtual testing platforms in industries like manufacturing, healthcare, and research, where precision and performance are critical.

title: Digital Process Design and Simulation of Slush Molding Based on Tecnomatix
authors: Qiming Gao; Chenming Wang; Haoran Gu; Chuanjiang Li; Yiyou Gao; Ziming Tom Qi
abstract: In the product development process, manufacturing flexibility requirements continue to increase, and with the emergence and development of digital twin technology, virtual scenes can be created to observe, analyze, and predict data. Compared with traditional models, the risk is lower and the investment cost is lower. The slush molding process is one of the important processes in the production of automotive interiors, and the difficulty of improving the process is particularly prominent. Based on the Tecnomatix Plant Simulation software, this paper digitally designed the slush molding process, built the corresponding simulation model and logic program, and carried out the production scheduling simulation according to the production work order; then used the simulation experiment method to optimize the process parameters, and after comparing the simulated production capacity data with the actual production capacity, the accuracy of the model is verified, and finally, the production capacity prediction under different production requirements can be realized, which can effectively reduce the cost of process improvement.

title: Realization of Fuzzy Control in an Auto Focusing System
authors: Fengchao Liang; Xiaolin Zhao; Shuang Tan; Jiankai Fan; Tingting Yu; Zhe Lin
abstract: The surface error of the workpiece, mechanical axis error, etc. will cause the defocus of the marking focal spot in the laser marking process and affect the marking accuracy. An important way to avoid defocusing is to introduce a focusing servo system to detect and compensate defocusing in real time. The critical angle method is selected to detect the focus, and the focusing servo system is established. According to the characteristics of linear and nonlinear coexistence of defocusing error curve, a focusing servo fuzzy controller is designed, which completes the linear control of defocusing error in linear area and the fuzzy control of defocusing error in nonlinear area. The focusing experiment results show that the focusing servo fuzzy control system can realize automatic focusing, and the focusing servo adaptive fuzzy control algorithm enhances the robustness of the control system and expands the dynamic range of focusing.

title: Automatic Docking of Drone Using Machine Learning for Power Line Inspection
authors: Aiswarya A; Kiran R
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have gained sig-nificant attention in the field of power line inspection due to their ability to access challenging locations and capture high-resolution imagery. However, the manual control and landing of UAVs on power line structures pose risks and operational challenges. To address these issues, we proposes a machine vision based automatic docking system for drones, specifically designed for power line inspection. A specially engineered gripper module enables the system to securely dock onto a power line. The proposed system incorporates a machine learning-based model that detects and tracks the power line using onboard cameras, enabling the drone to align itself accurately with the power line. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness and fea-sibility of the automatic docking system, showcasing its potential to streamline power line inspection processes. Utilizing machine learning for automatic drone docking in power line inspections is driven by the pursuit of safety, as drones eliminate human exposure to high-risk situations commonly encountered during manual inspections. This approach is time-efficient and cost-effective, offering the capability for real-time, highly accurate data analysis. The scalability of machine learning models enables consistent inspections over vast power line networks. As machine learning models continually refine themselves with more data and serves as a testament to modernization and safety.

title: Design and Implementation of Radiofrequency Ablation System Based on Power Closed-Loop Control
authors: Fuchun Liu; Haixing Deng; Zewen Huang; Ming Zeng
abstract: As an emerging device used in surgery, Radiofrequency (RF) ablation is widely used in minimally invasive surgeries. In the process of surgery, the system needs to output constant power to ensure the quality of surgery when the tissue location or ambient temperature and humidity change. The hardware of the RF ablation system was designed in this paper, and the power closed-loop control was realized. The system uses a microcontroller STM32F303VCT6 and the dual ADC alternate sampling method to require the RF output signal. The RF output power is obtained by frequency-domain analysis of the sampled signal using the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) algorithm, and the power is controlled using a PID controller so that the actual output power quickly tracks the user-set power. The experimental results of power control show that the controller can adjust the power of the RF ablation system to the set value within 500 ms, without overshoot in the control process and within ±1 W of power fluctuation after stabilization. Meanwhile, the controller can realize power tracking of the ablation system when the load changes.

title: Chicken Disease Diagnosis Model Using YOLOv8 Object Detection Algorithm with SE-Attention Mechanism
authors: Jinghui Quan; Hang Shi; Zhihua Zhang; Zhiyuan Zhao; Hongzhen Cai; Langwen Zhang; Bohui Wang
abstract: Traditional chicken disease diagnosis methods rely on manual observation and experiential judgment, which are inefficient and susceptible to subjective factors. This paper aims to construct a chicken disease diagnostic model with deep learning algorithm for enhancing the accuracy and efficiency. Firstly, this paper proposes a chicken disease diagnostic model based on YOLOv8 algorithm. An SE-attention mechanism is designed for YOLOv8 structure to improve the detection accuracy. The SE-Attention based YOLOv8 detection model can identify and classify diseases by analyzing the feces images of chickens. Experiments on chicken disease diagnosis are performed to validate the proposed model's feasibility and effectiveness. Ablation study is constructed to validate the advantages of the SE-attention mechanism.

title: A Multi-Policy Framework for Manipulator Trajectory Tracking Based on Feature Extraction and RL Compensation
authors: Yixuan Li; Yuhao Wang; Gan Wang; Tingna Shi
abstract: Trajectory tracking for manipulators, especially when faced with complex trajectories, remains a formidable challenge in robotics. This paper introduces an approach to address this challenge with the framework we propose called Cluster-SAC. Our strategy hinges on the integration of feature extraction techniques to segment complex trajectories, assigning each segment to be adeptly tracked by distinct SAC agents. Through this approach, the precision of trajectory tracking is optimized, as each segment benefits from a dedicated learning agent. Validated with the 7-DoF manipulator of Franka Emika Panda Robot in the Gazebo simulation, results showcase faster training convergence and superior tracking accuracy on arbitrary given trajectories.

title: Auto-Identification of Two-Mass System Parameters with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Grzegorz Kaczmarczyk; Mateusz Malarczyk; Radosław Stanisławski; Marcin Kamiński
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper presents an application of Reinforcement Learning (RL) to identify the mechanical connection parameters of a two-mass system. The issue of parameter uncertainty in complex mechanical systems is discussed. The RL method for parameter estimation is then briefly described. The applicability of the proposed approach is confirmed by the results obtained with the Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) strategy. The description of the laboratory stand equipped with BLDC motors is given and the experimental confirmation is presented.

title: The Harvesting Line Fitting for Intelligent Oolong Tea Harvesting Robot
authors: Ruidong Yu; Yuqiong You; Zhou Fang; Yinhui Xie; Qiming Li; Zhiqin Guo; Jiyou Zhang; Jun Li
abstract: Aimed to improve the quality of picked tea leaves and the efficiency of tea harvesting, an intelligent oolong tea harvesting robot with a cutter adjustment module and a harvesting curve fitting algorithm is proposed. A cutter adjustment module is designed to adapt to different shapes and densities of tea bushes, ensuring precise tea harvesting. An adaptive density-weighted RANSAC algorithm is proposed to fit a harvesting line that matches the contour of cutter. Our algorithm enhances the robustness of point cloud recognition by weighting the samples based on sparsity and improves response speed by dynamically updating the iterative threshold. Experiments were conducted using a dataset of 30,000 frames of tea bush point clouds collected by us in a tea garden in Wuyi Mountain. Our algorithm takes only 0.081 seconds on average to fit a single frame of tea bush point cloud, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.7270. The experimental results show that our algorithm exhibits great robustness and responsiveness in handling sparse point clouds of tea bushes.

title: Experimental Validation and Robustness Analysis of Ergodic UAV Control
authors: Luka Lanča; Stella Dumenčić; Karlo Jakac; Stefan Ivić
abstract: This study presents an experimental validation of coupled ergodic control for horizontal movement with model predictive control (MPC) for velocity and altitude of multi-rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) during search operations in hilly terrain. For ergodic control, we employ a two-dimensional potential-based algorithm called the Heat Equation Driven Area Coverage (HEDAC). This paper aims to compare search performance between simulation-based environments and real-world experiments, validating the most important flight parameters. The motivation stems from the critical role UAVs play in time-sensitive Search and Rescue (SAR) operations, where robustness to different uncertainties and errors is beneficial. Some of the uncertainties impacting flight accuracy are sensor inaccuracies from GPS and compass sensors, wind disturbance, and variability in communication lag duration, the difference between simulated and real flights is being investigated. By conducting two experiments, each consisting of one simulation and two field tests, we evaluate the motion control uncertainty under these unpredictable factors. The results show promising efficiency and robustness of the motion control system.

title: Wavefront sensorless aberration correction utilizing SPGD algorithm with adaptive coefficient for laser scanning confocal microscopy
authors: Tianyu Zhang; Zhizheng Wu; Xiang Wei; Feng Li; Jialiang Wu; Kongbin Zhu
abstract: Laser scanning confocal microscopy (LSCM) has become a common method for biological observation and medical science. Compared with traditional optical microscope, LSCM has the advantages of high contrast and three-dimensional (3D) imaging. However, with the increase of image depth, the resolution and contrast will be reduced due to the complexity of biological tissue aberrations. Adaptive optics system is an effective method to eliminate aberration. In this paper, a wavefront sensorless adaptive optics system is used to correct aberrations generated by complex refractive index of biological tissue. In order to increase the convergence speed and reduce the influence of photobleaching, an improved stochastic parallel gradient descent algorithm with adaptive coefficient is used to control the AO system. The optical path is simulated in ZEMAX and the feasibility of the proposed algorithm is verified in MATLAB. All simulation results demonstrate that the optimal algorithm can correct the aberration effectively with the designed optical system.

title: Properties of Distributed Filtering Under Scaled Noise Covariances
authors: Xiaoxu Lyu; Guangzhi Tian; Suyang Hu; Ling Shi
abstract: This paper investigates the properties of the distributed filter under scaled noise covariances. Initially, three performance indices, along with three auxiliary indices, are introduced to evaluate the performance of the distributed filter. By providing the specific assumptions on the scaled parameters, the proportional relations among three performance indices are revealed. The relations of the gain matrices under the nominal and actual parameter scenarios are also examined. Furthermore, the impact of the fusion step on these relations is elucidated. These results provide guidance for designing the nominal noise covariance and evaluating the performance of the distributed filter under the scaled noise covariances. The theoretical results are validated through simulations.

title: Concept Design of a Reconfigurable Robot for Assembly Lines
authors: Bin Wei; Dan Zhang
abstract: A reconfigurable robot for the assembly line is designed. A concept of combining the large octopus device used in amusement parks and assembly robotics is proposed. It is found that the octopus equipment in the amusement park can easily achieve multi-directional translation and rotation under heavy load conditions. One of the requirements for assembly lines is to use robotic devices to mount parts in a multi-axis and flexible manner under heavy load conditions. This paper proposes the design concept of a reconfigurable assembly robot.

title: Intensity and K-Means Clustering based Treatment Classification of Posterior Capsular Opacification
authors: Raisha Shrestha; Waree Kongprawechnon; Teesid Leelasawassuk; Nattapon Wongcumchang; Toshiaki Kondo
abstract: Posterior Capsular Opacification (PCO) is an after cataract complication which has been under continuous research over past couple of decades. Studies so far have been limited to it's grading, calculating severity and rate of occurrence. The grading can be more useful in practical world, if its severity level determined cases with requirement of treatment. PCO patients are treated only when they have pain in their eyes, resulting in need of regular check-ups. This paper presents an approach of PCO treatment classification, with two methods: intensity-based (method 1) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-means clustering based (method 2), to classify the requirement of treatment. When cross-checked to classifications made by expert ophthalmologists, methods 1 and 2 showed accuracy of 94.57% and 96.74%, with F1 score of 96.69% and 98.11% respectively. Also, the classifications made by method 1 and 2 were 83% and 87% correlated to the classification made by expert ophthalmologists.

title: Automated Knitting Instruction Generation from Fabric Images Using Deep Learning
authors: Xingyu Zheng; Haoliang Sheng; Songpu Cai; Meng Cheng Lau; Kaiyu Zhao
abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning method to generate knitting instructions from fabric images, reversing the traditional process of manual pattern coding.
