The survey made it possible to distinguish the most common behaviors among passengers and to identify differences in the choice of means of transportation among the identified groups of passengers. The results can support decision-making in the development of multimodal transportation modes taking into account different passenger behaviors.

title: Deep Learning for Insulator and Binding Fault Diagnosis in Smart Grids With YOLOv11 Instance Segmentation
authors: Santoshi Kanagala; Ramesh Palanisamy; K V Govardhan Rao
abstract: Smart grids heavily depend on insulators and their connecting components for reliability. Faulty components can lead to power outages, equipment damage, and safety hazards. This paper presents a design for a deep-learning-based system that employs the YOLOv11 instance segmentation technique to automatically detect and classify faults on insulators and their binders, central to smart grid reliability. Classical approaches to fault detection require manual recognition and basic image processing techniques, and thus they are tedious and unreliable. YOLOv11, on the other hand, offers better fault recognition accuracy, quicker processing, and segmentation. By using roboflow, a dataset of insulator images affected by faults such as cracks, pollution flashover, and binding failures are build and proved that YOLOv11 surpasses traditional and benchmarked methods by performing at a mAP of 84.1% and allowing for real-time diagnostics of faults under varying conditions. This allows a reactive maintenance approach, minimizing downtime and firing up grid reliability. Further, this research will involve making the model edge-computer friendly and enhancing its fault detection scope.

title: A Multi-strategy Improved Osprey Optimization Algorithm for UAV path Planning
authors: Long Yang; Weimin Wang; Binzi Xu
abstract: Addressing the challenges of reduced population diversity and susceptibility to local optima in the later iterations of the Osprey algorithm, this paper presents a Multi-Strategy Improved Osprey Algorithm (IOOA). Firstly, Piecewise mapping is employed to initialize the population, providing a robust foundation for global search. Secondly, during the exploration stage, we design an adaptive parameter Levy exploration method based on the fishhawk leader. Additionally, we integrate a random disturbance strategy inspired by trigonometric functions to enhance population diversity and improve global exploration capacity. During the exploring phase, we propose nonlinear control parameters to effectively balance exploration and exploitation, thus decreasing the risk of the algorithm stagnating to local optimum. Additionally, we introduce an update formula based on the positions of elite leaders to expedite convergence. Finally, we conduct simulation experiments and statistical tests on 13 benchmark test functions, comparing the performance of IOOA with seven popular algorithms. Simultaneously, we apply IOOA to the UAV path planning problem to validate its optimization performance in practical scenarios. The results indicate that IOOA exhibits faster convergence speed and higher effectiveness compared to other optimizers.

title: Design and Implementation of Hexacopter Drone with Integrated Suction and Lift Mechanism with Real-Time Depth Sensing for Precision Object Handling
authors: Aashish Sahu; R Prasanth Kumar
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an advanced hexacopter drone equipped with a novel suction and lift mechanism for precise object handling. The drone incorporates a dual-motor suction system affixed to a rotatable servo-controlled platform, enabling a 180-degree range of motion for accurate object placement. Integrated with a real-time camera system, the drone performs depth sensing, object detection, and size estimation, ensuring efficient and accurate operations. The control algorithm enables the drone to approach a target, lower the lift mechanism, and suction the object. Upon successful acquisition, the drone transports the object to a designated drop-off point, where it gently releases it. This versatile system is capable of handling various objects, including flat plates, small papers, and cylindrical items. The comprehensive functionality of this drone makes it a significant contribution to aerial robotics, with potential applications in logistics, warehousing, and precision delivery systems.

title: RoboTunes: A Multi-Player Learning Framework with Musical Programmable Robots
authors: Khalil Al-rahman Youssefi; Helmut Lindner; Wilfried Elmenreich
abstract: This paper proposes a novel learning framework that merges robotics and musical elements to create an engaging educational platform. With the increasing importance of robots in educational systems, designing a system that utilizes music and robotics as tools for teaching and learning is of high value. The concept involves a Colorized Music-based Maze (CMM) that integrates musical notes to create a challenging playground for robots. Students can instruct their robots to move on this playground utilizing a musical instrument (e.g., a piano or a flute). The proposed system offers a multi-faceted learning approach suitable for a broad spectrum of age groups, fostering collaborative learning and problem-solving skills in an interactive and eniovable manner.

title: Trajectory Generation for Wheel-Legged Robot Jumping Based on Maximum Torque Minimization
authors: Qian Zhang; Kai Chen; Yiqun Li
abstract: This paper proposes a method for optimizing the jump trajectory of a robot, aiming to minimize the maximum torque. By utilizing the dynamics of the entire machine and iteratively refining the range of joint torques, the maximum torque during the jump is effectively reduced. Validation was conducted on a self-developed wheeled-legged robot, and the results show that the generated trajectory is effective and reliable. This method significantly improves the robot’s jumping performance and has important implications for the motion planning of wheeled-legged robots.

title: Disturbance-observer-based Controll of the Underwater Vehicle for Manipulation
authors: Yiqun Wang; Qiyan Tian; Yiping Li; Shuo Li; Hailin Wang; Zhibin Jiang
abstract: Recently, more and more interventional underwater vehicles are widely used in marine industry and marine science. The vehicle-manipulator system is a hybrid vehicle composed of a remotely operated underwater vehicle (ROV) and an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV). An importance issue for the vehicle-manipulator system is to keep consistent control performance of underwater manipulation. In this paper, a control scheme based on the disturbance observer is proposed to maintain high performance even under lumped disturbance that includes the motion of the manipulator, model uncertainties and currents. The compensation item of the controller is able to achieve quick response to attenuating disturbance, and is also able to decrease in the absence of disturbance. In other words, the proposed control scheme alleviates the restriction of the feedforward control that is regarded as a valid method to relieve the influence of disturbance. The effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is demonstrated by lake experiments.

title: Non-Prehensile Whole-Arm Manipulation Grasping and Trajectory Generation in 3D
authors: Pascal Hinrichs; Christian Kowalski; Max Pfingsthorn; Andreas Hein
abstract: For manipulating large, bulky loads, whole-arm manipulation is a suitable method. It is often used in a non-prehensile way. However, non-prehensile manipulation is mostly considered only two-dimensional, for example, moving an object on a surface. Whole-arm manipulation, on the other hand, often requires 3-dimensional movements. If redundant manipulators are used for whole-arm manipulation, there may be several valid poses for a way-point on a trajectory but only one of these configurations allows to cover the largest possible distance on the trajectory without reconfiguration. Reconfiguration is not possible with whole-arm manipulation, as this would result in a loss of the object. Numerical methods, on the contrary, can only randomly select one of these configurations. Therefore, we propose a completely analytical trajectory generation method for moving cylindrical bodies, which allows exploration of the entire path for optimal robot configuration and redundancy resolution. The contact plane along the longitudinal axis of the cylinder can be passed as an allowed interval and is used by the algorithm for optimization. In experiments, we compare our method against RRTConnect and the impact of the shiftability of the contact plane on the performance of our method. The results show that the proposed method finds up to two and a half times longer distances than RRTConnect on a path without reconfiguration, but takes more time to do so. Finally, we demonstrate the applicability in a real-world scenario in nursing.

title: Analysis and Prediction of Fatigue Life for Suspension
authors: Zi Wang; Xintian Liu
abstract: The fatigue life study of the connecting rod of a composite double wishbone suspension of a formula car is carried out based on the load spectrum obtained from the dynamic simulation, with a certain formula car as the research object. Dynamic simulation of double wishbone suspension. The dynamics of the suspension is modeled based on the geometric model of the double wishbone suspension and the hard point parameters. Finite element analysis of suspension connecting rod. The finite element model of the suspension connecting rod is established based on the suspension connecting rod of a formula car, and the process of establishing the finite element model is briefly described, including geometric cleanup, mesh delineation, mesh quality control, etc. The stress state of the upper cross arm, lower cross arm and push rod of the suspension in the ultimate working condition and deformation displacement are obtained through finite element analysis. Based on the results of the static analysis of the suspension structure, the fatigue simulation analysis of the parts was carried out to obtain the fatigue life cloud diagrams of the key parts of the suspension, which provides a reference basis for the fatigue life estimation and fatigue durability validation of the suspension connecting rods.

title: Robotic Arm Design and Simulation for Remote Maintenance in the DTT Fusion Reactor
authors: Giulia Calvo; Davide Sorli; Pierpaolo Palmieri; Stefano Mauro
abstract: The need for low-carbon, predictable, and reliable power has driven the European community to establish the EUROfusion project, aiming to provide grid electricity by the mid-21st century through nuclear fusion plants integrated with renewable energy sources. A key component of this initiative is the Divertor Tokamak Test facility (DTT) in Frascati, Italy, by ENEA, which will test reactor configurations and technologies for the future DEMOnstration (DEMO) reactor. Due to neutron-induced radioactivity, remote-controlled robots will perform maintenance on plasma-exposed components, operating during non-active periods. This paper proposes a robotic arm designed to perform pipe extraction and positioning in confined environments as part of the DTT's Divertor Handling subsystem. The robotic system described and its working environment are tested using a model of the system built in a multibody environment. Results allow to to evaluate joints motors specifications and the capability of the manipulator to achieve the task. The end effector trajectory is designed to avoid collision with the environment during the maneuver.

title: Distributed Resilient Estimator for Networked Systems Under Deception Attacks
authors: Weiwei Zhan; Zhiqiang Miao; Yang Hu; Yizong Chen; Yanjie Chen; Yaonan Wang
abstract: Deception attacks are employed to compromise cyber-physical systems through fake data injection. This paper concentrates on the distributed resilient estimation issue of multi-sensor networked systems under deception attacks. In order to detect deception attacks, we utilize Kullback-Leibler(K-L) divergence as a criterion to distinguish the discrepancy between the deceived information and the estimated information. When the attack does not exist, the transmitted information can be restored to ensure the resilient estimation performance. Based on the extended Kalman filter design method, a distributed resilient estimation with a dual-gain mechanism is developed. This advanced approach dynamically adjusts the weighting balance between the predictive model and sensor data inputs, achieving the optimal estimation during the shutdown and activation of spoofing attacks. Finally, numerical simulations are provided to further illustrate the results.

title: Design of Helicopter Attitude Controller Based on Improved Explicit Model Following Control
authors: Xiang Li; Senkui Lu; Yujie Ma; Shanyong Zhao
abstract: Attitude control was the key to helicopter flight control which was the internal loop of speed and trajectory control. So, design of the helicopter attitude controller was the focus in the article. Firstly, the explicit model and inverse model module in traditional explicit model control systems was discussed. Then, the feedback compensation module was improved by the closed-loop gain shaping algorithm (CGSA). Finally, compared to the traditional explicit model following control (EMFC) controller, the controller designed in this paper had a simpler and more efficient structure which was easy to implement in engineering and had promotional value.

title: Coupling Attitude Control for Flexible Spacecraft with Rotating Structure
authors: Jie Wang; Jun Wu; Wang Liu; Haoran Ji
abstract: This paper is devoted to the precise attitude control of flexible spacecraft with rotating structures, which is modeled as a rigid platform with some attached flexible appendages. During attitude maneuver, the excited vibration of flexible appendages would downgrade the performance of the spacecraft. In order to address this key issue, the idea of a coupling attitude controller, in which the positive position feedback control method is introduced to suppress the elastic vibration based on piezoelectric materials is proposed, while a robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> controller with the consideration of uncertainties is utilized to control the attitude. Also, the stability of the coupling attitude controller is analyzed. The methodology is implemented on a spacecraft attitude control problem in which the platform undergoes attitude maneuver. The simulation results show the efficiency of the coupling attitude controller. The proposed theory is meaningful for flexible spacecraft to achieve high pointing precision and stability.

title: Topology-guided Online Trajectory Planning for UAV Navigation in Dynamic Environments
authors: Wendi Yu; Hongyun Xiong; Xiaohong Nian
abstract: UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) plays a crucial role in the research and application of autonomous navigation due to its advantages of small size and flexible movement capabilities. To solve the problem of UAV navigation in dynamic environments, a topology-guided online trajectory planning method is proposed. Multiple topological paths are searched by region-splitting and the pruning algorithm, which expands the solution space of trajectory optimization and effectively avoids trajectories falling into local minima. For dynamic obstacles, propose a receding horizon guide Point Assigning algorithm and a gradient-based B-spline trajectory optimization to generate obstacle avoidance trajectory. Simulation results show that the proposed method is robust and real-time in dynamic environments.

title: Research on Economic Optimal Dispatch of Microgrid Clusters Based on Improved Vulture Optimization Algorithm
authors: Zhuangzhuang Luo; Qing Ai
abstract: Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle to find optimal solutions for microgrid cluster economic dispatch. To address this, an Improved Vulture Optimization Algorithm (IBES) is proposed, integrating reverse learning with an adaptive factor and Cauchy mutation strategies. These enhancements help escape local optima and improve precision. Simulations show that IBES significantly reduces economic costs compared to PSO, BES, and WOA.

title: Fault Dictionary Based Optimal Sensor Allocation Strategy Considering Fault Undetectability
authors: Jian Sun; Yuanjin Wang; Wen Shi; Ningyun Lu
abstract: With the increasing complexity of equipment systems, the requirements for testability design are becoming more demanding. This paper proposes using an integer-encoded fault dictionary as the testability model, integrating fault propagation and test detectability for sensor allocation. The proposed approach is carried out in three main steps. First, an integer-encoded fault dictionary model is developed to represent the relationship between faults and tests. Second, the model’s ability to diagnose faults is evaluated by defining the performance index, which considers fault propagation and the detectability of tests. Third, the Discrete Cuckoo Search (DCS) algorithm is applied to optimize the sensor allocation based on the defined performance index. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach can achieve more accurate testability models under imperfect conditions, thereby enhancing fault diagnosis performance.

title: OFVO: A Visual Odometry Designed for Motion Trajectory Estimation of Autonomous Vehicles
authors: Fengchen Wei; Weiji Wang
abstract: Camera motion estimation is crucial for measuring the trajectory of moving objects. Fortunately, there is an odometry to help us solve this problem. Unlike other research works that primarily rely on odometry for indoor robots and drones, we aim to utilize visual odometry to enhance our autonomous driving perception system. The outstanding contributions of this paper are as follows: Firstly, by utilizing the feature point method in image processing, we explore various feature extraction and matching algorithms to develop a visual odometry system based on Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF (ORB) and Fast Library for Approximate Nearest Neighbors (FLANN) for autonomous cars, which is named the ORB-FLANN Visual Odometry System (OFVO). Secondly, we validate our algorithm in the self-driving simulator Carla and achieve satisfactory results.

title: Newton-Euler Modeling of Robot Dynamics Using Geometric Algebra
authors: Eduardo Bayro-Corrochano; Daniel Alvarado-Mejia
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: In this work, we present the modeling of the dynamics of a robot manipulator using the Newton-Euler algorithm in the conformal algebra framework. The modeling of the dynamics of robot manipulators is currently done using the Euler-Lagrange formulation which is a batch type of computation. In contrast, in this paper, we propose a recursive algorithm for the modeling of the dynamics of robot manipulators using the Newton-Euler algorithm in the conformal geometric algebra framework.

title: Intelligent Drug Delivery Vehicle System Based on STM32
authors: Lingyi Zhou; Chengke Wang; Xian Jiang
abstract: In the context of the new coronavirus epidemic, medical systems throughout the world has suffered tremendous pressure, the most intuitive problem is a shortage of human resources. In this regard, the ‘intelligent drug delivery vehicle’ puts forward a feasible scheme, which can replace manual work in a specific hospital area to complete the delivery of drugs. The system is based on STM32F103ZET6 core processor, controlling the OpenMV visual module to identify the hospital corridor information, and then through the pressure detection module, gray detection tracking module and angle sensing module information, the core processor controls the motor drive module to make the vehicle move. The system modifies the algorithm under the traditional NCC template matching algorithm, and uses the zoom image to reduce the pixels which improve the camera frame rate and recognition accuracy. At the same time, the Bluetooth communication module is installed to enable different vehicles to execute the drug delivery operations at the same time, therefore reducing manual work saving.

title: Output feedback sliding mode control of discrete-time systems
authors: Paweł Latosiński
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Sliding mode control strategies are useful for counteracting unpredictable disturbance affecting the plant. However, they are not devoid of shortcomings, as they typically require full state information to calculate the control signal. Moreover, such strategies are typically focused on the evolution of a virtual sliding variable and provide only indirect information about the actual state of the plant. Motivated by these issues, in this paper a new approach to sliding mode control of discrete time systems is proposed. This approach only requires information about the output of the plant to synthesize a robust control strategy. Furthermore, it is shown to guarantee boundedness of this output while the system is operating in the sliding phase.

title: Design and Implementation of a Cascade Vertical Pulling Artificial Intelligent Automatic Yarn Dropping Robot
authors: Qingguang Yu; Yuming Liu; Zhicheng Jiang; Gaoxiang Long
abstract: As of improving the automation level and the labor efficiency, yarn dropping robot takes an important role in the ring spinning textile machine. Design and implementation of a cascade vertical pulling artificial intelligent automatic yarn dropping robot in this paper. After researching of the yarn dropping process of ring spinning machines, the kinematics and dynamics analysis of the yarn dropping robot are put forward. The cascade vertical pulling strategy and the 3D circular arc interpolation algorithm and flying scissors algorithm of a 5-axis PAC control servo system is designed and implemented. The results of experiments and operating in the sites for years show high performance of the cascade vertical pulling artificial intelligent automatic yarn dropping robot for ring spinning.

title: Motion Simulation of Multi-type Surface Adsorption Robot for Power Energy Industry
authors: Congjun Ma; Hongxiang Zhang; Xiaolong Li; Songyi Dian
abstract: In the field of power energy industry, there exists a significant demand for equipment operation and maintenance. Amongst the various operation and maintenance scenarios, surface operation and maintenance is particularly ubiquitous. To overcome the challenge of surface operation and maintenance of key equipment in the power industry, an adsorption hexapod robot has been introduced in this study. The robot is capable of adapting to diverse surfaces and can achieve adsorption motion under specific configurations. In order to validate the robot’s ability to adsorb and traverse across multiple surface types, a full-real simulation platform has been developed in this research. The simulation verification has been conducted for three typical curved scenes, namely gas insulated switchgear in power grid with cylindrical surface, steam generator in nuclear power with spherical surface and wind blade in wind power with edge surface. The simulation results demonstrate that the designed robot can adeptly perform adsorption motion on various typical surfaces. These results can be utilized as a reference for further work to build a robot prototype and conduct adsorption experiments.

title: Acceleration Frequency Characteristic Compensation method of Electro-hydraulic Shaking Table
authors: Boxin Zhang; Guangfeng Guan
abstract: Electro-hydraulic shaking table (EHST) is the key equipment for vibration simulation. Feed-forward inverse model compensation (FIMC) control method is presented to compensate the acceleration frequency characteristic of the EHST. Firstly, the augmented UD identification recursive extended least square (AUDI-RELS) algorithm is used to identify the acceleration model of the EHST. The model order and the parameters are determined based on the loss function value. Secondly, the approximate inverse model of the non-minimum phase system is built based on the zero phase error method. Thirdly, the Lagrange function is used to design controllers and compensate for magnitude errors caused by zero phase error tracking control (ZPETC). Experimental results of the acceleration frequency characteristic analysis verify the validity of the FIMC control method.

title: Helical Propulsion in a Viscous Heterogeneous Medium
authors: Anke Klingner; Dalia Mahdy; Mostafa Hanafi; Barbara Adel; Sarthak Misra; Islam S. M. Khalil
publication_title: 2020 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: We characterize the propulsion of externally-actuated helical robots inside a viscous heterogenous medium. The method of regularized Stokeslets is implemented in three-dimensional space for computing the Stokes flow around a helical robot and immersed obstacles (spherical microparticles) in the medium. The helical robot is actuated using a permanent magnet-based robotic system with two synchronized rotating dipole fields. Our simulations and experimental results demonstrate propulsion enhancement with the concentration of the immersed obstacles in the viscous medium regardless of the actuation frequency. Numerical results show that the swimming speed is increased approximately by a factor of 2 for a 5% increase in the concentration of immersed obstacles with diameter of 30 μm, at actuation frequency of 1 Hz. At this actuation frequency, our experimental results show that the swimming speed is increased by a factor of 1.4. At relatively high actuation frequency (8 Hz), simulation and experimental results also show increase in the swimming speed by factors of 1.4 and 1.3, respectively.

title: Open-Source Tiny Two-Wheeled Inverted Pendulum Robot for Educational Purpose
authors: Kamil Przeczewski; Rafal Szczepanski
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The education of control theory requires experimental verification and interesting examples to keep the students focused during classes. In this paper a tiny two-wheeled inverted pendulum robot is presented for this purpose. The prototyped robot can be used for education related to microcontroller programming, discrete control systems, signal filtering, PID controller, wind-up phenomena, and cascade control structure. The paper presents the simplicity of the construction, firmware, and control application of a two-wheeled inverted pendulum. The possibilities are presented using the well-known cascade control structure with PID controllers. Moreover, the Madgwick's algorithm has been implemented to provide satisfactory tilt angle measurement using an IMU sensor. The results presented show that the prototyped construction of a tiny two-wheeled inverted pendulum robot may be used successfully for education purposes. The project has been published using the CC BY-NC license on GitHub repository.

title: Exoskeleton Upper Limb Robot: Classification; Key Technology and Research Direction
authors: Yecheng Ruan
abstract: As a human-computer interaction system, upper limb exoskeleton robots play an important role in rehabilitation medicine and human assistance by enhancing human strength and providing payload support. This article summarizes the functional classification, key technologies, and applications of upper limb exoskeleton robots. Firstly, the development status of upper limb exoskeletons at home and abroad was analyzed, and the classification of upper limb exoskeletons, including rehabilitation medicine and human assistance, was introduced. Typical exoskeleton robots with different driving and transmission modes were also detailed. Secondly, the key technologies of upper limb exoskeletons include control technology and drive technology. In terms of control technology, key technologies such as motion intention recognition, motion trajectory planning, and human-computer interaction were analyzed, and the application effects of different algorithms and methods were discussed. In terms of transmission technology, the advantages and disadvantages of electric motors, hydraulic and pneumatic modes, as well as direct transmission and cable transmission were compared. Finally, the future development of upper limb exoskeleton robots at the software and hardware levels was discussed, and improvement measures were proposed to enhance intent recognition intelligence, optimize trajectory planning, and enhance human-machine compatibility. This study provides theoretical basis and technical reference for the further development of upper limb exoskeleton robots.

title: Detection of Domain-Specific Hypernyms Using Named Entity Recognition and Extraction
authors: D.L. Prata; C.M. Mocan; C.I. Nandra; E.S. Chifu
abstract: This paper explores the task of hypernym detection in the medical domain, leveraging natural language processing techniques and machine learning. We address this challenge by presenting a solution to the SemEval-2018 Task 9: Hypernym Discovery, focusing on identifying hypernyms for specific terms within a given search space. Our approach involves integrating pattern-based and distributional methods to achieve wider coverage while maintaining accuracy. We illustrate the process of hypernym detection as a sentence segmentation problem, where each word is labeled based on its semantic category. Through empirical evaluation, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed solution, highlighting its performance metrics and execution times.

title: Improved Mapping Technique Based on ORB-SLAM2 in Dynamic Scenes
authors: Liangyu Wang; Zhijing Xu
abstract: At present, in the simultaneous localization and map construction (SLAM) algorithm, the more mature technology is the map construction in the static environment. However, there are currently moving objects in most environments, which will affect the accuracy and integrity of slam mapping. In this paper, we propose an improved vision SLAM based on ORB-SLAM2 that adds an independent parallel target detection thread to effectively filter low dynamic objects in the scene. Finally, we conduct an experimental evaluation using the TUM dataset, and the results show that our algorithm has a great improvement over ORB-SLAM2 in positioning accuracy and running time.

title: Instance Segmentation Based Non-Destructive Inspection of High-voltage Cable Defects
authors: Fangkun Shao; Xiaoxin Qi; Beiping Hou; Jianwei Dong; Wen Zhu; Jing Jie
abstract: The defect inspection of high-voltage cable is an important guarantee for the safe operation of cable. Traditional manual inspection is complex and costly. To solve this problem, this research combine X-ray NDT(non-destructive testing) with deep learning to propose an edge refinement mask network to improve the efficiency and accuracy of cable defect inspection. Specifically, in order to improve the accuracy of network inspection, this research employ a variety of data enhancement methods to extend the X-ray image dataset. For the cable defect edge, this study add the edge refinement operation after the basic example segmentation model, so that the segmented defect edge is more realistic.The experimental results show that the network defect detection accuracy proposed in this study reaches 91.6% and the detection speed reaches 54.7fps. Compared with the general defect inspection methods, the method in this paper has a greater improvement in accuracy and convenience.

title: A Leaf-Spring-Type Suspension Device for Compact Electromagnetic Vibrators
authors: Yu Gao; Wen He
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: The suspension device is important in an electromagnetic vibrator to provide linear elastic support for the moving component. This paper describes the design and modeling of a leaf-spring-type suspension device which is suitable for a compact electromagnetic vibrator. The suspension device consists of multiple horizontal and lateral leaf springs. Theoretical analysis mainly focuses on the internal forces and deformations of the suspension device under load, which is verified by simulation. Besides, the influence of thicknesses of lateral and horizontal leaf springs on the stiffness linearity and the modals of the support device are analyzed through simulation. Simulation results indicate that the use of lateral leaf spring can improve the stiffness characteristic significantly.

title: Steel Surface Defect Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8 Algorithm
authors: Wangqi Sheng; Ming Lu; Ying Zou
abstract: In steel surface defect detection, the typical characteristics of defects are irregular shapes and relatively small proportions of corresponding structures, which pose a challenge for conventional detection models. To address the issue of low sensitivity to these structures, this paper proposes an improved algorithm based on YOLOv8 for steel surface defect detection. The core innovation of the proposed algorithm is the design of a novel C2f_DSC module, which incorporates dynamic snake-like convolution to replace part of the C2f structure, thereby enhancing the model's detection performance. The approach begins by applying a convolution operation to the input feature map, which extracts higher-level feature representations. The receptive field of the network is then increased by stacking Bottleneck_DSC modules, allowing the model to better capture context information. Additionally, skip connections are introduced, enriching the gradient flow and facilitating the extraction of multi-scale defect features with greater diversity. Extensive experiments conducted on the NEU-DET dataset—an open-source collection of steel surface defects provided by Northeastern University—demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model. The results show a significant improvement in detection accuracy, with mAP50 and mAP(50-95) increasing to 81.6% and 47.0%, respectively. This demonstrates a substantial performance boost over the original YOLOv8 and outperforms other state-of-the-art detection models, making it a promising approach for real-world industrial applications.

title: On polynomial root distribution with respect to a sector
authors: Daniele Casagrande; Wiesław Krajewski; Umberto Viaro
publication_title: 2021 25th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper extends previous results of the same authors on the determination of the polynomial root distribution with respect to a sector by means of elementary vector analysis. Specifically, it is shown how the overall phase variation of any real or complex polynomial along the radii of a sector accounts for the number of roots inside and outside the sector. The method applies to both symmetric and asymmetric sectors with respect to the real axis. Its practical application only requires plotting a Nyquist-like diagram (a hodograph). The procedure proves particularly useful in the stability analysis of fractional-order systems. A pair of examples is worked out to show how the method operates.

title: Discrimination of the Near-Fault Pulse-Like Seismic Motions Based on Convolutional Neural Network
authors: Yucong Xu; Li Tan; Quan Li
abstract: Identification of near-fault pulse-like seismic motions are an important part of engineering seismic design. In recent years, the rapidly developing deep learning algorithm, with its powerful data feature mining and image recognition ability, can quickly and accurately constrain the attributes of earthquake events. By inputting seismic wave data and seismic time-frequency data, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to obtain the waveform and spectral features of the seismic events, thereby constructing an automatic classification network model based on the CNN algorithm for near-fault pulse-like earthquakes and non-near-fault pulse-like earthquakes. Based on the observed data of near-fault pulse earthquakes and non-near-fault pulse-like earthquakes recorded in the NGA-West2 strong-motion database, a deep learning training model is constructed and the model is trained to determine known near-fault pulse earthquakes. The results show that the CNN based on time-frequency data has a high recognition accuracy, with a recognition rate of up to 91.59%.

title: Restricted Spatial Perception-Based Robotic Unloading System Using Dynamic Grasping Strategy
authors: Zhaoguang Wang; Jinlong Wu; Jiabin Sun; Luning Zhu; Shuo Cheng
abstract: Unloading boxes from a container is daily operation in tobacco logistics warehouse which requires intensive manual labors. However, there are no existing proposals characteristic of versatile modules targeted for more general unloading scenarios. We present, in this paper, a more universal robotic manipulation system which can efficiently unload cardboard boxes from containers to subsequent storing cells. There are two novel contributions of our system. On one hand, we proposed an efficient restricted spatial perception framework which can precisely perceive, separate, and locate cartons randomly placed inside a container. A rotatable dual-camera setup provides a wide enough view window which assures our system could adapt to various containers of different internal dimensions. On the other hand, we designed a smart gripper with dual functionalities which can grasp a single or multiple cartons based on a novel reasoning and decision-making strategy. We deployed our system in a tobacco dock and carried out unloading tasks of more than 8000 cartons with no-prior unloading pattern, experiments not only indicated that our perception module could handle real-world scene in a precise way, but also showed a good result of grasping efficiency of more than 800 cases per hour.

title: Biomimetic Butterfly Robot Based on Flapping Wing Flight of Spotted Butterfly
authors: Chao Liu; Liuyi Shi; Zichang Deng; Siteng Ma; Aidi Zhang; Tangyan Song
abstract: With the advancement in bionic flying robot, flapping wing butterfly robots have become a hot research due to their unique flight mechanism and lightweight structure. This paper designs a bionic flapping wing butterfly robot, inspired by the flapping flight of the Papilio clytia. By mimicking the wing structure of the Papilio clytia and integrating micro servo and airborne component, the design can achieve flapping flight mode under low-frequency flapping. A SolidWorks-based kinematic simulation validates the rationality and stability of the robot's wing motion. Furthermore, a control system integrating PID and adaptive sliding mode control ensures flight stability under environmental disturbances.

title: Design Research on Shock Absorption in Biped Robots
authors: Fangzhe Shen
abstract: This study explores innovative design approaches for shock absorption in biped robots, emphasizing the integration of active and passive damping systems to mitigate the vibration issues encountered during locomotion on uneven terrains. As biped robots become increasingly important for intelligent services and automated operations, their stability and longevity are jeopardized by vibrations that may cause internal component damage and reduced operational efficiency. Our research presents a dual strategy combining an active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) model with a spring-running model, aiming to optimize shock absorption in response to varying operational conditions. Through dynamic simulations conducted in MATLAB, we analyze the impact of different values of spring stiffness k on the shock absorption performance, demonstrating that increased spring stiffness significantly enhances the system’s vibrational response. The implementation of the ADRC model further improved stability by effectively suppressing unnecessary vibrations. Overall, this research contributes valuable insights into improving the robustness and reliability of biped robots, ultimately enabling more efficient performance in diverse environments.

title: Automatic Reading System for Thermometer Verification Based on Image Recognition
authors: Yunguang Gao; Yaping Wang; Jibo Wu; Lü Wan
abstract: In order to improve the working efficiency and reading accuracy for glass liquid thermometer verification, an automatic reading system of thermometer was designed. On the one hand, the thermometer reading image was acquired after it automatically entered the reading window by the hardware; on the other hand, the image recognition and verification data processing were completed by the software. In the image reading recognition, an optimized image processing scheme was developed, the improved image tilt correction algorithm enhanced the reliability of thermometer tilt angle calculation; the gray stretch function and binarization algorithm were optimized and improved by the improved adaptive genetic algorithm to ensure to obtain the ideal binarization image; the combination of erosion and dilation algorithm got good image features while removing image noise, which provided ensure for the accurate reading; the verification efficiency was further improved by this optimized reading process. The experimental results show that the system can quickly and accurately recognize the thermometer verification reading, which also shows that the system can be effectively applied to the glass liquid thermometer verification.

title: Formation Control of Three Unstable Robots
authors: Dawid Knapik; Andrzej Turnau
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper focusses on distributed formation control, a task in which the desired formation shape is controlled by maintaining relative distances between robots. Robots are assumed to generate their own control only by observing each other in the absence of any central control unit. This task is based on the cyclic directed triangular formation with distance-based control. The novelty proposed in this work is the incorporation of unstable mobile robots that not only need to track distances in the formation control task but also stabilise itself around unstable equilibrium. An example application, serving as motivation for the analysis conducted, is the logistic task that requires a group of agile mobile robots to cooperate to achieve common goal, e.g. moving object.

title: Optimized PID Control for a Piezoelectric Bending Microactuator
authors: Mishek Musa; Uche Wejinya
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: In this work, an optimized PID control system based on the beetle antennae search (BAS) algorithm is proposed to be used to control the displacement of a piezoelectric bending microactuator. The microactuator is made up of a three layer composite beam with two layers of PVDF providing actuation and sensing while the third layer acts as a passive substrate. The system is controlled by a PID controller with optimized gains in simulation to minimize the mean squared error between the desired displacement and the measured displacement by the sensing layer of the microactuator. The theoretical model of the system, the working principle of the control algorithm, as well as simulation and experimental validation results are presented. The BAS optimized PID controller outperforms the standard Ziegler-Nichols PID tuning method in a simulated model of the microactuator and control system.

title: Mapping an unknown environment with explored area-detection
authors: Anna Barbara Ádám; Emese Gincsainé Szádeczky-Kardoss
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Mapping and exploring an unknown area is required in many fields of life. There exist rescue robots, which are able to explore dangerous, hard to reach areas. Other robots are used for exploring areas in order to find minerals or oils. This paper presents a method, which uses a lidar sensor for scanning the environment. The presented exploration method is applicable in corridor environments. The exploration path is planned by using an n-direction scanning detection algorithm. During the exploration, those areas are detected, which do not have to be visited again. In each step of the exploration, the currently seen area is approximated with a polygon, whose area is classified into two groups: those points, which do not have to be visited again, and those points, which should be visited again during the exploration. The exploration of example maps is presented.

title: Research on Wide Range Turbidity Detection Technology of Mine Water Based on Double Scattering Principle
authors: Baoyuan Chen; Xueming Wang
abstract: Aiming at the difficulties such as wide turbidity range of mine water, poor measurement stability, explosion environment of coal mine and stable uploading, a kind of wide-range turbidity detection technology of mine water based on double scattering principle is proposed, and an intrinsically safe wide-range turbidity sensor for mine is developed. In terms of hardware, the sensor utilizes high-performance imported photodiodes and precision operational amplifier integrated circuits. On the software side, through meticulous optimization of the signal conditioning circuitry, adoption of advanced sampling, filtering, and bubble elimination techniques, as well as implementation of multi-stage linear compensation, the sensor's turbidity measurement range and accuracy are significantly enhanced. The sensor uses OLED display technology to realize low power consumption design. In the digital interface communication design, anti-interference design is adopted and EMC Lv.3 experiment is passed, which is very suitable for use in the environment of strong electromagnetic interference in coal mine. The experiment proves that the measuring range of the wide range turbidity sensor used in the mine can reach 0~5000NTU, and the accuracy can be controlled within 4% F. S. By integrating with the mine monitoring system, the stable real-time monitoring of mine water turbidity can be realized on the surface.

title: Fault Diagnosis of Charging Piles Based on SPCA-ISSA-SVM
authors: Pangdi Peng; Xianbo Sun; Haoyu Jin; Kewen Dong
abstract: This study introduces a fault diagnosis approach for charging piles that integrates SPCA (Sparse Principal Component Analysis) with an ISSA (Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm) to optimize the SVM (Support Vector Machine), enhancing diagnostic accuracy. SPCA is used for dimensionality reduction, effectively capturing the nonlinear characteristics of fault data, reducing redundancy from external factors, and enhancing the accuracy of complex fault recognition. The sparrow search algorithm is enhanced by incorporating Levy flight and an adaptive t-distribution variation strategy, which ISSA then uses to optimize the hyperparameters c and g in SVM, a fault diagnosis algorithm utilizing SPCA-ISSA-SVM is presented. Experiments show that the accuracy of fault diagnosis reaches 94.4%, surpassing other diagnostic method and confirming the model’ s reliability and effectiveness.

title: A Systematic Framework for Design and Evaluation of Control Strategies for Continuous Manufacturing of Tablets
authors: Dana Copot
abstract: The pharmaceutical industry’s principal focus is on the move from batch to continuous manufacturing. The end-to-end continuous manufacturing process allows for ’on-demand’ tablet manufacture, with significant time, quality, and cost savings. To ensure an optimal production process and product quality, advanced solutions must be developed. However, the complexity of such production lines require a rigorous analysis and testing before deploying the control strategy to a lab-scale plant at first and then at industrial level. Thus, in this paper a novel and unique benchmark simulator for continuous manufacturing of tablets is presented. This unique en versatile simulator enable the design and evaluation of control algorithms in a systematic manner.

title: SLD-MAP: Surfel-Line Real-time Dense Mapping
authors: Xiaoni Zheng; Xuetong Ye; Zhe Jin; Tianyan Lan; Chaoyang Jiang
abstract: We propose a dense mapping algorithm based on surfel with line constraint, called SLD-MAP for room-scale and urban-size environment, which aims to improve reconstruction accuracy and reduce void space on the reconstruction surface. We apply visual odometry to estimate camera poses, and reconstruct the 3D environment according to the input depth image and RGB image. The first step is to optimize the pose with line constraints. The second step is to extract the superpixel and resize the radius and position of the superpixel with line constraints. The third step is to generate surfels and fuse them with local maps. The fourth step is plane fitting of local map. The last step is to update the local map and deform the global map. Finally, the reconstruction accuracy is evaluated on public datasets, compare with the state-of-the-art methods.

title: An Interface Design for Mooring and Refueling of Electric Propulsion Modules
authors: Kang Gong; Liming Hu; Licheng Liu; Dapeng Wang; Yongli Wang; Xiaoqing Liu; Tiejun Wang; Baiqing Tang; Gang Wang
abstract: Aiming at the insufficiency of the connection and separation technology between the space sub-star and the mother star, this paper puts forward a kind of electro-propulsion module mooring refill interface device, in which the electro-propulsion module establishes the mechanical connection, electric connection and gas circuit connection with the active end of the mother star interface through the passive end of the interface. After the completion of mass refilling, the electric push module is separated from the mother star and re-installed to the daughter star, realizing the connection separation function between the daughter star and the mother star, and the device has reusable characteristics. This paper designs the layout and structure of the electric push module mooring refilling interface, clarifies the working form of the electric push module mooring refilling interface, and carries out the static mechanics and kinematics simulation analysis of the electric push module mooring refilling interface, and analyzes the static mechanics and kinematics simulation of the electric push module mooring refilling interface. Modal analysis of the electric propulsion module mooring and filling interface can accomplish the task of connecting and separating the target reliably.

title: Effect of Network Size on Fractional-Order Dynamics in Large; Scale-Free Robotics Swarms and Platoons
authors: Bill Goodwine
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper studies the effect of the size of a large scale robot network on the fractional order of the dynamics of the step response of the system. We show that, for a scale free network with certain parameter values, as the number of robots increases the fractional order also increases up to certain size network, after which the order plateaus. In contrast, for a much more structured platoon network, the opposite happens. This paper presents those results and discusses some hypotheses attempting to resolve the apparent contradiction. We are interested in investigating the presence of fractional order dynamics in systems of this type because they are becoming increasingly common for large scale engineered systems. Very large scale systems can be difficult to design, analyze and control and understanding various approaches to determine effective and accurate reduced order models is important. A concise fractional order description of the dynamics offers insight into the nature of the system that may not otherwise be available through either the full, very large scale system dynamics or other types of reduced order models.

title: Magnetically Controlled Microfluidic Channels
authors: Ondřej Sodomka; Vojtěch Skřivan; Kateřina Jozová; František Mach
publication_title: 2022 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: A technological framework for entirely soft microfluidic channels controlled by an external magnetic is pro-posed. The crucial part of the channel is a multilayer structure compounded of a magnetorheological elastomer (MRE) and additional nonmagnetic layers that provide unique properties to the system. The proposed concept is studied by numerical simulations and experiments on laboratory prototypes.

title: Ship Dynamic Positioning Output Feedback Control with Thruster System Dynamics
authors: Dongdong Mu; Xiaomeng He; Qiulin Lu; Yunsheng Fan; Fei Pang; Fei Wang; Beibei Li; Mingyang Yin
abstract: In this paper, a novel backstepping controller considering thruster system dynamics is proposed. Firstly, a practical ship dynamic positioning control algorithm is formulated leveraging the thruster system dynamics, along with a finite-time convergent disturbance observer and an auxiliary dynamic system designed for finite-time convergence. The designed dynamic positioning closed-loop control system is uniformly ultimately stable. The advantages of the developed control scheme are that first, it addresses a multitude of potential challenges that the dynamic positioning system could encounter amidst intricate sea conditions, which is conducive to the implementation of the algorithm in maritime practice; Second, thruster system dynamics were considered to ensure smooth changes in actual control variables, aligning more closely with engineering realities. Finally, the control's effectiveness stays consistent. algorithm was validated through simulation, reinforcing its practical applicability.

title: Traffic Sign Classification Using Attention Fused Deep Convolutional Neural Network
authors: Shravan Venkatraman; A Abeshek; Santhosh Malarvannan; A Shriyans; R Jashwanth; P R Joe Dhanith
abstract: Autonomous vehicular technology, also known as self-driving or driverless technology, refers to the innovation that enables vehicles to operate without human intervention. Traffic sign classification (TSC) is a critical component in autonomous vehicular technology, as it allows vehicles to recognize and interpret traffic signs, which is essential for safe and rule-compliant navigation. This work proposes a novel attention-fused deep convolutional neural network (AFDCNN) for TSC. The proposed AFDCNN incorporates the capabilities of ResNet50 and EfficientNetV2 by combining their outputs through a self-attention mechanism which enhances its ability to classify traffic signs. Analysis of the GTSRB, LISA, and MASTIF datasets revealed that the proposed model exhibited superior performance compared to state-of-the-art models, as evidenced by higher scores in recall, precision, F1-score, and accuracy metrics.

title: Model-Compensated Active Disturbance Rejection Control for PMSM Based on Parameters Identification
authors: Hong Liu; Dewen Tian; Yaqing Wang; Huayuan Liu; Sifang Zhao; Ziyu Wu
abstract: To achieve high-speed and precise control of a servo permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) under multiple load conditions while mitigating the decline in dynamic performance caused by unknown disturbances and system parameter changes, an active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) method based on model compensation is proposed. Building on the foundation of a two-order position-speed compound ADRC, rotational inertia identification algorithm based on model reference adaptation is designed according to the mechanical motion equation of the PMSM. Additionally, a load torque observer based on the Luenberger observer is designed, which adaptively adjusts the control parameters of ADRC based on the identification and observation results. Simulation results show that the designed identification and observation algorithm are effective with a relatively fast convergence rate. The proposed control algorithm possesses superior parameter robustness and exhibits high control performance under multiple load conditions.

title: Paper-Based Microfluidic Assay for Gingipain Detection Using Fluorescent Quantum Dots
authors: Pavithra Sukumar; Mahmoud Elbeh; Zuzanna Bak; Mohammed Abdelhameed; Khalil Basil Ramadi; Mohammad A. Qasaimeh
publication_title: 2025 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: In this work, we developed and validated a waxpatterned, paper-based multiplex microfluidic device for the detection of Gingipain peptides, a biomarker associated with gum disease and Alzheimer's risk. The assay uses watersoluble fluorescent quantum dots (QDs) conjugated with Gingipain-specific peptides, confined within hydrophilic microspots on nitrocellulose membrane. The QDs were optimized for solvent compatibility, excitation wavelength (302 nm), and deposition volume. Plasma treatment improved fluid wicking on low-porosity membranes, enabling effective capillary-driven delivery within the multiplex layout. The final device includes three reaction chambers and one sample spot, with strong fluorescence observed only where QDs interacted with Gingipain, confirming detection specificity. This low-cost, disposable device shows promise for use in early-stage, point-of-care diagnostics, particularly for neurodegenerative risk assessment in dental or home-care settings.

title: Incremental nonlinear dynamics inversion for attitude control of high-lift hybrid mode UAV transition process
authors: Jiacheng Chi; Yujie Wang; Hongbo Xin; Qingyang Chen; Peng Wang; Zhongxi Hou
abstract: Hybrid mode UAV has a very broad application prospect in the future because it integrates the advantages of rotorcraft and fixed-wing. The high-lift hybrid mode UAV adopts the tailsitter configuration, but it has control difficulty lies in the attitude stability during the transition process. A complete dynamic model is established for the UAV. Based on the principle of time scale separation, attitude loop can be divided into angle outer loop and angular velocity inner loop. The attitude control of hybrid mode UAV transition is realized by incremental dynamic inversion method, and compared with the effect of the PID controller. The simulation results show that the proposed attitude controller is feasible, and has certain practicability, which can track the command attitude angle quickly with high tracking accuracy.

title: Research on the Role of MCP Regularization in Bearing Fault Diagnosis
authors: Hao Tian Jiang; Ting Zhang
abstract: In practical applications, the collection of bearing fault data often includes a significant number of invalid samples. When these data are used to train deep learning-based bearing fault diagnosis models, there is a risk of overfitting. Traditional methods, such as L1 and L2 regularization, are commonly employed to mitigate this risk. This paper proposes a novel regularization method based on the Minimax Concave Penalty (MCP) for deep learning models. Experimental validation was conducted using bearing fault data to train these models. Among the three groups of experiments, the highest average fault diagnosis accuracy after MCP regularization was 0.972. The results indicate that the MCP method demonstrates asymptotic normality in updating network weights and exhibits dynamic adaptability in penalizing the loss function. Therefore, the method proposed in this paper offers superior overfitting prevention in deep learning applications compared to L1 and L2 regularization.

title: Compliant Robotic Gripper with Integrated Ripeness Sensing for Blackberry Harvesting
authors: Arvyn De; Divyam Kumar; Ian Kwuan; Alex Qiu; Ai-Ping Hu
abstract: Global blackberry demand has been surging due to their antioxidant and nutritional value in a traditional diet. However, blackberries have extreme fragility (resulting in up to 85% of harvest batches sustaining damage) and near-ripe and ripe blackberries are difficult to distinguish in normal lighting conditions. These challenges in maintaining the blackberry supply motivate the development of an autonomous robotic solution to harvest fully ripe blackberries with minimal damage. The present paper details the mechanical design, methodology, analysis, and experimental results of a compliant robotic gripper created for this purpose. The gripper has a compact form factor and retractable fingers with specialized TPU finger pads for gentle picks, a near-infrared (NIR) reflectance-based probe for detecting full ripeness and a standardized harvesting sequence for effectively picking berries. In an outdoor harvesting experiment, the gripper attempted picking 26 berries without ripeness sensing, with 65.4% (17) being successfully picked and 38.5% (10) sustaining damage. The movements of the robot arm in the harvesting sequence were accordingly adjusted and finalized for following in-lab experiments, in which the gripper was also outfitted with ripeness sensing. Out of 40 berries, 62.5% (25) were successfully picked, with 0% of them sustaining damage. The ripeness probe classified 56 ripe and 11 near-ripe berries, with 89% (50) of the ripe and 64% (7) of the near-ripe berries being correctly classified. In a second in-lab experiment, 16 of 20 berries were successfully picked, with 2 sustaining damage.

title: Research on the Optimal Project of Unmanned Vehicles with Complex Constraints
authors: Mingxuan Zhang
abstract: With the continuous and rapid development of China's social economy, the number of motor vehicles continues to show a rapid growth trend, and the number of road traffic accidents continues to rise. The inducible factors of road traffic accidents include weak road infrastructure, imperfect legal system, vehicle failure and improper driver operation, etc. Among them, improper operation of drivers is the primary cause of major and malignant road traffic accidents, so improving the quality of driving behavior is the key to curb the situation of frequent traffic accidents [6]. And this also puts forward higher requests for autonomous driving technology. This paper mainly studies the optimal project of complex constraints for autonomous vehicles. By studying the optimal control problem model established by vehicle motion planning, the collision discrimination method based on graph area was found, and the constraints of collision avoidance between rectangular vehicles were established. Among the rectangular, double circle and single circle vehicle models, the rectangular model has a better constraint effect in the scene.

title: Development of Voice Controlled Wheelchair for Persons with Physical Disabilities
authors: Sumet Umchid; Veeraphab Sutthipibul; Arisara Vorapantrakool; Ponpalat Vipattipumiprates; Thidarat Wangkham
abstract: In the current day, wheelchairs are still used to help facilitate immobile disabled people to move to places. If a person with a disability can still use their hands and arms normally, they can easily control wheelchairs by pushing the wheels. However, current wheelchairs serve as a challenge for people with limited motor capabilities and missing limbs. Therefore, the objective is to develop a voice operated wheelchair, incorporating a speech recognition system to allow users to command the wheelchair's movements verbally. The voice commands are received through a microphone and processed by an Arduino UNO R3 microcontroller to control the motor circuit. To enhance the safety of the developed wheelchair, ultrasonic sensors are installed to detect obstacles and provide an audible warning. Additionally, an emergency stop button is included. The result from the testing of the voice controlled wheelchair show that it took an average of 98.2 seconds to travel over a distance of 30 meters, and the obstacle detection -in the 50-centimeter range- had an average error rate of 12.3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>.

title: Event-Triggering in Model Reference Quasi-Sliding Mode Control
authors: Katarzyna Adamiak
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This study considers a linear discrete time system subject to external disturbances and presents the design of event-triggered sliding mode control. The problem is organized in two main sections. First, we design a model-based reference trajectory. With application of a generalized non-switching type reaching law to the model, we achieve finite time convergence of the reference sliding variable to zero. Next, a model following reaching law is applied to the perturbed system in order to drive its representative point to the demand position in each step. However, we update the designed control signal only when a certain triggering condition is met, therefore implementing an event-triggered control scheme. In the model following approach this condition is based on the error between the reference trajectory and the actual position of the system's representative point. As a result we not only limit the impact of external disturbances on the system but also reduce the need for communication between the system elements and provide more time for the intersampling calculations.

title: Multimodal Spatiotemporal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for Extracting Metadata for Artwork Identification
authors: Huaitian Bi
abstract: As AI-generated art becomes more common, it becomes increasingly important to distinguish between works created by humans and those created by machines. This is essential for collectors, galleries, auction houses and museums. In this paper, we propose a convolutional neural network classifier for multimodal spatiotemporal graphs using metadata analysis. Key features are obtained by examining metadata obtained from digital artworks, including potential time spent on digital artwork, stroke order, and color selection, etc. These variables are then combined with digital artworks to form a data set, and digital art Item metadata is projected onto the graph structure, and then a multimodal spatiotemporal graph convolutional neural network classifier is employed to make classification decisions and generate spatiotemporal signatures of multimodal digital artworks. And the model is tested with other models on the existing digital artwork data set, and indicators such as F-1 score and Accuracy are obtained. The test results show that the method is superior in these indicators.

title: Enhancing Safety and Reliability of LNG Receiving Terminals through Data Security Monitoring Platform
authors: Lulu Chang; Jing Dong; Quanling Zhang; Cunsong Wang; Pengkai Wang
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the safety issues associated with LNG receiving terminals, which play a crucial role in the natural gas supply chain. Given the rapid growth of the LNG industry, ensuring the safe operation of these terminals has become a matter of paramount importance. The paper begins by introducing the process flow and highlighting existing safety concerns related to LNG receiving terminals. Subsequently, it proposes the implementation of a data security monitoring platform specifically designed for LNG receiving terminals, and explores key technologies for digital monitoring and intelligent operation and maintenance. Notably, this study focuses on equipment prediction maintenance technology and rollover prognosis technology, both of which contribute to the safe and stable operation of LNG receiving terminals. The findings presented in this paper are expected to significantly enhance safety, reduce accidents, and improve the overall efficiency of LNG receiving terminals.

title: Design And Trial Production Of Flying Flowers Detection And Information Processing Device Basis On Line Scan Camera
authors: Yuefei Wang; Kai Yu; Youyin Si; Kaiwen Duan; Ziyan Jiang; Haibing Gu; Zhanping Yang; Lin Shen
abstract: To address the inefficiency and error-prone nature of manual weighing methods used to detect the presence of short fibers, commonly known as “flying flowers,” in the acetate fiber tow used to make cigarette filter rods, a line scan camera-based visual inspection system was developed. This system operates on an open flying flower integrated machine, where the tow is subjected to specified speed ratios, and roll pressures on the roll, resulting in the opening and stretching of the tow. However, due to factors such as fiber wear and breakage, a certain amount of short fibers are produced. The newly designed visual inspection system aims to overcome the limitations of manual weighing methods and provide improved efficiency and accuracy in detecting the flying flower. This paper mainly focuses on presenting the comprehensive design scheme of the system, as well as discussing the structural composition and working principles of each component. The main objectives achieved include the automation of microfiber scene capture after manual sampling on the production line, the implementation of encoding, storage, reading and control of shooting light sources, and the successful development of Feihua intelligent detection system. In addition, through these information processing and development efforts, significant progress has been made in key technologies related to Feihua intelligent detection.

title: Flexible Target Grasping Strategy of Industrial Robot Based on Eye-in-Hand 3D Machine Vision
authors: Zhang XiaoYang; Muhammad Azmi Ayub; Fazlina Ahmat Ruslan; Shuzlina Abdul-Rahman; Sukarnur Che Abdullah
publication_title: 2025 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on [::Robotics::] and Technologies for Industrial [::Automation::] (ROBOTHIA)
abstract: Object grasping is the most common application direction of robots, and machine vision technology is also the most common application of grasping. With the deepening of the research of machine vision technology, the initial application in static target capture has gradually expanded to some moving target tracking and capture. Estimating and predicting the moving state of a target by detecting its position is a common method for obtaining a stable moving target. Once the target motion changes position due to unpredictable interference, the original predicted position will be invalid. Therefore, it is necessary to constantly locate and track the target and judge the deviation, so as to constantly approach the new target position and finally achieve the capture. In this paper, we utilize the open-source Robot Operating System (ROS) platform to investigate dynamic grasping strategies based on visual feedback. In this paper, we use ROS, based on UR5 robot arm and RealSense D435i camera, based on the eye-in-hand mode, to study the dynamic grasping strategy based on visual feedback. A visual feedback control strategy based on fixation approximation is designed to enable the grasping of moving targets on a conveyor belt. Finally, it is verified that the machine vision-driven feedback capturing algorithm substantially meets the practical application requirements of engineering, demonstrating high feasibility and accuracy.

title: Nano-Scale Fabrication and Characterization of Modified Re-Entrant Structures with Curved Corners Using EBL
authors: Kaustav Moni Bora; Ujjal Dey; Shailendra Kumar Varshney; Cheuruvu Siva Kumar
publication_title: 2024 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: In the domain of nanotechnology, the design and fabrication of intricate nanostructures tailored to specific functionalities have garnered significant attention, particularly in applications such as nanoelectronics, photonics, and sensor technologies. This study presents a pioneering approach to nanostructure engineering, focusing on a modified re-entrant structure featuring curved corners at the nano-scale. Departing from conventional re-entrant structures characterized by straight walls, our research introduces a novel innovation by integrating curved corners, thereby augmenting structural complexity and unlocking unprecedented possibilities in various applications. Central to our investigation are the design principles, fabrication methodology, and potential applications of this distinctive structure. Through meticulous optimization of parameters, including mechanical properties, we leveraged Electron Beam Lithography (EBL) as a precise and versatile technique to realize nanoscale features, including the desired curved corners. Subsequent SEM imaging and mechanical characterization employing a nanomanipulation tool provided invaluable insights into the behavior of the fabricated structure, thereby expanding its potential applications. The modified re-entrant structure exhibits promising prospects in the domain of nanoelectronics, offering enhanced mechanical and electrical properties. Furthermore, the tailored curved corners open novel avenues in photonics and plasmonics, presenting opportunities for the development of highly efficient optical devices. This study not only advances the frontier of nanostructure engineering but also lays the groundwork for transformative advancements with far-reaching implications in diverse technological domains.

title: Towards Efficient Motion Planning for UAVs: Lazy A* Search with Motion Primitives
authors: Wentao Wang; Yi Shen; Kaiyang Chen; Kaifan Lu
abstract: Search-based motion planning algorithms have been widely utilized for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, deploying these algorithms on real UAVs faces challenges due to limited onboard computational resources. The algorithms struggle to find solutions in high-dimensional search spaces and require considerable time to ensure that the trajectories are dynamically feasible. This paper incorporates the lazy search concept into search-based planning algorithms to address the critical issue of real-time planning for collision-free and dynamically feasible trajectories on UAVs. We demonstrate that the lazy search motion planning algorithm can efficiently find optimal trajectories and significantly improve computational efficiency.

title: Research on a Fin-Rudder-Propeller Integrated Underwater Robot
authors: Zhuo Ge; Bin Yang; Wen Xiong
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of a novel fin-rudder-propeller integrated underwater robot, which has high maneuverability and bionic movement ability. According to the structural form, Degree of Freedom (DOF) configuration and motion mode, the control model and vector control method of the robot is presented. In order to improve energy efficiency, driving performance, and obtain high torque density, electromagnetic design, simulation verification and structural design of the underwater rim motor used in the robot are carried out, and the physical prototype development of the underwater motor is completed. Based on the overall hardware design of the robot, the kinematics control model of the robot is established. Using the sliding-mode control method, a trajectory tracking controller is designed and verified by simulation experiments.

title: Enhancing Rehabilitation for Frozen Shoulder With a Two-Degree of Freedom Approach
authors: Shehla Inam; Faisal Amin; Hussain Al Faisal; Muhammad Waqar; Rahat Ehsan; Uzair Iftikhar
abstract: Frozen shoulder, also known as Adhesive Capsulitis (AC), is characterized by shoulder joint pain and restricted movement caused by capsule inflammation, which is frequently associated with injury, surgery, or illnesses such as diabetes. Current therapies, such as corticosteroid injections and rehabilitation exercises, have disadvantages, with injections being uncomfortable and potentially producing long-term damage, and rehab sessions commonly missed due to logistical difficulties. This research provides a remedy for AC using 2-degree of freedom (DOF) workout equipment designed specifically for the indigenous population to assist in executing critical rehab activities. Our results reveal that for flexion, the average angle at high speed was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$101.94^{\circ}\pm 11.26^{\circ}$</tex> and at low speed was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$103.10^{\circ}\pm 8.52^{\circ}$</tex>. For extension, the high-speed average was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$64.53^{\circ}\pm 14.42^{\circ}$</tex> and low speed was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$65.03^{\circ}\pm 14.06^{\circ}$</tex>. In abduction, the high-speed average was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$102.91^{\circ}\pm 6.84^{\circ}$</tex> and the low-speed average was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$102.56^{\circ}\pm 9.12^{\circ}$</tex>. For adduction, high-speed had an average of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$72.15^{\circ}\pm 13.70^{\circ}$</tex> and low speed was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$65.03^{\circ}\pm 14.06^{\circ}$</tex>. Thus, patients can utilize it independently or with physiotherapists, which will help reduce sessions and ensure effective exercise application at home.

title: How will Autonomous Robots be Viewed? The Influence of Robot Autonomy on Human Psychological Perception
authors: Yao Liu; Shilong Liao
abstract: Automatic machines have been controversial ever since their appearance, but the introduction of autonomous robots into the workplace seems to be inevitable. This article aims to explore how humans perceive autonomous robots. In this study, we examine the effects of robot autonomy on perceived behavioral control, perceived intelligence, behavioral desire, user intention, and eeriness. Participants watched a video of robots performing various tasks – these robots were presented as either autonomous and capable of disregarding human commands or non-autonomous and only capable of following human commands. Participants who watched the videos of so-called autonomous robots generally rated humans as having weaker control over their perceived behavior, behavioral desire, and user intention than those who watched videos of non-autonomous robots. On the other hand, exposure to an autonomous robot elicited a stronger sense of perceived intelligence and eeriness about the robot than those who watched videos of non-autonomous robots. Our research results provide help for the development of autonomous robots and provide new ideas for the relationship between robot autonomy and human perception.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning-Based Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance for Robotic Manipulators
