The results show that the proposed motion sensing model of the man-vehicle-moon system and the proposed driving motion sensing index can serve as the basis for motion sensing simulation training for the driving operation of manned lunar rovers and support the design of manned lunar rovers and ground simulation training for astronauts.

title: Research of a Predictable Wiebe Combustion Model for Engine Management System Development
authors: Wenli Wang; Zhengxing Dai; Yiqiang Liu
abstract: To match the real time requirement during ECU software development, the most common used engine model is map based. With increasing complexity of the software architecture, the need of a detailed engine model, which has knock phenomenon and response to spark angel retard, is also increasing. In this work, a predictable Wiebe combustion model is developed using MATLAB Simulink tool and integrated into GT-Suite environment to create a detailed 1D engine model, which can both accelerates software development process and increases ECU pre-calibration precision.

title: Research on Indoor Mobile Robot Localization Method Based on Improved MCL
authors: Yuqi Zhou; Huishen Zhu; Xunwei Wu; Yuanbo Chen
abstract: This paper proposes an indoor mobile robot localization algorithm based on improved MCL. The algorithm solves the kidnapped robot problem by introducing the average weight of particles to judge whether the localization fails suddenly; introducing KLD sampling to adaptively determine the particle set threshold according to the distribution of particles in the state space to reduce the algorithm computation, and designing the adaptive resampling rule to improve the particle degradation problem and improve the a posteriori confidence level. The odometer and lidar fusion localization simulation experiment is carried out with the two-wheeled differential mobile robot as the research object. The experimental results show that the algorithm proposed in this paper can enable the indoor mobile robot to recover from global localization failure, and can adjust the number of particles online over time to improve the stability, real-time, and accuracy of localization.

title: Predictor-Based State-Feedback Control of Lipschitz-Type Nonlinear Retarded State-Multiplicative Systems.
authors: Eli Gershon
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: We consider Lipschitz-type non-linear, discrete-time systems with statemultiplicative stochastic uncertainties in their state-space model and deterministic uncertain parameters that lie in a given polytope. We address the problems of predictor-based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> statefeedback control for both nominal and uncertain polytopic systems. The solutions to the said problems are achieved by applying a Luenberger-type predictor and via the use of linear matrix inequalities with a minimal number of tuning parameters. The theory is demonstrated by a numerical example that compares the various methods in our theory.

title: Research and Practice of CDN Accelerating Hot Internet Content Based on OLT
authors: Lingshan Kong; Zongze Liu; Guangyu Chen; Jing Yu; Chuan Fan
abstract: There are obvious differences between the popular network content accessed by end users covered by different OL T (Optical Line Terminal) network elements. The CDN (Content Delivery Network) network caches the popular content locally and schedules users to access it nearby through the DNS (Domain Name System) domain name system to achieve the content acceleration function. However, the traditional CDN cannot select different storage nodes according to the popularity differences of the content, and the user access scheduling can only be completed in the domain name dimension, unable to schedule different resources of the same domain name accessed by users to different node services. To solve the above problems, this paper innovatively proposes to reuse the idle board card position of the OL T device to set up a CDN logical sink node. Through the linkage of the hotspot identification algorithm and the BRAS information, it accurately judges the popular content accessed by users covered by different OL Ts, and caches the popular content to the CDN sink node. When users access, different nodes are selected according to the popularity difference of the content to provide services to users, so as to reduce the network transmission distance and improve the quality of service access for end users. Verified by the implementation in the existing network, this solution can significantly improve the hit rate and download rate of the service.

title: Parameter Optimization of Artificial Potential Field Algorithm for Local Path Planning Problem
authors: Rafal Szczepanski
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Local path planning problems are crucial for the safe operation of autonomous mobile robots in an unknown environment. One of the most commonly used algorithms is called an Artificial Potential Field. Its principle can be described as follows: the goal is pulling the mobile robot to itself, whereas the obstacles push it away. Although the principle is simple, the algorithm requires the definition of a few parameters. Improper selection may lead to unbalanced forces generated by the goal and the obstacles. This imbalance may cause a collision, highly unsmooth movement, or failure to reach the goal position. In this paper, the selection procedure for these parameters is considered. For this purpose, the optimization algorithm was used to provide the optimal solution for the dynamics of mobile robots and the environment for the defined objective function. The optimal parameters allow the selection of efficient Artificial Potential Field parameters, which provide superior performance for the considered scenario. The parameters obtained have been examined using a real mobile robot, Husarion ROSbot 2.0 PRO, in the Mobile Robotics Laboratory at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Torun.

title: Metal surface Feature Fusion for Defect Recognition
authors: Wenkai Lyu; Chengzhuan Yang
abstract: Metal sheets have been widely used in various industrial production and production life aspects. However, the surface of metal plates is prone to multiple defects, which affect the electromagnetic characteristics and coating effect of metal plates. Currently, mainstream inspection uses YOLO, PaddleClas, and other methods to detect flat metal surfaces. These algorithms are all very potent in their classification capabilities, but as generalized defect handling algorithms, they cannot be specific to each type of defect in a real problem. In this paper, we propose a multi-information fusion method for defect recognition. We consider both low-level texture features and high-level convolutional features of metal surfaces for defect recognition. We use a convolutional neural network as the main body and add extracted and processed prompts during training. Finally, we test the proposed method extensively on Camshaft and Kaggle metal surface defects datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves a state-of-the-art recognition performance that surpasses previous defect recognition methods.

title: Robustifying a Reinforcement Learning based Grasped Object Slippage Prevention Controller through Adaptive Sliding Mode Control
authors: Hirakjyoti Basumatary; Tamen Thapa Sarkar; Shyamanta M. Hazarika
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Maintaining a stable grasp on objects is a critical challenge in the realm of robotic hands and upper-limb prostheses. External disturbances often disrupt grasp stability, leading to slips. This paper explores the application of reinforcement learning (RL) for intelligent slippage control. However, RL-trained policies are susceptible to failure in perturbed environments due to dynamic variations. To address this limitation, we propose an approach of augmenting a pre-trained RL policy with an adaptive sliding mode controller, particularly suited for systems with continuous state and action spaces. Leveraging the invariance property of the sliding mode algorithm against uncertainties, our approach enhances the robustness of RL policies trained without accounting for diverse, dynamic variations in either simulated or real-world settings. Numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of our method in robustifying RL policies trained in simulated environments.

title: Addressing Different Goal Selection Strategies In Hindsight Experience Replay With Actor-Critic Methods For Robotic Hand Manipulation
authors: Ayman Shams; Thomas Fevens
abstract: One of the most challenging problems in reinforcement learning is dealing with minimal rewards obtained from an environment. We present a combined technique of Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient known as TD3, an off-policy Reinforcement Learning algorithm with Hindsight Experience Replay (HER). This combined technique allows for sampleefficient learning from sparse and binary rewards and avoids the need for complicated reward engineering. We use the challenge of moving things with a robotic arm to illustrate our methodology. We specifically tested six different tasks: pushing, sliding, picking up and placing in the Fetch environment, as well as manipulating a block, an egg, or a pen with our hands. We solely use binary rewards every time to indicate whether or not a task has been performed. In a comparative study, we primarily concentrate on the impact of various goal selection strategies of HER replay butter on both DDPG and TD3. We discovered that HER was crucial in enabling training in these demanding situations.

title: Tacking Control of Piezoelectric Stick-Slip Actuator Based on Integral Terminal Sliding Mode Strategy
authors: Piao Fan; YiKun Dong; Shai Yu; Zhenguo Zhang; Zengpeng Lu; Yan Li
abstract: Piezoelectric stick-slip actuators have influences such as model uncertainty, nonlinear factors and external disturbances that reduce control accuracy. In this paper, an integral terminal sliding mode controller is proposed for the precise positioning control of piezoelectric stick-slip actuators. The method can achieve convergence in finite time and serve to reduce the jitter steady-state error. The convergence law using a combination of power convergence law and exponential convergence law can reach the sliding mode surface at a faster rate. The stability of the control method is verified by the Lyapunov method. Finally, the effectiveness of the modified control method is verified by simulation. The results show that the control method improves the dynamic performance and stability accuracy of the system more than the traditional sliding mode controller.

title: The Exponential Turnpike Property for Neural Differential Equations
authors: Martin Gugat
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: We consider an optimal control problem where the tracking term in the objective function is related to a weighted <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{1}$</tex>-norm. To be specific, we study a system that is governed by a neural ordinary differential equation that is related to machine learning. We show that a simultaneous exact controllability property of the system implies an exponential turnpike property for the state. Moreover, we show that also the simultaneous exponential stabilizability of the system yields an exponential turnpike property.

title: A Practical HCI Evaluation Approach of Flight Deck
authors: Yuan Wang; Yuzhou Ding; Yao Zhu; Shasha Lu; Qian Shen; Pengyu Yang
abstract: To evaluate the Human-Computer Interface (HCI) of the flight deck effectively and thoroughly, a practical evaluation approach of flight deck has been proposed. This methodology involves conducting a series of crew-task-based human factors evaluations, and has gained widespread acceptance in both the design and iterative phases of flight deck. Through extensive practical application, this approach has demonstrated its importance and practicality, particularly in identifying potential human factors issues and analyzing design optimization requirements. It facilitates iterative upgrades of cockpit design during the initial stages effectively, thereby preventing potential human factors issues and ensuring design optimization and improvement.

title: Research on Motor Control Technology of New Energy Vehicle Based on MATLAB
authors: Kai Ma; Lige Ma; Chunhua Kong
abstract: As the world economy continues to grow, the rate of resource depletion is accelerating and global oil resources are becoming depleted, with the resulting environmental problems becoming increasingly acute. As a result, the use of fuel vehicles has gradually been restricted and the use of new energy vehicles is becoming more and more popular. New energy is shaping up to be more in line with the development of the times than traditional energy-driven models. At the same time, new energy vehicles promote the concept of environmental protection and are more competitive in the market. As one of the three major control components of new energy vehicles, the motor has extremely high requirements for its stability and safety, and more efforts should be made to develop and experiment with motor control technology to better meet the multiple needs of users. For example, the demand for miniaturisation, the demand for high kinetic energy, the demand for moderate price, etc. In this paper, the improvement of motor control technology for new energy vehicles is discussed based on the application of MATLAB for reference. The results prove that MATLAB is beneficial to improve the balance and efficiency of motor operation.

title: Attitude Recognition of Grasped Objects by Pneumatic Three-Jaw Manipulator with Flexible Electronic Skin
authors: Yuhao Zhao; Nengmin Liang; Chao Shang; Zhengchun Peng
abstract: When our hand grasping an object, the haptic system in the skin can perceive the pose of the object with high accuracy, even if the visual system is absent. In this work, we attach an electronic skin (E-skin) with an array of piezoresistive sensors to a pneumatic three-jaw manipulator to recognize the pose of the object grasped by the manipulator. With a 16×16 matrix pressure signal acquisition system, we collected about 260,000 sets of pressure data with spherical coordinate pose labels, trained the convolutional neural network (CNN) model and validated it with about 60,000 sets of data. The results showed that our system can recognize the attitude of the grasped objects with minimum errors of azimuth angle θ and polar angle ϕ in the pose angle reached 6.011° and 2.464°, respectively. For objects of different shapes, we employed transfer learning in the CNN model and the system can successfully perceive the postures of them with low errors.

title: Efficient Integration of Task and Motion Planner for Manipulation Tasks Using Geometric Spanner Graph
authors: Mukulika Ghosh
abstract: Integrating task and motion planning is challenging as task planners work in the discrete domain and computationally expensive motion planners in the continuous domain. A single-task action can be translated to infinite motion planning instances, resulting in a trade-off between computational cost and completeness. This paper proposes a novel approach to improve the performance of integrated task and motion planners by exploiting the spatial relationship of the objects, using a geometric spanner graph, namely, Yao graph. The proposed interface utilizes the spatial relationship to build constraints for the task planner, sample geometrically feasible poses for the motion planner to achieve and find objects to remove on failed motion planning attempts. The results demonstrate using spatial relationship improves the total planning time and success rate in benchmark environments for manipulation planning compared to traditional task and motion planning. The proposed method can automatically detect the inter-dependencies among movable objects with minimal overhead computation.

title: Nonlinear Convex Control Design for Differential Algebraic Equation Systems via LMIs
authors: Juan Carlos Arceo; Jimmy Lauber
abstract: This document presents an approach for nonlinear control design in singular systems by combining Lyapunov's direct method with exact convex structures. The conditions obtained are given in terms of linear matrix inequalities, the methodology proposed is illustrated by applying the nonlinear sector methodology to the mathematical model of a parallel robot for stabilizing it in a desired set point.

title: Autonomous Obstacle Avoidance for UUV Based on Global Guidance Vector Field and Local Particle Swarm Optimization
authors: Weining Li; Man Wang; Siyu Zhang; Junhao Zhou
abstract: Global trajectory planning and autonomous obstacle avoidance for unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) are crucial but difficult in unknown underwater environments. The paper proposes a comprehensive and efficient methodology, consisting of global planning with guidance vector field (GVF) and local autonomous obstacle avoidance with particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The initial GVF are first constructed based on pre-known currents and static obstacles, to guide an UUV to the destination or tracking a moving target along the shortest trajectory. In order to avoid unknown obstacles, the UUV must be equipped with forward-looking sonars (FLS) or other sensors processed in real time to provide obstacle detection information in the horizontal planes. The local PSO algorithm is introduced to modify the guidance vector field to guide UUV avoiding unknown obstacles safely. Finally, simulation results clearly demonstrate the proposed methodology enables UUVs to safely pass through obstacles in unknown environments.

title: Research on the Assessment Method of Lower Limb Muscle Fatigue Based on Surface Electromyography
authors: Bowen Li; Nan Su; Qing Tao; Zhiwei Zhou; Zhenning Yang; Hao Pei
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: Muscle fatigue frequently occurs in the rehabilitation process of patients. In recent years, time-domain parameters, frequency-domain parameters, and nonlinear methods have been widely applied in muscle fatigue assessment. This study introduces a new muscle fatigue assessment index: the Area Ratio Modification Index (ARMI). We compared it with seven common assessment indices - Mean Absolute Value (MAV), Root Mean Square (RMS), Integrated EMG (IEMG), Mean Power Frequency (MPF), Median Frequency (MF), Permutation Entropy (PE), and Approximate Entropy (ApEn). Ten healthy volunteers participated in muscle fatigue experiments involving isometric and isotonic contractions. The experimental results showed that as muscle fatigue intensified, the values of MAV, RMS, IEMG, and ARMI in the sEMG signals exhibited an increasing trend, while the values of MPF, MF, ApEn, and PE showed a decreasing trend. By comparing the change rates (CR) of these seven indicators before and after fatigue, it was found that the CR of ARMI was higher than the other seven indicators. Therefore, this study demonstrates that ARMI is an effective and sensitive muscle fatigue assessment index, offering higher sensitivity and effectiveness compared to the other seven indices.

title: Adaptive Multi-Scale Deep Feature Fusion Network for Joint Cardiac Registration and Segmentation
authors: Qifeng Zhao; Xuchu Wang
abstract: To achieve an effective representation of motion in cardiac anatomical structures, we propose an end-to-end adaptive multi-scale deep feature fusion network (AMF-Reg). AMF-Reg consists of two components: a registration branch and a segmentation branch. The registration branch employs an adaptive multi-scale feature fusion strategy, which enhances the model's ability to capture both local and global features by integrating multi-frequency and multi-scale information. The segmentation branch shares an encoder with the registration branch and utilizes the generated motion field information to perform anatomical structure segmentation. Simultaneously, weak supervision constraints are imposed on the registration branch to further optimize its performance, thereby improving the model's capacity for anatomical structure localization and topology preservation. Experimental results indicate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of registration accuracy and model generalization across both ACDC and CAP datasets, thereby underscoring its potential for application in clinical medical imaging. Our code is available at https://github.com/Pipixia911/AMF-Reg.

title: A Discrete-time Distributed Optimization Algorithm for Multi-robot Coordination Target Monitor
authors: Yanling Zheng; Qingshan Liu; Guoyi Chi
abstract: In this paper, the task of multi-robot coordination monitor as an optimization problem is formulated. The whole cost function consists of the sum of local cost functions for each robot to evaluate the best location. To encircle the target, a global equality constraint is introduced, and convex sets are built for the feasibility constraints of robots' location. Then, a distributed discrete-time algorithm is developed for the task of multi-robot coordination monitor, and it is also proven to converge to an optimal solution of the established optimization problem under certain initial restriction. Finally, a numerical simulation shows the effectiveness of the proposed distributed optimization approach.

title: Assessing the Stability of Linear Systems with Random Delays
authors: Jianqi Chen; Junfeng Wu; Qi Mao; Jie Chen
abstract: This paper explores the stability problems of discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) systems subject to random time delays. We first develop a general mean-square small-gain stability condition for feedback systems containing structured stochastic multiplicative uncertainties. Subsequently, we apply this mean-square small-gain condition to certain LTI random delay systems, where delays exhibit random delay lengths. Necessary and sufficient mean-square stability criteria are derived. These criteria, applicable to systems with either single or multiple sources of random delays, typically involve computing the spectral radius of a constant matrix. This computation allows us to determine whether a system's state variance matrix converges asymptotically despite the presence of random delays.

title: DADN: Data Augmentation-Driven Dual Network Framework for Node Classification
authors: Dengfeng Liu; Zhiqiang Pan; Siyuan Wang; Peihong Li; Shixian Liu; Yanying Mao
abstract: Node classification is an important task in graph neural networks (GNNs), aiming to predict the category of nodes in the graph according to their neighbours and their own characteristics. Current methods mainly focus on one level of data augmentation, ignoring huge potential in other underlying levels. Furthermore, existing models cannot fully exploit the information contained in the existing data, which undermines the performance of node classification. In order to solve the above problems, we propose a novel Data Augmentation-driven Dual Network (DADN) framework. Specifically, we first design a composite data augmentation module that comprehensively considers the local neighborhood level, the node level, and the edge level to augment the original features. Then, we copy the original features and the augmented features into the dual network framework with dropout for model training to capture the innermost features. Finally, we experimentally evaluate our method on three real-world public datasets, and the results show that our method outperforms the baseline models in the node classification task, except for individual metrics.

title: IoT-based Smart Municipal Garbage Management System for Fertilizer Processing System
authors: Riadul Islam; Anup Kumar Roy; Ali Ahsan; Md Mahfuzur Rahman Enam; Md. Tanvir Islam Mim; Abu Shufian
abstract: Food disposal is an important issue that has emerged in the modern world and has become more of a concern in our society in recent years, affecting both rich and poor countries. The Collection of waste is a much-needed municipal service for city people for environmental balance. This operation requires high expenses because of various factors such as manpower, navigation of vehicles, fuel, maintenance, and environmental costs. This study highlights a prototype that has been designed considering the above factors of essential implementation of the smart garbage bin to develop a proper municipal waste management system that is useful for the further fertilizer processing system. The prototype discussed here has been developed by a GSM module and ultrasonic distance measurement technology integrated into microcontrollers. This system has been simulated using EDA tools before hardware-based implementation according to the requirements. The proposed system offers a proper web server and SMS notification alert system to stop municipal garbage bins from overflowing. Using data server proper resources can be utilized such as creating location-based shortest paths and tracking worker’s performance, etc. A food waste management awareness system also can be displayed to raise public awareness for food scraps to be recycled and utilized to create fertilizer for new plantings. The suggested approach promises to contribute to a more sustainable and cleaner urban environment by encouraging citizen participation in recycling and trash reduction initiatives and optimizing waste management strategies for the respected organizations.

title: Application of PID Controller for Controlling Paddy Temperature in Hot Air Pneumatic Drying Process
authors: Aphisik Pakdeekaew; Krawee Treeamnuk; Tawarat Treeamnuk
abstract: This research aims to implement Ziegler-Nichols' method in tuning a PID controller for regulating the temperature of paddy during the drying process, referred to as the paddy temperature-controlled drying method (PTC method). The PTC performance and the quality of the dried paddy were compared with those of the air temperature-controlled drying method (ATC method). In the PTC method, the paddy temperature was consistently maintained at 42 °C, while in the ATC method, the paddy was dried using hot air at constant temperatures of 60 °C, 80 ° C, and 100 °C, respectively. It was found that the PID controller can effectively compensate for process errors. Although the maximum overshooting was 7.14%, the system was able to reach a settling time of 43 minutes, and process errors decreased with process duration. When comparing the PTC and ATC method at 60 °C of hot air temperature, the PTC method exhibited a higher drying rate and superior rice quality compared to ATC method by 15.21% and 6%, respectively. However, the specific energy consumption was found to be similar.

title: Single and Multiple Holes Image Visualization of Aluminum Surface Detected by Laser Ultrasonic Wave Technology
authors: Ali Wahab; Shaoyu Zhu; Weizhen Jin; Umair Iqbal; Hashir Azam; Yanjie Zhang
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: This study introduces a method for visualizing holes automatically utilizing ultrasonic wavefield pictures acquired by a noncontact laser scanning device. Hidden holes and leaks exist extensively in material structures in the industries, such as defense, aerospace, electrical power, oil and gas, and transportation, which affect the public safety and reliability seriously. Therefore, it is of great need to detect and monitor holes and leakage in materials. In this paper, based on the theory of laser ultrasound, an automatic laser scanner detection system (Lamb wave) was designed and developed. The laser scanning experiments were carried out on aluminum plates having holes through this system and the relationship among the laser wave energy, two-waves mixing interferometer TWMI and holes or leakage was analyzed. The visualization of the damaged area was achieved through the application of ultrasonic laser wave scanning principles. The efficacy of the suggested laser ultrasonic scanning equipment and imaging processing technique is confirmed through experimental validation using laser ultrasonic scanning images acquired from an aluminum plate. The results unequivocally demonstrated the successful detection and visualization of concealed and imperceptible openings or leaks on the scanned surface. In conclusion, the proposed method enables rapid detection and evaluation of defects, with the detection results being visualized. This highlights its great potential for market application in industries requiring efficient hole and leakage detection, addressing concerns related to public safety and reliability.

title: A Distributed Task Allocation Method for Reducing the Number of UAV Communications
authors: Shaokun Yan; Tao Wu; Fuming Wang; Shuo Zhang
abstract: The flexibility of UAVs and line-of-sight communication capabilities have made UAVs an effective solution to provide emergency services in many real-world applications. This paper solves the problem of invalid communication and excessive repeated communication between UAVs in distributed task allocation methods. Considering the time constraints of tasks and the range constraints of UAVs, the UAV clustering method is introduced into the Performance impact (PI) algorithm in this paper. The UAV clustering method can enable some UAVs to participate in consistency processing, solve task allocation conflicts between UAVs, and avoid repeated communication. Combined with the search and rescue application of UAVs, this paper studies the influence of the number of UAVs on the number of communications through numerical simulation and compares the simulation results with the PI algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce the number of communications between UAVs.

title: A Human Factors Validation Methods Incorporating the Degrees of Novelty; Complexity; and Integration of Cockpit Design Items
authors: Qian Shen; Shasha Lu; Yao Zhu; Yiyuan Zheng; Pengyu Yang
abstract: This paper introduces a comprehensive Human Factors validation framework for CS25.1302 regulation, explaining how the degrees of novelty, complexity, and integration impact the level of scrutiny required for aircraft cockpit design items. The background underscores the role of human factors consideration for new, complex, and integrated designs in aircraft cockpit. The study aims to provide designers and regulatory authorities with a systematic methodology for determining appropriate means of compliance tailored to the varying degrees of novelty, complexity, and integration of design items. This method outlines the process of selecting a reference aircraft, participants, criteria employed, and how to carry out the assessment. Furthermore, it proposes the framework for selecting appropriate means of compliance considering the level of scrutiny supported by a case study. This framework not only optimizes the Human Factors evaluation procedures but also develops more reasonable scrutiny strategies. This, in turn, contributes to the overall enhancement of cockpit design safety and reliability.

title: Enhancing Electromechanical Coupling: A Modified Model for Studying Uterine Myometrial Contraction
authors: Mengying Wang; Luyi Ruan; Yiwei Lin; Zhenqin Chen; Jinshan Xu
abstract: The mechanism of uterine electromyographic signals and mechanical contractions is a significant research topic. In this study, we propose a novel electromechanical model that utilizes the FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) model to simulate the enhanced excitability of uterine cells influenced by hormones, leading to the successful generation of pacemaker behavior upon the introduction of small perturbations. Furthermore, we observe that as pregnancy progresses, enhanced gap junction, anchoring junction, and electromechanical coupling activity contributes to global mechanical contraction synchronization. Our research results also demonstrate a considerable level of synchronization between electrical and mechanical signals, providing robust theoretical support for the practical application of electrical signals. These findings deepen our understanding of electromechanical coupling effects and offer new perspectives for research and applications in related fields.

title: Lightweight Underwater Target Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv7
authors: Huihui Guo; Liang Chen; Junwei Yang; Shaowu Zhou; Tao Yin
abstract: Underwater robots frequently grapple with challenges such as false detection and missed detection due to factors like turbid water and low contrast of detected objects. These issues significantly hinder the efficiency and accuracy of underwater exploration tasks. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel lightweight underwater target detection method based on an improved version of the YOLOv7 model. The core innovation lies in the integration of the GhostNet network as the backbone of the proposed method. By leveraging GhostNet's efficient architecture, we manage to drastically reduce the overall parameter quantity and eliminate excessive redundant feature information within the network. This not only results in a more compact network model but also enhances the overall detection accuracy. Furthermore, to broaden the network's receptive field and capture more intricate details, we introduce the MP-D module. This module cleverly employs dilated convolutions to replace the conventional downsampling convolutions, thereby enabling the extraction of more precise positional information of small targets without incurring additional computational overhead. The experimental results underscore the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm. Compared to the original YOLOv7 algorithm, our method achieves a significant reduction in model size by 24.6MB and a notable decrease in parameter quantity by 35.3%. Moreover, it boosts the recall rate by 5.5% and the mean Average Precision by 1.2%, demonstrating its robustness and superiority in underwater target detection tasks.

title: New Trends In Industry 4.0 – Voice Control
authors: Jakub Szaj; Janusz Pochmara
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper presents the possibilities of controlling a robotic arm using voice commands with the use of an external API responsible for speech-to-text translation. The article describes the creative process of designing the robot model and user interface included in the simulator used to control the robot. The software was developed in the Unreal Engine 4.27.2 environment using the built-in visual programming language - blueprint, as well as C++ and Python. The three-dimensional model was created entirely in Blender 3D software. The simulator's task is to faithfully reproduce manipulation of simple objects in real-time, as well as record and load the manipulator's trajectory along with all objects on the scene.

title: Advancements in Small-Scale Fuel Cell Controller Evolution through Automated Code Generation: A Scientific Approach
authors: Xiaojie Jiang; Fengxiang Chen; Yaowang Pei
abstract: The fuel cell controller, positioned at the core of the fuel cell system, orchestrates control and monitoring functions to ensure operational efficiency and stability. This paper outlines the design of a fuel cell controller characterized by robust versatility, abundant peripherals, and cost-effectiveness, leveraging the STM32F407 platform. Subsequently, a comprehensive suite of automatic code generation strategies, centered on Waijung1 within the Simulink environment, is introduced, streamlining algorithm development. These methodologies are then employed to rigorously experiment and validate the controller's performance. The test results showcase the controller's elevated precision in signal output and data detection. The output signal error remains under 0.1%, the captured signal error is contained within 0.4%, the sensor error is restricted to less than 1.5%, and the overall controller cost is reduced by 25%-30%, attesting to the precision and cost-effectiveness of the system. The automatic code generation solution significantly reduces the software development cycle by more than 30% compared to traditional C language development approaches, highlighting significant advancements in efficiency.

title: Mixed Node and Edge GraphSAGE Based Schema Encoding for Text-to-SQL
authors: Zhicheng Liao; Jiawen Yi; Guo Chen
abstract: In text-to-SQL tasks, it is important to construct a model that is applicable in databases of different domains, and how to improve the generalization and induction capabilities of the model is a pivot challenge to be addressed. Traditional approaches are limited by the following shortcomings: 1) limited to transductive models, which do not perform as well as inductive models when generating embeddings for unseen nodes of graphs in cross-domain scenarios; 2) insufficient attention to the importance of structural information in relational databases and do not distinguish local and non-local relations. Therefore, we propose a Mixed Node and Edge Graph SAmple and aggreGatE text-to-SQL model, MNEGraphSAGE for short, which is based on graph sampling and propagation algorithm for node and edge features and converges faster. We give full attention to graph network edge features by mixing the iterative process of edge features and node features in parallel. We also adopt different aggregation methods for edge features of different distances. In the Spider dataset covering multiple domains, our method achieves 64.02% without the help of pre-trained models, outperforming other models of the same size.

title: Design of seven-function master-slave underwater electric manipulator
authors: Zejun Sun; Zhenzhong Chu
abstract: This paper presented a seven-function master-slave underwater electric manipulator. The forward kinematics equation of the manipulator was deduced by the DH parameter method. And use the Robotics toolbox in Matlab to establish a model of the robotic arm. After that, the simulation model was compared with the kinematics structure of the manipulator. The calculated working space was more than 1.5m by the Monte Carlo method verified that the manipulator meets the design requirements. The master control part selects the touch tactile device. The main parameters of the haptic device were obtained by the callback function in the serial communication transmitted to the master to realize the master-slave control of the underwater electric manipulator.

title: Strategic Maintenance Optimization for Enhanced Operational Efficiency of Railway Station Infrastructure
authors: Katarzyna Grobler-Dębska; Rafał Mularczyk; Waldemar Bauer; Edyta Kucharska
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Effective maintenance is a hard but very important task allowing keeping assets in operation. In particular this is something very relevant for critical infrastructure that are railways and railway stations. European wide analyses show, that there is no harmonization in data standards nor there are good solutions allowing to assist station operators in maintenance management. In this paper we focus on handling available data streams, integrating them with a data lake based centralisation and using it to provide a decision support system. Such system, based on dashboards created with Business Intelligence software, can provide significant help in managing of assets. As an example we provide appropriate routing mechanisms allowing to use the available maintenance personnel with more efficiency.

title: Anti-Corner Reflector Jamming of Radar Seeker Based on Extreme Learning Machine
authors: Tianxiang Tang; Linmao Qiu
abstract: Radar seeker is the key equipment for terminal guidance of precision-guided weapons. It has significant advantages such as long-range detection range and weather protection, and plays a vital role in ensuring missile strike accuracy. In recent years, high-resolution radar seekers have been the main development object to ensure the improvement of identification accuracy and accuracy of missile-borne radar seekers. Corner reflector has the excellent characteristics of high scattering fidelity with real target, high combat cost-efficiency ratio, and has become one of the main deception and jamming means of radar seeker, which seriously affects the detection performance of radar target. Corner reflectors are often placed around armored targets. Because of the complexity of ground clutter, the scattering characteristics of corner reflectors under different ground conditions are complex and changeable, which is a powerful interference used to affect radar detection of ground armored targets. In this paper, based on extreme learning machine (ELM) training algorithm, the proposed framework can use a variety of feature mapping functions or kernels, and the proposed method can be directly applied to regression and multi-classification tasks to classify ground battlefield angular anti-jamming and real armored targets. Using the measured echo data of radar seeker, the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified, and the correct recognition rate is 90% in actual back-end data processing.

title: Application of a Deep Learning-Based Heuristic for Weighted A-Star Algorithm
authors: Bálint Boczka; Márton Pluzsik; Tamás Mocsai; János Botzheim; István Reményi
abstract: The A-Star algorithm provides an excellent graphical framework for optimal path generation between a designated start and goal position pair. Its performance comes from the fact that, at any time, it can estimate the amount of the remaining distance and steer the next step selection in the right direction. One of the main issues with the generally used heuristics is that it can not really do scene understanding, for example, to consider the obstacles. In scenarios with surrounding objects, the runtime of A-Star is considerably higher due to the spanning of the search tree with high-node expansion being hindered around the obstructions. The introduction of the weighted extension brought a trade-off between optimality and speed, and to further influence its calculation resource needs, we created a deep learning-based solution, to encode the surroundings in the format of a birds-eye-view image and utilizing this to regress the remaining path length to a given goal position. We used this estimation as a replacement for the classical heuristics and integrated it into the planning solution to measure its effect on system performance.

title: Applications of Hybrid Conditional Planning in Service Robotics
authors: Ahmed Nouman; Muhammad Khurram Saleem
abstract: Hybrid planning computes task plans in full observability (a sequence of possible actuation actions) via the integration of low-level feasibility checks in classical planning approaches. Conditional planning extends the classical planning framework to account for plans under partial observability. We use a hybrid conditional planning approach to compute plans that include sensing and actuation actions in solving real-world problems by addressing uncertainties due to incomplete information at the planning phase. We generate a hybrid conditional plan of actions using parallel instances of a non-monotonic hybrid HCPLAN that supports defaults, integration of external computations, and non-deterministic actions. We show our hybrid conditional planning framework's HCPLAN applicability through service robotics scenarios with manipulation and navigation tasks. Furthermore, we evaluate the effect of parallel threads on the computation of hybrid conditional framework on different benchmark scenarios for the service robotics domains.

title: PDAOD: An Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Method for Orchard Apple
authors: Zhiyu Yang; Yanan Li
abstract: Traditional unsupervised domain adaptation methods are limited in agricultural object detection due to small target sizes and cluttered backgrounds. The PDAOD-Net model is introduced, offering the capability to dynamically distribute attention between localization and classification tasks in a flexible manner. By utilizing point confidence matrix alignment to achieve precise domain adaptation, experiments show that PDAOD-Net achieves superior performance on apple orchard datasets, outperforming existing methods by approximately 5.8% in AP.

title: An Improved YOLOv5 Model for Detecting Citrus Shoots in Complex Orchard Environments
authors: Feng Xiao; Haibin Wang; Tianqi Huang; Yueqin Xu
abstract: The development of citrus shoots is of great significance for the growth, flowering, fruiting, and pest and disease control of citrus trees. In order to achieve accurate recognition of citrus shoots in complex orchard environments, an improved YOLOv5 model, named YOLOv5-RepVGG-SE, was proposed. Firstly, in order to enhance the feature extraction capability, the Rep VGG modules are used to replace the Conv modules in the backbone networks of the YOLOv5 model. Second, the Squeeze-Excitation (SE) attention modules are added to the neck networks of the YOLOv5 model to improve the feature fusion capability. A dataset of citrus shoots was established to evaluate the effectiveness of the improved YOLOv5 model. The experimental results show that the improved YOLOv5 model achieves a precision (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>) of 81.1 %, a recall (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>) of 76.8%, and a mean average precision (mAP) of 71.0% at a threshold of 0.5. These values are 0.6%, 9.20/0, and 9.4% higher, respectively, than those of the YOLOv5 model. This research can serve as a reference for the development of smart devices in citrus orchards.

title: Quasi-Phototaxis in Slime-Type Molecular Robots
authors: Shogo Hamada; Sota Kumagai; Shin-ichiro M. Nomura; Satoshi Murata
publication_title: 2025 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Light-responsive molecular robots that are capable of phototaxis are expected to be utilized in various applications, from biomedical to materials and to environmental fields. However, implementation of such reactive paradigm in molecular robots is still in its infancy. As a critical step towards achieving phototactic behavior, here we introduce 3-Cyanovinylcarbazole nucleoside (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${ }^{\text{CNV}}$</tex> K), a reversible photocrosslinker, as a light-induced trigger for the dynamic structure generation mechanism of artificial metabolism in slimetype molecular robots. Quasi-phototactic behavior is demonstrated through pre-irradiation of UV light with specific wavelengths to the generation mix of slime-type molecular robots. The reaction results in directional locomotion within Y-shaped microfluidic device towards the channel with the generationtriggered side, representing an analogy to Braitenberg vehicle 2a motion based on the molecular-level control of the metabolic pathway. Further development is anticipated to yield more dynamic and complex behaviors, paving the way for molecular cybernetics, and ultimately, the realization of active, intelligent, and adaptive synthetic matter.

title: Ab Initio Gene Identification Using Apache Spark
authors: Simion-Daniel Tatar; Gheorghe Sebestyen
abstract: Computer-assisted gene identification in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequences is a challenging task, which requires intelligent pattern recognition algorithms as well as significant computing power. Gene recognition has increased importance today, when medical treatment of a patient should be adapted to the inherited features of each individual; these features may be identified through the patients’ DNA. Gene recognition is also important for identify pathological organisms and their resistance to different treatments (e.g. antibiotics). In order to allow adaptive treatment of patients, gene identification must be fast, accessible and precise. In this paper we concentrate on formulating the problem of gene identification, on determining the most popular approaches and also on finding a parallelization procedure that can reduce the execution time of an identification algorithm.

title: Communication Relay Tasks Planning Algorithm for Multiple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
authors: Ruowei Zhang; Lihua Dou; Bin Xin
abstract: With the progress and development of technology, the application of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV s) has been greatly expanded. UAV s can be seen in agriculture, military, and express delivery industries. Now, UAVs performing various search, reconnaissance, and communication tasks in urban environments have become a hot research topic. For communication relay tasks, this paper proposes an iterative search optimization algorithm based on a time matrix to solve the task planning problem of multiple UAV s. Firstly, the rapidly-exploring random tree algorithm is used to construct the distance matrix between tasks. Then, the distance matrix is converted into multiple time matrices based on the speed of the UAV s. Secondly, the iterative search optimization algorithm is used to plan the task sequence of the UAV s. The constructed time matrices participate in the decoding and constraint judgment process. Finally, different scale instances are designed for experiments to compare the performance of the algorithms.

title: Frequency-Enhanced Dual-Domain Attention Network for Automotive Intrusion Detection System
authors: Weiming Ren; Yongyi Chen; Dan Zhang
abstract: For the security of autonomous vehicles in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), the intrusion detection system (IDS) is developed to detect malicious behavior and identify potential threats. Deep learning (DL)-based IDS for controller area network (CAN) bus have shown excellent performance. However, most existing DL-based IDSs only classify data into normal and attack categories, which is not conducive to subsequent datatargeted remediation. To more granularly detect and classify cyber-attacks, this paper proposes a frequency-enhanced dual-domain attention network for automotive IDS (FDAN-based IDS). FDAN-based IDS can classify the types of cyber-attacks more accurately enhancing frequency features and generating attention weights from the channel and spatial domains, respectively. To evaluate the performance of FDAN-based IDS, experiments were conducted on the Car-Hacking dataset used for most research. FDAN-based IDS has good classification performance in a wide range of cyber-attacks, which is superior to other similar algorithms.

title: Research on Hotel Comment Emotion Analysis Based on BiLSTM and GRU
authors: Tingting Wu; Gengsheng Zheng
abstract: Aiming at the problem that LSTM can not deal with the long-distance two-way semantic dependence, complex model calculation and long training time, this paper proposes a C-BiLG deep learning algorithm based on two-way LSTM and GRU for emotion analysis task. Two-way LSTM has fewer parameters and faster model training, which can effectively extract the deep-seated information of the text. The combination of BiLSTM and GRU can solve the problem of semantic dependence and gradient disappearance. According to the control experiment, the experimental results show that the algorithm can improve the accuracy and optimize the classification effect in the emotional analysis of hotel comment data set.

title: ES-MSCNN: An Echo State Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network for Multi-Step Prediction of Wastewater Quality Variables
authors: Yue Sun; Yiqi Liu
abstract: Given the limitations of hardware sensors together with strong nonlinearities and nexus between variables in wastewater treatment processes (WWTPs), the measurement of key quality variables is usually inaccurate or even impossible. Moreover, due to the short data sampling period, the single-output single-step prediction model cannot meet the actual demand. Therefore, this paper proposes a new soft sensor, termed as the Echo State Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network (ES-MSCNN), designed for accurate multivariate multi-step prediction. ES-MSCNN first generates an echo state representation (ESR) containing temporal information through an echo state network (ESN). Subsequently, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is employed to avoid the shallowness of ESN and further extract high-dimensional feature information from the data. Besides, a multi-scale learning strategy is used in the convolutional module to capture multi-timescale features and improve the multivariate prediction accuracy. Validation on the benchmark simulation model 2 platform and comparison with several models indicate that the proposed ES-MSCNN has higher accuracy and stronger robustness in multi-step prediction tasks with multi-input and multi-output.

title: Structural Design/Manufacturing and Cavitation Efficiency Calculation of the Bio-Inspired Snapping-Claw Apparatus
authors: Hang Yin
abstract: The snapping shrimp's unique claw structure enables it to produce high-energy cavitation bubbles instantaneously during hunting, inspiring the development of a high-efficiency cavitation generator. This paper simplifies the structure of the shrimp's claw to design a new bionic snapping-claw apparatus, and uses a torsion spring as its driving mechanism. The proper spring was selected by solving the relevant established kinetic equations, and the bionic snapping-claw apparatus was manufactured using a five-axis high-speed processing center. Additionally, the principles of energy conservation and equivalent thought were applied to calculate the cavitation efficiency of the bionic apparatus, revealing an impressive efficiency of 25.6%, outperforming most existing cavitation generating devices.

title: Research on Off-line Handwritten Digit Recognition Algorithm Based on Binary Classification Tree
authors: He Kai-lin; Luo Jia; Ding Xiao-feng
abstract: A handwritten numeric recognition algorithm based on holistic feature (concave and convex) is proposed in document [6], Although the effect is good, this algorithm is only suitable for the sample of the writing specification, in real life, the numbers have a variety of deformations by the randomness of people’s writing, it affects the recognition rate of this algorithm. This paper is proposed a novel off-line handwritten numeric recognition algorithm based on binary classification tree. It is improvement through background correction improvement, concave and convex features improvement and classification tree improvement. The experimental results show that the algorithm in this paper has been improved in the original recognition rate and is more adaptive to the deformation of handwritten numerals. The recognition of handwritten numbers is more extensive. At the same time, compared with other popular contour based features and neural network based algorithms, there is an obvious advantage in speed.

title: Reduced-Order Model-Based Gait Generation for Snake Robot Locomotion Using NMPC
authors: Adarsh Salagame; Eric Sihite; Milad Ramezani; Alireza Ramezani
abstract: This paper presents an optimization-based motion planning methodology for snake robots operating in constrained environments. By using a reduced-order model, the proposed approach simplifies the planning process, enabling the optimizer to autonomously generate gaits while constraining the robot's footprint within tight spaces. The method is validated through high-fidelity simulations that accurately model contact dynamics and the robot's motion. Key locomotion strategies are identified and further demonstrated through hardware experiments, including successful navigation through narrow corridors.

title: A Cloud-Based Remote Management System for Disinfection Robots: Integrating Alibaba Cloud IoT and WeChat Mini-Program
authors: Wei Dai; Lin Zhang; Limin Yu
abstract: Disinfection robots, as part of the prevention and control measures, are of great importance in the post-pandemic area. Traditional disinfection robots have faced challenges in manual operation risks and human-machine coexistence. This paper proposes a cloud-based remote management system using Alibaba Cloud IoT and WeChat Mini-Program. The system employs the MQTT protocol for real-time data transmission, with Alibaba Cloud handling device authentication, data storage and rule-based message routing. A WeChat Mini-Program serves as the user interface, enabling operators to monitor robot status (battery level, disinfectant volume) and control UV lamps/sprayers remotely. The experimental results demonstrate an average network delay of 1.989 seconds and operational prevision of 98 %. The system design provided a low-cost and scalable solution for reducing infection risks in public health scenarios, enabling safe and efficient disinfection operations in hospitals, schools, and public buildings.

title: Coupled; closed-system fluidic actuators for use in wearable rehabilitation devices
authors: James Greig; Maria Elena Giannaccini; Edward Chadwick
abstract: This paper presents a novel closed-system, coupled soft actuator that aims to increase the applied bending moment that can be powered by a single pneumatic pump. The actuator incorporates both positive pressure and vacuum actuators of established design. The purpose of this development is to enable the design of an effective soft robotic wearable device for the re-habilitation of the revolute joints in post-stroke individuals. The design of a test rig to provide consistent, quantitative data on the output of the soft actuators is presented, allowing a comparison of the positive pressure, vacuum and combined (positive and vacuum) actuators. This combination demonstrates the ability to significantly increase the torque output when compared to a single actuator using the same pump for input, potentially reducing the weight of a wearable device. The closed-system, coupled soft actuator system shows opportunity for use in a wide range of applications due to this reduction in pump weight and isolation from environmental conditions.

title: Camera Calibration Model Comparison for Marker Position Estimation
authors: Shannon Van De Velde; Risang Gatot Yudanto; Sam Weckx
abstract: In this study, we investigate the impact of different camera calibration models on the accuracy of fiducial marker position estimations. With a perfect calibration, the positions of detected marker corners in the image should precisely match the projections of their physical coordinates onto the image plane. The extent and nature of any divergence serve as crucial indicators of position estimation accuracy. Our findings reveal a symmetrical divergence, corresponding to low position estimation accuracy in the direction perpendicular to the image plane and in the plane an accuracy decrease with the distance from the center. This knowledge is important to be able to account for these errors in practical applications. Future research will aim to develop strategies to correct these errors effectively.

title: Vehicle Formation Matching and Simulation in Cooperative Vehicle Infrastructure System Environment
authors: Yuyan Wang; Shufeng Wang; Jie Zhang; Junyou Zhang; Yinhao Wang
abstract: In order to solve the problem that independent vehicles can choose the best formation to join, this paper proposes a vehicle formation matching strategy in cooperative vehicle infrastructure system (CVIS). Firstly, a description of the formation matching problem in the highway scenario is given, and secondly, the objective function of the formation matching problem is constructed and the corresponding constraints are set. In this way, matching algorithms for centralised and distributed formations are obtained. Finally, based on the set conditions, the formation matching strategy in the scenario of this paper is simulated and verified. The results show that based on the proposed formation matching strategy, the pass time is reduced by 381s and the energy consumption is improved by 38.7%,31.8%,40.6%,26.2%,22.1% and 29.4% in different degrees. This implies that the formation matching strategy, is more effective in selecting the best formation to join, resulting in a more efficient and energy-efficient traffic system.

title: A Multi-Feature Migration Fog Generation Model
authors: Xin Ai; Jia Zhang; Yongqiang Bai; Hongxing Song
abstract: The dehaze methods are limited because authenticity of the synthesized dataset has not yet met the requirements for dehazing in real-world scenarios. The traditional image domain migration methods exhibit an uneven problem in fog generation. We propose a characteristic transfer fog generative model (FogGAN) for the synthesis of haze datasets. Firstly, we propose a multi-feature fusion strategy for haze distribution based on the principle of atmospheric scattering. We use transmission maps, depth maps, and mask maps to obtain the distribution of haze and transfer the fused information to the source domain. Secondly, in order to improve the error fitting phenomenon of multicommon information in the target domain, we designed a multi-layer attention module (MAConv). It focuses the neural network on the features of fog and excludes interference from other content. To address the issue of missing details in generated images. We conducted experiments on the VOC2007 dataset. It demonstrates the effectiveness and the ability to improve existing dehaze methods.

title: Characterization of Tunable Multilayer Graphene Ink by a Microstrip Transmission Line
authors: Shakir Ullah; Warda Saeed; Muhammad Yasir
publication_title: 2024 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: This paper presents microwave characterization of multilayered graphene in the frequency range of 8–12 GHz. Thru, Reflect, Line calibration method has been used to shift calibration planes from the edge of a microstrip line to graphene. Transmission coefficient is measured for varying bias voltages. Values of complex impedance of graphene are derived from the transmission coefficient. Prototypes have been fabricated consisting of a microstrip line with different gaps on which multilayered graphene ink is deposited. By decreasing the gap size in the microstrip line, the resistance, reactance and the tuning range of graphene decreases.

title: Design and Implementation of VGA Image Transmission Based on FPGA
authors: Weijun Hao
abstract: With the increase of image data scale, a faster and more efficient image acquisition and processing system is needed. FPGA has good parallel performance, which is very suitable for algorithms dealing with basic parallel features, and can greatly improve the efficiency of image acquisition and processing system. Aiming at the problem of FPGA image acquisition, processing and display, this paper carries out the design of real-time image acquisition system, which has the function of real-time display after processing the acquired image. In this paper, the chip of EP4CE6F17C8 of Cyclone IV series is used, the CMOS camera is OV5640 and the monitor is VAG. After full experimental verification, the system is extensible, the later expansion goal can not be achieved without the cooperation of Bluetooth and other facilities, with the role of recognizing and positioning license plates, obviously this series of application prospects are considerable; With flexibility, can customize the algorithm for optimization; Low cost a series of advantages.

title: Consensus Protocol of T-S Fuzzy Positive Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Renjie Fu; Han Shen; Chongxiang Yu; Yuanyuan Wu
abstract: This paper investigates the consensus problem of T-S fuzzy positive multi-agent systems based on proportional-integral-derivative control protocol. To begin with, this paper utilizes the matrix decomposition technique to propose a proportional-integral-derivative control protocol. The consensus problem of the systems is transformed into a stability problem of augmented systems. By means of copositive Lyapunov functions and linear programming, some sufficient conditions for ensuring consensus and positivity of T-S fuzzy multi-agent systems are established. The contributions of the paper lie in that: (i) A novel proportional-integral-derivative control protocol is proposed for T-S fuzzy positive multi-agent systems and (ii) All presented conditions can be solved via linear programming. Finally, an example is provided to verify the validity of the proposed design.

title: Transformer Based End-to-End Speech Recognition with Linear Attention
authors: ShuHang Yu; Ping Li
abstract: Transformer models with dot-product attention have made great progress in speech recognition task in recent years. However, it suffers from the drawback of slow training speed because its memory and computational costs grow quadratically with the length of the input feature. In this paper, we apply the linear transformer to automatic speech recognition task which reduces its memory and computational complexity. To evaluate the effectiveness of linear attention based speech transformer, we conduct comparison experiments on the AISHELL-1 which is an open-source Mandarin speech corpus. Evaluated on AISHELL-1 speech recognition dataset, our best model achieves character error rate (CER) of 11.9%, while the whole training process only takes 21 hours on 1 GPU, significantly faster than Speech-transformer models.

title: Ten-Winged Butterfly Chaotic System Based on Julia Fractal
authors: Zichen Yang; Xiaonian Liu; Mao Li; Xuexing Hong; Ying Zhou; Zhipeng Yang
abstract: Modern methodologies have advanced in the study of fractals and chaos in the field of nonlinear disciplines, but there is still much room for advancement and research opportunities for the study of combined fractal and chaotic systems. In this work, a thorough investigation of the interaction between the classical Julia fractal and the conventional Lorentzian chaotic system is conducted to construct a rich multi-vortex system. The conventional Lorentzian family is extended and transformed into a chaotic system with ten wings. The Julia fractal mapping relations are applied to the chaotic system in the proposed novel method for the production of multi-vortex attractors. More multi-vortex attractors, including limit rings, are obtained after the characteristics of each element are examined. The study and design of multi-vortex chaotic systems are also covered, along with a variety of implementation strategies and analytical concepts.

title: Fixed-time formation control of fully-actuated surface vessels with input saturation and complex unknowns
authors: Yu Wang; Zhipeng Shen; Qun Wang; Haomiao Yu
abstract: This paper focuses on fixed-time formation control of a crowd of fully actuated surface vessels with input constraint and complex unknowns. First, an adaptive auxiliary system is introduced for each vessel to conquer the harmful effects caused by input saturation. Second, so as to enhance the robustness and anti-interference ability, the predictor-based neural network is utilized to estimate the unknowns, and adaptive laws are designed to evaluate bounds of neural network errors. Third, considering the timing requirement, a fixed-time formation protocol is proposed by using a novel fixed-time convergence nonsingular terminal sliding mode. Not only the trajectory tracking errors of single vessel and cooperative errors between vessels, but also the relationship between position and velocity errors is considered in the sliding mode. It can be proved that the proposed protocol can make the above-mentioned errors converge to a tiny neighborhood near zero in a fixed time. Simulation studies based on four supply vessels are comprehensively provided to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed protocol.

title: Research on Flight Control of High-Aspect-Ratio Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Based on L1 Adaptive Control
authors: Shiyu Hao; Xiaojun Duan; Ben Xiao; Tianshun Li; Shaoqian Chen
abstract: The geometry nonlinear aeroelastic problems of the high-aspect-ratio unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) are prominent, which will bring many adverse factors to flight control. A high-aspect-ratio UAV flight controller design technique in accordance with the L1 adaptive control algorithm is therefore suggested to increase the flight control system's robustness. First, the adverse effects brought by the aerodynamic lift surface model to the static aeroelastic problem of UAV are analyzed. Then, a longitudinal channel in accordance with L1 adaptive controller is designed, including the design of adaptive law, control law, and state observer. Next, the stability of the designed controller is analyzed to prove its stability. Finally, simulation validation is carried out, and the results show that the designed controller can still achieve good tracking performance of instructions under the adverse effects of static aeroelasticity and has strong robustness against uncertain disturbances caused by model and environment interference.

title: Spectral and Morphological Classification of Celestial Objects using Physics Informed Machine Learning
authors: Md Fairuz Siddiquee; Md Mehedi Hasan
abstract: The classification of celestial objects has traditionally relied on spectral analysis, which involves identifying unique patterns in the light emitted or absorbed by the objects. In this study, we present a novel approach to categorizing celestial objects based on their spectral properties and morphological structures, leveraging physics-informed machine learning (PIML) techniques to enhance the classification accuracy and efficiency. In the spectral analysis, using Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) dataset, we classified stars, galaxies, and quasars, focusing on redshift and near-infrared values with i and z filters. Our analysis employed three machine learning models (K-Neighbors, SVM, Random Forest), and the performances were verified to be resilient applying hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation. The best-performing model, Random Forest Classifier, achieved 98% accuracy. In the morphological analysis, the YOLO v5 model was utilized on a customized dataset of astronomical images to further classify the Galaxy Class into five distinct categories and the YOLOv5 model detected those with an average precision of 92.6% and recall of 68.9%. In addition, the interpretability of the model is enhanced by the incorporation of physical knowledge, allowing astronomers to gain deeper insights into the underlying processes. Integrating physical knowledge into these ML models enhances interpretability, facilitating automated real-time analysis of big astronomical data and advancing our understanding of the cosmos.

title: Modeling of FATP Factories in the Supervisor Layer Under Cyberattacks: A Case Study on CA-State Estimation
authors: Shengbao Zheng; Lin Han
abstract: In this paper, based on the theory of Discrete Event Dynamic Systems (DEDS), we study the modeling of a Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS)-based smart manufacturing system under cyberattacks, particularly at the supervisory layer. In our previous works, we proposed a modeling approach and state estimation algorithm (CA-SE) for DEDS under cyberattacks. Taking the FATP (Final Assembly, Test, and Pack) factory in a Bluetooth headset smart manufacturing system as a case study, we first construct an automaton of one of its modules based on the actual factory dynamics, describing its behavior at the supervisory level. Subsequently, we introduce four types of cyberattack strategies and establish the automaton of the factory under attacks. Finally, using CA-SE, we obtain the state estimation of the factory under cyberattacks.

title: Optimal Design of Magnetic Resistance of Permanent Magnet Linear Motor
authors: Xu Kong Kong; Yin Hai Tao; Liu Hua Qing
abstract: Reluctance is an important factor that affects the thrust fluctuation of linear motor. Based on the energy method, this paper carries out the analytical derivation of the linear motor end force and theoretically calculates the linear motor primary length under the minimum end force; The analytical derivation of cogging force is carried out and a unified expression of magnetic resistance based on Fourier series is given based on the Fourier series method. According to the theoretical analytical formula, the magnetic resistance is suppressed by weakening the harmonic amplitude of the magnetic resistance. First, the optimal primary length was verified by finite element model simulation. On this basis, the finite element model of the linear motor with 8 poles and 9 slots and the slotted linear motor was established for simulation verification. Compared with the initial model, the optimized linear motor reluctance The force is reduced by 77.1%, and the simulation results verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

title: Flatness Measurement of Steel Strip Using Three Laser Stripes
authors: Kaiyuan Zhu; Jianwei Zhao; Yibing Fan; Shuzong Yan; Xiaochen Wang; Quan Yang
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of machine vision technology, flatness measurement devices based on line-structured light have been gradually applied to strip steel production lines. However, in the complex and harsh environments of industrial sites, the vibration and rotation of the strip can impact the results of flatness measurement, leading to measurement errors. This paper proposes a flatness measurement device based on triple-line light sources to address this challenge. The device uses an industrial camera to capture the projection of three lasers on the surface of the strip. By repeatedly collecting data from the same position on the steel strip, it achieves high-precision measurement of strip flatness. We designed simulated experiments. The results indicate that the proposed method effectively eliminates measurement errors caused by steel strip vibration and rotation, thereby improving flatness measurement accuracy. This approach has certain reference value for the improvement of flatness measurement technology in industrial environments.

title: Fractional-order PID Plus Derivative Controllers for Speed Control of Serving Robot
authors: Kishore Bingi; P. Arun Mozhi Devan; Rosdiazli Ibrahim; Madiah Omar
abstract: PID controllers have long been the cornerstone of industrial automation and robotics due to their simplicity and effectiveness. However, the primary challenge in using PID control for the speed of serving robots is its inefficiency in dynamic environments. Therefore, this paper proposes an extended version of PID in both traditional and fractional forms, augmented with higher-order derivative terms, for enhanced speed control. The extended controllers will be incorporating second and third derivative actions (PIDD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, PIDD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) and their fractional counterparts $\left({P{I^\lambda }{D^\mu },P{I^\lambda }{D^\mu }{D^{{\mu _2}}},P{I^\lambda }{D^\mu }{D^{{\mu _2}}}{D^{{\mu _3}}}}\right)$,. The proposed controllers are designed for a one-wheel serving robot using a simplified transfer function model. The performance analysis under fixed and variable set-points, as well as disturbance rejection, demonstrates that the $P{I^\lambda }{D^\mu }{D^{{\mu _2}}}{D^{{\mu _3}}}$ controller achieves the best time-domain metrics, including minimal rise time (0.1225 s), reduced overshoot (20.8%), and improved stability. Results confirm that integrating fractional orders with higher-order derivatives significantly enhances control robustness and responsiveness compared to traditional PID designs.

title: Finite-Time Observer Based Three-Dimensional Tracking Control of an Underwater Robot with Multiple Unknowns
authors: Xingru Qu; Xiao Liang; Zhao Zhang; Wenyu Shi
abstract: In this paper, a finite-time observer based three-dimensional tracking control (FTO-TDTC) strategy is proposed for trajectory tracking of an under-actuated underwater robot (UR) with multiple unknowns involving system uncertainties and current disturbances. To avoid the explosion of complexity and simplify the dynamics controller design, virtual velocity-based backstepping control laws are proposed to control pitch rate and yaw rate, simultaneously. By virtue of the finite-time observer (FTO), the multiple unknowns are completely estimated and incorporated into dynamics controller, thus contributing to the UR tracking performance with strong robustness. Rigorous theoretical analysis is deployed by the aid of Lyapunov direct method. Finally, simulation verifications are exhibited to evaluate the maneuverability of the FTO-TDTC strategy when system uncertainties and current disturbances are acting on the under-actuated UR.

title: Integral Control for Nonlinear Systems Subject to Time-Varying Perturbations with Unknown Magnitudes
authors: Zhifeng Han; Xiandong Chen; Claire Walton; Chunjiang Qian
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of linear integral controllers for uncertain nonlinear systems subjected to various types of time-varying perturbations. We propose a method called the feedback domination method to address this problem. The time-varying perturbations can include constant step disturbances, exogenous time-varying disturbances with unknown magnitudes, and modeling uncertainties with unknown system parameters. The approach involves constructing a new linear integral controller with integral dynamics to drive the states of uncertain systems without nonlinear terms to the origin asymptotically Additionally, a high-gain technique is introduced to design a controller that can asymptotically drive the states of uncertain nonlinear systems to the origin. Finally, the paper introduces a new stability criterion and extends the results to a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with more general time-varying perturbations of unknown magnitudes.

title: A mathematical simulation and evaluation method for the flight control systems
authors: Min Huang; Xing-bao Yang; Chuan-wei Zhu
