abstract: To provide a reference for how to evaluate the flight control systems (FCSs) mathematically, a mathematical simulation and evaluation method for the flight control systems was proposed in this paper. Firstly, a brief description of the FCS was given. Secondly, the dynamic and kinematic parameters of aircraft were introduced. Thirdly, mathematical simulation structure for the evaluation of FCS was proposed to basically show how to mathematically simulate the aircraft and the FCS. Then, based on the dynamic, kinematic parameters and the simulation structure, mathematical simulation models were built, including the hardware model, the dynamic and kinematic models, and the aircraft disturbance model. Finally, an evaluation method of mathematical simulation for the FCS was proposed to illustrate how to evaluate FCS performances with the built mathematical simulation models.

title: A Concept of the Multivariable Inverse Model Control for Grünwald–Letnikov-Derived Systems Respecting the Time Delay $d=2$
authors: Emilia Helińska; Paweł Majewski; Wojciech P. Hunek
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: In the paper, the original procedure of the perfect control devoted to systems described in the Grünwald-Letnikov framework is proposed. The novel algorithm outperforms its predecessor in the context of the crucial time delay. Indeed, the phenomenon covering the time delay <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d=2$</tex> of multivariable plants defined in the discrete-time state-space domain is addressed here, enabling a possibility of complex investigations of its dynamic properties. In order to validate the newly introduced control solution, two fractional-order-originated simulation instances have been examined, confirming the broadly observed and accepted behaviors of the discussed control strategy. Ultimately, the materials presented within the paper should be treated as a preliminary step toward an advanced control and systems theory encompassing a set of findings, for example an essential stability issue.

title: Application of Multidimensional Information in Predicting Blue Side Attack Actions: A Matching Degree Calculation Method
authors: Qia Chen; Yanyan Huang; Yuqi Xia
abstract: In response to the problem of difficulty in accurately predicting the intention of blue troops to attack targets on the land battlefield, this paper proposes a prediction method based on matching degree, aiming to predict the intention of blue troops to attack. This article adopts a comprehensive analysis method based on multidimensional information to analyze the matching degree between the blue attacking force and the possible targets of the red side. Firstly, integrate the features of the blue attacking force obtained from the battlefield with the feature information of the red potential target to form a panel of data. Next, the position matching degree, marching angle matching degree, and force target matching degree between the troops and the target are calculated separately, in order to establish the matching degree relationship between the blue attacking troops and the possible attacked targets of the red side, and then use it to speculate on the probability of the blue army implementing the attack, thereby achieving the prediction of the target of the blue attacking action. Finally, an example analysis shows that this matching degree-based prediction method can more comprehensively consider the fusion of multi-dimensional intelligence information, which helps to improve the reliability and effectiveness of target attack prediction.

title: Research on Methods of Vehicle Image Retrieval in Expressway Scenarios Based on Deep Learning Neural Network
authors: Ke Yang; Ziyi Zhang; Chihang Zhao; Hao Li; Xinyi Ma; Xuan Li; Wenhao Deng; Yanxin Huang
abstract: The vehicle image retrieval in highway scenes is influenced by the complexity and diversity of vehicle types, as well as the impact of lighting and climate changes on vehicle image clarity. The paper aims to achieve high-precision vehicle retrieval in complex scenes on highways. Firstly, the paper constructs a vehicle image retrieval dataset of Southeast University (SEU) including whole vehicle image test set, vehicle face image test set, vehicle window test set, vehicle license plate test set. Secondly, three variants of CNN models are investigated for the vehicle image retrieval in expressway scenarios, including VGG16-VIR-ES, ResNet50-VIR-ES and DenseNet121-VIR-ES. Finally, based on vehicle image retrieval dataset of Southeast University (SEU), the research of compare experiment on VGG16-VIR-ES, ResNet50-VIR-ES and DenseNet121-VIR-ES are carried out. The experimental results show that DenseNet121-VIR-ES outperform the other models, and the accuracy of the vehicle image retrieval method based on DenseNet121 network is 92.12%, 91.55%, 92.86% and 84.98% for the whole vehicle image test set, vehicle image test set, window image test set and license plate image test set, respectively.

title: CETSP-based Trajectory Planning for Redundant Manipulators
authors: Shuangyi Gong; Suping Zhao; Chaobo Chen; Alejandro Gutierrez-Giles; Xiaoyan Zhang; Jichao Li
abstract: The trajectory planning problem for redundant manipulators is studied, where the DOF (degree of freedom) of the manipulator is larger than 6. The end-effector is constrained to visit a series of task areas, similar to the Close-Enough Traveling Salesman Problem (CETSP). However, the multiple inverse solutions of redundant manipulators must be considered. This paper proposes an improved genetic algorithm with the simultaneous introduction of three different types of genes. Each chromosome contains three parts, including the order of task areas, the sequence of joint configurations, and the unknown coefficients to be optimized. Numerical simulations are carried out to validate the proposed method. The results show that the end-effector of redundant manipulator accurately visits all task areas.

title: The Division of the Terminal Distribution Regions for Fresh Food E-commerce Based on the Complex Networks
authors: Ping Xu; Na Li; Wei-lai Zhong; Jing-yi Dai; Guan-chu Wang
abstract: The rapid development of fresh food e-commerce provides an effective solution for increasing farmers' income, meeting consumers' needs and reducing the loss of fresh food circulation. As the key link of fresh food e-commerce logistics, the distribution is of great significance to improve consumer satisfaction and reducing the operating cost of e-commerce enterprises. This article divides the distribution regions of fresh food e-commerce through the LinkRank community detection algorithm based on the complex networks, explores and constructs a method of the division of the terminal distribution regions for fresh food e-commerce logistics by using simulated annealing algorithm to optimizes the network modularity, and verified the effectiveness of the method by analysing the case of Jingkou District of Zhenjiang City. Hope to offer a reference for fresh food e-commerce to construct the logistics distribution system suitably.

title: Optimization Strategy of Dual Active Full Bridge DC-DC Converter
authors: Huaihua Zheng; Min Zhou; Hongsheng Huang; Zhi Wu; Canwei Zu; Nan Wang; Yang Wang
abstract: The efficiency of a bidirectional full-bridge DCDC converter is determined by the magnitude of the reverse power and inductor current stress. Although the presence of inner current shifting in the DPS control reduces the reverse power and inductor current stress, the reduction effect is not significant. Consequently, this research paper employs the approach of constructing the Lagrange function to segmentally optimize and regulate the inductor current stress and reverse power of single-phase shift (SPS) and double-phase shift (DPS) DC-DC converters. The objective is to minimize the inductor current stress and reverse power, thereby enhancing the converter's efficiency. A comparative analysis is conducted on the reverse power and inductor current stress of different optimization strategies. The feasibility and effectiveness of these strategies are verified through simulation on the MATLAB/Simulink platform, and the efficacy of relevant optimization algorithms is ultimately confirmed through experimentation on a dedicated platform.

title: Optimizing Arm Movement in Cartesian- Type Piano-Playing Robot with Dynamic Programming
authors: HyoJae Kang; InGyu Choi; Min-Sung Kang
abstract: Fingering plays a crucial role in piano performance. Accordingly, when using a robot to play the piano, appropriate fingering and arm movement is required. Research on piano-playing using various types of robots has been conducted. However, most studies have focused on robots with structures similar to humans. As a result, the same fingering algorithm cannot be applied to robots with different structures. In previous research, a robot with a Cartesian robot structure, where one finger is assigned to each key to ensure the same key point, was used to associate sound volume with music notation. In that study, arm movement focused solely on preventing collisions, which led to unnecessary arm movements and degraded the performance. Therefore, in this study, we propose a method to optimize the robot's performance as an extension of previous research. The proposed method uses dynamic programming to calculate the cost for all possible arm positions and find the optimal path. Additionally, to prevent performance degradation, arm movement is avoided for short-duration notes. The proposed method compares the results based on the hand's playable range, and performance improvement is verified through experiments by comparing the performance of the new method and the previous algorithm on the same musical score.

title: Studies on the Operation of Electromagnetic Actuators With Potential Use to Reduce the Level of Vibrations Generated in Piping Systems
authors: Vlad Mihai Panainte; Sanda Oltean; Ana Maria Moldovan; Horia Bălan
abstract: The scientific and technical advances in recent years allow designers and producers the use of different methods compared to the classical ones. One of them is represented by technological utilities in the field of generation, transmission, and distribution of thermal agents. It was found that in certain situations, the placement of heat generators on elastic floors or if the equipment has some faults, the vibrations generated are transmitted through the heating agent to the heating converters, negatively influences the acoustic inner environment. The compensation method is the technology through which the effects of the vibrations generated in the pipes in which the thermal agent flows can be mitigated and/or cancelled. The aspects highlighted in the following case study are the frequency and amplitude of vibrations along with the vibration force evaluated with a single restriction. The authors have considered systems consisting in one electromagnetic actuator, driven by an adjustable frequency converter. The analyzed solutions of one-touch electromagnetic actuators, respectively double-touch actuators, consider a system having an actuating coil for one-touch electromagnetic actuators or two actuating coils for double-touch electromagnetic actuators, with transistor static contactors powering the coils, a sinusoidal signal generator and a modulator that can modify the frequency and the amplitude of the vibrations. Since the harmonic response is not an issue analyzed in detail in this paper, the conclusions section highlights the prospect of using a voltage-modulated converter.

title: Effect of the Number of Conversations and Timings in Deciding the Number of Solved Problems Between the Learner and the Educational-Support Robot
authors: Hiroki Kaede; Taro Kono; Felix Jimenez; Tomoki Miyamoto
abstract: In recent years, educational-support robots have attracted a lot of attention. In conventional educational-support robots, the number of problems to be solved by the learner (the number of solved problems) is determined by the system. This prevents learners from achieving self-motivated learning, in which they decide the number of solved problems. In the previous study, several conversational methods were proposed to determine the number of solved problems through a conversation with the robot before learning. The results suggested that letting the robot decide the number of solved problems before learning improved the impression of the robot and the number of solved problems of learner. However, in the conventional method, the conversation of learner is limited before learning. Therefore, the optimal number of negotiations and timing of the conversations have not been verified. In this study, we investigate the optimal number of negotiations and timing of conversations between the robot and the learner to determine the number of solved problems. Specifically, through two types of experiments, we compare robots that talk before learning, after learning, and before and after learning, and verify the differences in the number of solved problems and in the impressions of robot.

title: The balancing problem for a reconfigurable flexible assemble line
authors: Fengyuan Shi; Shuo Wang; Long Zeng
abstract: In the ever-changing market environment, rigid production facilities and large bulk mode are becoming less and less able to cater to the trend. The demand for small-batch flexible automation production is becoming more and more urgent for enterprise, so the research on flexible assembly automation has attracted more and more attention. This paper proposes a reconfigurable flexible assembly line that can be used in actual production. Based on the type II robotic assembly line balancing problem model, for an actual production hydraulic valve product, we propose a mathematical model including cycle time CT, assembly tool replacement time RT and the assembly cell cost ST, then carry out the pre-optimization operator, and use the dual-population genetic algorithm to solve the problem to obtain a well-balanced assembly line layout, then guide the actual production.

title: On deployment problem of multi-agent systems with delays
authors: Katarzyna Topolewicz; Carlos E. T. Dórea; Sorin Olaru; Ewa Girejko
abstract: The paper analyzes the decentralized deployment policies for scalar multi-agent systems subject to delays. As a main contribution we obtain explicit conditions on the local feedback gains at the level of subsystems, which ensure safe deployment independent of the delays on the measurement of the positions of the neighboring agents. From the theoretic point of view, positive invariance of sets is used as a main concept for the proofs of the results.

title: Biohybrid muscle actuator driven by cardiomyocytes
authors: Zening Lin; Yun Yang; Tao Jiang; Yang Hong; Yuan Gao; Zirong Luo
abstract: Bionic robots, which aim to mimic the morphologies and functions of real living creatures, play an increasingly important role in military affairs, medical healthcare, industrial production, and so on. As a crucial part of the robots, actuators determine their overall performance to a certain extent. However, it is challenging to replicate the actuation behavior of real organisms using traditional electromechanical actuation systems (like motors) with flexible material actuation (like shape memory alloys). Potential solutions include biomuscular actuators assembled from living cells and biomaterials. As a result, this work created a biohybrid muscle actuator with primary cardiomyocytes and bioactive materials (Matrigel, fibrinogen, and so on). The muscle actuators started to produce spontaneous systolic-diastolic movements after a few days and could survive for at least five days. This study provides a reference for other researchers working on fabricating biohybrid muscle actuators.

title: Haptic-enabled Virtual Laboratory for Hands-on E-Learning: A Technology for and Beyond the Pandemic Era
authors: Muhammad Affan; Humayun Khan; Subhan Ahmed; Riaz Uddin; Muhammad Ayaz Shirazi
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has spurred drastic changes in the tele-education worldwide, especially Pakistan. Starting from the first phase of pandemic, Pakistani students have witnessed extensive use of tele-school and other e-learning platforms However, e-learning platforms are majorly characterized by audiovisual capability and thus, student learning is limited due to the lack of "experimentation and interaction". To cater this problem, we propose a haptics and teleoperation based inclusive teaching, comprising of a few introductory concepts of physics namely, friction, viscosity, and inertia as pilot cases. The mechanism employs single-master (teacher), multiple-slaves (students) system, each having access to affordable haptic device ‘Novint Falcon’. In teaching mode, apart from audio/visual, the demonstrator will explain concepts to students by interacting with force reflecting environments as master, whereas students feel the forces at their own haptic devices. Similarly, in other self-practice mode, students will independently perform experiments by haptic virtual interaction themselves.

title: The Method of Military Logistics Integration Based on SAEI@I
authors: Defu He; Xuejuan Huang; Xisheng Su
abstract: Academician Wang Shouyang, an expert in Chinese forecasting techniques, proposes a research method of integration and applies it to the analysis of realistic complex systems such as macroeconomic forecast. On the basis of this method, both strategic analysis theory and approaching transformation theory are introduced by the author to make significant improvements of this method according to the features of military logistics system, therefore it is named as SAEI@I methodology. This methodology has universal applicability to general complex giant systems. This paper focuses on the piecewise problem of nonlinear part in military logistics material demand calculation and simplifies and concretizes the methodology by taking the demand calculation of battlefield supplies as an example.

title: Deep Learning and Machine Vision Based License Plate Detection for Complex Environments
authors: Mingkun Guo; Yan Li; Jiyong Hu; Hongfei Yang
abstract: In order to train deep learning of number plates from datasets containing different types of noise, we propose a multi-level, end-to-end, number plate recognition detection method for extreme environments Firstly, a processing algorithm is used to remove part of the noise, and then the Encoder-Decoder Module is combined for effective licence plate location. Then, based on the extracted licence plate, the initial segmentation profile is determined, and based on the effectiveness enhancement network model, the threshold segmentation method is applied to obtain the approximate range of the target and reduce the segmentation of complex track samples containing noise.

title: Particle Swarm Optimization Based Control For a Controlled Floating Space Robot
authors: David Chaudhary; Senthil Murugan
abstract: This paper explores Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) based control of a morphing robot arm mounted on a Controlled Floating Space Robot (CFSR). CFSR is a new study spacecraft model allowing controlled adjustments of the satellite base's pose. The dynamic model of the chaser spacecraft is derived relative to the target in an inertial frame, using the Clohessy- Wiltshire model or Hills equations for defining their relative motion. It is assumed that both spacecraft are in an Inplane-elliptical formation. The manipulator dynamics are obtained through Lagrangian formulation. The PSO algorithm optimizes controller gain values while a quintic polynomial tra-jectory is provided as input to the arm joints. Results show that the PSO-based controller effectively reduces tracking error and power requirements, and it is also compared with a conventional proportional-derivative (PD) controller.

title: Target Enclosing Control of Unmanned Surface Vehicles Under False-Data-Injection Attacks
authors: Xingru Qu; Chu Li; Guanqun Liu; Rubo Zhang
abstract: This paper is concerned with the target enclosing control of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) suffering from false-data-injection (FDI) attacks. The enclosed target is dynamic and FDI attacks influence location information of USVs. Firstly, by virtue of the invariant manifold principle, the filtered signalbased FDI observer is designed for estimating false data and compensating vehicle locations. Then, by the aid of obtained target position and bearing angle, the target enclosing controller integrating the location compensation is developed for the USV, such that the vehicle can surround the dynamic target with a desired distance regardless of FDI attacks. And the global uniform asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system is rigorously proven using Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, simulation results validate the efficacy of the proposed target enclosing control method.

title: Research on Mobile Robot Path Planning Based on IHBS-A* Algorithm
authors: Hongbo Li; Hong Zheng; Gang Liu; Jianwei Guo
abstract: With the rapid development of mobile robot robots over the years, path planning has become one of the key technologies for mobile robot applications. Although the traditional A* algorithm has high search efficiency and fast computing speed, the planned paths are easy to collide with obstacles, have more inflection points and redundant nodes, and the robot keeps turning in the process of actual operation, which seriously affects the efficiency of robot operation, so this paper proposes the improved algorithm IHBS-A* (Improve heuristic, Bidirectional node and Smoothing path): for the safety problem by improving the heuristic function and introducing safety coefficient, which makes the mobile robot keep a certain For the safety problem, the heuristic function is improved and the safety factor is introduced to make the mobile robot keep a certain safety distance from the obstacles. The results show that the IHBS-A* algorithm not only retains the advantages of the fast computing speed of A*, but also makes the path safer, and the path is smoother, and shorter, which improves the efficiency of the mobile robot.

title: Control Allocation of X-form Rudder Based on Neural Networks
authors: Yueming Qin; Wubo Pei; Xing Shao; Yang Xu
abstract: At present, there are mainly two common frameworks for implementing the control allocation of X-form rudder: namely the pseudo-inverse framework and the optimization based framework. In order to obtain better allocation performance than the former and lower computational complexity than the latter at the same time, this paper proposes a new framework, namely the neural networks framework, for control allocation of X-form rudder. In this paper, neural networks are applied to fit the mapping from desired moments (roll moment, pitch moment and yaw moment) to the proper rudder angles. The experimental results show that the proposed method is effective and can fulfill the task of control allocation.

title: Control and optimum design for networks with nonlinear state equations
authors: Nikolai P. Osmolovskii; Meizhi Qian; Jan Sokołowski
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Optimal control problem for semilinear hyperbolic equations is considered on 3 -star metric graph. The distributed controls on the edges are considered. The tracking type cost for steady state equation is considered for the control problem. Using the Turnpike Property for dynamic control problem, the control problem is solved for the steady state equations. The necessary and sufficient optimality conditions are established for static control problems. Then the optimum design problem is considered for the topological perturbation of the graph. The small cycle of size $\varepsilon \rightarrow 0$ replaces the central node of 3 -star graph. The distributed controls are introduced on the edges of the cycle. The topological derivative of the shape functional indicates the possibility of nucleation of the small cycle.

title: Modeling of High Speed Maglev Operation Control System Based on AADL
authors: Yan Sun; Lei Zhang; Qian Xu
abstract: AADL is a formal modeling language for real-time embedded systems. This paper compares the differences between different formal modeling methods, introduces AADL modeling method into the field of high-speed maglev to model the operation control system(OCS) of high-speed maglev, and accurately describes the structure of each subsystem of OCS and the information interaction process between subsystems. This paper solves the problem that the conventional formal modeling method is insufficient to describe the system structure by OSATE tool.

title: Design of Automated Medicine-Liquid Proportioning System Based on Spectral Analysis
authors: Wenbin Zhang; Chengliang Zhang; Jingyi Su; Panling Huang; Jun Zhou
abstract: The medicine-liquid ratio is an important part of various industries such as medicine and has important applications in the field of medical research. However, the traditional drug-liquid ratios are all artificial ratios, and the efficiency is low. In order to improve the efficiency of practical applications and reduce labor costs, this paper designs a set of automated chemical-liquid ratio system based on spectral analysis. This system takes an ethanol solution as an example. The spectrum analyzer is used to analyze the concentration of ethanol in the chemical solution. The PC reads the concentration information and controls the single-chip computer based on the information. The single-chip computer controls the peristaltic pump to perform the chemical solution ratio to obtain the appropriate concentration of the ethanol solution., Its accuracy is within ± 0.5%.

title: Optimization Design of Electronic Fuel Injection System for Automobile Engines
authors: Wenfu Sun
abstract: The structural configuration and characteristics of an automobile engine's fuel injection system have a direct impact on the engine's performance. Computational analysis of the fuel system is a crucial method for improving engine performance. Based on the analysis of the structure and mathematical models of the components of the engine's electronic fuel injection system, a simulation model was established, and the structural parameters of the fuel system were optimized through matching calculations. The research results indicate that a plunger diameter and lift of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bm{\Phi} 23 \times 24$</tex>, along with a injection hole number and diameter of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7 \times \Phi 0.45$</tex>, provide superior fuel injection characteristics. Additionally, the flow area of the solenoid valve's drain port, as well as the timing and duration of the electrical activation, significantly influence the fuel injection characteristics of the system. The optimized structural parameters hold important reference value for the design of engine fuel systems.

title: Analytical Optimization Method for the New Redundant Configuration of the FAST Feed Cabin
authors: Jianing Yin; Rui Yao; Peng Jiang
abstract: The Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) is the largest single dish and most sensitive radio telescope in the world. As the number and difficulty of observation tasks increase year by year, it is decided to further improve the performance of FAST. Therefore, a new redundant configuration of the FAST feed cabin has been designed. This paper discusses the modeling of such redundant configuration and the analytical optimization method with 2 kinds of constrains. Then after simulation calculation, an excellent optimization result is obtained. It proves that at least 50° observation zenith angle can be achieved, which means that astronomical phenomena near the galactic center can be observed. The results provide the important foundation for the FAST’s future upgrade.

title: Human Avoidance During Robot Operations
authors: Delia Guran; Tassos Natsakis
abstract: This paper centers on a human avoidance algorithm designed to enhance the coexistence of humans and robots within industrial settings. While both humans and robots share a workspace, it is crucial to ensure the robot operates seamlessly without encroaching upon the human’s space. However, human space is not static and therefore robots need to adapt in real time to changes. The proposed approach involves employing a depth camera to actively identify and track humans in real time. It determines the distance between the human and the robot’s end effector and computes a repulsive vector. At the same time, an attractive vector is calculated from the robot end effector towards the target pose. Based on the addition of the repulsive and attractive vectors, a new trajectory for the robot is calculated, keeping the same goal pose. This enables the robot to steer clear of potential collisions while achieving its goal. Human detection is facilitated using an Astra Pro depth camera from Orbbec. We demonstrate this algorithm on the UR5 robot from Universal Robots which it is tasked with moving at a velocity of 0.1 m/s towards predefined targets. The avoidance algorithm remains constantly active, ensuring continuous trajectory for the robot post-avoidance of the human presence.

title: Multi-Robot Source Seeking and Field Reconstruction of Spatial-Temporal Varying Fields
authors: Deepak Talwar; Thinh Lu; Divyam Sobti; Wencen Wu
abstract: To effectively respond to environmental disasters, real-time monitoring and pollution control rely heavily on the ability to estimate, predict, and reconstruct constantly changing environmental conditions across different locations. In this research, we develop a multi-robot source-seeking and field reconstruction framework that enables a multi-robot group to detect multiple sources within a spatial-temporal varying field and reconstruct the field in real time. The strategy consists of two parts: source seeking and field reconstruction. The source-seeking part features a gradient-based source-seeking controller that directs the multi-robot group toward local sources and a destination selection algorithm that navigates the multi-robot formation beyond the local maximal. The field reconstruction part reconstructs the spatial-temporal varying field in real time using the limited measurements taken by the robots. We validate the strategy in simulations.

title: Research on SURF Feature Matching Algorithm Based on Lab Color Space
authors: Leng Han; Xia Sun; Jiawei Wang; Dingmei Xia
abstract: The alignment of images is an important task in the processing of images, which is also known as registration. Among the feature based registration methods, Speeded Up Robust Features (SURF) has been proposed as a computationally efficient approach. The SURF algorithm not only does not consider color information, but the matching accuracy is also rather low. In this paper, an improved SURF algorithm for feature extraction is proposed. An approach is proposed to use the Lab color space to extract the color information of the color image when extracting the feature points based on SURF, and adds the feature descriptors. In this sense, the feature descriptors of different feature points by proposing method are unique. And this method makes up for the shortcoming that SURF cannot use the color information of color images. This improved method promotes the precision of matching. The results show that the matching accuracy of this algorithm is higher than that of the original SURF when physical interference, rotation, brightness change, and scale change occur.

title: Design and Experiment of Distributed Seawater Carbon Sequestration Equipment
authors: Shuai Deng; Zheming Zhuang; Zhiwei Wang; Qingyu Bu; Kaiwen Hu; Yifei Gao; Yuntao Guan; Jiansheng Dai
abstract: A kind of distributed seawater carbon sequestration equipment is designed for achieving the target of carbon neutrality steadily and solving the problems including high energy consumption, high pollution and low conversion rate existing in the traditional carbon sequestration technologies. A single-step carbon sequestration technology is used to sequester the carbonate ions and obtain the by-product - hydrogen and preliminarily desalinated seawater by means of electrolysis reaction. The proposal is efficient in energy saving and emission reduction with simple chemical principles and a high availability for promotion. An ideal model is established, a corresponding control system is designed and a physical model of the core device is established for the experimental research to ensure feasibility of the proposal in the study.

title: Kinematic Parameter Solution for Automotive Hood Spraying Robot
authors: Zhang Yuhao; Xu Yong; Chen Yuhao; Li Huizi; Feng Guoxin; Guo Shuyan; Sun Weijun
abstract: With the continuous advancement of automation technology, robots are increasingly being applied in the automotive manufacturing industry. In particular, the precision, efficiency, and stability of spraying robots in the automotive parts coating process directly affect product quality and production efficiency. This paper mainly analyzes the kinematics of automotive parts spraying robots, exploring the establishment and optimization methods of their kinematic models. Through the kinematic analysis of the spraying robots, the aim is to improve the motion accuracy of the robots in the spraying operation, optimize path planning and control strategies, and thus enhance the overall performance of the spraying tasks.

title: Verification of Compliance on Funabot-Plate: Semisoft Assistive Robot with Artificial Muscle and Rigid Plate
authors: Shinichi Masaoka; Rin Yasuda; Yuki Funabora; Shinji Doki
abstract: Compliance is important for the rehabilitation of wearable assistive robots. Various methods have been studied to improve the compliance of wearable robots, such that the use of impedance control of actuators and soft actuators with high compliance. On the other hand, for robots whose degrees of freedom of movement are limited by rotational axes like conventional robots, compliance performance may deteriorate due to mounting misalignment even if the actuator is designed optimally. Soft wearable devices that do not have rigid joints and are composed of soft base materials also exist, but the force is dispersed and cannot exert great force. Our Funabot- Plate consists of a base cloth, McKibben-type pneumatic artificial muscles, and thin, rigid plates that efficiently transfer the exerted force of the artificial muscles to the human body. Thus, Funabot-Plate expects a high output efficiency while high compliance. To verify the structural validity of the Funabot- Plate, two experiments were conducted to quantitatively compare its compliance characteristics with the rigid-frame robot. Through the measurement experiments, we were able to quantitatively evaluate that the structure of Funabot- Plate exhibited higher compliance in both conditions, transparent mode and assist mode, when compared to conventional rigid-frame robots.

title: Trajectory Optimization of Robot Manipulator in Static and Complex Environment
authors: Di Zhu; Chuang Cheng; Kaihong Huang; Lin Lang; Huimin Lu; Zhiqiang Zheng
abstract: This paper presents an optimization-based approach for robotic motion planning in a static and complex environment. This method designs optimization functions and constraint in-equalities based on requirements, and then we use the functional gradient technique to improve the quality of the initial trajectory iteratively. It uses the numerical distance information between the environment’s point cloud and the robot’s boundary to describe the collision tendency. Constraint inequalities that are difficult to describe are handled by setting a threshold value γ, a maximum penetration depth point, and a bounding volume hierarchy. Finally, We do some experiments with this method on a six-degree-of-freedom manipulator UR3. Experiments demonstrate that the performance of the manipulators is improved, and the trajectory is effectively optimized while avoiding collisions with non-convex obstacles.

title: PID Controller Tuning for Capsubot with Standard and Fractional-Order PSO Algorithm
authors: Artur Babiarz
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The presented paper contains comparison two algorithms for searching optimal value of PID controllers: particle swarm optimization (PSO) and fractional-order particle swarm optimization (F-PSO) for the control system of capsubot robot. A cost function which is used with PSO and F-PSO is presented. At the end, the obtained simulation results are shown and discussed.

title: Unsupervised Full Transformer for Pose; Depth and Optical Flow Joint Learning
authors: Xiaochen Liu; Tao Zhang
abstract: The use of monocular cameras for ego-motion estimation in autonomous driving is a fundamental technique with significant potential for development. Recently, unsupervised CNNs based schemes have rapidly advanced due to their label-free advantages. However, traditional CNNs lack the ability to capture global dependencies, which are essential for sequential tasks like pose, depth, and optical flow estimation. In this paper, according to the characteristics of these three-independent tasks, we designed different network frameworks fully based on the transformer separately to improve performance by taking advantage of the global dependencies of different tasks. After unsupervised training, the model can independently predict the pose, depth, and optical flow results for the vehicle, solely based on a monocular camera. The experimental results conducted on the KITTI demonstrate that the proposed method obtain satisfactory results in all three tasks.

title: An End-to-End Model for Printed Uyghur Text Recognition
authors: Zhiwei You; Qiong Li; Chuang Liu
abstract: The recognition method based on the end-to-end model has a wide range of applications in Chinese and English text recognition, but there are few researches of Uygur text recognition. Using the end-to-end method can effectively avoid the wrong recognition problem caused by the mis-segmentation of Uyghur letters. Based on the Transformer model, we propose a model named EfficientNet-Transformer for printed Uyghur text recognition. By replacing the SE attention of EfficientNet with Triplet attention, the computing ability of the network for spatial and channel attention is improved. The encoder of the original Transformer model is replaced by an improved EfficientNet, which makes the model simpler and fewer parameters. The dataset is expanded by synthesizing words through Uyghur syllable rules, and comparative experiments are carried out on this dataset by using our model with other’s RNN-based model. Experiments show this model is superior to others models in Character error rate, recognition speed and space occupation.

title: VREP Platform: A Virtual Reality-Based Human-Computer Interaction Experimental Platform
authors: Bozhi Tan; Shikai Liu; Yuqi He; Yi Zhu
abstract: The deployment of human-computer interaction (HCI) experimental platforms across various domains is of paramount importance. Presently, conventional HCI platforms continue to be rooted in Personal Computer (PC), exhibiting limitations such as low immersion, reduced real-time responsiveness, and diminished accuracy. In light of these constraints, this research advocates for a Virtual Reality (VR)-based HCI experimental platform, with the aim of overcoming these limitations. The platform seeks to enhance user experiences, evaluate emerging interaction technologies, and facilitate scholarly research. Integrating VR technologies, this platform offers a simulated, realistic interactive environment supporting multimodal inputs. The architecture includes three main components: users, processing, and the computer, with submodules facilitating scene construction, tracking, and connectivity. The platform showcases its potential for immersive interaction through an intelligent collaboration experiment between humans and unmanned aerial vehicles.

title: Application of Untiree GO 1 in ORB-SLAM3 Map Building
authors: Yuxuan Bai
abstract: With the increasing urbanization, the proliferation of highways has significantly increased the workload involved in highway maintenance. In particular, the maintenance inspection of tunnels plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and functionality of these vital transportation infrastructures. Robots for intelligent highway tunnel maintenance inspections present a promising solution to alleviate the associated costs and efforts. This research focuses on utilizing the Unitree GOI robot dog, equipped with the ORB-SLAM3 algorithm, for efficient tunnel maintenance detection. This study outlines the process of setting up the GOI robot dog environment from the ground up and employing ROS2 to transmit video captured by the binocular fisheye camera mounted on the robot dog to a customer PC. Subsequently, the ORB-SLAM3 algorithm is executed on the customer PC for map building to overcome the the problem that GOI dog machine does not have enough computility. Through successful experimentation, this study demonstrates the feasibility of employing the GOI robot dog in conjunction with the ORB-SLAM3 algorithm to generate accurate maps of real tunnel environments. This study improves the reliability of the GOI dog operation and solves the problem of the bad result of map building due to insufficient computility and indistinct images.

title: Data-Driven Optimal Control for Continuous- Time Linear Nonzero-Sum Games
authors: Hongyang Li; Qinglai Wei; Ruizhuo Song
abstract: In this paper, the data-driven optimal control problem is studied for continuous-time linear nonzero-sum games. Two kinds of reinforcement learning algorithms, i.e., reinforcement learning algorithm with data-storage based least-square method and reinforcement learning algorithm with filter based least-square method, are presented to obtain the Nash equilibrium solution. The properties of the presented rein-forcement learning algorithms are analyzed. Simulation results show the efficiency of the presented reinforcement learning algorithms.

title: Low-Compute Trash Segmentation Using Pretrained Vision Transformers Without Fine-Tuning
authors: Philip Keller; Michael Möck; Georg Heppner; Rüdiger Dillmann
abstract: With more and more people in our world, there is unfortunately more and more garbage, especially in the environment. Collecting it can be tedious and requires valuable human labor. On the other hand, there are several projects for autonomous robots to take over this task. However, visual perception of garbage is still an open challenge due to its variance and diversity of objects. We propose a computationally inexpensive perception architecture that uses the attention-based skills of pretrained vision transformers to locate and coarsely segment trash in images. No special fine-tuning of the model for trash objects is required. In addition, we incorporate a distraction branch into our architecture based on LRP, which provides the ability to divert attention away from common objects, such as small animals, that were part of the initial general pretraining. Our experiments demonstrate the advantages of our approach when new classes are introduced during testing. Furthermore, the modular architecture enables future developments towards computationally efficient trash segmentation for mobile robots.

title: Identification of the Thermal Model Parameters of Industrial Supercapacitors
authors: Ryszard Kopka; Rafał Stanisławski
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper presents the results of determining thermal model parameters of the supercapacitors used in industrial applications. The energy losses inside the supercapacitor were determined based on measured current and voltage during the charging and discharging cycles. Based on them and measured temperatures, the thermal resistances of conduction and convection and the heat capacities were calculated. Thermal model parameters were derived for different charging and discharging currents leading to supercapacitor heating. Results will allow the temperature of supercapacitor housing and terminals to be calculated, depending on the charging and discharging currents at a constant ambient temperature.

title: Multimodal Physiological Signal for the Diagnosis of Parkinson's Disease
authors: Yiliu He; Mengxuan Hu; Boyan Fang; Guangying Pei; Tianyi Yan
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, characterized by a complex etiology and diverse clinical presentations. The intelligent diagnosis of this condition poses a significant challenge. Despite abnormal electrocardiogram (ECG), respiratory (RSP), and pulse signals in PD, which are closely linked to clinical symptoms, there remains a dearth of intelligent diagnostic models centered on multimodal physiological signals. In this study, we gathered multimodal physiological data from 55 PD patients and 30 healthy individuals, comprising ECG, photoplethysmogram (PPG), and RSP. Subsequently, we proposed a random forest classification model employing averaging probabilities, achieving an 89.41% accuracy in distinguishing between PD patients and healthy controls. Moreover, a feature ranking analysis was conducted on the time-domain features across the three modalities. This analysis unveiled the significance of time-domain features from diverse physiological signals in identifying PD, leading to optimization of the classification model and ultimately attaining a classification accuracy of 90.59%. In addition, the pulse and breathing characteristics in the open eyes state contribute more to disease identification, while the closed eyes state is mainly based on ECG characteristics. This research underscores the potential of machine learning techniques in amalgamating multimodal physiological data to enhance the diagnostic precision of PD, offering an objective and efficient clinical diagnostic approach.

title: Improving Hazy Image Recognition by Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
authors: Zhiyu Yuan; Yuhang Li; Jianfei Yang
abstract: Deep learning has achieved excellent performance in computer vision tasks, like image recognition, natural language processing, etc. However, in real-world applications, special circumstances brought about by the external world may create domain bias caused by distribution discrepancy between training and testing data, leading to degrading model performance. For example, when auto-driving meets hazy weather, the model performance will drop significantly. In this paper, we explore to solve this problem by utilizing modern Domain Adaptation (DA) methods, which generalizes from the source domain to the target domain by minimizing the distribution difference caused by dataset bias. We firstly propose the cross-domain haze image datasets and benchmark the five classic DA methods. The experiments show that DA methods can mitigate the negative effect of haze and significantly improves the model performance for visual recognition.

title: Tracking Controllers for a Second Order System Derived from the ADRC Design Methodology
authors: Patryk Bartkowiak; Dariusz Pazderski
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC)-based controllers and their equivalent PID-like counterparts (fPID) for a second-order system, taking into account both full-order ESO and reducedorder ESO (RESO) observers. The study includes the derivation of PID controllers with appropriate filters from the eADRC structure, providing a systematic approach to obtaining PID control laws. The analysis and experimental validation demonstrated the practical applicability of these controllers using an astronomical mount adjusted for ground observations in real-world scenarios. These findings suggest that both control structures provide comparable performance, allowing for flexibility in their selection depending on implementation constraints and application specific requirements.

title: Welding Simulation and Process Parameter Optimization of U-Rib Fillet Weld Based on Genetic Algorithm
authors: Sen Li; Hong Lu; Yongquan Zhan; Guangao Yang; Lang Yv; Zhi Liu; Neng Wang
abstract: In actual production, the welding process parameters of U rib plate are mostly determined by manual experience, which leads to unstable welding quality and low welding efficiency of U rib plate. In this paper, the single-sided double-pass welding of U-rib fillet weld is taken as the research object. The heat source simulation analysis is carried out by ABAQUS Unified FEA to solve the temperature of U-rib weld pool under different welding process parameters, and the mathematical analysis model between weld pool temperature and welding current, voltage and welding torch moving speed is fitted by MATLAB. Taking the molten pool temperature and welding efficiency as the optimization objectives, the genetic algorithm is used to optimize the mathematical model, and the optimized welding process parameters are obtained. The experimental results show that the optimized welding process parameters effectively ensure that the molten pool temperature is within the target temperature range, improve the welding efficiency and welding quality, and provide a reference for the selection of U-rib welding process parameters.

title: Design and Preliminary Experimental Result of a Lower Limb Prosthesis
authors: Honglei An; Jin Zhang; Qing Wei; Hongxu Ma
abstract: Powered prosthetic legs is one of the important means to improve the life quality of amputees by providing net positive work in the prosthetic knee and ankle joints. In order to further develop the research of active prosthesis, a prosthetic with active knee and ankle joint is designed in this paper. We identified the current gait category by the hip angle’s feature (median and amplitude) and used the smooth change of the feature as the basis for the gait transition. With the Improved Kalman filter (IKF) to estimate gait phase, we can get the current state’s position in the whole gait. By modeling the joint trajectory as a Gaussian Process and taking the phase variable as the input, the angle prediction of the knee and ankle joint is obtained. In the experiment, the motion trajectories of artificial limb and healthy human body are compared to verify the effectiveness of the platform and algorithm.

title: 3-D Trajectory Tracking in the Image Frame for Autonomous Navigation of UAV in UAV-AGV Multi-Agent System
authors: Ashok Kumar Sivarathri; Amit Shukla; Ayush Gupta
abstract: UAV-AGV multi-agent system is attracting the mobile robotics research community due to its applications in several engineering disciplines. It's a heterogeneous combination of UAV and AGV. Collaborative kinematics between both agents is necessity of the system for better utilization of independent capabilities. Vision-based method is most focused in the literature to build the collaboration between the agents which is of great use in the GPS denied environments. One of the collaborative tasks of UAV is to approach the AGV and hover over it at certain altitude. A trajectory tracking technique in the image frame is developed for the task in the present work. UAV detects the static target/AGV in the image plane and plans 3- dimensional trajectory to reach and hover at a desired depth from it. Minimum acceleration trajectories are designed using position and apparent size of the target in the image plane. Sliding mode control theory is applied for designing the controllers for approach, depth motion of UAV and validated with the simulations. The proposed image plane-based trajectory tracking technique is further validated in the Gazebo simulation environment. Simulation results shows that the method is useful in GPS denied environments for the UAV to plan its collaborative navigation in the image frame for smoothly reaching a desired position from the target/AGV.

title: Development and Application of a Model for Cold Strip Rolling Human Operating Frequency Determination and Evaluation
authors: Jingdong Li; Jinbo Zhou; Xiaochen Wang; Quan Yang; Youzhao Sun; Haotang Qie
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: Enhancing the unit's automation to achieve fully automatic rolling has become the current urgent challenge in cold rolling. In accordance with these requirements, automatic determination of human intervention in cold strip rolling was achieved by monitoring operational items. The results demonstrated that this monitoring method achieved an accuracy rate of over 99%. Additionally, a cold strip rolling evaluation model was established using a combination of the Combined Weighting (CW) method and the technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) algorithm. The evaluation results provide a direction for further improving the automation level of steel rolling. Furthermore, statistics on the automatic rate of operational items for each cold rolling equipment were compiled based on the level of human intervention. The changing patterns of each operational item's automatic rate over time were identified, along with areas requiring improvement. The industrial application of this approach provides evaluation indices and data support for minimizing human intervention in the rolling process, thereby significantly contributing to achieving fully automatic cold rolling.

title: Methods for Gastrointestinal Examination and Motion Simulation of a Roundworm-like Robot for Gastrointestinal Inspection
authors: Chang Xu
abstract: This article investigates the application of robotic systems, particularly a novel roundworm-like robot for gastrointestinal examinations. Unlike traditional endoscopic methods, this biomimetic approach leverages the movement patterns of roundworm-like to develop a non-invasive, efficient robotic system for navigating the human gastrointestinal tract. The proposed robot aims to enhance diagnostic accuracy and patient comfort by minimizing physical trauma and eliminating the need for anesthesia. This article utilizes a robotic model consisting of six rods and five joints to simulate the movement of a roundworm. The roundworm-like robot performs linear motion within a simulated model of the small intestine. By altering the length of each segment, the study aims to determine an appropriate size for the roundworm robot and analyze its feasibility. Initial simulations demonstrate the robot’s potential to adapt its movement through the simple environment of the gastrointestinal tract, offering a promising alternative to current diagnostic techniques.

title: Research on FPGA-Based Functional Safety Diagnosis System
authors: Huaye Zhu; Qingsong Lai
abstract: The deployment of SRAM-based Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) in robotic automation has increased significantly. In this paper, a functional safety diagnosis system based on FPGA is proposed in accordance with the IEC61508 functional safety standard. The system analyzes safety objectives and potential failure modes. It employs a Soft Error Mitigation (SEM) IP core for real-time monitoring and error correction of the Configuration RAM (CRAM). Additionally, Error Correction Code (ECC) technology is used to perform error injection testing on Block RAM (BRAM), while read/write test algorithms are utilized to diagnose potential functional failures in memory arrays. The system integrates the XADC module for real-time monitoring and threshold detection of external input voltages, ensuring the stability of the power supply. Furthermore, a watchdog timer and logical sequence execution monitoring are designed to supervise the operation of the entire self-diagnosis system, preventing the system from entering a deadlock or remaining unresponsive for an extended period. The proposed system not only diagnoses internal FPGA functional modules but also ensures the safety of the diagnostic system itself through the watchdog mechanism. This paper aims to enhance the diagnostic coverage of controller systems, ensuring the system meets the required diagnostic coverage range within Safety Integrity Level (SIL) standards.

title: Correlation mathematical model of video images with measuring information about geometrical parameters
authors: Igor Korobiichuk; Yurij Podchashinskiy
publication_title: 2021 25th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The article discusses the correlation of mathematical models of video images with measuring information about the geometric parameters of objects. A method for identifying the parameters of these models was proposed, and experimental results were obtained using the example of video images of the surface of products for which the quality of manufacture is controlled. The study results can be used to develop methods for the digital processing of video images and algorithmic compensation of errors of measuring information about the geometric parameters of objects. Such methods are part of the software and algorithmic support of automated systems that use video images as a source of measuring information about mechanical quantities and control the quality of industrial products.

title: Grasping Control of Planar Mechanical Claw
authors: Yizhou Liu; Ziwei Yang; Zihao Fan
abstract: The topic of our research is the grasping strategy of a planner two-joint mechanical claw. Our inspiration comes from a paper on the grasping strategy of soft things by a rigid mechanical hand. If we can get the force sensor's accurate data, how can we process these data to grasp an object correctly? In order to achieve our goal, we built a model of a mechanical hand on Matlab with two joints for each finger. We calculate many functions to process the data and simulate the model. With this model, we get our results. We get the evaluation of parameters alpha1 and alpha2, L, and tau. We increase the robustness of the entry of L. The mechanical claw can grasp a ball steadily and reach the stable point faster.

title: The buried target detection system based on unmanned underwater vehicle: Signal processing methods for parametric Ricker wave
authors: Hanyun Zhou; Wei Li
abstract: To promote the development of marine environment monitoring equipment which is adapted to shallow sea environments, a buried target detection system based on parametric acoustic array (PAA) technology deployed in unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) is proposed in this paper. Due to the technical advantages of PAA, this system is small size, light weight and cost-effective. However, the signal processing methods for PAA are more complex than that for linear sonar system because of the nonlinear effect of the sound field of PAA. Therefore, signal processing method for parametric Ricker wave are designed in this paper, including pre-processing and modulation method for transmitter and echo signal processing method for receiver. In detail, carrier-suppressed square root modulation is used to produce Ricker waves in the far field of PAA. CWT-based and STFT-based Synchrosqueezing transforms are proposed to improve time-frequency resolution and thus detection accuracy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods through simulation.

title: Efficiency Analysis of Cooperative Robot Based on Dynamic Parameter Identification
authors: Tian Xie; Yunfei Liu; Jinglong Liu; Chunlai He; Wei Sun; Shujian Liu; Shuo Cheng
abstract: The energy consumption of cooperative six-axis robot comes from many sources and is time-varying. The calculation of power involves dynamic model and power consumption analysis of electrical components. In the previous chapter, the modeling, analysis and parameter identification of dynamics are described. In this chapter, the power consumption model of the electrical components of the cooperative six-axis robot will be introduced in detail and the related parameter identification will be completed.

title: Reachability Analysis of a Rigid-Flexible Cable Robot for Interior Coating of Tanker Ships
authors: Hanqing Liu; Jinhao Duan; Zhufeng Shao; Zhaokun Zhang; Jing Rao
abstract: Tanker ship is an important transportation equipment for petroleum. Due to the strong permeability and solubility of refined oil product, the high-quality inner wall special coating of tanker ships needs to be carried out regularly, which relies on manual operation with poor working conditions in confined space, high labor intensity, long cycle and fluctuating coating quality. This paper designs a lightweight rigid-flexible robot with a cable-driven parallel robot (CDPR) and a symmetric mechanical arm in series. The workspace analysis of the CDPR is completed based on kinematic and static modeling. The size of the symmetric mechanical arm and the terminal reachability are analyzed considering the interference. The results show that the proposed rigid-flexible cable robot can cover all the areas to be coated, which provides a new automatic solution for the inner wall special coating of tanker ships.

title: Dynamics Model and Design of SMCNN Controller for 4DOF Car Motion Simulator
authors: Ngoc Pham Van Bach; Tan Ngo Duy; Khanh Bui Quoc; Thanh Bui Trung
abstract: This research briefly presents the model of four degrees of freedom (4-DOF) car motion simulators using the parallel and serial mechanism. Firstly, the kinematic and dynamics model of 4-DOF are presented. The actual model of the simulator is often deficient in the system's parameters or has the nonlinear uncertainties. Therefore a Sliding Model Control base on artificial intelligence neural network is proposed to approximate the uncertain elements and ensure the stability of the system at the same time. The stability of the system is proved based on Lyapunov theorem. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed algorithm and the comparison between using neural network and not using this element indicates the superiority of the proposed controller.

title: Novel Lorentz Anti-Roll Inertially Stabilized Platform
authors: Ying Xiong; Qiang Liu
abstract: Inertial stabilized platform, an actuator are used to stablize and point a broad array of sensors, cameras and weapon systems. Existing inertial stabilized platform with the defaults of a lot of interferences about mechanical bearings, high difficulty in using gas/liquid floating bearings and poor linearity for pure magnetic bearings. Now a novel Lorentz force anti-roll stabilized platform is presented to solve these problems. Its spherical structure and the working principle are introduced. The mathematical model of magnetic circuit of Lorentz force magnetic bearing is established by equivalent magnetic circuit method, and the radial deflection moment and current stiffness is obtained. Finally, the platform self-stabilized, large roll reduction and moment output functions have been preliminarily validated using the double closed-loop PID control strategy.

title: Research and Analysis of Load Characteristics of Upper Limb Exoskeletons
authors: Nan Zhang; Xiandao Huang; Wenjie Cao; Hao Chen; Zhenyu Zhang; Xu Gao
abstract: Based on the compatibility of wearing and movement comfort between upper limb exoskeletons and the human body, as well as whether it can assist the human body in handling goods, this study investigates the impact of changes in load quality on upper limb exoskeletons under two conditions: wearing and not wearing upper limb exoskeletons. Considering the strong adaptability of the human body, relying solely on intuitive judgment from the human body is not authoritative. Therefore, external device electromyographic signals are used for joint judgment with the human body. By analyzing the electromyographic signals of the biceps brachii muscle when carrying different mass loads, calculate the percentage decrease in electromyographic signal amplitude, muscle activation level (MPF value), and fatigue level (RMS value). The research results show that under the condition of wearing upper limb exoskeletons, the amplitude of electromyographic signals in both hands can decrease by more than 54% under a load of 5kg. Under a load of 10kg, the amplitude of electromyographic signals in both hands can decrease by more than 36%. Under a load of 15kg, the amplitude of electromyographic signals in both hands can decrease by more than 34%, Under a load of 20kg, the amplitude of the electromyographic signals in both hands can decrease by more than 31%; The degree of muscle activation and fatigue have significantly decreased. Verified the compatibility between the exoskeleton of the upper limbs and the human body, and provided assistance in handling goods.

title: Dynamic Flexibility for Resource Sharing Initialization with Fame and Confidence of Robot
authors: Nayyer Fazal; Zubair Ahmad; Tahir Khan
abstract: Enhanced system performance is always observed with sufficient resources and efficient utilization of resources. To overcome the shortage of resources, a resource-sharing technique is introduced here where the entire system is assigned a flexibility level The flexibility allows the robots to initiate a task despite resource shortage and acquire the deficient resources by generating a request message. The incorporation of flexibility compensates for the shortage of resources and enhances system performance despite resource shortage. Along with the flexibility of robots, the reliability of offering robots is evaluated before accepting the sharing offer which reduced the average delay in task completion by 16%.

title: Interaction Primitives for Robotic Manipulation Based on the Contact State
authors: Hechao Ji; Shiqi Li; Jia Wang; Jie Chen
abstract: Robots have important applications in handling various manipulation tasks. We propose an interaction primitives method for robotic manipulation. The contact-rich manipulation can be represented as a time series of interaction primitives based on four contact states: non-contact, contact, stick, and slip. With the proprioceptive joint velocity and torque as input, the inter-action primitives were solved using the LSTM-FCN framework. We built a dataset of the Baxter robot’s wipe and click tasks and conducted experimental verification. The results showed that the recognition accuracy of interaction primitives was 87.7%. LSTM-FCN outperformed other methods (SVM, LSTM, and FCN) in accuracy, precision, and recall. Interaction primitives translate low-level sensor signals to semantic physical interaction sequences that can be used for human-robot interaction, force control, dexterous manipulation, and task planning.

title: A Fast Method to Calculate the Parameter of Operational Capability Index Model
authors: Changfu Dong; Xue Zheng; Feng Zhu; Mingqian Wang
abstract: Due to the complexity of war and the variability of operational requirements, the parameters of any mathematical model to study warfare need to be adjusted according to the actual situation of war. Operational capability index model is an effective formula to evaluate the capability of combat system, and the current parameter calculation method of this model has a high time complexity. Based on the characteristic topology analysis, this paper presents a fast method to fast determine model parameter. Compared with the parameter calculation method based on genetic algorithm, the accuracy is similar while the speed is greatly improved.

title: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell Performance Decay Prediction Based on Relieff and Long Short-term Memory
authors: Guofeng Xie; Wenyang Qin
abstract: The PEMFC performance decay are closely linked to fuel cell maintenance and energy management. Existing PEMFC performance decay prediction algorithms generally have the problem of single feature selection, which cannot adapt to multiple operating conditions. In order to better predict attenuation under multiple operating conditions, this paper proposes a degradation prediction method based on the combination of Relieff's feature selection algorithm and the LSTM network, where Relieff selects the parameters that have high correlation with the degradation of the performance according to the operating parameters of the different conditions as the inputs of the LSTM prediction model in order to make this model more effective. The method's prediction performance is validated using real PEMFC experimental data. The experimental results confirm that the model can effectively selects attenuation-related indicators as input for LSTM, thereby enhancing the accuracy of the PEMFC performance prediction method across various operating conditions.

title: Optical Flow Clustering Fusion of Improved Artificial Potential Field Method for Robot Obstacle Avoidance
authors: Shuai Duan; Lina Li; Juxian Wu
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings existing in robot visual obstacle avoidance methods such as high requirements for acquisition hardware and obvious influence by environment, a robot visual obstacle avoidance method based on the fusion of optical flow clustering and artificial potential field method was proposesd in paper. Firstly, the optical flow of feature points is detected and estimated using the LK image pyramid optical flow algorithm improved by the polynomial window function estimation method, and then the optical flow information is clustered in two stages using the Density Peaks Finding Cluster (DPFC) algorithm. The first stage is clustering based on the optical flow mode size to eliminate the erroneous optical flow, and then the second stage clustering based on the Time To Contact (TTC) values of the feature points to judge and identify the obstacles, and then the repulsive force is calculated from the TTC values of each point, which is combined with the improved artificial potential field method to achieve the robot's target navigation and effective obstacle avoidance. The experimental results show that the method in this paper can effectively achieve the purposeful obstacle avoidance of the robot, and the algorithm is stable and reliable.

title: Modeling the Variable Pitch Screws by Using the Envelope Theory Based on Cubic H-Bézier
authors: Yanwei Wu; Gengbin Zhang; Yu Ling; Changqing Song; Tie Zhang
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to derive analytical expressions for variable pitch screw threads by employing three-segment composite H-Bézier curves as transitional curves at the beginning and end of the screw thread. Additionally, it introduces a methodology to represent the material surface as enveloping single-parameter surface families, enabling the calculation of the helical surface of variable pitch screw threads. The geometric model developed through this method finds applications in post-processing tasks such as material property analysis, numerical control machining, finite element analysis, and more. Finally, the proposed design and calculation methods for variable pitch screw threads are modeled and simulated within the MATLAB environment, demonstrating their practical value and feasibility.

title: A New Efficient Classification Method for Monkeypox Virus Skin Lesions Based on MPFormer
authors: Eryang Huan; Hui Dun
abstract: Monkeypox is a serious zoonotic disease caused by the monkeypox virus. Traditional laboratory detection methods are time-consuming and have high biosafety requirements; in particular, electron microscopy is expensive and complicated to operate. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel classification algorithm for monkeypox virus skin lesions based on the Vision Transformer-MPFormer. We adopted a transfer learning strategy to train the MPFormer model on a monkeypox virus skin lesion dataset for accurate classification. Experimental results on the MSLD dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves significant performance improvements compared to common models and other classification algorithms, with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score reaching 97.78%, 97.88%, 97.78%, and 97.78%, respectively. This study provides an efficient computer-aided diagnostic tool for rapid and accurate detection of the monkeypox virus, offering important practical application value.

title: EC-WGAN: Enhanced Conditional and Wasserstein GAN for Fault Samples Augmentation
authors: Lingli Li; Zhongxin Li; Xiuli Wang; Jianye Gong
abstract: Considering the issue of limited and imbalanced fault samples, an enhanced conditional and Wasserstein GAN (EC-GAN) is proposed for fault samples augmentation of bearing. At first, random noise along with fault category are inputted into the generator for synthetic samples. Then, the authenticity between real samples and synthetic samples are judged by the discriminator in a minmax cost function with Wasserstein distance. Moreover, the gradient penalty is applied for keeping continuous of the Lipschitz function and gradient vanishing in Wasserstein GAN training. As the collected samples are time series data, one-dimensional convolutional layers replace the fully connected layers of the generator and the discriminator. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed EC-GAN is verified under the limited data of Case Western Reserve University bearings.

title: Research on Improving Cryogenic Tribological Properties of Bearings by Surface Micro-texture Technology
authors: Dongchang Liu; Bin Wang; Zhuanghua Liu; Zhen Tian; Xiaodong Wang; Saipeng Xie
abstract: As one of the core components of rotating equipment, bearing is easy to wear under cryogenic conditions, short life and other problems will seriously affect the efficiency of the entire equipment. To further improve bearing stability and reduce bearing wear, 3 types of micro-textures were designed and prepared on bearing contact surface by fiber laser processing technology, and friction and wear tests were carried out on the three micro-textures under cryogenic conditions. The results show that the flute-channel micro-texture has better anti-friction and anti-wear characteristics under cryogenic conditions, and the anti-friction and anti-wear effects are better with the increase of load. In addition, compared with the type 1 and type 2 micro-textures, the type 3 micro-texture can better collect and transfer the abrasive particles and impurities mixed in the interface by means of the unique channel structure connected between grooves, reducing the abrasive debris retention on the surface of the friction pair. The research not only ensures the stable contact of the friction interface, but also effectively inhibits the occurrence of abrasive wear on the surface of the friction pair, which provides theoretical and technical support for further improving the bearing stability and improving the bearing life.

title: Heterogeneous Feature Dynamic Fusion Network for Pedestrian Re-Identification
authors: Guoyun Lian
abstract: Pedestrian re-identification (ReID) is a fundamental task in computer vision, focused on matching images of the same individual taken from different camera perspectives This paper proposes a novel Complementary Feature Dynamic Aggregation (CFDA) model, which reconstructs a dual-stream network into a main branch and an auxiliary branch. The CFDA model leverages a Shared Dynamic Aggregation (SDA) module to adaptively integrate multi-scale detail features from the auxiliary branch into the main branch, enhancing the model's ability to capture complementary and discriminative pedestrian representations. Additionally, a Neighborhood Feature Constraint (NFC) module is introduced into the main branch to focus on fine-grained local features, further enriching the pedestrian representation by concatenating global and local features. Experimental results on the DukeMTMC-ReID and Market-1501 datasets demonstrate the proposed model's superiority, achieving good performance in mAP and Rank-1 accuracy.

title: Improved Fully Adjusted Neural Network based Recursive Terminal Sliding Mode Control for MEMS Gyroscopes
authors: Luoyu Zhang; Zhiwei Wen; Cheng Lu; Yunxiang Guo; Xinsong Zhang; Laiwu Luo
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive recursive terminal sliding mode control (ARTSMC) using an improved fully tuned RBF neural network for Micro-Electro-Mechanical System (MEMS) gyroscopes. First, a mathematical model of a MEMS Z-axis vibrating gyroscope is introduced. Then, an ARTSMC is constructed with a recursive fast nonsingular terminal sliding surface to guarantee finite-time tracking error convergence. In addition, to release the dependence of the proposed controller on system parameters and to correctly estimate the angular velocity, an improved fully tuned RBF neural network is used to approximate gyroscope parameters. Simulation studies are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: Inter-vehicle Distance Aided Multi-vehicle Cooperative Localization using Split CIF
authors: Wenhao Li; Susu Fang; Hao Li
abstract: In autonomous driving, localization is very important to ensure the accuracy of all the other tasks, and multi- vehicle cooperative localization is a popular research direction in recent years for its improvement on state estimation. However, due to the complex environment, complete information about relative pose for cooperative localization could sometimes be hard to be obtained. Since the inter-vehicle distance is easily measured, the use of inter-vehicle distance for multi-vehicle cooperative localization has become a meaningful topic. In this paper, we propose a general decentralized framework for the inter-vehicle distance aided cooperative localization. In order to fuse the inter-vehicle distance with the state estimation of ego-vehicle, the split covariance intersection filter (Split CIF) is used as the data fusion method. Then, we verify the advantages of the proposed method through simulation-based experiments, demonstrate its applicable conditions and provide its practical application scenarios.

title: Network optimization simulation of wireless temperature sensing device in public area based on ant colony algorithm
authors: Hong-Xia Guo; Luo Sang Zhu Ba; Ji-Fu Zhang; Chao Bi; Tao Zhang
