abstract: With the strengthening of epidemic prevention and control in public areas in many areas, in order to ensure the health of people entering public areas, many public areas are equipped with multiple wireless temperature sensors, which not only effectively saves manpower, but also effectively realizes the real-time detection and data transmission of people's body temperature in public areas. a large number of wireless temperature sensor nodes deployed in the public area constitute a wireless sensor network, which is a multi hop self-organizing network system through wireless communication. considering the minimum energy consumption and optimal efficiency of the network, this paper proposes a routing algorithm based on ant colony optimization, which can fully consider the routing changes caused by the constant change of energy in wireless sensor networks. The algorithm is simulated in Visual Studio.Net development environment. Through the experimental simulation, the experimental results are analyzed to find the route with fast convergence and better path, which proves that the algorithm can be well applied in wireless sensor networks.

title: Reactive Navigation of the Ackermann Steering Robot in Unknown Environments
authors: ANA ŠELEK; IVAN HRABAR; SAŠA ŠTEKOVIĆ
abstract: Mobile robots are now widely used in numerous real-world applications that have complex navigation requirements, especially in environments used by humans. This requires highly accurate navigation that can be performed in realtime. In this paper, a method for generating a smooth motion of nonholonomic mobile robots is proposed. It enables robots to move optimally toward the desired goal and allows fast path replanning when encountering unknown or dynamic obstacles. The method generates smooth, collision-free trajectories based on clothoids, ensuring high computational efficiency and suitability for realtime path planning. By applying a smoothing algorithm, the proposed method improves the robot's efficiency in terms of travel time and trajectory length from start to goal, as demonstrated by a comparison with model predictive control.

title: Research on Key Technologies for Intelligent Monitoring in Drilling and Extraction
authors: HaoYu Jin; XianBo Sun; PangDi Peng; ZhiChao Wang
abstract: Frequent collapses of unstable rock masses in drilling and extraction operation zones pose serious threats to personnel safety and equipment operation. This issue is particularly challenging in geologically complex areas, where the hidden and sudden nature of unstable rock masses makes disaster prediction difficult. To address this issue, this paper first reviews the current state of research on unstable rock mass monitoring, both domestically and internationally, and then proposes an intelligent monitoring technology based on the Internet of Things (IoT). This technology utilizes sensors to monitor three-dimensional data generated by vibrations in real time, dynamically assessing the instability and collapse risk of unstable rock masses. The system offers high precision, low cost, and scalability, enabling continuous, multipoint synchronized monitoring. This provides effective disaster early warning and safety assurance for drilling operations, significantly improving the efficiency and accuracy of unstable rock mass disaster prevention and control.

title: Research on Salt Pool Ion Concentration Prediction Model Based on LSTM and Attention Mechanism
authors: Shaocheng Qu; Xiaocheng Xiang; Haiyang Tang; Guohong Yi
abstract: The Lop Nur Salt Lake in Xinjiang is rich in underground brine resources and serves as an important potassium fertilizer production area in China. Potassium, an essential nutrient for plant growth, not only improves plant quality but also enhances their resistance to lodging, drought, cold, and lodging, playing a crucial role in agricultural production. In the process of ion collection in Lop Nur Salt Lake, the predicted ion concentration serves as a significant reference for guiding the industrial automation of salt mining machines. The predicted ion concentration is not only a part of automated mining but also a crucial step in the automated separation and purification of potassium salt crystals, as the ion concentration at the collection site directly affects the method of impurity removal. The predicted ion concentration can guide the automated production of potassium salt, and its accuracy directly impacts the efficiency of automated potassium salt production. To improve the accuracy of current salt pond ion concentration predictions and reduce prediction costs, this paper proposes a model integrating LSTM and attention mechanisms for time series prediction. We collected measurement data for various ion concentrations such as K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>, Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>, $\text{SO}_4^{2 -}$, Cl<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup>, and Mg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> using ion concentration measurement sensors, recording features such as collection time, location coordinates, salt field number, temperature, and air humidity. By training and testing the sample set using different models and evaluating and comparing the experimental results using various performance evaluation metrics, we found that the proposed model can effectively model long time series data, outperforming RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) and CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) in terms of prediction performance.

title: The Mechanical Designing Process of Proposed Ventilation System For Home Environments
authors: Fevi Syaifoelida; Sharania Udhaya Kumar; Endang Jati; A. M Megat Hamdan
abstract: The research began with general idea to look regards to ventilation system performance in Malaysia. Ventilation is the mechanical system in a building that acquires “new” open air and evacuates the “defiled” indoor air. Ventilation system utilized to control disclosure to airborne contaminants. It is usually use to evacuate contaminants, for example, exhaust, cleans, and vapours. There are fundamental factors that need to be considered. The customer criteria were collected in Klang Valley through survey and interview. The conceptual design was selected by using morphological diagram and was translated to SOLIDWORK. There are four conceptual designs were generated. The confirmation result was gained by using Ansys, to stimulate, to run and able to verify that this product design will run automatically when the enclosed room temperature at 27°C to 30°C. Objective to reduce the waste of electricity and maintain the enclosed room temperature.

title: The Microrobotic System for Activation of the Insect Sensilla on the Base of Microtweezers with Shape Memory Effect
authors: V.V. Koledov; S.V.von Gratowski; V. Shavrov; M Zukovskaya; A.M. Lunickin; N.N. Sitnikov; A.V. Shelyakov; K.A. Borodako; S.F. Petrenko
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Insect pest control requires fundamental knowledge of their physiology and behavioral responses. However, due to the small size of insects in general and their sensory organs (sensilla), in particular, the study of the physiology of insect sensory systems has until recently been limited by insufficient accuracy and selectivity of experimental mechanical action. To eliminate this gap in the study of insects nervous system, a microrobotic technology is proposed based on a micromechanical device - microtweezers based on a layered structural composite of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ti}_{50} \text{Ni}_{25} \text{Cu}_{25}$</tex> alloy with a shape memory effect (SME), combined with a temperature control system and a three-coordinate piezoelectric micropositioner. Microtweezers with SME selectively capture the smallest sensilla of the studied insects, enabling their precise mechanical stimulation with simultaneous recording of physiological responses generated by sensilla by methods of electric impulse derivation in the nerve centers of the insect.

title: Case Studies of Multiphysics AI-Driven Inverse Design of Multifunctional Nano Products
authors: Dima Abuoliem; Vienna Rossmanith; Joel Cho
publication_title: 2025 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: This study presents two case studies validating a hybrid intelligence-guided Capillary Force Lithography (CFL) framework for fabricating multifunctional nanostructures. The framework integrates physics-based modeling with data-driven learning to control nanopillar height via spatially programmed UV exposure. A rubber-based soft robotic hand achieved a friction coefficient of 0.471 and bactericidal effectiveness of 0.916. A second design targeting structural coloration and grip reached a wavelength of 400 nm and a friction coefficient of 0.5576. Results confirm the framework's effectiveness in producing application-specific nanostructures, demonstrating its potential for scalable use in soft robotics and precision microengineering.

title: Research on the Positioning Accuracy of the Drill Pipe Manipulator Based on the Flexible Revolute Pair
authors: Hang Chen; Jun Wan
abstract: Because the analysis based on the rigid body hypothesis cannot meet the accuracy demand of the high speed motion, the analyzing method based on the flexible revolute pair is introduced to study the positioning accuracy of the drill pipe grasping manipulator of the automatic drilling rig. In the study of the manipulator pose accuracy, the flexible model of the revolute pair is constructed by comprehensively considering the flexible characteristics caused by material, structure, motion and transmission. The dynamic equation of the flexible revolute pair and the mathematical model of the terminal pose error are derived based on Lagrange function and equation. It is proved by the simulation and the application that the analyzing method based on the flexible revolute pair can inhibit the terminal pose error and is helpful to increase the one-time-success rate of the drill pipe delivery and the overall drilling construction efficiency.

title: Wireless Carbon Monoxide Level Control and Monitoring System
authors: Apinai Rerkratn; Vanchai Riewruja; Wandee Petchmaneelumka; Sirichai Tammaruckwattana
abstract: This paper proposes an online carbon monoxide control and monitoring system. The proposed system comprises an MQ-7 CO gas sensor module, a DHT11 digital temperature and humidity sensor module, an ESP8266 module, and a Relay Module. The ThingSpeak platform is used to create HMI for online monitoring of CO level, temperature, humidity, and status of the ventilation fan. This proposed system can measure CO and monitor all parameters of measurement data, alert users when CO values exceed the set value. In addition, the measured CO values are used to control the ventilation system operation (ON or OFF) to maintain the CO at a non-harmful level. The experiment testing and results with three conditions show that the proposed system can measure and monitor CO level, temperature, and humidity online with satisfying values. The ventilation fan can operate with function as a design procedure and maintain CO at a non-harmful level.

title: Intelligent Manufacturing Flexibility Scheduling Optimization Based on Hybrid NSGA-II Algorithm
authors: Zhuoya Hu; Jun Liu; Ji Xu; Chaoqian Ye
abstract: The flexible job-shop problem is one of the classical problems that have attracted much attention in the field of industrial automation and control. For the Multi-Objective Flexible Job-shop Scheduling Problem (MOFJSP), this paper proposes a hybrid particle swarm Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to solve the problem. The high-quality solution of the problem is obtained through particle swarm optimization as part of the initial population of NSGA-II, and an elite strategy is used to prevent the loss of outstanding individuals by mixing all the individuals of the parent and the offspring in a non-dominated sorting method. This approach not only facilitates automation in manufacturing and production but also enhances the control and optimization of complex systems. Furthermore, integrating intelligent transportation systems and the Internet of Things (IoT) into the scheduling process ensures real-time fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant control, thereby improving the overall efficiency and reliability of the production system. The experimental results show that the hybrid optimization approach combining PSO and NSGA-II exhibits superior performance in solving MOFJSP. This research contributes to the advancement of cyber-physical systems and the automation of complex industrial processes.

title: Research on the Evaluation of Lane-changing Models Based on Improved TOPSIS
authors: Yuelou Zhang; Lingshan Chen; Ning Li
abstract: An improved evaluation method based on the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) is proposed. This method incorporates the comprehensive weights of indicators to assess high-speed lane-changing models of self-driving cars. Firstly, based on safety, comfort, and efficiency, six indicators, including time to collision, collision margin, lateral acceleration, longitudinal acceleration, lane-changing time, and lane-changing distance, are selected to establish an evaluation system for lane-changing models. Secondly, the entropy weight method and hierarchical analysis method are used to calculate the objective weight and subjective weight of the evaluation indexes. The TOPSIS evaluation model is improved based on the calculated integrated weight. Finally, the TOPSIS model is used to evaluate the performance of different lane-changing models in different simulation environments. The results indicate that the lane change evaluation model integrates subjective experience and objective data information, reduces information overlap between indicators, and ensure that the evaluation results are made more reasonable.

title: Roads Wind Energy Harvesting Design and Analysis Using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)
authors: Hamid Yusoff; Muhammad Wafiy Mohd Mokhtar; Shafiq Suhaimi; Khairunnisa Johar; Wan Mazlina Wan Mohamed
abstract: Road energy capture has been a popular topic recently due to the need of a clean energy solution due to climate change and due to the untapped power generation potential of road traffic. However, the technology of road energy capture is still underdeveloped and most works that have been done focused more on larger vehicles such as lorries, buses, and trains. The objective of this study is to investigate the effects of car traffic configurations on the potential wind power harvesting of a road wind power harvester. This was done by running a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation of 4 different traffic cases with sedan car traffic. The cases are single car, two cars side-by-side, two cars in a single lane, and four cars with two rows of side-by-side cars. The simulation was done using the software Ansys and the car speed was set at 25m/s. The results of the simulation have shown that the configuration have a huge impact on the wind induced velocity where side-by-side cars can increase the induced velocity and delay the distance where induced velocity breakdown occurs. The results also shown that the presence of a rear vehicle can dramatically change the pattern of the induced velocity and increases the magnitude of the induce velocity as well as the harvested wind power. From the results, it was determined that the best location for the wing power harvester is on the side of the road that is 2m away from the body of the car. The results form this study can be used to inform the design on a roadside wind energy harvester of capture solution.

title: Design and Verification of An Avalanche Photodiode Device for Rare Earth Fluorescence Detection
authors: Jian Yang; Zhixiang Cao; Xiangliang Jin
abstract: The gain and spectral response range of photodiodes are very important for rare earth fluorescence detection. However, traditional photodiodes do not have internal gain, which cannot meet the requirements of the above fields. Therefore, an avalanche photodiode is designed and manufactured based on 0.18 μm CMOS process in this paper. N+/P-Well forms the avalanche multiplication region of the device, which is used for the detection of external photons. N-Well is used as the guard ring of the device to prevent the breakdown of the side junction of N+/P-Well. In addition, the principle of the device is verified based on Technology-Computer-Aided-Design (TCAD) simulation. The test results show that the avalanche breakdown voltage of the device is 11.7 V. When the reverse bias voltage is 11.7V, the dark current of the device is 9.8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> A, and the photocurrent of the device is 3.8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> A. The current after the avalanche breakdown of the device is 1 mA. The spectral response range of the device is 400 nm-1000 nm, the peak is 470 nm, and the responsivity is 6.7 A/W.

title: Fusion Model Based Identification of Anomalous Intrusion Behaviour in Network Facilities of Distributed Systems
authors: Can Lei; Anbang Hu; Huayun Wen; Yang Yang; Zhiyu Chen
abstract: Distributed networks, due to their huge systems in the communication process, data management, information transmission, etc., are weak in detecting and defending against increasing types of network intrusions, and there is an urgent need to design a more intelligent anomalous intrusion situational awareness model to cope with brand new network attacks and to guarantee the normal operation of the system. In this paper, we design an anomalous intrusion situational awareness model based on machine learning algorithms for the architectural features and defence deficiencies of distributed network systems, which is developed by combining a gated recursive unit (GRU) and an improved support vector machine (CTSVM), and enhances the system's ability to determine the detection of abnormal network traffic independently. Compared with the traditional machine learning model, the model shows the best performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and other rating indexes by testing and comparing 38 subtypes of anomalous intrusions on the NSL-KDD dataset, which provides new technical support to improve the network security defence capability.

title: Hybrid Deep Learning for Modeling Electro-Hydrostatic Actuators: A CNN-GRU Approach
authors: Linhai Zhang; Chen Jia; Chengjie Han; Wenbo Shen; Juan Wang
abstract: Electro-hydrostatic actuators are difficult to model accurately due to their nonlinear and time-varying behavior. To address this issue, this paper proposes a hybrid deep learning-based modeling approach. First, the dynamic characteristics of the actuator are systematically analyzed, and a simulation model is developed. Experiments are conducted under various operating conditions to construct a dataset comprising multidimensional time-series data, including motor voltage, current, and rotational speed. Subsequently, a hybrid deep learning network integrating a convolutional neural network, gated recurrent unit, and attention mechanism is designed to enable high-precision predictions of both displacement and rotational speed. The proposed method is validated through comparative experiments under multiple operating conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively models the characteristics of the actuator with high accuracy.

title: Design and Development of a Rigid-Flexible Coupling Humanoid Dexterous Hand Based on Flexible Joints
authors: Zilin Xing; Canjun Yang; Zesheng Yao; Anzhe Yi; Yurui Zhang; Xin Wu
abstract: The human hand has become one of the core objectives of bionic research due to its high degree of dexterity and versatility in grasping a wide range of tools and performing complex operations. The key to the dexterity of the human hand lies in the multiple degrees of freedom of its individual joints. However, most of the existing researches use rigid joints to achieve this goal, which, despite the enhanced dexterity, face many challenges in integration and lightweight design. In this paper, we propose a humanoid finger design based on flexible materials, employing flexible joints as moving parts, and develop a tendon-driven humanoid dexterous hand with multiple degrees of freedom. Through simulation and theoretical analysis, the flexible structure design applicable to the metacarpophalangeal joint is optimized and determined. Experiments show that the humanoid finger is capable of multiple degrees of freedom motion, and the performance of the dexterous hand is verified by Cutkosky taxonomy. The rigid-flexible coupling humanoid dexterous hand proposed in this study provides a novel solution for the design and development of humanoid hands.

title: Community Detection in Signed Networks Based on Normalized Laplacian Matrix and Convex Non-negative Matrix Factorization
authors: Yibo Zhang; Tian Nan; Zhaozhi Zhang
abstract: Signed networks can intuitively and flexibly describe the positive and negative interactions among entities in a complex network. Community structure detection is a basic research topic of signed network analysis, which is of theoretical significance and practical value to reveal the organizational structure, functional structure, and individual behavior of complex systems. However, it is still a challenging task to accurately detect the community structure in a signed network. In this paper, we design a community detection algorithm based on normalized Laplacian matrix and convex non-negative matrix factorization for signed networks. The proposed algorithm applies convex non-negative matrix decomposition to a signed network, and decomposes the adjacency matrix of the network into a community membership matrix and a node weight matrix. Meanwhile, the algorithm introduces normalized Laplacian graph regularization terms to reduce noise generated during the decomposition process. Experimental results verify that the proposed algorithm is effective in community detection.

title: Design of PMSM Controller with Continuous Function Reaching Law and Integral Sliding Surface
authors: Ruonan Yun; Jiachun Lin; Peixin Wu
abstract: An innovative improved reaching law (IRL) is introduced to overcome the inherent limitations found in the traditional sliding mode control (TSMC) that is based on the exponential reaching law (ERL). The ERL has been found wanting in its inability to concurrently achieve rapid convergence to the sliding surface and a reduction in chattering. The IRL addresses these issues by integrating a continuous function with an integral sliding surface, merging the advantageous aspects of both exponential and power reaching laws. This new approach abandons the conventional switching function in favor of a hyperbolic tangent function to create a unique continuous function reaching law. Through rigorous theoretical analysis, it has been shown that the IRL not only accelerates the reaching speed from the initial state to the sliding surface but also maintains certain switching characteristics while drastically minimizing chattering. With the IRL as its cornerstone, an improved sliding mode controller (ISMC) is developed specifically for permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). To guarantee stability, a comprehensive Lyapunov stability analysis is performed. Both simulation and experimental results validate the practicality and efficiency of the ISMC. When contrasted with the TSMC, the ISMC exhibits a quicker response time and more precise tracking of the required reference position sinusoidal signal, all while successfully reducing chattering to a significant degree.

title: Simulation and Experimental Validation of an Autonomous Perching and Takeoff Method for a Multirotor UAV on Vertical Surfaces using a Suction Cup
authors: Bruno Chapdelaine; Mathis Celce; Charles Vidal; Lionel Birglen; Bruno Monsarrat
abstract: This paper details the simulation and experimental validation of an autonomous perching and take-off method for a multirotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) using a suction cup perching mechanism on vertical surfaces. The suction cup interaction with different surface types is characterized with experimental tests to accurately model the perching manoeuvre. The resulting model is used to develop a realistic hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation of the perching and take-off manoeuvre of the UAV in Gazebo. A control method is developed to automate the perching and take-off manoeuvre. The method is tested in simulation and is experimentally validated with flight tests. Comparisons between simulation and experimental data demonstrate that the simulation is accurate and can be used to continue the development of autonomous perching methods.

title: Air Preheating Identification for Heat Pump Performance Improvement
authors: Claudiu Rafa; Maria M. Santa; Dahlia Al-Janabi; Octavian P. Cuibus; Tiberiu S. Letia
abstract: The current research concerns the model and the identification of an air preheating component used for increasing the performance of an air-to-water heat pump system. The proposed model involves the Fuzzy Logic (FL) integrated in an Object Enhanced Time Petri Net (OETPN). The model training was performed by a Genetic Algorithm (GA) using sets of experimental data. The model is used for the air switching mechanism. A platform was conceived for training of such kind of models used in identification processes.

title: Design of Multi-lane Formation Transformation Method Driven by Finite State Machine
authors: Xiangqian Ren; Xin Cai; Tingting Yuan
abstract: This paper studies the scenario of multi-lane vehicle formation maneuvering from any initial formation to any final formation. Firstly, a two-layer control framework is designed. The upper layer is based on the Hungarian algorithm to complete the target allocation of formation members, and the lower layer is based on the distributed model predictive control to complete the lane change maneuver of formation members. Secondly, the corresponding control barrier functions are designed for different stages of lane change as the anti-collision constraints between formation members, and the switching of constraints in different states is completed based on the finite state machine. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by numerical simulation.

title: Task-Oriented Trajectory Optimization For Planar 3R Robot
authors: Sławomir Romaniuk; Adam Wolniakowski; Roman Trochimczuk; Adam Pawłowski; Moulianitis Vassilis; Rabab Benotsmane; Kanstantsin Miatluk
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: In robotic writing, trajectory following tasks typically assume a constant tip orientation, with the pen held perpendicular to the surface. This assumption often stems from datasets containing only planar path data, without recording pen tilt. However, replicating such writing movements with industrial robot arms poses challenges due to their inertia and varying kinematic structures. This work addresses the problem of generating tip orientation in the absence of dataset information, while the main added value is presented in reducing torque requirements on the robot arm and improve writing profile accuracy. using a proposed set of objective functions and a numerical method utilizing genetic algorithm. The algorithm’s performance is verified in a simulated scenario involving a 3-DoF planar robot and a set of sample paths.

title: A comparison of Chaotic Key Sequence and Blockchain Hasher for the Privacy Protection of the Internet of Things Image Data
authors: Faizah Safwat; Ayesha Akter; Nakib Aman
abstract: The internet of things (IoT) is a system that requires interconnected computing devices with unique identifiers which can perform data communications without human involvement. In an integrated network of computer systems, IoT devices such as smart cameras and image sensors play a critical role. In the internet of things, images generated by these sensors are constantly at risk of disclosure and privacy invasion (IoT). Because of the presence of third parties in IoT environments, traditional options for securing sensitive data fade. To prevent such malicious tampering image encryption system, while being safe and easy to implement provides a high level of protection to the shared media files. Among them a new image encryption has been derived using chaotic sequence. In this study, a comparison of hybrid image encryption algorithms of a chaotic system based Logical map is described to encrypt and decrypt IoT image data for security purposes using various quality measures.

title: Development of ballast water control simulation system for solid bulk carriers
authors: Derun Yang; Baijun Tian
abstract: With the advancement of computer technology and intelligent navigation systems, the manual button-operated ballast water handling on bulk carriers has been upgraded to computer system operations. Addressing issues such as the independence of ship stowage calculation computer systems, the absence of interfaces connecting them to the ballast water system, and the inability to dynamically synchronize Calculation ballast water and cargo handling during loading and unloading operations, a virtual simulation system has been developed. This system simulates cargo loading and unloading as well as ballast water operations, serving both training purposes and providing remote ballast water control and intelligent vessel management capabilities. The advantages and applications of this system lie in its ability to enhance the safety and efficiency of ballast water management through computational integration while simultaneously strengthening crew training. Increase and improve the safety of the ship in operation, make the crew more realistic training related operations, and improve the integrity of the crew training program.

title: Development and Implementation of a 6-DOF Robotic Arm with Machine Vision for Sorting Application
authors: Angelie L. Umbay; Aldrin D. Calderon; Edward B. Ang; Ricky D. Umali; Jaime P. Honra
abstract: The automation of sorting tasks has been essential for various industrial applications, and this study focused on developing a 6-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic arm to accurately sort objects through QR code scanning. The researcher conducted 40 trials across four distinct sets, categorized by color (red/blue) and size (small/large), obtained from a comprehensive functionality test. This study used sorting time as the dependent variable, while the independent variables are the four sorting categories analyzed through Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). The results revealed no significant differences in sorting times among the four sets, indicating that the robotic arm performed consistently across all categories. This finding demonstrated the robotic arm's effectiveness, accuracy, and flexibility in handling variations in object attributes such as color and size. The study concluded that the developed 6-DOF robotic arm, combined with machine vision technology and advanced control algorithms, was a reliable and efficient solution for small-scale automated sorting applications, making a valuable contribution to the advancement of robotic systems in industrial automation.

title: Extended Kalman Filter-Based Vehicle State Estimation for Direct Yaw Moment Control Systems
authors: Jianan Huang; Yufeng Lian; Jicheng Wang; Bing Dong; Zuofei Shi
abstract: This paper presents a vehicle state parameter estimation method based on an extended Kalman filter with a three-degree-of-freedom vehicle dynamic model, and a simulation platform for the vehicle direct yaw moment control system is built using Carsim/Simulink to estimate the longitudinal vehicle speed, vehicle sideslip angle, and yaw angle respectively in real-time. The simulations were carried out at different vehicle speeds with steering wheel input angular step signals and modeled and estimated values are given for longitudinal vehicle speed, vehicle slip angle, and yaw angle, respectively. Simulation results show that the extended Kalman filter method is well for estimating vehicle state parameters with high accuracy and provides the necessary sensory information for the direct yaw control system of vehicles.

title: Distributed Tracking Control and Obstacle Avoidance of Mobile Robots Over Event-Triggered Communication
authors: Guoyong Liu; Moshu Qian; Cuimei Bo; Zhifeng Gao
abstract: This article studies the cooperative tracking control and obstacle avoidance problem for wheeled mobile robots (WMRs) under event-triggered communication. The dynamics of WMRs are considered first. To handle the constraint that only part of the robots can access the leader, the distributed state estimators are designed. Then, an event-triggered based tracking control and obstacle avoidance scheme is developed by utilizing a backstepping control technique and artificial potential field (APF). The stability of the closed-loop system is proved and Zeno behaviors are excluded. Finally, the simulation of three robots is implemented to illustrate the superiority of the presented scheme.

title: AI-Powered Delta Robot System for Real-Time Table Tennis Ball Tracking and Striking
authors: Vincent De Reu; Hsueh-Chu Hsu; Bing-Yuan Wu; Hsi Tseng; Shuo-Heng Kao; Hsin-Lin Chiu
abstract: The integration of AI and robotics has advanced sports automation, with table tennis serving as a challenging testbed due to its fast-paced dynamics. While systems like OMRON's FORPHEUS and PongBot's M-One demonstrate highend capabilities, their complexity limits accessibility. This study develops a cost-effective delta parallel robot system for table tennis ball striking, aimed at simplifying training applications. The system uses YOLOv5 for real-time ball tracking and trajectory prediction, MATLAB for motion planning, and TwinCAT with Scurve trajectory planning for smooth robotic arm control. A 3Dprinted paddle and ROS-based communication further enhance the system. Experiments achieved a 65.5 % success rate, with higher accuracy (74 %) for diagonal trajectories due to extended observation time. Challenges include image noise and simplified physics models affecting trajectory predictions. Future improvements will focus on advanced filtering and real-time adjustments. This research highlights the potential for integrating AI and robotics in dynamic object interaction tasks.

title: Real-time Object Detection and Distance Measurement for the Patients with Visual-Spatial Agnosia
authors: Adri Shankar Das; Fardin Rahman Sahill; Ababil Hossain Fahad; Mohammed Shakib; A. H. M. A. Rahim; Tasfin Mahmud; Md. Mehedi Hasan Shawon
abstract: Visual-spatial agnosia is a neurological visual impairment disorder that occurs after brain strokes in elderly people. These patients are unable to recognise objects surrounding them and also they cannot pursue the distance of the object. This creates a huge barrier between the real world and the world they perceive. This study proposes a smart eyewear assistive device that will help patients recognize the object as well as guide the patient toward the object by showing the distance of the object with the help of machine learning algorithms. A stereo vision algorithm is used to estimate the distance along with the MaskRCNN algorithm that detects the objects. Physical data has been recorded to analyze the models’ performance with the MaskRCNN algorithm with stereo vision algorithm. This study also proposes future works in this area.

title: Almost Sure ISS and iISS for Randomly Switched Time-Varying Systems with Time-Delays
authors: Qian Liu; Yong He; Kaifeng Dong
abstract: This paper delves into almost sure input-to-state stability (ISS) and almost sure integral input-to-state stability (iISS) of randomly switched time-varying systems with time-delays. We provide definitions for almost sure ISS and almost sure iISS, underlining their necessity with an example that shows the disparity between pth moment ISS and almost sure ISS. Following this, we derive criteria for almost sure ISS and almost sure iISS based on indefinite multiple Lyapunov functions and Razumikhin technique. Notably, these criteria give time-varying stability estimators which do not require subsystems to maintain ISS or iISS throughout the entire time interval. Finally, the effectiveness and advantages of our results are demonstrated through a numerical example.

title: Weather-Based Reliability Analysis System for Automotive Electronics: Assessing Environmental Impact on Component Performance
authors: Piotr Mydlowski
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This study introduces an methodology aimed at augmenting critical safety systems within the automotive sector. The proposed approach entails incorporating real-time environmental conditions’ impact on failure rates and involves continuously evaluating system reliability by leveraging sensor data derived from diverse vehicle components. This method presents prospective advantages, including expedited product development, reduced production costs, and enhanced user safety.

title: Practical Stability of Positive Switched Nonlinear Time-Varying Systems
authors: Ruonan Li; Ping Zhao
abstract: In this paper, practical stability is concerned for positive switched nonlinear time-varying (PSNTV) systems and positive switched linear time-varying (PSLTV) systems with disturbances. Based on a new definition on practical stability which can fully reflect the positivity of every component of the solution, sufficient conditions on practical stability of PSNTV systems are given by using the multiple max-separable Lyapunov function method. As an application of our criterion, sufficient criteria on practical stability are also provided for PSLTV systems with disturbances. Through our criterion, the systems' practical stability can be judged directly from the algebraic characteristics of the systems. At the end, examples are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of our results.

title: Model-Free False Data Injection Attack via Eavesdropping: An Online Approach
authors: Nachuan Yang; Xiaoxu Lyu; Ling Shi
abstract: This paper considers the design of false data injection attacks towards cyber-physical systems without knowing system parameters. The existing research usually assumes that the attacker knows the plant's parameters. However, this is often not the real case since the plant's parameters are sensitive information that is not transmitted and thereby cannot be eavesdropped by external attackers. We propose an inference-based CPS attack mechanism where an attacker simultaneously updates an inference system and designs the injection attacks. More specifically, we introduce the notion of system imitator to cyber-security for the first time and propose a bilevel imitation-based cyber-attack mechanism. We show that the attack mechanism can be implemented in an online manner and the convergence is theoretically guaranteed. Besides, we present a new cyber-threat model in communication networks, called network congestion attack, to illustrate the applicability of our approach.

title: RBF Neural Networks Model-Free Feedforward Control of Piezoelectric Actuator
authors: Tao He; Yinbing Wang; Zhicheng Lin; Kai Guo; Duo Li; Tao Huang
abstract: Piezoelectric actuator is widely utilized in ultra-precision position fields. However, it is challenged by difficulty modeling dynamic properties, such as hysteresis, creep, vibration, etc. Therefore, this paper presents a model-free feedforward control strategy of Radial Basis Functions Neural Network (RBFNN) for piezoelectric actuator. RBFNN is used to estimate the inverse dynamic model of the piezoelectric actuator, and avoiding the difficult modeling and impossible to invert problems. This feedforward controller has model-free advantage that it does not depend on the specific physics-based model and is only data-driven by references and control signals. The parameters of RBFNN are training by offline methods and online learning strategy especially. The offline learning method can compensate the trained trajectory with high precision, but for the untrained trajectory, the compensation accuracy is insufficient. For unknown target trajectories, the online learning strategy is proposed, which utilizes current data for parameter iteration and updating to improve control accuracy. Finally, simulation verify that the proposed model-free feedforward control strategy is effective. Especially the online learning strategy has the adaptive ability and generalization ability for unknown trajectory targets.

title: Pinch Detection of Power Window Using Disturbance Observer for Obstacles with Wide Range of Force Deflection Ratios
authors: Tsutomu Tashiro
abstract: This paper proposes a pinch detection method for an automotive power window. Due to a power window system, we can easily rise and lower a window glass only by pressing a switch. However, if the window is rising while there is a finger or an arm between the window frame and the window glass, it might occur a pinching accident. In order to avoid injuries by the accident, an anti-pinch control that detects the pinching and lowers the window glass, is installed in a power window system. In this paper, an anti-pinch control that can detect pinching of the object with both small and large force deflection ratios is proposed. In order to achieve it, the pinch state index is calculated from the motor angular speed and detects pinching when it exceeds the threshold. The main process of calculating the index is realized by a disturbance observer and a non-linear gain. When an object with small force deflection ratio is pinched, the index moves like a pinch force, and when an object with large force deflection ratio is pinched, the index increases faster than a pinch force by the non-linear gain. Performance and effectiveness of the anti-pinch control is evaluated by the experimental data measured on a power window test rig.

title: Exploration of Lower Limb Multi-Intent Recognition Based on Improved Transformer During Sit-to-Stand Movements
authors: Xiaoyun Wang; Changhe Zhang; Zidong Yu; Chao Deng
abstract: Recent developments in exoskeleton-assisted rehabilitation highlight the importance of lower limb motion intention recognition (LLMIR) through deep learning models. For effective control of exoskeletons, integrating motion pattern recognition and posture estimation is essential. This paper presents a multi-intent recognition framework based on improved Transformer model aimed at identifying locomotion modes and predicting joint trajectories during sit-to-stand (STS) transitions. The framework employs learnable queries and non-autoregressive inference to produce the entire output sequence simultaneously, without depending on previously generated components. Experiments conducted on a dataset of lower limb movements from seven healthy individuals and seven stroke patients demonstrate that the proposed framework performs well in both tasks. The healthy group achieved an average angle prediction mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.76° and a classification accuracy of 98.05%, while the stroke group recorded an MAE of 3.91° and an accuracy of 9 8. 8 3%. These findings indicate that the proposed framework could underpin adaptable rehabilitation exoskeleton controllers, enhancing human-robot interaction.

title: Depth Estimation for Oral Cavity by Shape from Shading with Endoscope
authors: Xi Wu; Gangtie Zheng
abstract: Tracheal intubation for patients with respiratory infectious diseases requires doctors to wear a full set of protective clothing, which takes a certain time. How to protect doctors from infection when facing an emergency operation has become an important issue. The intubation robot may solve this contradiction. To provide visual information for real-time path planning for robotic intubation, this study recovers depth information about the oral environment using the low-cost and widely used endoscopic. Since the oral cavity is small and has less texture, the Shape from Shading (SFS) method may be a good choice for oral depth estimation. This paper proposes the “oral elbow” hypothesis, filters outliers caused by saliva, calculates the 3-D contour map, and highlights the contour map features from different views. Oral images are obtained from a healthy person and a silicon dummy. This work expands the application scenarios of depth estimation to the oral environment; provides depth information for the visual navigation of the intubation surgical robot.

title: Research on Path Planning Technology for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles by Integrating Chaotic Bat Algorithm with Artificial Potential Field Algorithm
authors: Hengyi Huang; Sanli Fu
abstract: In the field of autonomous navigation for drones, efficient path planning is the key to achieving safe and fast arrival at the target. This article proposes a hybrid algorithm that combines artificial potential field and chaotic bat algorithm to solve the path planning problem of unmanned aerial vehicles in complex environments. However, when drones use pure APF algorithm for autonomous navigation, they may fall into local minima in some cases, leading to path planning failure. To this end, we introduced the Chaos Bat Algorithm, which is a metaheuristic optimization algorithm based on bat foraging behavior, with good global search ability and the ability to jump out of local optima. In order to further improve the algorithm performance, we applied chaos theory to IBCA, enhancing the exploration and development capabilities of the algorithm. The paper conducted comparative experiments on the proposed fusion algorithm on maps of different complexities, including traditional bat algorithm, hybrid bat algorithm based on differential evolution algorithm (DEBA), and chaotic bat algorithm combined with artificial potential field method (CPFIBA). The comparative experiments showed that the fusion algorithm achieved the expected path length, computation time, and success rate while significantly outperforming other methods. The improved fusion algorithm can effectively overcome local optima of a single algorithm, provide shorter paths, and better flight performance.

title: Reconstruction of Residual Stress Fields on Workpiece Surface Using Surrogate Models
authors: Junjie Tang; Kuanmin Mao
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: The knowledge of the distribution of residual stress fields on mechanical component surfaces holds significant implications for ensuring dimensional stability of workpieces and mitigating fatigue crack initiation. To address the limitations of current detection methods in capturing continuous stress fields, the bivariate high-order polynomial surrogate model incorporating L2 regularization terms was proposed to characterize stress components. The reconstruction analysis of surface stress fields was conducted by measuring a set of discrete sampling points as initial values. Analyses of two discrete experimental datasets were used to demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in accurately approximating stress values, while maintaining robust generalization capabilities. The influence of sampling point position on reconstruction accuracy was analyzed by reducing the dataset size, providing a novel proposal for surface stress field reconstruction and sampling point selection.

title: Multi-Covering a Point Set by $m$ Disks with Minimum Total Area
authors: Mariem Guitouni; Chek-Manh Loi; Sándor Fekete; Michael Perk; Aaron T. Becker
abstract: A common robotics sensing problem is to place sensors to robustly monitor a set of assets, where robustness is assured by requiring asset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> to be monitored by at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa(p)$</tex> sen-sors. Given <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> assets that must be observed by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> sensors, each with a disk-shaped sensing region, where should the sensors be placed to minimize the total area observed? We provide and analyze a fast heuristic for this problem. We then use the heuristic to initialize an exact Integer Program-ming solution. Subsequently, we enforce separation constraints between the sensors by modifying the integer program formulation and by changing the disk candidate set.

title: Mode Transition Strategies for the Leg-Wheel Robot: STransleg
authors: Zhong Wei; Jiwen Zhang; Yang Yang; Shen Xiang; Weixi Wang; Dapeng Chen; Huiyu Sun; Aiguo Song
abstract: Multiple motion modes allow the leg-wheel robot to adapt to complex terrain. To further exploit this advantage, it is necessary to design suitable mode transition strategies to make the transition process smooth and stable. In this paper, the elaborately designed mode transition strategies for STransleg are proposed. STransleg is a leg-wheel robot we are developing and has four locomotion modes which are four-wheeled mode, quadruped mode, carriage-like mode and two-wheeled mode. With the proposed mode transition strategies, STransleg can transform the mode from four-wheeled to quadruped, carriage-like and two-wheeled. The simulation is done to verify the feasibility of the mode transition strategies. The results reveal that STransleg can do smooth and stable mode transitions with the proposed strategies.

title: Development of Standing Posture Control for 4-Link Robots Using Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yiyang Jia
abstract: This study presents the development of a control system for a bipedal 4-link robot, aimed at achieving stable standing posture and recovery from external disturbances. Initially focused on constructing a speed controller, the study shifted towards ensuring the robot’s ability to stand stably, recognizing that without this foundation, speed control would be ineffective. The control system was developed using reinforcement learning (RL) methods, and a comprehensive reward system was integrated to penalize excessive joint velocities and proximity to joint limits while rewarding proper foot contact. Despite initial challenges in achieving the desired upright posture, modifications to the neural network’s complexity and reward mechanisms successfully led to the attainment of the target stance. The findings highlight the existence of energy barrier in random exploration, and the significance of model complexity and reward design in robotic control.

title: Compression Algorithm for Extended Grid Coordinates used in Mobile Robots Navigation
authors: Cosmin Marcu; Claudia Tigauan
abstract: The data compression algorithms are used in different fields to manipulate and store big amount of information. The data exchange between different systems has become crucial nowadays and it actively contributes to the systems’ efficiency. Besides the applications for file archiving, multimedia and communication, compression algorithms are used lately in embedded systems applications as well. In hardware environments with limited resources such as embedded systems, compression algorithms are used to save storage space and to improve the power consumption by reducing the amount of data that needs to be handled. This paper proposes a compression algorithm for GPS navigation data applied on extended grid coordinates. In addition, the paper presents a navigation method for mobile robots which uses compressed coordinates directly. The algorithm is validated by numerical identification of the results in different scenarios.

title: Dual-Path Neural Networks Enabled Fetal ECG Extractions From Abdominal Electrohysterograpgy
authors: Yiwei Lin; Zhenqin Chen; Kaixiao Zheng; Luyi Ruan; Jinshan Xu
abstract: Fetal heart monitoring is crucial for the early detection of potential risks to fetal health conditions. However, the non-invasive fetal heart monitoring technology using maternal abdominal electrocardiography (AECG) is susceptible to interference from maternal electrocardiography (MECG) and multi-source noise. To address the above challenge, we propose a novel Dual-path Encoder-Decoder Model to extract fetal electrocardiography (FECG) signals from maternal abdominal recordings. It can effectively separate and remove MECG interference to obtain FECG. Additionally, a Feature Augmentation Module based on attention-guided is introduced to optimize the quality of the remaining features after MECG removal. Finally, the optimized features are fed into a decoder with external skip connections to reconstruct the FECG signal. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves outstanding performance on two public datasets, providing an effective solution for fetal health monitoring and assisting physicians in diagnosing fetal abnormalities.

title: Health Status Estimation of Aircraft Engines Based on Clustering and Bi-LSTM with Attention Mechanism
authors: Zihao Zhou; Chuang Chen; Jiantao Shi; Dongdong Yue
abstract: Accurate health status estimation is one of the key technologies to ensure the safe operation of aircraft engines. To improve the accuracy of estimating the health status of aircraft engines, a health status estimation model based on clustering and bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) network with attention mechanism is proposed. On the one hand, attention mechanism is incorporated into the Bi-LSTM network to allow the model to dynamically focus on important information at different positions in the sequence when processing it, thereby improving the model’s understanding ability of the sequence. On the other hand, fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering algorithm is used to automatically partition the health status of multi-dimensional sensor signals in aircraft engines, to reduce the burden of manual labeling. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model are validated on the C-MAPSS public dataset.

title: Human-Robot Collaboration using Monte Carlo Tree Search
authors: Feng Yao; Huailin Zhao; Huaping Liu
abstract: Human-Robot collaboration as a challenging task has received great attention in the academic research field. Many existing search models are aimed at single agent or multi-agent, but there are some defects in the search efficiency of their task targets. Therefore, we propose a human-computer cooperative search algorithm in the indoor scene, where people and agents cooperate to complete the search of related objects. We have developed a platform for human-robot collaboration, and designed a set of algorithms for agent to integrate scene prior knowledge, target recognition, and path planning. The experimental results that the H-R cooperative search model proposed by us shows good efficiency in target search tasks.

title: A Kinematic Parameter Identification Method Based on Auxiliary Variable for Industrial Robots
authors: Fei Liu; Guanbin Gao; Jing Na
abstract: Accurate kinematic parameter identification is essential for enhancing the positioning accuracy of industrial robots. Traditional methods often struggle with poor convergence when faced with large initial parameter errors or noisy data, primarily due to the nonlinear nature of trigonometric functions involved in modeling joint angles and twist angles. In this paper, we present an auxiliary variable method that addresses these challenges by introducing auxiliary variables for the trigonometric terms. This transformation simplifies the nonlinear optimization problem into a linear one with equality constraints, making it more robust under challenging conditions. We establish the theoretical foundations of this approach and validate its effectiveness through simulations using a six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) robot model. The simulation results demonstrate that the auxiliary variable method significantly improves the robustness and reliability of parameter identification, particularly when large parameter errors and noise are present. The proposed method holds the potential for enhancing calibration accuracy in real-world industrial applications.

title: Lightweight Dynamics Model Based Whole Body Motion Control for Aerial Manipulator
authors: Zhenting Wen; Mingxi Chen; Wei Meng
abstract: This paper studies the motion control problem of an aerial manipulator that consists of a quad copter base and a robotic arm. We propose a novel control method that consists of a lightweight dynamic model and an MPC-based trajectory converter to perform accurate tracking control for the end-effector. The proposed method is verified by a step response experiment on the GAZEBO dynamics simulation platform. The experiment results show that the angular velocity disturbance of the end-effector is suppressed by the proposed method.

title: Research on Dynamic Construction Method of Command and Control Capability Packages Based on SOA
authors: Dong Li; Aiwei Zang; Jie Zhang; Chao Wang; Tianqi Lv
abstract: To address the limitations of integration and dynamic adaptability in cross-service command and control systems in a joint operations context, this paper proposes a dynamic construction method for command and control (C2) capability packages based on Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA). The C2 capability package is built on an integrated information service platform, where cross-service operational resources such as strike, reconnaissance, and support are digitally represented. These C2 capabilities are encapsulated into service-oriented, shareable model data packages. By combining operational capability requirements, the system selects, matches, and loads these model data packages to dynamically construct mission-customized C2 capability packages, providing precise operational capability support for executing joint operation tasks. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves construction efficiency, dynamic response time, resource utilization, and task completion rates compared to traditional static methods, non-dynamic SOA methods, and microservice-based dynamic methods.

title: Real-Time Fatigue Detection in Simulated Driving Using Facial Landmark-Based Deep Metrics
authors: He Yueyang; Siti Anom Ahmad; Nurul Izzah Abd. Rahman; Mahdi Mahfouf; Sawal Hamid Md; Noor Kamal
abstract: This paper presents a real-time fatigue detection system using facial landmark analysis for simulated driving environments. The system employs a standard webcam with OpenCV and Dlib libraries to detect and track key facial landmarks associated with eye and mouth movements. The system accurately identifies drowsiness and yawning behaviour by computing the Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) and Mouth Aspect Ratio (MAR). Fatigue is inferred when EAR remains below, or MAR remains above predefined thresholds across 15 consecutive frames. The detection process is integrated into a driving simulator setup using City Car Driving, providing a realistic and controlled environment to study drivers' behaviour under fatigue conditions. The system demonstrated over 95% accuracy in fatigue detection during frontal-facing sessions, highlighting its effectiveness in real-time applications. Challenges such as varying lighting and face orientation are discussed, with proposed directions for future improvements.

title: Qasync: A Dual Network Architecture for Value Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: Du Xu; Lu Jia; Yewei Wang; Qian Liu; Yong Zhang
abstract: In this work, we propose Qasync, a novel dual network framework for value-based multi-agent reinforcement learning, aimed at addressing the control decision-making issues of Connected Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) in merge scenario. The core contributions of Qasync include the following two aspects: 1) Qasync extends QMIX by integrating a feedforward network, which reduces the limitations of QMIX's linearity assumption. 2) Qasync introduces a periodic mixing mechanism that combines Q-values from both networks, enabling Qasync to better capture non-linear relationships and enhance agents' exploration of diverse strategies. We evaluated Qasync using the SMARTS platform in a mixed traffic merging scenario, where autonomous vehicles must merge onto a two-lane road from a slip road, interacting with vehicles that randomly generated at the starting point to simulate realistic traffic conditions. Qasync was compared against several value-based baselines, including VDN, QMIX, and QTRAN, achieving average merging success rates of 80%, 89%, and 94%, respectively. Qasync achieved an overall merging success rate of 95%, demonstrating its ability to effectively handle complex traffic interactions and highlighting its potential for enhancing autonomous driving systems.

title: OSCaR: An Origami-Inspired Shape-Changing Robot for Ground Coverage Tasks
authors: Zirui Fan; Hongying Zhang
abstract: This paper introduces a novel origami-inspired shape-changing robot OSCaR. The objective is to enhance the adaptability of vehicles engaged in ground coverage tasks, such as floor cleaning. The robot exhibits two distinct configurations: it can fold itself for agile navigation through tight spaces, and unfold to cover larger areas efficiently. The folding pattern has a deploy-to-stow ratio of 3 in the width dimension, and a kinematic model is established to simulate the deployment process for the pattern. The hinge design employs rolling contact elements to mitigate collision among the panels, particularly in regions with multiple colinear crease lines. Furthermore, the design exhibits one degree of freedom and features pivots, making it easy to actuate with motors. The system design of the prototype is also presented, including its structure, an embedded hardware system, and upper computer software. The results show that the robot has great adaptability in complex environments.

title: Backstepping Control for Reentry Vehicle Improved by Bioinspired Neuro-dynamic
authors: Liangbo Zhao; Guangsheng Zhu; Ling Zhuang; Baogang Lu; Chuxiong Yan; Jin Li
abstract: For the continuous and smooth control of the reentry vehicle's attitude, this paper proposes a backstepping control method based on bioinspired neuro-dynamic model, in order to avoid the “parameter explosion” caused by the complicated derivative operation in the design of traditional backstepping control methods. Firstly, according to the tracking error of the system, the backstepping controller is designed based on the Lyapunov stability principle. Then inspired by biological characteristics, a neural dynamic model is introduced into the controller design process and its output virtual signal is used as a component of the controller, using the smooth response signal of the above model to realize the continuity and smoothness of the differential signal. Finally, the designed controller is simulated based on the affine nonlinear mathematical model of the reentry vehicle, by which verified that the algorithm has good closed-loop control stability and rapidity, and the control command output is continuous.

title: Modelling and Simulation of a Synchronous Generator Connected to Infinite Bus in a Bond Graph Approach
authors: Gilberto Gonzalez-Avalos; Gerardo Ayala-Jaimes
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Synchronous generators are the main sources of electrical energy supply in power plants (thermoelectric, hydroelectric) because of this, it is important to know the implications of its connection through transmission lines to the infinite bus. In this paper, the modeling of a synchronous generator and its connection to the infinite bus considering decoupled transmission lines in bond graph is presented. Due to the characteristics of bond graph, it is shown that the model is more compact compared to what is traditionally done in other modeling techniques for three-phase electrical systems. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposal, simulation results are shown.

title: Design of a Low Voltage and High Capacitance Tuning Ratio Electrothermally Actuated RF-MEMS Varactor using Standard Microfabrication Constraints
authors: Zorah Bilal Ahmad; Muhammad Mubasher Saleem
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a symmetric radio frequency microelectromechanical systems (RF-MEMS) varactor mounted on a coplanar waveguide (CPW) for a phased array application at low gigahertz frequencies. This varactor is driven by single crystal silicon (SCS) electrothermal actuator capable of generating large contact forces, paired with a compliant mechanical amplifier (CMA) for an amplified and linear bidirectional in-plane motion. The RF-MEMS varactor, utilizing parallel sixty-four beam actuators and a micro displacement amplifier, having a loaded amplification ratio of 7.5, requires a driving voltage of 1.3 V for a 3 μm displacement. The varactor exhibits a high achievable tuning ratio of 1100 %. The RF characteristics of the device show a return loss of better than -10 dB at 2 GHz and an insertion loss better than -1 dB at 2 GHz. The device is designed according to SOI MUMPS constraints, covering an area of 4×4 mm. The varactor avoids problems related to stiction and dielectric charging, by measuring the nominal capacitance for a 0.5 μm gap.

title: Omnidirectional Mobile Robot for Upper Limb Rehabilitation Based Mirror Therapy
authors: Tarinee Tonggoed; Sarut Panjan
abstract: The design, development, and evaluation of an omnidirectional mobile robot system for upper limb rehabilitation based on mirror therapy are presented in this paper. The system consists of two main parts. The first part is a 2 DOF passive arm. It is utilized in transferring the motion of the user/patient healthy arm to the omnidirectional mobile robot. The second part is an omnidirectional mobile robot which a 6 DOF force-torque sensor is attached to its gripper. This robot has the responsibility for assisting the movement of the user/patient impaired arm according to the trajectory received from the passive arm and a force that the user/patient exsert to the robot's gripper. An admittance control method is applied in this system to control the motion of the robot depending on the external force. To evaluate the system, three experiments were set up. The results indicate that the robot with an admittance control can respond to the external force within 54 ms. The step response of this system consists of 105 ms of response time with 6.24% overshoot and the steady-state error is 4.32%. Furthermore, the robot can track the desired trajectory properly.

title: Design and Validation of an Automation Strategy for the Strip Test Process in the Semiconductor Industry
authors: Muhamad Arfauz A Rahman; Chengsi Lin; Paul G. Maropoulus; Woei Sheng Teoh; Azrul Azwan Abdul Rahman; Effendi Mohamad
abstract: The semiconductor devices may be individually tested or tested in a batch process. One type of batch process is strip testing. Strip testing is the electrical testing of a semiconductor while the device is still in the lead frame strip. Strip test offers the most cost savings for small devices and short test times. Despite their advantages, current strip testing is not a fully optimized solution. During the lot change, the operator must perform a series of system-to-physical validation and several steps of system tracking before the lot starts. Various manual activities are happening within the process, consuming many productivity issues. On top of that, human intervention during the process will increase the possibility of the quality issue. The research aims to investigate the current tasks during the strip test process. It also aimed to develop and validate a suitable automation strategy for the trip test process. The work starts with a detailed study of the current process, transaction, and hardware. Later a potential improvement using automation is proposed to replace the operator's repetitive job and simultaneously be fully integrated with the manufacturing execution system. This research is hoped to bring a significant contribution and readiness for the next level of automation in semiconductor manufacturing, especially in strip testing. Through automation functionality, this preliminary work shows an increase in productivity and quality upon implementation.

title: A Fall Detection Algorithm Based on Improved MobileNetV2
authors: Mengqi Gao; Jiangjiao Li; Bin Li
abstract: With the aggravation of the current social aging problem, the health problems of the elderly living alone have become the focus of attention in the medical and health field. Due to a large number of network parameters, the current deep learning-based fall detection algorithm takes a long time to train. To make the algorithm meet the demands of both lightweight and high accuracy, a new method for fall detection is proposed in this article. We improve the block of MobileNetV2 by means of adding channel attention and spatial attention mechanisms before channel convolution and spatial convolution in the block, respectively. The above operation can improve the performance of capturing essential information without additional network computation, which enhances the effectiveness of network feature extraction and detection performance. The computer simulation shows that the detection accuracy of the proposed algorithm on the public datasets Le2i and UR is 98.8% and 99.7%, respectively, which can accurately detect the falling behavior in the image frame column.

title: SLRNet: Shallow Convolutional Neural Network for Efficient Sign Language Recognition
authors: Lamia Mostafa; Faria Jerin Brishti; Eishita Sultana Akther; MD. Khaliluzzaman; MD Jiabul Hoque
abstract: In recent times, recognizing hand gestures from a sign image has become a vital research field in the areas of computer vision and human-computer interaction. Many researchers have taken advantage of various features and deep learning architectures (DLA) to update the performance of existing sign recognition systems. In small datasets such as ASL, shallow DLAs such as convolutional neural networks (CNN) work well. However, the deeper deep learning architectures are overfitted on the small datasets. To overcome this problem, in this work, two shallow CNN models, SLRNet1 and SLRNet2, are proposed. The proposed models use four convolutional layers to extract the features from the sign image and two fully connected layers to recognize the sign. The first and second models gain 98.94% and 99.14% accuracy, respectively. Both models achieve significant improvements with respect to the present state of the art.Contribution— Two regularized hand gesture recognition models, SLRNet1 and SLRNet2, were developed to work efficiently on small datasets without overfitting and perform fine-tuning to achieve better accuracy.

title: A Novel Chaotic Quantum Grey Wolf Algorithm for Optimizing the Task Allocation of Water Quality Monitoring Sensor Networks
authors: Dingyi Jia; Yuanjiao Zhu; Mengfei Wang; Jiahao Li; Tao Luo; Jingyi Wei; Baitao Zhang; Jie Zhou
abstract: Water quality monitoring sensor networks (WQMSNs) are crucial technological applications in environmental management, facilitating real-time monitoring and data collection of water quality. However, allocating tasks among sensor nodes in complex aquatic environments poses significant challenges to network efficiency. To tackle the task allocation problem in WQMSNs and enhance network performance, this paper introduces a novel Chaotic Quantum Grey Wolf Algorithm (CQGWA). This algorithm incorporates a new chaotic operator and a quantum operator to optimize the task allocation of sensor nodes. The chaotic operators introduce randomness, helping to avoid local optima and enhancing the global search capability. Meanwhile, the quantum operators utilize quantum bit representation and quantum rotation gates to refresh the evolutionary search. They select predefined candidate solutions from the candidate states and seek the globally optimal predicted solution for a given objective function. Extensive simulation experiments were conducted to validate the effectiveness of CQGWA. The results demonstrate that compared to the traditional Grey Wolf Algorithm (GWA) and Genetic Algorithm (GA), the task allocation efficiency in WQMSNs optimized using CQGWA increases by at least 8.46%. This significantly improves the effectiveness of water quality monitoring and enhances the network's performance and reliability.

title: A Descriptor with Rotation Invariance of Environment Expression Using Building Boundary of OpenStreetMap
authors: Yuxian Zhang; Runheng Zuo; Hao Liu; Zexing Li; Ruoyao Li; Yafei Wang
abstract: The precise static environment descriptions within high-quality pre-built maps are crucial for the localization of autonomous vehicles utilizing perception-map matching. However, the pre-built map faces significant cost challenges. OpenStreetMap (OSM) provides open access and extensive urban static environment descriptions and has the potential to serve as an alternative approach when the pre-built map is absent. Nevertheless, the environment description provided by OSM presents spatial precision issues that hardly align with the on-board perception. Thus, the perception-OSM association required a method that does not have a high reliance on prior precise spatial information. This paper discusses the environment description method based on building boundary orientations. And the relationship between boundary orientation and the effectiveness of environmental representation with rotation-invariance introduced by boundary orientation and observation direction. To validate the importation of rotation invariance, comparative experiments are conducted on the KITTI datasets. The results indicate that the description method using boundary direction with rotation-invariance can be effectively applied to perception-OSM matching for localization.

title: Dynamic Event-Triggered H∞ Fault-Tolerant Control of NCSs under Dual-Channel Deception Attacks
authors: Chongzhi Liu; Xiaojun Tang; Zeyu Zhang; Xiaoshan Li
abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic event-triggered H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> fault-tolerant control method for networked control systems (NCSs) with actuator faults under dual-channel deception attacks. Firstly, a novel control framework for NCSs is constructed by mathematically describing actuator fault, external disturbance, deception attack and network delay. A novel dynamic event-triggered mechanism is suggested for saving communication resources. Then, through the construction of Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional, the sufficient condition to assure that the system is asymptotically stable and the collaborative design approach for the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> controller and dynamic event trigger are further provided. Finally, the validity and advantages of the suggested control strategy are illustrated through an arithmetic example.

title: Motion Planning of Counterpoint Parallel Robot Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
authors: Guangyu Liu; Junjie Zhang; Lin Zhu; Yumeng Huang; Weijie Yu
abstract: In order to realize the high-efficiency and high-precision operation of the counter-parallel robot in a limited motion space, a method based on the Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO) algorithm was proposed to solve the optimal running trajectory of the counter-parallel robot in time and joint energy consumption. In order to solve the problem that the starting and ending attitudes of the moving platform are very close to the given motion limit boundary, and the optimal path without collision cannot be found, a trajectory planning method based on task-space partitioning and joint-space segmentation interpolation is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Through comparison, it is concluded that IPSO is more suitable for the optimal motion planning of time energy consumption of parallel robots than general PSO, PSOGWO, GWO and IVY.

title: LiDAR-based Robot Transplanter
authors: Masaki Asano; Takanori Fukao
abstract: In Japan, labor shortage of agriculture is becoming increasingly severe due to the lack of farmers and aging. Therefore, the development of automation of vegetable production such as transplanting, harvesting and transporting is required. In this paper, a self-localization method by using LiDAR and a robust control method of a transplanter are proposed for accurate transplanting. In this system, the path of transplanter is generated by using 3D point cloud data, and the transplanting part follows it and plant seedlings of cabbage accurately. Path generation is performed considering vehicle tilt in the roll direction depending on the environment of grooves. An accurate calculation of lateral and angular position of the transplanting part is also proposed. For path following control, sliding-mode control and inverse optimal control are applied to transplanter. The experimental results demonstrated the effectiveness of these proposed methods and problems we have to tackle on. Basically, it was possible to perform automated transplanting accurately, but there was an occasional problem of offset error from 0. It was confirmed that inverse optimal control is superior to sliding-mode control and is more robust to environmental changes.

title: Data-driven tracking control approach for linear systems by on-policy Q-learning approach
authors: Zhang Yihan; Xiao Zhenfei; Li Jinna
abstract: This paper develops an improved tracking control approach for discrete-time (DT) linear system. It's combining the on-policy Q-learning and an extended state space formulation of systems. The main merit of the proposed approach lies in the optimal tracking controller can be found using the measured augmented variables including input, output and their past values together tracking errors rather than utilizing the system model parameters or state of systems, since they are hard to be available in practice. First, the optimal tracking problem of linear system is formulated as minimizing a specific cost function containing the objective of tracking a reference signal with respect to an extended state space realization.
