Therefore, we present on-policy Q-learning method, only utilizing the measured data without need of designing state observer, and the optimal tracking problem can be solved, which under consideration can track the reference signal via the optimal approach. Finally, the validity of the simulation results is proved.

title: A Novel Defect Inspection Approach Based on Self-attention Convolutional Adversarial Auto-Encoder
authors: Jian Wang; Yakun Li; Zhiyan Han
abstract: Defect inspection based on computer vision has gradually replaced the traditional detection method, which is widely used in industry and greatly improving the efficiency of industrial production. Most defect inspection methods use supervised learning, which require vast amounts of label images for training. However, the complete defect inspection task is challenging due to some problems, such as diversity of defects, high similarity defects (e.g., low contrast, ambiguous boundary and small background difference) and large defect scale. To solve the above problems, a novel unsupervised defect inspection approach with Self-attention Convolutional Adversarial Auto-Encoder (SCAAE) is proposed in this paper, based on the encoder-decoder-discriminator structure. In this approach, we improve the encoder and decoder via the self-attention mechanism to enhance the feature extraction ability of convolutional autoencoder (CAE), and then the discriminator helps SCAAE impose the latent variable to cluster by a prior distribution. Finally, large number of experiments on four datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of SCAAE and outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

title: A Variable Speed Bearing Fault Diagnosis Method Based on BAACMD-IDBO-IMCKD and COT
authors: Jun Wei; Jie Ma
abstract: To address the difficulty of fault feature extraction in rolling bearings, caused by the non-stationarity of vibration signals under variable speed conditions and susceptibility to noise interference, a fault diagnosis method based on BAACMD-IDBO-IMCKD and COT is proposed. Firstly, the signal is decomposed using the Bandwidth-aware Adaptive Chirp Mode Decomposition (BAACMD) algorithm and then reconstructed according to the Gini Index (GI). Secondly, the parameters of the Improved Maximum Correlation Kurtosis Deconvolution (IMCKD) are optimized using the Improved Dung Beetle Optimization (IDBO) algorithm that enhanced with Levy flight and t-distribution strategies. Subsequently, the optimized IMCKD is applied to denoise the reconstructed signal. Finally, the bearing Fault Characteristic Orders (FCO) are obtained after Computed Order Tracking (COT). The results demonstrate that this method effectively reduces noise interference and accurately extracts the FCO of variable speed bearings.

title: FAST AND VALID $\mathrm{H}/\alpha$ DECOMPOSITION COMBINED WITH MODEL-BASED DECOMPOSITION FOR POLSAR DATA
authors: Gaofeng Liu; Ming Li; Peng Zhang
abstract: First, since time consumption for extracting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> will become quite tedious for very large images by pixelwise eigendecomposition, we proposed a fast <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> angle's solution. Second, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> may be not unique that results in the invalidity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}/\ \alpha$</tex> decomposition. So we early proposed a sound discriminant to distinguish <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> is unique or not. Third, since depolarization is serious and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> is unstable in high entropy zone, grass and flourishing canopy etc may be misclassified as double bounce scattering. Therefore we proposed a fast algorithm that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}/\alpha$</tex> decomposition is combined with the model-based decomposition, which overcomes the shortcomings of the invalidity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}/\alpha$</tex> decomposition and the misclassification in high-entropy zone, and its time consumption is much shorter than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}/\alpha$</tex> decomposition.

title: Multi-Source Information Fusion Based on DCAFN for Bearing Compound Fault Diagnosis
authors: Yuanhao Sun; Xiaojun Deng; Junfeng Man; Xia Peng
abstract: The bearing fault is one of the most common causes of failures in rotating machinery. Two or more single faults occur at the same time that can lead to compound faults in a machine. Under compound faults, multiple fault features overlap and interfere with each other. Traditional diagnosis methods often rely on single-source data, which limits their ability to capture complex compound fault features. Since the varying sensitivity of different sensors to different faults, we propose a novel multi-source data fusion method for the compound fault diagnosis. The proposed model utilizes the dual-channel Cross-Attention Fusion Network (DCAFN). It is designed with two channels to extract various features from vibration and torque signals. And feature-level fusion is achieved through the cross-attention mechanism. The proposed method provides a comprehensive representation of fault features and significantly improves classification accuracy compared to existing methods. On the Paderborn bearing dataset, it achieved a classification accuracy of 99.85%.

title: Design and Dynamic Simulation of Wheel/Track Transform Mobile Device
authors: Jing Leng; Ming Chen; Jianyu Xiao; Jun Liu; Jiahua Xie
abstract: At present, most underwater robots have a single walking mode which cannot adapt to all sorts of varied and complex seabed terrain. To solve these problems, this paper has designed a new type of wheel/track transform mobile device. Through this device, the robot can selectively switch the walking mode according to different seabed conditions. The mode is switched from wheel mode to quadrilateral track mode, which effectively increases the ground contact area and reduces the ground specific pressure. In this paper, the wheel/track transform mobile device is dynamically simulated on both soft and hard terrain. The simulation results show that the mobile device has the ability to change the shape of the track. It can walk smoothly on the ground with soft and hard terrain, it effectively improves the walking performance of the robot.

title: Non-Visual Semantics-Based Basement Floor Identification and Localization
authors: Guangxiao Shao; Wennan Chai; Wenjian Wang; Xiaohui Yang; Qingdang Li
abstract: With the advancements in computing, interaction, and environmental perception of smart mobile devices (such as smartphones and modern vehicles), precise and reliable floor recognition and localization have become increasingly important in unknown indoor environmental like large underground parking. This paper proposes a method for floor segmentation and localization in underground parking areas based on non-visual semantics, utilizing the general-purpose non-visual sensors embedded in smart mobile devices. The method identifies trajectory landmarks and parking spaces using data features from multiple sensors and constructs with Wi-Fi fingerprints and waypoints a trajectory semantic map. Subsequently, the elevation of the trajectory map is optimized based on pitch angle features, and the DBSCAN clustering algorithm is employed to achieve floor segmentation of the single trajectory semantic map. Finally, a landmark iterative matching localization method is proposed based on the constructed scene map. Validation results demonstrate that this method exhibits high accuracy in trajectory landmark recognition, floor segmentation, and localization.

title: Wireless Sensor Networks Outlier Detection Framework with LOF
authors: Muhammad R Ahmed; Thirein Myo; Badar Al Baroomi; Mohammed A Aseeri; Mohammed H Marhaban; M Shamim Kaiser
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are a class of technology in which low-cost, multi-functional nodes are used to send information over close range nodes using wireless connection. The technology is an open-media platform, it has also been built based on application-driven technology. Its use is not only limited to military applications but can also be applied to the monitoring of the environment, to the health sector, to emergency response, as well. In recent years, WSNs security had drawn quite a bit of interest, which is due to its characteristics and application scenario. A distributed network infrastructure that is built using nodes and other components is vulnerable to several types of attacks. It is vital to implement security mechanisms in WSNs so that their functionality can be ensured. There are several concerns when it comes to providing security in the WSN due to power constrained nodes and smaller network. This study uses the Local Outlier Factor (LOF) algorithm to detect the outlier nodes in WSN, for the purpose of securing the network. We conducted a research study by deploying 300 nodes of WSNs for the purpose of collecting temperature data from them. It was a promising result that could be implemented in a hardware structure in the future.

title: A Low Power Digital Addressable Lighting Interface System for Daylight Control
authors: Mattia Ragnoli; Tullio De Rubeis; Alfiero Leoni; Giuseppe Ferri; Vincenzo Stornelli
abstract: Daylight control is important to maintain adequate visual comfort in indoor environments, moreover providing energy efficiency for the lighting system. In this paper, the design of a low power Daylight Control System (DLCS) is presented. The aim of this work is the development of a low power electronic prototype system for the management of luminaires using Digital Addressable Lighting Interface (DALI). It is designed to allow a comfortable user experience with respect to other DLCS solutions that require a more complex setup and configuration. The proposed system was employed with success in regulating the luminaire power to maintain the illuminance values on the work plane as the daylight varied during the test. Comparing the proposed system to other state-of-the-art DALI-based units, the power dissipation proved to be minor, and the user accessibility good.

title: A Frequency Spectrum Calibration Detection Method for Motor Air Gap Fault
authors: Ya Gao; Yi Gao; Qinling Zhu; Bo Li
abstract: In this paper, aiming at the problem of inaccurate judgment of air gap fault detection results of asynchronous motors of different models, powers and manufacturers, a coordinate parameter correction and spectrum parameter processing method in the process of motor diagnosis is designed. In the coordinate parameter correction method, three-phase current signals are used for FFT transformation, and the corresponding current efficiency is converted according to the set current sensor range. Averaging, taking the three-phase current and the average value as the data source of sector division, dividing and calculating the coordinate parameters of the three-phase current and the average value according to the sector, and obtaining four coordinate reference parameters used as the motor fault diagnosis evaluation standard; According to the different content of fault feature information in different frequency sections, the spectral parameter processing method compresses the information according to different resolutions, extracts its symmetry information and absolute value information, reprocesses the information by using different excitation functions, adds probability parameters, normalizes the spectral information in different sections, and finally obtains the maximum parameter as a dimension in fault diagnosis evaluation by using 1-norm excitation function. This method increases the evaluation dimension in the evaluation mechanism of motor air gap fault diagnosis, improves the evaluation system and improves the accuracy of diagnosis. The method solves the problems that the traditional motor air gap fault detection method has inaccurate evaluation results in different motors and is not uniform in different loads.

title: Field Oriented Control of BLDC Motors for Unmanned Underwater Vehicle (UUV)
authors: Basavaraj S Talikoti; Devindra M Chitguppa; Rahul Kumar; Mohan Karnik
abstract: This paper delves into the domain of Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) Motors that have become significantly popular in modern day applications like automotive, aerospace, robotics (unmanned vehicles) etc. because of the edge they have over their brushed counterpart. Unlike brushed DC motors, which use brush and commutator segments for commutation, BLDC motors use electronic commutation which eliminates wear and tear of mechanical parts, frictional loss etc. This paper discusses mathematical modelling of a BLDC motor, presents the insights about design and implementation of Field Oriented Control (FOC), initial calculation of Proportional Integral Differential (PID) gains and final implementation of FOC algorithm for BLDC Motors of UUV. This technique is far superior than other traditional methods, like Trapezoidal control and sinusoidal control, and implements independent control of torque and flux with the help of various transforms. It is a very useful and precise technique which results in a superior dynamic response, less torque ripple and high efficiency. The key objective is to dispense a holistic approach for designing PID controller for a BLDC motor. The performance of the controller was tested for no load and load condition. The final results demonstrated the anticipated superior dynamic response.

title: Satellite Remote Sensing Application Model Parallel Training Technology Research
authors: Xuebo Zhang
abstract: In response to the long training time of satellite remote sensing application models, this paper first introduces the main methods of parallel training, as well as the support provided by PyTorch for parallel training. Based on this, the target detection model YOLOv4 and the U-Net-based land-sea segmentation model were trained in parallel, and the experiments showed that the training time of both types of models was significantly reduced.

title: Research on Phase Analysis Method of Fused Security Concept Based on Collaborative Tree
authors: Xingliang Liu; Zhichao Xing; Rui Fang; Lina Zhang; Xuan Wu
abstract: In order to identify the dependencies and conflicts among functional safety, safety of the intended functionality and cyber security within the domain of automotive electronics and electrical fields, and to establish a unified safety framework and analysis specifications, this paper proposes a research on a phased analysis method of safety fusion concepts based on collaborative trees analysis. Hazard analysis and risk assessment are conducted by defining collaborative-related items, utilizing collaborative Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment (HARA) or collaborative Technical Safety Analysis (TARA) to ascertain safety goals. Subsequently, through the integration of Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) and Causal Tree Analysis (CTA), functional safety and safety of the intended functionality goals are systematically decomposed. The overall safety goal is further broken down into events associated with functional safety and safety of the intended functionality; The fusion of Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) with Attack Tree Analysis (ATA) is employed to decompose the functional safety and information security goals. This process dissects the overall safety goals into events related to functional safety and cyber security, providing a basis and prerequisite for subsequent collaborative design. Finally, the fusion safety goals are derived based on the collaborative safety goals derived from the collaborative analysis. The proposed fusion analysis method can comprehensively consider the interrelationships and constraints of various types of safety, improve overall safety, form a standardized and unified safety framework, and improve development efficiency.

title: Application and algorithm research of proportional directional valve in speed control circuit of underwater hydraulic motor
authors: Jun Han; Xiufeng Li; Zhida Chen; Hao Liu; Hongtao Ji; Qingyong Zhang; Fei Xie
abstract: In this paper, proportional directional valve is selected as the control element in the speed control circuit of underwater hydraulic motor, and a complete set of control circuit is designed. The control circuit can realize the locking of underwater motor, and can adjust the opening and direction of proportional valve according to the position information of external load, so as to realize the closed-loop control of motor. To handle both the unknown external disturbances and parameter uncertainties of the hydraulic motor system and obtain finite-time convergence, a novel control method combining terminal sliding mode control and improved adaptive finite-time disturbance observer is adopted in this work. The stability of the controller is proved by the Lyapunov stability theory and verified by a numerical simulation example. A numerical example indicates that the proposed control method possesses satisfying dynamic characteristics and high accuracy against disturbances and system uncertainties, showing appealing and competitive characteristics compared to other control technologies.

title: Atomic-level Tracking and Analyzing of Quantum-dot Motion Steered by an Electrostatic Field Positioned by a Nanorobotic Manipulation Tip
authors: Zhi Qu; Wenqi Zhang; Lixin Dong
abstract: Field-control-based nanorobotic manipulation of ions at the single atomic level is an enabling technique for such applications as in-situ prototyping and characterization for fundamental research and rapid product development of nanoscale and quantum devices such as sensors, batteries, neuromorphic devices, and neuro/brain interfaces. Taking the motion of quantum dots (QDs) manipulated by an electrostatic field steered by a probe tip on a target surface as an example, here we show a deep-learning-based approach for their global motion tracking via the individual atoms both on the surface and inside the body. Transmission electron graphs, element analysis, and crystal topology acquired from an aberration-corrected transmission electron microscope (Cs-TEM) are used to identify the positions, types, and structures of the atoms to understand their kinematics. The results show the feasibility of multi-target tracking of homogeneous atoms by their spatial structure projection, which is very encouraging for further extension to the tracking and regulation of crystalline grains, swarms of ions, ion filaments, and single ions.

title: Fixed Wing Deflection Measurement using Sensor Fusion
authors: Jurek Z. Sasiadek; Julius O. Adoghe
publication_title: 2021 25th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The system presented in this paper integrates measurements from Deflection-Detection-Vision-System (DDVS) and strain gauge sensors to calculate the dynamic performance of the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) fixed-wing. The fusion results are more accurate and reliable than the measurement from the single sensor alone, and this is used to design an advanced control system. Unscented Kalmar Filter (UKF) is the choice of fusion method because it gives better performance in dealing with nonlinear systems and deals with white and color Gaussian noise. The presented novel measurement and control system gives accurate shape and deflection of the fixed-wing, which will be used to calculate the aerodynamic performance. The DDVS was verified in extensive experiments with the system installed in the wind tunnel. The objective of experiments conducted was to determine the wing's deflection in flight parameters' function. The results of the camera and strain gauges integration resulted in accurate measurements in comparison with results obtained from one sensor only.

title: Research on Circle Center Positioning Algorithm Based on Mean Shift Method
authors: Yujin Min; Zhuohang Chen; Faquan Zhang
abstract: Aiming at the problems of long-time consumption and low accuracy in the circle center positioning algorithm, a circle center positioning algorithm based on Mean Shift is proposed. Firstly, the grid method is used to segment the contour of a circle, forming a large number of small arcs. Secondly, a dataset of selected center points is constructed using small arcs, which are likely to fall near the neighborhood of true circle center points. Finally, a fast Gaussian kernel function with adaptive bandwidth is introduced to solve the weight problem of sample points, and the Mean Shift clustering algorithm is used to calculate the optimal solution for the data density of the selected circle center sample. This algorithm eliminates bad data from the dataset, resulting in higher positioning accuracy. The validation experimental results show that the circle center positioning algorithm takes the least time, and has an accuracy improvement of 23% compared to the Hough transform and 16% compared to the circle fitting algorithm.

title: Human Behavior Analysis in Virtual Environment for Human-Robot Collaboration
authors: Jiaxin Xu; Lekang Liu; Jie Ren; Yajie Liu; Yanzhi Dong; Xiaohu Yuan
abstract: With the rapid development of robot technology, there will be more and more opportunities for humans and robots to work together in the future. In order to enable robots and humans to better complete collaborative tasks, the analysis of human behavior is very important. Robots should make up for the lack of human work ability. weak parts, thereby helping humans complete tasks quickly and efficiently. This article designed three tasks of different difficulty through the VR simulation system and recorded the behavioral patterns of a single operator, thereby analyzing the tendency of people to ignore corners and other obscure locations during the search task, and to analyze the range that they have already inspected. Lack of clarity and subjective judgments are too obvious and lead to mission failure. At the same time, we compared the different performances of human behavior in human-machine collaborative tasks, and compared and analyzed various data, and concluded that robots are of little help to humans in simple tasks, robots can help to a certain extent in general tasks, and robots in difficult tasks will compensate for humans. Subjective thinking defects lead to higher task completion.

title: Dexterous Three-Finger Gripper based on Offset Trimmed Helicoids (OTHs)
authors: Qinghua Guan; Hung Hon Cheng; Josie Hughes
abstract: This study presents an innovative offset-trimmed helicoids (OTH) structure, featuring a tunable deformation center that emulates the flexibility of human fingers. This design significantly reduces the actuation force needed for larger elastic deformations, particularly when dealing with harder materials like thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU). The incorporation of two helically routed tendons within the finger enables both in- plane bending and lateral out-of-plane transitions, effectively expanding its workspace and allowing for variable curvature along its length. Compliance analysis indicates that the compliance at the fingertip can be fine-tuned by adjusting the mounting placement of the fingers. This customization enhances the gripper's adaptability to a diverse range of objects. By leveraging TPU's substantial elastic energy storage capacity, the gripper is capable of dynamically rotating objects at high speeds, achieving approximately 60° in just 15 milliseconds. The three-finger gripper, with its high dexterity across six degrees of freedom, has demonstrated the capability to successfully perform intricate tasks. One such example is the adept spinning of a rod within the gripper's grasp.

title: A NOA-AP based Typical Process Route Automatic Discovery Approach for Intelligent Manufacturing
authors: Xinyu Cao; Binzi Xu; Dengchao Huang; Chun Wang
abstract: With the continuous advancement of intelligent manufacturing, the efficient extraction of reusable typical process routes based on artificial intelligence for computer-aided process planning (CAPP) has emerged as a critical necessity. Because a good process route can not only effectively improve the efficiency of process planning, but also promote the transformation of traditional manufacturing to intelligent manufacturing. To address this situation, this paper proposes a Nutcracker Optimization Algorithm (NOA) enhanced Affinity Propagation (AP) algorithm under the consideration of clustering effectiveness to automatic discover the typical process routes from the massive historical data. First, two soft constraints (i.e., quantity constraint and size constraint) are introduced simultaneously in the clustering process to ensure the quality and validity of the obtained typical process routes according to the actual demand. In addition, previous research has emphasized that the selection of preference value and damping factor in the AP algorithm significantly influences clustering outcomes. Hence, NOA is implemented to identify the optimal individual within the search space to determine suitable preference values and damping factors, thereby enhancing the clustering quality of the AP algorithm. The numerical illustration shows that the proposed NOA-AP could improve the clustering quality and discover more representative and effective typical process routes.

title: Foot Trajectory Optimization of the Chebyshev Wheel-legged Robot Based on Quantum Particle Swarm Optimization
authors: Jianghao Jiang; Junjie Zhou; Huichen Ma; Lijun Meng
abstract: To obtain the optimal foot trajectory of the Chebyshev wheel-legged robot and improve its moving speed and obstacle-crossing ability, a method of foot trajectory optimization of the Chebyshev linkage mechanism based on a quantum particle swarm optimization algorithm was proposed. The motion process of the Chebyshev linkage mechanism is analyzed, and the displacement equation of the foot is derived by geometric relation. The design parameters are determined, the objective function of foot trajectory optimization is constructed, the constraint conditions are set, and the optimization coefficient is introduced to adapt to different actual optimization requirements. The elementary particle swarm optimization algorithm and quantum particle swarm optimization algorithm were used to solve the problem, the foot trajectory was drawn through calculation, and the motion performance of the wheel-legged robot was simulated and verified by simulation software. The results show that the quantum particle swarm optimization algorithm has fast convergence speed, strong optimization ability, high solving efficiency, and stronger applicability. The research results can provide a reference scheme for the dimensional design of the Chebyshev wheel-legged robot walking mechanism.

title: The Design of Cathode Copper Quality Inspection System Based on Machine Vision
authors: Juan Lin; Yuan Yuan; Yongjing Wang
abstract: in order to meet the market requirements for the surface quality of cathode copper, a copper plate surface quality detection system based on machine vision is designed. The surface quality of cathode copper is judged by image acquisition and processing. According to the actual production conditions of a cathode copper production workshop in Guangxi and the characteristics of the cathode copper itself, the hardware equipment related to the Jetson nano and camera are selected to ensure that the images that can meet the processing requirements are collected. The Yolo algorithm is used to train the target detection, feature extraction and target recognition on the Linux system to obtain a data set. The data set trained by the computer is run on the Jeston nano micro controller, After the CSI camera collects the image data, the data is compared and displayed on the LCD1602. The detection system can increase the efficiency to automatically judge whether the product quality is qualified, solve the problems of low manual detection accuracy and large amount of labor, and realize the full-automatic production of cathode copper.

title: Path Following Control for Human-Robot Collaborative Tasks
authors: Shaundell Dubay; William Melek; Christopher Nielsen
abstract: This paper presents a path following control designed for human-robot collaborative tasks. The path following strategy allows the task description and human-robot interaction to be defined according to components tangent and transversal to a nominal path. With this formulation, the control objectives for each task can be customized to generate motions towards task completion and getting on the nominal path when switching between tasks. Simulation examples of the path following control is presented, demonstrating the ability for the proposed controllers to be customized according to objectives of the human-robot collaboration.

title: A Hybrid Trigger Mechanism for Adaptive Function Allocation and Its Application on Airborne Self-separation
authors: Chencan Bi; Fei Gao
abstract: As the disadvantages of single trigger mechanism, this paper introduced a hybrid mechanism for adaptive function allocation. this mechanism proposed that the automation level of system should coordinate with task demand load (TDL) and mental load (ML), doing so by following some specific policies. To validate this mechanism, it was implicated on the function of airborne self-separation. The automation related to this function were categorized into three levels. Fuzzy logic was used when modeling the TDL and function allocator. At last, a analysis software was designed to illustrate the behavior of the hybrid mechanism under different task demand and pilots state.

title: A Two-stage Improving Scheme on Intelligent Aircraft Trajectory Optimization
authors: Hui Wang; Feng Li; Xiaojing Chen; Le Tian; Dongdong Song
abstract: This paper focuses on the Intelligent Aircraft Trajectory Optimization (IATO) problem. A two-stage mixed integer programming model is proposed to minimize the travel route of the aircraft and the number of visited correction points. Two strategies called SP-MNCP and MNCP-SP are presented to reflect the actual engineering requirements in the intelligent aircraft controlling. The trade-off between the shortest path and the minimum correction points is investigated in detail based on the numerical experiments in the real-world scenarios.

title: Human-Robot Interaction: A ROS2-Based Approach with Voice and Vision Integration
authors: Jing Zhang; MengCheng Lau
abstract: This project enhances human-robot interaction (HRI) by incorporating cutting-edge sensory feedback systems, real-time processing, and an intuitive architecture. A modular, scalable system architecture, developed using ROS2, integrates voice and vision systems to enable robots to execute commands precisely and interact seamlessly with users. Key contributions of this research include the fusion of voice and vision capabilities, the creation of a real-time audio segmentation algorithm, and the design of a flexible state machine controller. These outcomes highlight the potential of advanced HRI technologies and lay a strong foundation for future innovations.

title: Motor Fault Diagnosis of a Brushless DC Motor Using Fast Kurtogram on Convolutional Neural Network
authors: Joselito A. Flores; Conrado F. Ostia
abstract: DC motors are widely applied as reliable industrial machines. However, it may fail due to some defects, unfitting operations, or mechanical wear. Motor maintenance is necessary. To achieve this, detection of a probable problem such as a broken motor part before progressive problems occur. Detection of faults from a motor is the new trend to classify broken components of a motor. In this study, 2DCNN is classifying BLDC motor faults is used and determining its performance. By integrating the Fast Kurtogram algorithm as feature extraction, healthy and faulty signals can be converted into an image for the 2DCNN fault diagnostic algorithm. The fault-finding model was developed, and it classified healthy motor faults such as bearing, winding, and rotor faults with an overall accuracy of 83 percent. The superior performance of the 2DCNN model is evident compared to 1DCNN.

title: Neural Command: Real-Time EEG-Based Brain-Computer Interface for Assistive Robotic Control
authors: Nishat Vasker; Shakib; M D. Sakibur Rahman; Yasin Arafat; Raihan Ul Islam
abstract: This paper presents a method to help people with disabilities interact with their surroundings using brainwave signals. Since individuals with disabilities often depend on different types of transportation, this research focuses on enabling the real-time control of a robotic vehicle through non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCI).Can brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) based on EEG signals control a robotic car in real time? The MUSE headband is used to capture brain waves, and the signals are processed through PETAL metrics and a server within a Brain Wave Processing Unit. Subsequently, they are transmitted via WiFi/IPv4 to a Vehicle Control Unit with esp8266 microcontroller. The system underwent rigorous evaluation, achieving an 85% control accuracy and an average response time of 300 milliseconds. These results highlight the system’s effectiveness in real-time applications, offering precise and rapid response capabilities suitable for assistive technology. This research represents a contribution to the development of advanced BCI-based assistive devices, demonstrating the potential for improved human-machine interaction. The high accuracy and low latency of the system emphasize its suitability for environments where swift and reliable control is crucial, particularly for individuals with mobility impairments.

title: PLC-Based Villa Loft Straight-Line Module Lifting System Design
authors: Chen Xuerui; Li Wei; Li Xiaolei
abstract: Based on the position control requirements of the lifting system, a double DC servo motor-driven double-linked linear module has been developed, which is applied to the transformation of the villa attic unreasonable design. Design to effectively solve the household problem, with low-cost, small footprint, cost-effective, easy to achieve the characteristics.

title: Efficient speed control and comparison of voltage gain and efficiency of Separately excited DC motor with CUK converter and ZETA converter
authors: Mohosina Tabassum; Reaz Uddin Bhuiyan; Md. Muhibullah Shah
abstract: With an emphasis on important parameters like voltage gain and efficiency, this study investigates how well the CUK and Zeta DC-DC converters perform in regulating the speed of an independently excited DC motor. The efficiency of both converters in controlling motor speed was thoroughly compared by simulating them under various duty cycles using MATLAB. According to experimental results, the Zeta converter outperformed the CUK converter, which had an efficiency of 94.33% at the same duty cycle, with a greater efficiency of 96% at a 60% duty cycle. Furthermore, at 80% duty cycle, the Zeta converter achieved a maximum voltage gain of 4.84 as opposed to 3.37 for the Cuk converter, indicating a more stable and with less ripple voltage output. Because of its exceptional efficiency and voltage gain, the Zeta converter is especially well-suited for applications that demand a high degree of precision and stability, such renewable energy systems and electric vehicles. These results contribute to the development of more dependable and efficient electric propulsion technologies by providing insightful information for motor drive system converter selection Â optimization.ˆ

title: Research on the Control Board to Detect the IGBT Operating Condition in Switching Power Supply
authors: Xianzhe Yi
abstract: The high-mode experiment can be obtained by heating the plasma with the auxiliary heating system in the controlled nuclear fusion research. The performance of the auxiliary heating system can be affected by the output of main high voltage pulse power supply. The high-voltage pulse power supply based on Pulse Width Modulation (PSM) technology has the advantages of high effective frequency and little energy storage of the filter system. It is of vital importance that the stored energy released to the load should be very little when some protections occur. The power supply will be connected to the load when the IGBT is out of control, and the AC source energy will be transformed to the load through the air switch. So the air switch should be triggered to disconnect from the AC mains. The control board can detect the IGBT operating condition by the IGBT drive signal, output signal and control signal. So control board can be used to trigger the air switch in a short time, and the energy released to load is very little, which ensures that the load is very safe under protecting.

title: Kinematic Analysis of Pitch Angle for the Platform of a Shrimp Rover in an Unstructured Terrain
authors: Sehrish Shahnawaz; Raja Amer Azim; Uzair Khaleeq uz Zaman; Usman Asad
abstract: In this paper, a kinematic model for the platform pitch angle of a shrimp rover is presented with in-built passive adaptability and ability to move in unstructured environments. With the rhombus configuration of the shrimp rover, platform pitch angle was determined over different types of terrains. The kinematic model of the shrimp rover was established and the rotation angles and the Pitch angle for the Platform of the Front Fork, Boogies and rear Wheel were analyzed. The Kinematic analysis and the Simulations were performed using MATLAB, Solid Works.

title: A new approach to the analysis of linear continuous-time systems
authors: Tadeusz Kaczorek
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: New approaches to the transformations of the uncontrollable and unobservable pairs of matrices of linear systems to their canonical forms are proposed. It is shown that the uncontrollable pair (A, B) and unobservable pair (A,C) of linear systems can be transformed to their controllable $(\bar A,\bar B)$ and observable (Â,Ĉ) canonical forms by suitable choice of nonsingular matrix M satisfying the condition $\left[ \begin{array}{ll} A&B \end{array} \right]M = \left[ \begin{array}{ll} {\bar A}&{\bar B} \end{array} \right]$.

title: Analysis of Research Status and Development Trend of Industrial Robot Based on Knowledge Map
authors: Lanping Li; Yu Zhao; Yuzhe Xu
abstract: In recent years, the literature in the field of industrial robot research has increased significantly, but these literatures have not been systematically and quantitatively summarized. Based on the scientific knowledge map, this paper uses China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) database and Web of Science (WOS) core database 1990-2022 industrial robot related literature as the data base, and uses CiteSpace literature visualization software to analyze the countries, institutions, keywords, etc. of the extracted literature, so as to obtain the corresponding visual knowledge map. Through the interpretation of the visual knowledge map, researchers in the field of industrial robot research can have a more overall and macro grasp of the research history, research status, development trend, etc. in this field.

title: Non-homogeneous Multi-robot Collaboration for Environment Mapping and Inference
authors: Crockett Hensley; Parth Patel; Charles Koduru; M. Hassan Tanveer
abstract: Multi-robot collaboration is the subject of a great deal of research currently. This interest within the field of robotics is prominent because multiple robots can often complete complex tasks faster and more efficiently than a single robot. The majority of the research being done today is related to homogeneous robotic communities, wherein each robot has the same equipment and limitations. The scenario becomes more challenging by introducing non-homogenous teams of robots. In this paper, we explore a non-homogeneous robotic community where one robot (acting as master) is designated to map an area while a different robot (acting as slave) infers from that map. Such a system is demonstrated to be reliable within a small and primarily static environment using two mobile robots equipped with RGB-D cameras and planar LiDAR sensors. This type of role assignment allows for more specialized equipment for both robots as well as greater optimization of the robots’ tasks.

title: Optimization Design of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Cogging Torque for High Voltage Circuit Breaker
authors: Shibo Cong; Naiyuan Fan; Shumo Han; Jianying Zhong; Baoying He; Yuan Deng
abstract: In the motor-driven high-voltage circuit breaker, as the power executive part of the operating mechanism, the performance of motor plays a decisive role in the opening and closing speed of the high-voltage circuit breaker. Therefore, the design of a high-power permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) with high torque density and low torque ripple is the basis for the stable operation of high-voltage circuit breakers. According to the current use of PMSM, it is found that the cogging torque caused by the interaction between the permanent magnet field and the cogging of stator, it will cause oscillation at the end position of circuit breaker. According to the practical problems, the method of rotor slanting pole and opening hole is adopted. Through electromagnetic simulation calculation and actual product test, finally, we can get the optimal solution of the cogging design of PMSM for high-voltage circuit breaker.

title: Feature Extraction and Fusion for Anomaly Detection Using Hybrid Multi-Scale CNN-Transformer Model
authors: Ning Xu; Fuyang Chen; Zijie Wang; Yi He; Shize Qin
abstract: This paper explores the challenge of effectively detecting and analyzing human intrusion events using vibration signals from Distributed Fiber Optic Sensors (DFOS) in high speed train security monitoring. A novel Hybrid Multi-Scale CNN-Transformer Model is proposed to capture both frequency-domain and time-domain features from vibration signals. The model employs parallel networks—a multi-scale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for frequency-domain analysis and a Transformer network for time-domain analysis. The multi-scale CNN uses different convolution kernels to learn features at various time scales, enhancing its ability to capture diverse signal characteristics. Concurrently, the Transformer effectively models temporal dependencies and long-range relationships in the time domain, capturing sequential patterns and dynamics in the vibration signals. This dual approach aims to enhance signal understanding and analysis by integrating comprehensive information from both domains. It effectively handles the diversity and complexity of signals by capturing latent features even in inconsistent signal conditions. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves superior classification performance.

title: LSTM-based modeling of the Tangnaihai and Fen River basins Rainfall Runoff Simulation
authors: Zhengfang Jiang; Baohong Lu; Zunguang Zhou; Yirui Zhao
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: In this study, the Tangnaihai basin, characterized by weak human activities at the source of the Yellow River, and the Fenhe River basin, marked by significant human activities in the middle reaches of the Yellow River, were chosen as research subjects. Rainfall and runoff simulations with forecasting foresight periods of 1-3 days were conducted using LSTM and BPNN models. Despite declining simulation accuracy with longer forecast periods, LSTM consistently outperforms BPNN. Notably, the LSTM model effectively captures the hydrological nuances of different watershed types, although the precise internal hidden layer structure and historical information inputs remain ambiguous. The study reveals that watersheds experiencing strong human disturbances necessitate a complex hidden layer structure for accurate rainfall and runoff simulation. Furthermore, it is observed that the model’s dependence on historical information diminishes with the extension of the forecast period, highlighting the evolving relationship between historical data and forecasting accuracy.

title: Water Monitoring System Based on Computer Control
authors: Lixin Zhao
abstract: In today's society, water resources are increasingly becoming a topic of concern. Although China's water resources will not have a great impact in a short period of time, our country must also attach great importance to this direction. Attaching importance to water resources will help the smooth operation of our economy and provide more guarantees for the future development of mankind. This article talks about the method of water quality monitoring from the perspective of computer control, in considering the low cost, high accuracy, implementability, etc., through the sensor monitoring of water temperature and humidity, PH value and dissolved oxygen content and other aspects of the ZigBee technology network transmission to the data node, and then through the background processor for data transmission and analysis, in the form of a web page to the administrator to transmit the basic situation of water quality, complete the water quality related monitoring.

title: Obstacle Avoidance of Multiple UAVs Based on Reinforcement Learning
authors: Weiting Mo; Jinna Li
abstract: Improving the obstacle avoidance capability of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is crucial for maintaining their operational safety. UAVs with autonomous driving ability is the development trend of future aircraft. This paper introduces a novel UAV obstacle avoidance approach utilizing the Artificial Potential Field-Dueling Deep Q-Network (APF-Dueling DQN) method. According to the dynamic model of UAVs, the three-dimensional dynamic equation of UAVs is established, and the motion space of UAVs is constructed by combining pitch and heading angles. In order to improve the obstacle avoidance performance of UAVs, an improved Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithm is designed, and the algorithm is used to improve the reward potential function of DQN algorithm. Simulation studies demonstrate that the APF-Dueling DQN approach surpasses the traditional DQN in performance, exhibiting robustness against local minima and yielding efficient, smooth flight paths. This underscores the efficacy of the APF-Dueling DQN in addressing UAV path planning problem.

title: Simulation Study on Defect Detection of Penstocks Based on Kernel Principal Component Analysis
authors: XuTao Yi; LiJun Dang; DaiZhi Yan; Yang Yang; SongYi Dian
abstract: The pressure penstock of hydropower stations operates in harsh environments for extended periods, making the pipes susceptible to cracks, corrosion, and other defects. If these defects are not addressed in a timely manner, they may jeopardize the safe operation of the power station. Therefore, the efficient and accurate detection and identification of pipeline defects has become an urgent scientific problem to be solved. In response to this issue, this paper proposes a pipeline defect detection method that combines Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) with Support Vector Machine (SVM). Firstly, pulsed eddy current detection data is simulated using COMSOL software, and then this method is employed to judge the defects. Experimental results show that for the simulated data, the prediction accuracy of this method can reach 96.8%, enabling high-precision identification of the main penstock. This provides more reliable technical support for the safe operation of hydropower stations.

title: Equilibrium Stability Analysis in Neural Networks
authors: Xuecheng Zhao; Fei Wang; Zhiqiang Huang; Feng Lin
abstract: In this paper, the stability of equilibrium in neural networks is investigated. In a non-hierarchical neural network, the outputs of neurons are not explicit functions of the outputs of preceding neurons. The solution to these implicit functions are the equilibrium of the neural network. It is important to know whether the equilibrium is stable or not. The stability of equilibrium can be determined by first linearizing the neural net-work around the equilibrium and then checking the eigenvalues of the linearized neural network. The stability of the equilibrium is characterized by the largest absolute value of eigenvalues. This stability measure allows us to determine the stability of equilibrium, and enables us to investigate the impacts of various parameters on the stability. Simulations are used to numerically analyze the impacts of several parameters on the stability. We also discuss biological implications of our findings and biologically plausible learning using the Brandt-Lin algorithm.

title: Proposal for the Design of a Mechatronic Intelligent Irrigation System with Spraying for Fruit Trees
authors: Alexander Carlos Mendoza Puris; Angie Luisa Herrera Poma; José Alexis Del Aguila Ramos
abstract: This research work presents the design of an intelligent mechatronic sprinkler irrigation system for fruit trees using IoT technology. The design aims to help with the irrigation process through technologies and optimize the agricultural system, the mechanical design has pipes that will help the irrigation of 2 planting lines per pipe line in this way we optimize irrigation, as well as the ESP32 DEVKIT 1 microcontroller, which by its characteristics of being able to connect to a Wifi network is the ideal for the IoT aspect, in addition to comment on the solenoid valves or solenoid valves, The Cayenne Mydevices platform was chosen for its easy distribution, creation and design of this interface, and also for being free, having a version for mobile devices that allows an improvement and good performance in their work, to meet the objectives the VDI 2206 methodology was used, designed especially for mechatronic systems. The results of this research will improve the method of irrigation of fruit trees with internet of things technology, facilitating management through an interface for the farmer.

title: Leader-Follower Safe Formation Guidance for Multiple Unmanned Surface Vehicles Based on Local Sensing Information
authors: Xiaotian Shi; Nan Gu; Lu Liu; Dan Wang; Zhouhua Peng
abstract: This paper investigates leader-follower formation guidance for multiple underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) in the absence of global position information. A local-sensing-information-based formation guidance method is proposed to realize the leader-follower formation control and ensure a collision-free behavior of the entire formation team. First, a composite vector field is introduced to design a guidance law for the leader USV, enabling it to reach the goal point without colliding with obstacles. Next, by constraining the angular rate of the leader USV through the relationship of turning radii among the follower USVs, the collision-free requirement of the formation is satisfied. Then, an attractive vector field based on the leader-fixed frame is proposed, which allows the follower USVs to follow the leader within the sensible area. Simulation results affirm the validity of the proposed USV safe formation guidance method under multiple constraints.

title: Model-Predictive Control of a Two-Switch Forward Converter
authors: Shiv Prakash; Rangoli Singh; Sandip Ghosh
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: A forward converter is used for high-efficiency dc to dc converter applications. Modeling and control of a two-switch forward converter suitable for a wide range of input voltage applications is presented in this work. The third-order model for continuous conduction mode operation of the converter is considered for closed-loop operation for achieving output voltage regulation. The performance of a model-predictive controller vis-a-vis conventional proportional-integral and sliding-mode controllers is evaluated through simulation of the closed-loop forward converter with a voltage variation of 550V to 1000V as input and fixed output voltages of 15V and 24V.

title: Simulation and Optimization of On-Die Termination Based on DDR5
authors: Lu Zhang; Tuo Li; Xiaofeng Zou; Yongzheng Zhan; Menglong Wang; Qi Song; Qing Zhang; Jinfeng Song; Linlin Yang
abstract: With the continuous development of information technology, data is showing an explosive growth trend, and the huge amount of data requires higher requirements for fast transmission and stable storage. Double Data Rate Synchronous Dynamic Random Access Memory (DDR SDRAM) is often used as a cache space for massive data and has a wide range of applications in both industrial and civilian settings. The On-Die Termination (OTD) technology in DDR incorporates terminal resistors into the DDR chip to improve the signal integrity of the channel. DFE provides a good equalization scheme for DDR links. This article is based on the DDR5 protocol and builds simulation models under different configurations. Then, OTD optimization and DFE optimization are carried out under different configurations, effectively improving the performance of the DDR interface after optimization.

title: Integrated force and displacement sensing in active microcantilevers for off-resonance tapping mode atomic force microscopy
authors: Natã F. S. de Bem; Michael G. Ruppert; Yuen K. Yong; Andrew J. Fleming
publication_title: 2020 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Integrated on-chip actuation and sensing in micro-cantilevers for atomic force microscopy (AFM) allows faster scanning speeds, cleaner frequency responses and smaller cantilevers. However, a single integrated sensor suffers from cross-coupling between displacements originating from tip-sample forces and direct actuation. This paper addresses this issue by presenting a novel micro-cantilever with on-chip actuation and integrated dual sensing for AFM with application to off resonance tapping modes in AFM. The proposed system is able to measure tip force and deflection simultaneously. A mathematical model is developed for a rectangular cantilever to describe the system and is validated with finite element analysis.

title: Determination of Basic Probability Assignment Based on Membership Function and PCA
authors: Aoxiang Zhao; Junwei Li; Huanyu Liu
abstract: When using evidence theory to identify targets, how to generate basic probability assignment (BPA) based on the collected data is still an open issue. Based on this problem, a novel method to generate BPA based on membership function and principal component analysis (PCA) is proposed. First, this paper proposed a novel membership function and divide the data set into the training set and testing set, the membership model of each attribute is constructed based on the training set data. Secondly, the testing set sample is input to obtain the initial BPA of each attribute. Thirdly, the contribution rate of each attribute is used by PCA. Finally, the final BPA is obtained by discounting the initial BPA according to the contribution rate. The results of the experiment have demonstrated the classification accuracy under the Iris dataset is higher than other methods, and the average recognition rate of the Iris dataset is 97.3%.

title: Surround-View Road Scene Layout Estimation via IPM-Transformer for Autonomous Driving
authors: Haibin Zhou; Shuo Liu; Jun Chang; Huabing Zhou
abstract: Visual perception technology is crucial for autonomous driving. It can detect dynamic and static objects around the vehicle, which is used for downstream tasks such as obstacle avoidance and navigation. LiDAR-based methods face challenges from costly sensors and extensive computational demands. In contrast, camera-based approaches are more cost-effective, but achieving a bird's-eye-view (BEV) requires perspective transformation, often leading to image distortions. To address this, we spotlight our novel contribution: the IPM-Transformer. This transformative framework integrates the mathematical geometry of Inverse-Perspective-Mapping (IPM) with data-driven deep learning, offering a robust solution to mitigate the image distortions and improve the effect of perspective transformations. We have also developed a novel framework that reconstructs a local map, showcasing both the road layout and vehicle occupancy, in the bird's-eye-view using only surround-view images. Our model achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results in the vehicle occupancy category on public datasets and achieves SOTA results across all categories on our released HuanYu dataset.

title: Numerical Analysis of Internal Defect Detection in Aluminum Alloy Pipes Aims to Provid Data Support for AI Models
authors: Pengshihan Bai; Shang Wang; Jianqiao Long; Kexin Zheng; Jing Ma; Nandu Li; Steve Bruce
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: The online effective detection of internal defects in metals has long faced many challenges. The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has provided possibilities for improving defect detection techniques. However, AI algorithms rely heavily on large amounts of data, which are difficult to obtain through traditional experimental methods. To address this issue, this study proposes a method for the internal defect detection of aluminum alloy pipes and provides data support for AI models and algorithms. We established a "pinch roller-pressure roller-aluminum alloy pipes" model and obtained the variation rules of Mises stress, constraint reaction force caused by the change of internal defect position through numerical calculation. The results show that the position change of the internal defect has a clear functional relationship with the constraint reaction force of roller-A. When the defect is located near the lower part of roller-B, the constraint reaction force of roller-A reaches the maximum value (978.8 N). This study provides empirical evidence for establishing an online defectdetection AI models. It clarifies the evolution pattern of constraint forces related to crack location. These findings provide data support for developing efficient and accurate defect online detection systems based on AI to address the limitations of traditional methods.

title: Refraction Correction Algorithm for Visual Slam Based on Rgb-D Camera
authors: Xianshuai Sun; Yuming Zhao; Yabiao Wang; Zhigang Li; Zhen He; Xiaohui Wang
abstract: The visual SLAM algorithm is widely adopted in the air because of its superiority in simultaneous localization and mapping. However, applying the visual SLAM algorithm to environments in other media can lead to refractive errors in the generated images caused by light passing through different media, resulting in algorithm failure. To enhance the environmental adaptability of the visual SLAM algorithm and achieve simultaneous localization and mapping of specialized robots in special media, we construct a visual SLAM experimental device using a Raspberry Pi and an RGB-D camera. Specifically, we propose a refraction correction algorithm based on an RGBD camera, obtaining equivalent pixel images of distorted pixels in the air. We integrate the refraction correction algorithm into the front end of the previously proposed point-line visual SLAM algorithm. Through validation in a real experimentalenvironment, the refraction correction algorithm successfully draws semi-dense pointcloud maps underwater. Compared with not using the refraction correction model, our proposed algorithm better restores the structural information of the underwater environment and objects in the water.

title: PENG-IQ: Perceptive Entrance Greeting and IoT-Based Queueing Management System
authors: Krizele Joyce Dupa; Raymond Pizon; Ian Nietes; Glenda S. Guanzon; Kent Lexter Co; Adha Theza Naputol; Jopearlson Icy Ituriaga
publication_title: 2025 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on [::Robotics::] and Technologies for Industrial [::Automation::] (ROBOTHIA)
abstract: This research addresses prolonged waiting times and the repetitive greeting tasks of security personnel in a university setting. The proposed system combines a robot for greeting automation and a web application for paperless queue management and monitoring. Specifically, the robot comprises a microcontroller, an ultrasonic sensor, servo motors, a speaker, and an LCD. In addition, the web application utilizes a lightweight Flask framework, ensuring efficient performance and accessibility across various devices. Furthermore, testing of different network modes within the university shows acceptable performance. Consequently, the system demonstrates fast response times and efficient processing of queue requests. Moreover, the robot quickly updates when there are server changes, ensuring a seamless client experience. Based on the results, this research successfully integrated a robot with automated greeting and web application effectively that addresses repetitive greeting and waiting times in queue management within a university setting. Overall, the system's smooth operation across various network conditions underscores its practical benefits, offering a potential solution to enhance operational efficiency and client satisfaction.

title: Spatial Pooling Network For Lane Line Segmentation
authors: Yanteng Ge; Yang-Yang Chen; Faxiang Zhang
abstract: In this paper, a novel method named spatial pooling is proposed for visual lane line segmentation. Occlusion is one of the most common and difficult scenes among various and complex road environments. In most existing references, the structure of lane line is still not considered for the occlusion problem. To better solve this case and enhance the long-distance information fusion for lane lines, a spatial pooling module is proposed firstly by using a combination of horizontal and vertical pooling to achieve pooling in the direction across the lane line. This method can enhance the information fusion ability in oblique directions and improve the lane line detection performance. Then, for further study, we propose an end-to-end network for lane line segmentation based on the spatial pooling module. Finally, the experimental results on tuSimple lane line dataset verify the effectiveness of our method.

title: Flight Control of Tiltrotor Uavs: Pso-Optimized Neural Network Aerodynamic Modeling With Esobased Disturbance Compensation
authors: Xiaomei Cheng; Jiesong Yang; Bo Shao; Yingxun Wang
abstract: Tiltrotor UAVs, with their capability to operate in both fixed-wing and rotorcraft flight modes, hold significant potential for applications in complex environments. However, their nonlinear aerodynamic characteristics at low speeds are difficult to identify using traditional modeling methods, which limits control accuracy. This paper proposes an aerodynamic identification method based on neural networks and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), leveraging offline historical flight data processing to construct a high-precision aerodynamic model. This model is then integrated as a compensation term into the realtime control system to enhance model accuracy. To mitigate the impact of unknown disturbances during flight, extended state observers (ESOs) are further employed for real-time compensation, improving disturbance rejection and trajectory tracking accuracy. The simulation is conducted on a tiltrotor UAV using an eight-shaped flight trajectory experiment. The results indicate that this method significantly improves control performance under low-speed flight conditions, while also enhancing the system's robustness.

title: Path Planning of Mobile Robot Based on BiLSTM-D3QN Algorithm
authors: Shuhong Song; Zhenggang Wang; Shenghui Cheng
abstract: Aiming at the traditional deep reinforcement learning algorithms with slow network convergence, poor reward convergence stability, and low path planning efficiency, this paper proposes a BiLSTM-D3QN path planning algorithm based on the DDQN decision model. Firstly, bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) is introduced to make the network memorable and increase the stability of decision-making, so that the reward convergence is more stable; secondly, the adaptive reprioritization of experience replay based on frequency penalty function is proposed to extract important and fresh data from the experience pool to accelerate the convergence of the neural network. Lastly, an adaptive action selection mechanism is introduced to optimize the action exploration further. Simulation experiments show that the BiLSTM-D3QN path planning algorithm ha 2 fewer inflection points, 0.52s less planning time, and 4.4% higher success rate than the DDQN algorithm, and outperforms the traditional deep reinforcement learning algorithms in terms of the convergence speed of the network, the efficiency of the planning, and the stability of the convergence of rewards. The superiority of the BiLSTM-D3QN algorithm in network convergence speed and path planning performance is demonstrated.

title: The Generation Method of Simulation Scenario Sample Space Based on Sensitivity Analysis of Meta-model
authors: Jing An; Wei Liu; Wanting Rong; Haoliang Qi
abstract: To ensure the feasibility and effectiveness of exploratory simulation experiments, it is necessary to take the simulation scenario sample space with acceptable scale and typical representative as input. In this paper, a method of generating simulation scenario sample space combining qualitative and quantitative analysis is proposed. This method constructs a machine learning meta-model based on simulation pre-experiment, and screens the key experimental factors based on sensitivity analysis of meta-model to determine the factor levels. Finally, the space is sampled and compressed to complete the generation of the hypothetical sample space.

title: Fast; Reliable Constrained Manipulation Using a VSA Driven Planar Robot
authors: Andrew L. Bernhard; Joseph M. Schimmels
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance of a planar 3R robot capable of dexterous constrained manipulation when interacting with a stiff environment. A novel variable stiffness actuator (VSA) having a stiffness ratio of approximately 500 is also described. Variable stiffness actuation, together with a combined position/compliance manipulation path, is used to: 1) allow the robot to passively comply with its environment along kinematically constrained directions despite model error in constraint locations, and 2) generate high stiffness for accurate motion control along kinematically unconstrained directions despite resisting forces. This manipulation strategy provides dexterity for cases in which mechanical work must be performed while complying with constraints. The manipulation strategy and robot performance were evaluated with the task of turning a steel crank to lift a weight. Results show that, when using passive compliance control, the robot completed the task 29 times faster with constraint forces 80% lower than when using traditional active compliance control (with VSAs at their highest stiffness).

title: Rational Intelligence Model: Overcoming Data Handling Limitations in LLMs
authors: XueHong Tao; Yuan Miao; Guanhua Wang
abstract: Many human-computer interactions and automated processes are dependent on data. We need to correctly store data and retrieve data to support these processes. Large Language Models (LLMs) have made significant progress in comprehension and reasoning. However, we have found that their ability to handle professional data is weak, which significantly limits their applications in automated processes and professional applications. These scenarios often involve a large number of similar data entries, which are challenging for LLMs such as ChatGPT-4 Omni. In this paper, we propose a Rational Intelligence Model that comprehends human experts' knowledge of data structure and process requirements of data, automatically extracts data from conversations with end users, and effectively stores the data and retrieves it for supporting the interaction and process. Experiments show that ChatGPT-4o can achieve 0% error in simple queries, 2.6% errors when data entries are out of order, and 38% errors when the queries are reasonably complex. However, with our proposed Rational Intelligence Model (RIM), we can achieve 0% error rate in all tests. RIM fundamentally changes software engineering and expert system development approaches. Instead of having a software engineer understand expert knowledge of data processing, this is now achieved by RIM, which means it is much more flexible, lower in cost, and requires much less development time.

title: Detection of Building Infrastructure Elements in Layouts Using YOLO as a Foundation for Graph-Based Adversarial Attack Path Modeling
authors: Jan Kapusta; Waldemar Bauer; Jerzy Baranowski
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Protecting buildings—especially critical infrastructure—has become increasingly urgent amid evolving threats. Traditional assessments, based on visual inspections and expert analyses, struggle with the complexity and scale of modern structures. Meanwhile, although object detection is widely used in real-time surveillance, its application to static architectural layouts remains limited. This paper presents a novel use of the YOLOv8m framework to automatically identify structural elements in architectural plans, laying the groundwork for building topological graphs that map potential adversarial attack paths. Our work contributes by creating a curated dataset of real and synthetic building layouts with annotated architectural symbols, designing a customized YOLOv8m pipeline for effective object detection, and developing an initial framework for converting detections into graph-based security models. By integrating deep learning with traditional security methods, this research enhances the modeling and assessment of physical security.

title: Traversability Map Estimation for Agricultural Robots
authors: Paul-Stelian Sucală; Levente Tamás
abstract: The key component of the precision agriculture application is the integration of autonomous robots in outdoor fields. Autonomous locomotion is based on estimating the traversability zone, the zone without obstacles for safe navigation. This can be done by relying on 2D or 3D perception modules, which are also becoming affordable for these types of applications. In this work, we investigate the use of these sensors in the embedded application context. This is important because network connections usually have low bandwidth on agricultural sites. We report on our first experimental trial results from real-condition setups. The recorded code and datasets are available on the author’ s website.

title: Automated Detection of Korean Melons Based on YOLOv10 for Use in Quadruped Robot
authors: Do Hyeon Lee; Dong Seok Shin; Yoel Kim; Young Jin Seo; Do Yeon Won; Hyun Kwon Suh
abstract: The production of Korean melon, known as Chamoe, in South Korea faces significant challenges due to the decline of the rural labor force and the high labor demands of manual greenhouse harvesting. This study provides a critical step toward developing an automated Korean melon harvesting system using a quadruped robotic platform. This study focuses on the evaluation of a deep learning model, YOLOv10, for accurate melon detection in Korean greenhouse environments, which is a key component of the proposed automated harvesting system. We used YOLOv10, a state-of-the-art object detection algorithm, and the model was trained and tested on a custom dataset of Korean melon images. An NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU and an Intel Core i9-13900K (3.0-5.8 GHz) CPU running Ubuntu 22.04 were used for the performance evaluation. The YOLOv10-based model showed promising results, achieving a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.927 at an intersection over union (IoU) threshold of 0.5. This model is suitable for use in robotic systems where resources are limited due to its compact size of only 5.7 MB. The model used only 11 % of the GPU capacity for setup and 2–3 % for inference. This demonstrates its efficiency and potential for real-time applications.

title: Research on Crimping Quality Enhancement Technology of Tension Clamp in Overhead Transmission Line
authors: Fei Peng; Jinlu Ni; Fei Zhao; Yujing Hao; Zihan Xiang; Ying Zhang; Chi Zhang
abstract: Crimping of tension clamp is a key hidden project in the construction of overhead transmission line, and its quality directly affects the reliability and safety of the power grid. The existing crimping equipments have the problems of poor controllability and poor crimping quality. To solve above problems, an active control scheme of closing speed based on the sensor feedback unit is proposed. First, the crimping process of tension clamp was introduced, and the characteristics of the existing crimping process was analyzed. Second, a finite element model of tension clamp crimping was established to systematically analyze the deformation law of conductor and tension clamp during crimping process. Finally, the hydraulic oil circuit and control system of the automatic crimping machine were improved. Furthermore, the comparative experiment was carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the aluminum tube crimping fringe which can improve the quality of wire crimping and provide a new solution for improving crimping equipment.

title: Extraction of Weld Seam Centerline Based on Improved Canny Algorithm
authors: Yuxuan Yang; Bing Wei; Xiaoqing Cao; Pengtao Zhu; Yiran Guo
abstract: Based on the analysis of characteristics in weld seam images, this paper proposes an improved method for detecting the centerline position using an adapted Canny algorithm, addressing issues such as susceptibility to noise interference and poor connection of strong and weak edges. Initially, adaptive median filtering and enhanced bilateral filtering replace traditional Gaussian filtering in the Canny algorithm. Subsequently, histogram analysis and Otsu's method are employed to adaptively select thresholds for the Canny operator. Finally, the Canny algorithm is utilized for extracting weld seam edges. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to Gaussian filtering, employing adaptive median and bilateral filtering improves Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) by 9.2145 dB and reduces Mean Squared Error (MSE) by 33.32819, indicating superior effectiveness in preserving image details and eliminating noise. Pratt's Figure of Merit (PFOM) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) values approaching 1 further underscore the algorithm's enhanced precision.

title: Application of Time-Frequency Signal Processing Techniques for UAV Fault Diagnosis
authors: Radosław Puchalski
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The increasing number of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) elevates the risk of failures that may lead to infrastructure damage and pose safety hazards to humans. One critical failure mode in multirotor drones is propeller fault, which can significantly impact flight stability and safety. This study investigates the feasibility of early detection of such defects using advanced time-frequency analysis methods applied to onboard sensor signals. The experiment was conducted on a 3DR Solo drone equipped with a data acquisition system. Three types of propellers were tested: intact, and those with tip chip of 1- or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2-\text{cm}$</tex> depth. Nine flight scenarios were performed, each with different combinations of intact and faulty propellers, while recording data from onboard accelerometers and gyroscopes. The collected signals were analyzed using discrete wavelet transform (DWT), empirical mode decomposition (EMD), and HilbertHuang transform (HHT) to extract features related to vibration patterns that appear at propeller faults. Simple artificial neural networks (ANNs) were employed for fault classification. The results demonstrated that DWT provided the highest detection accuracy, reaching 99.04 % for accelerometer data and 99.10 % when combining data from accelerometers and gyroscopes. These findings highlight the potential of time-frequency analysis and machine learning for UAV health monitoring, contributing to safer drone operations and reducing the risk of failures.

title: Parkinson's Disease Identification Based on Instantaneous Amplitude Features
authors: Fangyuan Zheng; Yuhong Ma; Jinye Lu; Juntao Wang
abstract: Early identification of Parkinson's disease is crucial for detecting the disease, helping doctors determine treatment plans, and thereby delaying the onset of the disease. This study analyzes and extracts specific speech signal instantaneous amplitude features based on the dysarthria of early Parkinson's disease patients. The Hilbert transform is used to process audio data, overcoming the limitations of Fourier transform and wavelet transform, allowing for the analysis of nonlinear and non-stationary feature data. SVM is applied to train and classify the extracted digital features. Results show that the average classification accuracy of digital features based on instantaneous amplitude maps using SVM learning reached 91.05%, with the highest accuracy reaching 100%. The standard deviation of 0.056 is less than 0.1, indicating that the deviation of each classification result is small, and the classifier effect of SVM is stable. It is comprehensively demonstrated that using such features and classifiers can identify early Parkinson's disease patients, effectively assisting doctors in screening and diagnosing Parkinson's disease patients.

title: A Lightweight Object Detection Model for Complex Marine Conditions Based on Improved RT-DETR
authors: Wenxuan Xu; Yihong Zhang; Baolong Ding; Bei Liu
abstract: Object detection in complex maritime environments is particularly challenging due to factors such as dynamic backgrounds, varying object appearances, and limited computational resources available for deployment. This paper focuses on developing a lightweight and real-time object detection solution for such conditions. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework named MRL-DETR (Marine Real-time Lightweight DEtection TRansformer), built upon the RT-DETR architecture.
