The proposed model introduces two key innovations: (1) the integration of MobileNetV3-small as a lightweight backbone to effectively reduce parameter count and computational cost; and (2) the incorporation of a Dilated Reparameter Block (DRBC3) into the detection head to enhance semantic feature representation and enlarge the receptive field, while maintaining high inference efficiency. The objective of this work is to achieve a balanced trade-off between detection accuracy, speed, and resource consumption, suitable for deployment in real-world maritime applications. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that MRL-DETR reduces model parameters by 60.6% and FLOPs by 73.4% compared to the baseline RT-DETR-R18 model, while maintaining competitive accuracy and significantly improving detection speed. These results validate the effective-ness and deployment potential of MRL-DETR for maritime object detection tasks.

title: An Iterative Learning Control for Nonlinear Systems without Arimoto's Assumptions
authors: Chiang-Ju Chien; Chen Liu; Xiaoe Ruan; Dong Shen
abstract: The iterative learning control problem for nonlinear systems without the requirements of Arimoto's assumptions is investigated in this paper. Typical Arimoto's assumptions for iterative learning control require that initial state error, system parameters, desired trajectory, external disturbance, and trial length are all iteration-invariant. When the assumptions are not satisfied, we call the system exists iteration-varying uncertainties. In general, it is a big challenge to design an iterative learning controller for systems with all the iteration-varying uncertainties. In this paper, we transform the iteration-varying uncertainties into an additive-type uncertainty and modify the traditional adaptive law so that a novel adaptive iterative learning controller can be applied to successfully solve the repetitive control problem. Compared with the existing works dealing with a similar issue of iteration-varying uncertainties, this proposed approach can be applied to the more general class of iteration-varying uncertain nonlinear systems and achieve better learning performance.

title: Impact of Unmanned Aircraft Regulations on Autonomous Navigation Approaches for Indoor Multi-Rotor Applications — Survey
authors: Yong Kiat Tay; Henrik Hesse
abstract: Demand in unmanned aircraft (UA) technologies for real-world applications have increased over the recent years, driving national aviation authorities to implement weight dependent regulations across all UA operations. Introduction of registration for UA weighing 250g and above as well as other regulatory requirements for heavier UA systems have motivated manufacturers to consider weight as a part of design requirement. Although UA weight is not a major concern for most outdoor applications, weight requirements imposed by aviation authorities further emphasizes the importance to develop smaller and lighter UA for safer indoor or urban operations in GPS denied environments. Comparison across various sensors used for autonomous UA navigation methods suggested that benefits of using vision sensors outweighs other methods since most UA are equipped with onboard cameras and thus does not require retrofitting of additional hardware. In addition, vision sensor data can potentially be used for both navigation and non-navigation tasks resulting in a productive and lightweight UA system that is able to avoid or reduce regulatory burdens for GPS denied UA operations.

title: Extending Guiding Vector Field to track unbounded UAV paths
authors: Mael Feurgard; Gautier Hattenberger; Simon Lacroix
abstract: A recent advance in vector field path following is the introduction of the Parametric Guiding Vector Field method. It allows for singularity-free vector fields with strong convergence guarantees, usable even for self-intersecting paths. However, the method requires significant gain tuning for practical use. In particular, for unbounded paths, the gains will inevitably become ill-suited for efficient path following. We propose a method to overcome this issue by introducing a dynamic step adaptation strategy, which provides additional normalization properties to the field. This allows the following of unbounded curves and reduces the number of gains to tune. The proposed improvements are verified in simulations using the PaparazziUAV software.

title: A Satellite Safety Logic Control System and its Safety State Precise Transition Control Method
authors: Shixiang Qiao; Haojie Li; Hang Yu; Lingyun Zhang; Chuanhao Zhang
abstract: With the rapid development of space technology, the role of satellites in space operations is becoming increasingly important. Due to the complex conditions of the space environment, the utilizable environmental features are still ambiguous, so it is necessary to design the satellite safety logic control system. In this study, starting from the analysis of environmental information characteristics, we firstly select the available space environment information characteristics, subsequently we design the satellite safety logic control system. On this basis, we have developed a safety state precise conversion control method, which is referential to the design of safety state conversion strategy of satellite safety system.

title: Study of a Predator-Prey Model with Holling Type IV Functional Response
authors: Jie Yu; Fuqin Sun; Yuyuan Chao
abstract: Population ecology, is an important branch in ecology. The problem of mutual restriction between populations has been the focus of research in recent years. The interaction between populations can be represented by a function called a functional response function. According to different populations, the functional response functions are also divided into many categories. This article studies a predator-prey model with Holling type IV functional response, which is more in line with actual conditions. From a biological point of view, this paper divides the population into three major groups, namely prey, susceptible predator and infected predator. The local stability analysis of the ecosystem around the steady state near the biological feasible equilibrium point was carried out, and the global stability analysis of the model was carried out by using the Lyapunov function. Finally, Matlab software was used to carry out numerical simulation of the analysis results.

title: Multi-Scale Feature Learning Network for Bearing fault Diagnosis with Information Fusion
authors: Shuyang Luo; Qi Zhou
abstract: Multi-source information fusion fault diagnosis is a key technology in the development of rotating machinery, which can ensure the safe operation of equipment and reduce operation and maintenance costs. However, all existing methods focus only on linear features, and the neglect of nonlinear features limits the development of information fusion methods. In this paper, a multi-scale information fusion neural network (MIFNN) is proposed, which can effectively solve the problem of missing nonlinear features of traditional attention mechanisms. The MIFNN can effectively extract linear and nonlinear features from multi-sensors and performs adaptive fusion. The proposed method is validated on the KAT bearing dataset. The comparison results show that the proposed method can effectively extract the nonlinear and linear features of multi-source sensors, thus improving the fault diagnosis accuracy of model.

title: Ship Remote Driving and Monitoring Platform Architecture Construction Research
authors: Chunxu Li; Jianan Luo; Jie Wen
abstract: Ship autonomous navigation is an advanced stage of ship intelligent navigation. Domestic and foreign institutions have made many efforts in the technical progress of intelligent navigation development. Before the fully autonomous navigation technology is mature, autonomous ships need to rely on remote driving and monitoring platforms to monitor and control ships. In order to achieve the progress of the ship intelligent navigation, proposed the architecture construction ideas of remote driving and monitoring platforms. The platform construction ideas are provided from the perspective of platform positioning, platform functions, overall architecture, system design and information interaction. The construction of the platform is helpful to provide development direction and experimental verification platform for domestic and foreign scientific research scholars and engineers.

title: Design and Prototyping of a Real-Time Location Tracking System for Railway Track Maintenance Personnel
authors: Wilfred Yong Kang Loy; Andrew Keong Ng; Sean Yu Haw Goh; Wallace Thoy
abstract: Accurate real-time location tracking of railway maintenance personnel is crucial for ensuring safety and operational efficiency. However, Singapore's Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) network lacks a system that provides real-time location tracking of maintenance personnel for safety purposes. This paper introduces the RailTime Tracking System (RTTS), a solution that integrates Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and LoRa technologies to address this gap. Using a zone-based tracking strategy, the RTTS employs strategically placed BLE and LoRa devices for precise location tracking in complex environments. The system includes a user-friendly web application with a customizable tracking dashboard, analytics tools, and a book-in/book-out page for efficient personnel management. Field tests confirm the system's effectiveness, demonstrating its potential to enhance safety and efficiency in railway track maintenance.

title: Real-time path planning for Autonomous Navigation Systems of Unmanned Surface Vehicles
authors: Agnieszka Lazarowska; Andrzej Żak
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The paper presents results of research on the development of collision avoidance algorithms dedicated for the application in the Autonomous Navigation Systems of Unmanned Surface Vehicles. Autonomous vehicles constitute a dynamically developing area of research. One of the main issues related to this technology is the ability to avoid collisions with obstacles. Deterministic and non-deterministic algorithms developed for the purpose of the Unmanned Surface Vehicle real-time path planning are briefly introduced and results of tests carried out in order to evaluate the proposed methods are presented.

title: Single- Frame Background Reconstruction Based on Image Semantic Propagation
authors: Yang Zhang; Peize Li; Yuan Xu; Qunxiong Zhu; Yanlin He; Mingqing Zhang
abstract: Image background recognition and reconstruction is an important research content in the field of computer vision. Instead of paying attention to all the targets in the image, this paper only focuses on the static background in the scene. Therefore, an adaptive semantic propagation method is proposed to reconstruct the complete background of static images. It executes single-connected region division and edge detection on a single frame. Experimental results demonstrate the robustness and adaptability of the method, achieving convincing performance under both simple and complex road conditions.

title: A Multi-View-Assisted Semantic Segmentation Network on LiDAR via Multi-Level Mutual Learning Knowledge Distillation
authors: Yun Zhang; Kun Qian; Yixin Fang; Tong Shi; Hai Yu
abstract: LiDAR-based semantic segmentation is crucial in many robotic perception systems. Considering the data of LIDAR has various views with diverse spatial features, more and more semantic segmentation methods have been proposed to fuse them for better segmentation accuracy. However, compared to single-view segmentation, these multi-view methods that directly fuse all features face inferior real-time performance and higher computation costs. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-view-assisted semantic segmentation network via multi-level mutual learning knowledge distillation (KD) to implement a high real-time and accurate semantic segmentation at a lower cost. The keys of the multi-level mutual learning-based KD strategy are intra-view mutual learning and inter-view mutual learning. To accelerate the computation and improve accuracy, we also introduce a two-step fusion strategy to fuse features hierarchically. Finally, we evaluated our approach on the SemanticKITTI dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method competently improves efficiency and accuracy.

title: Research on bionic foldable wing for flapping wing micro air vehicle
authors: Shengjie Xiao; Kai Hu; Yuhong Sun; Yun Wang; Bo Qin; Huichao Deng; Xuan Wu; Xilun Ding
abstract: This paper presents a bionic foldable wing that imitates the hind wing of ladybirds. Based on the folding mechanism of the hind wing of ladybirds and the theory of origami, the motion model of the bionic foldable wing is established, yield the motion law of the crease angles and the variation relationship between the panels are obtained. Bionic foldable wings utilise shape memory alloy to drive wings to fold, and embedded torsion springs to release energy to realize the function of wing unfolding. In the experiments of the vehicle equipped with foldable wings, the lift and attitude torque of bionic foldable wings are measured by the F/T sensor. The experimental results indicated that its aerodynamic performance is basically close to that of our optimized non-foldable wings. Moreover, the vehicle with foldable wings has been able to overcome gravity to achieve flight, which provides a novel concept for the research on flapping wing.

title: Constrained Controllability of Second Order Systems
authors: Klamka Jerzy
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: In the paper constrained controllability of linear, second order infinite-dimensional, continuous-time control systems is considered. Using methods and results taken directly from functional analysis necessary and sufficient conditions for approximate controllability are formulated and proved. Moreover, illustrative example is also discussed.

title: Parkinson's Disease Recognition Using Hybrid CNN-Transformer Model
authors: Al-Nahiyan Khushbu; Zhenxing Yang; Yutao Liu; Xiaobo Zhang
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurological disorder that affects the physical and mental health of millions of people. Thus, the early detection of PD is significantly essential for timely intervention. In this paper, we propose a simple yet influential deep learning framework, named a Hybrid CNN-Transformer, for the automatic recognition of PD patients using MRI scans. In particular, the model architecture integrates the merits of CNN with the Transformer for feature extraction in different feature dimensions. The Transformer in the model also captures the long-range dependences, which enables the model to handle both local and global statements effectively. Our proposed method is evaluated on the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) dataset. Based on experimental results, our model performs better with a test accuracy of 80.51 %, precision of 80.49%, recall of 79.89%, F1-score of 0.80, and AUC-ROC of 0.84 compared with traditional CNN models such as VGG16 and DenseNet121.

title: Evaluation of System Capability Based on Optimized Wavelet Neural Network
authors: Chao Zhang; Dong Li; Yunze Wang; Aiwei Zang
abstract: Aiming at the bottleneck problems such as the lack of effective evaluation methods and the difficulty in quantifying the capabilities of military information system equipment, this paper proposes a system equipment capability evaluation method based on optimized wavelet neural network. Combining the characteristics of weapons and information systems at brigade level, it constructs a four level index system, proposes a system capability verification model based on optimized wavelet neural network, and designs simulation tests, The effectiveness of the method is verified by evaluating the effectiveness of the brigade scale information system equipment system.

title: Lessons Learned from Utilizing Guided Policy Search for Human-Robot Handovers with a Collaborative Robot
authors: Alap Kshirsagar; Tair Faibish; Guy Hoffman; Armin Biess
abstract: We evaluate the performance of Guided Policy Search (GPS), a model-based reinforcement learning method, for generating the handover reaching motions of a collaborative robot arm. In a previous work, we evaluated GPS for the same task but only in a simulated environment. This paper provides a replication of the findings in simulation, along with new insights on GPS when used on a physical robot platform. First, we find that a policy learned in simulation does not transfer readily to the physical robot due to differences in model parameters and existing safety constraints on the real robot. Second, in order to successfully train a GPS model, the robot’s workspace needs to be severely reduced, owing to the joint-space limitations of the physical robot. Third, a policy trained with moving targets results in large worst-case errors even in regions spatially close to the training target locations. Our findings motivate further research towards utilizing GPS in humanrobot interaction settings, especially where safety constraints are imposed.

title: Kinematics Analysis and Trajectory Planning of Package Sorting Manipulator Based on D-H Method
authors: Wanmin Wu; Zeen Gou; Hua Su
abstract: In the process of modern industrial automation, manipulator is widely used in industrial production line. Aiming at the problem of a large amount of repetitive work such as sorting, grasping and packaging, which is common in automatic production lines, the Mitsubishi RV-4FL-D manipulator is taken as the research object, and the kinematics model is established using the standard D-H method, and the six degree of freedom manipulator is analyzed and studied. The forward and inverse kinematics analysis and trajectory planning simulation of the manipulator were carried out using the Robotics Toolbox on the MATLAB simulation software platform, and the simulation data was tested on the actual Mitsubishi manipulator. The experimental results show that the established kinematics equation is correct and feasible and the data obtained by simulation can be applied to the motion control of the actual manipulator to achieve the accurate and reliable operation.

title: Design and Implementation of a Locomotion Suspension System for a Desert Terrain UGV
authors: Thani Althani; Rufaidah Salim; Mohammed Minhas Anzil; Prashanth Subramaniam; Khuloud Almaeeni; Amit Shukla
abstract: Unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) are currently used to collect data and deliver payloads across industries. Most wheeled UGV implementations for uneven terrain are based on a combination of rocker and bogie. This paper proposes a variation of a suspension system for locomotion suitable for desert terrain. This variation is the transformation of the traditional inclined bogies parallel to the ground surface as the front of the rover, along with an additional transversal bogie as the rear of the robot. The design parameters, material selection, and fabrication process were performed to achieve the highest possible performance of the UGV in navigation on desert terrain. To test stability and obstacle climbing ability, experiments were carried out in desert terrain and concrete surfaces.

title: Manufacturing Knowledge Graph-Based Disentangled Prediction Framework and Industrial Practices
authors: Qingkai Sui; Yalin Wang; Chenliang Liu
abstract: Quality prediction assumes a pivotal role in manufacturing processes, serving as a linchpin to uphold product uniformity while mitigating the incidence of defects. However, the wealth of prior knowledge inherent in the manufacturing process is often underutilized, leading to limited predictive performance. Simultaneously, the integration of fragmented knowledge in the manufacturing industry often overlooks the ubiquitous presence of time series data, resulting in incomplete knowledge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a manufacturing knowledge graph-based disentangled prediction framework (MFKG-DP Framework). First, a comprehensive manufacturing knowledge graph construction method is proposed, which completes graph relationships through Bayesian network analysis of time series. The second part is the knowledge graph-based disentangled prediction method, which aims to design disentangled mapping matrixes according to the variable relationship provided by the knowledge graph. This facilitates the segmentation and disentanglement of hidden layer features, contributing to enhanced prediction capabilities. Furthermore, this paper incorporates the proposed disentanglement method into deep state space models, creating a disentangled deep state space model called DisSSM. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed MFKG-DP Framework and DisSSM is validated in industrial processes within manufacturing enterprises.

title: Algebraic criteria for a class of contractive symmetrical sets invariant with respect to arbitrary switching linear dynamics
authors: Octavian Pastravanu; Mihaela-Hanako Matcovschi
abstract: The paper considers the discrete- or continuous-time dynamics of arbitrary switching linear systems, for which new results are developed on set invariance testing. The invariance analysis refers to a class of contractive sets, previously studied only for a few simple cases; our developments cover the general circumstances of polyhedral sets exhibiting full “orthant-symmetry”, i.e. symmetry with respect to each of the state-space axes. We provide algebraic criteria (stated in terms of matrix equalities, constrained by some matrix norm / measure inequalities), which are necessary and sufficient for the characterization of the considered contractive sets. Simplified forms of these results are derived as sufficient conditions. The paper also comments on the connections to other works and illustrates the applicability of the theoretical points for a numerical example.

title: Cycle Time Range Determination based on Minimum Difference Method and Weighted Score Method
authors: Xiaomao Xia; Haomiao Li
abstract: This study presents two innovative methods for determining the cycle time range in industrial production lines: the Minimum Difference Method (MDM) and the Weighted Score Method (WSM). These methods are designed to enhance accuracy in establishing cycle time ranges, crucial for optimizing production efficiency. MDM focuses on minimizing the variance between upper and lower cycle time limits, facilitating better process control and predictability. WSM, on the other hand, integrates multiple parameters, including density and falling probability, to derive a more comprehensive and tailored cycle time range. The effectiveness of both methods is compared and analyzed in diverse industrial settings. Results indicate that accurate cycle time range determination is pivotal in streamlining production planning and resource allocation, significantly impacting process efficiency and cost-effectiveness. The study contributes to the field by offering a detailed comparative analysis of these methods, providing a practical framework for industries to enhance their production line efficiency.

title: Map fusion algorithm for multi-unmanned systems in GNSS-denied environment
authors: Jianlin Tang; Liangcai Ren; Shengnan Que; Jin Wang
abstract: The collaborative mapping of multiple-unmanned systems has been widely used in many fields such as national defense, digital mines, and smart cities. As a positioning device that unmanned systems rely heavily on in outdoor environments, intermittent denial of INS/GNSS will occur, which affects the positioning accuracy of unmanned systems and the accuracy of mapping. This paper proposes a multi-unmanned system map fusion algorithm based on lidar point cloud registration, which mainly includes point cloud preprocessing, point cloud coarse registration, fine registration and map fusion. At the initial moment of mapping, the noise points and outliers of the point clouds in the overlapping area are first removed by voxel filtering, ground segmentation and radius filtering; then 3D_HARRIS key points and corresponding FPFH feature descriptors are extracted for initial rough registration of sampling consistency ; Then take the coarse registration result as the initial transformation matrix, and use the voxel-based generalized iterative closest point method VGICP to perform fine registration to calculate the coordinate system transformation matrix between local maps; Fusion of local maps. The experimental results of map fusion in an outdoor GNSS-rejected environment show that the map fusion algorithm can construct a 3D point cloud map accurately and quickly.

title: Active Fault-Tolerant Thermal Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries Against Air Cooling Input Fault
authors: Chengzhi Liu; Zhengce Liu; Zi-Peng Wang; Ping Jiang; Kezhen Han
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries, known for their high energy density and long life, are the heart of modern portable mobile electronics, energy storage devices and electronic cars. However, lithium-ion batteries release a lot of heat during use, so a cooling system is needed to maintain the temperature of the battery pack at the optimal operating temperature. Therefore, once the cooling system fault, the temperature of the battery pack will continue to rise, which damages the life of the battery pack and even causes thermal runaway. Therefore, it is necessary to study the active fault-tolerant control of the cooling system of the battery pack. The heat generation and heat transfer model of battery pack is established and the state space is described. Then, in order to reduce the impact of air cooling input faults on battery temperature control, three types of fault-tolerant control strategies are adopted, namely, the traditional robust fault-tolerant control method (RFTC), the fault-estimation and compensating-based robust control method (FEC-RFTC), and the traditional fault-tolerant control method (RFTC). And a model predictive fault-tolerant control method based on fault estimation and compensation (FEC-MPFTC). Finally, through simulation verification and comparative analysis, it is proved that the FEC-MPFTC method has better smoothness and execution efficiency for air cooling input fault processing.

title: Analysis of the Effect of the Indoor Environment on L-shaped Movement of Small Size Four Rotor Drone
authors: Shota Ishii; Hideki Toda
abstract: In this paper, L-shaped movement control experiment assuming the narrow passage movement inside the building of four rotor helicopter was confirmed and the control stability was evaluated in a small size room (4× 4m, 3m height). In this experiment, a small 4-rotor drone was used and I made measurements in an L-shaped corridor, creating an environment with walls by means of partition board. To verify the problem of the orbit control with an L-shaped bend passage, an autonomous flight movement control experiment was conducted by 10 times with two different control strategies. Experimental result shows that (1) the stability of the L-shaped movement of the drone was seen the S.D. of the between trajectory of two 90 degree curves, and the overshoot fashion of the second 90 degree curves position. (2) The stability depends on the control method the PID and the proposed V<sup>2</sup> control methods. (3) In an environment with obstacles, the overshoot is larger than when there are no obstacles, and the V<sup>2</sup> control works effectively. This means that in such a case of drone flight of the L-shaped corridor in the building, the above two evaluation methods are useful, and stable flight can be achieved by reducing overshoot in corridors with walls. Our proposed the V<sup>2</sup> condition control would be more useful in these case. As a result, it is necessary to carefully select the control method of the drone according to the usage scene.

title: Model Merging with Lightweight Fine-Tuning
authors: Yan Pan; Yong Wang
abstract: Recently, model merging techniques have emerged as a solution for combining multiple models into a multi-task framework. However, merging often results in a significant drop in accuracy, necessitating fine-tuning to enhance performance. In this work, we refer to the performance of a model fine-tuned to convergence as the model potential, decided by which error basin model lies on when initialized. We identify that prior research on model merging has primarily focused on the performance of the merged model rather than its fine-tuned performance, and this oversight suggests that a better-performing merged model does not guarantee has better model potential. To address this issue, we propose a novel model merging method that facilitates better integration of knowledge from Model A and Model B, thereby enabling superior model potential. Specifically, we conceptualize the parameters of the merged model as a linear combination of those from Model A and Model B, allowing us to optimize the linear combination parameter (LCP) through training. To mitigate random fluctuations, we typically initialize the LCP at 0.5, ensuring that the initial merged model does not exhibit a preference for either Model A or Model B. Comprehensive experimental comparisons demonstrate that the features of Model A and Model B are more effectively combined with lightweight fine-tuning of the LCP.

title: Research on Double-Motor Cooperative Control of Dexterous Finger with Variable Stiffness
authors: Jianfeng Yao; Yiwei Liu; Handong Hu; Kening Gong; Yang Liu
abstract: As a kind of end effector of grasping robot, the bionic dexterous hand has been widely concerned by researchers since its birth for its high flexibility and strong adaptability to different scenes. This paper aims at a new type of adversarial flexible joint finger mechanism with variable stiffness, develops a multi-motor cooperative controller combined with Hall sensor AS5048A and brushless motor motion controller MC5004P. Aiming at the motion coordination problem of each finger joint, combined with a low-pass filter, a cross-coupling synchronous controller including synchronization error and position error feedback is designed. Finally, the experiment result demonstrates that the synchronous controller has advantageous accuracy and realizes the variety of the finger’s stiffness.

title: Autonomous Drone with a Compact and Coaxial Redundant Motor System for Disaster Relief Using Spatial AI
authors: Aron Rodrick Lakra
abstract: This paper illustrates and discusses a novel design - a ready prototype of a compact autonomous drone leveraging Spatial AI in the form of depth mapping for the aid in disaster relief, rescue and recovery. This design features a custom 3D printed compact frame comparable to a F450 in size, featuring a coaxial X8 motor configuration for motor redundancy in case of a motor failure. It presents a prototype with a compact design with additional implementation ideas and is an excerpt of a larger project, which hasn't gone through practical and empirical field testing at the moment regarding the motor redundancy.

title: Design Principle of Daily Hooks Based on the Affordance Theory - a Case Study of Daily Products
authors: Di Lu; Jun-Feng Wang; Bao-Yi Zhang; Yu Jiang
abstract: This paper aims to clarify the definition in the minds of users about “easy to use” of daily-use related products and provide guidance for the design and application of daily-use related products. First, the development and present situation of affordance theory and daily-use product design are introduced, and the development status and trends of design innovation are summarized. Then, the design characteristics of daily-use products as the main category are explored based on affordance theory. Besides, statistics and daily-use-related products are sorted out through domestic and foreign online selling channels and categorized according to the form. Afterward, the experimental scores of the subjects’ selection of physical linkages are quantitatively conducted. A product design principle of daily-use related products based on affordance is proposed. The results laid a foundation for the design of other product categories with experimental methods.

title: A Novel Scheme for Controlling Intelligent Television by Using Intelligent Camera
authors: Zhaoxiong Zhou
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: Although the home intelligent camera contains many functions, its application scenarios are still very limited. Based on the widely used big data analysis method and the face recognition function of intelligent camera, this paper designs a novel scheme of using intelligent camera to control intelligent television. The scheme combines intelligent camera, intelligent television, cloud platform and mobile App. The face recognition function of the intelligent camera recognizes people watching intelligent television, and reports to the mobile App remotely through the cloud platform; users can set the duration and period of watching intelligent television through the mobile App, and can also talk with the intelligent camera through the mobile App or send a language prompt message through the mobile App. In addition, the cloud platform can use big data analysis technology to recommend the best intelligent television playback time and duration to the mobile App, so that children can learn and entertain at the same time. The experimental results also show that the scheme has the conditions for popularization. This scheme can effectively realize the control of the intelligent camera on the intelligent television.

title: LLM-Based Task Planning for Mobile Robots Using a Novel SLAM Method for Materials Distribution
authors: Aphilak Lonklang; Pedro Alejandro Cordero Jara; Haichen Xu; Wentao Zhang; Natabara Máté Gyöngyössy; János Botzheim
abstract: This paper presents a novel autonomous mobile robot system for material distribution, integrating dynamic map generation, natural language processing (NLP), and efficient path-planning for real-world factory applications. The system begins with a top-view image capture of the environment using a fisheye-lens camera, followed by image correction and color-based object detection to identify stations and generate an occupancy map for navigation, eliminating the need for traditional SLAM techniques. User interaction is facilitated through an NLP module connected to a large language model (LLM) trained on predefined assembly manuals, enabling the robot to interpret requests and determine the required materials for specific assembly tasks. The global path-planning is managed by the Improved RRT* with Reduced Random Map Size (IRRT*-RRMS) algorithm, ensuring optimal and efficient motion in dynamic environments. Experimental validation using a TurtleBot3 Waffle Pi equipped with an OpenManipulator-X demonstrates the system's effectiveness, particularly in handling assembly model H, which includes bolts, nuts, and screws.

title: Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance in Cobots with Multiple Random Moving Obstacles
authors: Laasya Kodandaramu; Maalavika Srikantan; Jacob V Sanoj; Kaushik Narayan; Shikha Tripathi
abstract: Traditional industrial robots are generally massive, heavy, and dangerous and are therefore generally isolated from humans. Collaborative robots or COBOTs are designed to collaborate and work with humans in a shared workspace. These are typically smaller and lighter than traditional industrial robots and are therefore more flexible and easier to deploy in a variety of settings. One of the most crucial problems that need to be addressed for cobots is Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance as they will be working in an environment where there will be constant human movement. This paper presents an efficient solution to this problem employing a Non-Linear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC) for realtime path planning. It has been used to obtain the most optimum trajectory while avoiding dynamic obstacles. The KINOVA Gen3 manipulator has been simulated with static and dynamic obstacle modelling. The NMPC controls the arm to minimize differences between the system's current state and the desired goal position while avoiding obstacles. A detailed visualization of the system motion has also been included. The work has been tested and the results have been shown for 4 different cases - reference case with no obstacles, case 1 with three obstacles, case 2 with four obstacles and case 3 with a simulated human-like obstacle to mimic a typical cobot scenario. Detailed error analysis including end-effector and implementation errors has also been shown for each of the 4 cases and is promising.

title: Development of an Autonomous Navigation System Using Google Maps API for a Package Delivery Device
authors: Yuliarman Saragih; Resi Sujiwo Bijokangko; Agatha Elisabet Saragih; Carolan Ignatius Saragih; Tiarmin Saragih; Bahterayudha
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Control & [::Automation::]; Electronics; [::Robotics::]; Internet of Things; and Artificial Intelligence (CERIA)
abstract: This research explores the development of an autonomous navigation system for package delivery devices, utilizing the Google Maps API as the core navigation framework. As the demand for efficient logistics grows, the integration of advanced autonomous technologies can enhance operational effectiveness, reduce reliance on human labor, and optimize delivery times. The autonomous robot car, designed with specific operational specifications, operates at a frequency of 0.75Hz, allowing it to query the Google Maps API every 1.5 seconds for route updates. The system processes GPS data and communicates with the Google Directions API to determine optimal routes, incorporating essential parameters such as origin, destination, and travel mode. By analyzing real-time data, the robot can adjust its path, avoid obstacles, and ensure safe navigation. This innovative approach demonstrates significant potential to improve delivery accuracy and customer satisfaction through enhanced route management and operational efficiency.

title: Pure State Control Theory for Non-Ideal Quantum Systems
authors: Shuang Cong; Fangfang Meng
abstract: A quantum control theory of pure state in non-ideal quantum systems is proposed in this paper. A non-ideal closed quantum systems means that the controlled quantum system is in two degenerate cases: one is at least two transition frequencies between different energy levels are the same, or/and another is at least two eigenstates of the internal Hamiltonian are not directly coupled. The implicit Lyapunov control method based on the average value of an imaginary mechanical quantity is used to design the control laws. The design procedure of the imaginary mechanical quantity is derived. The relationships among the implicit Lyapunov control methods based on the state distance, the state error and the average value of an imaginary mechanical quantity are analyzed. Finally, some numerical simulation experiments are studied.

title: Acquisition and Processing of PCG Signals Originating from the Heart
authors: Gabriel Oncea; Ovidiu Buza
abstract: This paper presents a system for the acquisition and processing of phonocardiogram (PCG) signals. The aim was to develop a system with the following facilities: automatic control of input signal amplitude, signal filtering, digital processing for heart beat rate (HBR) detection, and storage of signal samples for further automatic classification and pathology identification.

title: Design of a Vehicle-level Test System for In-vehicle Emergency Call System
authors: Yuxuan Yang; Zhijing Xu
abstract: The in-vehicle emergency call system has the ability to decrease the waiting time for assistance following a car crash, resulting in a decreased fatality rate for road accidents. According to domestic and international regulations, it is necessary for the system to undergo comprehensive testing to ensure its reliability prior to being utilized in vehicles. The whole vehicle triggering characteristics serve as the final evaluation in the certification process, requiring strict testing and verification to guarantee the technology's maturity and dependability. This paper presents a vehicle-level test system designed to meet vehicle-level test requirements. The system was tested from four perspectives, including in-vehicle system (IVS) triggering characteristics, minimum set of data (MSD) correctness, positioning accuracy, and voice call quality. The experimental results indicate that the testing system effectively tests the whole vehicle triggering characteristics of the in-vehicle emergency call system, thereby confirming its efficacy. The testing system can offer a budget-friendly and productive emergency call (eCall) certification testing solution to automobile companies. Additionally, it can provide substantial technical and data support for the creation of mandatory standards in China. Consequently, it promotes the expansion of related domains in China.

title: Locating Screw Grooves in Non-Visual Environments Based on Force Feedback Control
authors: Jia Quan Liu; Zhi Feng Zhou; Hong Wei Ren
abstract: To address the challenge of quickly and accurately locating screw grooves in visionless environments using a robotic arm, this paper proposes a low-cost improved scanning-based search method. The method eliminates the influence of force sensor bias and load to obtain precise environmental force data. Subsequently, Fourier Transform is employed to convert time-domain signals into the frequency domain, identifying and recording specific frequency changes corresponding to contact with the screw groove. The torque variation signals generated when the screwdriver contacts the groove are primarily determined by the physical characteristics of the groove, such as its depth and width. This specific frequency can be used as a reference standard to rapidly locate grooves of screws with identical specifications. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed scanning-based search method, repeated simulations were conducted. The simulation results demonstrate that once the dominant frequency is stabilized through multiple scans, it is no longer necessary to make incremental adjustments or validations, enabling rapid detection and precise localization by directly utilizing the dominant frequency.

title: A Quantum Annealing Approach to Target Tracking
authors: Michel Barbeau; Farrokh Janabi-Sharifi; Houman Masnavi
abstract: This paper delves into the fusion of quantum computing and robotics, focusing on motion planning in cluttered environments. Traditional algorithms struggle with complex problems where many constraints need to be satisfied. Hence, optimization-based approaches such as Constrained Quadratic Models (CQM) have become increasingly popular. Our work presents a 3D tracking algorithm based on CQM uniquely adapted for quantum computers to address computational challenges. With their parallel processing capabilities, Quantum computers offer a groundbreaking approach to optimizing complex problems. We formulate the CQM problem for efficient resolution on the D-Wave quantum computer, showcasing its superiority over classical counterparts. Our application centers on real-time planning in a target-chaser tracking scenario, highlighting the quantum advantage in handling the computation complexity of constrained problems. This paper bridges the quantum-robotics gap and sets the stage for future research in quantum-enhanced robotic motion planning.

title: New approach to functional safety work products for advanced automotive projects
authors: Piotr Mydlowski; Szczepan Moskwa
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The dynamically developing automotive industry poses increasing challenges to manufacturers due to the increasing complexity of electronic systems used in cars and high safety requirements. The ISO 26262 standard gives guidelines for project management in the field of functional safety. It included lists of work products, which usually prepare fundamental documents in the field of functional safety, such as development interface agreement or functional safety plan, etc.. The degree of implementation of the mentioned work products helps in the arguments about the ultimate safety of the product. ISO 26262 is a standard aimed at the possibility of its wide application (also for the simplest products), unfortunately for highly complex products such as integrated safety systems, such high-level work products can be too general without contributing key information at the start of the project. The article presents a list of additional, more precise work products dedicated specifically to highly advanced safety systems in automotive projects. It can be used at the request for quote stage when building documentation for functional safety. In addition, the list of work products listed and introduced to the additional process helps to determine the scope of responsibilities in the organization at the beginning of the project. Especially where the issues of functional safety and safety of the intended functionality are presented. This helps to avoid the risk of security liability gaps with potentially fatal consequences for the end-user.

title: Observer-Based Controller of Two-Dimensional Large-Scale Polynomial Fuzzy Systems*
authors: Lizhen Li
abstract: This study focuses on the observer-based feedback controller design of two-dimensional(2-D) discrete large-scale polynomial fuzzy systems. Firstly, a two-dimensional large-scale fuzzy system is established, with the 2-D polynomial Roesser model as the local model, including unknown interconnection terms. The separation property is established under the 2-D large-scale fuzzy framework. By this way, the fuzzy controller and the fuzzy observer can be individually solved and the corresponding closed-loop 2-D polynomial fuzzy system is asymptotically stable. The developed design algorithms are convex SOS conditions, which can be directly solved by the SOSTOOLS. Finally, a numerical example is shown to demon-strated the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: An Intelligent Video Surveillance Recognition and Warning Method for Tornadoes
authors: Ping Wang; Jingjing Ma; Xuemei Zhu
abstract: A method for tornado formation recognition and early warning was introduced based on video surveillance. The video surveillance image is preprocessed, and then the GMM model is used to extract the background image 5 minutes ago. The static scene is used as the background, and the moving object is extracted by background subtraction. The foreground and background in the image are extracted to separate the region of interest (tornado target) from the background area in the image. Then the moving image is binarized and the pixel statistics are performed. Since the tornado has a shape feature of being large at the top and small at the bottom, this feature can be used to perform template matching and identification on the moving object. Therefore, the foreground 0-value pixel statistics are performed row by row from top to bottom on the foreground image. If the number of pixels in the upper part of the foreground image is greater than 1.5 times the number of pixels in the lower part, it is determined to be a suspected tornado image. Finally, after the monitoring personnel make a judgment and confirmation, a tornado warning is issued to the people in the affected area to reduce the loss of life and property.

title: Research on Localization Algorithms for Mobile Robots Based on Laser and Inertial Navigation Fusion
authors: Zhao Liang; Zhou Shenghao; Shi Weiguang
abstract: This paper primarily investigates localization algorithms for mobile robots based on laser reflectors. It proposes an ICP (Iterative Closest Point) laser odometry method based on sparse point clouds from reflectors, which provides motion updates for the particle set. Continuous localization of the mobile robot is achieved through particle filtering. Experimental comparisons indicate that this localization algorithm has high positioning accuracy and strong robustness against abnormal interference.

title: Research and Application of Tablet Backplane Detection Algorithm Based on Machine Vision
authors: Xin Huang; Yuqiang Wang; Yuezhong Li; Xianen Zhou
abstract: The detection of tablet backplane accessories is one of the important links in whether the tablet computer can be qualified to enter the market. The traditional inspection link usually uses artificial visual inspection, which has problems such as low efficiency and error rate increasing with workers' working time. Therefore, this paper proposes a system based on machine vision and industrial control computer, which studies and applies the vision algorithms. The system acquires pictures by a specific camera, perform two extraction of template area center points on the tablet backplane on the pipeline and the affine transformation to get the accurate location. The film detection algorithm is used for the film in the system. The nut adopts the nut detection algorithm. Foam uses statistical methods based on describing textures. After verification in 300 samples provided by the factory, the results show that the average detection time is 49.37 milliseconds, and the accuracy rate is 97%.

title: Direct Thrust Control of Aeroengines Based on Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
authors: Zhen Yu; Kaimin Huang; Xinxin Zhu; Jiawei Su; Rongrong Qian; Lijun Liu
abstract: Aeroengines are complex, strongly nonlinear, multi-variable, and time-varying objects. With the change of working state and flight conditions, the range of engine changes is large. Taking aeroengines as the research object, this paper studies the direct thrust control of aeroengines based on nonlinear model prediction method, so as to improve the engine performance under the thrust control system. The basic idea is to construct the input and output data set, based on the polynomial state space mathematical model structure, and use the method of system identification to construct a specific mathematical model, and use the nonlinear model predictive control method to design the optimization target for direct thrust. function and solve it to achieve the control objective of the direct thrust of the aeroengines. Finally, the experimental results show that the proposed aeroengines direct thrust control strategy based on nonlinear model prediction can better control the direct thrust of aeroengines within the safety limit.

title: An Adaptive Collision Avoidance Decision Method for Various Driving Conditions
authors: Juqi Hu; Caini Wang; Hejia Gao
abstract: With the continuous advancement of autonomous driving technology, enabling the vehicles to avoid obstacles has gained increasing attention. However, traditional obstacle avoidance strategies have certain limitations as they often focus solely on nearby obstacles. In light of this, this paper proposes a more comprehensive collision avoidance approach. Suitable obstacle avoidance modes are firstly designed for various driving scenarios. The optimal collision avoidance mode is subsequently determined based on the actual distance to the obstacles. Effective obstacle avoidance for autonomous vehicles is finally achieved through the coordinated steering and braking control systems. To validate the feasibility of the proposed strategy, joint simulations using Carsim and MATLAB/Simulink have been conducted with consideration of two scenarios with different driving conditions. Experimental tests were further carried out using Quanser's latest autonomous vehicle-QCar platform. Both the simulation and the experimental results have verified the successful implementation of the obstacle avoidance approach under various driving conditions.

title: Design and Research of a New Quadruped Mechanical Single-leg Prototype
authors: Yuhai Zhong; Huashan Feng; Weiwei Yu; Hongbo Wang; Jingze Gao; Runxiao Wang
abstract: As an important and basic component of a quadruped robot interacting with the external environment, the mechanical leg determines the core application performance of a robot such as walking speed, load capacity, and operational adaptability. Therefore, research on mechanical leg has important practical value and theoretical significance. This paper develops a new quadruped mechanical single-leg prototype, which has a novel knee motor arrangement and transmission mechanism. The novel transmission mechanism consists of a bevel gear train, a ball screw mechanism and a four-bar linkage. To be better promoted and used, the transmission mechanism is modeled and analyzed, and the influence of several important parameters of the mechanism on the torque and speed of motor is studied. Finally, the mechanical properties of the bearing structures are analyzed, and the results show that the structural strength can meet the design requirements.

title: An Efficient Software Framework for Synchronizing RGB and Depth Cameras for Robotic Applications
authors: Aayush Shah; Meet Gandhi; Sunil Kumar; Sagar Dhatrak; Amit Gupta; Mohammad Imran
abstract: Synchronizing RGB and ToF depth cameras is a critical challenge in RGB-D imaging systems due to differences in timestamps, exposure times and frame rates, leading to misaligned data and artifacts in 3D object reconstruction, which can impact various robotics applications. This paper proposes a novel software-based synchronization framework for time synchronization of RGB and depth camera streams by coordinating frame capture processes and managing timing disparities, eliminating the need for costly hardware solutions. A comparative analysis conducted on collected datasets demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves sub microsecond-level synchronization, ensuring accurate, artifact-free 3D reconstruction with consistent frame rates. The results confirm the efficiency of the proposed software framework, demonstrating its capability to achieve precise synchronization in RGB-D imaging systems.

title: WiBot 1.0: A Modular Reconfigurable Glass Cleaning Robot for High-rise Buildings
authors: S. A. Kariyawasam; G. H. Sandeepa; M. K. A. Pathirana; Y. W. R. Amarasinghe; A. G. B. P. Jayasekara; H. A. G. C. Premachandra; U-Xuan Tan
abstract: Cleaning glass surfaces is a prevailing maintenance problem in high-rise buildings. In the traditional methods of cleaning windows, hanging on ropes poses significant occupational hazards to workers. Furthermore, most glass facades feature window frames to securely fasten the glass panels to the building structure, ensuring durability and elegance. In this context, existing robotic cleaning methods are limited by their capability to move-over window frames and need more flexibility to access tight corners and curved surfaces. This paper presents a novel reconfigurable glass cleaning robot called "WiBot" to address these limitations. WiBot is a kinematic chain comprising modular linkages with a prismatic joint and two revolute joints at each end. Each revolute joint has a suction unit that enables locomotion and adhesion. Window frames are detected using image processing with an onboard camera, and design optimizations were performed to improve the robot’s capabilities. The prototype WiBot 1.0 was developed, and several experiments were conducted to evaluate the feasibility of the proposed system focusing on robot motion, window frame detection and move-over mechanism. The results show that WiBot can overcome the limitations of existing window cleaning solutions. Finally, several promising research directions are mentioned involving the proposed reconfigurable robot architecture in cleaning operations.

title: One-Handed Gesture Recognition Based on Improved ST-GCN and CA Attention Mechanism
authors: Guixin Wang
abstract: The article takes one-handed gesture video as the research object, and mainly focuses on the recognition process and method of “isolated words” and static gesture mixtures. Firstly, the algorithm of extracting the key point positions of frame pictures is proposed by grouping rules of frame sequences of different gestures. This algorithm solves the problem of invalid gesture images affecting the recognition due to the redundancy of gesture images when extracting gestures from traditional gesture videos. Finally, a new network (ST-GCN-CA) is proposed, which improves the traditional spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (ST-GCN) and adds the CA attention mechanism. The method and network in this paper are applied to the Chinese isolated word sign language dataset (CSL-500) single-handed video, and the experimental results show that the recognition accuracies in the isolated word gesture video and the hybrid video reach 94.3% and 94.1%, respectively, which improves the recognition accuracies in comparison with other methods in the public domain.

title: Students' Attitudes Towards the AI-Based Automated Essay Scoring System: An Influencing Mechanism from Perceived Interactivity to Criticism
authors: Ying Zhang; Yuna Yao; Shu-Jing Wu
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has penetrated our lives by way of web search engines and mobile applications. AI-based Automated Essay Scoring (AES) is playing an increasingly important role in the field of education. This study explored the relationship between students' perceived interactivity of AES and their individual innovativeness as well as their reflective thinking about AES, and how these variables influence their criticism of AES. This study employed Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) for the data analysis. Valid data were collected from 442 students (40.05% male, 59.95% female, average age= 19.7) who had experience of AVE in private universities in China. The findings showed that: (a) Students' perceived interactivity of AES positively affected their individual innovativeness and reflective thinking about AES; (b) Students' individual innovativeness of AES positively affected their reflective thinking and criticism of AES; and (c) Students' perceived interactivity and reflective thinking about AES did not positively affect their criticism of AES. The findings not only revealed students' attitudes towards and experiences of this technological tool, but also provide valuable support for enhancing teaching effectiveness and improving teaching methods.

title: Verification of Inrush currents from electromagnetic transients influencing the stability of voltage in Smart Microgrids connected to systems with electric vehicles
authors: Vicente Tiburcio dos Santos Junior
abstract: In this research the instability of voltage in microgrid is still the focus of study and determination. Specifically, First-Swing Instability is experienced in the system in noted changes with characteristics of making the system unstable or returning to a state of stability. The latter calls itself as a phenomenon of re-synchronization. Oblivious to system instability aspects, it is believed that when connecting fast electric vehicle chargers to the electricity distribution system coming from microgrids, they increase basic electrical loads and reduce the stability of the power system. Transitional currents have the characteristic of severely impacting microgrids not prepared in connected or islanded states. The influences of electromagnetic incompatibility of the inrush current, due to their condition of unpredictability and intermittent, have complex identification studies. With increasing electricity demand for electric vehicle chargers, concerns about the effects of network integration increase proportionally. This article emphasizes the influence of initialization of fast chargers on the power variation related to the re-synchronization phenomenon and its mitigating to the stability of microgrid.

title: Object Localization Based on a Single RGB Camera for a 4-DOF Robotic Arm
authors: Elvira Chebotareva; Adel Mukhamedshin; Niyaz Imamov; Evgeni Magid
abstract: This study presents a method for constructing metric depth maps based on relative depth maps for a 4-DOF manipulator with a single RGB camera, which is attached to an end effector. To create a relative depth map of a scene, we utilize the Depth Anything V2 model along with a system of twelve ArUco markers positioned at varying distances from one another. Unlike traditional methods for determining distances to objects using ArUco markers, the proposed approach does not require a continuous presence of markers within a camera's field of view; it only necessitates measuring a distance to a few markers in an initial frame. The proposed method enables the robot to perform object localization using a relative depth map concurrently with an object search process.

title: Railway Track Joints and Fasteners Fault Detection using Principal Component Analysis
authors: Muhammad Owais; Imtiaz Hussain; Gul Shahzad; Bilal Muhammad Khan
abstract: This works presents a machine learning based fault detection algorithm specifically for condition monitoring of different types of railway tracks. The algorithm relies on one of the most commonly used machine learning algorithms, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), for extracting the patterns of various defected and nondefected railway track components including rail fasteners and joints like fishplate. The algorithm ensures a very fast yet robust feature extraction workflow primarily by virtue of its inherently offered dimensionality reduction resulting in lesser computational burden. The classification task is handled by the Euclidean distance classifier that identifies the nearest neighbor of the test image in the subspace spanned by the most dominant eigenvectors extracted from the training dataset during feature extraction workflow. Two varying railway track datasets, from Bangladesh and Pakistan, have been used in this work to validate the proposed algorithm using standard training to test ratios. Multiple classification scenarios are presented and analyzed in detail for both datasets with supporting results. MATLAB_R2022a has been used for development of the proposed algorithms that offers an overall efficiency of more than ninety percent under varying scenarios.

title: Research on Application of Stewart Platform in Uniform Scanning
authors: Fengchao Liang; Shuang Tan; Jiankai Fan; Ai Zhang; Zhe Lin; Zhicheng Shi
abstract: The space spectral imaging camera is planned to use a Stewart 6-DOF platform to drive a mirror for scanning and imaging, which requires the accuracy of the platform to reach the order of arcsec under the condition of multi-struts dynamic coupling. A Stewart platform realizes high angle resolution mainly by designing high-resolution linear driving struts. The resolution index of the 6-DOF Stewart platform is 2”, which needs the struts to achieve a high resolution of 60 nm. Based on this requirement, a driving strut with 50 nm resolution based on BLDC motor, ball screw, grating ruler is designed, which effectively ensures the high resolution of the platform. The transfer function of the single drive strut is identified by time domain method, and the closed-loop control model of the single drive strut is established. The dynamic performance of the single drive strut is simulated and analyzed. Finally, the dynamic performance of the 6-DOF scanning platform is experimentally studied. The experimental results show that the angular resolution of the 6-DOF Stewart platform is 2”, the swing angle range of the constant speed scanning is −1~1 degree, the nonlinear error of scanning angle in place curve is less than 0.2%, and the rotational speed is adjustable from 40”/s to 1800 ”/s, all the indicators meet the design index. This research has laid a solid foundation for the aerospace application of Stewart Parallel Platform.

title: Design of a Flexure XY Micropositioning Stage With Large Hollow Platform
authors: Hanlun Zhang; Zehao Wu; Qingsong Xu
publication_title: 2020 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a new flexure-based XY micropositioning stage with a large hollow platform, which is suitable for practical use with a microscope. The designed mechanism has a parallel-kinematic structure and is actuated by two voice coil motors. By employing multistage compound parallelogram flexures (MCPF), the stage is designed as a four-layer structure, which produces a motion output platform with a large hollow space and large motion range. Analytical modeling is carried out for the parametric design of the stage. Evaluation results show that the designed XY stage exhibits a large safety factor and high natural frequency. Moreover, the large hollow platform is well-suited for practical application with a microscope.

title: Angular Motion Compensation Scheme for Dual-Axis Rotational Inertial Navigation System
authors: Usung Park; Minsu Jo; Chanju Park
abstract: To improve navigation performance, rotating inertial navigation system(RINS), a navigation system that rotates the inertial measurement unit(IMU) to compensate errors in the inertial sensors, has been the subject of several studies aimed at optimizing the rotation method and period for enhancing the compensation effect. The rotational motion occurring during maneuver affects not only the attitude stabilization of the IMU but also the performance of rotating modulation. Therefore, this paper proposes a rotation scheme applicable to the gimbal that stabilizes a vehicle's roll motion and compares the compensation performance with a conventional rotation scheme based on simulation results.

title: ACL-YOLO: A Novel Real-Time Network for UAV-Based Infrared Object Detection
authors: Fei Gao; Haiqin Xu; Yihong Zhang; Ling Cheng
abstract: With the widespread adoption of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technologies in disaster rescue, agricultural monitoring, and border patrol, the demand for onboard infrared camera-based small object detection has been growing rapidly. However, UAV-captured images present inherent challenges, including small object sizes (e.g., pedestrians and vehicles often spanning merely tens of pixels), complex backgrounds prone to thermal noise interference, and computational constraints of embedded systems. These factors collectively lead traditional detection algorithms to face critical limitations such as excessive model parameters, loss of small object features, and insufficient real-time performance. This study introduces ACL-YOLO, an optimized detection architecture derived from YOLOv11. Unlike the existing YOLOv11n, our approach introduces ADown module in the backbone, which enhances feature extraction while reducing computational costs. Additionally, we integrate the feature fusion CCFF structure module into the neck network and incorporate a small-object attention mechanism (LSKA). Benchmark evaluations using the HIT-UAV thermal infrared imagery dataset demonstrate that ACL-YOLO reduces the number of parameters by 44.23% and the computational complexity (GFLOPs) by 33.33%, while improving mean Average Precision (mAP) by 2.1% compared to YOLOv11n. This work provides an effective approach for real-time small object detection in UAV-based infrared imagery applications.

title: Monocular Multi-Perspective 3D Reconstruction for Robotic Ultrasonic Testing in Remanufacturing
authors: Zezhong Wang
abstract: Inspection is one of the main processes of remanufacturing. As an important inspection method, contact ultrasonic testing (UT) needs surface scanning on the objects. The transducer should contact and be vertical to the surface. When implementing UT using a robotic arm, path planning on a complex surface is challenging as the parts are deformed from the original CAD model. Computer vision can be used to reconstruct the object surface to plan paths for the surface scanning application. However, the accuracy of reconstruction using structure from motion (SfM) is still critical. The features of images and feature matching directly affect the reliability of the reconstruction of the model. In this study, a method of object reconstruction is established for robotic UT. Only one monocular camera is installed on the end effector of the robotic arm to acquire images from multiple views. After the image acquisition, an improved segmentation method is used to separate the object from the background. This helps to decrease mismatches of feature points and irrelevant feature points. The features are searched in the region of interest using an improved descriptor to increase the number of features in the object area. Subsequently, the poses and positions of the camera are computed using SfM. The 3D model is reconstructed according to the pose information and feature points. The proposed method outperforms the traditional method and also reduces the reconstruction time.

title: Observer-based Practical Predefined-time Distributed Formation Control for AUVs
authors: Yunkang Sun; Yuquan Chen; Yu Zhang; Ashaduzzaman Md Nur
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed practical predefined-time formation control scheme for multi-AUV system in the presence of external disturbances. Firstly, a novel predefined-time sliding mode disturbance observer (PTSDO) is constructed , with which the external disturbances can be precisely estimated. On this basis, the predefined-time control theory and backstepping technique are integrated to guarantee the practical predefined-time convergence of the formation states. Furthermore, a novel predefined-time command filter is designed to cope with the repeated derivation calculation explosion problem. Finally, the effectiveness and rationality of the proposed formation control scheme are validated by numerous simulations.

title: Tracking Control for the Geomagnetic Field Chaotic Model
authors: Pengyu Hou; Xiaoshan Zhao; Yongfeng Guo; Tao Xu; Ya Lu; Xiang Li
abstract: Based on the dynamic system stability theory, the dynamic behavior of geomagnetic field chaotic model is studied. The process of chaos generation can be better revealed by the change of parameter H. On this basis, a suitable controller is designed in this paper, and the tracking control is applied to realize the tracking of geomagnetic field chaotic model to any reference signal, and the numerical simulation shows that the method can quickly and effectively control the geomagnetic field chaotic model.

title: Optimization-Based Trajectory Planning for Multiple Robots in Unstructured Environments
authors: Lixiang Zheng; Gang Zhang; Zhangduan Chai; Jie Niu; Chengran Lin
abstract: This work focuses on a trajectory planning problem for multiple ground mobile robots in unstructured environments. Considering the problem, we propose a safety-enhancing multi-robot trajectory planning method. Our proposed method uses a two-stage strategy, path planning and trajectory optimization, to solve the multi-robot trajectory planning problem. To re-duce computational burden of the trajectory optimization, we construct safe corridor for each robot. In the safe corridor construction, we introduce an extended distance to solve its invalid construction problem. In a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90\mathrm{m}\times 90\mathrm{m}$</tex> experiment sce-nario, our method saves almost 91 % safe corridor construction time. Moreover, to enhance safety of the trajectory that the proposed method generates, a distance penalty term is added to the objective function of trajectory optimization problems. Compared to a state-of-the-art method, the proposed method outperforms it. Simulations and real-world experiments validate the feasibility of the proposed method.

title: VOIS+: A Video Over Intercom Service with Home Automation Features for Advanced Security and Safety
authors: Angkon Deb; Asif Islam; Arnab Nath; Mayesha Haque; Rudra Roy; Md. Jawad Ul Islam; Celia Shahnaz
abstract: The advent of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the Web of Things (WoT) has greatly influenced the development of smart home systems, providing enhanced convenience, security, and automation. This paper introduces a novel solution that integrates video intercom systems with smart home automation features, addressing communication and safety concerns. In addition to traditional intercom capabilities, the proposed system incorporates fire hazard detection and electrical safety controls, automating household safety measures. A mobile and web-based interface allows remote monitoring and control, including smart door lock management, face recognition, and emergency contact alerts. Developed with affordability and accessibility in mind, the system—termed VOIS+, offers a comprehensive approach to home automation and safety, achieving high performance across multiple test scenarios, including face recognition accuracy and rapid emergency response times. This paper presents both the hardware architecture and software framework, demonstrating the system’s potential to revolutionize smart home technology by merging security, automation, and artificial intelligence into a single, efficient platform.

title: Design Method of Mode Transition Control Law for TBCC Engine
authors: Yongliang Zhang; Lingcong Nie; Bingqiang Yu; Feng Lu; Jinquan Huang
abstract: In this paper, a mathematical model of tandem turbine-based combined cycle (TBCC) engine is studied based on the component-level concept, and then the mode transition is focused on with the controller design. The aerodynamic thermodynamic equations are drawn out in the establishment of engine component-level model, and Newton-Raphson method is applied to solve the common operation equations. In addition, the modal transition process is simulated and analyzed, the mode transition operating point of the TBCC engine is determined in the flight trajectory. Thus, the combined engine modal transition control quantity adjustment plan is formulated. Finally, a multi-variable controller based on neural network estimation and inverse control is designed and verified in the TBCC simulation.

title: Experimental Validation of Collision Safety in Prismatic Joints Using Magnetic Coupling
authors: HyoJae Kang; Min-Sung Kang
abstract: This study presents a prismatic joint structure that utilizes magnetic coupling to enhance safety during collisions. Conventional prismatic joints using electric motors typically involve components such as gearboxes and rigid couplings. In contrast, the proposed design features permanent magnets arranged on the motor output shaft and the gearbox input shaft, enabling non-contact power transfer through an axial magnetic coupling mechanism. The proposed design prevents overload by utilizing the decoupling of the magnetic coupling in the event of a collision. This results in improved safety of mechanical components during impact situations compared to conventional designs. Prior to experimentation, magnetic film was employed to verify the magnet arrangement, and the transmitted torque via the distance between magnet array was experimentally determined. The experiment compared the motor speed, q-axis current, and the load applied to the impact surface during the collision process, based on the presence or absence of magnetic coupling. Experimental findings confirmed the proposed effect provided by the magnetic coupling.

title: Research on Virtual Subsystem Architecture of Intelligent Data Platform
authors: Lu Gao; MingChuan Yang; Bing Qian
abstract: This paper introduces the current development of distributed machine learning, federated learning and big data platform, then proposes a virtual subsystem architecture of intelligent data platform based on algorithm model, data model, resource model and security model. At the same time, the technical details of resource model scheduling, the definition of security model, the construction principle of virtual subsystem are stated. In addition, this paper also introduces the practical application of the architecture from two aspects: subsystem construction and data processing flow.

title: Enhancing Motivational Driver Model Using Model Predictive Control for Autonomous Decision-Making
authors: Niayesh Zamani; Saeed Mozaffari; Shahpour Alirezaee; Bruce Minaker
abstract: This study investigates the integration of Model Predictive Control (MPC) with a cognitive human driver behavior model to enhance autonomous vehicle decision-making in dynamic traffic environments. Building on a foundational driver model informed by psychological theories, the research refines decisionmaking processes by leveraging MPC to anticipate and account for potential traffic events. A three-degree-of-freedom vehicle dynamics model, combined with sliding-mode and proportional controllers for lateral and longitudinal motions, respectively, is developed to facilitate simulations. The simulation results reveal that the proposed MPC-enhanced driver model significantly improves the ego-vehicle's ability to respond to dynamic traffic scenarios, such as a sudden lane change by a moving obstacle in front of the vehicle. Our method avoids collisions during critical maneuvers while achieving smoother and more stable trajectories compared to the conventional driver model.

title: A Distributed Multi-Robot Collaborative Hunting Method in Dynamic Cluttered Environments
authors: Chang Wang; Jianyu Li; Meng Zhou; Lin Zhang
abstract: The paper proposes a distributed multi-robot cooperative hunting method in cluttered environments with guaranteed collision avoidance. First, to achieve collision avoidance, a robot safety region collision avoidance method based on Buffered Voronoi Cells (BVC) is proposed. Then, under the BVC collision avoidance framework, a Kalman filer is designed to estimate the evader' position. Next, a hunting cost function based on the evader's position probability density function is constructed. Furthermore, the hunting controller for the pursuers is designed inspired by Voronoi coverage control. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that under the influence of this controller, the distance between the pursuers and the evader continuously decreases until the hunting is successful.

title: Leg Kinematic Parameter Identification of Quadruped Robots Based on a Virtual Fixed Base
authors: Chenxiang Yuan; Zhigang Ren; Hui Chen
abstract: The leg kinematic parameters of quadruped robots, including connecting rod length and joint angle, often deviate significantly due to machining and assembly errors. This inaccurate knowledge can lead to foot-end position errors and ultimately affect precise state estimation and control. Directing against this issue, this paper introduces the concept of a virtual fixed base and designs a non-redundant parameter identification method. The virtual fixed base is established by 4 marking points on the body, determining a hypothetical coordinate system, which is used to solve the hand-eye calibration problem of quadruped robots. This study provides the overall process of the kinematic parameter identification method.
