Simulation and experiment results show that the identified kinematic parameters converge to their actual value and the foot-end position accuracy is improved by over 80% after parameter compensation.

title: Modular Robot Task Execution Framework for Industrial PCB Handling: A Behavior Tree Approach
authors: Sharath Chandra Akkaladevi; Markus Ganglbauer; Kapil Deshpande; Sebastian Ukleja; Sharath Chandra Akkaladevi; Andreas Pichler
abstract: Handling printed circuit boards (PCBs) in industrial environments presents significant challenges due to design variability, high precision requirements, and the need for scalability. Traditional manual workflows are laborintensive and error-prone, while fixed robotic systems lack the adaptability to manage diverse PCB types and task variations. This paper proposes a Behavior Tree (BT)-based framework for automating PCB handling tasks, integrating advanced robotic skills such as detection, grasping, and precise placement. The framework is enhanced by a multimodal Vision System for robust pose estimation, an intuitive Human Interface for task reconfiguration, and a modular Robotic Manipulation Module for reliable execution. The BT-based architecture ensures modularity, and adaptability, addressing the demands of dynamic industrial workflows. Experimental validation demonstrates the framework's ability to handle PCB variability and execute precision-critical tasks efficiently, showcasing its potential for scalable deployment in industrial settings.

title: Finite-time Robust Fault-tolerant Trajectory Tracking Control for QUAVs with Actuator Fault
authors: Rongsheng Xia; Chunlei Bu; Han Jiang
abstract: This paper proposed a finite-time robust fault-tolerant trajectory tracking control strategy for quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (QUAVs) suffering from actuator saturation, unknown external disturbance and actuator fault. Firstly, robust compensation terms are used to handle unknown external disturbance in position subsystem. On this basis, parameter adaptive method is introduced to remove the adverse effects of actuator saturation in attitude subsystem. Then, a fault detection mechanism is designed to estimate the actuator fault in real time. Subsequently, a finite-time robust fault-tolerant tracking strategy based on backstepping framework are proposed and and the finite-time convergence of all error signals are ensurend. Finally, a numerical simulation result is displayed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed trajectory tracking control scheme for the QUAVs dynamic system.

title: Design of Synchronized Pulse Signals for Bump Magnet Power Supply with FPGA-Based System
authors: Surapong Kokkrathoke; Nattawat Yachum; Somjai Chunjarean; Keerati Manasatitpong; Natthawut Suradet; Apichai Kwankasem
abstract: A new in-house pulse generator for bump magnet power supply at Siam Photon Source (SPS), a synchrotron light source managed by Synchrotron Light Research Institute (SLRI) in Thailand, has been designed with the Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA)-based system for replacing the malfunctioning previous module. The power supply is required to generate synchronized current outputs of approximately 3 k <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> maximum for the bump magnets in the precise time from the timing system in which the trigger pulses are applied to create events of magnets in SPS. Particularly, the pulse width of 1.2 µs from the timing system is designed to operate the three bump magnets for beam injection into the storage ring. Therefore, the FPGA pulse generator is proposed to detect the trigger pulses from the main timing system with its real-time capability of the FPGA board to obtain the output pulses in the specific widths and individual delay time to the bump magnet power supply. This paper presents the design and the experimental results of the pulse generator, which demonstrates the excellent performance of this equipment leading to the accomplishment of beam injection for the SPS.

title: Mobile Robot for Cleaning and Enhancing Energy Efficiency at Solar Photovoltaic Installations in Peru
authors: Jose Javier Zavala Porta; Dante Inga Narvaez
abstract: This research presents the development of a mobile robot designed to clean up and improve energy efficiency at solar photovoltaic (PV) installations in Peru. PV energy has seen significant growth as a sustainable and renewable energy source, but its efficiency is often hampered by the accumulation of dirt and debris on the surfaces of solar modules. The proposed robot addresses this challenge by integrating autonomous navigation, advanced cleaning mechanisms, and data-driven optimization using sensors and machine learning techniques. The system is equipped with mechanical and electronic components to ensure robustness, as well as reliable operation in different environmental conditions and module configurations. In addition, the robot incorporates a cloud-based data management system to monitor and analyze performance metrics, enabling continuous improvement of operational efficiency. By automating the maintenance of PV modules, the system not only improves energy production and reduces operating costs but also extends the lifetime of PV modules, offering a cost-effective and environmentally friendly solution for residential and industrial applications. It also contributes to the preservation of renewable energy technologies.

title: Granadilla Pulper Specialised: Innovative Blade System and Gravity Separation for Peruvian Producers
authors: Aroon Rodriguez-Rafael; Karlo Revollar-Richle; Anderson Granados-Ames; Zarate Peña Frank William
abstract: Products derived from granadilla, such as the processed pulp of this fruit, represent one of the main sources of income for producers in the fruit-growing areas of Peru. In addition, within the market of this product there is a high competition and a clear lack of machines dedicated exclusively to this process for this fruit, so that if small producers want to be at the forefront of the industry, they are forced to reduce labor and production time and not having a machine that meets their requirements, they opt for other types of pulpers specialized in other fruits. In this context, the idea of carrying out this research of basic or pure type and of mixed approach arises, where the main objective of this research is to design a pulping machine specialized in granadilla using a system of blades and separation by gravity. The machine has a knife system for tearing the fruit in which the peel is separated and then passed through a vibrating screen to separate the fiber and seeds. Since it is a semi-automatic process, it will be able to satisfy the needs of producers and small industries. The non-experimental design is done through the use of Autodesk Inventor software; this is a program that allows to design and simulate in 3D, it also has collaborations with other programs such as AutoCAD, which makes it a complete software. In the end, the design of a pulper with a capacity of 2.5 kg per minute, which has a system of blades and a vibrating screen for the separation of granadilla pulp, has been successfully achieved thanks to a calculation process that meets the required specifications.

title: Design and Research of Intelligent Mechanized Ridge-up Bed Trail Machine for Root Crops
authors: Wenliang Liu; Gang Luo; Caiyu Jiang; Runjian Dong; Liang Zhang; Jiang Li
abstract: Ginseng, Panax notoginseng and other root crops of Chinese herbal medicine are mostly planted on the mountainside of dense forest. Their cultivation is characterized by scattered plots, small single plot area and large ground slope. According to the agronomic requirements of furrow cutting, an intelligent mechanized ridge-up bed trail machine which can be used for trail excavation of root crops such as ginseng and notoginseng was studied. Using SLDWORKS, CAXA, virtual prototype and other technologies, a variety of innovative structures such as non-linear and vertical transmission boxes, paddle wheel wide-width soil-throwing blades, and adjustable depth-limiting land wheels were designed. For the machine, the gasoline engine drives the land wheel to walk autonomously and the working part soil-throwing blades to rotate. It can complete trail excavation and ridge-up bed soil-supporting at one time, and has the functions of trimming and compacting the side wall. It can significantly improve the work efficiency and reduce the labor intensity and operation cost. The machine can also be equipped with intelligent remote control equipment and sensing equipment to realize unmanned driving and independent adjustment of excavation depth.

title: Development of an Enhanced Bilateral Nanorobotic System Using an X3D-Based Haptic Interface for Multi-Scale Manipulation Within an SEM Environment
authors: Ujjal Dey; C S Kumar
publication_title: 2024 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Manipulation of micro-nano materials inside an electron microscope requires accurate position control of the micromanipulators and precise management of the forces involved in the manipulation process. While visual data is vital for object tracking and path planning, incorporating force feedback is critical for ensuring controlled physical interactions. Relying solely on visual feedback to execute any experimental task on nanomaterials is inadequate. Since human operators are more adaptable to force changes than robotic systems, developing bilateral controllers is essential for precise human intervention in nanorobotic-based experimental tasks. Therefore, a bilateral SEM-based nanorobotics system with haptic feedback has been developed for multi-scale manipulation. Adding haptic feedback to these tasks enhances manipulation precision and reduces completion time as well as the mean force exerted on the object. This work also introduces a new user interface for 3D modeling and haptic interactions.

title: Learning-based calibration of a high-precision monocular vision system for macro-micro manipulation
authors: Sheng Yao; Xianmin Zhang; Hai Li
publication_title: 2020 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Calibration is critical for the optical vision measurement system (OVMS) that requires high measuring accuracy within a large field of view. In this paper, we propose a practical two-step calibration method that improves measuring accuracy for the multi-scale vision measurement system based on a learning-based approach. In this method, an OVMS combined with a degenerated perspective-n-points algorithm is established for macro-micro manipulation systems. After the OVMS is coarsely calibrated by the analytic technique, the fine calibration is performed using the Artificial Nerual Network to compensate for both geometric and non-geometric measuring errors. Simulations, experiments and comparisons are carried out with a laser tracker, and the results show that the proposed two-step calibration method can remarkably minimize measuring errors and shows stronger robustness and stability, which enables the OVMS to be capable of macro-micro manipulation tasks.

title: Active Lateral Riding Comfort Control Strategies of High-Speed Train
authors: Xianhui Su; Yufei Zhang
abstract: Based on the lateral vibration control of bogie frame for improving hunting stability in high-speed trains, three control strategies including linear quadratic regulator (LQR) control, Fuzzy Proportional-Integral (Fuzzy-PI) Control and Particle Swarm Optimization Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PSO-PID) Control are compared in this study. For the simplified linear lateral dynamics model of single bogie, the control parameters under the three control strategies are acquired, then they are applied to the vehicle dynamics model co-simulated by the SIMPACK and MATLAB codes. The different train operating conditions are taken into account and the improvement of dynamics indexes under the three control strategies are evaluated from the aspects of lateral riding quality of the car body and lateral force of wheelsets. The results show that the three control strategies lead to obvious mitigation on lateral vibration, and the improvement of PSO-PID control is the most obvious, but the LQR control effect is the worst.

title: Evaluating Robustness of Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Autonomous Shipping
authors: Bavo Lesy; Ali Anwar; Siegfried Mercelis
abstract: Recently, there has been growing interest in au-tonomous shipping due to its potential to improve maritime efficiency and safety. The use of advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence, can address the current navigational and operational challenges in autonomous shipping. In particular, inland waterway transport (IWT) presents a unique set of challenges, such as crowded waterways and variable environ-mental conditions. In such dynamic settings, the reliability and robustness of autonomous shipping solutions are critical factors for ensuring safe operations. This paper examines the robustness of benchmark deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms, implemented for IWT within an autonomous shipping simulator, and their ability to generate effective motion planning policies. We demonstrate that a model-free approach can achieve an adequate policy in the simulator, successfully navigating port environments never encountered during training. We focus par-ticularly on Soft-Actor Critic (SAC), which we show to be inherently more robust to environmental disturbances compared to MuZero, a state-of-the-art model-based RL algorithm. In this paper, we take a significant step towards developing robust, applied RL frameworks that can be generalized to various vessel types and navigate complex port- and inland environments and scenarios.

title: Research of Testing Technology of Distributed Safety and Stability Control System
authors: Fei Yang; Jingfu Tian; You Yu; Wuyang Zhang; Lu Zhang; Shida She
abstract: The large-scale security control system involves multiple stations and cross regions. When testing security control stations of different scales at the same time, there are high requirements for communication data bandwidth, signal strength, control distance and communication delay. AS6802 defines a deterministic, high fault tolerance and non-blocking communication synchronization technology. The fault tolerance of the clock synchronization of the security control test system is enhanced by using the unique synchronous handshake system of AS6802 protocol standard to synchronize with the existing Ethernet time. Through simulation analysis, it is verified that the scheme is more flexible to receive and send Ethernet frame data, reduces dynamic delay, and its synchronization accuracy fully meets the requirements of distributed testing.

title: A Trajectory State Switching Mechanism for Nonholonomic Mobile Robot Trajectory Tracking
authors: Changjiang Jing; Xiaomin Wang; Zhou Zheng; Zhendong Sun; Jinshu Han; Min Xue
abstract: This paper presents a switching controller that effectively exerts the excellencies of Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Linear Quadratic Regulation (LQR) to handle the trajectory-variant tracking problem. The good balance between accuracy and computational cost is achieved by designing a novel trajectory state switching mechanism (TSSM) that considers both trajectory curvature and tracking error. The TSSM assigns computation-unexpensive LQR to address trajectory tracking when the trajectory exhibits smoothness and minimal lateral error. Conversely, LQR seamlessly transits to the performance-focused MPC by TSSM when substantial changes in curvature or pronounced lateral errors occur. The TSSM precludes the Zeno phenomenon, since the curvature and error will not change suddenly result from the continuity of the trajectory state. Furthermore, to mitigate potential oscillations during control algorithm transitions, a continuous control strategy is reported. In addition, the stability of the system is analyzed by constructing a common Rayapunov function. The experimental results demonstrate the performance of the proposed TSSM control in trajectory tracking.

title: Fuzzy Active Disturbance Rejection Control Technology for Quadcopter UAV in Flying Manipulator Arm
authors: Shuai Meng; Junlin Wang; Xinyue Zhang; Yuxin Li; Fan Chen
abstract: As the core content of the flight manipulator system to provide a stable platform for the operation of the manipulator and achieve accurate grasping, the attitude angle control must have strong anti-interference control ability. In order to improve the robustness of the aircraft, a fuzzy active disturbance rejection control strategy for the quadrotor in the flight manipulator system was proposed. Based on the fact that the traditional ADRC integrates fuzzy control logic into the design of the nonlinear error feedback control law, which reduces the difficulty of adjusting the parameters of the traditional ADRC, and the fal function is used in the design of the traditional ADRC extended state observer, when the deviation is large, the gain of the observer will increase sharply, resulting in the decrease of the anti-interference ability of the system. For the above problems, the faln function is used, when the error is large, this function limits the gain of the system, so as to enhance the immunity of the system. The attitude model of the quadcopter UAV was built in the MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment, and the simulation effect of the traditional PID attitude control was compared under the condition of interference. The simulation results show that the designed attitude controller has good anti-interference ability under the condition of external interference. According to the attribute information of the physical platform, a 1:1 virtual simulation model is built in Solidwork, which can be imported into the Gazebo virtual physical simulation platform to verify the control effect of the controller, providing a method for the virtual simulation of the flight manipulator. According to the attribute information of the physical platform, a 1:1 virtual simulation model is built in Solidwork, which can be imported into the Gazebo virtual physical simulation platform to verify the control effect of the controller, providing a method for the virtual simulation of the flight manipulator.

title: A Trajectory Planning Method for Autonomous Vehicle in Narrow Passages
authors: Juqi Hu; Dongliang Liu; Hejia Gao
abstract: Autonomous driving technologies have been developed rapidly in recent years, resulting in wide applications of lane following, auto parking and pre-collision systems in commercial vehicles. To make autonomous vehicles more versatile, path planning in complex scenarios should be considered. One critical challenge is to plan trajectories for vehicle in narrow passages. A common method, by establishing spatiotemporal corridors, may result in only a small or even empty safety margin. Therefore, this paper proposes an enhanced hybrid A* algorithm with a novel cost function taking into account comfort, obstacle avoidance and short path length in complex structed environments. Moreover, a new expansion strategy is further introduced to reduce the number of the expanded nodes and to improve the efficiency of trajectory planning. In addition, an obstacle cost-map for hybrid A* is designed to ensure a safe distance from obstacles. Typical driving scenarios in narrow passage are considered in simulations and experiments. The efficiency of the proposed trajectory planner has been validated by both simulations and experiments.

title: Design of Hysteresis Control based Adaptive Sliding Mode Control and Cuckoo Search based PI Control for DC-DC Boost Converters
authors: Tamen Thapa Sarkar; Ashruti Upadhyaya; Chitralekha Mahanta
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Due to the underlying complexities and nonlinear behavior of the DC-DC boost converters, its control becomes a difficult operation. The non-minimum phase behavior of the DC-DC boost converters also makes it tough to control. This paper proposes two different techniques based on hysteresis based Adaptive SMC and Cuckoo Search (CS) based Proportional-Integral (PI) control methods for controlling DC-DC boost converters. The two techniques applied in this research are compared in terms of various performance indices such as Integral of Absolute Error (IAE), overshoot, rise time and settling time. The effectiveness of the two proposed controllers are evaluated in relation to changes in input voltage, reference voltage and load. The two proposed methods are also compared against a conventional PID tuned by Internal Model Controller (IMC). The hysteresis control based adaptive sliding mode controller performs better than CS based PI controller and IMC based PID controller with lesser IAE against fluctuations in terms of reference voltage, load, and input voltage.

title: Experimental Study of Structural Vibration Control Based on Piezoelectric Shunt Control System
authors: Zhuang Xu; Shengquan Li; Luyao Zhang; Juan Li
abstract: This paper proposes a composite piezoelectric shunt damping control method based on the improvement of negative impedance technology to achieve structural vibration suppression. First, the mathematical model of beam structure with the piezoelectric path is established. Besides, the modal analysis is carried out. Second, the shunt damping controller is designed based on the negative impedance technology. Moreover, the influence of partial internal resistance on inductance is attenuated by a negative impedance circuit. Finally, based on NIDAQ data acquisition system, experiments are carried out on the designed shunt damping controller. Experimental results show that the structural vibration can be effectively reduced and the vibration amplitude is attenuated by 7.82dB.

title: A Novel Index-based Assessment Method for Rural Homestead Utilization
authors: Chengquan Xu; Youwen Liu; Shaofei Jin
abstract: Due to the lack of basic data and long-term lack of scientific management of rural homestead in China, homestead construction shows great randomness and dispersion, and there is no centralized layout. Based on the recently completed Rural Cadastral and housing survey results, the paper constructs an index system for the evaluation of rural homestead utilization from three aspects: density dimension, functional dimension and social dimension. The index system includes building floor area ratio, residential unit density, three-dimensional center of gravity, homestead density, average building floors, proportion of public building area, one household multi residence rate and other indicators. The data on house bases in four different villages in Putian City, Fujian Province, including the island, the coastal plain area, the suburban hilly area and the mountainous area, are analyzed from the index system to analyze the current situation of rural homestead use and provide a scientific basis for the construction and management of homestead land.

title: Model-Based Design of Distributed ROS2 Systems Using IEC 61499
authors: Jörg Walter; Malte Grave
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: ROS2 systems are distributed applications built from strongly isolated components (nodes). Communication is realized through a publish/subscribe mechanism. Despite having these modern software architecture elements, ROS2 has no canonical modelling language that captures overall application design and helps in mapping nodes across distributed platforms. We propose a model-based design approach based on the graphical programming language IEC 61499, mapping ROS2 constructs to native IEC 61499 model elements. Code generation creates native ROS2 nodes from IEC 61499 code. As an additional benefit, this approach also eases integration of ROS2 systems with non-ROS components.

title: Lower Limb Prosthesis Gait Cycle Prediction Analysis Using Gyroscope and Load Cell
authors: Syed Sohaib Ali Shah; Syed Irfan Shah; Muhammad Adnan Khalil; Umar S. Khan; Mohsin I. Tiwana
abstract: Prediction of the accurate and continuous ankle angles during gait cycle is a great challenge faced in biomedical science. To overcome this challenge, potential of two sensors i.e., a gyroscope and load cell (strain gauge) in predicting ankle angles and load during a Gait cycle was evaluated. Precision values presented by the gyroscope are 95% accurate however values offered by the load cell have a precision of around 88.2%. In addition to this, the image of the current Gait stance is also displayed in real-time. The results obtained using these sensors proved the ability of the method to be efficient and capable in the prediction of Gait cycle ankle angles. This accuracy model can be further refined as a future work for implementation in balance-based calculations and control of lower limb prosthesis.

title: Proposal of a Swimming Pool Drowning Detection System using Cameras and Raspberry Pi based on Machine Learning
authors: Christopher Urruchi; Daniel Cervantes-Chauca; Deyby Huamanchahua
abstract: Drowning deaths represent the third leading cause of accidental deaths worldwide. This is because traditional techniques for the supervision and care of people, especially children, in large pools are inefficient or, in some cases, nonexistent. Nowadays, this problem has become a topic of interest for several researchers who seek to propose different methods of drowning detection. This research work seeks to propose the process to be followed to develop a drowning detection system in swimming pools using cameras and Raspberry Pi based on Machine Learning. To achieve the objective, the use of the Triple Diamond design methodology was proposed. In the development of the first diamond, the information was organized in a Lotus Blossom Diagram, then the problematic situation and the main objective were described. In the development of the second diamond, a bibliometric analysis was performed, searching for information with search equations and then sorting and filtering it, and finally including it in morphological matrices. As a result, an electrical diagram of the system and a flow diagram of the algorithm based on a Support Vector Machine were proposed.

title: Intersection Feature Analysis and Signal Control Optimization Based on VISSIM
authors: Haoyue Wang; Zundong Zhang; Shilin Zhang
abstract: This study aims to enhance the traffic efficiency at the intersection of South Science Park Middle Street and North Anxiang Road, as well as the intersection of West Science Park Middle Street and South Science Park Middle Street through comprehensive analysis and simulation optimization. The research initially conducted a detailed organization and analysis of traffic flow data at both intersections, clarifying the traffic characteristics and existing issues at each approach. A traffic simulation model built with Virtual Interactive Simulation of Transportation Systems was used to assess the current traffic organization and signal timing, and a series of optimization measures were proposed, including improvements in traffic channelization, signal timing optimization, design improvements of traffic signs and markings, and the design and implementation of traffic detection and monitoring systems. The results of the study indicate that the proposed optimization measures can effectively reduce vehicle delays and queue lengths, enhancing the capacity of the intersections. Additionally, the study explored the design of traffic data detection and monitoring systems, providing technical support for real-time traffic management. Ultimately, the outcomes of this research not only provide a scientific basis for the traffic improvement of the two intersections but also offer a reference for addressing similar urban traffic issues.

title: Transfer Learning for Ultrasound-Based Kidney Stone (Urolithiasis) Detection with Augmented Regularization and Saliency Maps
authors: Omar Faruq Shikdar; Arifa Sultana Mily; Tanzia Haque; Ashraful Islam; Sujana Islam; Ruba Sazeda
abstract: Urolithiasis, commonly known as kidney stones (KS), can have serious health implications. In 2019, around 115 million people around the world suffered from this disease. It is extremely important that the disease be diagnosed quickly. Among all the possible diagnostic imaging options, ultrasound is the safest option, as it has no risk of radiation. The goal of this study is to create a system that will detect kidney stones from ultrasound images. The dataset used in this research had 2 classes: normal (4414) and kidney stone (5002), in total 9416 images. The dataset was preprocessed applying proper methods such as resizing, rescaling, and center cropping and then split into train, validation, and test sets. We deployed four pretrained deep learning models, which are DenseNet201, ResNet50, InceptionV3, and MobileNetV3. Methods like MixUp and CutMix, known as augmented regularization, were used to make the model more robust. Hyperparameter tuning was done for optimal results. The layers of the pretrained model were frozen, and on top of them our CNN model was placed. The research was conducted using two methods: one where pretrained models were only used for feature extraction and another where pretrained models were fine-tuned for training. The highest accuracy of 99.73% was achieved by DenseNet. The model’s output prediction has been explained by using saliency maps. After 1000 iterations, the 99% confidence interval for the model is [0.993,0.999]

title: A Residential Home Energy Management System using Hybrid Particle Swarm-Grey Wolf Optimization
authors: Vikas Deep Juyal; Sandeep Kakran
abstract: With the evolution of technology since the last decade, smart appliances are now the trend in most developed countries and soon will be a part of a typical user all over the world. The phenomenon of the smart grid allows controlling the time of operation of the appliances through two-way communication with the utility by employing a demand response program with the help of an energy management centre. In this paper, a hybrid of particle swarm optimization and grey wolf optimization technique is proposed and implemented for scheduling home appliances to minimize the electricity consumption bill. Real-time pricing (RTP) and inclined block rate RTP demand response programs have also been implemented to limit the peak-to-average ratio (PAR). Several cases have been compared with different conditions and found that the proposed strategy gives improved results in terms of electricity cost as well as PAR value.

title: 3D Localization of Tomato Harvesting Points Based on YOLOv5-Seg
authors: Jin Chen; Huanyu Jiang
abstract: The acquisition of tomato harvesting points is of paramount importance for the realization of automated harvesting. To achieve effective and precise localization of tomatoes in a hanging vine cultivation mode within a greenhouse environment, this study proposes a method for identifying and localizing cherry tomato harvesting points based on binocular vision and deep learning principles. The proposed method, which is built upon tomato pedicel contour segmentation, combines the binocular ranging principle of cameras to accurately obtain the 3D coordinates of cherry tomato pedicel harvesting points in environments. First, YOLOv5-seg is used to detect the contours of the tomato pedicel, followed by skeleton curve fitting using a contour detection algorithm. To address the significant depth loss in tomato pedicels, the depth at both ends of the fitted pedicel contour curve is used to estimate the depth at the midpoint of the curve. The internal and external parameters of the Orbbec Gemini 335 camera are then combined to determine the actual distance between the harvesting point and the camera. Finally, the conversion relationship between the pixel coordinate system and the world coordinate system is applied to obtain the 3D coordinates of the cherry tomato harvesting points. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, harvesting point localization experiments for cherry tomatoes were conducted on an optical platform. Through experiments under different positions, heights, and depth distances, the spatial average localization error was found to be 8.24 mm, with an average segmentation speed of 27 ms. The results meet the requirements for fast and precise localization of cherry tomato harvesting points, enabling real-time and accurate segmentation and spatial localization. This study provides a technical reference for the development of cherry tomato harvesting devices.

title: Evaluation of Steering Characteristics of Smart Hand-Tractor with Inner Wheel Locking Mechanism
authors: Saki Shigenobu; Tsuneo Nakanishi; Takuya Fujinaga
abstract: The two-wheeled hand-tractor, which is suitable for operation in small and irregular arable lands, is modified as a smart hand-tractor, or an agricultural robot. In unmanned operation under remote control or autonomous operation, un-like manned operation, movement of the smart hand-tractor is not adjusted by the operator gripping its handlebars with force. In this paper, a comparative experiment is conducted to confirm whether straight driving and tilling are possible in such unmanned operation as well as in manned operation. The authors' walking tractor is equipped with an inner wheel locking mechanism that not only disengages the power transmission to the inner wheel but also applies braking when turning, which is effective to ensure turning with a smaller radius on any ground with different rolling resistance. The experimental results showed that straight driving and tilling can be performed with the same quality regardless of the presence or absence of an operator and quantitatively showed that straight driving is adversely affected when tillage with a rotary hoe in the case of the authors' hand-tractor, in which the inner wheel locking mechanism is always activated during turning. It was found that the inner wheel locking mechanism should be dynamically enabled/disabled depending on the situation such as adjusting movement for straight and turning, in order to allow better autonomous operation of the hand-tractor.

title: Design of real-time enhanced monitoring terminal based on FPGA
authors: Fengyan ni; Ningzhuang liu
abstract: In the power system, when monitoring various devices and transmission lines, because the transmission lines are generally in the wild, the surrounding weather environment and geographical environment are very complicated. Therefore, during video monitoring and recognition, the collected video images will be Affected by the weather and light, the quality of the collected images is reduced. However, the recognition in the later stage does not consider how to filter out these influences, and it is often difficult to achieve the desired results when performing subsequent image processing such as target recognition and tracking. For ARM+FPGA, DSP+FPGA image processing system, the cost is high, Low resource utilization, it is difficult to use simple FPGA to control the process and complex branch judgment, therefore, this paper designs a real-time enhanced monitoring terminal based on FPGA based on the idea of FPGA-based hardware and software collaborative processing. Complete image acquisition and real-time enhanced preprocessing in the monitoring terminal to improve the ability to accurately identify the transmission line during subsequent processing and achieve accurate identification. Use an FPGA chip as the core of the system, cache the image through SDRAM, use Sopc as the control core, coordinate software and hardware to perform image processing, easy to use hardware implementation (such as filtering, edge detection, etc.) are implemented using Verilog hardware language, Control these image processing modules through Sopc, realize the corresponding image processing function. And the part that is difficult to realize in the hardware, use NiosII in Sopc system to realize.

title: A Fractional-Order Active Disturbance Rejection Controller Design for a PMSM Servo System
authors: Bolin Li; Lijun Zhu
abstract: This paper proposes a parameter tuning method of fractional-order active disturbance rejection controller (FOADRC) for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) servo system with frequency-domain analysis. In this method, a fractional-order proportional derivative (FOPD) and a fractional-order [proportional derivative] (FO[PD]) controllers design combining with active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) are proposed. A systematic parameter tuning scheme is presented, and a flat phase constraint is applied as a design specification, which guarantees the phase is flat around the gain crossover frequency point. The closed-loop system is robust to gain variations. The simulation results illustrate that the response of the PMSM servo system using FO[PD]-ADRC has a smaller overshoot, less tracking error, and better resistance to load disturbance than that using fractional-order proportional derivative ADRC (FOPD-ADRC).

title: A Novel Adaptive Just-in-Time Learning Soft Sensor Modeling Method With a Density-Based Data Update Strategy
authors: Yueli Song; Yili Chu; Yanan Du
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology, data-driven soft sensors are often used in industrial process quality control. In recent years, soft sensor modeling method based on just-in-time learning (JITL) has been widely studied and applied due to its strong adaptability to time-varying characteristics of processes, simple modeling principles, and easy implementation. However, when the working conditions of the production process migrate due to various reasons such as sensor drift, catalyst deterioration, and raw material changes, the historical data used for modeling may not cover the current working condition, and the performance of the JITL model will also sharply decline even fail. Therefore, this article proposes a density based modeling data adaptive update management mechanism under the JITL framework to effectively enhance the adaptive tracking ability of soft sensors for process condition migration, thereby maintaining the longterm effectiveness of the model in practical use. Finally, the advantages of the proposed method were verified through numerical simulation and comparative analysis.

title: Implementation and analysis of Ryze Tello drone vision-based positioning using AprilTags
authors: Mariusz Pawlicki; Kacper Hulek; Adrian Ostrowski; Jakub Możaryn
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The paper describes the method of the Ryze Tello drone to move autonomously using a basic vision system. The drone's position is determined by identifying AprilTags' position relative to the drone's built-in camera. The accuracy of the drone's position readings and distance calculations was tested under controlled conditions, and errors were analysed. The study showed a decrease in absolute error with decreasing drone distance from the marker, a little change in the relative error for large distances, and a sharp decrease in the relative error for small distances. The method is satisfactory for determining the drone's position relative to a marker.

title: An Improved Optimal Trajectory Planning Method of Six-axis Robotic Manipulators along Prescribed Path Constraints
authors: Ziyao Xiong; Liping Chen; Jianwan Ding
abstract: Optimal Control Problem (OCP) is a kind of classical problem with the state space equations, containing the optimal trajectory planning problem of robotic manipulators with complicated path constraints. The optimal control method (OCM) which contains direct and indirect methods is efficient to solve this kind of problems. The Pontryagin maximum principle is the core of the indirect method which includes tedious mathematical derivations, and is hard to work with the complex mechanical system. As the result, the direct methods represented by direct collocation method (DCM) are widely used in the engineering field. They transform the original optimal control problem to nonlinear programming problems (NLP), so that the general NLP solver can be used. There are mainly three different methods based on the above direct methods, including convex optimization (CO) methods, numerical integration (NI) methods and dynamic programming (DP) methods. This paper proposes a brand new idea which can streamline the problem description compared to the CO method, extend the general objective function compared to the NI method, and reduce the cost of storage compared to the DP method, and provides a feasible local optimal solution for the problem. In addition, the simulation experiment satisfies the kinodynamic constraints properly, and the validity of the proposed method is confirmed.

title: Rolling bearing fault diagnosis using multisynchrosqueezing transform under time-varying conditions
authors: Chaoang Xiao; Jianbo Shao; Lichun You; Jianbo Yu
abstract: In engineering, vibration signals of rotating machinery are nonstationary and complicated under time-varying conditions. Due to Heisenberg uncertainty principle, the traditional time-frequency analysis methods cannot extract the time-varying features accurately. In this paper, a multisynchrosqueezing transform (MSST) and frequency ridges extraction method is proposed to diagnose the rolling bearing fault with time-varying speeds. Firstly, the SST is combined with an iterative computation procedure to generate a more energy concentrated time-frequency representation. Secondly, multiple ridge curves extraction algorithm is proposed to identify the time-varying rotational frequencies and fault frequencies. Finally, the extracted frequency ridge curves are compared with theoretical fault characteristic coefficients to detect the fault types. Experimental results and comparative analysis demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively improve the resolution of time-frequency representation and extract instantaneous features.

title: Prediction of Contour Errors for an H-Bot Gantry CNC Machine Using Neural Networks and NURBS Toolpaths
authors: Krystian Erwinski; Patryk Ustaszewski
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper presents a method for predicting contour error in H-Bot non-cartesian CNC gantry machine. Contour error is defined as the difference between the desired and actual trajectory of a CNC machine. This error can be caused by defects in the machine's mechanics and dynamic errors caused by following errors in the machine's drive axes. The error can be predicted using a black box model in the form of a neural network. This paper presents a method for training a NARX neural network-based contour error predictor for an H-Bot noncartesian machine. Contour error prediction is performed for toolpaths defined as Non-Uniform Rational B-Spline (NURBS). The neural network-based contour error prediction accuracy is verified experimentally on an actual H-Bot gantry machine. The presented results prove that the proposed neural contour error predictor is viable for use in H-Bot non-cartesian machines with kinematically coupled drive axes.

title: Moving Target Recognition in Noisy Environment Based on Sound Seismic Fusion Signal and PSO-SVM
authors: Jingwei Song; Nan Wang; Kunsheng Xing
abstract: Recognition of moving targets (pedestrian and vehicle) by ground seismic signal has been a hot research topic in recent years. The methods proposed in previous studies mainly focus on seismic signal recognition in field environment. However, studies involving target recognition in noisy environment suffer from low recognition rate and slow recognition speed. To solve the problem of target recognition in noisy environment and to improve recognition performance, a method based on sound seismic fusion signal and particle swarm optimization support vector machine (PSO-SVM) is proposed. The method consists of three parts: signal acquisition, feature extraction and classification method. The method innovatively introduces sound seismic fusion signal as sampling data to improve the feature extraction efficiency of the target, and uses particle swarm optimization support vector machine to further improve the recognition accuracy. Compared with other methods, the fused signal can better collect the features of the target in noisy environment, and the optimized algorithm has the features of simple structure, high efficiency and high accuracy. After experimental verification, the recognition accuracy of the method for moving targets in noisy environment is 93.21%.

title: Design of the Control System of a Flexible Line for Manufacturing Metallic Parts by Using Programmable Logic Controllers
authors: Vasile Alexandru Dulgheriu; Eugen Ioan Gergely; Laura Coroiu; Helga Maria Silaghi; Adrian Codoban
abstract: The paper presents the design process of a control system for a line which manufactures metallic parts for the automotive industry. The manufacturing line is designed so that it can produce several product models. The control system, based on a programmable logic controller (PLC), is designed to allow on-the-fly reconfiguration of the line based on the recipe selected by the operator. Equally, the hardware configuration and the PLC program allow the further development of the manufacturing line by adding new stations (and obviously new recipes). By incorporating into the control system modular programming techniques, a large amount of safety measures, tools necessary to ensure product traceability and a modern human-machine interface (HMI), the design ensures high efficiency of the manufacturing line, a high level of safety of the operators and of the plant, compliance with current quality requirements and the possibility to expand the line for extending the product range without considerable effort.

title: Error accumulation effect in Xsens based manipulator teleoperation
authors: Tomasz Grzejszczak; Adam Gałuszka; Natalia Bartosiak; Martyna Wojnar
publication_title: 2021 25th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to find and examine the impact of error of MTw Xsens IMU sensors. The sensors are used for manipulator control by means of teleoperation. The serial connection of the sensors generates the effect of error accumulation such that the orientation of last element of kinematic chain is measured with cumulative error of all sensors. In this paper the results of test is presented where the sensors are connected in series for yaw and roll error calculations. Two types of errors are present: constant accumulated over time and temporary error in form of spikes. Final discussion presents the possible accuracy of the kinematic chain depending on the number of used sensors.

title: Res-UNet Based Fetal Electrocardiogram Extraction via Time-Frequency Representation
authors: Zhenqin Chen; Yiwei Lin; Jinshan Xu
abstract: The fetal heart rate variation serves as an effective means of fetal health monitor. Although can be captured through abdominal electrocardiogram (AECG) of pregnant women, the AECG signal contains interference from maternal heart activity and other sources. Due to the higher-amplitude maternal ECG (MECG), the waveform of the fetal ECG (FECG) is obscured, making FECG separation challenging. However, the similarity of the frequency patterns of both types of ECG signals implies the possibility of reconstructing FECG using the frequency and the strength information of FECG. To this end, we employ the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) to convert the AECG signal into its time-frequency representation, and utilize a neural network model for extracting FECG from the time-frequency domain. The model can obtain high-quality FECG by capturing the amplitude differences between fetal and maternal heartbeats in different frequency components of AECG. Moreover, a combined time-domain and frequency-domain loss is introduced to enhance the model's separation performance. The proposed method is validated on public databases and demonstrates outstanding performance, providing an effective and feasible solution for non-invasive monitoring of fetal health.

title: Development of an Intelligent Wheelchair System Utilizing Raspberry Pi for Enhanced User Mobility and Safety
authors: Zhi-hui Meng; Zi-hui Zhu; Yu-zhe Li; Rui Yang; Xin-yue Fu; Yuan-xin Cai
abstract: This paper presents the development of an intelligent wheelchair system, which is controlled by a Raspberry Pi microcontroller. It has six major functions: remote-controlled umbrella canopy, navigation and positioning, emergency assistance, obstacle warning, automatic lighting, and anti-slip reminder. It achieves high intelligence and convenience. The wheelchair uses Raspberry Pi as its core control board, connected to sensors and actuators via GPIO interfaces for precise control. Research shows it enhances users' travel experience and safety, with broad application prospects and promotional value. The paper also offers insights for future smart wheelchair research and development.

title: Research on Identification Method of Groove Inflection Point of Medium and Thick Plate Based on Line Structured Light
authors: Xu Feng; Hong Lu; Zhe Zhang; Yongquan Zhang; Xujie Yuan; Jinchao Feng; Weijie Dong
abstract: The identification of the characteristics of the groove inflection point of the medium and thick plate is one of the important processes to determine the geometric information of the groove. In the actual working conditions, the interference of the workpiece burr or the external environment will affect the identification accuracy of the groove inflection point. Aiming at the demand of feature recognition of groove inflection point of medium and thick plate, the line structured light vision sensor is used to collect the point cloud data of groove, and the data is processed in the computer, that is, the high-precision recognition of groove inflection point is realized by the designed multi-algorithm fusion inflection point recognition strategy. The experimental results show that the method has strong adaptability and anti-interference, as well as high accuracy.

title: Application of Large Language Models in Magnetically Manipulated Microrobots
authors: Artur Kopitca; Usama Sattar; Quan Zhou
publication_title: 2025 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs), machine learning systems trained on massive internet-scale datasets, have recently been applied across diverse domains-including robotics-due to their ability to generalize, reason over complex data, and adapt to a wide range of tasks with minimal fine-tuning. In robotics, LLMs have enabled advancements in planning, instruction following, and high-level decision-making. However, their potential in microrobotic systems, such as magnetically manipulated microrobots, remains largely unexplored. Compared to macroscale robotics, this domain poses unique challenges, including complex nonlinear dynamics, sparse observations, and limited data availability, while offering diverse applications ranging from biomedical solutions to environmental cleaning. In this work, we present the first demonstration of LLMs applied to physical microrobotic control by automating the design of reward functions within a reinforcement learning (RL) framework. We train an RL policy using LLM-generated rewards and deploy it to control the motion of a ferromagnetic particle (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varnothing \sim \mathbf{5 0 0} \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>) using solenoids at the air-water interface. Furthermore, we evaluate the impact of LLM model scale, prompt design, and reward configuration on learning performance. The results show that LLM-based reward design enables effective training and experimental deployment, opening a new direction for LLM-driven control in microrobotics.

title: Particle Filtering in Multivariable Systems: All Weights Equal to Zero Problem
authors: Piotr Kozierski; Jacek Michalski; Marek Retinger; Mikolaj Mrotek
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This article focuses on a problem that typically occurs in multivariable systems, i.e. the case where all calculated weights are equal to zero. The cause of this problem was explained and several different solutions (algorithm modifications) were proposed. The studies were performed for 12 different objects (4 connection structures, each with three different measurement models) with state vector lengths ranging from 2 to 25. Results presented are for the effective number of particles, the number of iterations in which all weights were zero, and for average root mean squared error.

title: A New Approach for Detection and Analysis of Lung Pleural Line Morphology
authors: Rusu-Both Roxana; Popa Alexandra; Toderean Bianca; Chira Romeo Ioan
abstract: Interstitial lung diseases represent a large category of disorders which carry significant mortality burden at a worldwide level. Diffuse lung diseases are usually diagnosed and followed-up using radiological methods, mainly computed tomography and radiography. Those radiation-based procedures expose the patient and the environment to an accumulative radiation and can also produce complication after contrast medium injection, renal injury. Transthoracic ultrasound (TUS) examination represents a viable alternative to evaluate patients with lung interstitial damage proven in multiple published studies. In this paper we aim to develop a new method for diffuse lung diseases diagnosis and follow-up based on pleural line morphology evaluation in a lung TUS standardized examination through image analysis and artificial intelligence algorithms which is non-invasive, cheap, accessible and radiation free diagnosis method able to aid physicians in an accurate and non-invasive manner.

title: Recognition of colonial and multicellular microplankton organisms in surface waters using computer vision
authors: Igor Korobiichuk; Dmytro Reut; Volodymyr Drevetskyi
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: When assessing the quality of surface water by biological indicators, there is a problem of measuring the concentration of microplankton by individual classification groups, and this involves the recognition of microorganisms. A method is proposed for increasing the accuracy of an information-measuring system that measures the concentration of microplankton in a running stream. The article considers the problem of accuracy increasing in recognition and counting of colonial and multicellular microplankton organisms in determining the biological indicators of water quality in natural reservoirs using computer vision. In the paper was presented a method has been developed to improve the recognition accuracy of colonial and multicellular organisms of microplankton, which is notable for low computational complexity and allows increasing the accuracy of measuring the concentrations of various groups of microplankton. Experimental results confirmed that the use of the developed modified algorithm allows to increase the accuracy of recognition of colonial algae Pediastrum duplex and multicellular Ulothrix and reduce the number of false-positive recognition of them as several unicellular organisms.

title: Space Launch Group Planning Technique for Manned Space Station Construction
authors: Xue-jun Dong; Zheng Yan; Xin Ye; Shao-jiang Chen; Hui Xue
abstract: The launch mission for manned space station construction is characterized by strong constraints of spacecraft orbit and launch site, as well as tight coupling between multiple launch missions. It is a huge challenge for space launch planning to meet the overall requirements of engineering for reliability, safety, and efficiency. The space launch group planning technique is proposed based on the constraints of space rendezvous and docking and the coupling relationship between space launches using different types of launch vehicles, within the background of manned space station construction. The objective is to design space launch programs that meet the requirements of reliability, safety and efficiency within the specified timeframe. First and foremost, the four-dimensional space launch group-planning diagram is designed using isochrones, referring to the in-orbit space station, two launch sites, and the aerospace manufacturing plants. In the second place, a reliability evaluation function based on reliability growth, launch opportunity increase and launch window lengthening is proposed. Additionally, a safety evaluation function based on emergency rescue launch, and a benefit function based on parallel operation of multiple launch sites is introduced. Finally, the feasibility of the technology proposed is verified taken the construction of Tiangong space station as an example. The result indicates that the launch mission group planning designed using the technology proposed is highly consistent with the engineering practice results.

title: Multi-Objective Small Gap Coal Gangue Recognition Method Based on Semantic Segmentation
authors: Yanwei Wang; Yulong Wang; Wenbin Tao; Jiaquan Yang; Xiangyu Zhang
abstract: A multi-objective coal gangue recognition method based on semantic segmentation is proposed to improve the grasping reliability of mechanical claws under complex conditions, with the improved SegFormer model used for coal gangue identification. The model incorporates a Bottleneck module to reduce computational complexity, an ASPP module for multi-scale fusion, and Criss Cross Attention to enhance spatial contextual information. The experimental results demonstrated that the enhanced SegFormer outperformed other models, achieving a precision of 96.19%, recall of 95.14%, F1 score of 95.66%, and mIoU of 92.24%. These improvements significantly improve the model's capability to identify small gaps, providing reliable information for precise grasping by gangue sorting robot.

title: Markerless Adaptive Visual Servoing Based on YOLOv11-OBB Oriented Object Detection
authors: Xingye Liang; Jianliang Mao; Chuanlin Zhang
abstract: This paper presents a markerless visual servoing framework that combines YOLOv11-0BB-based oriented object detection with adaptive gain control to achieve precise rotary switch alignment. By directly detecting the switch through its geometric features, the system eliminates the need for fiducial markers and uses the four-corner points as visual features for image-based visual servoing (IBVS), enabling real-time alignment. Furthermore, the adaptive gain strategy dynamically adjusts control parameters based on image error, improving robustness against noise and environmental variations. Experimental validation on a UR5 robotic arm with an Intel RealSense D435 camera has demonstrated superior adaptability and high precision compared to marker-based methods, making the proposed approach well-suited for autonomous substation inspection. Overall, this work enhances automation efficiency and control robustness in dynamic environments, contributing to the advancement of markerless visual servoing technologies.

title: Tinyml-Empowered Climbing Robots for Real-Time Structural Defect Detection: Case Studies on Bolt and Tile Inspection
authors: Tzu-Hsuan Lin
abstract: Structural inspection of critical infrastructure presents significant safety challenges when performed manually, particularly for bolt connections in steel structures and exterior wall tiles. This paper presents an innovative approach integrating Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) with climbing robots to enable autonomous, real-time structural defect detection in resourceconstrained environments. Two complementary case studies are examined: a magnetic climbing robot using the FOMO algorithm for visual bolt defect inspection in steel structures and a vacuumbased climbing robot employing CNN-based acoustic analysis for tile defect detection on building exteriors. The magnetic robot achieved 82 % accuracy with an inference time of just 86 ms while requiring minimal memory resources <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{(} \mathbf{0. 0 7 2 M B}$</tex> flash, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2 3 9. 1 K B}$</tex> RAM). The vacuum-based robot demonstrated 74.62 % accuracy in distinguishing between defective and intact tiles through acoustic signature analysis. Both implementations showcase TinyML's versatility across different sensing modalities and structural inspection domains. This approach enhances inspection accuracy and consistency and significantly improves safety by eliminating human exposure to hazardous environments. The methods presented demonstrate TinyML's broader applicability for autonomous inspection tasks in resource-constrained robotic systems.

title: A Predictor-like Controller for Linear Ito Stochastic Systems with Input Delays
authors: Hongxia Wang; Minyue Fu; Xiao Lu
abstract: Linear quadratic regulation (LQR) is very fundamental in modern control theory. The theory has been developing for several decades. However, a more general problem, the LQR problem for stochastic systems with multiple control channels and delays still remains outstanding. To better understand our idea, the paper focuses on dealing with the problem with two control channels and a delay, which is more difficult than the one with a single delayed control channel since the former actually encounters interaction of control channels besides the delay. A new value function is proposed, which is key for finding the predictor-like controller. The idea is also suitable for handling the LQR problem for Ito stochastic systems with multi-control-channel and multi-delay.

title: Detecting Polycystic Ovary Syndrome with Convolutional Neural Networks: Enhancements through Adversarial Training and Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM)
authors: Omar Faruq Shikdar; Ruba Sazeda; Sujana Islam; Ashraful Islam; Tanzia Haque; Arifa Sultana Mily
abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most common causes of infertility for women around the world. It is a metabolic and hormonal condition that affects women of reproductive age. It is vital to detect this problem as soon as possible. Among all the possible diagnostic imaging ultrasound is the safest option as it has no risk of radiation. This research aims to create a system that will detect PCOS from ultrasound images. A dataset containing 3840 images of 2 classes which are infected and non-infected has been used in the research. Using techniques such as resizing, rescaling, center cropping the dataset has been preprocessed. A feed forward model using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture with 8 layers has been deployed for that task. The dataset was split into train, validation and test set. After training the CNN model with training data, the model has been trained further using adversarial training through Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM). Hyper parameter tuning was done for optimal result. The highest accuracy achieved by the model is 99.07% for epsilon=1.6 (adversarial training). The model’s output prediction has been explained by using Gradient Weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). After 1000 iterations, the 99% confidence interval for the model is [0.985,0.996].

title: Research on a Strapdown Inertial Navigation Algorithm Based on Unmanned Driving
authors: Yuan Yue; Zongping Yang
abstract: Strapdown inertial navigation can be applied to intelligent connected vehicles due to its simple and small size, low cost, high short-term accuracy, and strong stability. The efficiency and reliability of its system depend on the calculation algorithm of strapdown inertial navigation. Therefore, this article designs a strapdown inertial navigation algorithm that uses MATLAB programming to calculate the navigation parameters of the carrier, such as attitude, velocity, and position. The dual sample algorithm is used to dynamically compensate for attitude and velocity. Based on vehicle test data and comparison of test results, it is concluded that the algorithm proposed in this article has certain theoretical significance and practical value.

title: Juzu Type Gripper That Can Change Both Shape and Firmness
authors: Shunya Hara; Osamu Fukuda; Mitsuru Higashimori
abstract: This paper presents a novel gripper capable of actively changing both shape and firmness. The gripper increases its grasp ability by changing its finger posture and firmness suitable for given target objects. In the proposed gripper, each finger is constructed by serially connecting multiple Juzu units. By controlling the angles between neighboring Juzu units individually using two actuators used for sending and bending, arbitrary finger shapes can be generated. In addition, by controlling the tension of the wire that penetrated all Juzu units in each finger, the friction between Juzu units is adjusted and the firmness of finger can be varied. A prototype gripper was designed and developed, and experiments to evaluate the capabilities of changing shape and firmness were conducted. Furthermore, through experiments of preshaping and grasping for various objects with different shape and size, the validity of the proposed method was demonstrated.

title: Proposal for the Design of an Educational Robot to Enhance Learning and Support Children with attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder from the Fifth Year of Age at Low Cost-Nubox
authors: Angie Luisa Herrera Poma; Alexander Carlos Mendoza Puris; José Alexis Del Aguila Ramos
abstract: This research work presents the design of an educational robot that enhances learning in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder at low cost. The design of the educational robot aims to support learning through structured and focused interaction with games and activities that improve attention and memory, this enhances and keeps children engaged with immediate and positive feedback, it also has a striking mechanical design for the user being the PLA material, as well as a Raspberry Pi 3 controller that controls the educational robot with great efficiency and with enough memory to store and carry out the purpose for which it was designed, also mention about the 7″ touch screen that improves the interaction with the user and the speakers that produce white noise for the improvement of attention. A mixed methodology between VDI 2206 and MIT was used to meet the proposed objectives. The results of this research will improve attention and memory with a pleasant and practical design, a stable structure, intuitive mechanism and electronic components suitable for children with mild ADHD.

title: Automatic classification of specification of ERP modifications documents
authors: Katarzyna Grobler-Debska; Bartlomiej Zak; Marcin Ciurla; Adam Domagala; Adam Czarnoleski; Jerzy Baranowski
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Producing ERP software modifications during implementation is one of the longest lasting and most expensive stages of implementation.Although methodologies for conducting implementation projects are constantly being refined due to changing customer demands or technology, there are no tools to support the automation of implementation work. The paper presents the results of the InfoConsulting research and development project related to development of an NLP solution for implementation documentation in order to significantly shorten work and costs by automatically searching for similar solutions in previous implementations.

title: Gearbox Fault Diagnosis Based on Local Domain Adaptation Network under Different Working Conditions
authors: Zhuang Ye; Mingyan Ma; Peilun Liu; Jianbo Shao; Jianbo Yu
abstract: Fault diagnosis is essential to ensure the reliability of the mechanical systems. However, the working conditions of mechanical systems are highly extreme and varying. This results in the significant domain shift between different domains. In this paper, a transfer learning method, named local domain adaptation network (LDANet) is proposed for fault classification. Firstly, a subdomain adaptation model is proposed to perform fault classification. Secondly, a local feature metric is adapted in LDANet to align the local features of two domains in the class level. Thirdly, a convolutional network-based generator is utilized to obtain common features and a fully connected layer-based generator is adopted to extract specific features. Finally, a gearbox fault diagnosis test is utilized to demonstrate the performance of LDANet. The comparison tests indicate that LDANet obtains the best fault diagnosis performance among other transfer learning methods.

title: Automated Non-Contact Vibration Measurement with Dynamic Vision: Framework and Signal Component Analysis
authors: Jie Xiong; Xiang Li; Yaguo Lei; Naipeng Li; Bin Yang; Wei Zhang
abstract: Vibration analysis is of great importance for condition monitoring of mechanical systems. Non-contact vibration measurement methods are generally more flexible for application. However, deployment calibration is usually complex and difficult in practice. To address such issues, we propose an automated non-contact vibration measurement framework with dynamic vision. By utilizing the event stream filtering method, a vibration signal reconstruction algorithm is proposed, which is implemented with a robot arm through feedback control. A quantitative evaluation method is established for evaluating the efficiency of vibration component analysis. Compared with the traditional contact vibration sensors through experimental validation, the proposed method demonstrates significant potential in analyzing machine vibrations and performing fault diagnosis. Through experimental validation on the pump test rig, it has been validated that the proposed framework is highly efficient and user-friendly. That shows promising application prospects in the real industrial scenarios.

title: Laser Weld Defect Detection Based on Laser Vision and Region Growth
authors: Dejian Li; Yajun Zhang; Jianing Xu; Zhibo Ding; Shaoli Li
abstract: In this paper, we propose a laser vision-based approach for detecting defects in steel laser welding. The Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) algorithm is combined with region growing to effectively segment point cloud data. This segmentation process leverages both local region features and the interrelationships among neighbouring points. Initially, the BVH algorithm is utilized to group the point cloud data, identifying optimal seed point locations for subsequent analysis. Subsequently, the region growing algorithm is applied, with the establishment of specific growth criteria to determine point inclusion within their respective regions. These defined growth criteria serve as guidance for expanding the regions from the initially selected seed points. This expansion process culminates in the derivation of segmentation results and facilitates the identification of defects. Importantly, this process eliminates the need for pre-emptive defect type confirmation or the conversion of 3D data into 2D data, as typically practiced in conventional point cloud processing. This enhancement significantly enhances detection efficiency. Experimental results underscore the effectiveness of this approach in overcoming potential interferences such as light source noise, leading to successful defect segmentation. At the same time, compared with other typical methods, our method takes the shortest time. Consequently, this method holds potential for detecting welding defects within industrial settings.

title: A Robot for Quickly Picking Clone Colony
authors: Longlong Huang; Zhenlin Jin; Wenliang Zhao; Wei Zhu; Kai He
abstract: The key of microbial breeding is how to quickly select the target colony from the mutant library. High-throughput clonal colony selection technology is to solve this problem. The selection of clonal colonies is a key link in biotechnology, and it is also a very heavy workload. The traditional picking method is manual, which has low efficiency and low precision. Compared with manual picking, the automatic screening and picking of colonies by robots can greatly improve the production efficiency and picking accuracy. In this paper, a robot is designed, which can quickly pick out cloned colonies. The robot can carry out picking, inoculation, cleaning, sterilization and drying at the same time. It uses servo motor and pneumatic drive mode, combined with machine vision to coordinate the colony positioning and the multi-axis motion control card controls the cooperative work of all parts of the robot, and equipped with a variety of sensors to assist the operation of the robot.

title: Active Power Filter Controller Applied to Quality Improvement of Periodic Loads
authors: Krzysztof Kołek
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The paper addresses the problem of improving the spectral characteristics of load currents of a periodic nature by the application of an Active Power Filter (APF). APF generates compensating current, which aims to compensate the asymmetry, reactive power and harmonics arising from nonlinear load currents. The equations of a system and the equation determining the duty cycle of the PWM waves controlling the APF transistors are presented. Because of its design, the compensating current generated by the APF has a limited rise time. At the same time, power electronics devices can change the load current significantly faster. A case arises in which rapid load changes are poorly compensated, lowering the spectral efficiency of the APF. The paper presents a method of reshaping the APF reference current, leading to an improvement in the response to the periodic impulse load changes.

title: Analysis of the decoupling control loop for a plant with input dynamics in the ADRC structure
authors: Patryk Bartkowiak; Dariusz Pazderski
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This study addresses the decoupling issue within the Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) framework, taking into account the existence of additional dynamics in the plant input path. These additional dynamics are not directly incorporated into the observer equations. The paper proposes a compensation strategy that employs a filter to shape the observer’s input signal. The transfer function forms for the structure under analysis, as well as the matching conditions in the input path, have been established. The findings indicate that while the use of an input filter can enhance the stability of the decoupling loop, it may also reduce the disturbance attenuation. The conclusions drawn from analytical studies and numerical simulations are validated by experimental results.

title: l1 PID Controller Synthesis via Delta Operator Approach
authors: Rui Li; Kairui Cao; Jinmei Xie; Hairui Du; Ming Zeng
abstract: This paper proposes a systematic way of designing PID controllers for discrete-time systems with l<inf>1</inf> performance. By using the system augmentation techniques, the PID control system is converted into a static output feedback (SOF) control system. Then, the SOF control system is represented in delta domain. A cone complementary Linearization (CCL) algorithm is presented to calculate the desired SOF controller, from which the PID controller can be recovered. Simulation examples are given to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Fixed-Time Tracking Control for Robotic Arm with Performance Constraints
authors: Li Pinwei; Dai Jiyang
abstract: The problem of fixed-time tracking control is investigated for single-link robotic arm using backstepping control strategy and Lyapunov stability theory, and the robot arm's output angle is constrained. The proposed control algorithm ensures that the system tracks to a given signal in a fixed time, and the tracking error converges in any small neighborhood near the origin, and the convergence time is independent of the initial states of the system. Finally, the effectiveness of the scheme is verified by a MATLAB simulation example.

title: Applying Inertia Matrix Decomposition to Determine Controller Gains for Marine Vehicles
authors: Przemyslaw Herman
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This work concerns an attempt to solve the problem of selecting controller gains based on decompositions of the inertia matrix. The results presented are limited to the task of trajectory tracking by fully actuated underwater vehicles. The proposed approach uses properties of Inertial Quasi-Velocities (IQV) known from the literature. The novelty is to show that by means of the examination of vehicle dynamics, it is possible to tune the controller described by classical variables and to show the effects of disturbances not adequately taken into account due to the displacement of the vehicle’s center of mass. An algorithm for conducting gain selection and simulation examples of its application to a 6 DOF underwater vehicle model are proposed.

title: A RNN Based Self-Learning Audio Generating Chatbot For French Language Learners
authors: Rifat Sarker Aoyon; Yamin Ara; Tahsin Anzum Baptee; Mehrin Afroz; Md Tanzim Reza
abstract: A chatbot is an artificial intelligence-based virtual conversational agent that is one of the most potential technologies in the modern era. There are so many sectors where chatbots are providing outstanding performance. This technology has the ability to be an assistant for those who are trying to learn a new language. That is why we have done research to make a chatbot based on an RNN algorithm in order to help people learn French. Although there are many online platforms available to learn French, many of these are not sufficient enough to learn a language as it is mandatory to have a conversational partner to practice a language. Without practicing a language with anyone, it is difficult for a person to keep memorizing a lot of vocabulary. French pronunciation rules are not the same as English. Therefore, we have added a feature for sending text along with audio messages and getting replies in French audio alongside text.
