Because of having these features, users will not only know the French vocabulary and grammatical rules but can also be introduced to French pronunciation systems and learn to speak French with a native French accent. The self-learning feature assists this chatbot to increase its capability of giving correct responses to the users day by day by having continuous conversations and removes the problem of collecting so much data to make this kind of chatbot. Also the paraphrasing feature will help users to get different replies to a particular question at different times, enriching their vocabulary and familiarizing them with the variety of replies to a particular question.

title: Research on a Hierarchical Optimal Control Algorithm
authors: Yuanmin Zhang; Zhu Jiang; Junfeng Lu
abstract: Based on information of the real-time OD matrix estimation and prediction, according to the distributed and hierarchy idea, a novel optimal control strategy on urban expressway is proposed. Firstly, the total traffic demands in a long time was predicted in advance, and the upper bound of the future queue length was made; Secondly, the future traffic state was predicted and the harmonious restrictions for each ramp were built based on global optimum in order to supply a criterion for ramp rate. The simulation results show that the control system is of good dynamic performance. It harmonizes the benefits of every ramp and optimizes the whole performance of the urban expressway network.

title: On the Optimal Location of Multiple Compressor Stations in Pipeline Networks Under Uncertainty
authors: Michael Schuster
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Compressor stations are essential in the transportation of gas through pipeline systems, ensuring that pressure levels remain within operational bounds over long distances. In this contribution, we analyze the optimal placement and number of compressor stations on gas pipeline networks. An optimization framework is introduced to determine the number and location of compressor stations that minimize the control cost. Existence results for optimal solutions are provided, the non-uniqueness of solutions is discussed, and numerical examples are presented.

title: Prospects of Algebraization of Deformable Exponential Functions Through Ordinary Differential Equations And Partial Differential Equations
authors: Iulia Clitan; Tiberiu Colosi; Mihaela Ligia Unguresan; Adrian Codoban; Mircea Cohut
abstract: Deformable exponential functions are used for solving concrete real problems in a variety of research areas. A previous part of this research focused on the utility of analogical modeling for certain categories of nonlinear propagation processes, using deformable exponential functions. This paper however, describes the prospects of algebraization of these deformable exponentials by means of ordinary differential equations and also by means of partial differential equations. Thus, expressing the deformable exponential functions as solutions of some categories of the derivative equations previously mentioned, customized for different deformable coefficient's values.

title: Intelligent Energy Management in Smart Grid using Heuristic Optimization Algorithm
authors: Govind Rai Goyal; Shelly Vadhera
abstract: Classical economic-emission dispatch considers only conventional generators. But the need of environment sustainability has promoted the penetration of renewable energy sources (RES). RES can help to provide clean energy at decreased generation cost. A major problem faced by generating plants is network reliability issues in power system arising from the peak hour's power demand. Application of demand side management (DSM) measures can help to ease the enormous peak hour's pressure in smart grid system. This paper presents a solution of peak hour's demand management with dynamic economic-emission dispatch (DEED). This paper provides a comparative analysis of the implications of deploying DSM strategies in smart grid system with/without integration of RES. The proposed system uses Grasshopper optimization algorithm to find the solutions. Optimal control of conventional generating units and energy storage system with application of DSM programs demonstrates the potential to diminish the peak overload and economic power dispatch with emission control.

title: High Precision Long Endurance Attitude Algorithm for Marine Control Based on MEMS Sensors
authors: Yanyan Pi; Yongbo Li; Zeyuan Feng
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: Currently, MEMS-based attitude systems are widely used in the field of UAVs. In the maritime field, most of the attitude systems are based on high-priced gyroscopes such as optical gyroscopes, flexible gyroscopes, etc. Aiming at the problem of attitude accuracy distortion under long- term drift and swing conditions that systems built based on MEMS components face, a high-precision long-endurance attitude algorithm is proposed. This algorithm considers the zero bias and random walk noise of the gyroscope, uses the variance of the measurement residual as a criterion to adaptively compensate for the impact of external acceleration. Combined with the lever arm compensation algorithm to compensate for the impact of rotation angular velocity on the acceleration reference information, it improves Attitude solution accuracy. This article used MEMS inertial elements and the domestically produced ARM building an attitude measurement system to verify the feasibility of the algorithm. The system’s static attitude accuracy, attitude repeatability, dynamic attitude accuracy and attitude accuracy in the eccentric state were verified basing on the turntable. Experimental results show that the static accuracy of the MEMS attitude system based on this algorithm is better than 0.01°, the attitude repeatability is better than 0.015°, and the attitude dynamic accuracy is better than 0.02°. In the case of eccentricity, the attitude accuracy of the system is improved by 3 times compared with before compensation.

title: AMR For Luggage Delivery Robot with Navigation Using Lidar and 3D Camera
authors: Ahmed Mohammed Ahmed Greynoon; Suresh Gobee; Djati Wibowo; Vinesh Thiruchelvam
abstract: This paper presents the development of Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) for hotel luggage delivery using ROS 2. A review of 14 research papers identifies key technologies and challenges in AMR implementation. LiDAR, 3D cameras, and a stable drive base are found essential for obstacle avoidance and load handling. Efficient processing is also crucial for real-time navigation. The study addresses limitations in LiDAR accuracy and ROS 2 control, proposing improvements such as sensor fusion, better user interfaces, and automated docking. This work supports the growing demand for automation and contactless service in hospitality environments.

title: Distributed Event-Triggered Nonconvex Optimization under Polyak-Łojasiewicz Condition
authors: Chao Gao; Lei Xu; Kunpeng Zhang; Yuzhe Li; Zhiwei Liu; Tao Yang
abstract: This paper considers the distributed nonconvex optimization problem, where the goal is to minimize the average of local nonconvex cost functions through local information exchange. Firstly, we propose a distributed optimization algorithm that integrates the gradient tracking method with a dynamic event-triggered communication scheme, thereby reducing communication overhead. Secondly, we demonstrate that the algorithm linearly converges to the global optimum under the Polyak-Łojasiewicz condition, which indicates that every stationary point is a global minimizer. The numerical experiment is presented to validate the theoretical results and confirm the algorithm's effectiveness.

title: A Novel Feature Emphasis Mechanism on Traffic Flow Prediction
authors: Jie Zhou; Wenqi Xie
abstract: Traffic flow prediction is a challenging application in temporal prediction, especially in a small amount of dataset. Recently, most of the studies are based on a large data set, which will lead the huge waste of resources and time. In the case of small data sets, some state-of-the-art models cannot achieve the desired results due to the large deficiency of features. In this work, the main idea is to use our proposed Feature Emphasis Mechanism (FEM) to augment, re-extract and emphasis the small amount features by using Linear-Emphasis (LE) and Conv-Emphasis (CE). To capture and emphasis features more effectively, we apply Bi-training to capture the parameters in model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Feature Emphasis Mechanism can be applied to classical models, and improves the prediction accuracy in small dataset background.

title: Experiment Investigation of Energy Harvester Based on Piezoelectric for Indoor Air Quality Sensor Node
authors: C. Bambang Dwi Kuncoro; Arvanida Feizal Permana; Maria Mahardini Sakanti; Muhammad Arman
abstract: Sensor nodes play a pivotal role in the Internet of Things by collecting data from the environment. The reliance on batteries for these nodes presents challenges in maintenance and replacement. To enhance energy efficiency and reduce operational costs, this study explores the potential of piezoelectric energy harvesters as an alternative power source for indoor air quality sensor nodes. The research involves the careful selection of piezoelectric elements, followed by measurements and performance analyses in various environmental conditions. Mechanical vibrations induced by ambient movements or machinery are harnessed to generate electrical energy. The experimental setup includes integrating piezoelectric elements onto the sensor node, exposing it to optimized conditions for energy harvesting. Initial tests vary frequencies and amplitudes to maximize energy conversion efficiency. Results indicate that piezoelectric energy harvester element placed in constant airflow of 5m/s can produce substantial power for 489-1819mV under suitable conditions, offering a promising solution to sensor node energy challenges. The generated power proves to be a viable solution for enhancing autonomy and reducing maintenance costs associated with sensor node operations.

title: Real-Time Object Detection and Grasping with an Autonomous Mobile Robot: A Case Study
authors: Heba Ragab; Salma Ali; Sama Fahmy; Mohamed Alkalla
abstract: This study presents an autonomous mobile robot with advanced grasping capabilities designed to perform two missions: Pick and Place and Hold and Run. The robot’s four-wheeled chassis ensures stability and maneuverability, while an articulated arm with a specialized gripper manipulates 8-cm-diameter balls. Utilizing YOLO algorithms for accurate object detection, the vision system offloads image processing to a laptop via Wi-Fi for real-time monitoring and decision. Extensive tests validated the robot’s consistent task execution, demonstrating dexterity and intelligent navigation. Challenges such as hardware integration and vision system optimization were innovatively addressed. The modular design allows for easy upgrades and adaptability, highlighting significant future potential. The proposed robot fulfilled the preset goals of picking any defined colored ball and placing them into a box autonomously. Besides, achieving the athletic runner task around the classroom interior. This project showcases the interdisciplinary nature of robotics, combining mechanical engineering, computer vision, and software development with potential applications in service robotics.

title: An Improved Monocular ORB-SLAM Using Scaled-Invariant Features
authors: Jingjing Fu; Ping Ma; Zhaohong Jia
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) is significant in unmanned systems. SLAM algorithms based on stereo cameras and RGB-D cameras have achieved relatively good results. However, monocular SLAM algorithms negatively affect mapping and localization due to the lack of sufficient scale information. In this paper, we employ a new scale-invariant feature to provide better scale invariance and adopt a consistency-based feature point equalization strategy. We conducted experiments on the TUM, EuRoC and KITTI datasets. In conclusion, this algorithm provides a practical and effective solution for feature extracting and matching in computer vision applications.

title: Modeling and Compensation of Hysteresis of Piezoelectric Actuators by Utilizing Asymmetric Play Operator
authors: Shengyu Shi; Xuancheng Huang; Zhiguang Liu; Xinyuan Lin
abstract: Piezoelectric ceramic actuators have been widely used for developing nano-positioning stages. However, their inherent hysteresis property remarkably hinders the positioning accuracy. The classical Prandtl-Ishlinskii model is effective for characterizing symmetric hysteresis loop, but real-world hysteresis is often asymmetric. To address this limitation, this paper presents an improved Prandtl-Ishlinskii model by employing asymmetric play operators, enabling the accurate characterization of the asymmetric hysteresis loop. Furthermore, play operators with unevenly spaced thresholds are introduced, replacing the traditionally evenly spaced ones, which allows for a more effective modeling, also, with higher accuracy. To compensate for the hysteresis property, the inverse of the improved Prandtl-Ishlinskii model is derived and applied as a feedforward compensator.

title: A geometric measurement system using a robot as handling system and reference system
authors: Kevin Blümel; Marco Gerlach; Alexander Winkler; Christian Thormann
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Collaborating robots are used at production processes to interact with workers and they don’t need separation by protective devices. These robots could be used for in-place geometric measurements through some adjustments. This paper deals with the advantages of highly accurate geometric measurements using a cobot, steps of adjustments are described and some first startup measurements are presented.

title: Inverter Fault Diagnosis based on GASF-Alexnet
authors: Xu Feng; Yu Liao; Bing Geng; Yuhang Hu; Yibo Cui; Kun Cui
abstract: To tackle the challenge of extracting fault features from Voltage Source Inverters (VSI) under dynamic conditions, this paper introduces a novel fault diagnosis method utilizing GASF-AlexNet. Initially, the Gramian Angular Field (GASF) transformation encodes time-series data into images, enhancing feature visualization and discriminability. Subsequently, an enhanced AlexNet deep learning architecture autonomously extracts critical fault features from these images. Moreover, this study employs an adaptive moment estimation (Adam) optimizer combined with a dynamic learning rate decay strategy to optimize the training process and enhance the model's diagnostic accuracy. Comparative analysis demonstrates that the proposed method exhibits superior fault identification performance and efficiency under various conditions compared to traditional techniques. Experimental results validate the effectiveness and superiority of this method in practical applications.

title: Fruit Recognition Using Color Statistics
authors: Qiang He; KangLi Xia; Hui Pan
abstract: Because of aging and very low birthrate, agricultural labor force has become seriously insufficient. In order to solve this problem, researchers have developed a series of agricultural robots for different purposes, including fruit picking robots. For fruit picking robots, detection and recognition of fruits is an important task. Here a fruit recognition technique based on the statistical characteristics of HSV color was developed. First, the RGB color fruit images were converted into HSV color. Then the hue distribution of HSV color of fruit is approximated with a Laplace distribution. Further, this Laplace distribution can be adopted as the characteristic description of this fruit. The fruit was segmented out of the input image. If the segmented fruit image falls in some Laplace distribution with 90% confidence interval, then input fruit belongs to this special fruit. In practice, the Mahalanobis distance (MD) corresponding to the 90% confidence interval of the Laplace distribution for each fruit class was set as the reference evaluation. If the input fruit data has a smaller Mahalanobis distance than the reference evaluation, the input belongs to this type fruit. The experimental results have shown the good performance for this fruit recognition technique on different kinds of fruits.

title: Research on Path Planning Simulation of Mobile Robot Based on ROS
authors: Mingtao Yao; Chenhao He; Jiawei Wang
abstract: For the problem of ROS robot path planning research, this paper is based on Ubuntu20.04-ROS-noetic system, using urdf, xacro to depict two-wheeled differential mobile robots, and a 3D indoor simulation environment has been established by the Gzaebo simulation platform in ROS. Then, the created 3D map was scanned using LIDAR sensors and a 2D grid map was constructed using SLAM package. Ultimately, the global path planning algorithms used A*, Dijkstra and RRT navigation algorithms, the local path planning algorithm used DWA algorithm. Based on the simulation study of various path planning algorithms for ROS mobile robots from the starting point to the target point, the map building results show that the 2D grid map effect is good, high accuracy, suitable for indoor small scenes and low-featured environment mapping, path planning algorithms can make the mobile robot to complete the autonomous navigation as well as obstacle avoidance tasks in the self-constructed raster maps, which has a certain significance for the research of the robot based on the path planning as well as the This is of some significance for the study of the path planning and the comparative understanding of navigation algorithms.

title: Development of Online Monitoring System for Mine Hoist Cage
authors: Yang Zhao; Yu Feng
abstract: The cage of mine hoist is an important device for personnel and vehicle transportation in vertical shaft hoisting system. In order to timely and accurately monitor the internal environment of the cage, miners' dynamics and cage working conditions, the online monitoring system of mine hoist cage based on ARM has been developed. The overall scheme of online monitoring system is proposed, which is composed of WIFI wireless communication network, upper computer monitoring platform, video monitoring platform, online monitoring system sub-station and generator power supply. The on-line monitoring system substation based on stm32f103zet6 microcontroller realizes the functions of cage working condition monitoring, historical data query, alarm threshold setting and threshold alarm. Finally, the wireless transmission base station, wet temperature sensor and encoder are tested by setting up a testbed. The experiment shows that the parameters meet the expected requirements, can provide support for the safe operation of the hoist cage.

title: Research on Control Strategy for Waist-assisted Exoskeleton
authors: Yangyang Li; Dingan Song; Jing Hu; Lin Li; Chao Guo; Jian Lv
abstract: In order to alleviate the muscle fatigue of industrial workers who undergo repeated, intensive waist motions, a waist-assisted exoskeleton control strategy is presented. Firstly, the assistance principle is introduced. Then, an overall control method for waist-assisted exoskeleton is proposed, in which the finite state machine algorithm is adopted to identify the human motion intention, and corresponding control strategies, where no assistance is provided in squatting state, a slightly smaller constant torque is given in maintaining state, a torque similar to the net joint torque curve is designed in the getting-up state, are put forward according to different needs in different phases of bending down to assist workers to lift up heavy objects, reduce muscle fatigue, and increase operation efficiency. The electromyogram test results showed that the exoskeleton can reduce the erector spinae muscle activity by a maximum of about 24.45%, and an average reduction of about 11.13%, showing a significant assistance effect.

title: Detail-Enhanced Attention Metric Convolutional Network for Anomaly Detection in Mobile Robotic Systems
authors: Yu Wang; Zhitao He; Yongyi Chen; Dan Zhang; Hui Zhang; Marek Jasinski
abstract: The reliability and safety of robots in various fields have emerged as critical research focal points. Anomaly detection is pivotal for sustaining the normal operation of mobile robots, enabling the timely identification and resolution of anomaly scenarios such as path deviations and sensor failures. Traditional methods often encounter limitations when confronted with largescale data and complex scenarios. This paper introduces a novel deep learning algorithm, i.e., Detail-Enhanced Attention Metric Convolutional Network (DMCN), designed for anomaly detection in mobile robotic systems. A dual-channel embedding module with shared weights is integrated into the DMCN, which automatically extracts and selects salient features from sensor data. The representation of time-series features is optimized, and the Squeeze-Enhanced Axial (SEA) attention mechanism is incorporated to efficiently capture global information and allocate adaptive attention to critical feature channels. The DMCN's effectiveness is validated through experiments using real sensor data of mobile robots, demonstrating its superiority over other methods in terms of detection accuracy.

title: A Study of Multi-Beam Bathymetric Based on Geometric Intuition and Optimization Algorithms
authors: Jiaqi Xu; Junyu Chen; Mengyang Sun; Tao Liu
abstract: Multi-beam survey technology breaks through the limitations of traditional survey technology and greatly improves the accuracy of seabed topographic survey, resolution and work efficiency, realizing a revolutionary breakthrough in the history of bathymetric technology. This paper firstly uses the geometric intuitive method, applying similar triangles, sine and cosine theorems and other tools to calculate the depth of seawater, and the coverage width of the two indicators. For the overlap rate, we give the exact definition of the formula for the seabed slope and calculate it. And then, the relationship between the original slope and the changed slope is found by looking for geometric relationships between slopes. We proceeded to improve the model in Phase 1 under this condition so as to obtain the formula for the relevant index. At last, we consider a rectangular sea area, and carry out the survey line design under the condition of guaranteeing the maximum overlap rate (i.e., ensuring that the survey line can cover all the sea area). We first determine the preliminary wiring when the ship sails from south to north, and then calculate the total length of the line at different angles by changing the angle between the line and the projection of the normal vector of the seabed slope in the horizontal plane, and finally get the final line design results.

title: Zero-sum differential game-based fault tolerant control of 3-DOF model helicopter systems
authors: Chencheng Zhang; Bin Jiang; Hao Yang; Ningbo Li; Qingkai Meng
abstract: This paper presents a pioneering study that simultaneously addresses the optimal tracking and fault-tolerant control problems for a 3-DOF model helicopter system. Leveraging an optimal FTC approach inspired by zero-sum differential game theory, we explore the intricate dynamics of helicopter systems under both system and actuator faults. Unlike previous work on fault-tolerant control, our study considers the controller and composite faults as adversarial players with "intelligent" strategies in a differential game setting. This novel perspective results in the coupled solutions for the optimal fault-tolerant controller and the worst-case composite faults, posing significant analytical challenges. This work provides a foundation for the optimal design of controllers that achieve desired flight performance even in the presence of nonlinear faults, thereby advancing the robustness and reliability of helicopter systems in operational environments.

title: Continuously Estimate and Control Prosthetic Grip Force by an Optical Waveguide Sensor
authors: Linhang Ju; Hanze Jia; Yanjun Shi; Xilun Ding; Yanggang Feng; Wuxiang Zhang
abstract: The emergence of intelligent prostheses has facilitated the life and work of disabled patients. The interaction aspect of prostheses has become a highlight research topic in the field of rehabilitation robotics. However, most of the existing prosthetic interaction methods focus on the use of myoelectricity to classify finite gestures, rather than continuous (infinite) force detection, which greatly limits the use of prosthetic scenarios. In this study, a novel optical waveguide sensor was used to collect muscle deformation information from the human arm for continuous control of the prosthetic grip force. The optical waveguide sensor was embedded with carbon fiber to limit the stretching of the waveguide, which led to the optical waveguide sensor being sensitive to bending deformation. Compared with EMGs, the accuracy of continuous grip force control based on the optical waveguide sensor is higher. The R-Square for prosthetic grip force and hand grip force were 0.867 and 0.9724 in the periodic and sustaining grip force experiments, respectively. The results suggested that the proposed method could provide a new approach to the interaction of prostheses.

title: IA*QB: An Efficient Trajectory Planning Approach for the Automatic Berthing of Unmanned Surface Vessel
authors: Shouzheng Yuan; Zhilin Liu; Yuxin Sun; Simeng Song; Zhongxin Wang
abstract: Trajectory planning plays an important role in the automatic berthing of Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV). This study proposes IA*QB approach for the USV's berthing trajectory planning in the harbor. First, a global path is obtained by the A * algorithm. Considering the path generated by the traditional A * algorithm is unsuitable for the USV to track at the corners, quasi B-spline is employed to smooth the path. Subsequently, path points with approximately equal spacing are selected as waypoints in the trajectory. Furthermore, the quadratic interpolation method is proposed at the end of the berthing trajectory. Thus, the USV's velocity can be decreased to zero linearly. Simulation results show the effectiveness and the superiority of the proposed approach.

title: Research on calibration method of magnetic gradient tensor tracking system based on magnet
authors: Guang Zhang; Qingbo Wang; Baisen Yang; Yue Gao; Silin Li
abstract: In the magnetic gradient tensor tracking system there are errors among single triaxial magnetometer and misalignment errors of coordinate systems of triaxial magnetometers. In the conventional calibration methods the homogeneous magnetic environment should be known beforehand, but the homogeneous magnetic environment is not easy to be built. Thus, a calibration method in the nonhomogeneous field is proposed in this paper. Firstly, we measure the nonhomogeneous environmental field using the magnetic gradient tensor system and then put a magnet at the known position. We record the increased magnetic field value of each sensor, and establish the nonlinearity equations about error parameters for single sensor and magnetic moment of magnet. Through changing the magnet position, we can obtain the adequate nonlinearity equations. By solving the nonlinearity equations, the error parameters can be got. According to the component values of magnetic moment of magnet in the coordinate systems of different triaxial sensors, we can get the attitude rotation angles relative to the reference coordinate system. By simulation experiment, it is proved that the calibration method can decrease the error very well in magnetic gradient tensor tracking system.

title: Research on Path Tracking of Wheeled Mobile Robot Based on Adaptive Sampling Time MPC
authors: Suna Zhao; Peijun Han; Jie Zhang; Taishan Lou
abstract: This paper proposes an improved adaptive sampling time adjustment model predictive control (AST-MPC) method to improve the path-tracking performance of a wheeled mobile robot (WMR). Considering the nonholonomic constraints in the motion control of WMR, the change of angular velocity during movement is continuously monitored, and the sampling time in the prediction interval is dynamically adjusted to reduce the inherent tracking error of the traditional MPC algorithm. Firstly, the MPC controller is designed to increase the speed change rate based on the traditional model. Then, the real-time optimization is carried out based on the adaptive sampling time. Finally, the tracking performance of WMR is tested in ROS to verify the feasibility of AST-MPC, and the influence of adaptive variable sampling time on the path tracking accuracy is analyzed. The experimental results show that the AST-MPC can dynamically respond to various terrains and challenging, complex trajectories when facing curved paths.

title: Research on MPPT with Improved Perturb-observe Method
authors: Shengli Fang; Long Wang; Chao Zeng; Peng Li; Xiangping He; Chunyan Ma
abstract: Since the output of photovoltaic cell changes with the light intensity and temperature of the environment, and the properties has a typical characteristic of nonlinearity, the maximum power point of the photovoltaic module must be tracked to improve the efficiency of photovoltaic power generation. The output characteristic of photovoltaic cell was analyzed at first in the paper, then the perturb-observe method was improved by introducing the fuzzy control, and impedance matching optimization is realized by the PI closed-loop control Boost circuit. Finally, simulation models of the relevant control algorithm were built in Matlab, and the result showed that the ameliorated control algorithm possesses higher speed and accuracy in MPPT by simulation analysis and contrast, so it improved the photovoltaic efficiency of electricity generation.

title: Intelligent Fire Surveillance: A Deep Learning Framework for Accurate Indoor Fire Detection
authors: Md. Maruf; Bishow Jit Paul; Labanya Talukder; Mahmuda Islam
abstract: Fire is a naturally occurring but destructive phenomenon capable of causing extensive property damage and loss of life. Early detection is crucial for mitigating fire hazards, as it helps prevent the spread of fire, saves lives, and min-imizes infrastructure damage. Traditional fire detection often face challenges including low sensitivity, difficulties in large-scale deployment, high false alarm rates, and detection delays. This research presents an innovative fire detection system that integrates a Deep Learning model framework to monitor, detect, and warn about fires in indoor environments like buildings, rooms, and restaurants.The framework utilizes a pre-existing Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), specifically leveraging the VGG16 model, as the basis for its Deep Learning architecture. Through transfer learning, we develop a FireNET architecture specifically designed for fire detection tasks with an accuracy of 99.50%. This integration of Deep Learning in fire detection provides real-time detection with high speed and accuracy and effectively overcoming the limitations of traditional fire detection sensors.

title: An Accurate Online Circular Hole Measurement Method Based on Multi-Camera
authors: Fangyuan Wang; Renbo Xia; Jibin Zhao; Tao Zhang; Liang Zhao; Tianyu Zhang
abstract: In the production of industrial parts, the precise measurement of circular features is critical, as circular holes often serve as reference points for positioning and installation. Achieving high-precision measurement of circular features poses significant challenges due to the complexity of surface characteristics and the demands for real-time processing in industrial environments. This paper proposes a high-precision and fast measurement method for circular objects using a multi-camera system. Specifically, an ellipse center matching algorithm based on epipolar geometry is used to achieve robust center matching. Then the center coordinates of circular objects are then obtained, serving as prior knowledge for determining the object's radius and the plane's normal vector. A closed-form solution for the circular objects is derived, and an extension of bundle adjustment(BA) algorithm using ellipse as primitives is proposed to refine the information of circular objects. Finally, extensive experiments demonstrate that our method can achieve high accuracy, whose standard deviation is 0.175mm, robustness in complex industrial environment and fast runtime.

title: Model-Based Control of Automatic Excavator Using Kinematic Models of Operation Part
authors: Giseo Park; Pilsoo Jeon; Kyoungkwan Ahn
abstract: Automatic excavators, which do not require direct operator intervention, have great advantages in terms of operator convenience and work efficiency, and are receiving a lot of attention. In order to improve the automatic work performance of an excavator, precise motion control of the upper operation part of the automatic excavator is essential. To do this, a model-based control algorithm for an automatic excavator, which is accompanied by a kinematic modeling process of the operation part, is newly designed in this paper. Based on sophisticated simulation, the characteristics of the proposed control algorithm are evaluated by comparing it with the existing proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller.

title: Dual-Discriminator GAN with Channel Attention for Underwater Image Super-Resolution
authors: Jiaxi Li; Haiyan Xie; Wei Li
abstract: Underwater image super-resolution (SR) technol-ogy is of great significance for marine resource exploration and ecological monitoring. Current methods exhibit limitations when processing low-resolution images degraded by complex underwater factors including light scattering and chromatic absorption. To address issues like texture blurring and color distortion in underwater images, we present CA-SRDDWGAN - an enhanced dual-discriminator GAN architecture incorporating channel attention modules into the SRDDWGAN-LP framework. The proposed model is applied to the underwater image dataset UIEB to improve degradation characteristics in underwater scenes. Experimental results show that the improved model achieves a 2.05% increase in PSNR (peak signal-to-noise ratio) and a 3.98 % improvement in SSIM (structural similarity index) on the UIEB dataset, providing valuable insights for mitigating color distortion and texture blurring in underwater images.

title: Design of a Microforce Sensing Gripper for Micro/Nano Manipulation Based on Optical Fiber Sensing
authors: Haoyan Zang; Xianmin Zhang
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: In the micro/nano manipulation system, grippers with high precesion force feedback is of great importance for the precise manipulation of small samples, especially those fragile ones such as cell. This paper proposes a microgripper with high precision force feedback, which is composed of two microforce sensors and a stick-slip platform. The sensors are all based based on silicon cantilever beams and used single-mode optical fibers with fiber Bragg gratings as the sensing elements. Factors affecting the maximum reflectance as well as the maximum reflected wavelength are all analyzed theoretically. The force feedback accuracy of the gripper is also tested. The designed gripper can realize the force feedback with 5 µN precision. The experimental results of clampping of a zebrafish embryo shows that the designed gripper can realize the real-time force sensing of micro-Newton force.

title: MPI Planar Correction of Pulse Based ToF Cameras
authors: Marian-Leontin Pop; Levente Tamas
abstract: Time-of-Flight (ToF) cameras are becoming popular in a wide span of areas ranging from consumer-grade electronic devices to safety-critical industrial robots. This is mainly due to their high frame rate, relative good precision and the lowered costs. Although ToF cameras are in continuous development, especially pulse-based variants, they still face different problems, including spurious noise over the points or multipath inference (MPI). The latter can cause deformed surfaces to manifest themselves on curved surfaces instead of planar ones, making standard spatial data preprocessing, such as plane extraction, difficult. In this paper, we focus on the MPI reduction problem using Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN) which allow the mitigation of this type of artifact for pulse-based ToF cameras. With our end-to-end network, we managed to attenuate the MPI effect on planar surfaces using a learning-based method on real ToF data. Both the custom dataset used for our model training as well as the code is available on the author’s Github homepage.

title: Switching of Assist Motion by Voice Recognition for Exoskeleton That Supports Lifting and Walking
authors: Chiharu Ishii; Takahiro Yamashita
abstract: In our previous study, an exoskeleton that can be used for both lifting assistance and walking assistance was developed, in which motions of the wearer's hip joint are assisted by motor actuation. In this study, in order to make the exoskeleton highly practical, a control system that allows the user to switch lifting assistance or walking assistance through voice recognition was developed. In addition, since workers in transportation work carry objects of various weights, a control strategy of walking assistance which allows the user to choose one of three walking speeds (fast, normal and slow) in accordance with the weight of the object to carry, was proposed. To verify an effectiveness of the developed control system for the exoskeleton, experiments of lifting and carrying a heavy object were carried out under the conditions of not wearing the exoskeleton and wearing the exoskeleton. Then, the assist effect was evaluated by expired gas analysis. As a result of the experiments, the assist effect of the developed exoskeleton was confirmed. To verify a usefulness of the proposed control strategy of walking assistance with variable walking speed, experiments of lifting and carrying heavy objects were carried out under the conditions of changing the weight of heavy object and the walking speed. Then, mental workload of subjects was calculated from CSTLX (card-sort TLX) and compared. As a result of the experiments, the usefulness of the proposed control strategy of walking assistance with variable walking speed was confirmed.

title: Design and Analysis of an Flapping Wing Robot
authors: Wei Sun; Shujian Liu; Yunfei Liu; Weijun Wang; Feng Shi; Jiawen Yang
abstract: The mechanism design of flapping wing robot with planar flexible wing is studied. This paper introduces a space four-bar mechanism to realize the flapping movement of wings, and focuses on the design of the robot system. According to the transmission ratio, motor and wings, the prototype of flapping wing robot is made. Some flight experiments show that the proposed transmission mechanism and optimization method are feasible.

title: Research on Multi-depth-of-field Electronic Image Stabilization Algorithm for In-Vehicle Videos
authors: Xuewen Qiu; Huawei Liang; Jie Wang; Junsen Jing
abstract: The vehicle-mounted cameras provide video streaming information for the post-processing phase of the intelligent vehicle, such as control and decision making. According to the characteristics of in-vehicle videos, this paper studies a video stabilization algorithm considering different depths of field. On the motion estimation stage, for the problem of inaccurate estimation inter-frame motion vectors caused by different depths of field of feature points, this paper proposes a method to repair inter-frame motion vectors. The method can correct the feature point position of the current frame and improve the estimation accuracy of the global motion vector. In the motion smoothing phase, a real-time online optimization framework and adaptive weights are used to balance the relationship between motion smoothing and motion following. Experiments prove that the accuracy of motion estimation of the algorithm in this paper is better than other improved algorithm, and the average value of PSNR after video stabilization is increased by more than 3dB compared with the original videos.

title: Method of Eliminating Reflection Interference for Image Recognition in Autonomous Driving
authors: Qu Bo; Feng Yan; Pan Ruizhi; Zhao Fengzhi; Wang Xurui; Yan Xiyan
abstract: In the field of automatic driving and visual detection, it is easy to be disturbed by the reflective light and the mirror surface of the reflective images. To overcome it, this paper proposes a mirror recognition model using EfficientNetV2 Medium as the backbone module. And we have utilized parallel convolutional layers and a lightweight convolutional attention module based on guided convolutional neural networks to capture low-level and high-level features for edge detection. The research results indicate that the model has better recognition accuracy, recall and F1 value, and the accuracy of 0.8331, maximum recall of 0.8366 and maximum F1 value in the test set are 0.8211. The research results provide a theoretical method for eliminating mirror image interference, which can be applied to autonomous driving and assisted safe driving.

title: Digital Twin for Feeding; Conveying; Rejecting and Assembly of Caps Using FESTO Meclab Modules
authors: Ariel Gutierrez-Calderón; Fabian Terrones-Zelada; Sergio Aranda-Egusquiza
abstract: Digital twins (DT) are virtual replicas of physical systems that enable real-time simulation, monitoring, and optimization, enhancing accuracy, efficiency, and decision-making. However, accessibility to digital technologies poses a challenge to their implementation. This work develops a DT for a process involving the feeding, transportation, rejecting, and assembly of metal and plastic caps using FESTO MecLab modules. The modules are modeled in 3D using Inventor. Communication between the physical asset and the virtual asset via OPC DA is managed through FluidSIM. The process logic is implemented in CoDeSys, and the DT is developed in MATLAB, following the guidelines of the Digital Twin Consortium (DTC). The control architecture, based on the ISA 95 standard, is evaluated using the Industrie 4.0 Toolbox from the Association of German Mechanical and Plant Engineering (VDMA, by its German acronym).

title: Design and Construction of a Dynamic Equipment for Diagnosis of Electronic Ignition Devices of Internal Combustion Engines
authors: A Santos Arias; F Acuña Albites; J Flores Limaylla; A Calcina Sotelo
abstract: The purpose of this study was to design and build a dynamic equipment for the diagnosis of electronic spark ignition devices in internal combustion engines. To achieve this, a module was developed specifically designed to carry out tests and diagnose the operational status of the electronic ignition system in vehicles of various brands. Likewise, a study was carried out to select appropriate materials for the construction of the equipment, including a detailed analysis of each component of the power transmission. Studies were carried out both on the structural part to guarantee the integrity of the user and on the power transmission of the dynamic engine and the electronic ignition components. These studies allowed the identification and diagnosis of possible failures in said components.

title: Energy optimal UAV path planning for full area coverage: A Review
authors: Quan Nguyen; Loulin Huang; Achala Perera
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly utilised for infrastructure inspections, and search and rescue missions. These missions often are a remote area and requires UAVs to cover extensive areas with limited onboard power supplies, making energy-optimal path planning crucial. This paper reviews the current challenges in UAV path planning and underscores the need of integrating both point-to-point and coverage path planning strategies, specifically for missions that require a UAV to travel from a depot to a region of interest (ROI), then conducting a coverage mission, and returning under stringent energy constraints. Additionally, this paper addresses the significant impact of real-world environmental factors, such as wind on path planning. Our findings highlight the need for a more holistic approach to UAV path planning to optimize both mission effectiveness and energy efficiency.

title: CNN Structure Optimization Based on MI-EEG Channel Information Density
authors: Kai Xi; Peng Ling; Peng Chen
abstract: This paper proposes a method to effectively extract Motor Imagery Electroencephalography (MI-EEG) features and optimize a convolutional neural network (CNN) model for classification accuracy improvement. In this paper, 10 subjects were enrolled to collect the data of the motor imagery experiment with left-hand and right-hand holding. After data pre-processing, the information density of MI-EEG signals was determined according to the Phase Locking Value (PLV), and 20 channels with high information density were retained. The EEG after channel screening was used as the input signal of CNN. And according to the characteristics of the input data, the CNN network structure and parameters were optimised. The results show that the average classification accuracy of MI-EEG signals of 10 subjects is improved from 86.29% to 90.46% by using the optimised CNN classifier, and the accuracy of the optimised CNN classifier is also improved compared with EEGNet. The results confirm the significant effectiveness of the proposed method on improving the classification accuracy of MI-EEG signals.

title: Design and Simulation of a Novel Humanoid Robotic Arm
authors: Yuhang Hu; Chanchan Xu; Yucheng Wang; Xiaojie Wang
abstract: This paper introduces a novel robotic arm that achieves remote driving of each joint through a specialized transmission design, enabling motors and other drive components to be mounted on the base. This reduces the ineffective load on the robotic arm and improves its motion performance. The arm comprises a base, shoulder joint, elbow joint, wrist joint, and hand. The shoulder and wrist joints utilize 3-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) 3 Revolute-Revolute-Revolute (3-RRR) spherical parallel mechanisms, connected by a 1-DOF elbow joint, resulting in a total of 7 degrees of freedom. This paper discusses forward and inverse kinematic analysis, and simulation validation of the robotic arm, ultimately demonstrating its human-like motion capabilities and performance.

title: Design; Development and Implementation of an Effective and Efficient Emergency Third Rail Fishplate Joint Clamp
authors: Shawn Jun Jie Pang; Andrew Keong Ng
abstract: A third rail joint is an indispensable asset ensuring electrical continuity and third rail alignment in a railway network. When a faulty third rail joint issue is reported during train revenue service, track maintenance staff will implement an interim solution to address it. However, considerable time and effort are often spent on the emergency recovery process. This paper, therefore, aims to design, develop, and implement an Emergency Third Rail Fishplate Joint Clamp (ETJC) that can effectively and efficiently overcome faulty third rail joint issues, while minimizing operational costs. ETJC design, modeling, and simulation were performed using Creo Parametric and Ansys software packages. A static structural analysis of ETJC was conducted. Materials for manufacturing ETJC were carefully selected to withstand any loading and environmental conditions that may occur on the ground. The ETJC was implemented in a train depot track and evaluated via hammer impact tests. Acceleration signals were acquired and analyzed at different locations on the third rail joint with ETJC. Results from simulation and field experiments are consistent and promising, thereby implying that the ETJC can firmly support and align a defective third rail joint.

title: Ynet: Deep learning model-based detection of insulators and self-detonation defects
authors: Long Yujiang; Wang Ce; Su Haibin; Gan Rundong; Liu Bin
abstract: Insulators are important components of transmission lines, and insulator defects increase the risk of fault outages on transmission lines; therefore, early discrimination of insulator defect conditions is important. In this paper, we propose a Ynet model based on the YOLO framework to determine the insulator defect condition. Based on the SFID dataset, we let the Ynet model be trained on fogged, fog-free and data augmented datasets to finally obtain the diagnostic model. The backbone of the Ynet model can effectively extract the features of the images. The Neck module merges the image features and forms a new feature matrix by up-sampling and jump concatenation of features. The final prediction results are output through the convolution layer. the Ynet model achieves 0.8797, 0.9943, 0.9918 and 0.825 for accuracy, precision, recall and mAP respectively for testing unknown images on the SFID dataset. its test results proved that the Ynet model can effectively diagnose insulator defect problems.

title: Bearing Fault Diagnosis with Multi-source Information Fusion and Deep Transfer Learning
authors: Shikai Lu; Jun Fei; Bin Nie; Qilei Zhou; Yi Le; Ruixue Li; Guohong Lai; Yu Liao
abstract: In the fault diagnosis of bearings in hydropower station units, the information provided by a single sensor is limited, and the dynamic characteristics of the operating conditions vary under different load conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a bearing fault diagnosis method that integrates multi-source information with deep transfer learning. Firstly, multi-scale features of the input signals are extracted through a fusion convolution module to ensure the completeness and effectiveness of fault information. Subsequently, channel attention and spatial attention mechanisms are used to retain effective information with minimal data, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of information fusion. Finally, the fault diagnosis method based on transfer learning effectively copes with detection under different loads. To more comprehensively mine and utilize the hidden features in fault signals, this paper combines vibration and temperature signals to build a bearing fault diagnosis experimental platform, collecting vibration and temperature signals at different speeds to generate a dual-channel dataset. Compared to common domain adaptation methods such as deep correlation alignment and domain adversarial neural networks, the proposed model's fault diagnosis performance under different working conditions is validated. Experimental results show that the proposed multi-source information fusion method performs with higher diagnostic accuracy both under the same and varying working conditions, significantly outperforming traditional methods.

title: Design and characterization of a low mechanical loss; high-resolution wearable strain gauge
authors: Addison Liu; Seun Araromi; Conor J. Walsh; Robert J. Wood
abstract: Soft, wearable systems hold promise for a wide variety of new or enhanced applications in the realm of human-computer interaction, physiological monitoring, wear-able robotics, and a host of other human-centric devices. Soft sensor systems have been developed concurrently in order to allow these wearable systems to respond intelligently with their surroundings. A recently reported sensing mechanism based on the strain-mediated contact in anisotropically resistive structures (SCARS) is an attractive solution due to its high sensing resolution, low-profile nature, and high mechanical resilience. Furthermore, the resistance-based output provides a simple electronic readout, facilitating its use in a wide variety of applications. However, previous iterations of the sensing mech-anism have exhibited stress relaxation and hysteretic behaviors that limit the scope of its use. Here, we report an iteration of the SCARS mechanism that uses silicone-based materials with low mechanical loss in order to improve the sensor signal stability and bandwidth. A new fabrication approach is developed which permits the incorporation of a liquid elastomer adhesive layer while also preserving the SCARS sensing functionality. The silicone-based SCARS sensors exhibited fast stress relaxation response (< 1 s) and reduced cyclic drift properties by more than half that of previously reported designs. A physiological monitoring demonstration is presented, validating that the new sensor design is mechanically resilient to such applications and has potential for use in real-world wearable use cases.

title: A Dynamic Control System for Robotic Goalkeeping Using YOLOv9 and Path Planning
authors: Wenyu Luo; MengCheng Lau
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a control system for a wheel-legged robot to function as a soccer goalkeeper. The proposed solution leverages a re-tuned, task-specific tiny YOLOv9 model to achieve a realtime balance between detection accuracy and speed. Using a depth camera, the system estimates the 3D position of a fastmoving soccer ball, while a two-phase path planning algorithm guides the robot to the optimal intercept point. To further enhance performance, the method mitigates noise interference during interception. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, showcasing the synergy between deep learning techniques and classical control methods for dynamic and real-time robotic tasks.

title: Segmentation and Shape Estimation of Multiple Deformed Cloths Using a CNN-Based Landmark Detector and Clustering
authors: Daiki Sonegawa; Koichi Ogawara
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for segmentation and shape estimation of multiple deformed cloths stacked on a floor from an image using a CNN-based landmark detector and clustering. The proposed method first estimates landmark positions from the heatmaps generated from the landmark detector and then clusters them using their attributes also given from the landmark detector. The contributions of the proposed method are twofold: (1) it can perform segmentation and shape estimation of multiple cloths of the same type or different types simultaneously by modeling a cloth as a grid of landmarks and estimating their positions and attributes, (2) it can correctly segment severely occluded or seemingly disjointed cloths by estimating and classifying landmark attributes including grid index, cloth position, cloth orientation, and cloth type. We evaluate the proposed method on both synthetic and real image datasets and show that the proposed method outperforms three baseline methods. We also show that the proposed method enables our humanoid robot to pick up the desired type of cloth from a pile of cloths.

title: Hook-Shaped Bending and S-Shaped Bending of Soft Robotic Arm
authors: Li Xiaohui; Zhao Liping; Zhang Wei
abstract: Soft robotic arm is an emerging research field. It has an extensive application prospect because of its soft body and theoretically infinite degrees of freedom. However, the general soft robotic arm of pneumatic actuator only researched arc-shaped bending. It limits the application environment of the soft robotic arm. A new structure of soft robotic arm is presented in this paper. The entire soft robot arm was designed as a cylinder with two drive cavity segments. The section of each cavity segment was designed as two chambers. The soft robotic arm of this structure can achieve hook-shaped bending and S-shaped bending. It is verified by simulation that the soft robotic arm of this structure can bend after through a slit and it also can operate across obstacles. These three bending structures expand the range of applications of a soft robotic arm and qualify it to operate in a complex and hostile environment.

title: An Improved Rapidly-exploring Random Tree Star Algorithm for Manipulator Path Planning
authors: Cong Yao; Yunhong Xin; Yuming Ning; Wenqian Du
abstract: The rapidly-exploring random tree star (RRT*), which is a variant of the rapidly-exploring random tree (RRT), has been used in the path planning of robots and gained good practicability during the last decade. However, because the algorithm parameters are fixed in the whole process of path planning, the RRT* is inefficient for the complex environment. For addressing this problem, this paper proposes two schemes to improve the efficiency of robot path planning by dynamically adjusting the parameters of RRT*. First, the dynamic incremental distance scheme (DID) is proposed to promote the flexibility to avoid obstacles by adjusting the incremental distance of RRT* according to the obstacle density of environment. Then, in order to guarantee the RRT* is not trapped in the local minima and covers the unexplored areas quickly, the subregion sampling scheme based on Gaussian distribution (SSG) is presented. Based on the proposed schemes, the improved RRT* can rapidly explore a valid path by reducing the number of iterations. Finally, a series of experiments based on the various complex 2D environments and a 7-DOF manipulator in complex environments are adopted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the improved RRT*. The results show that the improved RRT* can significantly improve the efficiency of manipulator path planning without increasing the path distance.

title: Analysis of the Asteroid Sampling Process Performed by Free-Floating Space Robot
authors: Long Zhang; Shuquan Wang
abstract: This paper provides a detailed analysis of the asteroid sampling process performed by free-floating space robot. Firstly, the inverse dynamics model and the direct dynamics model of free-floating space robot are established by the Newton-Euler method and the Lagrange method respectively. Secondly, the continuous contact dynamics model is established, and the calculation flow of the entire contact process of the space robot is given. Finally, taking the asteroid sampling task performed by a 3-degree-of-freedom free-floating space robot as an example, the detailed analysis of the contact process is carried out. The method described in this paper is of great significance to the design of sampling robot and the assessment of contact risk.

title: 2023 8th International Conference on Robotics and Automation Engineering Quantifying the Performance of Deep Neural Networks in Predicting Curvature and Force Output Response of a Pneumatic Soft Actuator
authors: Ememobong N. Livinus; Maria Elena Giannaccini; Andrew Starkey; Sumeet S. Aphale
abstract: Soft robotics promises new opportunities for solving problems that were limited by rigid robots due to their compliant physical structure. Pneumatic Soft Actuators (PSA) are a class of soft robots that have gained popularity due to their cost-effective manufacturing and high force-generating capability. Due to their highly nonlinear dynamics, accurate prediction of their response to input pressure (curvature) as well as force output is challenging. Artificial Neural Networks were employed to this effect. This work shows a comparative analysis of three variants of the recurrent neural network used in this paper for predicting the behavior of soft robotic actuators. Each network was trained using the same data set to predict the position, curvature, and applied force by the soft robotics on an external force. The result shows the different performance of the three models, evaluating them using Mean Square Error (MSE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). The Long Short-term Memory (LSTM) model outperformed both the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) models, producing the lowest error in the three metrics.

title: Shape Optimization for Inverse Problems Solution. Gradient Flow Dynamic System
authors: Jan Sokolowski; Yixin Tan
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This work investigates an interface problem involving two subdomains, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega^{+}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega^{-}$</tex>, governed by Poisson equations with distinct diffusion coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_{1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_{2}$</tex>. To address the complexity introduced by the heterogeneous material properties and boundary conditions, the problem is decomposed into two auxiliary subproblems: a Dirichlet problem and a Neumann problem, solved by functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$w$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v$</tex>, respectively. The full solution is expressed as the superposition of these two components. To evaluate the optimality of the interface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex>, the Kohn-Vogelius energy functional is introduced, measuring the discrepancy between the gradients of the Dirichlet and Neumann solutions. The shape derivative of this functional is derived, enabling the formulation of a geometric gradient flow model for the evolution of the interface. A regularization term, consisting of elastic (curvature-based) energy and perimeter, is included to promote smoothness and stability of the interface evolution. Under radial symmetry assumptions, the problem is further reduced to a one-dimensional model where the interface is characterized by a time-dependent radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R(t)$</tex>. An explicit ordinary differential equation governing the evolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> is obtained, incorporating both the mismatch energy and geometric regularization. Numerical experiments are conducted using the fourth-order Runge-Kutta method for various initial radii and regularization parameters <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex>. The results demonstrate that, regardless of whether the initial radius is larger or smaller than the optimal value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{*}=1.0$</tex>, the unregularized gradient flow (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon=0$</tex>) leads to convergence toward the optimal configuration. Regularized flows exhibit modified trajectories and slower convergence but ultimately preserve the correct limiting behavior. These results confirm the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed theoretical and numerical framework for shape optimization via geometric flows.

title: Indoor Following Model Based on TDOA Positioning and Q-Learning Algorithm
authors: RenBin Shu; JinDong Feng; YangKai Xu; TengFeng Shu; ZiHuan Shu
abstract: This paper presents an indoor tracking algorithm model designed specifically for the unique scenario of supermarkets. Firstly, the UWB positioning technology is utilized to replace the RFID radio frequency positioning due to its superior performance in all aspects. Additionally, to account for the vast area of supermarkets, the TDOA algorithm is employed to cluster and combine all UWB positioning base stations, thereby reducing non-line-of-sight errors and improving the overall positioning accuracy. Furthermore, the supermarket is abstracted into a two-dimensional plane with insurmountable obstacles, and the Q-learning algorithm and its improved version are utilized to obtain the optimal and suboptimal paths between two points in the supermarket, which can be used to determine the general direction of travel. In the event of obstacles along the travel path, the DWA algorithm is employed to perform local dynamic obstacle avoidance, ultimately achieving the goal of shopping cart tracking.

title: CORA: A Chain of Robotic Actions Reasoning Model for Autonomous Robotic Arm Manipulation
authors: Yu Hao; Fan Yang; Nicholas Fang
abstract: The integration of large language models, combined with pretrained skills, has emerged as a powerful tool for proposing natural language actions that are both feasible and contextually appropriate to perform real-world tasks. In this paper, to further enhance both the feasibility and contextual appropriateness of actions within physical environments, we introduce CORA (Chain Of Robotic Actions), a model that leverages the chain of thought methodology within multimodal foundation models for robust robotic arm manipulation. CORA initiates the task-grounding process through the chain of thought approach, adeptly identifying action chains from high-level hu-man instructions. This method decomposes complex tasks into transparent, intermediate steps, boosting the model's precision and clarity in problem-solving. The chain of thought methodology not only provides a granular and explicit breakdown of the task-solving process but also improves the model's capacity to address complex, multi-step, and implicit instructions with enhanced interpretability. In the subsequent phase, CORA utilizes a multimodal foundation model for world-grounding, assisting the robot in completing the action plan within the physical environment. In a rigorous experimental setup, we evaluate our method in multiple contexts, including simulated and real-world environments. Ablation studies are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the Chain of Robotic Action Reasoning strategies in comprehending action chains explicitly and implicitly stated in human instructions. A comparative analysis with existing approaches further substantiates its superior performance. The results conclusively demonstrate the method's effectiveness and efficiency across various components.

title: Delay Margin for Containment Control of Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems Over Directed Graphs
authors: Xueyan Ma; Dan Ma
abstract: In this paper, we mainly study the delay robustness on containment control of second-order multi-agent systems with uncertain communication delays over directed graphs. Our purpose is to find the maximal delay range that can be tolerated under which the multi-agent system can maintain containment robustly. We consider a second-order multi-agent system under position and velocity feedback protocols in which each agent has two unstable real poles. We derive the exact expression of the delay margin for multi-agent system containment. Furthermore, based on the analysis of the exact delay margin, we obtain its explicit upper bound. The results show that the position of poles and the network connectivity will affect the bound of delay margin. Finally, a numerical example is used to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed theoretical results.

title: Application Research on Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance and Navigation of Intelligent Vehicle Based on ROS
authors: Zhengyang He; Dong Ran
abstract: The research and application of autonomous driving technology are rapidly entering a stage of vigorous development, in which dynamic obstacle avoidance navigation technology is the key to achieve autonomous driving. In this paper, an intelligent car based on ROS (Robot Operating System) is studied and applied for dynamic obstacle avoidance and navigation. This paper aims to use the laser radar, so that the system can sense the surrounding environment in real time, through the SLAM algorithm to build a map, and combined with advanced path planning algorithm. At the same time, it can achieve intelligent avoidance of dynamic obstacles for vehicles. In the process of navigation, in order to adapt to the dynamic environment, A * and TEB path planner algorithms are used by the system to select the optimal path to the target location, and at the same time, it can dynamically avoid obstacles, and finally through the test to ensure the rationality of the design. The experimental results show that the global path planner and TEB local path planner can realize the dynamic obstacle avoidance of intelligent vehicle in the process of navigation. This research can bring certain reference for the development and application of unmanned driving technology in the later period.

title: Research on BIM and Numerical Control Technology Based on Mechatronics
authors: Dawei Qiao
abstract: With the rapid development of computer technology, Building Information Modeling (BIM) is no longer only used in the construction industry, which has been gradually integrated with data technology and other fields. BIM has promoted the change of production mode in China's construction industry, which has gradually developed to the direction of efficient new industrialization. Through the integration with Management Software Computer Aided Design (CAD), cam and other information technologies, BIM has also been integrated with the mechanical and electrical industry, which has also changed the application of traditional mechanical and electrical engineering, which will be based on the data creation mode. Through the establishment of database files, BIM can calculate the green index, economic index, budget and other values of the project from the beginning of architectural design. Through the reverse calculation, BIM can improve the traditional numerical control design method, which will improve the electromechanical calculation method. Therefore, BIM has been widely used in many fields of mechanical and electrical engineering. Firstly, this paper analyzes the impact of Mechatronics on China's industry. Then, this paper analyzes the application process of BIM combined with Computer numerical control (CNC) technology. Finally, some suggestions are put forward.

title: Research on information interaction design of underwater multi-platform of deep-sea vehicle based on acoustic optic and electromagnetic transmission technology
authors: Ren Yugang; Zheng Sen; Yang Lei; Liu Kun; Liu Yanjun; Zhang Jianhua; Ding Zhongjun
abstract: Deep-sea underwater connection and information interaction technology, including core technologies such as electromechanical hydraulic interface connection and underwater signal interactive transmission, is an effective technical means to solve the problem of information interaction and collaborative operation between underwater multi-platform and sensor nodes. With a large number of deep-sea vehicles in service in China, the energy, signal, data and other interfaces of the vehicles have not been unified, which leads to the difficulty in realizing multi-platform collaborative operations, so it is urgent to carry out corresponding research. In this paper, based on the analysis of the current situation of the information interaction technology of Jiaolong manned submersible, we carried out the research and summary of the multi-platform information technology of the deep-sea vehicle, and focused on the requirements of the exploration of the complex terrain and the detection of the morphology of accumulation body in the deep-sea hydrothermal region, proposed the design idea of the underwater multi-platform information interaction based on acoustic optic and electromagnetic transmission technology with Jiaolong manned submersible as the carrier, and completed the scheme design of the information interaction system of acoustic, optic and electromagnetic, which will provide technical support for the realization of the cooperative operation and high-efficiency application of the deep-sea vehicle cooperative operation.

title: 3D-TRANS: 3D Hierarchical Transformer for Shape Correspondence Learning
authors: Hao Huang; Shuaihang Yuan; Congcong Wen; Yu Hao; Yi Fang
abstract: Motivated by the intuition that one can find correspondences between two 3D shapes in a coarse-to-fine manner, we propose 3D-TRANS, a novel learning-based model to match deformable 3D shapes hierarchically. Specifically, we first propose a new subspace feature learning approach that takes advantage of local and global geometric structures of 3D shapes. Then, we design a new hierarchical 3D transformer that adaptively learns the spatial relationships of different space partitions, which correspond to different regions of shapes at multiple scales. Inside the transformer, low-rank self-attention is utilized to extract discriminative region-aware shape descriptors, capturing both short- and long-range geometric dependencies of different shape regions at an economical computational cost. Finally, we develop a new multiple templates fusion scheme to fuse multiple deformed templates using region-aware shape descriptors to predict correspondences between input shapes and templates. We demonstrate that our approach improves over the state-of-the-art results on the difficult FAUST-inter and -intra shapes. Our model also performs well on real partial shapes from the SCAPE dataset and non-human shapes from the TOSCA dataset.

title: Hover-Bvi: Handover Vision-Language Embodied Robot System for Bvi Users
authors: Narasimha Bonda; Qin Chenxin; Yukiko Iwasaki; Hiroyasu Iwata
abstract: We present HOVER-BVI, a robot system designed to help blind and visually-impaired (BVI) users by dynamically planning and executing grasping tasks in indoor environments. Unlike traditional rigid assistive robots, our approach uses a large language model (LLM) as a flexible task planner combined with a hierarchical state machine system to sequentially execute action primitive functions. The system maintains an object memory, generates natural-language scene descriptions of the workspace, and interacts via speech. By leveraging an LLM for high-level planning, the system interprets diverse voice commands and compiles them into a sequence of primitives, making dynamic tasks possible. To validate the system, we designed experiments with blindfolded users to evaluate the system's effectiveness in tasks such as object search, description, and retrieval. Preliminary analysis suggests that in a semantically constrained indoor setting, the LLM-based planner can achieve high success rates while providing intuitive user interaction. We highlight the system's modularity and extensibility and discuss usability considerations for real-world blind users. This work takes LLM-task planning in general situations (e.g. in RoboCup GPSR) and adapts it to the BVI domain, exploiting the semantically rich, yet structured indoor context to improve reliability and user trust in assistive robotics.

title: Sentiment Analysis on Dirty Vote Movie in X (Twitter) Using Convolutional Neural Network
authors: Ainur Rafiq Abdillah; Widodo; Murien Nugraheni
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Control & [::Automation::]; Electronics; [::Robotics::]; Internet of Things; and Artificial Intelligence (CERIA)
abstract: This research focuses on Sentiment Analysis of Dirty Vote based on Twitter users' opinions by utilizing the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method. In this study, a total of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1 0 1 0}$</tex> tweets were used after going through the labeling and pre-processing process, with a division of training data and test data of 80:20. The results showed a True Positive value of 44, True Negative of 104, False Positive of 26, and False Negative of 28. The accuracy value obtained was 73.27 % with a precision of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8 0 \%}$</tex>, recall of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{7 8. 8 \%}$</tex>, specificity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6 2. 8 6 \%}$</tex>, and f1-score of 79.4%. Word cloud analysis revealed that the majority of opinions on the Dirty Vote movie tend to be positive, indicating significant support or appreciation from the public. Based on these results, future research is recommended to expand the data collection period, integrate more data sources from Other algorithms from machine learning and deep learning fields were used, such as KNN, SVM, Naïve Bayes, and LSTM. Improvements in the pre-processing stage are also recommended to increase the accuracy of the model, especially in overcoming the use of slang and slang terms that are often used on social media.

title: Online Distributed Optimization with Stochastic Objective Functions: High Probability Bound Analysis of Dynamic Regrets
authors: Hang Xu; Kaihong Lu
abstract: In this paper, the problem of online distributed optimization with stochastic and nonconvex objective functions is studied by employing a multi-agent system. When making decisions, each agent only has access to a noisy gradient of its own objective function in the previous time and can only communicate with its immediate neighbors via a time-varying digraph. To handle this problem, an online distributed stochastic projection-free algorithm is proposed. Of particular interest is that the dynamic regrets are employed to measure the performance of the online algorithm. Existing works on online distributed algorithms involving stochastic gradients only provide the sublinearity results of regrets in expectation. Different from them, we study the high probability bounds of the dynamic regrets, i.e., the sublinear bounds of dynamic regrets are characterized by the natural logarithm of the failure probability's inverse. Under mild assumptions on the graph and objective functions, we prove that if the variations in both the objective function sequence and its gradient sequence grow within a certain rate, then the high probability bounds of the dynamic regrets grow sublinearly. Finally, a simulation example is carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of our theoretical results. Index TermsOnline distributed optimization; Noncon-vex optimization; Stochastic gradients; Dynamic regrets; High probability.

title: Design and analysis of target-attacker-defender games under limited observations*
authors: Qingqing Ren; Jinghua Sun; Yuhang Xu; Bin Jiang; Li Guo
abstract: This paper designs a game control strategy for the target-attacker-defender (TAD) games under limited observations that occur on both sides of the defender and target. Three different cases of TAD games are taken into account: 1) protecting a fixed target, 2) protecting a target moving along a fixed trajectory, and 3) protecting an escaping target.
