For each case, the pursuit strategy, evasion strategy, and defense strategy are particularly designed based on linear quadratic (LQ) game theory. Furthermore, it rigorously proves that the Nash equilibrium is achieved under the designed strategies. The simulation results verify the rationality of the proposed method.

title: A Double Node Thin-Film Thermocouples for In-Situ Measurement
authors: Rong Ma; Meiju Zhang; Zhongkai Zhang; Manguo Huang; Xiaobo Liang; Jiangjiang Liu; Zhaojun Liu; Bian Tian
abstract: The design, fabrication, testing and implementation of a new high-performance tungsten-rhenium thin film thermocouple are introduced. In this paper, tungsten-rhenium TFTCs are taken as the research object, after simulation analysis in COMSOL software and design, it is made by screen-printing technology and magnetron sputtering. This kind of thin film thermocouple primarily utilizes two kinds of electrode materials with varying composition combination, mainly tungsten with 5% rhenium and tungsten with 26% rhenium. Furthermore, high-temperature annealing is performed to maintain the mechanical properties and thus improve thermoelectric performance. The results demonstrate that the performance is reliable in the temperature range of 150-600 C° with a repeatability of 2.02%, providing application value for high-temperature in-situ sensing.

title: Modeling Bi-directional Wedge-type Segmented Soft Pneumatic Bending Actuator for Hand Rehabilitation using Finite Element Method
authors: Mark Joseph B. Enojas; Manuel C. Ramos
abstract: Models of different actuators for hand rehabilitation gloves have been sought by many developers. Hand rehabilitation exercises require flexion and extension of the fingers. However, existing actuators for this application do not conform to these requirements. In this paper, a bi-directional wedge-type segmented soft pneumatic bending actuator is proposed that could accomplish flexion and extension with positive and negative (vacuum) pressure, respectively. The model is simulated in finite element software and is characterized according to the varying pressure at each joint to its equivalent force depicted by each of the links of the finger. The results show that the model was able to bend in flexion -90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>at a pressure of 220 kPa and in extension at +15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>at -60 kPa pressure. An artificial neural network was set up with 2484 data sets as an inverse kinematic solution in deriving a pressure-to-bending angle function. An R of 0.99997 was obtained for both the training, validation, and test. The force and torque generated at the tip of each joint in an axial direction of the actuator have been evaluated to measure the actuator model's bending ability. This model can be used as an assistive device that can do hand rehabilitation exercises requiring flexion and extension such as tendon gliding exercises.

title: An Approach to Evaluate the Dynamic Stability for Walking Robots
authors: Jianxun Fu; Chengze Liu; Zhijun Li; Feng Gao
abstract: In recent years, the dynamics of walking robots was studied based on dangerous environments. A more complete dynamic model is essential for the further of a practical legged robot. As an important enrichment in stability study for a walking robot, a stability measure named as Moment Ratio Stability Margin (MRSM) is introduced, which takes all stability factors into formulation. In this paper we attempt to explore a dynamic stability margin for a walking robot to analyze and evaluate the stability problem t during its locomotion.

title: Autonomous Navigation of UAV in Dynamic Unstructured Environments via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
authors: Kai Kou; Gang Yang; Wenqi Zhang; Chenyi Wang; Yuan Yao; Xingshe Zhou
abstract: Autonomous navigation of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is one of the fundamental yet completely solved problems in automatic control. In this paper, an option-based hierarchical reinforcement learning approach is proposed for UAV autonomous navigation. Specifically, the proposed method consists of a high-level and two low-level model, where the high level behavior selection model learns a stable and reliable behavior selection strategy automatically, while the low-level obstacle avoidance model and target-driven control model implement two behavior strategies, obstacle avoidance and target approach, respectively, thus avoiding the dependence on manually designed control rules. Furthermore, the proposed model is pre-trained on large public dataset, allowing the model to converge quickly in various complex unstructured flight environments. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method indicates an overall advantage in various evaluation metrics, which indicating that the proposed method has a strong generalization capability in autonomous navigation task of UAV.

title: H∞ Fuzzy Reliable Tracking Controller Design for Nonlinear Systems
authors: Mourad Kchaou; Badr Alshammari
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of fault-tolerant tracking controller design for for non-linear systems subject to external disturbances, uncertainties, and actuator failures. The approach is built upon three main aspects: 1) Utilising Takagi-Sugeno (TS) fuzzy models to handle nonlinear systems, along with a non-linear failure model to describe actuator failures. 2) Investigating the fuzzy Lyapunov function to establish less conservative criteria for analysing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> tracking performance. 3) Employing linear matrix inequality techniques, with the help of slack matrices to design the controller gains. Finally, the reliability and availability of the presented control method are validated by a Duffing forced oscillation system

title: Sinusoidal Vibration Control Technology of Two Degrees of Freedom Electro-hydraulic Shaking Table
authors: Zhongli Jiang; Guangfeng Guan
abstract: A sine vibration control technique for multi-degree-of-freedom electro-hydraulic shakers is proposed in this paper to realize high-precision sine vibration environment simulation experiments. The 2-DOF sinusoidal control based on the SR1 quasi-Newton method includes the generalized impedance iteration and the driving spectrum iteration. The generalized impedance matrix correction formula based on the SR1 quasi-Newton algorithm can effectively reduce the system’s online calculation time and improve the convergence speed. The variable step-size update formula derived from the steepest descent method is used to drive the spectral iteration, which can effectively improve the convergence speed and accuracy of the iterative algorithm. A digital tracking filter for the sinusoidal signal is developed to reduce the high-frequency noise. Compared with the 2-DOF sinusoidal control based on the Broyden quasi-Newton method, the simulation results show that the sinusoidal vibration control technology for the multi-degree-of-freedom electro-hydraulic shaking table has better performance.

title: Motion Planning for Quadrupled Teams: An Experimental Evaluation Using a Dynamic Fluid Flow Model
authors: Mohammad Ghufran; Sourish Tetakayala; Hossein Rastgoftar
abstract: This paper applies the principles of fluid mechan-ics to develop a new method for motion planning in contented environments where multiple groups of agents want to reach their target while guaranteeing inter-agent collision avoidance. Assuming <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> groups of agents exist in the same motion space, we propose a time-varying ideal fluid flow model to safely plan the desired coordination of each group in the presence of other groups that are considered singularity points in the fluid flow field. To ensure that each group reaches its target destination, we propose to define the desired trajectory of each group along the streamlines of the fluid field but continuously direct the streamlines toward the target destination. The proposed solution, is experimentally evaluated by using quadruped robots in an indoor robotic facility.

title: A Highway Entrance Ramp Control Method Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Lin Wu; Zhenlong Li; Mengxiao Diao; Xiaobo Dong; Jushang Ou
abstract: Considering the intricate traffic flow dynamics between the mainline and entrance ramp areas of highways, a ramp control model based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is proposed. Leveraging the characteristics of traffic flow, this study builds upon existing reinforcement learning (RL) ramp control models and optimizes the design of the state space, action space, and reward function. Utilizing the PyCharm platform, SUMO simulation software is adopted for secondary development. Simulation experiments are conducted in various scenarios involving different congestion durations and demand distributions. Under identical road network conditions, four distinct control methods are devised: the no-control (NC) scenario, the ALINEA ramp control method, the RL control method, and the proposed DRL method. The experimental outcomes indicate that, compared to the NC method, all three alternative methods substantially reduce the average travel time. The proposed DRL method exhibits an average travel time reduction of 12.77% compared to the ALINEA method and a 5.22% reduction compared to the RL method. Furthermore, the proposed DRL method achieves a reduction of approximately 39.01% in the ramp queue length compared to the ALINEA method.

title: Research on Prevention and Management of Crew Errors in Aircraft Cockpit Design
authors: Yao Zhu; Xinrong Liu
abstract: This research focuses on the prevention and management of crew errors in aircraft cockpit design. Crew errors pose a significant safety challenge in the aviation industry. Therefore, the motivation behind this study is to propose a comprehensive approach to reduce the occurrence of such errors and effectively address crew error incidents that have already occurred. First, the background introduces the impact of crew errors on flight safety, emphasizing their critical role in air traffic management and flight operations. Furthermore, the potential risks and safety hazards associated with crew errors are discussed in detail. The main objective of this study is to identify various types of crew errors and their potential consequences and provide corresponding prevention and management strategies. To achieve this, we conducted an extensive literature review, covering various aspects such as crew error cases, pilot training, and design improvements. The key contribution of this paper lies in providing a systematic approach to prevent and manage crew errors. We not only focus on improvements in human factors engineering and training but also explore the potential of new technologies and design innovations to enhance the performance and safety of pilots and crew members.

title: Scalable; Compact and Easy-to-Control Linear Electromagnetic Actuator
authors: Jakub Tureček; Jří Kuthan; Martin Vítek; Martin Juřík; František Mach
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: The design of a compact and scalable linear electromagnetic actuator with spatially selective actuation and magnetic stabilization is presented. The concept is based on multi-layer coplanar coil topology, which operates rare-earth-based permanent magnet sliders and takes advantage of all the parts formed by a printed circuit board (PCB). With its potential applications in the precise manipulation of small loads and control of mechanisms in microgravity environments, the actuator stands out in compact and scalable dimensions, low weight and inertia, ease of deployment open-loop control, low manufacturing demands, material resistance, and durability. The paper discusses the basic design, construction, and actuator operation and presents the first experimental verification of the actuator concept.

title: Teleoperated Mobile Robotic Manipulator for Rescue Scenarios
authors: Huaihang Zheng; Shangfei Liu; Junzheng Wang
abstract: This paper introduces a teleoperated mobile robotic manipulator specifically designed for rescue operations. The system integrates a robotic manipulator, a mobile platform, a hybrid power system, an environmental perception system, and a teleoperation console, forming a modular and highly adaptable architecture. A key innovation is the Feedback Correction Loop, which improves manipulator control by mitigating issues like communication delays, workspace constraints, and packet loss. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the framework, demonstrating that the system can execute tasks smoothly, continuously, and safely under teleoperation.

title: Facial Emotion Recognition Based on Local Feature
authors: Jinye Lu; Yuhong Ma; Fangyuan Zheng; Juntao Wang
abstract: Facial expressions are categorized into seven types: happiness, sadness, fear, disgust, anger, surprise and neutral. Due to factors like uneven lighting and minute expression variations, current facial emotion recognition algorithms often struggle with accuracy. To address this, this paper presents a novel approach to recognizing facial emotions. Firstly, applying Gamma correction to homogenize lighting in facial images, enhancing lighting conditions for precise recognition. Secondly, using anthropometric methods to precisely locate and segment key facial areas like eyebrows, eyes and mouth, and extract the primary emotion-reflecting areas. After that, a feature plane is created based on these facial emotion components, so as to eliminate redundant data from non-emotional facial areas to boost recognition efficiency and accuracy. Lastly, deep facial features are extracted using a convolutional neural network to complete facial emotion recognition. Experiments demonstrate the efficacy of the constructed feature plane and a notable improvement in recognition accuracy over geometric feature-based methods, achieving a 90.12% accuracy rate on the JAFFA public expression datasets.

title: Active Disturbance Rejection with Continous Sliding Mode Control for Lower Limb Rehabilitation Exoskeleton
authors: Mao Qin; Lingzhen Lian; Xiaoyuan Dang; Baolei Wang; Huiming Wang
abstract: Lower limb rehabilitation exoskeleton robots play a crucial role in assisting patients with limb movement disorders to recover their walking ability. For precise control of lower limb rehabilitation robots, this paper suggests a robust control strategy, which combines an extended state observer with continuous sliding mode control(CSMC-ESO). First of all, this paper uses the Euler-Lagrange equation to establish the mathematical model of the lower limb exoskeleton. Then, the ESO is utilized to estimate the total disturbances of the system, including unmodeled dynamics and external disturbances. Subsequently, this paper introduces a Continuous Sliding Mode Control method, with the estimates provided by the ESO. This method is introduced for its strong robustness and capabilities in suppressing chattering. Finally, experimental results illustrate that the proposed control strategy is effective in achieving satisfactory tracking performance.

title: Physics- Informed Neural Network Approach for Numeric Modeling of Rapid Thermal Processing System
authors: Ao Yang; Tengfei Xiao
abstract: In order to obtain a numeric model of the temperature distribution on the wafer in a rapid thermal processing system, a neural network method named Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) is proposed in this paper. The PINN architecture is constructed with a network structure where the loss function is restricted to satisfy the partial differential equation and the boundary condition of the physical laws of the system. The network is trained with a sampling which depends on the spatial topology of the system. The proposed PINN is compared to the finite element method with experimental results showing the effectiveness of the PINN approach.

title: LiDAR-Based Orientation Monitoring of an Unknown Object During Manipulation with an Industrial Robot
authors: Fabio Pietryga; Mike Duddek; Saulo H. Freitas Seabra da Rocha
abstract: Picking unknown objects in an automated process is a particular challenge in industrial robotics. Besides the actual pickup process, it is also important to check whether the picked object retains its orientation in the gripper while being manipulated in order to perform reliable collision-free path planning and ensure that the subsequent process continues without failure. This paper discusses the prerequisites, development, implementation, integration and evaluation of such monitoring of an unknown handling object in industrial robotics using LiDAR sensor technology.

title: Estimation of Rock Compressibility for Indonesian Limestones by Artificial Neural Network
authors: Fathaddin M. T.
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Control & [::Automation::]; Electronics; [::Robotics::]; Internet of Things; and Artificial Intelligence (CERIA)
abstract: Compressibility is one of the important physical properties of rocks. Rock compressibility greatly influences the calculation of the volume of oil and gas in a reservoir based on pressure drop data. In addition, compressibility plays a role in the process of pushing oil and gas through rock pores towards production wells. Compressibility is influenced by overburden and pore pressure. In this study, three ANN models were applied to estimate rock compressibility. The optimum number of neurons and number of hidden layers were determined for the three ANN models based on the highest correlation coefficient. The ANN 2 model with porosity as an input parameter is the most accurate model because it has the lowest mean absolute relative error value and the highest correlation coefficient value. Based on the correlation coefficient value, the optimum number of neurons and number of hidden layers for the ANN 2 model are 8 and 3 respectively. In general, compared to conventional models, all ANN models have better accuracy. Among conventional models, the use of the Horne equation shows the best accuracy in predicting the compressibility of limestone in Indonesia.

title: Lithium Battery Capacity Estimation Based on Improved Convolutional Neural Network with Self-Attention Mechanism
authors: Mingyang Du; Yujie Zhang; Qiang Miao
abstract: At present, lithium batteries are very significant in the field of new energy, so the performance evaluation of lithium batteries in industry has become very important. Capacity estimation as one of the important indicators, its accuracy not only determines the service life and health of batteries, but also enables better dynamic monitoring and management of battery state, and optimization of energy use strategies. Among them, BP neural network is a classic algorithm applied in lithium battery capacity estimation systems, but this algorithm cannot effectively capture key information in input data and its learning ability is relatively weak. Therefore, an algorithm based on one-dimensional convolutional neural network and self-attention mechanism is proposed. One dimensional convolutional neural network can effectively capture the local features in the input sequence, and the self-attention mechanism can filter the information with high relevance to the target by calculating the weight of different positions. The combination of the two can improve the overall understanding ability of the model to the input data. Finally, two lithium battery data sets are used for experiments. The experimental results show that the algorithm of one-dimensional convolutional neural network combined with self-attention mechanism significantly improves the accuracy of prediction.

title: Modular Design of Substation Video Monitoring Equipment
authors: Xianyue Luo; Jingyu Zhou; Kui Xu
abstract: In order to solve the power special video equipment can not realize the modular replacement of wearing parts caused by a large number of waste problems, research on the modularity of video equipment functions, wearing parts of the hardware module design; substation video monitoring modular installation structure research, the realization of the modular installation of wearing parts, easy to replace, easy to overhaul; video equipment access process standardization research, to complete the consistency of the access model of the video equipment; video equipment Self-inspection method research, real-time monitoring of video equipment status, the realization of the alarm open node module, improve equipment reliability; research station video situational awareness module, real-time monitoring of video equipment and video network security.

title: Multi-Sensor H∞ Filter Design for Networked Control Systems with Unknown Communication Delays
authors: George Nartey; Duanjin Zhang
abstract: In this paper, the problem of multi-sensor H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> filter for networked control systems with unknown communication delays is investigated. A filter for the unknown communication delays system is developed to guarantee the exponentially mean-square stability of the closed-loop system provided its equivalent robust filter is designed. The measured output is prone to sensor saturation which has sector-nonlinearities capability to measure the physical plant. The unknown communication delays are considered in the sensor to the controller link. Given the limitations in communication delays, a filtering scheme is designed via linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) and Lyapunov stability theory. A simulation result is given to prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Research on Scenario based Test for auto-landing system
authors: Tan Ru; Yao Zhichao
abstract: The current commercial aircraft is adopted the large scale integration design method, it is a big challenge to high integration and complex system. The traditional test method is based on specification or requirement, it is mainly focus on internal and external logic and function interface, but it is not test for severe scenario influence to the aircraft system, such as pilot maneuver, limit condition, complex environment, control mode transition.etc, so some issues which should be found on laboratory are found on flight test or operational test later. This article proposes a scenario based test method on auto-landing system. Firstly, capturing the test scenario based on auto-landing system function analysis, build the traceability between scenario and requirements. Secondly, developing the operational scenario model and flight scenario model, build the test environment. Finally, validating the related requirements based on auto scenario test.

title: Kalman Filter Embedded MPC for Stochastic Systems
authors: Keerthi Chacko; S. Janardhanan; Indra Narayan Kar
abstract: This paper considers a computationally efficient Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework to design control for stochastic systems. The probability distribution function of the disturbance is utilized in the design of control. The computational efficiency is contributed by three factors: monotonically weighted cost function, reduction in prediction horizon and the concept of event triggering. Kalman Filter is embedded in the MPC in order to achieve a more accurate value of states to be used in the optimization problem. Monte Carlo simulation is carried out on a benchmark system to verify the advantage of the proposed technique.

title: The Estimation Method of Regression Model and Its Comparisons
authors: Keyi Cao
abstract: Machine learning is one of the current development trends of computer technology, and regression algorithm is an important algorithm in machine learning. For the accuracy of the algorithm, it is essential to select good evaluation indicators. This paper proposes a curve for evaluating the regression equation, which has similar characteristics to the Receiver-Operating Curve. This article describes the calculation and drawing method of the curve. Compared with other regression equation evaluation indicators, this curve can more intuitively reflect the sensitivity and specificity of the model. The area under the curve can be used to compare the performance between different models, and it has stronger robustness. However, it can be further optimized in terms of accuracy and time cost, and it may be combined with other evaluation indicators in the future to improve its accuracy.

title: Optimization and Control of a Perfusion Bioreactor System in Tissue Engineering
authors: Ioana Nascu; Ioan Nascu; Wenli Du
abstract: This work focuses on developing control strategies for a continuous perfusion bioreactor which are capable of increasing the cell density while minimizing the consumption of nutrients. This will set the basis for advanced control strategies which will advance manufacturing for a cell growth process. The optimal oxygen and glucose concentrations for perfusion bioreactors that will reduce the time required to reach maximum cell density are analyzed. Moreover, the optimum profile for the oxygen and glucose concentration is determined and used as a set-point for the developed control loops. The mathematical model that will be used in this work is implemented using Computational Fluid Dynamics and it presents the spatio-temporal evolution of glucose, oxygen concentration and cell density in a 3D polymeric scaffold. To close the loop, the last step is to validate the performances of the developed controllers on the high-fidelity CFD model. Two different scenarios are designed, implemented and tested. The simulations show satisfactory behavior and good performances.

title: Comparison of decision support models -- a recruitment case study as a multiclass classification problem with limited data
authors: Artur Morys - Magiera; Marek Długosz; Paweł Skruch
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: We present a comparative case study of machine learning models, evaluating their efficiency in a practical task of multiclass classification of samples being submissions to a recruitment survey and assigning them scores denoting the match level for a given candidate to a given workgroup (committee) in the AGH Students’ Council. This research is based on the Council’s recruitment applications that carried candidates’ responses to a set of 10 hypothetical Council member activity scenarios, where they were to choose one of four given solutions to the problems. The data was collected from a web quiz in 2020, validated on a voluntary insider control group’s responses to these questions and finally the best-performing model was evaluated in practice in the 2021’s recruitment inside an in-browser adventure minigame. This work provides insight into how models ranging from classical methods to deep learning perform in a very specific not yet well-explored in literature, practical non-linear problem that is dependent on individual features of the participants, with the data volume being very limited due to a restricted population of candidates. This information may provide a starting point for applications of machine learning in decision support systems in recruitment processes.

title: Event-Triggered Adaptive Dynamic Programming of Load Frequency Control
authors: Jin An; Xiaoming Tang
abstract: Due to the super rapid development of computer communication network technology, the power system is developing more and more rapidly. In addition, with the increase of measuring instruments and the use of intelligent instruments, when the measurement data of Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) is transmitted to the control center, the communication burden will increase. Therefore, introduction of event-triggered control can save communication resources and reduce the network burden. This paper put forward this design method of event-triggered Adaptive Dynamic Programming (ADP) Load Frequency Control (LFC). The controller adopts aperiodic update mode and ADP evaluation-execution module to update the control law. ADP is implemented by two three-layer artificial neural networks. Simulation study on a one-area IEEE LFC system proves the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

title: Ibex: A reconfigurable ground vehicle with adaptive terrain navigation capability
authors: Senthur Raj; R P Manu Aatitya; S Jack Samuel; J Veejay Karthik; D. Ezhilarasi
abstract: This paper presents a unique unmanned ground vehicle with a dynamic wheelbase and an adaptive thrust based friction optimization scheme that aids in the traversal of steep slopes and slippery surfaces. The vehicle is capable of adapting itself to the surface topography using an impedance-based stabilization module to minimize the mechanical oscillatory transients induced during its motion. A detailed analysis of its modules has been elucidated in this paper based on the vehicle parameters. The proposed methodologies have been integrated and tested on a customized prototype. Experimental validation and simulation for the proposed modules at various terrain conditions have been carried out to authenticate its performance.

title: Event-triggered Decentralized Fault-tolerant Control for Multi-fault Modular Manipulator with Input Constraints
authors: Ziyao Song; Tianhao Ma; Yadan Zhao; Fan Zhou
abstract: In this paper, a fault-tolerant controller based on event-triggered is proposed for multi-fault modular manipulator with input constraints. The joint torque feedback (JTF) technique is used to establish dynamic model of subsystem. The performance index function designed in this paper included the compensation term for model uncertainty, and the observer for fault estimation and tracking error. The hyperbolic tangent function is introduced to input the system. Adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) is introduced to reduce the dimensionality disaster of the system, and combined with the event-triggered mechanism to reduce the update frequency of the system. Hamilton Jacobi Bellman (HJB) equation is mainly solved by neural network. The stability of the closed-loop system is proved by Lyapunov theorem. The effectiveness of this control method is verified by simulation.

title: Advanced Structural Design for Humanoid Robot Upper Limbs
authors: Yifan Liu; Hongwu Wang; Dianzheng Wang; Yunji Li; Xiangkun Zhang
abstract: In this paper, the humanoid robot is taken as the object to study the influence of the design parameters of the dual-arm base on the workspace in the logistics handling scene. First, the humanoid robot and the handling target object are modeled, the influence of the dual-arm configuration and the base constraint conditions on the dual-arm workspace is quantitatively analyzed, the mathematical relationship between the variables is established, and the parameters of the dual-arm base are optimized to achieve the best workspace. Finally, the optimization effect is verified by experiments. The results show that the method can effectively improve the cooperative workspace of the two arms and provide ideas for the design of the base.

title: Metaheuristics for scheduling on parallel machines under deteriorating and maintenances
authors: Tomasz Marchel; Radosław Rudek
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the parallel machine scheduling problem with the deteriorating effect and mainte-nances to minimize the makespan. The involvement of condition based maintenance activities not only gives a potential to construct better models and more accurate decision support systems for real-life issues, but it also implies difficulties on search space traversal techniques to guarantee feasibility of results and not omitting optimality. Therefore, we propose well known and reliable metaheuristics that proved their efficiency for various combinatorial optimization problems, i.e., simulated annealing and tabu search. However, our implementations are based on a representation that due to multiple redundant solutions gains its significant advantage to cover all feasible schedules, therefore, the related optimization algorithms guarantee that the optimum is not excluded from the search space. The efficiency of our approach is verified on the basis of computational experiments.

title: Modeling a Cross-Domain Distributed Personnel Records System Based on Zookeeper and Erasable Bloom Filters
authors: Xu Liu; Zhousen Zhu; Lu Lin; Xuehua Liao
abstract: Aiming at the problems of cross-domain file query and file transmission difficulties in the current file system, an improvement scheme of personnel file management system based on zookeeper and erasable Bloom filter is proposed. The multi-node distributed system is constructed through the node monitoring and data synchronisation mechanism of zookeeper, and each sub-system uses Bloom filters to improve the efficiency of archive query, achieve efficient collaborative query between multiple archive systems, and improve the performance and scalability of the system. For the dispersed independent and huge number of stock archives, it is proposed to achieve fast positioning of single-point system based on Bloom filter filtering. There are frequent file transfer operations in the archive system, and the traditional Bloom filter can no longer meet the demand. This paper analyses the structure and characteristics of the traditional Bloom filter, and on the basis of the traditional Bloom filter structure, adopts the idea of collision counting to realize the erasable Bloom filter. Compared with the traditional Bloom filter, this method solves the problem of undeletable elements that exists in the traditional Bloom filter and effectively reduces the storage overhead of the counting Bloom filter. Experimental results show that the model can effectively achieve cross-domain archive query and archive forwarding, and maintain good performance and stability when the archive data increases.

title: Tracking Control for Thermoelectric Ice Clamping Using a Gain-Scheduled Observer and Proportional-Integral State Feedback
authors: Harald Aschemann; Felix Van Rossum; Benedikt Haus; Paolo Mercorelli
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper deals with a novel nonlinear control application, the ice clamping of workpieces during the manufacturing process using feedback-controlled Peltier cells. For practical reasons, only the hot-side temperature is measurable. Consequently, a nonlinear state and disturbance observer is designed to estimate the hot- and cold-side temperatures of the Peltier element, and an unknown disturbance heat flow. Given these estimates, the nonlinear system is reformulated and a nonlinear input transformation is proposed for a favorable design of a proportional-integral state feedback. It aims at the tracking of desired trajectories for the cold-side temperature despite disturbing process heat losses from the manufacturing process. The feedback part is enhanced by appropriate dynamic feedforward control as well as a static disturbance compensation using the estimated heat flow stemming from process heat losses. Considering a typical ice clamping scenario under the impact of unknown process disturbances, both a high tracking precision and an accurate estimation can be achieved in simulation studies. The simulation results are discussed and the paper closes with conclusions.

title: Advancing Humanoid Robotics: Leg Control and Locomotion
authors: Emanuel Muntean; Monica Leba
abstract: In this study, we introduce a control system tailored for biped humanoid robot legs, drawing inspiration from human locomotion patterns. This system leverages inertial measurement units (IMUs) to accurately track the orientation and motion of human lower limbs. The core of our data processing and control algorithm implementation relies on the Arduino Uno and Arduino Nano microcontrollers. For motor control, the PCA9685 16-channel 12-bit PWM servo driver is employed, facilitating precise command of the servo motors for refined movement control. The robot’s leg incorporates three servo motors to manipulate its joints, thereby allowing for lifelike and agile leg movements. This control system is crafted for agility and precision, enabling the robotic leg to navigate varied terrains and execute walking tasks, mirroring human leg patterns. Through integrating IMU data with an effective motor control system via Arduino platforms and the PCA9685 driver, our goal is to attain good stability and functionality in the biped humanoid robot’s leg movements.

title: Fault Detection Robotic System: Controlling and Experimental Validation of Overhead Crane Climbing Robot
authors: Arun Kumar Yadav; Janusz Szpytko
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The involvement of robots has increased rapidly in the last few years in many applications. A variety of robot performs numerous type of task in a hazardous environment. In order to prevent server damage to the infrastructures of overhead cranes in an industrial environment, a Fault Detection System (FDS) and Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) has a significant role. Mainly enhancing the safety, reliability, and availability of industrial overhead cranes requires timely continuous monitoring. This research proposes a wide approach for inspection that applies to various types of physical machines by mainly focusing on overhead crane bridges. The study of fault detection using a robotic system by NDT & SHM is relatively new, as only a few types of research has been performed. To be more specific, this paper provides a detailed insight into an autonomous robot for crack detection in overhead cranes bridges and girder using an array of GMR (Giant magneto resistive) sensors and magnetic climbing mechanisms. Firstly, we focused on the challenges and issues in the monitoring of the overhead cranes and the possibility of cracks and faults. Concerning these challenges and issues, we have proposed a new approach applicable for overhead cranes bridges crack detection. The intention of conducting this research is to make the inspection process cost-effective, reliable, and safe. This paper provides detailed insight into crack detection robots and sensor systems by considering all attributes.

title: Adaptive Fuzzy Control for Nonlinear Systems in Nonstrict-Feedback Form with Full State Constraints: A Feasibility Condition Free Approach
authors: Junjie Gao; Xiaotong Zhou; Anqing Wang
abstract: In this paper, we aim to solve the full state constrained control problem for nonstrict-feedback nonlinear systems subject to completely unknown nonlinearities, unknown control gains and external disturbances. The full state constraints are assumed to be asymmetric and time-varying. Fuzzy logic systems (FLSs) are utilized to approximate the completely unknown nonlinearities. A shifting function is first introduced to remove the feasibility condition on the virtual controllers while using the traditional barrier Lyapunov functions (BLFs). Then, a dynamic surface control (DSC) based adaptive fuzzy controller is developed to prevent the state constraints from being violated. The main feature of this paper lies in that a unified structure for both symmetric and asymmetric full state constraints is constructed without feasibility condition, and the Lyapunov stability of the closed-loop system is proven. Simulation results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control structure.

title: Poles sequence selection in implementation of fractional-order difference via Takenaka-Malmquist functions
authors: Marek Rydel; Rafał Stanisławski
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The paper presents a new algorithm for the selection of poles for modeling fractional-order difference based on Takenaka-Malmquist functions. The main advantage of the proposed approach to the selection of poles is better approximation accuracy in the chosen frequency adequacy range as well as in the time domain of finite-length implementation of the Takenaka-Malmquist-base fractional-order difference. The proposed Takenaka-Malmquist-based difference implementation can also be applied to model fractional-order integrators and non-commensurate state-space systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Trajectory Planning for Multi-Robot Collaboration in Complex Components with Heterogeneous Materials
authors: Xinyu Wang; Yueyu Wu; Gong Zhang; Jianzheng Qi; Heyu Wang; Si Di; Qunxu Lin
abstract: A multi-robot collaboration can reliably perform complex tasks that would be difficult for a single robot to accomplish, especially advanced welding operations in complex components with heterogeneous materials. We focused on a three-dimensional (3D) trajectory planning for complex components with heterogeneous materials, and carries out the research of multi-robot collaboration. By using the software of robot simulator CoppeliaSim, the comparative simulation analysis of multi-robot active-slave and distributed in 3D intersecting line was proposed. Through the establishment of multi-robot collaborative experiment system, the trajectory planning of multi-robot axial motion with semi-∞ was put forward. Simulation and experimental results show that our proposed multi-robot system is feasible and is capable of realizing 3D trajectory planning for complex components with heterogeneous materials.

title: Vehicle Video Stabilization Combined with Vestibular Reflex Effect
authors: Jie Wang; Junsen Jing; Xuewen Qiu; Zhaosheng Xu; Huawei Liang
abstract: In the closed-cabin driving environment, the camera video image shakes violently due to bumpy road conditions. The method of combining vestibular reflex effect with electronic image stabilization is adopted to ensure that the driver can obtain stable images of external road conditions. Firstly, the improved Harris corner response function and increased distance constraint are used to complete the corner detection of the image, and then complete the electronic image stabilization. Secondly, the vehicle vestibular reflex model was established to predict the position of eyeballs by measuring the driver’s head position. Finally, the position information of the eyeball is combined with the image stabilization, so that the image is always displayed in the screen area facing the eyeball after image stabilization. Experimental results show that the error matching rate of the improved Harris corner detection algorithm is reduced by 10.1% compared with common algorithms under the premise of ensuring the efficiency of the algorithm. After image stabilization, the signal to noise ratio of the image increases by 6.525dB, and the processing time of single frame is 22.479ms. Simulation results of vehicle vestibular reflex model show that the simulated Angle of eye movement conforms to physiological vestibular reflex effect, and the average tracking time of single frame image is 30.9ms.

title: Experimental Study on the Influencing Factors of Leakage Performance of Hydraulic Motor
authors: Haitao Qian; Xiangdong Guo; Biao Li
abstract: This study takes a certain brand of hydraulic cycloidal motor as the research object, and analyzes and researches the influence of the brand of hydraulic motor, the viscosity of hydraulic oil fluid, the temperature of hydraulic oil supplying, and the fit clearance of the hydraulic motor rotor to the stator on the leakage of the motor through experiments. The results show that there is a significant difference in the leakage between different brands of hydraulic motors with the same displacement; for the same hydraulic motor, the greater the viscosity viscosity, the smaller the leakage; for the same hydraulic motor, the higher the oil supply temperature, the greater the leakage; for the same hydraulic motor, the greater the clearance between the stator and rotor of the hydraulic motor, the greater the leakage. Therefore, in engineering practice, the evaluation of the leakage performance of hydraulic motors needs to comprehensively consider the effects of oil viscosity, oil temperature and hydraulic motor machining clearance.

title: Research on logistics AGV vehicle path planning based on improved Q-learning algorithm
authors: Zhao Han
abstract: Logistics AGV car as an important part in the intelligent manufacturing, the path planning problem by the attention of many scholars. at present, the path planning algorithm based on reinforcement learning exists the problems of slow convergence and the result is not stable, logistics AGV car in order to get a better return function, you need to perform different actions to gain more experience and information. In order to balance exploration and utilization problems, the traditional Q-learning algorithm introduces the probability value of an exploration factor into the action selection strategy of AGV, selects the state-action pair of the largest Q-value function every time, which leads to the system is easy to fall into the local optimal solution, which also slows down the convergence rate of the whole process. And the final action selection results will also have fluctuations. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes an improved dynamic adjustment of exploration factor ε strategy, that is to choose different exploration factor ε values in different stages of reinforcement learning, which can better solve the contradiction between exploration and utilization. Through simulation and real experiments, it is proved that the convergence speed of the improved reinforcement learning algorithm is faster and the stability of the convergence result is improved.

title: Manipulation of aqueous droplets in two-phase flow system using patterned surface wettability
authors: Anas Alazzam; Nahla Alamoodi
publication_title: 2020 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: This work reports the fabrication and experimentation of microfluidic systems with patterned surface wettability. The system is fabricated from two components; a cyclic olefin copolymer (COC) substrate and a Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) element that includes a microchannel. The wettability of the COC substrate is altered using standard microfabrication processes. Graphene oxide hydrophilic film is patterned on the surface of the hydrophobic COC substrate using plasma-enhanced liftoff approach. The device is used to manipulate dye-water droplets dispersed in silicone oil. The movement of the water droplets inside the device is found to be influenced by the GO film patterned inside the channel.

title: Robotic Applications in Generation Plants
authors: Hon Sing Yu; Yat Sing Kelvin Sa
abstract: The word “Robot” is derived from the Czech word “Robota”, which means labour. From the word, we understand that robot, in the certain extent, is to replace the work of labour in the old days. Nowadays, robots can do more than what an ordinary engineering personnel can do. At the same time, to cope with the new challenges foreseeable to the power industry, digitalisation of power generation plant will be inevitable, whilst robots will be in the key roles at many aspects. CLP Power Hong Kong Limited has been proactively exploring the robotic applications in the daily operations and maintenance tasks in recent years, focusing on those areas which can be beneficial to the business in terms of productivity enhancement, safety improvement, cost saving and better data analysis. This paper presents 2 robotic application examples, namely “Boiler Water Tube Inspection Robot” and “Economiser Inspection Robot” in the boiler system of generation plant from a user point of view, which demonstrate great value of the robotic applications to the plant operation and maintenance.

title: Safe Adaptive Dynamic Programming Method for Nonlinear Safety-Critical Systems with Disturbance
authors: Jinguang Wang; Dehua Zhang; Jishi Zhang; Heyang Zhu; Shaolin Hu; Chunbin Qin
abstract: In this paper, a safe adaptive dynamic programming (SADP) method based on the barrier function (BF) is proposed for the optimal control problem of nonlinear safety-critical systems with the safety constraints and external disturbance. Firstly, the barrier function is used to transform the nonlinear system with the security constraints into a transformed system without the security constraints. Secondly, based on the transformed system, a new barrier-disturbance-related term is proposed to approximate the effect of the external disturbance. On the premise of satisfying the security constraints and stability, the neural network (NN) approximation method is used to approximate the optimal cost function and optimal control strategy of the system online. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed method can make the system state convergence well and does not violate the security constraints.

title: UAV Localization Based on Signage Text Recognition and Matching with POI
authors: Yu Liu; Jing Bai; Jinyong Chen; Gang Wang; Fangde Sun
abstract: Localization is the most important basic information for UAVs during their missions, but within cities, the multipath effect formed by high-rise buildings will significantly reduce the positioning accuracy of GNSS. To achieve autonomous UAV localization in low-altitude scenes within cities, we propose a UAV image scene localization method based on signage text recognition and matching. First, extracting the text in store signages from UAV images, then fuzzy matching them with the POI names in electronic maps, finally, achieving scene localization of UAV images using multiple POIs jointly. The distance between image scene position and UAV flight trajectory in flight experiments is no more than 40 meters, which is consistent with the actual situation. Therefore, this method has good autonomous localization capability under urban low-altitude conditions.

title: Design and Analysis of an Enhanced In-Pipe Inspection Robot for Complex Structure
authors: Zeyad Almabrouk Saed Rashed; Mohamed Kara-Mohamed
abstract: This paper presents a novel wheeled wall-pressing in-pipe inspection robot that consists of a central body (cylinder frame), a driving system, and a wall-pressing mechanism. The locomotion system of the robot consists of only a single worm gear and a single DC motor. The proposed robot can move freely in horizontal, vertical pipelines and bends using a simple passive-based wall-pressing mechanism to adapt to the complexity of pipelines with various diameters between 170 mm and 270 mm. SolidWorks software package 2024 is utilized to design, model, and assemble the virtual prototype of the proposed robot. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is conducted on the designed parts to investigate if they can withstand the stress acting on them while passing through a complex pipeline network. The motion study is conducted to verify the performance of the proposed robot traveling in complex structures. The performed analysis shows that the proposed robot has good performance in various pipeline sections.

title: Active Fault Tolerant Control for a UAV Subject to Sensor Faults Using Sliding Mode Control
authors: Wasif Shabbir; Li Aijun; Muhammad Taimoor; Cui Yuwei; Muhammad A. Shehu
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) pitch tracking control in the presence of pitch rate gyro sensor faults is addressed in this work using sliding mode control (SMC). Fault estimation is carried out using two different observers, a high gain observer (HGO) and a radial basis function neural network (RBFNN). Real-time fault estimations are used in the control law to counter the effects of the faults. The chattering problem of SMC is resolved using a power reaching law in the switching part of the control. This forms an active fault tolerant control without the need for controller reconfiguration. The stability of the faulty system is proved using the Lyapunov method. The proposed strategy is applied to pitch tracking control of a scaled Yak-54 UAV. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

title: Recognizing Human-object Interactions for a Home Assistive Robot
authors: Liangliang Wang; Guanglei Huo; Xinwei Chen; Chengxi Huang
abstract: To enable robots to understand a specific assistive task during human-robot interactions under complex home scenes, at the center is the problem of human-object interaction (HOI) recognition. In particular, aiming at identifying <human, verb, object> efficiently, this paper proposes a graph convolutional network (GCN) by considering the similarity and proximity of human and object nodes, based on which the geometric positions and morphological relationships are explored. Also, a supplementary convolutional neural network (CNN) is fused to GCN to extract the global semantic features, which also ensures the recognition applicability for the cases where detectors fall into failure. Experiments on V-COCO demonstrate our approach, and results in real-world scenes on our assistive robot – Xiaozhi II verify its robustness.

title: Quantized Stabilization of Neutral Systems with Time-varying Delay
authors: Yingqi Zhang; Qing Zhang; Xiaoyu Wang; Caixia Liu
abstract: The quantized stabilization is discussed for a neutral system with delay of time-varying in this paper. In the first place, a suitable Lyapunov functional is constructed, and a stability criterion that has less conservativeness is given by utilizing the negative determinative property of the quadratic function and matrices of free-weighting. Furthermore, the strategy of quantized control is added to the neutral system with delay of time-varying to optimize the structure and improve the transmission rate of the network. Then, the designed state quantized controller can maintain stabilization of the neutral system with time delay. Finally, an example of numerical is given which verifies the feasibility of the result.

title: Design of High Temperature Anticorrosion Diagnosis System for Atmospheric and Vacuum Distillation Unit Based on Forcecontrol and SQL Sever2014
authors: Liang Zhao; Zexin Zhang; Lida Wang; Guichang Liu
abstract: Due to the complex composition of the oil flowing through the refining unit, the equipment anticorrosion work has always been a major problem in petrochemical enterprises, and the corrosion problem is a key factor related to shortening the service life of the atmospheric and vacuum distillation unit. Aiming at the problem of high temperature corrosion of atmospheric and vacuum unit in a petrochemical enterprise and the current situation of corrosion management in the enterprise, this paper designs a high temperature corrosion diagnosis system of atmospheric and vacuum unit based on Forcecontrol configuration development platform. The system uses three dimensional interpolation algorithm to calculate the corrosion rate, and uses Microsoft SQL sever2014 database technology and ForceControl 7.1 configuration development platform to realize the comprehensive management of corrosion data, corrosion rate calculation, early warning, expert advice and other functions. Through the function test of each module in the system, and using the actual corrosion data provided by the enterprise to simulate and verify the system, the test results show that the system can achieve the expected functions, and ensure the calculation accuracy of corrosion rate.

title: A Model-Based Approach to Evaluate Electromagnetic Responses in Vehicle Control Systems Influenced by Harness Shielding and Grounding
authors: Bowen Wang; Shuyan Zhang; Zhe Zhang
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: Modern vehicles are equipped with numerous electrical devices and instruments to function intelligently and facilitate daily life. However, this makes modern vehicles more sensitive to electromagnetic (EM) disturbance, so it is necessary to evaluate EM responses in vehicle control systems during design phases. This paper proposes a model-based approach to evaluate influences of harness shielding and grounding on induced EM responses in vehicle control systems. It takes the control system of a commercial aircraft engine as an example, and constructs the engine control system model integrated from electrical devices and interconnecting multi-branched cable harnesses. The control system is then grounded onto an engine casing serving as the conducting ground, and exposed to EM disturbances generated by plane waves from four directions respectively. Numerical experiment results conclude that: perfect electrical conductor (PEC) shall be used as the conducting ground for vehicle control system EM response evaluation processes; harness shielding may change control system resonant frequencies and shall be equipped for EM response reduction; the grounding of electrical loadings negates the harness shielding effects and amplifies the induced EM responses. These study results provide guidance for designing vehicle control systems immune to EM disturbance who improves the performance reliability of vehicles.

title: Implementation and Evaluation of Networked Model Predictive Control System on Universal Robot
authors: Mahsa Noroozi; Kai Wang
abstract: Networked control systems are closed-loop feedback control systems containing system components that may be distributed geographically in different locations and interconnected via a communication network such as the Internet. The quality of network communication is a crucial factor that significantly affects the performance of remote control. This is due to the fact that network uncertainties can occur in the transmission of packets in the forward and backward channels of the system. The two most significant among these uncertainties are network time delay and packet loss. To overcome these challenges, the networked predictive control system has been proposed to provide improved performance and robustness using predictive controllers and compensation strategies. In particular, the model predictive control method is well-suited as an advanced approach compared to conventional methods. In this paper, a networked model predictive control system consisting of a model predictive control method and compensation strategies is implemented to control and stabilize a robot arm as a physical system. In particular, this work aims to analyze the performance of the system under the influence of network time delay and packet loss. Using appropriate performance and robustness metrics, an in-depth investigation of the impacts of these network uncertainties is performed. Furthermore, the forward and backward channels of the network are examined in detail in this study.

title: Application of Improved Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm in constant pressure water supply system
authors: Mingzhu Li; Xi Feng
abstract: Due to the hysteresis and non-linearity of constant pressure water supply control system, it is difficult to realize accurate control of water supply pressure. To address this problem, an IABC-PID control algorithm based on improved artificial bee colony algorithm is proposed in this paper. To address the shortcomings of the basic artificial bee colony algorithm, which converges slowly and is prone to local optimality, a full dimensional learning strategy is introduced in the neighborhood search of the employed foragers. At the same time, Gaussian variation and chaotic perturbations are introduced to enhance the local search capability and increase the population diversity, thus speeding up the convergence speed and improving the search accuracy. The simulation results show that the IABC- PID control algorithm outperforms the ABC-PID method in terms of convergence speed, search accuracy and operational stability. Compared with the response curve method, the IABC-PID algorithm has no overshoot, small adjustment time, better dynamic performance, steady-state performance and robustness. The algorithm provides a theoretical basis for real-time online PID parameter rectification of constant pressure water supply system and provides an effective means for energy saving and consumption reduction of pumps.

title: A Launch Device for Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Used in Water Conveyance Tunnel
authors: Cheng Zhang; Wenyang Gan; Zhenzhong Chu; Haikun Di
abstract: This paper addresses the problems of low efficiency and poor safety during the launch of autonomous underwater robots (AUVs) in tunnels, and proposes a launch device based on a crawler chassis for overcoming the strong currents at the tunnel entrance and effectively improving the environmental adaptability of AUVs when operating in the tunnel environment. In this paper, the overall scheme and hardware platform of the launch device are introduced in detail.

title: Study on the Psychological Acceptance of Level 3 Autonomous Driving
authors: Yilian Li; Wenyu Wu; Chang Gao; Chenhao Li
abstract: The emergence of autonomous vehicles (AVs) has brought numerous conveniences and development opportunities to human society, but it has also raised safety concerns. In recent years, AVs have been involved in multiple traffic accidents for various reasons, resulting in a continuous decline in user acceptance. In response, we need to propose some hypotheses to investigate the relationship between traffic accidents and the decline in user acceptance. This paper aims to summarize and generalize the objective problems observed during a real vehicle observation experiment and conduct in-depth interviews with participants regarding their usage scenarios, objectives, interactive behaviors, and operational methods related to AVs. By analyzing the factors that influence user acceptance, we will further develop, improve, and integrate the psychological factors affecting drivers' behaviors based on AVs, ultimately creating a model for the influencing factors of user acceptance in AVs.

title: Biomechanical Study of Passive and Active Exoskeletons for Analyzing the Dependent Parameters for an Intelligent Control System
authors: Rajal Nagwekar; Joscha Sonnenschein; Seyed Milad Mir Latifi; Ramazan Gökay; Robert Weidner
abstract: In recent years, various exoskeletons have been developed to support specific movements and body regions. Exoskeletons are normally designed taking into account particular use cases and developed to support a certain body region and movement. While conducting a biomechanical study with different exoskeletons, it was realized that certain parameters could be efficiently used to control an exoskeleton. The present biomechanical study analyses the dependent parameters of exoskeletons, which inform the potential merits of integrating an intelligent control system. In the study, five test subjects were required to perform three distinct tasks, which were inspired by real-world scenarios, using a passive, active, and exoskeleton-free approach. The data was collected using electromyography sensors, a force plate and motion capture as well as using questionnaires. Firstly, it was demonstrated that active exoskeletons have a stabilizing effect on their wearers. Secondly, it was shown that these exoskeletons are fundamentally suitable for supporting their users in specific tasks. Nevertheless, the evidence also indicated that the incorporation of intelligent systems into exoskeletons can be particularly beneficial for predicting movement. This leads to the conclusion that active exoskeletons have a distinctive potential that can be harnessed through the integration of intelligent control systems.

title: A Review of Security Threats and Response Scheme for Wireless Sensor Networks
authors: Weiping Feng; Cuilian Liu
abstract: To gain a deeper understanding of the security problems of wireless sensor networks (WSNs), to analyze the current developments, and to enhance their vulnerability, this paper introduced knowledge about WSNs, analyzed the various attacks faced by WSNs, and proposed a set of solutions based on network security techniques. Additionally, WSNs security solutions such as key management, route management, and digital signatures are explored and concluded. Finally, several techniques to protect against attacks at various levels of WSNs are presented.

title: Decoupling Analysis of Maglev Variable Stiffness Joints Based on Permanent Magnet
authors: Kang Luo; Mingda Zhai; Jianbin Chen; Chengtao He; Xinwei Li; Ming Zhang
abstract: Variable stiffness joints, due to their variable stiffness feature, have promising application prospects in fields such as human rehabilitation and military surveillance. However, currently, variable stiffness joints generally have problems of weak nonlinearity and difficulty in decoupling. Based on this and previous related work, the paper proposes a novel maglev variable stiffness joint, which contains permanent magnet repulsion force that provides a nonlinear property similar to that of the human elbow. And through structural and static research, a decoupling analysis method of joint stiffness and rotational angle is proposed. The research not only provides a technical path for the hominine nonlinear characteristics of variable stiffness joints but also provides theoretical support for the subsequent control of maglev variable stiffness joints.

title: Semantic Segmentation Algorithm of Remote Sensing Images Based on Improved Panoptic
authors: Tong Zheng; Liu Liu; Qimeng Chen; Zhong Chen; Longji Yu; Zeyu Zhao
abstract: Semantic segmentation of images can play an important role in land use, building extraction, road extraction and vehicle detection using remote sensing images. In the scenario of applying Panoptic FPN algorithm for remote sensing images, we found that the decoder of this algorithm is not robust in feature extraction and cannot do weighted enhancement of key spaces and channels, and its encoder loses a lot of high-dimensional semantic features when simply fusing semantic information at all levels by simple addition. To address these two problems, we propose the Se-Resnext encoder based on the attention mechanism and the Concat-based feature fusion mechanism, respectively, and verify the effectiveness of the methods through experiments. The accuracy of semantic segmentation is improved in both suichang dataset and posdam dataset.

title: Research on Emergence Reconnaissance Mechanism of Electromagnetic Agent Based on Sand Pile Model
authors: Yongkun Zhou; Guiquan Cai; Di Zhao; Bin Rao; Wei Wang
abstract: Based on the theory of self-organized criticality, an emergence reconnaissance model of electromagnetic agents is provided by applying the sand pile model. Firstly, the evolutionary rules of the traditional sand pile model are reviewed. Then, the emergence reconnaissance model of electromagnetic agent is developed based on the actual scenario. When the pheromones of an electromagnetic agent exceed a certain threshold, an "avalanche" phenomenon occurs and the electromagnetic agent reports the reconnaissance results through remote communication, which means that an emergence reconnaissance is completed. At the same time, to ensure sufficient reconnaissance resources were provided, all pheromones of the radiation source will be gradually eliminated through the link of short-range communication. Finally, through simulation experiments, the power-law distribution characteristics of the electromagnetic agent emergence reconnaissance model are verified.

title: Stable Capturing Strategy in the Dual-arm Time-Delay Capturing System with Hardware Closed Chain
authors: Xiaoyu Zhao; Yang Liu; Zongwu Xie
abstract: When a multi-manipulator system is employed to carry out a capturing task, the hardware closed chain is formed. The capturing process with hardware closed chain may fail when the robot control system has non-negligible time delay. In this paper, the mathematical model of the capturing system is built and simplified for a feasible stability analysis. Three-dimensional root-locus is applied to explore the system stable condition and promote the stable capturing strategy. Simulations are carried out to validate the proposed theory and the results show that the system controlled by the strategy shows a considerable convergence.

title: Image Enhancement and Detection of Courier Slips Based on Affine Transform
authors: Xin Wang; Fan Xu; Yan Ye; Yishen Xu
abstract: Aiming at the problem of courier slip information extraction in a complex environment, a courier slip image enhancement and detection algorithm based on affine transformation is studied and proposed, which enhances the courier bill image in a complex environment by gamma transformation and automatic color equalization algorithm, and quickly locates the courier slip subject based on the barcode position in combination with the actual situation Then the affine transformation is introduced to detect the courier slip. Simulation and comparison experiment is conducted using Python and OpenCV, the results of which show that the algorithm can effectively improve the traditional OCR algorithm when the picture has low brightness or high exposure, the courier bill has a small proportion in the picture and the direction is difficult to determine, and improve the positioning efficiency and recognition success rate of the courier slips. It can be combined with technologies such as robotic arms and AGV omnidirectional mobile chassis and is widely used in various sorting scenarios such as logistics transfer.

title: Towards a Self-Describing Gateway-Based IoT Solution
authors: Bogdan Iancu; Andrei Gatea
abstract: This paper proposes a solution to the problem of connecting non-interoperable IoT protocols, standards and hardware and to achieve interoperability by providing a unified solution. The main goal is achieved by creating a IoT gateway along with a self-describing protocol which allows interoperability between heterogeneous devices and systems and provides secure communication capabilities. An experimental proof of concept was deployed, combining both hardware and software components, in order to demonstrate the solution’s capabilities and present the possible limitations. The proposed system is designed as a secure, open-source, vendor-agnostic and device-agnostic solution.

title: Adaptive Disturbance Observer-Based Trajectory Tracking Control for the Follower of Close Formation UAVs
authors: Hengyuan Chang; Dawei Lu; Xin Peng; Dehua Chen; Gun Li; Changrong Zhang
abstract: This paper studies the trajectory tracking control problem of slave aircraft during close formation flight. The aerodynamic disturbances caused by the pilot aircraft are considered. In order to compensate for the disturbance in close formation, an uncertainty and disturbance estimator (UDE) based on low-pass filtering is considered. However, the estimation performance is determined by the constant parameters adjusted by the designer, which could make the performance unsatisfactory, especially under discontinuous disturbance. So the corresponding adaptive disturbance observer is designed for each channel of the aerodynamic model and compensated for in the controller design. In addition, the controller design is based on the idea of backstepping control to cope with matched and unmatched disturbances to ensure the performance of asymptotic tracking control. The stability of the system is demonstrated by Lyapunov theory. The effectiveness and performance advantages of the proposed strategy are verified by numerical simulation and simulation comparison. The result shows that both the transient time and steady-state errors are optimized by nearly three orders of magnitude, indicating superior performance of adaptive disturbance observer-based trajectory tracking controller.

title: Classification Accuracy and Speed Search Using Career Site Page Focus-Based Web Crawler and Harmony Search Algorithm
authors: Fahrurrozi Lubis; Ainul Hizriadi; Arya Pratama Tarigan
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Control & [::Automation::]; Electronics; [::Robotics::]; Internet of Things; and Artificial Intelligence (CERIA)
abstract: Career site pages contain valuable information for job seekers, but effectively classifying these pages into relevant categories remains a challenge. This study aims to develop a classification system for career website pages using the Harmony Search algorithm, enhanced by a Focused Web Crawler for data collection. The Focused Web Crawler extracts relevant job tags and features from career site pages, which are then used as training data for the classification algorithm. Experiments were conducted with various parameters, including job tags, the number of features (50), and Harmony Search algorithm settings. The results show that with 500 web pages and optimized algorithm parameters, the system achieved a classification accuracy of up to 95%. The system outperforms alternative parameter configurations, demonstrating that the combination of 50 features and specific Harmony Search parameters, such as HMCR and PAR set at 0.5, leads to the best performance. This system can assist users in efficiently finding job information tailored to their needs and skills. Moreover, it serves as a reference for future classification systems using similar techniques and algorithms.

title: (r; Q) Inventory Control in Multi-Modal Distribution Systems with Flexible Channel Allocation
authors: Przemysław Ignaciuk
abstract: In order to improve supply system robustness, or gain cost advantage, multiple delivery modes may be used. In this work, the (r, Q) inventory policy is formally investigated as a tool to control the resupply process of a remote depot that answers uncertain market demand. In the considered scenario, the goods are relocated using multiple channels with diverse properties concerning transportation delay, lot size, and quality, e.g., trucks, or trains. The lot partitioning strategy is adapted on the fly to the current channel characteristics. A dynamic model of the supplier-depot interaction is built and used to evaluate the policy properties in a robust control framework. Using the constructed framework, it is explicitly shown how to select the policy parameters to obtain full demand realization, thus eliminating backorders, irrespective of the pattern of delay and demand fluctuations. It is also discussed how to assign the warehouse space at the depot so that emergency storage will not be required even though, as a result of channel disruptions, deliveries from a few periods arrive simultaneously, or out of order.

title: Research on Visual Odometry of Planar Motion Wheeled Robot Based on RGB-D Camera
authors: Chenggong Wang; Gen Li; Lin Li; Ruiqi Wang
abstract: Based on the motion characteristics of the planar motion wheeled robot with RGB-D camera, the contour constraint conditions were proposed in the image processing part of visual odometer to screen out the mismatched feature points, and a new calculation method was proposed in the inter-frame motion calculation part. Firstly, the contour constraint condition was established according to the motion constraint of the planar wheeled robot camera. This constraint condition could not only screen out the color map mismatch, but also screen out the matching point pairs with correct color map matching but large depth value error. Then, in the inter-frame motion calculation part of the camera, the transfer matrix was reduced in dimension and the least squares problem was constructed on the basis of linearization approximation. Finally, the linearization approximation calculation error was dynamically compensated to obtain the two-dimensional motion parameters of the robot camera. The experimental results showed that compared with RANSAC algorithm, the algorithm exhibited higher calculation accuracy. Compared with RANSAC algorithm and ICP algorithm, the operation time of this algorithm was reduced by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$89.08{{\% }}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$52.38{{\% }}$</tex>, respectively.

title: Design of a Soft Hand Rehabilitation Robot
authors: Xiaohui Wang; Qinkun Cheng; Zhifeng Wang; Naishi Feng
abstract: This paper presents a novel soft pneumatic hand rehabilitation robot equipped with bidirectional bending actuators. It is capable of performing various rehabilitation postures and assisting with grasping tasks. The main bending module features a three-chamber structure, which increases the range of rehabilitation training postures and bending angles for the fingers. The reverse bending module has a trapezoidal chamber design to enhance reverse bending capabilities. The experimental results show that at a pressure of 130 kPa, the thumb can generate a 2.5 N fingertip force, and reverse bending can generate a 1.2 N fingertip force. Other single fingers can generate a 1.6 N fingertip force, with reverse bending producing a 1.0 N fingertip force. The robot can grasp up to 260 g and perform various object grasping tasks. By supplying air to different finger joints, it can assist in both finger extension and flexion. This is significantly advantageous for the rehabilitation of patients suffering from partial hand function impairment.

title: An Optimal Multi-Agent Path Planning Method Based on Priority Setting and Collision Detection
authors: Long Zhang; Haining Zhang; Qian Zhang; Yameng Zhao
abstract: In traditional multi-agent path planning research, algorithms typically focus on single-instance path planning problems, with limited consideration given to path disruptions caused by unforeseen circumstances. When such disruptions occur, re-invoking global path planning algorithms often neglects the agent's prior state of movement, which can lead to reduced efficiency, such as unnecessary deceleration. This paper proposes a novel path planning algorithm based on Yen's algorithm, aimed at addressing the issue of inconsistencies between the initial paths and subsequently planned paths. During experimental tests, the proposed method demonstrates its ability to effectively enhance both the path planning efficiency and fault tolerance of multi-agent systems, offering a better solution for multi-agent path planning.

title: AES Model with Logic Rule Reasoning and Self-Explanation Based on AMR and LLM
authors: Jiaxing Sun; Qing Zhang; Jie Liu; Liyuan Zhang
abstract: Automated Essay Scoring (AES) has great potential in real-world applications. However, AES models function as black boxes, which makes it challenging for users to comprehend the rationale behind scoring decisions and ultimately diminishes trust.
