Moreover, to simulate the presence of IMU noise, the accelerometers' biases are estimated and treated as time-varying variables rather than fixed constants. A simulation study is conducted to demonstrate the validity and efficacy of the proposed angular velocity estimation methodologies.

title: Improving Road Safety With Enhanced Vehicle Detection for Night-time Traffic in Mirpur
authors: Usama Younis; Faisal Riaz; Umar Raza; Gokhan Atali; Hamid Rabnawaz
abstract: This paper presents a study on improving night-time vehicle detection in the Mirpur region through a modified neural network model. Given the challenges of low visibility at night, the research focused on optimizing a deep learning algorithm to enhance detection accuracy. A dataset of 10,000 images covering various vehicle types was collected and annotated to train and test the model. The study found a 7% increase in detection performance compared to the standard model, highlighting the potential for tailored algorithms in specific environmental conditions. The findings suggest significant implications for road safety and autonomous driving systems, particularly in regions with similar night-time driving challenges. The research contributes to the broader field of computer vision by showing the effectiveness of model optimization in real-world conditions.

title: Dynamic Temporal Convolutional Networks for Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearings
authors: Jingxiang Hu; Haojie Chen; Yongyi Chen; Dan Zhang
abstract: Since rolling bearing plays a crucial role in rotating machinery, the fault diagnosis research of it has been widely concerned in recent years. However, the collected fault signals often contain a lot of noise interference due to the complex and changeable operating environment. The anti noise capability of traditional deep learning methods is weak, resulting in poor feature extraction performance. Therefore, the dynamic temporal convolutional network (DyTCN) is presented for rolling bearing fault diagnosis in this article. Specifically, the causal dilation convolution is first designed to acquire fault feature of vibration signal by enlarging receptive field of the network. Then, the dynamically adjusted convolution kernel parameters are used to achieve adaptive acquisition of dynamic features and improve the robustness. Extensive experimental results on real dataset demonstrate that DyTCN has excellent accuracy in fault diagnosis.

title: Jerk-limited Traversal of One-dimensional Paths and its Application to Multi-dimensional Path Tracking
authors: Jonas C. Kiemel; Torsten Kröger
abstract: In this paper, we present an iterative method to quickly traverse multi-dimensional paths considering jerk constraints. As a first step, we analyze the traversal of each individual path dimension. We derive a range of feasible target accelerations for each intermediate waypoint of a one-dimensional path using a binary search algorithm. Computing a trajectory from waypoint to waypoint leads to the fastest progress on the path when selecting the highest feasible target acceleration. Similarly, it is possible to calculate a trajectory that leads to minimum progress along the path. This insight allows us to control the traversal of a one-dimensional path in such a way that a reference path length of a multi-dimensional path is approximately tracked over time. In order to improve the tracking accuracy, we propose an iterative scheme to adjust the temporal course of the selected reference path length. More precisely, the temporal region causing the largest position deviation is identified and updated at each iteration. In our evaluation, we thoroughly analyze the performance of our method using seven-dimensional reference paths with different path characteristics. We show that our method manages to quickly traverse the reference paths and compare the required traversing time and the resulting path accuracy with other state-of-the-art approaches.

title: The Influence Factors on High Frequency Primary Calibration of Single-Ended Accelerometers
authors: Jie Zhou; Wen He; Yanan Yu
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Being different from the low frequency or medium frequency primary calibration of the accelerometers by the laser interferometer, the high frequency primary calibration of the single-ended accelerometers suffers some influence factors for the calibration result, including the amplitude distribution asymmetry of the mounting surface, the rocking motion, the contact stiffness, etc. The reasons of these influence factors are theoretically analyzed and verified by experiments, and correspondingly a series of methods are adopted to eliminate or decrease the influence of these factors. The proposed methods can provide a reference for the high frequency primary calibration of single-ended accelerometers.

title: Adaptive Finite-Time Preassigned Performance Control for Hypersonic Vehicles with Lumped Perturbations
authors: Chengfeng Luo; Rugang Tang; Xin Ning; Zheng Wang
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive finite-time preassigned performance control (PPC) approach to solve the attitude control problem of hypersonic vehicles (HSVs) suffering from lumped disturbances. A specific preassigned performance function guaranteeing finite-time stability and small overshoot is presented to constrain the attitude tracking errors. Moreover, a novel synchronous disturbance estimation is presented to build a disturbance observer (DO). Based on the devised preassigned performance function and the information from the DO, an adaptive finite-time preassigned performance controller is devised to solve the attitude control problem. Finally, numerical examples demonstrate the validity of the presented algorithm.

title: Research and Implementation of Unknown Environment Map Construction Method with Lidar-based Robot
authors: Cheng-gang Lu; Jin-xiang Wang; Xu Cui
abstract: The role of mobile robots is becoming more and more important. In the meantime, It is the basis for the robot to build a map in an unknown environment autonomously. In this paper, by using ROS robot and 360 distance laser sensor LDS-01, the laser scanning information is acquired in real-time, Synchronous map construction in real-time through the fusion of robot self-positioning information and environmental information. Update existing maps in real-time during the build process, ultimately enabling map construction of the entire unknown environment. By testing in the simulator Gazebo and building an indoor environment map, the test results in the actual environment show that the method of this paper can construct the unknown environment map more accurately and in real-time.

title: A Method for Constructing Building Structure Grid Map Based on a Climbing Algorithm
authors: Xidong Zhou; Hang Zhong; Hui Zhang; Mingyuan Chen; Haoyang Yu; Weizheng Wang; Yaonan Wang
abstract: Aerial-terrestrial amphibious robots excel in search and rescue tasks in unstructured terrains but face challenges in autonomous navigation indoors. Traditional full-mapping methods can degrade global path planning performance, especially when semi-static obstacles shift, leading to suboptimal paths. We propose a method for constructing building structure grid maps that are unaffected by semistatic obstacles. Our approach includes a building structure recognition algorithm based on an octree structure to differentiate between occupied and free grid cells. Experimental results demonstrate that coverage path planning on building structure grid maps produces superior global paths compared to traditional grid maps, offering a more streamlined and robust solution for autonomous navigation of aerial-terrestrial amphibious robots in indoor environments.

title: Workspace Analysis of 6-RSS Parallel Robot to Assist Cervical Laminectomy
authors: Jianze Liu; Jiangzhen Guo; Xianglong Li; Jia Liu; Jipeng Song; Lixiang Ding
abstract: Cervical laminectomy is a common clinical procedure to decompress the cervical spine. However, because of the limited operating space of cervical spine surgery, the surgeon's operation precision is required to be high. Robot-assisted surgery can usually achieve good precision by precise positioning and manipulation of the robot, while parallel robots can attain better precision due to their mechanical characteristics. Compared with other types of parallel robots, the 6-RSS has a simpler structure and lower mass of moving parts, and therefore performs better in human-robot interaction, which ensures the surgeon's precise operation. However, the kinematic analysis of 6-RSS parallel robots is usually more complicated than other types, making the workspace analysis difficult. In this paper, the theoretical mechanism model of the 6-RSS parallel robot was built and coordinates were defined. The workspace was analyzed to evaluate end rotation and movement ability, which can optimize the structural design and guide the robot design.

title: Autonomous Drone Shark Shield: A Novel Shark Repelling System for Protecting Swimmers and Surfers
authors: Xiaohui Li; Hailong Huang; Andrey V. Savkin
abstract: Aiming at protecting swimmers and surfers from shark attacks and preventing hurting sharks, we present a novel shark repelling system: Autonomous Drone Shark Shield, which uses flying drones to impede and prevent shark attacks. We introduce the design of the shark shield system and the strategy for expelling sharks. A shark interception algorithm was developed to steer drones to intercept moving sharks. The effectiveness of the proposed method is proved by computer simulation.

title: A Fatigue Detection Algorithm for Manufacturing Workers Based on Face Alignment
authors: Jinlei Cui; Honglei Shao; Fangyan Dong; Kewei Chen
abstract: To address the issue that the recognition rate of face fatigue features decreases rapidly with the change of face posture of workers at fixed site stations in manufacturing industry, an algorithm FatiguePoseNet(FPN) is proposed for face posture correction and fatigue recognition. Based on the improved Retinaface face detector and the 3DDFA face alignment model, the algorithm firstly detects the worker's face image with high accuracy, and extracts 68 3D key points coordinates of the face. Subsequently, key points around the eyes and mouth are projected onto planes defined by the selected left eye, right eye, and mouth points. Based on the projected key points, the eye aspect ratio (EAR) and mouth aspect ratio (MAR) are calculated, from which the eyelid closure rate (PERCLOS) and yawning rate (YR) are derived to assess the worker's fatigue level. Experimental results from three datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can accurately compute and recognize eye and mouth states within a facial yaw angle range of (−90° - +90°), effectively detecting facial fatigue. The algorithm shows high accuracy and robustness in recognizing worker fatigue, offering a viable solution to mitigate the performance degradation in face recognition caused by changes in the working environment or worker postures. This approach presents a promising tool for fatigue monitoring in the manufacturing industry.

title: Polarization-Guided Domain-Adaptive Network for Underwater Image Enhancement
authors: Guangyao Ju; Jiqing Zhang; Xianping Fu
abstract: Marine exploration heavily relies on underwater imagery, yet these images often suffer from significant quality deterioration caused by harsh aquatic imaging conditions, such as color distortion, haze effects, and non-uniform illumination. While recent advances in underwater image enhancement have revealed that deep learning techniques can produce significant improvements, most approaches rely exclusively on RGB intensity information, overlooking polarization, a valuable optical property that can significantly improve restoration. To overcome these challenges, we introduce UPDD, a polarization-guided underwater image enhancement network that systematically integrates polarization cues (AOP/DOP) with intensity data through a novel Polarization-Aware Guidance Module (PGM) for effective multi-modal fusion. Furthermore, UPDD incorporates a domain-adaptive decoder with gradient reversal layers to enhance generalization across diverse underwater environments. Extensive experiments on the RGBP-UIE dataset demonstrate UPDD's superior performance, particularly in turbid and low-light scenarios. UPDD providing a practical solution for real-world underwater imaging applications. Additionally, the proposed framework offers a flexible foundation for future multi-modal UIE research.

title: Exploring the Capability of Deep Neural Network on Ship Sub-Assembly Weld Seam Recognition
authors: Xuyue Yin; Shihao Kang; Ruixue Zhang; Naikun Wei; Jun Jiang
abstract: To address the problem of robot weld process planning for complex ship sub-assembly work-pieces, this paper explores the capability of the deep neural network models on seam cloud point segmentation tasks. By studying and leveraging the performance of three popular point cloud segmentation models, we choose PointNet++ as the backbone and introduce three improvements to enhance its performance on the weld seam segmentation problem. First, a multi-perspective edge detection method is proposed to improve segmentation accuracy. Second, neighborhood sampling and fast farthest point sampling are introduced to improve the sampling efficiency. Finally, we use fewer convolution layers to reduce the time and space complexity and resolve the overfitting problem. A dataset of sub-assembly models containing 4 plate type classes and 5 seam type classes was established. The training and recognition performance of the advanced PointNet++ model was evaluated and compared with the traditional geometrical weld seam recognition method. The experimental results prove that the proposed method can adapt to 5 typical weld seam classes at a mIoU 83.38%, and it is robust to arbitrary work-piece layout positions, meanwhile, it reaches a speed at 15fps. All the above results demonstrate the great potential of deep neural networks on the robot weld applications for ship sub-assembly work-pieces.

title: Research on Ship Wake Measurement in Sea Based on Hyperspectral Imaging
authors: Dawei Li; Yunxuan Jiang; Zhifei Zhou; Haixin Deng; Mo Lin
abstract: Based on the UAV and hyperspectral measurement technology, the spectral energy density of the wake center region and the kelvin region is obtained. In contrast, the spectral absorption peak of the two regions is little different. The kelvin wake can be regarded as the modulation effect of the target on the rough sea surface waveform, which does not change the spectral absorption coefficient of the sea surface itself, and the modulation degree of the wake in different regions is different. As a result, the reflection degree of the sea surface to the background light is different, so the wake region presents the characteristics of light and dark changes, the principle of which is consistent with the detection principle of the convergence and divergence of the sea surface in SAR.

title: A study of IIoT as an enabler of next-generation intelligent manufacturing
authors: Purvi Manish Charde; A. Seetharaman
abstract: The advent of Industrial Internet of Things (IoT), has changed the definition of efficiency and operations for manufacturing companies. Assimilation of machine learning, cyber-physical systems and Artificial Intelligence through Industrial IoT is emerging into an intelligent manufacturing system that transcend beyond the linear expectations of operational efficiency. This manuscript brings forth; through the systematic review of multivocal literature, a study about the impact of Technology Adoption, Data security and Human-Cyber-Physical system on the Industrial Internet of Things (IoT) as a key enabler of next-generation intelligent manufacturing, along with the prepositions for the transformation of industries and opportunities for future research.

title: Gameplay Generation System Based on Game Description Language
authors: Zetao Zhang; Yiran Sun; Chaohui Du; Jinsheng Jiang; Xing Sun
abstract: This study defines a specialized game description language, CCGDL, and develops an automated gameplay generation system called Creative Game Machine based on CCGDL. The system facilitates automated gameplay generation and quality evaluation by employing techniques like parent selection and rule crossover, ensuring controllable gameplay quality. Additionally, the study introduces a quantitative analysis method for gameplay quality, utilizing machine learning algorithms to predict gameplay quality. The system significantly reduces design cycles and development costs, demonstrating the potential to enhance traditional game design methodologies.

title: Microporous Magnetic Soft Materials with Programmable Locomotion and On-Demand Liquid Cargo Release
authors: Youyi Zhou; Fatih Kocabas; Yunus Alapan
publication_title: 2025 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Magnetic soft elastomers with spatially programmed magnetization profiles can generate complex shape-morphing and locomotion dynamics. Enabled by their unique locomotion capabilities, magnetically programmed soft robots have been proposed for various biomedical applications, including targeted and localized delivery of aqueous cargos, such as therapeutic drugs. Current magnetic soft material designs for targeted cargo delivery employ dedicated chambers for loading and integrated valve mechanisms for release, which can severely affect the locomotion capabilities or necessitate complicated designs for actuation. Therefore, new strategies are required for incorporating liquid payloads into magnetic soft materials without affecting their locomotion modality, preserving these payloads during transport, and on-demand release via external stimuli once the target location is reached. In this paper, we present magnetic soft elastomers with an interconnected porous internal structure, enabling loading of aqueous payloads into the material while preserving magnetic programmability. Furthermore, microcrystalline wax sealing on the outer surface allows selective functionalities of locomotion at lower magnetic fields and on-demand release of cargos at greater magnetic fields. The cargo loading and on-demand release strategy introduced here enables magnetically co-encoding locomotion and cargo-release and establishes the groundwork for multifunctional magnetic soft materials with potential applications ranging from soft robotics to medical devices and biointerfaces.

title: Trinary Relationship Interaction Detection
authors: Fangqun Gao; YunTao Wu; Yanduo Zhang; Tao Lu; Pan Tang; Liwei Wang; Jifeng Han; Wanghui Wu
abstract: In various specialized operational scenarios, particularly those involving tool usage, the capacity to detect relationships between entities is crucial for understanding complex interactions. Traditional methods, which typically focus on unary or binary relationship detections, often fall short in capturing the subtleties present in such environments. This paper introduces the HTOI (Human Tool Object Interaction) model, a novel and pioneering approach to trinary relationship detection that addresses these limitations. The HTOI model has been designed to excel in complex interaction scenarios, including those characterized by the use of tools, as evidenced by its exceptional performance on our TData dataset. This dataset specifically highlights the nuanced actions of electric utility workers during tool-assisted operations, underscoring the model’s ability to detect intricate interactions with higher accuracy and reliability compared to existing HOI (Human Object Interaction) techniques. Our study aims to showcase the HTOI model’s significant advancement in the field of relationship detection, offering a valuable tool for analyzing and interpreting complex operational interactions involving tools.

title: Integration of IoT Platform Environment for Web Server and Global Connectivity Based on ESP32
authors: Daniel Amani Noordin; Nur Zulaikhah Nadzri; Raja Fazliza Raja Suleiman
abstract: This study aims to simplify IoT development by creating a comprehensive platform environment centered on the ESP32 microcontroller, known for its low cost, power efficiency, integrated Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth capabilities. The platform will address the complexities of traditional IoT development, such as multiple development stages and diverse peripheral requirements, by integrating key components into an easy-to-use library. The library developed includes a dashboard system, SPIFFS management, Wi-Fi setup, a web server, and support for the MQTT protocol. The created environment introduces a Docker Compose setup featuring Node-RED, an MQTT broker, and a database, alongside a web-flasher tool and example projects for developers. A Cloudflare tunnel ensures global accessibility, allowing local servers to be accessed from anywhere. A "Smart Home Application" was applied to demonstrate the platform's capabilities, with innovations such as precompiled binaries that simplify device deployment. This user-friendly IoT platform enhances scalability, security, and manageability, making it easier for developers to build efficient and innovative IoT solutions. Several users with basic embedded coding experience were asked to use the library to evaluate the platform's acceptance based on two popular survey approaches: the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTUAT). The survey results have shown that more than 80% of users accepted the platform, with an average mean score of 4.488 out of 5.0 on the components highlighted in TAM and UTAUT. Therefore, this integrated platform enables developers to simplify IoT development, making it more efficient and accessible, and allowing them to create innovative IoT solutions.

title: Optimal control of unmanned robotic platform
authors: Sławomir Stępień; Marcin Chodnicki
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper proposes an infinite-time horizon suboptimal control strategy based on state-dependent Riccati equation (SDRE) to control of unmanned ground vehicle (UGV). Cruise control of unmanned robotic platform is modelled and simulated. For vehicle modelling purpose a full 6 DOF model is considered and described by nonlinear state-space approach. Also a stable state-dependent parametrization (SDP) necessary for solution of the SDRE control problem is proposed and presented. Solution of the SDRE control problem with adequate defined weighting matrices in performance index shows possibility of fast and optimal vehicle control in infinite-time horizon. The method in this form can be used for mission planning of each ground vehicle tracking and dynamics control.

title: Inference about Transient States of Innovative RCM Structure for Soft Tissue Surgery Using FEM Taking into Account Inputs from in Vitro Experiment on Cardiovascular Tissue
authors: Grzegorz Ilewicz
abstract: -Surgical robots with the RCM mechanical systems are used clinically in such areas of surgery as: laparoscopy, heart surgery and urology. Transient state analysis using the FEM method of the innovative surgical robot structure based on the RCM mechanism with four degrees of freedom was performed. Such the mechanism enables the movement of the constant point, which extends its possibilities in relation to classic constant point mechanisms used in hospitals. The mesh computational model enables determination of: stresses, displacements and strains during transient analysis based on the von Mises hypothesis. Experienced cardiac surgeon performed in vitro experiment on cardiovascular tissue using endoscopic instruments for positioning and tissue incision activities. The trajectory of endoscopic instruments was determined using four optical CMOS sensors. A problem of the endoscope position was solved using APAS software and DLT algorithm. The Savitzky - Golay polynomial smoothing was used to filter a signal from the random component. The width of the numerical window for the SG procedure was determined based on the Durbin-Watson formula. Values of stresses related to the safety factor, displacements related to the positioning accuracy and repeatability as well as strains determining a susceptibility of the surgical robot structure were obtained. On their basis, the safety factor was determined and it was found that from the point of view of its value, the structure is safe in relation to the analysis of transient states. The work made it possible to observe and evaluate the stress values and the susceptibility of the structure of the surgical robot during the analysis of transient states, taking into account inputs that occur during cardiac surgery.

title: HILO: A Large-Scale Heterogeneous Object Dataset for Benchmarking Robotic Grasping Approaches
authors: Xinchao Song; Sean Banerjee; Natasha Kholgade Banerjee
abstract: Robust object manipulation is essential for robotics applications in real-world environments, especially when handling diverse and complex everyday objects. To facilitate this research, we present HILO, a large-scale dataset of 253 real-world everyday objects and 288 diverse scenes. HILO bridges a crucial gap in existing manipulation datasets through its heterogeneity and dual-resolution approach, combining high-resolution individual object scans with low-resolution scans of cluttered scenes. This provides both the precise geometric data needed for grasp planning and realistic environmental context. The dataset's comprehensive representations enable rigorous benchmarking of robotic grasping algorithms. Our evaluation of three leading grasping algorithms-Contact-GraspNet, GraspNet Baseline, and DexNet 4.0-reveals critical trade-offs between grasp quantity and quality, demonstrating the dataset's value in advancing robotic grasping research. HILO's rich object diversity and dual-resolution methodology provide a foundation for developing more versatile robotic systems capable of reliable real-world robotic manipulation. Our dataset is available at https://terascale-all-sensing-research-studio.github.io/hilo_dataset/.

title: Path Following Control for Underactuated Marine Robots Based on Direct Dynamic Programming of Desired Yaw Angle
authors: Jiang Long; Chao Yang; Bo Geng; Xing Liu
abstract: For the problem of straight-line cruise, a control method for the path following of marine robots based on direct dynamic programming of the desired yaw angle is proposed in this paper for underactuated marine robots. Different from the typical path following control method, i.e., the line of sight algorithm (LOS), the desired yaw angle of marine robots is dynamically programmed directly according to the lateral error on the desired path in the Serret-Frenet (SF) frame, Hence, the lateral error of the robot is guaranteed to converge to zero. Meanwhile, the longitudinal error of the robot is reduced by timely adjusting the virtual velocity on the tangent line of the desired path point. Furthermore, the control law is obtained based on the programmed desired yaw angle and prescribed longitudinal velocity, together with RBF neural network estimation. Finally, the control scheme proposed in this paper is used on a marine robot for simulation verification by comparing with an extent improved LOS path following control method. The simulation results demonstrate that the longitudinal and lateral following accuracy and the smoothness of the control signals have better performance when applying the proposed control scheme.

title: Autonomous Inspection for Mobile Robot Based on Visual and Inertial SLAM
authors: Jiajun Chen; Fei Xie; Guisheng Yao; Shuai He
abstract: This paper introduces a position acquisition method and post-matching processing technique tailored for Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) based on visual -inertial fusion. In visual-inertial SLAM systems, the position estimation accuracy is improved by trust region dogleg optimization algorithm combined with manifold optimization in response to the problem of the limited accuracy of Direct Linear Transform (DLT) in the initialization stage. An inlier set generation technique based on second-order spatial compatibility (SC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) is proposed to improve the problem of partial error matching which is unavoidable in feature matching. In the feature tracking stage, a number of compatible point pairs are selected as seed points. In the loop closing stage, points with higher confidence are selected as seed points based on the principal eigenvector of the adjacency matrix of the graph. The VI-SLAM system is deployed and integrated to the physical prototype of the inspection robot, and the inspection capability of the robot is verified in indoor and outdoor scenarios with different characteristics. The results show that the inspection robot system built in this paper can stably complete inspection tasks in multiple scenarios.

title: Advancements in Theranostic Nanorobots for Early Detection and Targeted Therapy of Thrombosis
authors: Divyah Vengkadesvararamana; Wong Yung Keong; Eugene Chow Ho Meng; Densingh Samuel Raj Rajkumar; A.H. Irfaunul Azees
abstract: Relevance: The formation of thrombi within blood vessels plays a cardinal role in the mortality rate due to cardiovascular diseases, and recent advancements in nanotechnology have shown significant potential in addressing this issue. Standard medical treatments for thrombosis usually have drawbacks such as delayed detection, off-target effects, and increased bleeding risks. Due to the advancement of technology, theranostic nanorobots have emerged and offer a better solution for precise and safe thrombolysis.Aim: To investigate the possible application of multifunctional theranostic nanorobots in the diagnosis and treatment of thrombosis.Material and method: A systematic literature review search was performed across databases and journals including PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, ACS Nano, Journal of Nanobiotechnology using keywords related to theranostic nanorobots and thrombosis management. The searches were performed from studies published between January 2019 to March 2025 to compile the latest advancement in the field. Out of 41 studies selected, 31 articles were included for primary analysis, while 10 review and theoretical studies were used for introductionConclusion: Theranostic nanorobot have been proven as a transformative strategy in thrombosis management due to its combination of therapy and diagnostics. Continued development and implementation are strongly recommended to overcome the current barriers and increase therapeutic efficacy.

title: Disparity Error in Advanced Vision Sensors
authors: Jurek Z. Sasiadek; Mark J. Walker
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper reports research in which feature-based disparity error is reported against corresponding features identified in a subset of images in the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and Toyota Technological Institute (KITTI) stereo 2012 benchmark. The dataset provides real-world imagery. The theory behind finding corners or features, matching them across image pairs, and then calculating the resultant disparity is explained. These disparity results are compared against disparity data provided by the KITTI stereo 2012 dataset, to produce disparity errors. The disparity errors are graphed. Concluding remarks are discussed.

title: Multilingual Speech Command Recognition for Voice Controlled Robots and Smart Systems
authors: Askat Kuzdeuov; Huseyin Atakan Varol
abstract: Speech Command Recognition (SCR) has many applications in smart home systems, voice-controlled robots, and voice assistants. The modern SCR systems employ deep learning models trained on speech command datasets. Nowadays, the Google Speech Commands (GSC) dataset serves as a benchmark for training and evaluating SCR models, but it only includes English commands. In this work, we introduce an equivalent of the GSC for the Kazakh, Tatar, and Russian languages. We collected the dataset via a Telegram bot in real-world settings. The dataset includes the same 35 commands as GSC and contains 3,623 utterances for Kazakh, 3,547 for Tatar, and 1,625 for Russian. We trained and evaluated both monolingual and multilingual SCR models. The experimental results show that the multilingual model outperforms the monolingual models with an accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9 8. 5 7 \%}, \mathbf{9 9. 3 3 \%}, \mathbf{9 6. 8 6 \%}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9 7. 3 3 \%}$</tex> on the test sets of the Kazakh, Tatar, Russian datasets and GSC, respectively. Furthermore, we deployed the model on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16GB, achieving an average inference time of 0.008 seconds. This performance makes it suitable for real-time applications. We have made the dataset, source code, and pretrained models publicly available<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>https://github.com/IS2AI/Multilingual-Speech-Command-Recognition to encourage further research in this area.

title: A Cost-Efficient Scheme for Learning Robotics via Modeling; Simulation & Control Implementation
authors: Haoxuan Li; Xinye Lu; Yutong Chen; Liangjing Yang
abstract: This paper presents a learning scheme for the subject of robotics based on a cost-efficient practical procedure encompassing modeling, simulation and control. The proposed method combines analytical design with simulation-based visualization and interactive control implementation using an educational robot arm. Results of the interactive control are presented demonstrating the user interaction with the developed system. Finally, control implementation on hardware is described. It is hoped that this preliminary demonstration of a cost-efficient learning model could lay the foundation for prospective development of a more widely available learning paradigm for experiential active learning in robotics education.

title: Pulse Signal Peak Detection Algorithm Based on Improved Slope Method and Partitioning Method
authors: Guangda Lu; Wei Cai; Tinghang Guo; Zhuangzhuang Zhao; Xiaoqian Guo; Wenhao Sun
abstract: Chinese medicine has a long history, and pulse diagnosis can detect physiological and pathological changes in the human body. With the rise and development of artificial intelligence, the objectification and modernization of TCM has also come a long way. In the process of pulse diagnosis objectification, the extraction of feature datum points in the time domain is an indispensable step. In this paper, starting with the pulse wave time domain feature extraction method, we systematically summarize the feature point extraction methods, including single-period feature point feature extraction and multi-period feature point extraction, and then on this basis, combined with the extraction experience of the collected data, we propose an improved slope method and partition method (ISPA) for pulse wave feature extraction research.

title: Simulation and Optimization of Industrial Disassembly Paths using Position Based Dynamics
authors: Robert Hegewald; Nicola Wolpert; Elmar Schömer
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The finding of plausible assembly paths of industrial components is a relevant, actual, but not yet fully resolved research topic. For a fast and robust computation of such paths, rigid body sampling-based motion planning is used. To tackle the problem of unavoidable collisions due to overpressure of components or due to flexible fastening elements, the tolerance of minor collisions is necessary. Tolerating minor collisions always means the manipulation of the configuration space or the direct manipulation of objects in the workspace. These actions enable the computation of assembly paths on industrial data, but they affect (explicitly or implicitly) the shape of the objects and thus the physical plausibility of the computed paths. This makes it important to further analyze the assembly paths. In this paper, we propose a postprocessing method for indus-trial assembly paths that is based on Position Based Dynamics (PBD) and is able to simulate and optimize given assembly paths. We use the PBD framework to simulate and measure the object deformation along the assembly path. For the optimization of the path, we compare the deformed object to the original rigid object and we apply small corrections to the path that decrease the overall deformation. We show the effectiveness of our approach on an academic dataset that provides industrial disassembly scenarios.

title: Anesthesia Control Using Fractional Order Controller
authors: Eva-H. Dulf; Paul A. Pintea; Cristina I. Muresan
abstract: Anesthesia plays a crucial role in every surgery. Clinicians are faced with numerous conditions that need to be monitored and controlled. A computerized monitoring and control system would help them in this challenging task. Designing a control law for general anesthesia presents numerous challenges, particularly due to the nonlinear mapping of outputs and the complexity of achieving a feasible input trajectory. While the internal states of the mathematical model are linear, the output exhibits nonlinear behavior. This paper introduces a decomposition of the standard pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) model to develop an effective control strategy for drug administration in anesthesia. It is proposed a method to control the bispectral index (BIS), the main measure of unconsciousness of the patient. This approach aims to optimize anesthesia delivery by maintaining the BIS within a desired range, thereby enhancing patient safety and comfort. The methodology involves designing a fractional order controller to accurately track BIS reference values and adjust anesthetic infusion rates. The effectiveness of the controller is validated through simulations, demonstrating its potential to enhance the precision of anesthesia management. Key findings reveal that such type of control outperforms traditional methods in maintaining target BIS levels, minimizing the risks of over- or under-dosing.

title: Optimization Algorithm of Multi-Attribute Group Decision-Making Based on Information Entropy Theory
authors: Xuan Feng; Youbao Cai
abstract: The problems of complex mathematical models, high computational complexity, and repeated parameter adjustments in the subjective and objective weighting method is studied. Such problems are generally defined as multi-attribute group decision-making models. Multi-attribute group decision-making models have been widely applied in fields such as achievement evaluation, scientific research performance assessment, and project review, and are a popular research direction in the field of artificial intelligence. How to balance the subjectivity among experts and the objectivity of attribute weights is a challenging problem in the research of multi-attribute group decision-making models. The entropy weighting method is firstly used to obtain the objective weights of attributes. Then, the grey correlation degree method is applied to adjust the subjective weight. Finally, based on the minimum Kullback-Leibler divergence method criterion reflecting the distance between different weights, an optimization model is established to solve the integrated weight. It is provided a feasible weight integration method based on information entropy theory for multi-attribute group decision-making. A numerical experiment shows the feasibility and practicability of the method. It is provided a new solution to the problems of prioritizing quantity over quality in the performance evaluation of scientific research in universities and research institutions, which can effectively promote the enthusiasm of scientific and technological workers for scientific research innovation.

title: Research on Adaptive Friction Compensation for Electric Linear Load Simulator Based Backstepping controller
authors: Cao Da-wei; Fan Yuan-xun; Pan Wei-dong; Lu Peng-cheng; Zhang Jian-wei
abstract: The electric linear load simulator (ELLS) is one kind of servo system with uncertainties and disturbances such as friction nonlinear characters. In order to improve the loading accuracy of ELLS system, aiming at the friction torque existing in the system, we present adaptive friction Backstepping controller based on the LuGre friction model. Using Lyapunov stability theorem to prove the global asymptotic stability of the system. Backstepping control theory reorganizes system equations into multiple virtual subsystems. Design virtual control variables for each virtual subsystems, and obtain the system nonlinear controller by Backstepping recursion. Finally, simulation results show that: compared with the traditional force command feedforward compensation + PID controller, the adaptive friction Backstepping controller can better suppress the excess force, ELLS system output can achieve asymptotic tracking of the given force reference signal. The proposed control method can better suppress the effect of friction on ELLS system and improve the loading accuracy.

title: Optimized Object-aided SLAM for robots Based on Shufflenetv3 and Relocalization
authors: Qinyang Liu; Zhaoting Wu; Zhiyu Lu; Ruyue Jiang; Fei Xie; Jing Zhao
abstract: Autonomous mobile robots have experienced rapid development over the past few years, and real-time object detection and localization are considered to be their basic capabilities. In order to improve the robot’s object detection and relocalization performance, an optimized object SLAM based on Shumenetv3 and relocalization is proposed. Firstly, an enhanced lightweight object detection model Shufflenetv3 is suggested to be used to obtain the object detection of a specified object or multiple objects in the to-be-tested frame, which provides it with the benefits of quick computation and excellent accuracy. Secondly, the accuracy of relocalization is increased by employing the refined target object-aided technique. Finally, to validate the effectiveness of the improved lightweight target extraction, we evaluate the performance of our method utilizing the Pascal VOC 2012 datasets and compare it with YOLOv5 and YOLO-shufflenetv3 in precision and efficiency. Comparing the proposed method to YOLOv5 and YOLOshumenetv3, these quantitative evaluations demonstrate that it performs well with competitive inference times and the most memory-efficient inference. Additionally, we conduct experiments using a public TUM dataset, and the outcomes showed that our approach is far more reliable and consistent to guarantee robot application.

title: Virtual Motoneuron Learning Network for Trajectory Generation of Legged Robot
authors: Pengfei Yan; Yaguang Zhu; Qianru Yang; Chunchao Liu
abstract: Walking animals in nature have shown complex behavior tracks and motion patterns when adapting to their environment. In order to imitate these natural characteristics of animals in the motion system of legged robots, a virtual motoneuron learning network (VMLN) is constructed to convert goal-directed behavioral instructions into neural signal strength, thus generating signal processing mechanisms and behavioral responses similar to animals. The network is composed of a central pattern generator (CPG), a virtual motoneuron module (VMM), a foot motor nerve strength modulation module (FMM) and an error- based fast online learning mechanism called the dual integral learner (DIL). VMM receives rhythmic signals from CPG and generates different motions. These motions are controlled by global and local shape parameters of muscles activation and target guidance points. Then, the signals for driving the joint motors of the robot are obtained through the inverse kinematics module. Finally, we integrate the DIL into the virtual motoneuron network to ensure that the entire generated trajectory can be followed with low tracking error, so as to achieve more complex and flexible movements. The experimental results show that: 1) VMM can flexibly select the desired curve or surface from a group of curves or surfaces by modifying the shape parameters appropriately; 2) DIL can track the whole trajectory automatically, quickly and accurately, and realize fast learning of complex trajectory. Therefore, our proposed VMLN can generate active adaption and stress behavior according to signal feedback, and improve the motion agility, coordination and diversity of robots.

title: Spectral Clustering Based on Relation-Invariable Persistent Formation
authors: Xiaofeng Zhang; Bin Fu; Dengxiu Yu
abstract: In this paper, a spectral clustering method based on relation-invariable persistent formation (RIPF) is proposed, which can character the similarity graph succinctly. RIPF is an optimal formation, which can remain the formation by using least edges in the comminution graph. After generating the RIPF, the algorithm builds a network graph weighted according to distance between neighborhoods, and then applies spectral clustering. Three methods to construct similarity graphs in standard spectral clustering are ε -neighborhood graph, k- nearest neighbor graph, or fully connected graph. However, ε -neighborhood graph or k -nearest neighbor graph is sensitive to the parameters ε or k, and fully connected similarity graph of which is redundant. The similarity graph is constructed by generating RIPF, which can model the concise local neighborhood relationships by using the least edges in similarity graph. In this paper, a new algorithm is proposed to weaken the parameter dependence while maintaining the solution quality. Experimental results show that out algorithm performs as well as or even better than the state-of-the-art standard spectral methods.

title: Miniature Dielectric Elastomer Actuator Probe Inspecting Confined Spaces Embedding a CMOS Sensor
authors: Sahib Sandhu; Ang Leo Li; Codrin Tugui; Mihai Duduta
abstract: Navigating and inspecting confined space is crucial for the aerospace and healthcare industries. Exploring smaller and narrower spaces allows for problems to be identified earlier, preventing negative outcomes for patients and equipment. The challenge is to scale down the navigation probe while preserving degrees of freedom (DOF) and functionality. Dielectric elastomer actuators (DEAs) are promising probe candidates because they are solid-state, electrical-driven, and can be scaled down favorably. This work demonstrates a modular 2-DOF DEA miniature probe with an embedded CMOS sensor for visual data acquisition. The modularity achieved by a novel connector system enables switching between single and dual DEA probes based on 2D or 3D pathway structures. The probes can be controlled using a pocket-sized circuit with two knobs to turn. We present the operating mechanism, device assembly, fabrication, and characterization of DEA bending actuators with widths below 2 mm. In the end, we demonstrate the ability of devices to navigate through various complex and confined pathways.

title: Research on Bird Tracking Algorithm Based on Infrared Target Recognition
authors: Hanwu Luo; Wenzhen Li; Shikuan Chen; Guangxin Jiang; Hongguang Wang; Peng Lv; Junpeng Wang
abstract: Frequent bird activities in substations, converter stations and other important power places could cause short circuit, tripping and other serious accidents. To ensure the smooth running of power equipment, the acousto-optic mode method is now applied to disperse birds, while the broadcast method is not aimed at bird targets, in this case, birds can adapt quickly and make the dispersal device fail. To solve the above problems, this paper proposed a bird autonomous tracking algorithm based on infrared target recognition, which realizes the recognition and positioning of bird targets through fast template matching, and carries out the research on pointing and tracking control method for a two-dimensional PTZ based on the positioning information. The simulation and experimental results show that the method can accurately identify bird targets and achieve directional tracking, which can effectively improve the defects of bird driving equipment, such as insufficient directivity and general pertinence, and greatly enhance the automation of bird driving operation in power grid stations.

title: Self-Recovery of Quadrupedal Robot Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yusuf Eren Kılıç; Yunus Emre Akar; Hakan Temeltaş; Ecem Sümer
abstract: Quadruped robots are commonly used for navigating difficult terrains. However, they remain vulnerable to falls in unpredictable and unstructured environments. To ensure continuous operation, a self-recovery behavior is necessary. In this paper we present a self-recovery mechanism using Proximal Policy Optimization. This method eliminates the need for complex kinematic calculations. The proposed approach was trained and tested on the UnitreeA1 quadruped robot within the simulation environment to achieve effective self-recovery behavior. The results demonstrate the potential of this method as a reliable solution for self-recovery in quadruped robots.

title: Multi-Path Restorative Pre-Training with Localized Adaptive Graph Convolution for 2D Tooth Segmentation
authors: Haibin Wang; Yang Li; Li Liu
abstract: Segmenting teeth in 2D oral CT images is crucial for diagnosing dental conditions. However, many current models for 2D tooth segmentation depend solely on end-to-end segmentation loss during training, which can fail to capture the image's intrinsic features. Additionally, neighboring regions may interfere with tooth segmentation, leading to less-than-optimal results. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel framework named Multi-Path Restorative Pre-training with Localized Adaptive Graph Convolution (MPRP-LAGC) for 2D tooth segmentation. The MPRP utilizes two paths—one for image reconstruction and another for tooth edge reconstruction — as auxiliary tasks for pretraining the segmentation model. This enables the model to better capture both global image characteristics and the specific features of tooth edges. After dividing the feature maps to correspond to the tooth, maxillary, and mandibular regions, dynamic convolution is applied to emphasize the distinctions between the tooth area and surrounding tissues in the feature space. Experiments on one publicly available 2D oral CT dataset show that the proposed method surpasses current state-of-the-art models and accurately segments the boundaries of teeth, particularly where they meet the maxilla and mandible.

title: Design and experiment of fork robot for trays in industrialized seedling production
authors: Yanli Yang; Qi Chu; Meizhang Gu; Delong Jiang; Song Gu
abstract: At present, the movable container is widely used in industrialized seedling production. The cultivation objects in the container are mainly plug seedlings. The operation of trays in and out of the container is frequent in production, and the automatic equipment can automatically input the tray into the container. However, due to the factors such as the position deviation of trays caused by container transportation, there is little research on the equipment of trays automatic output container at home and abroad, At present, most of the production is done manually, which is the key node to improve the comprehensive efficiency of automatic production of seedlings. In this paper, the overall design of the fork robot for trays is carried out to realize the two-way transportation of the tray in the container and the conveyor line; The design of the key mechanism fork is studied and the experimental on the displacement range of the fork picking trays is carried out. The results show that, When the level values of vertical displacement were less than 4 mm, and the level values of horizontal displacement were less than 10mm, the picking success ratios of forks were 100%. The vertical displacement of forks has a stronger influence on picking success ratio of seedling tray compared with the horizontal displacement of forks, and the rounding of fork end plays a role in correcting deviation.

title: A Fault Handling Scheme for Remote Guidance of Autonomous Quick Rendezvous and Docking
authors: Chen Changqing; Xie Yongchun; Zhang Qiang; Zhang Hao
abstract: A phase modulation method for remote guidance faults in autonomous and quick rendezvous and docking is proposed. According to position and attitude navigation information, ground fault judgment instructions, various fault modes corresponding to different autonomous quick rendezvous and docking fault conditions are given. The chaser spacecraft is guided to the frozen orbit behind the target spacecraft by using the two impulses orbit change strategy for typical fault modes. After the fault is removed, new rendezvous and docking can be achieved by guidance from ground for one or two days according to the current phase angle.

title: Lightweight Hardware in the Loop Setup for Research and Rapid Prototyping
authors: Attila Medgyesi; Gabriel Harja
abstract: This paper presents a cost effective Hardware in the Loop environment for educational purposes, used for development of control strategies for simulated systems, but using a real controller, to be as close to the reality as possible. The environment has a custom hardware interface device, which creates connection between the physical signals of the real controller and the digital signals of a personal computer (PC). All these digital signals are processed in the real-time simulation, running on a normal Windows machine, under the Simulink Desktop Real-Time software environment. The paper presents the development steps of hardware interface device, as well as the Simulink environment, which connects to and controls the hardware components. The created environment was validated with multiple applications, to ensure its proper functioning.

title: Multi-agent Task Decomposition and Resource Scheduling Algorithm Construction
authors: Hang Yi; Ruliang Lin; Hao Wang; Xinyang Liu
abstract: In the context of ubiquitous connectivity and collaborative multi device applications, the functionality of physical device resources is decomposed into discrete atomic models to enhance the flexibility and reusability of device cluster services. In current practical applications, assembling and efficiently scheduling discrete resources in a task-oriented manner has become an urgent issue. Therefore, we propose a task decomposition algorithm based on the capability model, which splits and matches tasks based on the resource capability model. Then, according to the proposed bitmap-based hybrid resource scheduling algorithm, we achieve fine-grained and efficient collaborative scheduling of service-oriented resources.

title: Further research on optimal interval observer design for switched systems
authors: Haoran Zhang; Jun Huang; Haochi Che; Yueyuan Zhang
abstract: This paper focuses on the research on interval estimate method for discrete-time linear time-invariant switched systems. When real-time state of the system is estimated, it is necessary to eliminate the influence of external interference on the estimation results and consider the problem of switching modes. For these reasons, the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> observer design is combined with reachability analysis. First, we need to design a H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> observer so as to reduce the impact of external disturbances. Then, the observers based on reachability analysis technology are applied in it to obtain the interval of the states. In the end, a simulation for one example is completed to test the quality of the interval observer.

title: Development of an IoT-Integrated Automated Air Exchanger for Indoor Air Management in Computer Laboratories
authors: Leonard Nathaniel S. Majaducon; Jose Ryandale D. Gonzaga; Joost C. Besonia; Glenda S. Guanzon; Adha Theza Naputol; Jopearlson Icy Ituriaga
publication_title: 2025 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on [::Robotics::] and Technologies for Industrial [::Automation::] (ROBOTHIA)
abstract: The study develops an IoT-integrated automated air exchange system, addressing the issue on poor IAQ within computer laboratories. The developed system addresses gaps in previous solutions by introducing IoT integration and automated interventions to improve IAQ management within computer laboratories. This system is equipped with sensors capable of real-time monitoring of key indoor pollutants, such as carbon dioxide, particulate matter 2.5, and volatile organic compounds. Also, it comprises of an air exchange mechanism that automatically triggers when the pollutants' thresholds exceeded, ensuring timely and efficient way of reducing pollutants to maintain the optimal level of environment conditions. The air exchange mechanism comprises two fans, one for air intake and the other for air exhaustion to provide proper air circulation. Upon simulating real-world conditions in a prototype room model, results show that the system is effective in reducing pollutants' concentrations by measuring the levels of air parameters before and after operation of the system. With IoT-driven and automated intervention capabilities, the system's adaptable design and scalability provide a promising solution for improving the air quality of high-occupancy indoor spaces, allowing for a foundation to support broader real-world applications in industrial settings.

title: Fully 3D printable Robot Hand and Soft Tactile Sensor based on Air-pressure and Capacitive Proximity Sensing
authors: Sean Taylor; Kyungseo Park; Sankalp Yamsani; Joohyung Kim
abstract: Soft tactile sensors can enable robots to grasp objects easily and stably by simultaneously providing tactile data and mechanical compliance to robotic hands. If there are low-cost and easy-to-build robotic hands equipped with soft tactile sensors, they would be highly accessible and facilitate many robotics projects. To this end, we propose an accessible robot hand capable of tactile sensing, which can be produced through digital fabrication. We made the robot hand using commercial servo motors as well as components 3D printed from PETG, TPU, and conductive TPU. These materials allow the robot hand to have a soft, durable, and even functional structure. Specifically, the soft fingertip was crafted from TPU and conductive TPU, and their mechanical and electrical properties enable easy implementation of tactile sensing capabilities, such as force and capacitive touch, simply by adding off-the-shelf sensors (air-pressure and capacitance). The proposed robot hand could effectively sense interaction forces and proximity to conductive objects, and its utilization in various tasks was also demonstrated successfully.

title: Frequency Response of Transmission Lines with Unevenly Distributed Properties with Application to Railway Safety Monitoring
authors: Xiangyu Nil; Bill Goodwine
abstract: This paper proposes a method to efficiently compute the voltage and current along a transmission line which can be “damaged”; that is its electrical properties can be unevenly distributed. The method approximates a transmission line by a self-similar circuit network and leverages our previous work regarding the frequency response for that class of networks. The main motivation arises from research for railway track circuit systems where transmission line models are often employed. Determining deviations from baseline properties of the railway circuit is important for health monitoring of the system and furthermore, changes in circuit properties due to a train occupying a segment of the track also is of great interest as a means to ensure safety. Thus, in addition to monitoring the integrity of the railway circuit, our approach also could provide a means for safe operation in that it can be used to detect segments of the rail system that are occupied by trains.

title: Output Cluster Synchronization of Heterogeneous Networks via Pinning Control
authors: Lu Sun
abstract: This paper studies an output cluster synchronization problem of heterogeneous networks. Based on the internal model principle, heterogeneous networks are transformed into networks with a heterogeneous layer and a virtual nonidentical layer. By means of pinning control, a novel output cluster synchronization strategy is proposed. Three algebraic and graphic conditions are derived to specify control parameters. It is shown that the outputs of agents in heterogeneous networks are synchronized according to the clusters as long as fewer agents are pinned. Compared with the existing results, cluster tracking can be further achieved and control parameters can be always determined no matter how the magnitudes of coupling strengths among agents vary. Application cases on heading cluster synchronization of heterogeneous ships are provided to verify the effectiveness of theoretical results.

title: Integrated Nanophotonic Control of Thermal Bimorph Microactuators*
authors: Maziar P. Nezhad
publication_title: 2024 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: A new type of thermal bimorph microactuator is presented, in which energy delivery to the actuator is achieved through an integrated nanophotonics approach. This approach has been adopted from existing photonic device and optical communications technology. The microactuators are fabricated on a silicon nitride platform using a silicon nitride/aluminum bimorph structure. Integrated nanophotonic building blocks, such as waveguides, tapers and grating couplers are designed and fabricated using photonic design and nanofabrication tools. During operation, laser light from a telecommunications laser source at milliwatt levels is focused onto the device and is captured by the grating coupler. The captured light is routed on the surface of the microstructure and delivered to the bimorph limbs by the waveguides and subsequently converted to heat using chromium optical absorbers integrated onto the waveguides. To provide additional mechanical flexibility and increased bending range, solid rib waveguides are replaced in parts by arrays of etched ridges which are periodically spaced at a fraction of the laser wavelength. These 1-D photonic crystals act as flexible subwavelength grating waveguides. As an added feature, the grating couplers are implemented as 2D arrays of etched holes, enabling polarization-based beam separation on the device, thus enabling control of different limbs through polarization switching at the laser source. In addition to in situ characterization, the microstructures are also transferred to an optical fiber tip which delivers laser light to the device while also providing a useful means for packaging and using the microactuators.

title: Multi-Resolution Collision Detection-Based Motion Planning Method and its Application in Live-Line Working Robots
authors: Mingyue Liu
abstract: Starting from the safety requirements of operations, live working robots in the distribution network have extremely high requirements for motion planning efficiency. The current planning algorithm is difficult to meet the requirements. Considering that most of the motion planning time is spent on collision detection, this paper proposes a multi resolution collision detection method that reduces the computational cost of collision detection while ensuring security. And the combination of RRT algorithm greatly reduces planning time. And verify the advantages and feasibility of this algorithm in the constructed distribution network operation simulation environment.

title: RELA: An Online-Offline Framework for Rules Enhanced Logs Analysis Based on Large Language Models
authors: Xin Ji; Ruibo Chen; Yikai Chen; Nan Xiang; Kui Zhang
abstract: Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have played a pivotal role in the field of Artificial Intelligence Operations (AIOps), particularly in the analysis of log data. However, the use of open-source LLMs for automated log analysis often falls short of expectations in offline environments in practice. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an innovative Online-Offline framework named RELA to enhance the performance of LLMs in log analysis. In the online phase of our framework, GPT-4 meticulously analyzes logs to determine the presence of anomalies and deduces rules based on these determinations, which are then compiled into a comprehensive rules base. In the offline phase, open-source LLMs leverage this rules base to significantly enhance the effectiveness of log analysis by retrieving the most applicable rules. To validate the effectiveness of our proposed framework, we meticulously annotated a dataset specifically designed for a distinct offline scenario, focusing on two primary tasks: the detection of log anomalies and the explanation of these anomalies. Our experimental results demonstrate that the implementation of the rules base leads to a 3% to 25.3% increase in the accuracy of anomaly detection. Additionally, assessments conducted by domain experts validate the improvements, highlighting a substantial enhancement in the credibility of the explanations provided by LLMs within this framework. These findings not only underscore the practicality but also the efficacy of our approach, establishing a solid foundation for further research and application in AIOps.

title: Satellite Attitude Control for Emergency Mode Using Reaction Wheels and Magnetic Torquers
authors: Yikang He; Sen Yang; Shuyu Lin; Wen He; Zhen Yang
abstract: To recover the satellite operations in emergency conditions, a control design scheme for emergency mode that utilizes reaction wheels and magnetic torques is presented in this paper. Firstly, based on a highly reliable sensor suite comprising sun sensors and magnetometers, a suitable attitude control law is designed to complete the satellite attitude missions of rate damping and sun-pointing. Then, considering that there are only two workable reaction wheels due to one reaction wheel failures, a control allocation law is designed to determine the control torque provided by two reaction wheels and the magnetic moment provided by magnetic torquers. Finally, the proposed method is compared with the purely magnetic control method by numerical simulations. The results indicate that the proposed method can achieve the attitude control missions after the satellite enters emergency mode, and performs better in terms of convergence and accuracy.

title: Fractional Discrete-Time Variable Order Equation with Infinite Delay
authors: Dorota Mozyrska; Małgorzata Wyrwas
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The paper explores the analysis of fractional discrete-time systems with the Caputo-type operator and infinite delay, addressing a gap in current research. The study focuses on the existence, uniqueness and stability of solutions for fractional systems with infinite delay, providing a framework for analyzing these systems and offering tools for numerical simulations and control design in applications involving complex memory-dependent dynamics.

title: Lung Cancer Classification Using CNN and Random Forest
authors: Nowshad Hasan; Md. Maskat Sharif; Md Saiful Islam; Arafat Anam Chowdhury; Miskatur Rahman; Md Rokibul Fahad Khan; Anamul Bahar
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Early detection of lung cancer is crucial for improving survival rates and enabling more effective treatment options. However, manually detecting and classifying various forms of lung cancers is time-consuming and can be inaccurate. Traditional classification methods rely on manual feature extraction, necessitating the experimenter's expertise and professional knowledge. This research introduces a streamlined feature selection method using a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to effectively tackle the issue. The aim of this proposed lightweight deep CNN is to enhance accuracy while reducing the number of parameters. The established approach involves three key stages: pre-processing, feature extraction, and classification. In the pre-processing phase, K-fold cross-validation ensures robust classification, complemented by data augmentation to augment the image dataset. In the feature extraction stage, modified CNNs effectively extract pertinent features, followed by Random Forest (RF) utilization to distinguish various forms of lung cancer from CT scan images. The proposed Deep CNN-RF model demonstrates effective detection and classification of various types of lung cancer, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 97.1%.

title: Application of Tool-Work Contact Electrical Resistance Measurement to Flat End Milling
authors: Yutaro Koga; Mitsuaki Murata
abstract: Our previous studies have shown that the change in tool-work contact electrical resistance is highly correlated with the progress of tool flank wear. This makes in-process detection of face milling tool flank wear possible. The measurement system we developed for this method starts measuring with a binary signal of the thermal electromotive force (E.M.F.) generated by the contact between the tool and workpiece. The polarity and voltage of this E.M.F. differ depending on the combination of tool material and workpiece material. We developed an operation timing circuit so that the conventional system can respond to the E.M.F. of various tools. Then, we installed it in a measurement system and conducted cutting experiments using a new end mill. As a result, it was found that the tool-work contact electrical resistance also changes with changes in the contact area during end milling.

title: Design of Velocity Control Model in Robot Vehicle Platoon
authors: Yuki Yoshida; Eisuke Kita
abstract: The vehicle platoon is a technology in which multiple vehicles runs in a short vehicle distance. When the velocity control algorithm is defined based on the vehicle following model, some model parameters should be determined. The aim of this study is to discuss the design of the model parameters. Three objective functions are defined by terms related to the velocity, the vehicle distance and so on. The parameters are defined by solving the optimization problem including the objective functions. Model 1, which emphasizes the velocity terms, tends to reduce the overshoot amount of velocity, but the reaction to the velocity change tends to be poor. Model 2, which emphasizes the vehicle distance, tends to react the velocity change sensitively and has a large overshoot amount. However, there is a tendency to quickly accommodate the vehicle distance. Model 3 tends to reduce vehicle distance quickly. Next, models are implemented in LEGO MindStorms EV3 and an actual machine experiment is conducted. The experimental results were similar to the results obtained by numerical simulation.

title: Throttle and Brake Control Using Fuzzy-Neural Algorithm in Car Following
authors: Albert Paolo P. Bugayong; Manuel C. Ramos
abstract: A throttle and brake controller was designed using fuzzy neural networks (FNN) and artificial neural networks (ANN). ANN and FNN regression models for the throttle control block were compared and an ANN classification model for the brake controller block was developed. All were trained and evaluated using a locally generated dataset from 6 drivers in the University of the Philippines. Both single hidden layer and two hidden layer FNN models for the throttle controllers exhibited lower errors against their ANN counterparts with FNN 2L incurring the lowest RMSE and MAE for both position and velocity simulations. FNN 1L was the safest model with the most stable space headway. The brake controller ANN 1L Br achieved 74.88% precision for throttle and 65.11% recall for brake cases.

title: Test Bench for HIL Simulation of Centrifugal Pump System with Variable Speed Drive
authors: Levon Gevorkov; José Luis Domínguez-García
abstract: A laboratory hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) workbench for the simulation of a centrifugal pump system equipped with a variable speed drive (VSD) is proposed in the paper. The coupled electric drive systems represent the pump and pipeline simulators respectively, connected with the help of a communication device and programmable logical controller (PLC). The electric drives together with interface devices make up the entire HIL simulator. A major component of the modeling methodology is the mathematical analysis of the pumping system. The examinations were conducted in order to investigate the suggested simulator. Tests have demonstrated the proposed system's accuracy and flexibility in modeling centrifugal pumping system behavior and operation modes.

title: A Novel Soft Modeling Framework for Real-time State Prediction in Strip Galvanization Process
authors: Jinbo Zhou; Youzhao Sun; Yamin Sun; Quan Yang; Xiaochen Wang; Jiaqi Chen
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: In the galvanization process of strip steel, the removal of floating substances formed within the nose end of the furnace is crucial for improving product quality and production efficiency. Due to the complexity of the composition inside the furnace nose and zinc pot, as well as the diverse operating conditions, production personnel find it challenging to predict the state and movement of materials such as strip steel and zinc fluid within the equipment. To overcome these challenges, this study trained the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to predict the zinc fluid state under various operating conditions based on data from finite element simulation. Additionally, digital twin technology is employed to visualize the spatial states of the furnace nose and zinc pot under stable conditions. Experimental results indicate that this system not only accurately predicts the galvanization process of strip steel under different operating conditions but also operates at speeds several hundred times faster than finite element-based simulators. Furthermore, it enables real-time monitoring of the production conditions in the furnace nose and zinc pot areas, providing a basis for operational adjustments of equipment parameters by operators.

title: Introducing CEA-IMSOLD: an Industrial Multi-Scale Object Localization Dataset
authors: Boris Meden; Pablo Vega; Fabrice Mayran De Chamisso; Steve Bourgeois
abstract: We introduce the CEA Industrial Multi-Scale Object Localization Dataset (CEA-IMSOLD), a new BOP format dataset for 6-DoF object localization, crucial for robotics. This dataset aims to evaluate the current localization methods with respect to a new difficulty: large variations in observation distance and, consequently, large variations in image appearance. Compared to the other publicly available datasets, our dataset provides both images with objects small and completely visible in the image, and images where objects are observed close enough so they appear larger than the field of view of the camera. We also propose to consider the observation distance in the evaluation process and introduce new metrics to do so. Finally, our dataset contains a large variety of industrial objects, from small and simple objects such as bolts to sizable and complex ones such as large car parts. We provide baseline results and the dataset is made publicly available to support the community at https://cea-list.github.io/CEA-IMSOLD/.

title: Mixed Precision Level Based Sparse Grid Quadrature Filter for Nonlinear System
authors: Chen Qian; Huikun Pan; Yuan Qian; Qingwei Chen
abstract: In order to reduce the computational burden of the sparse grid quadrature filter (SGQF) in nonlinear filtering system, the mixed precision level based sparse grid quadrature filter (MPLSGQF) is proposed. The formulations of the Gaussian approximation filter and the SGQF for the nonlinear discrete-time system are presented. The MPLSGQF uses the different precision level SGQF algorithms for the time prediction process and measurement update process in the filtering cycle. For the more frequent time prediction process, the level-2 sparse grid quadrature (SGQ) rule is utilized for sampling, and the level-3 SGQ rule is used in measurement update process. The algorithm reduces the computational burden by reducing the number of sampling points in time prediction process. A 5-dimensional target tracking problem is used as a simulation application to compare the filtering performance and running time of the MPLSGQF. The simulation results show that compared with the unscented Kalman filter (UKF), the level-2 SGQF and the level-3 SGQF, the MPLSGQF can reduce the computational burden while maintaining the filtering accuracy. It proves that the MPLSGQF is a better choice to balance accuracy and computational amount.

title: System Integration and Verification of Reagent Preparation Robots for in Vitro Diagnosis
authors: Guanru Li; Yiwei He; Kangming He; Jiaxing Chao; Qi Lu
abstract: In order to relieve the pressure of manual drug dispensing in hospitals and address the problem of medical powder spraying due to the negative pressure inside the bottles during manual dispensing. This conference paper presents a robotic system used to accomplish the task of in vitro diagnostic (IVD) dispensing for medical freeze dried bottles which is sealed with rubber stopper. This device is mainly composed of four modules: the cap-processing module, the transportation module, the needle-puncturing module, and the injection module. The function of the robotics system is to open the cap of the freeze-dried bottle, insert the needle, inject the corresponding reagent, and tighten the cap, thereby completing the drug preparation process. It is expected that the reagent preparation time will be shortened within two minutes per bottle of medicine, while the accuracy of reagent preparation is controlled within 5% of the error. Experiments are conducted for the performance evaluation of the proposed robot. Results show that, with the liquid injection accuracy reaching 97.6% and the reagent preparation time reaching about 51 seconds.

title: Experimental Investigation of the Solidification and Melting Processes of PCMs
authors: Octavian G. Pop; Cristina A. Iuga; Lucian Fechete Tutunaru; Mugur C. Balan
abstract: A key component of the concept of Smart City is the use of energy efficient technology for household and nonresidential building applications.
