Through MATLAB simulation results, it is shown that the current-control mode is superior to the voltage-control mode. A DC 46 V output closed-loop feedback control switching power supply is fabricated, and the experimental and simulation results verify the superiority of the design. From this study, the current control mode is suitable for use in flyback switching power supplies, because of the current mode method shows more stable characteristics with GM = 11.975 dB and PM = 46.073°.

title: Design of Upper Limb Rehabilitation Assistance Training System Based on Unity 3D
authors: Zejing Niu; Haoran Wang; Xuyang Sui; Linling Tan; Taian Xu; Wendong Xiao
abstract: Cerebral stroke is a disease with a high incidence and disability rate. As its most common sequela, upper limb motor dysfunction seriously affects patients' daily activities when it occurs. Traditional rehabilitation training requires patients to go to medical institutions, which is limited due to the lack of human resources. In recent years, the development of virtual reality has provided a novel technology for rehabilitation training, which has attracted more attention in the medical field. In order to overcome the limitations of traditional rehabilitation approaches, this paper develop a virtual reality upper limb rehabilitation training assistance system based on wearable devices and Unity 3D engine. This system combines monotonous training movements in rehabilitation training with virtual games, achieving interaction between human arms and virtual training scenes. The system consists of two upper body training games. It has entertainment, sustainability and real-time feedback functions, providing users with an immersive gaming experience and meeting their training demands for different parts of the upper limbs.

title: Stability Control of Quadrotor UAV with Manipulator
authors: Chenghang Wang; Suping Zhao; Chaobo Chen; Alejandro Gutierrez-Giles; Xiaohua Song; Kun Yan
abstract: Compared with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV), a UAV with a manipulator (UAVM) exhibits significant trajectory deviations. Due to the coupling of the UAV and the manipulator, the stable control of UAVM represents a challenging problem. To address this issue, a PID-based control approach is proposed. First, the dynamics of UAVM is developed using the Euler-Lagrange method. Second, a PID-based controller is designed to achieve stable control of UAVM. Finally, numerical simulations are carried out to verify the proposed approach. Simulation results show that the manipulator accurately track its trajectory while the stability of UAV is achieved.

title: Research on Methods of Pavement Distress Detection Based on Object Detection Convolutional Neural Network
authors: Xingang Wang; Yaxin Huang; Yongjun Shao; Chihang Zhao; Youfeng Zheng; Xinyi Ma; Wenhao Deng; Ziyi Zhang
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the accuracy of pavement distress detection is easily affected by complex texture, noisy background, uneven illumination conditions and external environmental interference of highway pavement distress images, this paper studies the methods of pavement distress detection based on object detection Convolutional Neural Network. Firstly, the methods of pavement distress detection based on Faster-RCNN, YOLO-V5s, and SSD are compared and analyzed. Secondly, three variants of CNN models are investigated for pavement distress detection, including FR-PDD, YOLO5s-PDD and SSD-PDD. Finally, the comparative experiments were conducted, and the results showed that the average of Yolov5s-PDD network is superior to the other two methods, with an average accuracy of 98.1%.

title: OOD-ENS: Cross-Validated Out-of-Distribution Ensemble Detector
authors: Zhengjiang Liu; Wen Zhang; Ruibo Wang
abstract: The task of out-of-distribution (OOD) detection aims to identify abnormal test records for preventing the degradation of the performance of a well-deployed deep learning model on abnormal records. Existing studies have developed several state-of-the-art OOD detection algorithms based on sufficiently pre-trained deep neural models on the large-scale data sets provided in advance. However, the performance of existing OOD detection algorithms is sensitive to a small disturbance in a pre-training data set attributing to the overfitting phenomenon of a pre-trained neural model on the pre-training data set. In this paper, we attempt to reduce the effect of the disturbance on an OOD detection algorithm and improve the OOD detection performance through employing a popular model aggregation method. Specifically, we resample multiple training sets from a pre-training data set by using a $K -$fold cross-validation method and aggregate the corresponding multiple OOD base models into a high-performing ensemble OOD model based on a majority-voting technique. The proposed OOD algorithm, named an OOD-ENS algorithm in this study, is a simple yet effective framework to use most of the existing OOD detection algorithms as the prototype of an OOD base model. Extensive numerical experiments on five well-known image data sets are conducted to illustrate the superiority of the proposed OOD-ENS algorithm.

title: Adaptive Distributed Label-Free Fencing Control of Disturbed Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems for a Freely Moving Target
authors: Song Jiang; Jiang Zhao; Pei Chi; Yingxun Wang
abstract: This paper investigates the freely moving target fencing problem for disturbed heterogeneous second-order multiagent systems. Without the need for the disturbance bound, we propose an adaptive distributed label-free target-fencing controller. The controller is designed via backstepping techniques and adaptive techniques without predefined distances. The target is asymptotically fenced under the proposed fencing controller and in the presence of unknown disturbances, ensuring no interagent collisions and achieving velocity convergence, even with unexpected agent losses. The results are proved by rigorous theoretical analysis and verified by numerical simulations.

title: Cascade Aggregation Network for Ship Instance Segmentation
authors: Yuxin Sun; Li Su; Shouzheng Yuan; Hao Meng
abstract: Instance segmentation technology has great application in the field of intelligent ships. However, existing methods still have many problems when used directly for ship instance segmentation. For the problems of imprecise bounding box and poor segmentation of detailed contour of ships. We propose a new Cascade Aggregation Network (CAN) for ship instance segmentation. The GIoU loss function is used to optimize the bounding box. And we propose an aggregation segmentation net-work with multi-scale edge aggregation information can improve mask. Finally, CAN can predict more accurate bounding boxes and generates higher quality masks. Experimental comparison and visual analysis show that our CAN outperforms Cascade Mask R-CNN on the ship instance segmentation dataset.

title: Impulsive EEG in Drug Users with Naive Bayesian Classification Approach
authors: Delima Sitanggang; Novi Antika Nainggolan; Kevin Daniel Marpaung; Mertfil Efrat Preditus; Igo Fahrezy; Mardi Turnip
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Control & [::Automation::]; Electronics; [::Robotics::]; Internet of Things; and Artificial Intelligence (CERIA)
abstract: Measuring impulsivity is essential for understanding mental health and interpersonal relationships. Identifying impulsivity levels can help in detecting potential mental disorders, such as impulse control disorders or ADHD, which may require further evaluation and treatment. This study aims to develop a classification system using EEG (Electroencephalography) data to assess impulsivity in drug users. The system uses the Naïve Bayes algorithm to classify data into five categories: very active, active, less active, likely active, and inactive. Data were collected from 21 participants and analyzed based on alpha and beta brain waves. The results indicate a classification accuracy of 95.3%, demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in interpreting brain activity related to drug use and classifying EEG patterns. This research provides practical benefits for understanding impulsivity patterns in drug users, thereby supporting more targeted assessment and treatment processes.

title: Method for Road Occlusions Handling in Generic Sensor Models
authors: Michał Jasiński
publication_title: 2021 25th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Due to the increasing complexity of Advanced Safety systems, a strong endeavor is required to acquire realistic and real-time capable simulations, in order to enable robust and easily reproducible system verification in virtual environments. To make simulations reliable, high-fidelity sensor models are required. One of the approaches is to implement a generic sensor model that explicitly emulates the output of an object detection algorithm, based on high-level simulation data. However, such a model has to accurately handle object-based occlusions, to assure that shadowed objects are not detected. Various generic sensor models available in the literature already solve the problem of how to estimate occlusions, given a set of objects. Nevertheless, none of the models takes into account a road profile, i.e. hills. The method proposed in this paper provides an accurate and easy to implement road profile estimation using a set of bounding boxes. Thanks to the generated structures, a road-based shadowing can be enabled in any of the object-based generic sensor models. The obtained results clearly show the robustness and usefulness of the proposed methodology.

title: Effluent BOD soft measurement based on MNN
authors: Guiping Dong; Siyuan Wang; Zhongli Yao; Song Meng
abstract: Aiming at the difficulty of real-time and accurate measurement of biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) in effluent of wastewater treatment process, a design method based on modular neural network is proposed to predict BOD in effluent. Firstly, the BOD sequence is decomposed by Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (CEEMD) algorithm, Fuzzy Entropy (FE) is used to quantify the complexity of each subsequence. Then, using density clustering to determine the adaptive RBF sub-network structure, and Error Feedback and Sensitivity Analysis (SA) could dynamically adjust the number of neurons. On this basis, the network width is adjusted by clustering algorithm. Experiments verify that this method has a more concise network structure and higher prediction accuracy.

title: Design of Haptic Sensing Snake Robot
authors: Yang Zhang; Hao Wu; Peng Li; Deen Bai; Shuai Guo; Chaoquan Tang
abstract: Snake robots, a category of bionic robots, have garnered significant interest due to their capacity to adapt autonomously to complex unstructured environments. This is achieved through the flexibility and versatility of their bodies and gaits, as well as the coordinated movements of their bodies. However, in unknown or complex environments with obstacles, snake robots are unable to plan their next locomotor actions based solely on the sensory information obtained from the camera they carry. The incorporation of haptics is anticipated to facilitate the snake robot's perception of the interaction between its body and the external environment, thereby enabling more precise and effective guidance for efficient movement. This paper presents the design of a flexible tactile sensor based on the principle of photoconductivity, which has been developed to enable a snake robot to perceive and interact with its environment through tactile sensing. The sensor is intended to enhance the robot's autonomous movement capabilities in complex environments where visual recognition or human observation alone is insufficient.

title: Design of Forest Fire Alarm System Based on GSM
authors: Shibing Bai
abstract: This project designed a smoke fire anti-theft alarm based on GSM, which can automatically detect smoke and flame, and send real-time alarm message to the user through GSM network, so as to improve the fault tolerance rate when the house is in danger of fire. The alarm mainly includes smoke detection sensor, human infrared detection sensor, control center, GSM module and power supply components. When smoke or flame is detected, the control center will send instructions to the GSM module, and the GSM module will send alarm information to the user's mobile phone.

title: Modular Design of Multi-Unit Pipeline Inspection Robot for Low Pressure Gas Pipeline
authors: Puikuan Chang; Muzhou Wang; Zhufeng Shao; Alimu Maimaiti; Wanli Zhou
abstract: Aiming at the problem of inspection inside low-pressure gas pipelines in cities and towns, this paper proposes a modularized multi-unit wheeled pipeline robot, which breaks through the technical limitations of traditional PIG inspection equipment that relies on high-pressure fluid drive. This paper proposes a multi-unit coordinated drive wheel type pipeline robot, the robot has four dynamic units, each unit is connected using a steering module, but also able to replace the steering module into the inspection unit, to become a pipeline inspection robot. The robot is suitable for DN300 pipeline, can pass through straight pipes, bends, T -branches and some obstacles in the pipe, and has a certain adaptive ability to change the diameter of the pipe. Through the bend traffic ability the analysis and simulation to verify the robot's configuration of geometric parameters designed to complete the 1.5D radius of curvature of the 90-degree elbow through the pipe, and traction inspection unit experiments to complete the straight pipe and bend traction load experiment.

title: Bifurcation Investigating of a Fractional Neural Networks Involving Incommensurate Delays
authors: Tongxing Li; Xin Wang; Hui Zhang; Yan Wang; Yongfeng Zhang
abstract: In this current article, an issue of Hopf bifurcation control about a novel fractional-order network owing multiple delays and feedback gain is formulated. The bifurcation parameter time delay is selected as the bifurcation parameter. The stability conditions and the bifurcation point are established. Ultimately, a simulation example is provided to verify the validity of the obtained newly results. The important results obtained in this paper have important theoretical significance and application value for the regulation and control of fractional-order neural networks with time-delay.

title: Research on Matching of Motor Control System Based on Electric Drive of Engineering Vehicle
authors: Zongjun Feng
abstract: In this paper, on the basis of the control research of a single inverter controlling dual motors in the power battery-powered mode for the scenario of parallel motor application in engineering vehicles, the mathematical model applied to electric drive motor control was derived, the motor stator parallel current control strategy was analyzed, and the research of energy-saving operation strategy based on bus-type topology was innovatively proposed. The research equipment was used to develop a reference correlation between the wheelside speed parameter K and the average rotor magnetic field directional parallel control method under loose pavement wheelside slip rotation conditions. In order to improve the starting performance of parallel motors under unbalanced load and reduce the unbalanced degree of parallel motor speed, this experiment applied a parallel control strategy based on weighted vector based on the average rotor magnetic field orientation control. The results show that the machine intelligence level was improved and the energy saving effect of reducing the heat loss of the motor was achieved.

title: Building Disease Image Recognition Network based on Improved SRM Attention Mechanisms
authors: Yanna Liao; Zhehui Mi; Sayda Elmi
abstract: To address the problems of shallow information loss, texture detail distortion and insufficient weight of fine-grained features when using basic convolutional neural networks to detect building surface disease images, the SRMM module is improved on the basis of the Style-Based Recalibration Module (SRM), and it is introduced into the Spatial Pyramid Pooling - Convolutional Spatial Pyramid Pooling - Convolutional (SPPCSPC) module of the convolutional neural network YOLOv7 to propose an improved YOLOv7 algorithm to improve the detection accuracy, enhance the weight of fine-grained features, and improve the robustness and generalization ability of the model. Secondly, by introducing the residual idea in the Neck part of YOLOv7, the connection between deep and shallow information is enhanced, and the loss of shallow information and distortion of texture details are reduced. Experimental results show that the improved YOLOv7-Mix has better detection accuracy in the task of concrete surface disease image detection, and the mean Average Precision (mAP) is increased from 82.70% of the original YOLOv7 to 88.14%, which is 5.44% higher than the original network.

title: HSSAS: Optimizing NLP Models by Combining Self-Supervised Learning and Neural Architecture Search
authors: Shuocheng Qi; Dong Wang; Yuling Fan; Likai Dong
abstract: With the increasingly widespread applications of Natural Language Processing (NLP), many algorithms based on deep learning have been proposed and introduced, which have achieved outstanding achievements. However, these algorithms now face challenges due to their strong dependence on labeled data and high computational costs. These issues negatively impact the generality, efficiency and scalability of the algorithms in practical applications. This study proposes a Hybrid Self-Supervised Architecture Search (HSSAS) method combining Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) and Neural Architecture Search (NAS), which can effectively alleviate the challenges of dependency on labeled data and high computational costs. Before conducting Neural Architecture Search (NAS) to explore model architectures, Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) defines specific tasks to compel the model to understand contextual relationships, enabling it to extract high-quality feature representations from unlabeled data. These features encapsulate core information of the data with high generalization ability. Traditional NAS typically requires evaluating hundreds of architectures. However, by leveraging the feature representations obtained from SSL, NAS can efficiently evaluate architectures on a condensed feature set, filtering out unsuitable options. This substantially reduces the search space, decreases computational complexity, and saves both time and resources. Experiments are carried on the BBC news dataset and the results demonstrate that the HSSAS method outperforms traditional NAS methods and NAS methods without SSL on multiple performance metrics, while also maintaining lower computational overhead.

title: Precision Repairs: Achieving Accuracy During Repair Missions at the International Space Station
authors: Suhail Haque Rafi; Md Mubin Ul Islam Chowdhury; Mazharul Islam Rakib; Mizanul Chowdhury; Md Khalilur Rhaman
abstract: This paper proposes an autonomous approach for repairing leakage at the International Space Station (ISS) using the NASA Astrobee robot with the 3rd Kibo Robot Programming Challenge (KRPC) guidelines provided by JAXA. We bring into play image processing and analysis from the Astrobee Nav Cam data, circle detection algorithms, AR tag detection techniques, autonomous navigation, and a Visual Projective Localization And Mapping (VPLAM) approach for irradiating lasers with excellent precision at the Astrobee Robot Simulator. In addition, we discuss the various capabilities of the Astrobee Robots onboard the ISS and how they can facilitate the delivery of such an autonomous mission in emergencies. Lastly, we walk through ways to deal with randomness and uncertainty while operating, ensuring robustness and accuracy. Ultimately, we scored a precision of up to 0.03 cm on the KRPC online simulator.

title: A Passive Electrical Network for Reducing Current Requirement While Driving Piezo-Actuators with Periodic Waveforms
authors: P. Abhishek; A.K. Mohanty; G.R. Jayanth
publication_title: 2025 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: The piezo-actuator is a vital element in many nanopositioning and nano-robotic applications. However, being a capacitive load, the piezo-actuator demands high currents when driven at high frequencies, which, when combined with its high voltage requirements, leads to high heat dissipation. Here we propose the use of a network in the Foster-II form connected to the piezo-actuator to achieve zero driving point susceptance for the overall network. This enables the piezo-actuator to follow arbitrary high-frequency periodic waveforms with greatly reduced current requirements. A systematic process is presented to design the network. Next, the performance of the network is validated by means of simulations for a 3-branch network that achieves zero susceptance at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \text{kHz}, 15 \text{kHz}$</tex> and 25 kHz. Finally, the 3-branch network is experimentally realized by winding the necessary inductors in-house. It is demonstrated to track square and triangular waveforms with substantially lesser error. Subsequently, a circuit is devised to measure the current supplied by the source and is used to demonstrate an over 5-fold reduction in current consumption compared to direct actuation of the piezo-actuator.

title: Research on Matching Degree of Agricultural Landscape Based on UAV Space Ranging
authors: He Zhang; Yixin Cai; Min Zong; Wenbo Zhang; Xiaofei Ma; Da Cong
abstract: Agricultural landscape is a form of expression of the earth's landscape achieved through agricultural planting, usually presenting a design image of the earth with different types of plants working together. In the specific implementation process, due to spatial errors in plant planting, there are often some errors in the presentation of the final effect compared to the initial design image, which becomes an important factor affecting the appearance of the final effect. This article aims to use unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) spatial ranging technology to calculate the error values between agricultural landscape products and design patterns based on several feature points, comprehensively measure their presentation effects, and provide evaluation criteria for the planting quality of agricultural landscapes.

title: Accumulation Efficiency Augmentation of Mono C-Si Solar Cell using Photon Concentration Method
authors: Ashrafun Nushra Oishi; Meer Shadman Shafkat Tanjim; Sourav Barua; Nikan Chakma; Pranab Chakma; Mohammad Ali
abstract: Expense reduction and environment friendliness in power production are just two of the numerous advantages of using solar panels for energy generation. Energy users can now achieve new degrees of independence and pollution-free power sources due to solar panels. Toxic particles in vast amounts escape from air filtration devices and reach the atmosphere even though coal power plants purge their carbon emissions. Communities and surroundings around solar power installations are safer when solar power is used instead of coal-fired power plants since it produces no pollution. But due to less photon conversion or accumulation efficiency, the PV panel installation requires more area to meet the demand, which is a major drawback for roof-top solar-power implementation. For this, the research is focused on honing solar accumulation efficiency with mirrors along with concentrators to reduce initial panel size over demand. Compared to the findings, it can be seen that, reflecting more photon to the panel area meets the objective of this research successful, considering heat tolerant point. Using multiple photon concentrator for photon accumulation, the efficiency got improved from 4.65% to 11.61% in case of Mono Crystalline Silicon (C-Si) Solar Cell. Residential consumers will surely become benefitted for using this method by getting 6.96% more power to meet the required electricity demand.

title: Robot Ground Laser Point Clouds Segmentation Algorithm Based on Adaptive Slope Threshold
authors: Liuzhao Li; Xiaonan Hou; Jinxin Xu; Qihan Fan
abstract: In view of the problems of sensor installation error, poor real-time performance and low accuracy of ground point cloud segmentation in robot obstacle detection technology based on Lidar, a robot ground laser point cloud segmentation algorithm based on adaptive slope threshold is proposed. First, the extrinsic parameter calibration algorithm of the Lidar and robot body coordinate system based on trajectory matching is used to improve the extrinsic parameter installation accuracy of the Lidar; secondly, in order to improve the real-time performance of ground point cloud segmentation, the original laser point cloud is preprocessed; then, In order to improve the efficiency and accuracy of point cloud segmentation, polar coordinate mapping is used to order the laser point cloud, and the idea of adaptive slope threshold is used to complete the reliable segmentation of ground point cloud; finally, an experimental comparative analysis is conducted. The results show that under the same environment, the segmentation efficiency and accuracy of this algorithm are higher.

title: Analysis on the Application of Cryptographic Technology in the Communication Security of Intelligent Networked Vehicles
authors: Xianfeng Jia; Tianyu Liu; Chunhui Sun; Zhi Wu
abstract: Intelligent networked vehicles are rapidly developing in intelligence and networking. The communication architecture is becoming more complex, external interfaces are richer, and data types are more complex. Different from the information security of the traditional Internet of Things, the scenarios that need to be met for the security of the Internet of Vehicles are more diverse and the security needs to be more stable. Based on the security technology of traditional Internet of Things, password application is the main protection method to ensure the privacy and non-repudiation of data communication. This article mainly elaborates the application of security protection methods using password-related protection technologies in car-side scenarios and summarizes the security protection recommendations of contemporary connected vehicles in combination with the secure communication architecture of the Internet of Vehicles.

title: Decoupled load swing control of an overhead crane using Arduino controller
authors: F. Javier Garcia; Luis R. González; Alfonso V Poncela; Moya Eduardo
abstract: The paper presents a practical anti-sway crane controller based on classical PID and fuzzy logic as well. The proposed control consists of a position servo control and a load swing control, studying the interaction effects between both controllers. The proposed controllers provides practical gain tuning criteria for easy application. The effectiveness of the proposed control is shown by experiments with a two-dimensional prototype overhead crane, that it is used to serve the learning and practicing needs of the learners.

title: Adaptive Formation Strategy for Enclosing and Tracking a Mobile Target with Motion and Field of View Constraints
authors: Yu Wen; Jiangshuai Huang
abstract: This paper introduces a system developed to tackle the challenge of enclosing and tracking a moving target in multi-robot systems, taking into account motion and field of view (FOV) constraints. Initially, a method utilizing relative position measurement is proposed. Following this, a reference trajectory is crafted to adhere to the motion and FOV constraints. Finally, considering the uncertainty in mobile robots and incorporating the prescribed performance bound (PPB) technique, adaptive tracking control solutions are devised. Experimental results show that the robots efficiently follow the designated reference trajectory, ensuring guaranteed transient performance for position and direction tracking errors, complying with motion and FOV constraints, and achieving swift enclosure and tracking of target objects.

title: Large Fixture Calibration Method Based on Point Cloud Scanning for Robotic Drilling
authors: Yongzhuo Gao; Haibo Gao; Dexin Cheng; Wei Dong
abstract: The rocket fuel tank requires the splicing of multiple sub-parts, which is difficult to be processed in an integrated manner. Among them, the short shell parts of the storage tank play a linking role and need to be drilled on the surface. Due to the large size of the tooling of the parts, there are problems such as large installation and positioning errors and low precision of robot automatic drilling. Therefore, a robot automatic hole making calibration method is proposed to solve the current problems. In order to achieve automated control, a large-scale robot automatic drilling system must have large-scale flexible tooling, control algorithms, human-computer interaction interfaces, execution units, and integrated tool rooms. It is essential to build effective calibration procedures as a foundation for this automation. The calibration plane is fitted, positioned, and calibrated using the point cloud scanning method. Subsequently, the hand-eye calibration method is employed to establish the relationship between the coordinate systems. Using this approach, the calibration process is ultimately finished, resulting in the successful implementation of automated drilling. The experimental findings demonstrate that, in the designated quadrant, the drilling rate of the robot can achieve 5 holes per minute. Furthermore, the average variance of the hole position is below 0.2mm, and the highest error is 0.5mm. These results align with the requirements of practical production.

title: A Faster and Less Parameterized Detector of Arbitrary Shapes Text Detection
authors: Siyang Liu; Tongwei Lu; Xuanxuan Liu; Cong Wang
abstract: Arbitrary shape text detection is a challenging task due to the high variety and complexity of scenes texts. The existing text detection algorithms can be roughly divided into three categories: the Connected Component (CC) strategy, regression method and segmentation method. These methods are either costly for character annotation or are determined by the interaction of multiple phases and components in the pipeline, which is generally not suitable for real-time applications. This paper presents a simple and powerful pipeline for fast and accurate detection of arbitrarily shaped text in natural scenes. Our contribution is threefold: 1) Use a single neural network to directly predict the text of any shape in the whole image, without intermediate steps (such as candidate set and word division), and greatly improves the detection speed of the text of any shape. 2) The B-spline Curves were proposed to fit the curved text boxes, which require fewer predicted parameters compared with the existing curved bounding boxes. The algorithm was tested on full-text and CTW1500 arbitrary shape standard datasets, and the average score improved by nearly 2% with almost no additional computational overhead, achieving a balance between speed and accuracy.

title: HandEEGnet: A Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Hand Movements Classification from Motor Imagery EEG
authors: Tasnimul Hasan; A. B. M. Aowlad Hossain; Shuvagata Biswas; Farhana Tazrin
abstract: Motor imagery-based BCI plays a vital role in controlling hand movements by processing and recognizing features from EEG signals associated with the imagination of those movements. In this paper, we present a Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) based framework in order to classify the left and right-hand movements along with the absence of movement's intention from the electroencephalogram (EEG) signal. The emergence of KAN is expected to be a breakthrough concept in the artificial intelligence paradigm considering its learnable activation functions mechanism and interpretability opportunities. Preprocessing of the collected raw EEG data has been accomplished with band-pass filtering of EEG components of five well-matched channels and corresponding power spectral density feature extraction. We have used 15282 samples with annotated classes from a publicly available dataset to train, validate, and test the classifier. A comparative analysis of the performance of KAN and conventional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) networks has been conducted in order to investigate the effectiveness of the KAN for this classification task. The proposed framework attains 96.14% classification accuracy for 3057 blind test samples, which is found to be better than the conventional MLP neural network approach (76.64% accuracy) and compatible with the existing techniques. The finding of this research might be useful in hand movement-related applications for robotics, prosthetics, and neuro-rehabilitation supports.

title: A Computer Vision System for Defect Contrast Enhancement on Transparent Materials with Structured Light and Neural Network
authors: An Liu; Chaoqing Tang; Haichao Qiu
abstract: Transparent materials are widely used in industrial applications like screens and precision optical instruments. However, due to its special optical properties, current computer vision systems that use dark-field illumination schemes suffer from poor defect contrast. Many tiny defects are even invisible. To address this problem, this paper proposes a computer vision system for defect contrast enhancement on transparent materials. Firstly, based on physical modulation effects, structured light illumination is used to enhance regional defect contrast. Then an unsupervised generative adversarial network is designed to fuse regional high-contrast information and remove the uneven illumination background from sub-images. Experiments are carried out on specimens with different types of defects and material thickness, the results show that the contrast of our method has improved by 34% compared with the traditional dark-field illumination. This computer vision imaging system enhances defect contrast physically and computationally, which brings much more defect information than current solutions for subsequent inspection tasks like defect localization and segmentation.

title: Implicit Lyapunov Robust Tracking Control of Oscillatory-Base Manipulators
authors: Ruilin Mei; Yufei Guo; Zhigang Wang; Zhiqiang Hao; Van Thanh Huynh
abstract: This paper is concerned with the robust tracking problem of oscillatory-base manipulators in the non-inertial task space. A novel control strategy based on the implicit Lyapunov method is proposed. Firstly, robust feedback linearization of the system dynamical model is carried out relying on the computed torque method, which could be interpreted as a proportional derivative control with continuous time-varying gains, is used to stabilize the linearized uncertain system. Moreover, stability of the closed-loop perturbed system is theoretically proved. Finally, hardware experimental results indicate that the proposed controller offers superior robustness against the base-oscillation-induced uncertainties. Results also demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method in that neither measurement nor prior knowledge of the uncertainties is required in the implementation.

title: Anomaly Detection for Escalators Based on Feature Optimization and Improved GMM Algorithm
authors: Long Qiang; Ningyun Lu; Jianfei Chen; Jianhua Lyu
abstract: Escalators, as vital components of modern urban transportation and commercial buildings, necessitate stable operation. However, due to prolonged usage and environmental influences, key components of escalators are prone to failures, leading to operational anomalies. Traditional periodic inspections and manual maintenance methods suffer from low efficiency, high cost, and poor real-time performance. To address these issues, this paper proposes an unsupervised escalator anomaly detection method based on feature optimization and an improved Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) algorithm.The method initially employs the Pareto principle for feature selection, enhancing computational efficiency and generalization capabilities. Subsequently, to overcome the limitations of traditional GMMs in determining the number of clusters and their application to anomaly detection, a bidirectional Fuzzy C-Means-Expectation Maximization (FCM-EM) algorithm is proposed. This algorithm determines the optimal number of clusters and optimizes the model’s fit to the data, thereby enabling accurate identification of anomalous states in escalators.Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high diagnostic accuracy across four escalator fault modes. Furthermore, comparative experiments show that the proposed method outperforms the comparison methods, providing reliable technical support for intelligent maintenance and safe operation of escalators.

title: Path Tracking Method of Forklift AGV Based on Fuzzy Adaptive PID
authors: Qiang Wang; Zhongfan Xiang; Jianxin Liu; Dechang Zhang; Senyao Wu
abstract: Precise path tracking is essential for forklift AGVs (Automated Guided Vehicles) to safely and efficiently complete loading and unloading tasks. External environmental changes can significantly affect the path tracking accuracy of forklift AGVs, posing challenges to their operational reliability. To address this issue, this study began with a comprehensive kinematic analysis and pose error analysis of the forklift AGV, aiming to understand the underlying mechanisms that influence its movement precision under varying conditions. Based on these analyses, the research adopted the concept of hierarchical control to design both a traditional PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) controller and a more advanced fuzzy adaptive PID controller. These controllers were specifically tailored to adjust for lateral deviation and heading angle deviation, which are critical parameters in maintaining accurate path tracking. The effectiveness of the two controllers was rigorously tested through simulations and real-world experiments using MATLAB. The results from these tests not only validated the feasibility of both the PID and fuzzy adaptive PID controllers for path tracking but also highlighted the superior performance of the fuzzy adaptive PID controller. This advanced controller demonstrated a notable improvement in the linear path tracking accuracy of the forklift AGV, as well as enhanced operational stability, especially when faced with unexpected environmental changes. The findings suggest that the fuzzy adaptive PID controller, grounded in hierarchical control principles, offers a robust solution for improving the overall performance and reliability of forklift AGV systems.

title: Research on Dynamic Characteristics of Aircraft with Floating Material
authors: Juan Zhang; Wenya Yang; Weida Zhu; Lanling Ma; Changyuan Dong
abstract: This paper establishes a simplified aircraft with floating material, and conducts modal analysis and random vibration analysis. The purpose is to analyze the influence of floating material on the inherent characteristics of aircraft, and the number of detection rods and the metal shell on the inherent characteristics of aircraft with floating material. The results show that the floating material can make the low order frequencies of the aircraft more intensive. The aircraft will be more likely to resonate, and the weak part of the aircraft will change. The more the number of detection rods, the denser the low order frequencies, and the easier it is to see the resonance frequency of the aircraft. The influence of metal shell on aircraft is to increase the frequency of the same order and increase the stiffness of the whole model. The calculation results of the response points basically correspond to the modal calculation results of the aircraft. It can prove that the establishment and setting of the aircraft are correct, and the whole process can effectively analyze the random vibration of aircraft with floating material. The results of modal analysis can be used in engineering practice to prevent resonance, and provide a reference for the test.

title: A Space Information-Enhanced Dense Video Caption for Indoor Human Action Recognition
authors: Bin CHEN; Yugo NAKAMURA; Shogo FUKUSHIMA; Yutaka ARAKAWA
abstract: Dense video captioning tasks are used to detect interesting events and provide descriptive text for these events from untrimmed videos. This technology has the potential to be used in security surveillance and human care applications. However, current methods often overlook the relationships between objects in the video, which limits their applicability and makes it challenging to adapt them to specific domains, such as video summarization for indoor human activities. In these scenarios, human activities are closely intertwined with the objects in the scene. In this paper, we propose a plug-and-play module designed to enhance existing dense video captioning methods with spatial information. Specifically, we extract spatial information about the interesting objects using Red-Green-Blue-Depth (RGB-D) images and the results of image segmentation. We then integrate this information into the captions generated by the Dense Video Captioning (DVC) method using a fine-tuned Large Language Model (LLM). We evaluate the performance of our model on a custom dataset and demonstrate that our system provides a convenient and effective approach for obtaining space-enhanced captions.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Network for Transient Modeling of Large-Scale Wind Farm
authors: Hongyi Wang; Pingyang Sun; Georgios Konstantinou; Zhe Chen
abstract: The complexity of transient characteristics in large-scale wind farms (WF) hinders the application of machine learning algorithms. This paper proposes a neural network-based learning method to model the transient characteristics of large-scale WF. The complexity of the physical information library is simplified through an iterative algorithm. The dynamic library obtained based on neural networks can induce the machine learning framework to rapidly learn the transient characteristics of large-scale WF. Moreover, there is no need for excessive mechanistic analysis and speculation regarding the transient behavior of WF. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified in the simulation model of a WF.

title: Prediction of Particulate Matter in a Mining Environment via Machine Learning
authors: Milka C.I. Madahana; John E.D. Ekoru
abstract: The objective of this research work is to present an investigation in the application of machine learning algorithms in the prediction of particulate matter concentration in an open cast coal mine. Three types of neural networks, Long Short Term Memory, Gated Recurrent Unit and Recurrent Neural Networks are used to estimate and forecast the particulate concentration in the mine. The neural networks are bench-marked using Linear Regression and support vector machines. The results indicate that the Recurrent Neural Network performs well under conditions with short time lags, whereas both the Long Short Term Memory and Gated Recurrent Unit neural networks perform well over a wider range of lag times. Future work includes the implementation of these algorithms in early warning and intervention systems.

title: A Course Recommendation Algorithm Based on Global Directed Graphs and User Behavioral Sequences
authors: Peng Lu; Pengcheng Xiao; Qian Zhao; Zhousen Zhu; Xuehua Liao
abstract: Existing course recommendation methods typically rely on static course learning records to infer users' overall learning preferences. However, such approaches fail to account for the dynamic evolution of user preferences and short-term interests over time. In this paper, we propose a novel recommendation algorithm, referred to as DPGD, that incorporates a global directed graph and user behavior sequences to address these limitations. The algorithm begins by constructing a global directed graph based on user behavior sequences. This graph is then stored in a graph database to facilitate efficient access and analysis. This representation enables the model to capture both long-term learning preferences and short-term, evolving interests. Subsequently, we compute the similarity between behavior sequences using an appropriate similarity measure, which allows us to assign varying weights to relevant courses, ensuring that the recommendations reflect users' current learning needs. Additionally, we propose a global preference propagation strategy that accounts for the evolution of user preferences over time, thereby improving the accuracy and relevance of recommendations. The final personalized course recommendations are generated by calculating the ratings of the recommended courses based on the propagated preferences. Experimental evaluations on a real-world course learning platform dataset demonstrate that the proposed DPGD algorithm outperforms existing recommendation methods in terms of both effectiveness and feasibility, offering a promising approach for real-world applications.

title: Sketch Recognition Library Applied for an Image Replication with a Humanoid Robot in a Simulated Environment
authors: Steven Pacheco-Portuguez; Martín Naya-Varela; Francisco Bellas-Bouza; Esteban Arias-Méndez
abstract: Sketches have been one of the most ancient techniques used by humans to portray their ideas and thoughts. Replicating this ability would help us to better understand the way in which human beings obtain their capabilities. In this work, we implemented an architecture using convolutional neural networks capable of transforming an image to a sequence of strokes to be replicated by a Poppy humanoid robot using inverse kinematic to reproduce the sketches.

title: Joint Delivery Path Optimization Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
authors: Tianyu Luo; Yunbao Xu; Lining Xing; Jun Li
abstract: Aiming at the characteristics of low transportation efficiency and high transportation cost in the joint delivery path optimization problem, a mathematical optimization model is established to minimize the total cost of transportation, transshipment, and waiting costs by considering the diversify-cation of multiple transportation materials and transportation tools. A new improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is designed to solve the problem. The dimension update strategy of particle velocity is improved to improve the search performance of the algorithm. A new inertia weight update formula is proposed to balance the gap between the local optimum and the global optimum. Six examples of different scales are constructed and compared with the other three classical heuristic algorithms to verify the effectiveness of the model and algorithm in this paper.

title: Development of a real-time framework between Matlab/Simulink and SIEMENS PLC for automated relocation of products in the warehouse
authors: Damian Ignacy; Leszek Gomółka; Ryszard Kopka
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The control system design proposed in the article is a work platform that enables the implementation of control algorithms developed in many different programming languages. This functionality is made possible by integrating the MATLAB/Simulink and TIA Portal programming environments using tools such as: SIMATIC S7-1500 ODK 1500S and SIMATIC Target 1500S for Simulink. The combination of these software tools with the physical execution system implemented in the area of automated warehouse system with product relocation function is a new solution, not yet found in the literature. The above described configuration of software and devices provides the opportunity to implement advanced analytical tools in an industrial environment. Such a configuration also gives the possibility to use other programming languages, such as Python, $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{C}++$, in the algorithm for controlling the automatic warehouse system. The proposed working environment gives the researchers the opportunity to develop and implement complex control algorithms faster in an industrial environment. This allows us to apply advanced artificial intelligence algorithms to control technology.

title: A Teleoperation Method Based on Posture Shared Control Strategy
authors: Xin Wang; Jing Zhao; Ziqiang Zhang
abstract: Because of the superior scalability of teleoperation technology, it is widely used in various fields. However, due to collection errors and structural errors, the master arm may avoid obstacles and collide with the hands of the slave arm. Therefore, this paper proposes an obstacle avoidance teleoperation method based on the posture human-robot shared control strategy, which realizes obstacle avoidance through the joint control of the human arm and the mechanical arm. First, transform the slave arm into a three-link mechanism similar to the human arm, thus realizing the correspondence between the human arm and the heterogeneous mechanical arm. Then, a shared control strategy was developed to synthesize the motion of the manipulator by sharing the control of the end-effector posture, and calculate the joint angle of the manipulator to realize the avoidance of various obstacles by the manipulator. Finally, numerical simulation and physical prototype experiment verify that the method proposed in this paper can avoid obstacles in the process of teleoperation.

title: Vision-based mobile robotic grinding path generation for large castings
authors: Lufeng Chen; Aobo Chen; Yiqun Kuang; Shuai Fan; Jing Qiu
abstract: Given the numerous drawbacks of manual grinding for castings, the use of robots for intelligent grinding is quickly becoming an unavoidable trend. This paper introduces the design of a grinding robot system for the intelligent grinding of medium and large non-standard castings. The proposed system uses labels to identify and scan the surface that needs grinding, subsequently registering and segmenting the obtained point cloud. From here, it converts the select grinding area into a triangular mesh surface, and maps it onto a parametric domain using the re-parameterization method. The system then plots a path on the plane and maps it back onto the original workpiece, acquiring the final grinding path after necessary tool axis adjustments. The grinding head is then manipulated to perform constant force grinding, employing the PID control. Tests have shown that the system can effectively grind the surface of medium and large nonstandard castings in real-world industrial settings.

title: Discrete Fourier Transform-Based Point Cloud Compression for Efficient SLAM in Featureless Terrain
authors: Riku Suzuki; Ayumi Umemura; Shreya Santra; Kentaro Uno; Kazuya Yoshida
abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is an essential technology for the efficiency and reliability of unmanned robotic exploration missions. While the onboard computational capability and communication bandwidth are critically limited, the point cloud data handled by SLAM is large in size, attracting attention to data compression methods. To address such a problem, in this paper, we propose a new method for compressing point cloud maps by exploiting the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT). The proposed technique converts the Digital Elevation Model (DEM) to the frequency-domain 2D image and omits its high-frequency components, focusing on the exploration of gradual terrains such as planets and deserts. Unlike terrains with detailed structures such as artificial environments, high-frequency components contribute little to the representation of gradual terrains. Thus, this method is effective in compressing data size without significant degradation of the point cloud. We evaluated the method in terms of compression rate and accuracy using camera sequences of two terrains with different elevation profiles.

title: Automatic Detection Device for Ripple of Mine Power Supply
authors: Wenqiang XIE
abstract: Power supply ripple, as one of the important indexes to measure the quality of power supply, has an important influence on the stability and reliability of mine electronic equipment. Because of its special working environment and load requirements, mine power supply puts forward higher requirements for the suppression and detection of power supply ripple. This paper expounds the generation mechanism of power supply ripple, analyzes the difference between linear power supply and switching power supply in ripple generation, and puts forward an automatic detection device for mine power supply ripple. The hardware of the device is highly integrated with high-precision detection equipment such as oscilloscope, source voltage and electronic load, and the software adopts virtual instrument technology to design an automatic detection system for mine power supply ripple. The experimental results show that the automatic detection device for mine power supply ripple has been improved in accuracy, stability and automation, which provides a more efficient and reliable solution for mine power supply ripple detection.

title: Adaptive Dynamic Programming-Based Distributed Coordinated Control for Dual-Arm Reconfigurable Manipulators
authors: Guanting Liu; Yuanchun Li; Meng Qu; Tianjiao An; Mingchao Zhu; Bing Ma
abstract: In this paper, a distributed coordinated control method of dual-arm reconfigurable manipulators based on adaptive dynamic programming is proposed. Through kinematic analysis, the dynamic models of the reconfigurable manipulators and the grasped object are established, respectively. According to the load distribution method, the motion induction force is effectively distributed on each arm. Then, the dynamic model of a single reconfigurable manipulator is obtained. The performance index function is defined to reflect the joint position tracking error and internal force tracking error. The neural network is utilized to approximate the performance index function to obtain the optimal control strategy through the Policy Iteration (PI) algorithm. Thus, a distributed optimal coordinated controller is acquired. The tracking error of the manipulator system is proved be ultimately uniformly bounded (UUB) through Lyapunov's stability. Finally, the effectiveness of the developed control method is verified by simulations.

title: Adaptive Safety Control of a Constrained Uncertain Robotic System
authors: Haijing Wang; Jinzhu Peng; Fangfang Zhang; Yaonan Wang
abstract: The safety control problem of a constrained uncertain robotic system is investigated in this paper. First, the high-order control barrier functions (HoCBFs) are introduced to deal with the output constraints for he system. And to solve the uncertain problem and revisit the HoCBF-based framework, an adaptive approach is proposed to updating the unknown parameters online. In this way, the system safety can be achieved adaptively by keeping the system output within the predefined constrained region even in the presence of parametric uncertainty. Finally, simulation tests are carried out to verify the validity of the proposed controller.

title: Control Design on a Non-minimum Phase Bilinear System by Output Redefinition and Particle Swarm Optimization Method
authors: Ahmadin; Janson Naiborhu; Khozin Mu'tamar
abstract: In this paper, we present a technique for designing the input control to asymptotically track the output of a nonminimum-phase bilinear system. The bilinear system becomes minimum phase as a result of the control input's design, which is based on a redefinition output. Additionally, the chosen output's intended output will be set based on the system's original desired output. Particle Swarm Optimization chooses the output that produces the desired outcome from the output that has been chosen. This design enables the system's output to match the desired output of the original system.

title: Joint Space Variable Impedance Control in Stair Descent of a Wheeled Humanoid Robot
authors: Xiyuan Li; Yibo Song; Guoli Sun; Changwei Cheng
abstract: This paper conducts a comprehensive investigation into joint space Variable Impedance Control (VIC) for a Wheeled Humanoid Robot (WHR) during stair descent. It starts by examining the structural characteristics, kinematics model, and equivalent dynamics model of the WHR, thereby establishing the theoretical foundation for designing the control algorithm. Subsequently, the principles of joint space VIC are elaborated, including impedance parameter selection, adjustment mechanisms, and how the control algorithm ensures joint compliance and stability. By continuously monitoring torso acceleration, roll angle, wheel-ground contact status, and dynamically modulating the joint impedance characteristics of the WHR accordingly, while simultaneously adjusting the target hip joint angles based on the torso's pitch angle, the proposed control strategy effectively manages joint torques. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the VIC approach compared to traditional fixed impedance control strategies in joint space. The findings clearly indicate that the VIC method enhances the stability and smoothness of the WHR's motion, enabling it to descend stairs with greater precision and confidence. This research significantly contributes to the field of WHRs by offering a more robust and adaptable control strategy for navigating complex terrains.

title: Aggregation Algorithms for Graph Coloring
authors: Krzysztof Pieńkosz
publication_title: 2021 25th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Many practical applications in production systems can be formulated in terms of graph coloring, for example task scheduling or planning a robot moves. In the paper a class of heuristic algorithms for graph coloring is considered which use the technique of aggregation of vertices. It is shown that some well known constructive heuristics like GIS and RLF belong to the class of vertex aggregation algorithms. In fact, they only differ in the rule that is used to select a pair of vertices to aggregate in the successive steps of the algorithm. In the paper various variants of the aggregation algorithm have been examined and some new rules have been developed that result in better coloring than RLF with the same computational complexity.

title: A Low Complexity Parameter Extraction Digital Predistortion Technique for Frequency Hopping Transmitter
authors: Yaqi Wu; Xu Lu; Xinyue Zhu; Zunyan Liu; Zhang Chen
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: In wireless communication systems, frequency Hooping (FH) is one of the anti-jamming communication systems. However, the nonlinear distortion of power amplifier (PA) in FH communication systems, it will lead to serious signal distortion. This paper proposed a low complexity digital pre-distortion parameter extraction mothed for FH transmitter. The signal's distortion characteristics are integrated into an operator matrix. Consequently, a single set of coefficients is applied to linearize the different carrier frequencies. Finally, the proposed algorithm is experimentally verified. The experimental parameters are set to 20 MHz QAM for the baseband signal and then up-converted to different carriers from 5.6 GHz to 5.7 GHz, with the step of 50MHz.

title: Rapid Release of Micro-Objects by Using Compound Drive Vibration
authors: Shunfa Liu; Rixin Wang; Lixin Yang; Hai Li; Xianmin Zhang; Benliang Zhu
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: A release operation method based on vibration control of a compound-driven microgripper is proposed for the adhesion phenomenon of micro-objects released by the microgripper in micro assembly. The gripper is driven by a composite of a piezoelectric stack and a single-layer piezoelectric ceramic, and the gripping stroke can be expanded to 115. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$26\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> by a two-stage amplification mechanism. The pull-off forces required to release different objects are analysed using JKR elastic adhesion theory, and the feasibility of using the vibrations of the piezoelectric cantilever beam to generate inertial forces for release is demonstrated. Finally, an experimental system was built to test the gripper stroke. Release experiments were performed with 200 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> polystyrene spheres and 160 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> precision-printed cylinders. The results show the effectiveness of the vibration release strategy.

title: Design and Implementation of Coal Mine Equipment Management System
authors: ChangJun Yang; Wei Li; Jin Xu; ZhenMing Zhang; Chunhua Huang; Yong Li; Bo Yang; Dong Chen
abstract: There are many types of mechanical and electrical equipment in coal mines, and the management tasks are heavy. In order to improve the management level and utilization efficiency of equipment, this paper analyzes the main requirements of coal mine electromechanical equipment management, designs a business process for cross-departmental full-cycle equipment management, and uses the software layered architecture design method to develop a coal mine equipment management system based on ASP.NET and MySQL database. The system realizes the dynamic management of equipment information, and provides reliable technical support for the online management and efficient maintenance of equipment.

title: Design of an Automatic Locking Nut Tightening Control System for a Vision Guided Robot
authors: Kai Chang; Bolin Lu; Jian Yin; Guangchao Tan
abstract: A set of automatic locking nut tightening control system for a vision guided robot is designed and implemented. Through hand-eye calibration, the coordinate system is unified. By the designed tool plate and tapered tooling, the calibrated reference location for the tightening tool is realized. According to the position and orientation of the reference screw, the vision system detects the offset of the current screw position, and guides the robot to adjust the pose of the tightening tool. By setting up the network topology of the control system, the data interaction of each subsystem is completed, and the automatic workflow is realized. The application of the system can avoid the relative movement between the tool and screw during the tightening process, and improve the tightening quality.

title: Estimation and Control of Nodes in an Abstract Space
authors: Anish Sridharan; Vinay Venkanagoud Patil; Samarth Bhat; M J Venkatarangan
abstract: It is very common to deploy multi-mobile robots in swarm robotic applications that is targeted for co-ordinated tasks that needs specific formations. The coordination and hence the formations require a good framework of communication, positioning, and controls. Many proposed architectures for indoor systems depend on a camera or another kind of beaconing system for positioning the robots. The paper describes a method using a relative coordinate system without the need for external sensors and is applicable to indoor systems. The initial setup needs the designated global master node and all other nodes to be placed in pre-determined form so that the initial relative distances between the global master and other nodes are known. At the start-up of the system, the configured global master robot node scans and builds the list of all available robot nodes. The global master node will assign the roles of leaders and followers including the global master node itself so that the controls will be distributed. The formation controls are achieved by limiting the communication of the local master to the slaves. Each local master also has the role of a slave to propagate the position with master being the head of the swarm in this chain. The formulated system has been prototyped with generic flow charts and the performance measured show the results to indicate that they can be well utilised in real time system projects.

title: An Automated Magnetic Micro-Robot Assembly System
authors: Oliver J. Shindell; David J. Cappelleri
publication_title: 2025 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: This paper presents the Automated Magnetic Micro-Robot Assembly System, a novel system that is used for fabricating micro-robots with embedded permanent magnets. Micro-robots featuring embedded magnets are more controllable and observable, and capable of tasks requiring higher forces. A micromanipulator is used to control tweezers, and stepper motors are used to control a system of four stages where various assembly steps are performed. Vision-based feedback from an overhead microscope camera ensures precise assemblies, employing contour-based image processing algorithms to identify robots, magnets, and other features. Embedded magnets are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$250 \mu ~\mathrm{m}$</tex> cubes. A single robot takes approximately 192 seconds to assemble, plus 119 seconds for each additional embedded magnet beyond the first, for more complex designs. These times are 45.7 % and 51.8 % of the times required for a practiced human manually performing the task. A total of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20 \mu$</tex>-magnets can be embedded in a single batch. This work is an advancement in the field of micro-assembly, pushing micro-robotics closer to real medical use by establishing a basis for mass production.

title: A Structure Design and Finite Element Analysis of a Dual Servo-Driven Gripping Manipulator
authors: Jing Sheng; Shuliang Wu; Guoman Liu; Xin Ma; Tao Sun; Chengjian Huang; Yongwei Chen
abstract: In response to the difficulties in grasping irregular objects and the single grasping angle issue of mechanical claws carried by small multi-rotor aerial vehicles, this paper takes the grasping mechanical claw carried by multi-rotor aerial vehicles as the research object and designs a four-finger mechanical claw driven by dual servos that can rotate. First, the mechanical claw model was established in SolidWorks, and then it was imported into ANSYS Workbench for static and transient dynamic analysis of the push-pull crank and meshing gears of the mechanical claw, obtaining the total deformation and stress distribution cloud diagrams of each component. The analysis results indicate that during the process of grasping objects, the maximum stress of the push-pull crank and meshing gears of the mechanical claw is far less than the material yield strength, and all meet the working requirements. This provides a reference for the design and optimization of similar structures such as mechanical claws carried by rotor aerial vehicles.

title: Research on the Application of Robot Technology in the Field of Education
authors: Chenggong Zhai; Shiqiang Yuan; Liyong Zhou; Wenke Yao; Hongsi Xu; Qing Wan
abstract: The rapid rise of robotics technology is currently the most popular technological development in the world, and some people believe it is the biggest technological transformation since the Industrial Revolution. This article summarizes the significance and advantages of the application of robot technology in the field of education, studies the application of robot technology in preschool education, basic education, and higher education, and explores the future development trends and challenges of robot technology in the field of education. It has been proposed that if robot technology is used in the right way, teachers will have more time to teach directly, try new ideas, and teach their courses more deeply than ever before.

title: Experimental Validation of a Proposed Effective Linear Variable Differential Transducer Bogie Mounting Bracket for Circle Line Trains
authors: Zheng Jie Fermi Toh; Andrew Keong Ng; Sher Lin Ting
abstract: The Linear Variable Differential Transducer (LVDT) system plays a critical role in condition monitoring (CDM) of the Circle Line's (CCL) third rail and facilitating comprehensive network-wide visibility. However, recurring failures in the bolts attached to the LVDT Bogie Mounting Bracket (BMB) have compromised the system's intended function, impairing its availability and reliability. To address these issues, a redesign of the LVDT BMB that reduced stress concentrations, frequency resonances, and vibrations was proposed. Before live implementation, the LVDT BMB must be experimentally validated with Hammer impact tests, incremental tensile tests, and fatigue tests to evaluate the effectiveness of the redesigned LVDT BMB as compared to the existing solution. The hammer impact tests demonstrated a reduction in vibrations of 3% to 26% across eight points of incremental excitations. The incremental tensile tests revealed that the redesigned LVDT BMB outperformed the current design at all displacement levels (-1 mm to +1 mm), achieving stress reductions of 75 % to 97 % due to strategic chamfers that minimized stress concentration. Run-to-failure fatigue tests showed that the current LVDT BMB failed at 139,717 cycles (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.4 \text{mm}, 700 \mathrm{N}$</tex>) and 526,368 cycles (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.5 \text{mm}, 900 \mathrm{N}$</tex>). Attempts to recreate the forces with similar displacement values resulted in elevated forces that exceeded operational boundaries. These tests have successfully validated the redesigned LVDT BMB's resistance to fatigue failure and its potential to enhance the reliability of the LVDT BMB, reduce corrective maintenance, and increase CCL network train availability.

title: Simulation analysis and experiment of unpowered roller conveying for culture bottle in tissue culture plant
authors: Yanli Yang; Qi Chu; Meizhang Gu; Hanhan Ji; Song Gu
abstract: At present, the commercial production of tissue culture seedlings at home and abroad is mainly manual, and most of the culture frames in tissue culture factories are fixed, with many layers and high shelves. The work on the upper and lower culture frames of culture bottles is frequent, and the labor intensity of operators is high and the risk is high. In this paper, the inclined unpowered roller culture frame is adopted, and the automatic transportation of tissue culture bottles in the culture frame is realized by gravity without setting electric drive mechanism. It can not only reduce the intensity of manual operation, but also facilitate the subsequent use of lifting device to automatically take and place the culture bottles at both ends of the culture frame, so as to realize the automatic transportation of culture bottles. Firstly, based on ADAMS motion analysis software, the simulation test of 20 m long distance inclined unpowered roller conveying operation is carried out, and the results show that the roller inclination angle has the most significant impact on the conveying speed. The test results show that the roller length is 500mm, the distance between rollers is 100mm, the rolling resistance torque of common roller is 7.5 ± 0.43n. m, and the rolling resistance torque of damping roller is 22.88 ± 1.98n. m When the inclination angle of the roller is 3 degree and the damping interval is 3, the normal conveying of culture bottles can be ensured.

title: An Average-Distance Minimizing Motion Sweep for Bounded Spatial Objects and Its Application in Bézier-Like Freeform Motion Generation
authors: Huan Liu; Qiaode Jeffrey Ge
abstract: This paper uses the ellipsoidal parameters associated with volume moments of inertia of a bounded solid object to construct a motion sweep joining two poses of the solid object, in contrast to earlier works on motion interpolation in SE(3) without taking into account the shape of the moving object. The paper borrows the concept of shape-dependent object norms introduced by Kazerounian and Rastegar [1] and refined by Chirikjian and Zhou [2] to compute as a metric the average of the squared distances (or ASD) among all homologous points of the bounded body between two given poses and seeks to obtain an optimal interpolating motion that minimizes a combination of two ASD distances from each intermediate pose to the two given poses. It is found that the ASD minimizing motion sweep is a novel straight-line motion such that while the centroid of the object follows a straight line, the orientation of the object is constrained so that the ASD metric is minimized. Furthermore, the rotational component can be determined by polar decomposition of the linearly interpolated rotation matrices, scaled by the object's inertial parameters. As an illustration of one of its applications, this motion sweep is repeatedly applied using the de Casteljau algorithm to generate Bézier-like freeform motions, whose paths are in general dependent on the shape of the inertia ellipsoid.

title: Design of A Rigid-soft Hybrid Robotic Glove with Force Sensing Function
authors: Hexin Li; Li Jiang; Ruichen Zhen; Ming Cheng; Kehan Ding
abstract: Soft robotic gloves can not only provide timely, effective, safe and cheap rehabilitation training for patients with impaired movement function of hand, but also assist in completing daily grasping activities. However, most soft robotic gloves are completely composed of flexible structures. Although they have high flexibility and safety, there are problems such as poor fit and low output force. In order to solve these problems, this paper refers to the structure of the human hand and designs an articulated rigid-soft hybrid robotic glove, which combines the advantages of rigid robotic gloves and soft robotic gloves, and has high flexibility, high output force and good fit. In addition, soft robotic gloves generally lack the ability to sense the force between the human hand and the glove. Therefore, this paper designed an array flexible force sensor, and studied the structure, signal acquisition and preparation process of the sensor. Finally, a complete test platform was built to test the performance of the rigid-soft hybrid robotic glove with force sensing function. The test results show that the robotic glove has good fit and high output force, can effectively assist training and assist grasping, and can perceive the contact force.

title: A Few-Shot Anomaly Detection Method Based on BYOL Contrastive Learning Framework
authors: Zhipeng Deng; Junfeng Man; Zhiguang Song; Gen Yang
abstract: In industrial image detection tasks, traditional anomaly detection methods often heavily rely on extensive normal samples to establish the distribution of normal features. However, in the case of insufficient data, the performance of these methods usually degrades significantly. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a new fewshot anomaly detection (FSAD) method. This method leverages the BYOL (Bootstrap Your Own Latent) contrastive learning framework to fine tune pre-trained neural networks, minimizing the distances among normal features. Consequently, the proposed FSAD method enables the model to capture variations in features across diverse samples more accurately, thereby enhancing its anomaly detection capabilities in few-shot scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly surpasses other prevalent anomaly detection techniques. This innovative approach offers new perspectives for anomaly detection tasks in industrial scenarios.

title: Accelerating Robotic Picking of Rigid Objects with a Compliant Pneumatic Gripper and an Impact-Aware Trajectory Plan
authors: Frederik Ostyn; Bram Vanderborght; Guillaume Crevecoeur
abstract: Industrial robots are capable of moving at high speed. Each time they come into contact with their environment, e.g. to pick up an object, they decelerate to a near standstill. A solution involving a compliant pneumatic gripper and adapted trajectory plan is presented to initiate contact at a higher speed while remaining within hardware limits. By adding overload clutches in either the robot arm or gripper, tolerance to errors is provided. The key parameters such as gripper compliance and maximum allowed initial impact velocity are identified. Results show that by properly optimizing these parameters, robot picking of rigid objects can be accelerated. The complete high-speed picking solution is experimentally verified. A time reduction of 16% was obtained when making contact at 0.65 m/s.

title: Research on Precision Control Strategy of Space-Borne Pointing Mechanism
authors: Xia Chang; Chun Wang; Zhihong Liu
abstract: In order to achieve accurate imaging and positioning of targets with a wide field of view in the ocean, and to accomplish high-precision imaging in the region of space-borne point calibration, this article utilizes a design approach for controlling the position of a spatial pointing mirror based on closed-loop control using dual feedback of position and velocity. The article explains the composition of the system, the position closed-loop control algorithm, the angle solving method, and the quantization error. Aiming to address the issue of rounding errors in PWM, the software utilizes a delay correction compensation method for error compensation. The test results show that the design method can meet the requirements for high-precision pointing in orbit. This finding can serve as a reference for the subsequent development of high-precision pointing control software and similar products in space.

title: LAV-ACT: Language-Augmented Visual Action Chunking with Transformers for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
authors: Dhurba Tripathi; Chunting Liu; Niraj Pudasaini; Yu Hao; Anthony Tzes; Yi Fang
abstract: Bimanual robotic manipulation, involving the coordinated use of two robotic arms, is essential for tasks requiring complex, synchronous actions. Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) is a representative framework that enables robots to break down complex tasks into manageable sequences, facilitating autonomous learning of multi-step actions. However, we observe limitations in the ACT framework: it relies solely on visual observations as input, focusing on task-specific action predictions, and it uses a simple ResNet-based feature extractor for image processing, which is often insufficient for complex and multi-view bimanual arm observations. In this paper, we introduce an enhanced language-augmented version of ACT that leverages Voltron-a language-driven representation model-to incorporate both visual observations and language prompts into dense, multi-modal embeddings. These embeddings are used to condition the ResNet backbone feature maps through Featurewise Linear Modulation (FiLM), allowing our model to integrate contextually relevant linguistic information with visual data for more adaptive action chunking.
