Extensive experiments show that our approach significantly improves the performance of bimanual robot arms in executing complex, multi-step tasks guided by language cues, outperforming traditional ACT methods. Project website: https://dktpt44.github.io/LAV-ACT/

title: Mechanical Characterization Analysis of Kirigami Structure for Soft Robotic Design
authors: Muhammad Niaz Khan; Amin Lotfiani; Umair Javaid; Zhufeng Shao
abstract: This paper provides a detailed mechanical characterization and stress analysis of kirigami sheets across various structural configurations, highlighting their potential applications in soft robotics. The study examines linear, circular, triangular, and trapezoidal kirigami patterns through finite element simulations, complemented by experimental validation. Deformation parameters are systematically applied to both single and multiple units of kirigami sheets to assess their capacity for mechanical elongation and load sustainability. Additionally, friction analyses are discussed via simulation to explore the anchoring effects of these kirigami structures when applied to soft robots. The results of this study enhance our understanding of the mechanical properties of kirigami structures and their practical implications for soft robotics design.

title: Automatic Summary Generation of Chinese News Text Based on Cross-Layer Parameter Shared Transformer-Encoder-PGN Model
authors: Yuan Wu; Changhui Liu; Yangwenhao Liu
abstract: To address the problems that the traditional neural Seq2Seq model is difficult to replicate factual details, cannot handle words out of word list, and the generated content is prone to self-duplication, a generative summary model based on Transformer Encoder-PGN with cross-layer parameter sharing is proposed for Chinese news texts. The contextual word embedding vector is first obtained using a Transformer Encoder pre-trained model with across layers shared parameters combined with word location features. Words are then copied from the original text using a copying mechanism through a pointer generator model, or extracted from a glossary to form a summary. Finally, the model uses the coverage mechanism to dynamically adjust the attention distribution to avoid repeated content generation. Experiments on the Chinese dataset of Weibo news, Rouge-l, Rouge-2 and Rouge-L reach 39.35%, 27.60% and 37.86%, respectively, which are 1.16%, 2.01% and 2.22% higher than the PGN model using LSTM-Attention, and the generated abstracts are more concise and accurate, indicating that the model has a more comprehensive and adequate understanding of the original text.

title: Understanding Internet Usage Patterns and Behaviors Among College Students: A Machine Learning Approach
authors: Alvin T. Remolado; Darrel A. Cardaña
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Control & [::Automation::]; Electronics; [::Robotics::]; Internet of Things; and Artificial Intelligence (CERIA)
abstract: This study explores internet usage patterns and behaviors among students enrolled in Information Technology Education (ITE) programs in the province of Bohol, Philippines. Despite the widespread availability of Internet resources, there is limited understanding of how ITE students utilize the Internet for academic and personal purposes. This research aims to identify key patterns and factors influencing internet usage frequency at school, home, and other locations. Utilizing machine learning techniques and exploratory data analysis (EDA), the study analyzed data from a structured questionnaire administered to ITE students through Google Forms. Classification models, including Random Forest Classifier, Decision Trees, and Support Vector Classifier, were employed to predict internet usage levels based on demographic and behavioral data. Results indicate that ITE students exhibit high levels of internet usage, with significant correlations between the frequency of internet usage at school, home, and for various purposes with overall internet usage levels. Among the models, SVC achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 99.53%. In comparison, Random Forest Classifier attained 92.63% accuracy, while Decision Trees performed at 84.02% accuracy. These insights can inform educational institutions and policymakers in developing strategies to enhance internet accessibility and digital literacy among students, ultimately improving educational outcomes and digital inclusion.

title: Design of a Novel Pneumatic Soft Gripper for Robust Adaptive Grasping
authors: Xiantao Sun; Mingsheng Zhong; Zhouzheng Tang; Wenjie Chen; Weihai Chen
abstract: Soft grippers have shown promising performance in safe and adaptive grasping tasks. However, they often suffer from limitations in grasping force. To address this challenge, this paper presents a novel pneumatic three-finger soft gripper to achieve robust adaptive grasping. The gripper consists of three identical fingers, each containing a pneumatic bending soft actuator and a pneumatic lateral soft actuator. The bending actuator features a tilted pneumatic network structure, which provides superior bending performance compared to traditional vertical pneumatic network structure. The lateral actuator is equipped with three deflection chambers at the finger root to mimic the lateral motions of a human finger. Kinematic and static models are established to predict the bending angle and grasping force of the soft finger under pressurized air. The performance of the proposed soft finger is analyzed through finite element simulations, and the effect of the chamber tilt angle is also examined. The theoretical and simulation results are compared to verify the validity of the analytical models. Finally, the proposed soft gripper is fabricated by 3D printing and molding. Experimental results show that the gripper is capable of grasping various objects of different sizes, shapes, materials, and weights, and can perform dexterous manipulation tasks, such as cap unscrewing. The proposed soft gripper exhibits significant potential for applications in robotic robust grasping tasks.

title: Anode Current for Aluminum Electrolysis Cell Condition Identification Based on Improved Temporal Convolutional Network
authors: Jiuliang Zhou; Xiaofang Chen; Shiwen Xie; Yongfang Xie
abstract: The stable operation of the aluminum electrolysis cell is the basis for the safe and efficient production of the electrolytic aluminum industry, and the cell condition identification technology is an important means to ensure the normal operation of the aluminum electrolysis cell. The cell condition identification technology based on anode current signal has played an increasingly important role in identify and fine control large aluminum electrolysis cells. This paper proposes an improved temporal convolutional network, which uses the time characteristics of the current signal to classify the current sequence for cell condition identification. The classification result can help people identify and monitor the conditions of the electrolysis cell. In this paper, the proposed method is verified on the real current signal, which can be used to identify various cell conditions such as anode effect and anode sliding.

title: Servo system Cascade Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control Based on Motor Models
authors: Yuang He; Qijia Zheng; Jialun Liu; Yan Wang; Qian Fan
abstract: The electromechanical servo system is usually implemented by three closed loops, with the inner loop being the current loop, the middle loop being the speed loop, and the outer loop being the position loop. The traditional system tuning method is the PI parameter trial and error method, which cannot achieve the optimal performance of the system. This article innovatively adopts the LADRC three closed-loop cascade control method. Compared with previous control methods, the control method applied in this article can ensure that the current loop, speed loop, and position loop control circuits all meet the requirements of the Bode theorem, which provides a basis for the control objectives. This article provides a detailed description of the selection methods for the control order, observer bandwidth, controller bandwidth, and loop gain of each control loop. This method was validated and ultimately achieved stable control of the electromechanical servo system.

title: Research On The Key Frame Selection Method Of YOLOv5-Based Intelligent Damage Determination System
authors: Qianqian Zhu; Yingnan Liu; Xuening Wu; Jiaying Huang
abstract: In vehicle damage claims, the intelligent damage determination method based on computer vision instead of manual observation has become the future direction of technology. In the process of wise damage determination, because of the difficulty that the images taken manually cannot be quickly shot with the image quality applicable to the system, this paper proposes a keyframe selection method based on the YOLOv5 model, which solves the problems of convenience and ease of use of the intelligent damage determination system by adding the real-time operation guidance function at the time of the shooting. Firstly, the mobile real-time detection model YOLOv5 detects and counts the vehicle appearance parts. Secondly, the underlying logic determination model guides the user to complete the shooting distance adjustment. Experimenting with the self-built vehicle image data set, the average accuracy of mAP50 reached 94.10/0, and YOLOv5 can meet the requirements of real-time and accuracy of keyframe selection in shooting environments such as uneven lighting and complex surrounding background.

title: Road Scene Image Segmentation based on Deep Learning and Meta Pruning
authors: Pindeng Wang; Mengbo Jia; Yaocong Hu; Ke Xu; Huicheng Yang; Xiao Liu; Jixing Zhao
abstract: Semantic segmentation of road scenes is crucial in autonomous driving technology, as it involves identifying and understanding the surrounding environment in real time and accurately, which requires a segmentation network that can process a large amount of image data quickly in real time and accurately distinguish different objects in a complex and changing environment, usually this model is too complex to guarantee real time or too simplified, resulting in a large reduction in accuracy. Existing lightweight models primarily focus on reducing computational load and the number of parameters, but the significance of network parameters to model performance is ignored or difficult to distinguish. To overcome the issue, we propose a novel approach combining deep learning with meta pruning to construct a light weighted road scene segmentation model, The advantage of meta pruning is that it evaluates the significance of different parameters to the network model, retaining the significant parameters and removing the minor ones to achieve precise pruning. The current results show that the method performs well on standard data sets.

title: Nonlinear Output Voltage Control of Triboelectric Nanogenerator System
authors: Ryusei Shimane; Mingcong Deng; Guang Jin
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in energy harvesting, driven by the increasing focus on IoT (Internet of Things) and carbon reduction. The triboelectric nanogenerator(TENG) harnesses the triboelectric effect and electrostatic induction to convert mechanical energy, such as vibrations, into electrical energy, serving as an energy harvesting device. Therefore, TENG has attracted attention. While it offers advantages such as low cost and high robustness, a drawback lies in the instability of the output voltage. The objective of this paper is to design a control system that combines operator theory, sliding mode control(SMC), and a disturbance compensator to mitigate modeling errors, ensuring the output voltage tracks the setpoint. This article is organized as follows: Section II provides an overview of the TENG system, while Section III outlines the design of the control system. Section IV presents the results of simulations controlling the DC-DC converter with and without disturbance compensator included in the control system. Finally, Section V concludes the article.

title: Analysis and Structure Design of the Underwater Hexapod Robot Leg
authors: Zhang Lianzhao; Wang Pengfei; Zha Fusheng; Bi Xiuwen; Guo Wei; Chen Chen
abstract: In this paper, the leg structure design of an underwater hexapod robot was carried out based on the establishment of the dynamics model considering the influence of the water dynamics. The basic leg structure was selected and the kinematics model of the leg was analyzed firstly to obtain the leg link velocities and the Jacobian matrix. Based on the link velocities and the Jacobian matrix obtained, the leg dynamics model of the underwater robot considering the water influence was constructed through the combination of the Lagrange equation and Morison equation. With the dynamics model established, simulation experiments were carried out based on Fluent and Adams platforms to get the maximum joint torques. According to the maximum joint torques achieved, appropriate joint motors were chosen to finally fulfill the detailed leg structure design.

title: Extending the Cooperative Dual-Task Space in Conformal Geometric Algebra
authors: Tobias Löw; Sylvain Calinon
abstract: In this work, we are presenting an extension of the cooperative dual-task space (CDTS) in conformal geometric algebra. The CDTS was first defined using dual quaternion algebra and is a well established framework for the simplified definition of tasks using two manipulators. By integrating conformal geometric algebra, we aim to further enhance the geometric expressiveness and thus simplify the modeling of various tasks. We show this formulation by first presenting the CDTS and then its extension that is based around a cooperative pointpair. This extension keeps all the benefits of the original formulation that is based on dual quaternions, but adds more tools for geometric modeling of the dual-arm tasks. We also present how this CGACDTS can be seamlessly integrated with an optimal control framework in geometric algebra that was derived in previous work. In the experiments, we demonstrate how to model different objectives and constraints using the CGA-CDTS. Using a setup of two Franka Emika robots we then show the effectiveness of our approach using model predictive control in real world experiments.

title: Ground Contact and Reaction Force Sensing for Linear Policy Control of Quadruped Robot
authors: Harshita Mhaske; Aniket Mandhare; Jidong Huang; Yu Bai
abstract: Efforts have been made in the past years to reduce the cost of entry into legged robotics research, which has extended into development of computationally light-weight control policies that can be deployed on cost-effective hardware. While there is no restriction to the nature of inputs to such policies, they typically rely only on inertial data to observe the robot state. However, since legged robots primarily interact with the environment through ground contact and reaction forces, it is crucial to include these data in the observation space of a policy. This paper investigates the effect of including terrain sensing via ground contacts and ground reaction forces in the observation space on the ability of the policy to adapt robot behavior to terrain variations. Further, a comparison is made between the performance improvement when using ground contacts versus ground reaction forces. We present experimental data that demonstrate the advantages of including terrain sensing in combination with inertial data by improving robot survivability and stability. Lastly, based on the results of the comparison between the two methods of terrain sensing, we present a low-cost hardware implementation of ground contact detection.

title: Biasing Bending DEA-enabled Serial Kinematic thin Soft Robot for Locomotion and Manipulation in Confined Spaces
authors: Xi Wang; Jung-Che Chang; Siqian Li; Feiran Wang; Xin Dong
abstract: Soft robotics, actuated by smart materials and compliant mechanisms, offer significant potential for miniaturization, enabling deployment in confined spaces for inspection and maintenance tasks—areas where is a challenge for traditional robots. However, existing miniaturized soft robots generally exhibit limited locomotion modes, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios. This research introduces a novel serial kinematic thin soft robot (SK-TS-Robot) featuring a biasing bending dielectric elastomer actuator (DEA) as active joint. The SK-TS-Robot comprises two thin soft robots (TS-Robot) connected by the basing bending DEA and is capable of five gaits. It is able to perform crawling, steering, climbing, transitioning, and manipulation in confined spaces. The biasing bending DEA, constructed with an elastic bending frame and four-layer dielectric elastomers, can bend up to 90° when unactuated and unfold to a flat state when actuated. The joint provides sufficient force to ensure effective transitioning and manipulation. Using this active joint, we demonstrated the SK-TS-Robot's ability to 'repair' an electric circuit, lighting an LED, and program Morse code 'SOS' through controllable joint actuation.

title: Neural-Network-Based Finite-Time Fault-Tolerance Consensus Control of Second-Order Systems Under Channel Fading and Input Quantized
authors: Zijing Li; Kai Zheng; Shuanghe Yu
abstract: In this article, the main focus is finite-time fault-tolerant consensus problem of second-order nonlinear multiagent systems with input quantization and channel fading. By using neural networks to approximate nonlinear terms, more accurate estimation of nonlinear functions can be achieved. Combining sliding mode controller with neural networks to improve the robustness. Combining control theoretical knowledge, a detailed analysis was conducted on the consensus analysis under channel fading and input quantization. Examples and simulation results were provided to verify the effectiveness of theoretical results.

title: A Framework for Model Sailing Simulation in Gazebo
authors: Adam Wolniakowski; Maja Czarna
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Recently there has been increased demand in wind power usage in maritime transportation. At the same time, due to numerous advances, interest in autonomous mobile platforms is at its all-time peak. The utilization of green Unmanned Surface Vehicle fleets could provide enormous benefits in research, security and transportation. The development of autonomous sailing vehicles can be greatly assisted with the usage of simulation where the control, planning and navigation systems can be tested and implemented. Furthermore, great synergy can be achieved through integration of software systems of such platforms with existing popular robotic frameworks, such as ROS. In this paper we propose a flexible ROS-based framework for simulation of customizable sailing vessels, focusing on small scale models.

title: Research on a Multi-Sensor-Based Wearable System for Monitoring Infant Vital Signs
authors: Yue Ma; Huaijiang Li; Long Huang; Siyao Ji; Huaihai Li
abstract: In contemporary society, people lead increasingly hectic lives, and for families where both parents are employed, caring for an infant presents significant challenges. Maintaining constant vigilance over an infant's well-being during the night can be particularly distressing. Some disadvantages are associated with manual nursing, such as the high cost and the inability to achieve continuous monitoring at night. To solve this issue, the microchip STM32F103 was employed as the central control unit to develop a wearable intelligent monitoring system for tracking infants’ vital signs during sleep. A wearable design is employed by the system to monitor not only the baby's vital signs but also the baby's sleeping position. These data are wirelessly transmitted to a mobile phone, allowing parents to conveniently monitor their infant's vital signs in real-time. Moreover, in the event of any abnormal conditions, the mobile phone promptly emits a vibrating alert, preventing parents from missing the critical ‘Golden Hour’ for infant rescue, even during deep sleep. Through the analysis and processing of physiological signal data test results, it has been proven that accuracy and reliability are possessed by the equipment detection system. When the preset threshold is exceeded, the phone activates an alarm, successfully achieving the intended outcome through the implementation of the intelligent infant monitoring function.

title: Pose Estimation via Concentric Circles and Lines
authors: Li Xin; Hu Xiaoping; He Xiaofeng; Fan Chen
abstract: Accurate pose estimation is an essential premise for many robotic applications. In this paper, we present a novel method based on a single image of coplanar concentric circles and lines, to achieve the six degrees of freedom (6DOF) pose estimation problem. Concentric circles are proved to be useful in both disambiguating process and achieving the estimate results, and lines can take parts in heading calculation as well as the optimization parts. Numerical simulation experiments in different imaging scenarios and a set of actual flight data are taken in use to verify the effectiveness of our method.

title: Domain Contrastive Alignment Network for Pipeline Fault Diagnosis
authors: Chuang Guan; Chuang Wang; Hongli Dong
abstract: The general domain adaptation (DA) approach focuses on making the source and target domains of the feature space as close as possible, while ignoring the inter and intra-class distances of the domain samples, leading to poor generalization performance of the model. To tackle this issue, a novel Domain Contrastive Alignment Network (DCAN) algorithm is proposed in this paper, which extracts fine-grained information by minimizing the intra-class distance and maximizing the inter-class distance. The proposed DCAN algorithm is applied to the fault diagnosis of oil and gas pipeline networks to verify its performance, and the results of cross-domain experiments show that the DCAN algorithm effectively improves the accuracy of fault diagnosis in comparison with state-of-the-art algorithms.

title: A 3D-Printed Centimeter-Scale Pneumatically Actuated Robotic Manipulator for Micro-Manipulations
authors: Xingwen Zheng; Hao Mo; Haoran Yao; Fumihito Arai
publication_title: 2024 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: This paper presents a centimeter-scale robotic manipulator fabricated using 3D printing technology. It consists of three mechanisms: a grasping mechanism, an RCM (remote center of motion) function mechanism, and a rotational mechanism, actuated by bellows-driven soft pneumatic actuators. Thus, the robotic manipulator enables the grasping of tools for micro-manipulations and the 2-DOF orientation adjustment of the tools, including the rotation around the axis of the rotational mechanism (0° - 45°) and the rotation around an RCM (−10° - 10°). Finally, one 5-DOF robotic manipulation system consisting of the 2-DOF rotational centimeter-scale robotic manipulator and one 3-DOF translational external manipulator (moving speed ~ 500 μm/s) was used to conduct micro-manipulations, in which a printed needle was grasped to carve the desired trajectory on the agar (gel strength ~ 650 g/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) resembling biological tissues. the external manipulator controlled the displacement of the needle while the robotic manipulator adjusted the orientation of the needle insertion into the agar. Results showed that the 5-DOF robotic manipulation system had mechanical stability while achieving micron-level accuracy (200 μm) in the micro-manipulation task.

title: Torque Measurement Using Regression-Based Calibration Approaches; A Mobile Robot Perspective
authors: Harinarayanan Nampoothiri M G; Robin Babu; Rahul Antony
abstract: This study presents a methodology for calculating the rotational torque values of the DC actuators, which is then applied and evaluated in a mobile robot scenario. The influence of torque-sensing on robot applications is substantial. This study focuses on enhancing the accuracy of torque measurement by constructing a regression model that establishes the relationship between torque and the input voltage applied to the motor and the angular velocities of the motor and wheel. The model is trained using data from an electrodynamometer framework that utilizes a counterweight mechanism to generate linear torque. The input voltage is adjusted as a percentage of the entire load value. Relevant sensors are used to monitor the electro-mechanical characteristics, and this data is utilized to generate the model. The framework is compared to a second model that establishes a relationship between torque and current signals. The previous model exhibits superior performance in the regression analysis. The model's efficacy is evaluated in a mobile robot through a case study that predicts wheel slippage. This prediction is accomplished by employing machine learning algorithms that utilize torque signals as input features. Both models are utilized to compute the torque values, and the average performance of the learning algorithms is compared, with the first regression model demonstrating superior results over the second. Therefore, the suggested method of measuring torque by calibrating voltage and angular velocity through regression analysis is suitable for achieving both cost-effectiveness and accuracy in measuring torque in robot actuators.

title: Lidar-only 3D SLAM System Comparative Study
authors: Wenhu Ren; Xueyuan Li; Mengkai Li; Qi Liu; Zirui Li
abstract: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) is an attractive and hot research topic in computer vision, robotics, and artificial intelligence. Autonomous vehicles driving in unknown environments try to perceive and map the surrounding environment while recognizing their location and trajectory. In this paper, five state-of-the-art open-source 3D lidar-only SLAM algorithms are reviewed: LOAM, LeGO-LOAM, F-LOAM, BALM, and MULLS. We briefly introduce the characteristics of these algorithms. Finally, the experimental comparison is carried out to compare the absolute pose error (APE), efficiency, and operation memory occupation of each algorithm.

title: A Data-Driven Fault Detectability Analysis Approach Based on Actuator and Sensor Performance
authors: Yang Song; Weihang Zheng; Yijia Lu; Jiajing Song
abstract: This paper proposes a data-driven method for analyzing the detectability of faults in dynamic systems considering actuator and sensor performance. Firstly, the data-driven residuals are generated using orthogonal factorization and singular value decomposition (SVD) methods. The dynamics of the residuals are then characterized by mean vectors and covariance matrices, which are used to assess the difficulty of distinguishing between fault-free and faulty scenarios. Additionally, the performance evaluation indices of actuators and sensors are introduced, and a bank of performance-based quantitative indices is further employed to evaluate the detectability of various faulty scenarios. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated through a case study involving an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV).

title: Adaptive Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Manipulator with Local Dynamic Linearization
authors: Peng Chen; Qiang Chen; Huihui Shi; Yimin Zhou
abstract: The study delves into the design about Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) for robotic manipulators subjected to external disturbances, with a focus on systems that adhere to universal Lipschitz conditions. A localized linear dynamic modeling method is proposed, such that eliminating the need for precise robot modeling. Furthermore, a law for parameter updating and an flexible extended state estimator are developed to evaluate the control parameters and cumulative uncertainties, respectively. The proposed adaptive feedback controller takes into account the target reference path, parameter adjustment, error feedback, and compensation for overall disturbances caused by estimation inaccuracies of parameters and unidentified nonlinear factors, resulting in improved control performance. This control strategy for the manipulator is data-driven and does not rely on any model information apart from the universal Lipschitz property and the nonzero quality of the gradient of the nonlinear system in relation to the control input. The conceptual findings are validated through manipulator tracking experiments.

title: Numerical Simulation Analysis of Flow and Temperature Fields in Large U-Shaped Heat Exchanger
authors: Chenli Song; Lifeng Li; Lixia Zhu; Shuai Wang
abstract: Based on the comprehensive analysis of the complex structure and material characteristics of a large U-shaped heat exchanger, combined with the thin-shell heat transfer model and the similarity principle, the 3D geometric model of the heat exchanger of the original stabilizing device is constructed. Then, the grid size is greatly reduced by using boundary layer meshing technology. Finally, the temperature field and flow field distribution of the fluid in the heat exchanger are obtained by finite element calculation. The results show that, on the one hand, the condensate temperature is in a local overheating state and the oil flow rate is too low, and there is a retention zone; on the other hand, the temperature in the overheating region decreases with the increase of the shell flow rate. Therefore, the coupling effect of condensate oil retention and local overheating may accelerate the corrosion rate of heat exchanger tube bundle. It is suggested to adjust the operation parameters of the heat exchanger and optimize the internal structure to make the internal flow rate and temperature distribution more reasonable, so as to improve the service safety and reliability of the heat exchanger.

title: Road Tunnels Defects Detection and Classification using Deep Learning
authors: Christos Petrou; Eleanna Kouletou; Yannis Kopsinis; Aikaterini Karagiannopoulou; Georgios Tsimiklis; Angelos Amditis
abstract: A two-step approach is presented in this paper for defect detection and classification in tunnel inspection images using data-driven technologies. In the first step, a denoising auto encoder based on convolutional neural network architecture is employed as an unsupervised defect detector. This detector identifies potential defective regions within a vast collection of inspection images. The annotation process is streamlined by the defect detector, precisely pinpointing defective areas and reducing the overall workload for annotators. The second step involves an ensemble defect classifier that combines a large vision transformer and a U-Net convolutional model to classify the extracted defective regions. The proposed methodology's effectiveness is demonstrated through its successful implementation on a robotic platform for automated visual inspection in the Egnatia Motorway in Greece. This implementation is part of the PILOTING project supported by the European Union's Horizon 2020 innovation action program.

title: Flatness Analysis of a Micro Tandem Helicopter
authors: Joachim Horn
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Considering the dynamic model of a micro tandem helicopter, it is shown that the system is flat and that a flat output is given by the position and attitude of the helicopter.

title: An Averaging Ensemble Method for Multiclass Brain Tumor Classification Using Transfer Learning
authors: Shahajalal Hossain Shahin; Sk. Shariful Alam; Shah Muhammad Azmat Ullah
abstract: A brain tumor is a disease that is caused by the abnormal growth of cells inside the brain or central spinal canal. It originates from the brain or, may spread to the brain from the other parts of the human body. While the exact causes of brain tumors remain unknown, environmental exposure and mutations in genes are the primary factors that significantly influence their progression. It is very difficult to diagnose whether the tumor is cancerous or not by analyzing the MRI images with bare eyes. For this, we need to use computer-aided diagnoses (CAD) to make the treatment easier. We have proposed an ensemble model that consists of the prediction of two deep learning models- Xception & InceptionV3 with accuracy of 97.89% and 91.56% respectively. We have used the data augmentation technique here. The proposed model gives an accuracy of 98.82%. We have also used the DenseNet121 for comparison purposes but among them, the proposed model performs better and gives high accuracy for the dataset contains about 7023 human brain MRI images which are categorized into 4 classes: glioma, meningioma, no-tumor & pituitary. The model averaging ensemble method results demonstrate that utilizing it can successfully categorize the samples that are incorrectly classified by the individual models.

title: Design and Development of a Prototype Upper-limb Rehabilitation Robot Based on Multi-body Dynamics Analysis
authors: Hsiu-Hsien Sung; Chih-Kun Hsiao; Cheng-Kang Lee; Chin-Yu Wang
abstract: The nerve plexus damage of the upper limb provokes the disability of patients and makes a drastic impact both mentally and physically. Therefore, rehabilitation treatments for patients are indispensable. This study focuses on developing a 3-axis rehabilitation robot with targets including the geometric design of body structure, mathematical modeling of the multi-axis mechanism, the multi-body dynamic analysis, the selection of mechatronic systems, and the assembling and solid test of the rehabilitation robot. Through the precedent design, analysis, and simulation using software, the specification and performance can be ensured in advance. The realized rehabilitation robot is quickly developed with a further professional evaluation of the rehabilitating movements. Thus, the most suitable rehabilitating movement for patients can be achieved to enhance the effectiveness of the rehabilitation treatment.

title: Synthesis and Design of Cable-Driven Parallel Robot for High-Speed Metal Sheet Picking and Placing
authors: Zhiyuan Wu; Hanqing Liu; Jinhao Duan; Zhufeng Shao; Chuanying Wang; Guoming Feng; Luwei Liu
abstract: This paper introduces a design of a suspended cable-driven parallel robot (CDPR) tailored for high-speed production line applications, with the objective of accommodating a 180 kg payload, a 5.6 m feed stroke, and an operating speed of 22 strokes per minute (SPM). The robot employs a dual three-parallel-cable configuration, enabling two degrees of freedom (DOF) translational motion through coordinated cable actuation. The study addresses the robot's configuration design, kinematic and dynamic modeling, workspace and anti-disturbance performance analysis, and power optimization. Simulation results demonstrate that within the working trajectory the force margin index (FMI) reaches 809–1431 N, and the moment margin index (MMI) achieves 93- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{147}\ \mathbf{N}\cdot \mathbf{m}$</tex>, fully satisfying the disturbance rejection demands of the production line. By optimizing the S-curve acceleration trajectory, the maximum power of any individual cable is effectively limited to 12.8 kW.

title: Planning Research and Simulation Analysis of Distributed Generation in Distribution Network
authors: Qingtong Sun; Qing Liu
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: Reasonable planning in distribution network can effectively improve power distribution, improve node voltage quality and reduce network loss while unreasonable division may also lead to loss increase, node voltage quality decline and other problems. This paper focuses on the site selection and determination of DG, whose main work is a two-stage programming model used to plan the distributed power supply. In the first stage of distributed power planning, the method of calculating the variance index of network active power sensitivity is used to preliminarily determine location and capacity of DG. In the second stage of planning, minimum investment cost and maximum annual income are objective functions. Minimum of voltage deviation and network loss are objective functions of the third stage of planning, in which multi-objective gray Wolf optimization algorithm is used to optimize the distributed power supply. Then apply this model into IEEE33 node system, whose simulation results verify the effectiveness of the established model. At the same time, planning scheme and variation trend of voltage and under different load capacity are discussed.

title: An Improved Semantic Segmentation Model Based on FCN with Channel Attention and Feature Fusion
authors: Jing Wang; Ruiyao Xing; Meng Zhou; Xiaoping Zhang
abstract: This paper proposes an improved semantic segmentation model based on Fully Convolutional Network(FCN). Firstly, this paper integrates the channel attention module into the backbone of FCN to identify the channels that are more important for semantic segmentation. Secondly, this paper adds a multi-scale feature fusion module to the network to integrate multi-scale feature information. Thirdly, this paper replaces some of standard convolutions in the backbone network with dilated convolutions to increase the receptive field. Experimental results demonstrate that after adding the two modules, the pixel accuracy can reach 75.8%, and the mIOU value has increased by 2.8% compared to the original FCN model. Moreover, utilizing pre-trained weights during the training process can greatly enhance the performance of the model.

title: Fall Detection by 1D-CNN Based on Public Dataset Using a Wrist-Worn Smartwatch
authors: Songsheng Li
abstract: Falls among the elderly population pose a significant threat, often leading to severe injuries, loss of independence, and even fatality. To address this critical issue, researchers have been exploring various approaches to develop effective fall detection systems. In this study, we present a novel fall detection algorithm that leverages the WEDA-FALL dataset, a comprehensive dataset that includes data from wrist-worn sensors capturing both simulated and real-world fall incidents involving elderly individuals. The key insight behind our approach is the observation that falls often exhibit distinct patterns in sensor data. To capture these patterns, we employ a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) architecture, which has been shown to be well-suited for time-series data analysis. By training our model on the WEDA-FALL dataset, we were able to achieve an impressive accuracy of 94% in fall detection, surpassing the commonly reported accuracy levels of around 90% in the existing literature. The high performance of our algorithm can be attributed to the use of the WEDA-FALL dataset and the effectiveness of the 1D-CNN architecture in extracting and learning the characteristic patterns in the sensor data. Notably, our algorithm offers the key features of being quick, highly accurate, and cost-effective, making it a promising solution for practical deployment in real-world settings to improve the safety and well-being of the aging population.

title: Research on the Calculation Model of the Influence Function Method for the Complete Roll System of a 20-High Rolling Mill
authors: Yang Zhao; Xuming Liu; Jinlan Bai; Junsheng Wang; Jie Sun; Guodong Wang
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: This study presents the development of a novel calculation model for the influence function method, specifically tailored for the complete roll system of a 20-high rolling mill, a critical component in strip shape control. The research incorporates a hybrid approach, leveraging both simply supported beam and cantilever beam models, to accurately determine the elastic bending influence function for the segmented support rolls characteristic of 20-high rolling mills. The proposed method achieves a notable enhancement in calculation precision, with a validated error rate of less than 3% using real-world data from Ansteel’s 20-high rolling mill. This advancement is expected to facilitate the optimization of the rolling process, thereby improving product quality and boosting production efficiency.

title: Research and Development of Intelligent Warehouse Management System Based on RFID Technology
authors: Yang Xu; Xiaochen Huang; Jingjing Zhang; Tengfei Li; Ruiyao Ou; Guangda Lu
abstract: Under the background of industry “4.0” era, warehouse management has higher requirements for efficiency and quality. Through RFID technology, fast data acquisition and identification, automatic article management, and accurate positioning and searching can be realized. This paper introduces the basic principle and application status of RFID technology, analyzes the advantages of the combination of warehouse management system and RFID technology. The overall structure design and detailed business process of warehouse management system based on RFID technology are given, aiming at providing reference for warehouse management personnel, saving costs and improving efficiency for enterprises, so as to better meet the needs of current warehouse management.

title: Kinematics and Workspace Analysis of Target Alignment Sensor for ICF
authors: Luchun Zhang; Yanan Zhang; Linyong Shen; Jinwu Qian
abstract: Inertial confinement fusion(ICF) is one of the main ways to realize controllable thermonuclear fusion energy. It has high precision requirements for the aiming and positioning of experimental targets. The target alignment sensor for ICF is used to achieve beam-target coupling, and its adjustment accuracy will directly affect the accuracy of the target experiment. First, this article introduces the function and structure of the ICF target alignment sensor(TAS). Then, the inverse kinematics solution of the 6-PTRT parallel manipulator with parallel posture adjustment mechanism is calculated, and the constraints of the inverse solution are given. Finally, the three-dimensional search method is used to search the working space of the parallel robot in a given attitude and convert it into the working space at the end of the target alignment sensor.

title: LK-ORB-SLAM3: An RGB-D Visual SLAM Algorithm Fusing Optical Flow Tracking and Feature Matching
authors: Juan Dai; Shengqiang Sun; Jingwei Liu; Zhong Su
abstract: In response to the issue of poor real-time performance caused by the large computational load of feature-based methods, this paper proposed an RGB-D visual SLAM algorithm which integrates optical flow and feature-based methods. This algorithm combined optical flow with the feature-based method, effectively improving the real-time performance of the algorithm while maintaining high precision. Firstly, keyframes are matched using feature-based methods, and camera motion is computed by minimizing the reprojection error. For non-keyframes, keypoints are extracted without computing descriptors and tracked using the optical flow pyramid, and pose estimation is achieved by minimizing the photometric error. Secondly, a dual mechanism based on time and space is employed to execute keyframes insertion which ensures tracking stability. Additionally, an adaptive threshold algorithm is proposed to enhance tracking robustness in low-light environments. Experimental results on the TUM dataset indicated that, with comparable average localization accuracy, the proposed algorithm reduces average tracking cost by 37.19%, achieving real-time frame rates of up to 45 fps on mid-to-low-performance CPUs.

title: Fixed-time Trajectory Tracking Control for Marine Surface Vessels based on Fixed-time Disturbance Observer
authors: Jingqi Zhang; Shuanghe Yu; Yan Yan; Ying Zhao
abstract: This paper proposes a novel fixed-time control scheme for trajectory tracking of marine surface vessels (MSVs). A fixed-time disturbance observer (FDO) is introduced to improve the robustness. Taking advantage of the FDO, a fixed-time adding a power integrator (FAPI) control law is employed to trajectory tracking control design. The proposed scheme can guarantee an MSV track a desired trajectory accurately, and the tracking errors converge to zero in fixed time under disturbances. Meanwhile, note that the convergence time is independent of the initial conditions. Finally, the performance and advantage of the developed fixed-time control method are manifested by comparative simulations.

title: Meta-Learning 3D Shape Segmentation Functions
authors: Yu Hao; Hao Huang; Shuaihang Yuan; Yi Fang
abstract: Previous deep learning methods for 3D shape part segmentation often require extensive labeled training data, which can limit their effectiveness on unfamiliar classes with limited data. To tackle this, we introduce a novel meta-learning strategy that regards the 3D shape segmentation function as a task. By training over a number of 3D part segmentation tasks, our method is capable to learn the prior over the respective 3D segmentation function space which leads to an optimal model that is rapidly adapting to new part segmentation tasks. To implement our meta-learning strategy, we propose two novel modules: meta part segmentation learner and part segmentation learner. During the training process, the part segmentation learner is trained to complete a specific part segmentation task in the few-shot scenario. In the meantime, the meta part segmentation learner is trained to capture the prior from multiple similar part segmentation tasks. Based on the learned information of task distribution, our meta part segmentation learner is able to dynamically update the part segmentation learner with optimal parameters which enable our part segmentation learner to rapidly adapt and have great generalization ability on new part segmentation tasks. We demonstrate that our model achieves superior part segmentation performance with the few-shot setting on the widely used dataset: ShapeNet.

title: Multi-Agent System for Closed Loop Model-Based Control of Dissolved Oxygen Concentration
authors: Jakub Pośpiech
publication_title: 2021 25th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper presents a proposition of Multi-Agent System design dedicated to control dissolved oxygen concentration inside reactor with activated sludge. Designed Multi-Agent System is able to switch between multiple available control algorithms to reach the best possible control quality. Design goal was to create encapsulated agents where modification of one agent's code would not cause the necessity to change any other agent in system. Created Multi-Agent system was tested in laboratory setup with a well-mixed bioreactor. Experimental comparison with conventional on-off controller showed improvement in control precision.

title: Stability Analysis of Milling on Parallel Machine Tools
authors: Pengjia Wang; Yushuo Zhu; Wei Wu; Baoying Peng
abstract: From the analysis of static and dynamic characteristics of parallel machine tools, it can be found that the stiffness and vibration response of machine tools in different positions are obvious, which will inevitably cause the phenomenon of instability in the milling process, so it is especially necessary to study the milling stability of parallel machine tools. First of all, this paper takes 6SPS parallel machine tool as the actual operation object, establishes the milling vibration model of its tool, and determines the key elements affecting the milling vibration model. The vibration signal of the parallel machine tool is collected through experiments, and the milling stability of the parallel machine tool is reflected by the method of expressing the vibration intensity through the root mean square of the vibration signal. The influence of milling parameters on milling stability under different positions is analyzed, and the spectral analysis method is adopted to identify the chattering phenomenon in the milling process. Finally, the weights of each milling parameter on vibration were determined by gray correlation analysis.

title: High Performance Energy Tracking Control of Direct-Drive Wave Energy Converters System
authors: Meng Joo Er; Bohua Wang; Zhongkun Li
abstract: In this paper, a high performance energy tracking control methodology for direct-drive wave energy converters (WECs) based on both backstepping and sliding mode approaches is developed. It is well known that the high frequency of chattering affects the control accuracy of traditional sliding model control (SMC). In order to alleviate chattering and the effect of external disturbances, a backstepping sliding model control (BSMC) scheme is proposed. The salient features of the proposed approach are: (1) Maximum wave energy can be generated. Moreover, velocity tracking of the permanent magnet linear generator (PMLG), which is a subsystem of the WEC, is carried out in real time. (2) Close-loop system is asymptotically stable. (3) By virtue of the robustness of the proposed BSMC, perturbations can be effectively tackled by the BSMC. Comparative studies with the state-of-the-art methods demonstrate superior performances of the proposed method in terms of wave energy tracking.

title: qcROS2: An Architecture to Secure Network Communication of ROS2-based Environment
authors: Yash Patel; Parag H. Rughani
abstract: This paper reveals the network security vulnerabilities of applications utilizing the Robot Operating System 2 (ROS2) and presents a novel solution through the integration of quantum cryptography. Our investigation disclosed that data messages within the ROS2 ecosystem are currently transmitted in plain text, rendering them susceptible to security breaches. This exposure represents a significant concern for robots operating in sensitive sectors such as military, defense, healthcare, and industry. We propose the qcROS2 architecture, a unique framework that secures the network security of ROS2 applications by using quantum cryptography for data message encryption. The architecture is founded on the BB84 protocol, instrumental in constructing secure quantum pipelines for the transmission of data messages from ROS2 nodes. Despite its robustness, the qcROS2 architecture has specific limitations, which are thoroughly examined in the paper. These limitations, coupled with the rapid development of quantum technologies, led to the direction of future research and evolution of the architecture.

title: Data mining for identifying trends in markets
authors: Adela Puscasiu; Alexandra Fanca; Dan-Ioan Gota; Honoriu Valean
abstract: Data Mining is the process of analyzing and gathering proper information from giant data warehouses by the use of different algorithms, patterns, and tools. This knowledge can be then classified using specific rules or patterns by translating raw data into useful information. Furthermore, the collective data benefits any user/organization such that they can predict trends and user behavior by processing and analyzing this information. Web Data Mining is a subdivision of Data Mining concerning publicly available information on the internet. The concept of Web Data Mining is that of extracting relevant data on different web pages and shaping it into consistent information. Moreover, the common use case of Web Data Mining is to acquire information about what users of search engines are interested in such that statistics of tendencies can be devised to serve different purposes. The paper presents a solution that allows, based on the mining of public data existing within different online car sales platforms, the identification of trends in the Romanian car market. Moreover, this application allows the user to calculate the correct price of a car, taking into account all the vehicles whose specifications correspond to those chosen by the user.

title: Research on Worldview-3 Panchromatic and Shortwave Infrared Image Fusion Method
authors: Qian Wang; Ying Bao
abstract: Worldview 3 is one of the most advanced high-resolution optical satellites. Aiming at the problems of large difference in spatial resolution between panchromatic band and short wave infrared (SWIR) band of Worldview 3 remote sensing satellite data and inconsistent spectral range, resulting in massive effect of fusion results and limited effect of spatial resolution enhancement, pannet network training is used for fusion. Firstly, the network reduces the spatial resolution of panchromatic band and realizes the preliminary integration with SWIR band; Then the preliminary fusion results are fused with the original resolution panchromatic band again. For spectral preservation, pannet adds the sampled multispectral image to the network output, which propagates the spectral information directly to the reconstructed image. The network trains the network parameters in the high pass filter domain rather than the image domain, so as to preserve the spatial structure. The results show that deep learning can achieve good results in image fusion. Pannet network structure can effectively enhance the spatial resolution of SWIR band, and also has a certain reference significance for the integration of traditional panchromatic and short wave infrared band.

title: Double-layer integrated thermal protection design based on corrugated structure
authors: Jiabin Zhao; Longbin Liu; Shaozhe Ding; Mengyang Fan
abstract: In order to study the thermal response of double layer corrugated structures under harsh aerodynamic and thermal environments, an integrated thermal protective structure with double layer corrugated structures was designed based on the same single layer integrated protective structure. The two structures were applied to the exterior structure of the rocket cabin, and thermal coupling analysis was performed. The results show that the double layer corrugated structure has no advantages over the single layer corrugated structure in terms of weight, and its mechanical properties are slightly better than that of the single layer corrugated structure. However, for the thermal protection effect, the double layer corrugated structure could effectively reduce the temperature of the lower bottom plate compared to the single layer corrugated structure, and the thermal protection effect of the double layer corrugated structure is more obvious than the single layer corrugated structure.

title: The LSTM Models with Gated Recurrent Unit Applied for Shaft Torque Estimation of Two-Mass System
authors: Mateusz Żychlewicz; Marcin Kamiński
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The paper deals with the application of neural networks designed to estimate torsional torque. The estimator is used in a control structure that utilizes a state controller for a two-mass system. Two topologies of a deep neural network are tested. Typical Deep Neural Network (DNN) is combined with a parallel branch of an LSTM or GRU layer. Neural models do not require direct identification of the system parameters. To train the network, easily attained variables such as motor speed and electromagnetic torque are used. The result shows a high precision of the estimated signal in comparison to the signal measured from the experimental bench. The networks are evaluated for different number of training epochs, the reference trajectories differ from the signals applied for training.

title: Stochastic Stability and $\mathscr{L}_{1}$-gain Control of Positive Markov Switching Systems with Impulses
authors: Meng-Jie Hu; Ju H. Park
abstract: This paper studies the stability and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{L}_{1}$</tex>-gain control of positive systems with Markov switching parameters and impulses. Markov process is applied to describe the switching parameters and structures. The positivity constraint, Markov stochastic processes and impulsive jumps are taken into account in a unified framework. By utilizing the stochastic co-positive Lyapunuov function, some new conditions on stochastic stability and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{L}_{1}$</tex>-gain characterization of positive impulsive Markov switching systems (PIMSSs) are acquired. The stochastic stability and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{L}_{1}$</tex>-gain characterization of the closed-loop systems can be ensured via the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{L}_{1}$</tex>-gain mode-dependent state-feedback controller. Moreover, an example is presented to exhibit the usefulness of the obtained results.

title: Smart Meter Outlier Detection Using PCA Dimensionality Reduction and K-Means Clustering
authors: Xiang Gong; Lisha Ma
abstract: Smart Meters (SMs) are widely used for electricity metering but face complex and varying environmental factors in practice, leading to a sharp increase in data volume. To enhance outlier detection efficiency, we propose a method based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and K-means clustering. First, the dimensionality of the multidimensional environmental variables is reduced using PCA. This process generates a two-dimensional dataset consisting of the combined environmental values and the daily timing errors of the SMs. Subsequently, the K-means clustering algorithm is applied to analyze the clustering of this dataset. Finally, the outliers of SMs are detected by calculating the distance of each data point from its respective cluster center and setting a reasonable threshold. Taking the monitoring data of meters from a typical environmental experimental base in Xinjiang, China, as an example, we apply the method proposed in this paper for outlier detection. The experimental results indicate that for high-dimensional data variables, the smart meter outlier detection method based on PCA dimensionality reduction and K-means clustering analysis has low computational complexity and high interpretability. Additionally, it significantly improves the efficiency of outlier detection.

title: Research on Tomato Maturity Detection Based on YOLOv8s and Attention Mechanism
authors: Huimei Wei; Jing Li
abstract: Tomato is the vegetable crop with the largest facility cultivation area in China. For such a large amount of vegetables, harvesting is particularly crucial. Tomato harvesting robots are of great significance for reducing production costs, lowering labor intensity and improving work efficiency. In the design and implementation of automatic tomato picking robots, the primary task is to identify whether tomatoes are ripe. Traditional image recognition methods often lack precision in detecting tomato maturity. This paper integrates advanced YOLO models into tomato maturity detection by applying computer vision technology, and proposes a model that combines YOLOv8 with an attention mechanism for tomato maturity detection. Firstly, a dataset of tomatoes at various stages of maturity, collected from tomato farms, is annotated using LabelImg and subjected to data augmentation processing. Secondly, to address the complexities of tomato cultivation environments, an attention mechanism module is incorporated into the backbone network, enabling more flexible computational allocation and feature perception, and enhancing its fruit detection capabilities in complex environments. Finally, a comparative analysis of the model training results is conducted. The experimental results show that, compared to the traditional YOLOv8, the improved YOLOv8s-attention-SE achieves enhanced recognition performance, with improvements of 14.22%, 4.41%, 6.12%, and 3.50% in precision, recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95, respectively. The improved YOLOv8s-attention-SE exhibits higher detection accuracy, providing support for tomato target detection in subsequent automatic tomato picking robots.

title: Design and Application of Communication Technology System for Mine Power Supply
authors: Wenqiang XIE
abstract: This paper deeply discusses the present situation, development and application of communication technology of mine power supply. The communication technology of mine power supply plays a vital role in modern mining production. With the improvement of automation and intelligence in coal mines, the requirements for power supply and communication technology are increasingly strict. The harsh working environment under the mine, such as high dust, high gas concentration and high noise, poses a severe challenge to the stability of power supply and the reliability of communication. Therefore, this paper studies the communication technology of mine power supply, puts forward the system design and application of mine power supply communication technology, and gives a detailed explanation from hardware design to software design and system integration and testing. The test shows that the system improves the safety, efficiency and intelligence level of mine production, which is of great significance for ensuring the safety of miners, optimizing the energy structure and promoting the sustainable development of mines.

title: MEMS Array Tactile Sensors with a Self-Calibration Structure
authors: Yuxin Zhong; Mengyi Hu; Yunhong Xing; Jiabo Zhao; Weilong You; Guoqiang Wu; Chaoran Liu; Linxi Dong
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a self-calibration technique for MEMS array tactile sensors based on the demand for high precision and high performance of tactile sensors in robotics applications. The chip is fabricated using the piezoresistive principle with high sensitivity and low nonlinearity. The area of the sensitive part is no larger than 5mm x 5mm, and the chip includes 16 groups of silicon beams for measuring x-axis stress, 16 groups of silicon beams for measuring y-axis stress, and 32 groups of silicon beams for measuring z-axis stress. To solve the problem of device measurement accuracy and the complication of machine calibration operation, this proposed design of a tactile sensing array is self-calibrated by both single-electrode drive and double-electrode drive. The finite element simulation proves that the z-axis self-calibration range is 0-0.76N and the x/y-axis self-calibration range is 0-0.097N under 20V drive. Overall, the present work can be used in the field of robot hands with high precision requirements and provides a good prospect for the development of robot haptic applications.

title: Production Allocation and Distribution for Bottled Water Manufacturing
authors: Apinya Anusorn; Wipawee Tharmmaphornphilas
abstract: This paper studies the production allocation and distribution process of a bottled water manufacturing in Thailand. The case study company has 16 products that produced by 6 manufacturing plants located in the different regions. There are different production costs in each plant and also different transportation costs from plants to the distribution centers, while the selling price of the same product is not different. Each plant can produce different types of products by sharing resources; furthermore, each production line uses the different setup time for changing products. This research proposes a mixed integer programming (MIP) model to minimize the total cost, including production cost, holding cost and transportation cost. Results from the proposed model help reduce company cost 24.77%.

title: Application of Automatic Welding System on Aluminum Alloy Corbel
authors: Dongnan Su; Cuihong Wu; Xijia Tao; Lei Wang; Yongfu Hai; Yang Cong
abstract: The body corbel is the link of traction transmission between train and bogie. It is a key component on the car body that bears both tensile and compressive loads. Its strength and stiffness have an important impact on the safety and reliability of vehicle operation. In this paper, according to the structural and technological requirements of aluminum alloy corbel products,A research plan for an automated welding system with high productivity and good welding quality was developed. Through the comparison of welding quality between manual welding and automatic welding system, the advantages of automatic welding system are summarized.

title: GA Cascaded P-PD Control on Ball and Beam System with Two-Stage Objective Function
authors: Joseph K. P. Tsoi; Nitish D. Patel; Akshya K. Swain; Xu Huang
abstract: This paper proposed a two-stage objective function with genetic algorithm (GA) based tuning on two controller schema - a PD/cascaded P-PD control on a traditional ball and beam system, serving as a prototype for a friction fruit conveyor system. The ball and beam system governed under such controllers is excited with step input, the corresponding system performance factors are captured - rise time, settling time and overshoot. A probabilistic random search on optimum controller parameters is carried with GA method, multiple cost functions - ISE, IAE, ITSE and ITAE, with are evaluated to form a performance cost matrix, which is the first stage of the objective function. The optimum parameter search stops with two conditions; one is that the maximum number of chromosome generation is reached, and the other one is that the performance cost stops improving consecutively for ten generations. The second stage of the objective function is proceeded to decide the found optimum controller parameter solution. The result is decided by taking account of the previously captured performance factors. These factors are normalized and combined with a heuristic weight set to determine a minimum decision cost. The minimum cost chromosome, with ITSE, is the optimum from global found solution space. With two-stage objective function, the GA tuned cascaded P-PD control result on the ball and beam system, meets all system requirements and is satisfactory. Such method can be later implemented on the friction fruit conveyor system for fruit position control and sorting applications.

title: Shape Uniformity Analysis of Injection Molded Cooling Fan Using Laser Camera
authors: Won Ho Kim; Hyun Sul Lee; Jin Ho Kim
abstract: This paper describes quality uniformity inspection of injection molded parts based on 3D laser camera. The shape uniformity of the automotive cooling fan is an important quality control indicator. An algorithm for automatically measuring the groove width and depth of the injection molded cooling fan is presented and its practicality was evaluated. As result of computer simulation, it was confirmed that the measured two shape parameters of cooling fan can be applied to vision inspection for the classification of defective parts or used as a reliability indicator for quality control.

title: Research on BERT-Based Audit Entity Extraction Method
authors: Rui Xiang; Weibo Li; Hua Yan
abstract: Addresses the problems faced in extracting audit-specific knowledge and manual extraction of entities when using knowledge graph methods in intelligent auditing. A BERT-based entity extraction method is proposed. Firstly, word vectors with fused features are generated by word embedding using BERT, then the text information is extracted by BILSTM, and finally the final entities are extracted using CRF with the addition of sequence annotation links and rules. The experimental results show that the method achieves an F1 value of 98.03% on the audit meeting business dataset, which has good applicability and practicality.

title: A Distributed Robust Fusion Filter Design with Randomly Occurring Parameter Uncertainty and Sensor Resolutions
authors: Zhibin Hu; Tana Guo
abstract: This paper discusses the distributed fusion (DF) filtering problem for a class of multi-sensor (MS) nonlinear systems undergo randomly occurring parameter uncertainty (ROPU) and sensor resolutions. Among them, the ROPU is considered in the state model. which can be depicted by using the norm-bounded uncertainty and Bernoulli distributed random variable. In addition, the sensor resolution that can not be ignored in the process of algorithm design is a basic parameter of the sensor. In this case, the goal of the presented DF filtering issue is that by exploiting the covariance intersection fusion rule, the DF filter is designed. Meanwhile, the local upper bound concerning on the filtering error covariance is presented by using the matrix inequalities and inductive approach, and this upper bound is minimized in terms of choosing the proper filter gain. A numerical simulation is performed to test the effectiveness of the presented fusion method.

title: Characterization of a trilateration method using Hall effect sensors for microrobot position tracking
authors: G. Géron; J. Terrien; M. U. Khan; C. Prelle; H. Al Hajjar
publication_title: 2022 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: This article presents a 2D measurement system using Hall effect sensor array for micro robotic applications. This system uses a trilateration method to track the position of a microrobot equipped with a permanent magnet. The objective of this work is to characterize the impact of different physical parameters (i.e., sensors density, number of measurements, etc.) on the localization errors. The simulation and experimental results have shown a good correlation for the measurement system. The tracking trajectory of a mobile permanent magnet in xy-plane was successfully measured with a mean error of 43.9 ± 27.8 μm and of 47.5 ± 28.0 μm along x- and y-axis, respectively.

title: An Adaptive Feedforward Optimization Mechanism for Improving Industrial Robots Trajectory Tracking Performance through Iterative Learning
authors: Chengzhi Wang; Sikai Zhao; Tianjiao Zheng; Hegao Cai; Jie Zhao; Yanhe Zhu
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive feedforward optimization method based on iterative learning control mechanism, improving trajectory tracking accuracy from trial to trail. Conventional feedforward control researches focus on the precise prediction and compensation of torques, either by means of dynamic modelling and parameter identification or by data-driven approaches. However, there exists unpredictable time-delay for torques to work. The proposed method takes the previously less-concerned velocity feedforward part of the servo control system into consideration, and a self-adaptive fine-tuning mechanism is designed and established. The error measurement and feedforward optimization processes are integrated into an iterative learning framework to obtain efficiency and precision. The effectiveness of proposed method is validated by physical experiments on an EFORT ER15 industrial robot, and an averagely 90.71% error reduction is witnessed.

title: Design and Development of Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV) with Spherical Wheels
authors: Mamoon Sarfraz Ahmad; Rameesha Yunas; Khushbakht Shah; Waleed Haider; Amir Hamza; Nasir Rashid
abstract: An unmanned ground vehicle is a mobile robot that moves around without any human, and it is generally remote operated. Its quality of being lightweight and compact makes it highly desirable to be used in missions that involve high levels of risk and danger like surveillance, inspection, reconnaissance. Typical UGVs that consist of two- or four-wheels experience limitations in the maneuverability of the robot. This research is aimed to design and develop a prototype of UGV which is omni-directional. Spherical wheels, introduced as new type of omni-wheels were designed, 3D printed, and the rest of the body was manufactured keeping in mind to keep the robot as lightweight as possible. The wheels had an active rotational component as well as a passive one. Complete calculations and analysis of the wheels were done using ANSYS. A comprehensive outlook on the mobility controls of the UGV was explored and the research concluded with suggestions of materials that could be used for the manufacturing of wheels on an industrial scale to make the UGV robust and able to withstand impacts.

title: Transfer-Robot Task Allocation Algorithm Considering Production Priority for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Problem
authors: Meng Zhou; Xinheng Wang; Zhongxing Liang; Chang Wang; Jing Wang
abstract: This paper proposes a flexible job-shop scheduling problem optimization method, which focuses on providing solutions for industrial production. First, in terms of model construction, the method further considers the cost of automated guided vehicles and the priority of workpiece production based on previous methods. Then, this method solves the model by non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm with self-cross and delete-mutation. It reduces the production time and energy by an average of 6.4% and 19.4%, which are 5.4% and 15.1% with the priority. Finally, the simulation verifies that the method effectively reduces the production cost while realizing the adjustment of the automated guided vehicle number and the workpiece production sequence.

title: POE-Based Inverse Kinematics Analysis for a Six-DOF Robotic Manipulator
authors: Yinghao Ning; Rongfang Hu; Yanwei Chen; Xuli Chen; Shiyong Ren; Bing Li
abstract: The inverse kinematics analysis is an important basis for the trajectory planning and real-time control of a manipulator. In this paper, the inverse kinematics of 6-DOF manipulator is analyzed based on the exponential product method. Firstly, the configuration of the manipulator is introduced and the correlated parameters are discussed. The mapping relationship between the posture of end-effector and the parameters of joints is established by using the exponential product formula. Then the process of achieving inverse kinematics solutions is developed based on the Paden-Kahan sub-problems. The developed process avoids establishing the local coordinate systems of each link and the complex spatial geometric analysis that the D-H method involves. Finally, the efficacy of the inverse solution is further verified by two cases.

title: Design and Analysis of Zero Backlash Structure for Gear Driven Robot Joint
authors: Yupeng Li; Jie Yang; Bing Teng; Guohua Cui; Zhijiang Chen
abstract: Aiming at the problem of ensuring the precision and stability of robotic arm joint gears under high-speed, sudden stop, and reverse meshing conditions due to the large impact force caused by the backlash of the gears. this paper proposes a method to eliminate the clearance by adding a pair of meshing gears. The article combines a large grinding robot's joint transmission device, applies the backlash elimination principle to establish a three-dimensional model of a gear pair without backlash. By using finite element simulation software, the influence of backlash on gear meshing characteristics is studied under the loading conditions of the mechanical arm input device's driving parameters and the load torque during operation. The contact pressure and stress of the gears during the meshing process are analyzed in detail. The results show that the existence of clearance has a small effect on the contact pressure but a significant effect on the stress during the meshing process.

title: Disturbance Observer-Based H∞Control for Flexible Spacecraft Systems Under Deception Attacks
authors: Boming Chen; Zipeng Wang
abstract: A disturbance observer-based $H_{\infty}$ composite control method under disturbances and deception attacks is addressed in this paper. Firstly, the control model is constructed. Secondly, a disturbance observer-based $H_{\infty}$ composite controller via linear matrix inequality (LMI) is developed based on a Lyapunov function. Finally, we present simulations to verify the validity of design method.

title: Equipment Failure Prediction Based on the Gray Markov Model
authors: Qifan Yin; Youbing Chu; Qinglian Zhang; Zhipeng Liu; Sheng Cheng; Zhongliang Jing
abstract: On the basis of the gray GM (2,1) model and Markov model, this paper predicts the failure of the electronic and electrical measurement equipment. Once the electronic and electrical measurement equipment fails, it will seriously affect the measurement and test results, which causes the quality of the products out of control. In order to reduce risk of failure, the gray model is established with the raw data of the failure prediction history which predicted the future failure of the equipment. According to the gray model, the state interval of the Markov model is divided, the state transition probability matrix is constructed, the predicted value of the model is corrected, the prediction of the equipment failure is completed. The failure of electronic and electrical measurement equipment of a company for 7 years or more is analyzed. The example results show that the average relative error of the combined prediction model is 0.063. The average relative error of the combined prediction model is 0.093 smaller than that of the single GM (2,1) model. The accuracy of the combined prediction model is comparatively higher.

title: Cross-Weather 3D Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation
authors: Yuxin Liao; Wei Li; Pengxiang Su; Jie Liu
abstract: In the future, the applications of autonomous driving and unmanned aerial vehicles will no longer be confined to clear weather conditionsbut must adapt to all-weather operations. Despite this, current research on semantic segmentation often overlooks the challenges posed by nonstandard weather conditions, and the existing 3D semantic segmentation LiDAR point cloud datasets predominantly cover only normal weather conditions, with a notable lack of coverage for adverse weather. Consequently, the development of a semantic segmentation network that can be trained under normal weather conditions and maintain high performance in adverse weather scenarios is of paramount importance. To address this, we innovatively integrated point-cloud attention mechanisms into PointDR and proposed a feature extraction module, Point Attention Block, to effectively achieve this goal. This novel approach not only enhances the network's adaptability to data under various weather conditions but also provides robust technical support for the stable operation of autonomous driving and unmanned aerial vehicles in complex environments.

title: Automatic Control of Drug Infusion and Spinal Fluid Drainage Through Data Collection and Look-Up Table Learning
authors: Kicheol Yoon; Jung-Soo Lee; Min Chan Kim; Kwang Gi Kim; Sun Jin Sym
abstract: This paper builds and tests the performance of an automatic control algorithm for injecting drugs and draining spinal fluid during hospitalization after cancer surgery.
