Our approach enhances generalization without increasing inference complexity by integrating Regularization Branches and Regression Focal Loss. On the GazeCapture dataset, we achieve angular errors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.43^{\circ}, {3.23^{\circ}}$</tex>, and 3.15° for input images of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$112 \times 112,224 \times 224$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$448 \times 448$</tex>, surpassing the full-face baseline by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.48^{\circ}, 0.26^{\circ}$</tex>, and 0.23°, respectively. Moreover, our method enables a 16 times reduction in input size while preserving the accuracy of the full face pipeline, demonstrating its effectiveness for gaze estimation on resource-constrained edge devices.

title: Parameter Identification of Respiratory Mechanics Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Jiangzhen Guo; Siru Feng; Guifeng Gao; Ruiqiang Wang; Meng Wang; Chunjing Tao
abstract: Mechanical ventilation using a ventilator is a common method for the treatment of acute and critical illnesses, and ventilator-associated lung injury is one of the main complications during mechanical ventilation, usually caused by poor matching between ventilation parameters and patients' lung function, and currently, respiratory mechanics parameters such as airway resistance and lung compliance are mostly used to characterize the lung function, therefore, the study of respiratory mechanics parameter identification has important clinical significance and application value for guaranteeing the therapeutic efficacy of mechanical ventilation. and application value. In this paper, a first-order single-chamber respiratory mechanics model of the mechanical ventilation process was established, and a respiratory mechanics parameter identification algorithm based on the least squares method and convolutional neural network was designed. The data of main airway flow, pressure and tidal volume changes under different values of mechanical parameters were simulated, and the deep learning model was trained. A mechanical ventilation simulation experimental platform was constructed using an active simulated lung and a ventilator to simulate the mechanical ventilation process, and an airflow analyzer was used to record pressure, flow, and other simulated ventilation data. The simulation data were used to experimentally validate the respiratory mechanics recognition algorithms based on the least squares method and deep learning, respectively, and the results showed that the two were close to each other in terms of airway resistance and lung compliance recognition errors.

title: Two-Stage Optimization Model for Parcel Replenishment Delivery Based on Mobile Lockers
authors: Yanbing Gao; Qin Lei; Zhibin Wu
abstract: This study addresses the replenishment delivery of packages received at the warehouse during the mobile lockers delivery process by establishing a two-stage optimization model. The first stage plans the delivery of parcels that arrived at the warehouse the previous day, while the second stage focuses on supply vehicles replenishing parcels that arrive during the delivery period. And the large neighborhood search algorithm is developed to solve the problem, and its accuracy and effectiveness are validated through numerical experiments. The results indicate that incorporating replenishment delivery significantly enhances customers' requirement for timeliness, with 400% to 600% of parcels successfully replenished on average. Additionally, replenishment contributes to substantial cost savings, reduces the travel distances of mobile locker, and decreases carbon emissions.

title: Differentiable Boustrophedon Paths That Enable Optimization Via Gradient Descent
authors: Thomas Manzini; Robin Murphy
abstract: This paper introduces a differentiable representation for the optimization of boustrophedon path plans in convex polygons, explores an additional parameter of these path plans that can be optimized, discusses the properties of this representation that can be leveraged during the optimization process and shows that the previously published attempt at optimization of these path plans was too coarse to be practically useful. Experiments were conducted to show that this differentiable representation can reproduce scores from traditional discrete representations of boustrophedon path plans with high fidelity. Finally, optimization via gradient descent was attempted but found to fail because the search space is far more non-convex than was previously considered in the literature. The wide range of applications for boustrophedon path plans means that this work has the potential to improve path planning efficiency in numerous areas of robotics, including mapping and search tasks using uncrewed aerial systems, environmental sampling tasks using uncrewed marine vehicles, and agricultural tasks using ground vehicles, among numerous others applications.

title: Memory-Efficient Hardware Implementation of Time-Ordered Recent Event (TORE) Volumes
authors: Mateusz Komorkiewicz; Piotr Wzorek; Paweł Skruch
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: There are many different approaches for Dynamic Vision Sensor events representation. Most of them rely on aggregation in a given time window, often discarding previous knowledge about the scene. Recently, a new approach was proposed to use the bio-inspired method named as Time-Ordered Recent Event (TORE) volumes. It contains “local memory” that is compressing the spiking information and can improve state-of-the-art performance in such tasks as event denoising, image reconstruction, classification etc. However, for applications in mobile robotics or automotive systems, not only high accuracy but also low latency and real-time performance are crucial. The solution to these requirements is the use of a computationally and energy-efficient specialized hardware platform. Although the method is presented as easy to implement and memory efficient, hardware acceleration of TORE is not straightforward. In this article we address the modifications to the original method that enables Time-Ordered Recent Event implementation for FPGA reconfigurable logic. The presented approach ensures real-time processing with 2.5 x memory reduction. Additionally, it allows for the use of either integrated or external memory resources, increasing the scalability and applicability of the proposed method.

title: Path Planning for Mobile Robots Based on Improved A* Algorithm
authors: Weijing Wang; Xiangrong Xu; Haining Miao; Petar B. Petrovic; Aleksandar Rodic; Zhixiong Wang
abstract: Addressing the issues of excessive redundant nodes, non-smooth paths, and low search efficiency in the path planning process of the traditional A* algorithm, this paper proposes an improved Dynamic Expansion Neighborhood A* algorithm for optimal path planning. Firstly, building upon the traditional A* algorithm, the search neighborhood is dynamically expanded by combining the 8-neighbor and 24-neighbor search algorithms, dynamically adjusting the search scope to reduce redundant nodes. Secondly, through modification of the heuristic function, introducing weights, and optimizing the estimation function to enhance path search efficiency. Finally, the obtained path is subjected to smoothing processing to eliminate corner sharp points, improving path smoothness. Simulation results demonstrate that the improved A* algorithm outperforms the traditional algorithm in terms of length, node count, and smoothness of the planned path.

title: Path Planning of Non-Particle Model Robot in Confined Space
authors: Jiang Zhan; Chengzhi Su; Mingzhen Li; Duo Zhang; Zichao Zhao
abstract: In view of the problem that when the indoor robot model size is not negligible relative to the operating environment, the planned global path is prone to collision with environmental obstacles or cannot pass through the restricted area smoothly, a confined space path planning method based on robot model and kinematic constraints is proposed. Firstly, by identifying the typical indoor environmental features, a simplified topological map is established. The type and number of confined spaces that need to be passed are preliminarily determined according to the starting and ending positions of the robot. The path is roughly planned first to reduce the path search range; secondly, a collision detection method for the continuous path of the robot endpoint is established. When searching for the path, whether the corner points of the robot are in contact with the grid occupied by the map is considered at the same time to improve the accuracy of the collision-free path search; finally, a cost function with robot kinematic constraints, posture angle, obstacle distance and path length as constraints is established, and a path and motion difficulty evaluation mechanism is proposed to obtain the optimal solution to obtain the global path.

title: Relative-Information-Based Adaptive Formation Control Method for Heterogeneous Nonlinear Uncertain Multi-Underwater-Unmanned System*
authors: Hao Wen; Zixuan Liang; Baoheng Yao; Lian Lian
abstract: This study presents a formation control method based on relative information for heterogeneous nonlinear uncertain underwater unmanned system. Furthermore, the robustness of the proposed method is strong without prior knowledge. Moreover, the convergence boundary of the tracking error system can be predefined. In addition, the results of this research can be a foundational method for other formation planning strategies.

title: Design and Experimental Verification of Underactuated Prosthetic Hand
authors: Jianan Zhang; Yadong Yan; Haotian Yao; Jiangzhen Guo; Chang Cheng; Yu Wang
abstract: Underactuated prosthetic hand has attracted growing attention due to its light weight and easy control. In this paper a single linear motor is used to drive the prosthetic hand, and the palm of the hand has three arches similar to that of human hands. Besides a series of experiments were carried out to test the power grasp and the precision grasp function of the prosthetic hand. The factors influencing the success rate of power grasp and the stability of precise grasp are analyzed, and the direction to improve its performance and usability is given.

title: Software Model for Robot Programming and Example of Implementation for Navigation System
authors: Samira Chaychi; Denis Zampunieris; Sandro Reis
abstract: In this paper, we are going to consider a current challenge in a robotic software system. We consider a problem, which is the lack of separation of concerns in robotic systems, and propose a software model to address the problem and resolve the current challenges. The core purpose of this paper is to demonstrate the advantages of using separation of concerns principles to create a well-ordered model of independent components that address separated concerns individually. Considering the problem, we developed a software model with the help of a proactive engine to address the challenges. We use robotic operating systems to help us to implement the robot simulator.

title: A Comparative Analysis of Short-Term Solar Power Forecasting Using Machine Learning Methods
authors: Nasrin Sultana; Md. Samin Safayat Islam; Md. Rashidul Islam; Md. Rafiqul Islam Sheikh; Md. Omer Faruque
abstract: Integrated power systems encounter a multitude of challenges due to the variability observed in solar energy. As a result, it is requisite to make precise predictions regarding solar power. This study conducted a comparative analysis of various models including categorical boosting (CatBoost), random forest (RF), adaptive boosting (AdaBoost), gradient boosting (GB), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and gated recurrent network (GRU). The objective of this paper is to determine the most accurate model for predicting global horizontal irradiance (GHI) in Canberra, Australia. This research used data collected at 60-minute, 30-minute, 15-minute, 10-minute, and 5-minute intervals throughout the year to ensure each model’s consistency in performance. As the number of samples increased in the dataset, each model’s performance improved significantly. This research made it quite evident that GRU outperformed all other models in producing the best results for this dataset.

title: A Retrospective Analysis Method of Missile Guidance and Control Process Based on Measured Data
authors: Min Huang; Dou-dou Huang; Jia-qi Zou; Yu-liang Sun
abstract: After the live firing training of the missile, it is necessary to analyze the working process of the missile based on the measured data, so as to accurately locate the reasons why the missile works abnormally or misses the target. Among them, the guidance and control of the missile is often one of the important reasons causing the missile to miss the target. The analysis of the guidance and control process of an air defense missile was taken as an example. Through the comprehensive analysis of the guidance and control principle of the missile and the actual telemetry data collected, a retrospective analysis method for the missile's on-board equipment was put forward. This method includes the theoretical analysis of missile guidance and control process, the reading method of missile guidance and control telemetry data, the comparison analysis between the missile's theoretical guidance and control process and the actual guidance and control process, the in-depth analysis of missile's miss reasons, which can provide the method basis for the relevant scientific researchers to accurately and quickly find the reasons for the abnormal work of the missile or miss the target.

title: Scheduling Method for Non-Emergency Medical Cases
authors: Camelia Avram; Ovidiu Stan; Claudiu Domuţa; Vlad Mureşan; Corina Răcăşan; Valentin Sita; Adina Aştilean
abstract: A patient scheduling method for non-emergency medical cases on short and medium term is proposed in this paper. It aims to establish a balanced workload of medical personnel and resources considering their availability during a future specified time periods and possible fluctuations of number of medical emergencies due to epidemic periods. Another main objective is the minimization of the waiting time of patients programed for appointments at multiple medical specialties. A stochastic Petri nets based model, using statistic registered data is used to determine the workload, then transposed in a number of daily available appointments for non-emergency cases. Finally, a genetic algorithm was applied to minimize the waiting time of patients programmed for specialized medical examinations. The method was implemented and tested proving its efficiency. The stochastic PN based model is easy to be updated taking into account different changes, leading to the workloads modifications and the obtained response time of the implemented genetic algorithm corresponds to the necessities of a real application.

title: AI-based Lower Upper Bound Assessing Framework for Predicting Mechanical Properties of Hot-rolled Seamless Steel Pipe
authors: Jingdong Li; Xiaochen Wang; Quan Yang
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: Mechanical properties are one of the most critical indicators of hot-rolled seamless steel pipe. Seamless steel pipe served in harsh working environments for a long time, putting strict requirements on product quality and mechanical properties. Due to the "data barrier" between each production process's detection and control systems, the process data is impossible to use in predicting and improving product quality. To overcome the above difficulties, this research developed an industrial big data platform to realize a single steel pipe's data interconnection in the hot rolling line. The lower upper bound assesses framework of mechanical properties was established based on quantile regression long short-term memory networks (QRLSTM) model to meet the customer's requirements for the mechanical properties interval of each finished steel pipe. The proposed framework can completely replace manual sampling and inspection at industrial sites, improve production efficiency, and reduce production costs.

title: A Kalman Filter-Based Submersible Position Prediction Model and a Multi-Target Dynamic Search and Rescue Scheme
authors: Yujie Tian; Yuxi Luo; Sitong Zhou; Kun Zhang; Yan Wang
abstract: Aiming at the deep-sea submarine search and rescue problem, this paper proposes a universally applicable submarine position prediction model and search model. The position prediction of the submersible is realized by Kalman filtering and dynamics modeling. Meanwhile, Monte Carlo method is used to construct the initialized population of the motion trajectory and optimize the search path step by step by iterative genetic algorithm. In this paper, the optimal search path is taken as the objective, the main ship SAR trajectory is simulated, and the probability of the diver is fitted as a function of time and cumulative search results. For the multiple submersible search and rescue problem, this paper proposes two possible search and rescue schemes and compares the search and rescue time. Then we propose the optimal multi-objective dynamic search and rescue method. In addition, this paper adopts the G1-entropy weight-coefficient of variation combined assignment method to evaluate different search devices and creatively adopts the CRITIC method to secondary assign the weights obtained from different evaluation methods to select the optimal search device. Finally, sensitivity and robustness analysis are also carried out in this paper.

title: Efficient Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Pursuit-Evasion Game of Unmanned Surface Vessels with a Faster Evader
authors: Wenpeng Zhang; Shaohui Li; Lanfeng Wang; Yu Liu
abstract: This paper presents a multi-agent reinforcement learning method that effectively learns the strategy for cooperative pursuit in the pursuit-evasion game of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) with a faster evader. The proposed method is based on the multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm, which allows us to learn a position-free policy for the cooperative pursuers. Furthermore, we shape the reward function according to the Apollonius circle, which alleviates the sparse reward problem during learning. Experiments show that the proposed method can successfully learn a cooperative pursuit strategy for USVs to capture the faster evader and outperforms the vanilla MADDPG.

title: Design of a Lower Limb Energy Harvester Based on Clutch Management
authors: Xin Zhou; Xiaoli Liu; Mengcheng Wang; Yang Liu
abstract: This paper presents the design of a lower limb energy harvester based on clutch management for assisted walking. The energy harvester was designed to collect the energy consumed by walking and provide it as energy input to join the energy circulation system. Through harvesting the energy of the healthy side of the lower limb, release it when the affected side works, to realize the movement assistance independently. The energy harvesting and transmission exoskeleton (EHTE) has been developed to capture and utilize the energy, the end tooth meshing structure was designed, realizing a clutch function to store and release energy during the gait cycle. The sEMG experiment was carried out to explore the influence mechanism on the main muscles, the result indicates that the function of walking has enhanced with the help of the lifting effect from the exoskeleton. The exoskeleton based on human bioenergy is verified to participate in energy management, which can provide unilateral lower limb assistance, realize energy migration, and improve the ability of autonomous activities.

title: Multi-objective Path Optimization Method for Inspection and Control Systems in Traffic Management
authors: Chunyan Yu; Yu Cheng; Yuting Yan; Xue Cui; Yajuan Guo
abstract: In the field of traffic management operations, in order to realize the effective inspection and control of the same target vehicle by multiple police resources, this paper proposes a multi-objective path optimization method for inspection and control systems in traffic management to improve the enforcement efficiency. Based on the analysis of the probability of vehicle arriving intersections, the decision tree model is used to optimize multiple inspection and control points. Further, the optimal trajectory planning of multiple police resources under the time constraints and maximize the sum of arrival probabilities at the control points is realized by Dijkstra dynamic optimization search algorithm. Finally, based on the joint simulation of Python and SUMO, the proposed method is simulated and simulation results show that the method effectively improves the probability of capturing target vehicles by traffic management authorities.

title: Matrix-Scaled Consensus on Switching Networks
authors: Xin Zhang; Lulu Pan; Haibin Shao; Dewei Li; Shaoying He; Wenbin Yu
abstract: This paper examines matrix-scaled consensus problems on switching networks where each agent holds time-varying matrix-valued scaling matrices that are either positive definite or negative definite. Matrix-scaled consensus amongst all agents can be achieved if the switching networks have frequent spanning trees and the scaling matrices remain unchanged within a time interval with a spanning tree. On time-varying networks, agents with the same time-varying scaling matrix will converge to the same point, differing from the virtual consensus value by the inverse of the scaling matrix. Both discrete-time and continuous-time cases are discussed. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the theory.

title: Airborne test switching network status automatic monitoring technology
authors: Ruizhen Song; Xiaohong Yang
abstract: The status monitoring of the airborne test switching network is the key to ensuring the reliable and effective collection of flight test data. To address the issues of protocol inconsistency, high link reliability, and real-time requirements brought about by heterogeneous networks, a state automatic monitoring technology for airborne test switching networks based on SNMP protocol and Pcap data source parsing is proposed. On the basis of analyzing the nodes of the airborne testing network, the author defined and graded the key attributes of the network nodes by studying the data structure of the MIB library of the airborne testing equipment; Monitored the status of onboard switching network nodes through low-level access to collectors and switches; By converting the INET-X data packets of the airborne switching network, real-time access was made to the source data of all nodes such as collectors and switches, and the communication situation of the switching network architecture was analyzed. Finally, automatic access and control of the collector and switch are implemented in a laboratory environment, and the status recognition function of the airborne switching network is verified. The experimental results indicate that the key status information of airborne testing equipment can be monitored in real-time.

title: Stochastic Resonance in Excitable Gene Regulatory Networks with Gaussian Colored Noise
authors: Ruonan Liu
abstract: The molecular noise plays an important role in biological systems. In this paper, we investigate the effect of the colored noise in the process of information transfer in the excitable general regulatory model. With the input signals being a random Bernoulli sequence, calculation by an information-based methodology discloses that both the noise intensity induced stochastic resonance and the correlation time induced stochastic resonance might appear. The finding illustrates noise can amplify information transfer. We also find an approximate region where the two kinds of stochastic resonances occur.

title: Modeling and Simulation Study of Hydraulic Turbine Governor Based on SIMULINK
authors: Haiming Zhang; Jun Liu; Yun Liang
abstract: The turbine governor is one of the most important devices for the automatic and intelligent control of hydropower stations. As a key part of the hydraulic turbine governor, the structure and control mode of the electro-hydraulic servo system is crucial, which has a direct impact on the quality of the AC power output and is also related to the operational safety of the power station equipment. In this paper, a hydraulic turbine electro-hydraulic governor based on PLC using PID control algorithm is developed. A hydraulic servo system is established with a high-speed switching valve as the core. The system consists of two small diameter high-speed ball valves and a large diameter electromagnetic reversing valve as the control circuit, and the two high-speed switching valves are controlled by PLC outputting two PWM pulse signals respectively. A mathematical model of the hydraulic turbine speed control system is established and simulated in the Matlab SIMULINK environment. The static characteristics test under no-load condition and the follow-on system disturbance test are carried out in the laboratory to verify the control performance of the system under this operating condition.

title: Kinematic Modelling and Simulation of Six-DOF Collaborative Robot
authors: Zhilong Luo; Shuimiao Du; Wanyu Liu
abstract: In order to ensure the development and application of self-developed 6-DOF collaborative robot (from CETC 21st Institute), this paper establishes an model using modified D-H method and conducts forward and inverse kinematic analysis. And based on Matlab, kinematics and dynamics simulation are carried out, and the feasibility of the mechanical arm structure and joints is verified through parameters such as speed, acceleration, and torque in the results.

title: Flight Path Simulation of Maneuverable Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Based on Kalman Filter
authors: Wenda Yang; Xiangxi Wen; Maolong Lv; Minggong Wu
abstract: This paper introduces the basic concept of maneuvering target tracking by improving the tracking algorithm of the UAV maneuvering target. Finally, we simulate several typical UAV maneuvering models and analyze and compare the performance of each algorithm and the influence of parameter changes on the algorithm. Experiments show that the Kalman filter algorithm can filter linear systems and nonlinear systems after improvement. The filter precision, computational complexity, and storage capacity are considered, which is easy to meet the requirements of real-time calculation and has great engineering practical value.

title: Distributed Online Optimization Based on One-Step Gradient Descent and Multi-Step Consensus
authors: Yingjie Zhou; Xinyu Wang; Tao Li
abstract: We propose a distributed online optimization al-gorithm with continuously learning ability. In this algorithm, we first perform one-step gradient descent with fixed step size to ensure the ability of tracking the optimal solutions, and then use multi-step consensus to ensure the collaboration between neighboring nodes. For strongly convex and smooth objective functions, we provide a dynamic regret analysis of the proposed algorithm and show that the dynamic regret is upper bounded by the initial values, the path variation of the optimal solution, and a linear growth term. The coefficient of the linear growth term can be made arbitrarily small by adjusting the step size of gradient descent. We also demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithm by numerical simulations.

title: Application of man-machine hybrid intelligence in ground unmanned combat
authors: Yan Xiaodong; Chu Kaixuan; Zhao Liyang; Chang Tianqing; Zhang Jie
abstract: Compared with combat in other fields, ground combat has the characteristics of complex environment, fierce confrontation and difficult coordination. The inherent shortcomings of artificial intelligence in understanding, interpretability and controllability restrict the development speed of unmanned ground combat. In order to give full play to the advantages of artificial intelligence, overcome deficiencies and promote the development of ground unmanned combat, this paper starts from the advantages of man-machine hybrid intelligence, Combined with OODA(Observatio, Orientation, Decision, Action) ring theory, this paper analyzes the application and prospect of man-machine hybrid intelligence in ground unmanned combat, and finally briefly analyzes the key technologies that should be grasped in the development of man-machine hybrid intelligence, hoping to provide inspiration and reference for the research of ground unmanned combat.

title: An Adaptive Reweighting Method Based on the Effective Area for Fault Severity Classification under Class Imbalance
authors: Zhenglei Jin; Qifa Xu; Cuixia Jiang; Shixiang Lu; Tianming Xie
abstract: In real-world scenarios, fault severity data follows an imbalance distribution, meaning that normal and low-level faults constitute a large portion of the training data. In contrast, high-level fault instances are relatively scarce. This imbalance leads to the decision hyperplane of classifiers to skew in favor of higher fault levels. Typically, reweighting methods ensure that hyperplanes fairly divide the feature space by assigning weights based on the number of instances. However, we found that the number of instances fails to represent the effective area within a fault level in the feature space. To tackle this issue, we first analyze the distribution and their correlations of different instances within each class. Second, we calculate the effective area by treating instances of the same class as identically distributed random variables. Third, we introduce a novel weighting approach, with weights inversely proportional to the effective area. This method results in more flexible weights, allowing for adaptive adjustments based on feature optimization during the training process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the comparative methods on a real-world fault severity dataset and enhances fault diagnosis performance under class imbalance.

title: A Class of Active Fault-tolerant Loop Filters for Phase-Locked Loop
authors: Ping Lin; Rui Wang
abstract: This paper investigates a class of fault-tolerant loop filters designed by improved active disturbance rejection algorithm for phase-locked loop (PLL), which can accurately estimate the the phase of three-phase power grid in consideration of phase voltage unbalance, voltage harmonics and direct current offset. Firstly, this letter proposes a class of fault-tolerant loop filters derived from part known fault information. Furthermore, simulations are finished to validate that the performance of the proposed loop filters is better than the conventional loop filters.

title: Automated Inspection and Fault Detection in Rooftop Solar PV System Using YOLO-Driven Tello Quadrotor Drone
authors: Goh Yu Xiang; Alicia Loh I-Ling; Kishore Bingi; Rosdiazli Ibrahim
publication_title: 2025 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on [::Robotics::] and Technologies for Industrial [::Automation::] (ROBOTHIA)
abstract: This study presents an AI-driven drone inspection system for rooftop solar PV panels, employing the DJI Mavic Mini drone and YOLOv11 AI model to streamline defect detection. The methodology involved capturing high-resolution images via autonomous drone missions, annotating data with RoboFlow, and training the YOLOv11 model to accurately identify defects such as cracks, discolouration, and delamination. The system achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.577 at an IoU threshold of 0.5, validating its accuracy in real-world scenarios. A significant innovation was the creation of a user-friendly application automating orthomosaic image generation, segmentation, defect detection, and reassembly of annotated maps, minimizing manual effort and errors. Results demonstrated efficient localization and classification of defects across the panels, though challenges persisted with subtle defect types. Future efforts will focus on refining detection algorithms, expanding datasets, and scaling the system for large-scale solar farms to enhance operational scalability and sustainability.

title: Form-finding of Tensegrity Structures via Monte-Carlo Force Density Random Search
authors: Zhengyin Du; Mingxiang Zheng; Min Lin; Zhifei Ji
abstract: In this paper, a novel random search algorithm on the basis of the Monte-Carlo method is proposed to solve the form-finding problem of tensegrity structures. The optimization model of tensegrity structures has been developed under the conditions that semi-definite force density matrix should satisfy the rank deficiency constraints. Given the structural topology and the types of the members of tensegrity structures, by searching the force density vectors, the node coordinates are obtained. It follows that equilibrium configurations are derived. Afterwards, numerical simulations have been conducted. The results indicate that the proposed random search algorithm can solve the form-finding problems of tensegrity structures effectively.

title: Robust GMVC algorithm undermining the employment of the Moore–Penrose inverse
authors: Paweł Majewski; Wojciech P. Hunek; Marek Krok; Tomasz Feliks; Emilia Helińska
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: In the paper, a set of new findings derived from the application of the nonunique $\sigma$-inverse into the generalized minimum variance control (GMVC) algorithm is given. In such a way, the robust instance of the discussed control strategy is proposed strictly devoted to the right-invertible LTI systems defined in the discrete-time transfer-function-originated framework. The alternative inverse-based control procedure clearly outperforms the classical one giving rise to the introduction of the generalized $\sigma$-inverse rather than the Moore-Penrose (MP) one. Two numerical examples address a huge impact of the so-called degrees of freedom at least in the minimum-energy considerations.

title: Efficient Edge Server Computing on a Scaled IoT Based Sensory Network
authors: Syed Asad Amin; Mujtaba Rafique Ghoto; Umar S. Khan; Hamid Jabbar
abstract: Edge server-based computing is one the most effective way of approaching and dealing with the problem of a wide or scaled sensory network where we have an excessive amount of data to deal with. The approach to implementing such a system used here offers not just a singular set of sensor networks but allows users to control, add and/or maintain the entire daisy chain of the sensory network on a local scale controlled by IoT cloud access and local computing potential using Raspberry Pi as the main edge computing resource. In this method, the ESP32 sensor node will do a small computation on the sensed data. It can be read in any form either analog or digital. After computation, it will send these data packets by publishing them to the locally connected edge node created by using Edge X Foundry service, management tools, and Mosquitto as the main broker. This edge node gathers the data from all the sensors and then publishes them accordingly to the cloud server based on subscriptions configured by the cloud host. The main objective of this project is to achieve a high level of control that allows users to manipulate a local system that is capable of locally administering and governing the data and release them upon requests with minimal possible power draw, having a potential of scalability as well as portability as compared to the solutions currently available and used. This method has the potential to be applied on any kind of application ranging from consumer, industrial or infrastructural levels.

title: Design and Model of a Car Based on Wireless Charging
authors: Shuai Deng; Qi Zhang; Zheming Zhuang; Chengcheng Xu; Yuntao Guan; Jiansheng Dai
abstract: the idea of charging vehicles with the surplus energy of WiFi is put forward, and a complete RF energy collection and electric vehicle charging system are designed. With the aim of reasonable layout, the system is analyzed and optimized. Additionally, appropriate scenes of life and electric vehicle models are selected for calculation and application experiments to validate the theoretical feasibility of the system. Combined with the 5G network which will be popularized in an all-round way, a prediction is made with the help of reasonable calculation, the development potential of RF energy collection in the field of electric vehicles is expounded, and a feasible scheme is provided for enhancing the endurance capability of electric vehicles.

title: Adaptive Synchronization of Stochastic Chaotic Delayed Neural Networks with Discontinuous Activations
authors: Qian Wang; Zhiyi Lu; Zi-Peng Wang; Zhijie Liu; Xiao-Wei Zhang
abstract: This article examines the adaptive exponential synchronization of stochastic chaotic neural networks (SC-NNs) that incorporate time-varying delays and discontinuous activation. At first, utilizing stochastic differential inclusion theory, we established the solution of SCNN. Then, through the application of Lyapunov stochastic stability theory and stochastic analysis techniques, the investigation of stochastic adaptive exponential synchronization issue is conducted for SCNNs with time-varying delays and discontinuous activations (DAs). Discontinuous adaptive controllers is designed to ensure the global exponential synchronization of the control system with a target system. As a special case, the obtained result is also applicable to continuous NNs. At last, numerical simulation is presented to validate the theoretical result.

title: Viscometer with Remote Electromagnetic Control
authors: Kabdushev Sherniyaz; Kadyrzhan Kaisarali; Bakirov Akhat; Sedlakova Zdenka; Suleimenov Ibragim
abstract: A new modification of a smartphone-controlled viscometer is proposed, in which a significant part of the operations performed by the electronic components of existing analogs are transferred to operations performed by software installed on the user's smartphone. The principle of operation of the viscometer is based on the Stokes method, i.e., the speed of falling of a ball in a tube filled with the test solution is measured experimentally. A distinctive feature of the design of the proposed equipment is the use of a rotary mechanism that turns the tube over. There are also two electromagnets on the turntable that hold the ball in position at the ends of the tube when it is turned over. The advantage of this design is the possibility of multiple repetitions of measurements: when the ball falls to the bottom of the tube, one of the electromagnets is turned on, fixing the position of the ball, and then the tube is turned over and the process is repeated again. The most significant advantage of the proposed design is a significant reduction in operating costs associated with the washing of the measuring unit.

title: Cooperative Target Encirclement Control of ASVS via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: Ziying Li; Xingru Qu; Linghui Zeng; Guanqun Liu
abstract: This paper proposes a cooperative encirclement control method for autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) against multi-targets via multi-agent reinforcement learning. First, a dynamic target allocation algorithm is designed based on location information of both vehicles and targets, enabling ASVs to select encirclement targets in real-time. Second, the whole encirclement process is divided into multiple stages, and a multi-stage reward function is developed based on curriculum learning to guide vehicles in completing encirclement tasks progressively. Then, the actor and critic networks incorporating long short-term memory are constructed respectively, and a multi-agent soft actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm is employed to train ASVs. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through a six-on-two encirclement simulation.

title: Performance Evaluation of an IoT Based Dual Axis Prototype Solar Tracker Over Fixed PV Installations
authors: Md. Abdullah Kawser; Rittik Das Gupta; Zahirul Islam; Kanoge Roy; Md. Asaduzzaman Sarker; Md. Hazrat Ali
abstract: A clean, quiet, reliable process with minimal environmental impact is the conversion of solar energy to electrical energy. A dual axis solar tracker prototype model is designed to track sun's rotational positions increasing total energy optimization and average output. A dual axis tracker provides more than 30.79% production than a fixed PV system. The annual and monthly energy generation is previously estimated in dual axis tracker that is 20% more than a fixed 1-axis tracker. In proposed prototype, Arduino Uno as central processing unit that controls mechanism in response to inputs from multiple sensors linked with Blynk interface. The interface allows android users to view real-time statistics including electrical parameters from solar PV. Collected data wirelessly sent to the Blynk interface and spreadsheet through an ESP 8266 module which assist to monitor the parameters having several security levels to ensure IoT safety protocol. Average power output of the prescribed model tested 18% better than a static solar PV. Database readings for the prototype were recorded throughout a certain time-period of 9:00 am to 9:45 am. To validate the project model, several tests were performed such as paired t-tests, correlation and normality tests, q-q plots of different electrical parameters.

title: Comparison of Algorithm and Kernel Accuracy in Defect Detection Using Pressure in Sleeve Soldering Equipment
authors: Kan Watanabe; Hidetake Uwano; Hiroshi Fukuoka
abstract: As the degree of device integration increases, detecting soldering defects on electronic boards becomes more complex, and the need for automatic inspection increases. In this study, we propose a method for distinguishing the quality of soldering for sleeve-soldering equipment. The object to be soldered is covered with a heated sleeve, and the solder pieces dropped in the sleeve are melted for soldering. Nitrogen gas is injected into the sleeve, and the pressure inside the sleeve changes as the solder pieces melt and flow into the through-hole. The proposed method identifies the quality of the solder using the features extracted from the pressure change. We compare the prediction accuracy when applying multiple kernels to the support vector machine (SVM) and relevance vector machine (RVM). The experimental results show that the Polynomial kernel of the SVM exhibits the best performance with an average accuracy of 100% and average False Negative of 0%.

title: Multi-camera multi-robot visual localization system
authors: Artur Morys Magiera; Marek Długosz; Paweł Skruch
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The article presents a general framework for detecting the boundaries of, stitching, adjusting perspective and finally localizing robot positions and azimuth angles for any rectangular map designated with AprilTag markers in the corners and possibly in the interior area. At the same time, the focus of the researchers was to minimize the configuration required for the algorithm to operate - here limited to just the orientation and data of markers, dimensions of the map, markers and robots. The location of cameras can be freely changed without the need to reconfigure anything or restart the program. This work has been tested on and turned out to be especially helpful for working with the DuckieTown project.

title: A Heterogeneous Approach for the Traffic Sign Segmentation and Classification
authors: Syed Tahir Hussain Rizvi; Denis Patti; Francesco Savarese; Mohsin Ali Khan
abstract: Deep learning-based image segmentation provides state-of-the-art accuracy and performance for real-time scenarios, but the segmentation of a street is a challenging and complex task. This complexity derives from the huge number of classes that are required to be taken into consideration. In some cases, a vast number of classes can also decrease the classification accuracy of a network. Moreover, the process of image segmentation cannot distinguish between two objects of the same class. In this work, a heterogeneous approach for the traffic sign segmentation and classification is presented. The proposed heterogeneous approach is comprised of an image segmentation block that identifies the different objects on a street especially traffic signs using a deep architecture named ENet (efficient neural network) and the second block distinguishes between segmented traffic signs using Support Vector Machine (SVM) model. The results obtained by the proposed approach are promising.

title: Design of Smart Trash Can for Waste Management Using MobileNet Model
authors: S. Selvi; M. Suhash; R. Lingeswaran; N. Soundar
abstract: The Smart Trash Can is an innovative waste management system designed to automatically classify and sort waste into three categories: recyclable, non-recyclable, and hazardous. This system leverages a MobileNet model for efficient image classification, running on a Raspberry Pi 4 for real-time processing. A USB camera captures images of the waste items as they are placed into the trash can. The MobileNet model, trained to recognize different types of waste, classifies each item into one of the three categories. The recyclable and non-recyclable waste is directed to separate compartments, while the hazardous waste is directed to a third compartment, specifically designed to handle materials such as batteries, e-waste, and chemicals. The system stores waste classification data, including timestamps and item types, in a MongoDB database for easy tracking and analytics. This smart trash can not only automate waste sorting but also ensure the safe disposal of hazardous materials, promoting efficient recycling and environmental safety. The use of MobileNet ensures the model runs efficiently on the Raspberry Pi 4, making the system suitable for edge device deployment. To enhance user interaction, the system can be integrated with LED indicators or a small display to provide instant feedback on waste classification. A mobile application can be developed to allow users to track their waste disposal habits and receive recommendations for better waste management.

title: Target Recognition and Tracking with a Rat Robotborne Camera System
authors: Haobo Xie; Haoze Xu; Kedi Xu; Chaonan Yu; Wei Yang; Canjun Yang
abstract: Bio-robots, a novel type of robots combing brainmachine interface and living organism, have shown great potential in search and rescue tasks after disasters due to the adaptability and sustained energy efficiency. Nevertheless, image information, the most intuitive source of data, is not effectively utilized in current research. The reason for the lack is the difficulty in the development of camera equipped electric backpack and smooth control of bio-robot to acquire stable and effective images. Regarding this problem, we propose a new method for bio-robot recognizing and tracking target with acquired image information and verify it under experiment. With the new developed camera mounted electric backpack, rat robot system could effectively acquire images. Based on Yolo, we can recognize multiple targets in the images. This research enhances the environmental sensing abilities of bio-robot and promoted it towards practical application in research and rescue tasks.

title: Biomimetic Convergence-Based High Resolution Depth Estimation
authors: Achintya Harsha; Prashanth Jonna; Nitheezkant R; Madhav Rao
abstract: Accurate depth estimation is a fundamental challenge in robotics and computer vision, crucial for applications ranging from autonomous navigation to complex object manipulation. While traditional techniques such as RGBD cameras and 3D Lidar systems provide high precision, their high costs and computational demands restrict their use in many scenarios. Conversely, monocular depth estimation (MDE) offers a more affordable solution but often struggles with depth accuracy and real-time performance. In response, this research introduces a novel convergence-based stereo vision system that leverages two independently movable cameras for dynamic depth estimation. The system facilitates depth tracking of any selected object by adapting camera orientation and extrinsic matrices to achieve millimeter-level accuracy with less than 1 % error in depth estimation over 5 meters, which is significantly better than few state-of-the-art Stereo systems that offer up to 2% error over a similar range. ArUco tag-based calibration mechanism was used to improve accuracy due to precise angle calculation. Further, the system successfully tracks and localizes multiple human body joints simultaneously using the Google Mediapipe Joint Detection model, providing a 3D approximation of the subject's position concerning the system in real-time. This approach not only offers a cost-effective and precise solution for real-time depth perception but also opens new avenues for dynamic, high-resolution environmental interaction in robotics.

title: Development of Ship Fuel Supply Simulation Training System
authors: Hongen Yang; Jianbo Sun
abstract: The main function of ship fuel supply system is to provide fuel oil of suitable pressure and viscosity for the main engine, auxiliary engine and auxiliary boiler of the ship. Practice has shown that in ship accidents, it is not uncommon to see downtime or even engine damage caused by crew's mismanagement of fuel supply system. Therefore, it has become one of the important contents of the training of the engine simulator to strengthen the training of the crew in the fuel supply system. Due to the complexity of the fuel supply system structure, the simulation model of the fuel supply system in the existing engine simulators has been simplified to different degrees, which can no longer meet the training requirements of maintenance, troubleshooting and emergency handling. In this paper, to address the problems of simplified model and insufficient training functions in the existing fuel supply system simulation model, a mathematical model of the ship's fuel supply system is established by using the modular modeling method, which includes: fuel pipe network and valve parts, fuel tank , pump and safety valve, regulator, quick-closing valve, self-cleaning filter, fuel heater, viscometer, viscosity controller, pressure controller, etc. the calculation program of the above model is written by using VC++. The simulation experiments show that the calculation results basically match the data of the navigation test, and the simulation error is less than 5%, and the simulation accuracy and real-time performance of the model can meet the requirements of the marine engine simulator training. The simulation experiments show that the Human Machine Interface (HMI) is similar to the physical interface of the actual equipment, and can realize the operations of maintenance, troubleshooting and emergency handling. The simulation model and HMI are integrated into the existing turbine simulator, replacing the original system model and HMI, and meeting the training requirements of the engine simulator.

title: Analysis of Desilting Efficiency of Spiral Dredging Auger Based on EDEM
authors: Li Ti-Jin; Wu Ming-Hui; Feng Ye-ning; Zhou Wei
abstract: The screw pitch and diameter of the blade of the helical desilting cutter, the speed of the cutter and the forward speed of the robot will directly affect the efficiency of the robot. According to the characteristics of underwater desilting, through analysis and theoretical calculation, the parameters of pitch, diameter, rotational speed and forward speed of the skein dragon blade are determined. Taking the desilting efficiency of the skein dragon as the optimization objective, using discrete element software EDEM as the simulation tool, orthogonal experiment method was used to study and analyze the influence of each parameter on the desilting efficiency. The simulation results show that the blade diameter and forward speed have the greatest influence on the desilting efficiency, and the pitch and speed also have positive effects, but not as obvious as the blade diameter and forward speed. The optimal parameter combination scheme is sthe pitch 110mm, the speed 90r/min, the forward speed 90mm/s and the blade diameter 250mm. The study provides a reference for better design of spiral silting stranding dragon and improving its silting efficiency.

title: Genetic Algorithm-Based Image Segmentation Strategy for Laser Rapid Processing of Bitmap Scanning
authors: Tian Zhang; Youmin Rong; Yu Huang
abstract: Due to its high precision and flexibility, laser marking bitmap is widely used in medical, food, packaging and building materials, etc. Traditional methods based on ablation time or multiple scanning to match the grayscale of each pixel are time consuming. A novel bitmap scanning and marking method is proposed for reducing the processing time of repeated scanning operations in order to match different gray levels. Genetic algorithm-based multi-threshold image segmentation algorithm was used to transform the target bitmap into blocks of different gray levels, and subsequently adjusts the input power by matching different scanning speeds within the blocks. This method was successfully integrated into a home-made laser oscillator control system and experimentally validated with a set of exemplary bitmaps. Compared with conventional spot scanning and filling strategy, the results show a reduction in processing time with the new algorithm of up to 68%. This finding indicates, that the new strategy is a promising approach for improvement of productivity for areal laser processing applications.

title: Laser Active Alignment Algorithm based on Spot Features and Curve Fitting
authors: Fuchun Liu; Zeyong Liu; Xiangyang Li; Dong Jiang
abstract: This paper addresses the active alignment problem in manufacturing solid-state LiDAR systems and focuses on image processing and alignment algorithms within a visual laser auto-collimation platform. By extracting features from laser spot images, a non-linear discrete optimization is applied to determine the optimal position of the laser emitter, minimizing the laser beam divergence angle. To overcome the challenge of inaccurate size extraction of Fraunhofer diffraction patterns, Gaussian filtering, adaptive thresholding, and circle fitting based on distance transformation are employed to estimate the spot size. Active alignment algorithms are implemented using improved hill climbing, genetic, and curve fitting algorithms. Experimental comparisons demonstrate that the curve fitting-based active alignment algorithm achieves better efficiency and stability, with an average adjustment count of 29.35 and a variance of 97.50.

title: Digital Instrument Reading Detection and Recognition Based on Improved YOLO11
authors: Li Teng; Zhou Zhi-Feng
abstract: Aiming at the issues of traditional digital instrument recognition methods, such as difficulties in accurately segmenting individual characters, completely recognizing valid characters, and the diversity of digital instruments, this paper improves the character detection and recognition network based on YOLO11. To reduce computational load, the depthwise separable convolution module GSConv has been introduced into the backbone network of YOLO11 to decrease the number of parameters. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can adapt to various digital instruments, achieve accurate recognition of readings and equipment operating states, and contribute to promoting the automation of operation inspection and calibration for digital instruments.

title: A Novel Approach for Multi-Criteria Workspace Optimization of Parallel Kinematic Machines
authors: Sheikh Muhammad Muneeb Hamid Rasheed; Adnan Shujah; Sadia Ayub; Aamer Baqai; Kunwar Faraz Ahmad
abstract: Parallel kinematic machines (PKM) or parallel robots have been a topic of research for the last two decades. Serial robots, due to their inherent drawbacks (Higher error amplification at the end effector, Greater weight to payload ratio, etc.), cannot be used in applications that require high accuracy across the workspace. Parallel robots overcome these drawbacks, making them a natural replacement for serial robots. However, they also have associated drawbacks (Small irregularly shaped workspace, many singularities in the workspace, etc.). For complex applications, the use of parallel robots instead of serial robots is preferred. For large-scale deployment of parallel manipulators in industries, remedial measures to overcome their drawbacks need to be developed. Most importantly, workspace optimization is required to exploit the full potential of these robots. This optimization is subject to one or more performance parameters (objectives) that often have conflicting requirements i.e. improving one objective deteriorates the performance of another, which is by far a severe challenge in this domain. An example of conflicting goals is “To purchase a car that is cheap, comfortable, safe, environment-friendly, high power and fuel-efficient”. In such cases, “best compromise between conflicting goals” is the best solution. Thus far, workspace optimization of parallel robots focuses on optimization concerning a single objective at a given time. The basic idea of this work is to propose a methodology to optimize the workspace of a PKM subject to multiple objectives simultaneously. Several optimization schemes including weighted averages, gradient descent, surrogate optimization, and genetic algorithms were studied. Pareto front optimization appears to be most suited to the application at hand.

title: Research on Robot Calibration Method Using Single PSD to Construct Local Line Constraint
authors: Ziyi Wang; Jiakai Lu; Hailiang Kang; Xinran Chen; Lan Qin; Jingcheng Liu; Min Li; Jun Liu
abstract: The accuracy of industrial robots will decrease after long-term use, and field calibration of kinematic parameters is needed to improve accuracy. This article proposes a calibration method for industrial robots using unit position sensitive device(PSD) to construct local line constraint. Using an optical system composed of a single PSD to detect the imaging position of the point light source at the end of the robot, a vertical image plane line constraint is formed by constraining the imaging points to zero. Establish a kinematic error model for robots using the D-H rule and differential principle, and propose a parameter identification method based on local line constraint using the Levenberg Marquardt(LM) algorithm. By conducting prototype experiments and comparative experiments, the feasibility of the calibration method has been confirmed. The experiment shows that this method can effectively improve the accuracy of robots and is suitable for field calibration of industrial robots.

title: Distributed Prescribed-Time Observer Design Under Homologous Sensor Attacks
authors: Ming Zhu; Gongdi Fu; Shuai Liu
abstract: This paper investigates a distributed prescribed-time observer design for a type of multi-agent systems under homologous sensor attacks. First, we design Luenberger-like observers based on attack consensus which can accurately obtain the state of the system at prescribed time. Then, the sufficiency condition and construction algorithm of the observer gain matrix design are given. Compared with the existing results of distributed state estimation under homologous sensor attacks, the observer proposed in this paper does not need to use all data in the time window and the prescribed convergence time is independent of the initial value of the system. Simulation results validate the usefulness of the designed observer.

title: Topology Unshared Graph Convolutional Networks for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
authors: Tao Li; Xiaoyang Chen; Shengfeng Huang; Fuchun Liu
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for human skeleton-based action recognition using a Topology Unshared Graph Convolutional Network (TU-GCN). This approach enhances recognition accuracy and network flexibility by dynamically modeling the spatiotemporal features in skeleton data. We introduce the concept of Topology Unshared Graph Convolution (TU-GC) and design a Multi-Scale Temporal Convolution module (MST) to enhance the extraction of temporal features. Experimental results on the NTU-RGBD and Kinetics-Skeleton datasets demonstrate that TU-GCN achieves significant performance improvements in action recognition tasks.

title: VSG Based Cooperation Control for Battery Energy Storage to Enhance Power System Frequency Stability
authors: Sitong Yan; Junjie Ma; Junfeng Man; Wei Yan; Haifeng Yu; Linxing Lv
abstract: Battery energy storage (BES) is considered as a promising solution for frequency stability in modern power systems. Aiming at solving the frequency stability problem in modern power system that caused by the uneven inertia distribution, a VSG based cooperation control strategy for multiple BES integrated power system is proposed. Based on the dynamic characteristic analysis of multiple BBES integrated power system, an inertia distribution index was put forward to evaluate the uneven level of inertia distribution and used as the control signal for the VSG control of BBES. State space model of multiple BESs integrated power systems is established to analyze the impact of control parameters on system stability through root trajectory. Simulations carried out in IEEE 39-bus system validate the effectiveness of the proposed method

title: Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Based on Improved YOLOv8 Networks for Visual Relationship Detection
authors: Yixuan Chen; Wensheng Sun
abstract: Despite its high efficiency in real-time detection, YOLOv8 faces limitations in dense scenes with many overlapping objects. Its deficiencies in multi-scale feature handling and deep feature extraction affect the recognition of subtle scene differences. This paper proposes RelYOLOv8, an enhanced visual relation detection model based on YOLOv8 network, aiming to improve object detection accuracy and visual relation reasoning in complex scenes. It replaces YOLOv8's original C2f module with the C2f_Lite module, combining standard and depthwise separable convolution to optimize computational efficiency, reduce the load, and enhance detection performance, especially for small objects. The Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module is added to better handle multi-scale features, and the Slide Loss function is integrated to strengthen the model's ability to distinguish difficult samples. Experimental results on the VRD dataset show a marked increase in detection accuracy from 0.716 to 0.861, with a 14.5% improvement in accuracy and a 14.2% reduction in missed detection rates. Moreover, RelYOLOv8 clearly outperforms Faster R-CNN and YOLOv8 in complex scenarios.

title: Design and Simulation of a Tubular Permanent Magnet Linear Generator with Doubly Salient Structure
authors: Yongnan Chen; Lei Mei
abstract: Based on the structural characteristics of switched reluctance linear motor and doubly salient permanent magnet motor, a new type cylindrical doubly salient permanent magnet linear motor is proposed. The structure, working principle and design method of the motor were expounded in detail. By using the finite element simulation software, the static characteristic parameters of the motor were obtained. Simploer and Maxwell were used to simulate the motor running with load, and the results showed that the designed motor could output the required twophase square wave voltage, which preliminarily verified that the designed motor was suitable for direct drive linear power generation such as wave power generation.

title: Nature-Inspired Bubble Magnetic Microrobots for Multimode Locomotion; Cargo delivery; Imaging; and Biosensing
authors: Zichen Xu; Qingsong Xu; Hon Ho Yu
abstract: Wirelessly actuated magnetic microrobots are promising tools in medical applications due to their tiny sizes and attractive robotic properties. However, it remains a huge challenge to integrate sufficient functionalities in a limited volume. Microscopic natural phenomenon is a great reference for current microrobot design, where the underlying intelligence and subtlety spurs related modern artificial systems. Inspired by air bubbles in nature, herein, we report a kind of novel magnetic air bubble microrobots. The air bubble-based structure enables multiple functionalities including cargo delivery, multimode locomotion, micromanipulation, medical imaging, and biosensing. The proposed microrobot is essentially Pickering bubbles composed of magnetic particles and air bubbles. Their hollow structures help produce lighter microrobots with density less than 1 g/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, enabling buoyancy-based self-propulsion. Buoyancy and magnetic forces actuation enables flexible 3D locomotion in fluidic environments. Experimental results show that the microrobots can be controlled properly for designated assignments. Furthermore, the introduction of air bubble enhances ultrasound imaging, facilitating further in vivo applications. These findings offer a significant microrobot design paradigm by exploiting natural physical intelligence at the small scale.

title: Test and Research on Energy Management Control Strategy of 4WD Plug in Hybrid Electric Vehicle
authors: Wei Wang; Fufan Qu; Wenbo Li; Chong Guo
abstract: The article researches on the energy control strategy of Energy control strategy of four-wheel drive Vehicle with Series-Parallel hybrid power system based on pattern classification. A kind of four-wheel drive hybrid system whose structure is front axle driven by series-parallel hybrid system and rear axle driven by a single motor is designed, and its components are introduced. In addition, mode switching boundary and mode switching dynamic control are designed. According to the system efficiency, the operating points of the powertrain in each mode are optimized. Finally, the economy of the system is verified in a variety of working conditions by vehicle test, and the energy-saving mechanism are verified through the analysis of working condition characteristics, working mode proportion and operating point distribution.

title: Dynamically Adjusted Genetic and Fireworks Algorithm for Deployment Optimization of Indoor Positioning Signal Sources
authors: Zhe Dong; Shuangjiang He; Huijuan Zhao; Shiqi Wen; Jianhui Zhao
abstract: The performance of indoor positioning systems is affected by spatial deployment of signal sources, thus we presented a combined method of adjusted Genetic algorithm (AGA) and Fireworks algorithm (FWA) to provide the optimal deployment solution. The threshold value of fitness function is dynamically adjusted in GA, which reduces the probability of falling into local optimum and decreases the number of trivial solutions. With fireworks of fine chromosomes, the number of explosion sparks and radius of all explosion sparks are set as explosion factors. Through explosion and random generation, supplemented individuals are produced to increase population diversity and guarantee individual quality. Population evolves to the next generation by crossover and mutation, and the optimal result from evolutions is one solution of deployment with a number of signal sources and their locations. Based on a set of experiments, the AGA&FWA algorithm has been proved with good performance of convergence ability and computing expense. AGA&FWA has the best searching ability compared with the existing optimization methods, considering only the positioning error, or together with the cost of iBeacons. Our proposed AGA&FWA approach thus can provide the optimal signal sources' deployment for indoor positioning.

title: Pilot Misoperation Control Based on L1 Adaptation and INDI Methods
authors: Jin Wan; Dan Huang; Lei Song; Lu Ding; Shan Fu
abstract: The pilot's error is one of the important factors affecting flight safety, which may cause serious consequences. This article mainly discusses the continuous operating deviation and sudden large-scale misoperation during the flight process. For the two types of error models, the controllers are designed to reduce the impact after the misoperation occurs, and simulation verification is performed. Simulation results show that the L1 adaptive controller can effectively suppress the impact of continuous operating deviation on control performance and improve flight comfort; the incremental nonlinear dynamic inverse controller can effectively reduce the impact of large misoperation and restore the original flight state.

title: Impact-Resistant External Torque Estimation for Robot Joint Using Optimized Compliant Model
authors: Mingyue Qin; Jiayu Liu; Juyi Li; Lin Cheng
abstract: External torque estimation is important for collab-orative robots. But sharp acceleration or deceleration motion could result in motor current impact, which would lead to undesired estimation error. In this paper, to eliminate the large estimation error caused by the motor current impact, we propose a compliant robot joint model based external torque estimator, and optimize the model through minimizing the weighed sum of maximum and normalized mean squared estimation error. The experimental results on a collaborative robot joint show that the proposed method can effectively estimate the external torque, and resist the error produced by the current impact.

title: Finite-Time Model Predictive Control for Constrained Continuous-Time Systems
authors: Bing Zhu; Xiaozhuoer Yuan; Xianming Ye
abstract: In this paper, a finite-time model predictive control (MPC) framework is proposed for continuous-time systems subject to constraints. The proposed finite-time MPC is ex-tended from the methodology for discrete-time systems, where the control horizon is set equal to the system dimension, and only terminal cost is penalized in the optimization. Zero-Order-Holder (ZOH) is applied to ensure that no ripple exists between two consecutive sampling intervals, such that finite-time tran-sient process and zero steady-state error can be guaranteed. Combined with feedback linearization, the proposed deadbeat MPC is applicable to nonlinear continuous-time systems.

title: An Approach of Implementing IoT Based Rooftop Rainwater Harvesting & Monitoring
authors: Md. Sabit Shahriar Haque; Wazed Al Islam; Tasmia Raunak Ferdousi; Shaira Senjuti Oyshee; Tanvir Mahabub Tamim
abstract: With the continual increment in population and severe droughts, we are facing receding water levels in urban areas. Where The water demands have only gone up, Rainwater harvesting is becoming a more important aspect of the toolset for long-term water management. Hence we have chosen an IoT-based approach to solve the issue which was missing in this particular field even though there have been some microcontroller-based approaches. With the installation of a reservoir and a few sensors, this proposal will ensure better water management for the urban areas, whether in the presence or absence of a power supply. This solves many preexisting problems like overfilling of the reservoirs as the monitoring is done at all times. As samples of our Approach-Water of all qualities, clear, opaque, and dirty were tested- and it was possible to distinguish successfully.

title: Positioning Obstacle Avoidance Control of AGV with no Local Minimum Problem via Safety LOS Guidance
authors: Yuanpei Ding; Pengfei Zhang; Ye Chen; QiYuan Chen
abstract: This paper studies the positioning and obstacle avoidance control of automated guided vehicles (AGV). First, we have established the kinematics model for AGV by equivalent the obstacle to a circle. Different from the conventional obstacle avoidance methods, we use the polar coordinate method to express the obstacle position. Second, for the presented AGV system, we propose a safety heading angle base on the Line of sight (LOS) method. Unlike the traditional LOS method, this paper introduces the tangent angle of the circle formed by AGV and obstacles as the guidance of LOS. Therefore, AGV's heading will not be toward obstacles to achieve obstacle avoidance control. Then, to ensure that AGVs reach the target point, we propose a positioning heading angle that can achieve obstacle avoidance based on the above safety guidance algorithm. Compared with the traditional artificial potential field (APF) obstacle avoidance method, the proposed method has no misalignment of the balance point. Finally, experiments are conducted using a ROS-based AGV experimental platform to demonstrate the algorithm's feasibility. The experimental results show that the algorithm can effectively solve the problem of misalignment of target points in the traditional artificial potential field algorithm.

title: Research on Servo Motor Control System Based on Adaptive Neural Network
authors: Jie Liu; Xinrui Hu; Qingfeng Wang; Shaohui Zhan; HengXu Cui; Lin Wang
abstract: In response to the issue of model uncertainty in servo motors, a control method based on an adaptive neural network with global approximation capability is proposed. Firstly, the mathematical model of the servo motor is established and simplified into a third-order numerical model containing unknown nonlinear functions. Secondly, an adaptive neural network with global approximation capability is designed to address the unknown nonlinear functions in the model. Based on this, a controller is designed, and the stability of the system is demonstrated through Lyapunov theory, ensuring the convergence of the algorithm. Finally, traditional PID control algorithm is introduced for comparison and verification. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method effectively reduces tracking errors and improves control accuracy.

title: Object Grasping Assist System with Reading Human Intention and Predicting Object Position
authors: Tomohiko Hayakawa; Tomohiro Sueishi; Yuka Hiruma; Himari Tochioka; Taku Senoo; Shouren Huang; Masatoshi Ishikawa
abstract: In recent years, research on handing an object to a person using a robot arm has been increasing. However, the dynamic characteristics of the robot arm have been an issue in improving high-speed performance. In this study, we developed a system helps a person who has intention to grasp an object at high speed by bouncing the target object when it senses the human hand's intention to grasp it, especially for objects that are too far away to be reached by human hands. High-speed cameras are used to detect a hand and the target object motion on a desk. Next, when the hand begins to move, the solenoid actuator pushes to bounce the object in the direction of the human hand. At the same time, the laser pattern is projected on the desk to predict the destination of the target motion. Experimental results using a lightweight cup as the target object showed that a laser pattern was displayed around 450 ms ago before the moving object stops, and a series of movements were faster when the system was used than when the system was not used.

title: Modeling and Study of Actuation of IPMC from the viewpoint of Small-Scale Manipulator Development
authors: Arko Biswas; Manjesh K. Singh; Bishakh Bhattacharya
publication_title: 2024 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Ionic Polymer Metal Composite (IPMC) is consid-ered as an Electro-Active Polymer (EAP) with high application potential in the field of soft and small-scale manipulator and robotics. It responds to external electric voltage by bending in a specific direction. This bending is caused due to the migration of movable ions present within the IPMC in response to the electric voltage applied. In this article, a suitable transfer function (TF) between bending moment produced in the IPMC and applied voltage (to the IPMC) has been derived using a Resistance-Capacitance-Warburg element (RCW)-based equivalent circuit of IPMC. Further, rigorous experiments have been carried out to observe the voltage-displacement characteristics for an IPMC strip by applying diverse voltage signals. Excitation voltages ranged from 1 - 5V. The forward relationship between voltage and bending moment of IPMC is expected to be very useful for developing highly dexterous soft and small-scale robots and manipulators.

title: LTE Network Planning Using AI and AR
authors: Mohammad Taha; Mohammad Abu Shukur; Mohammad Atallah; Yahya Gosheh
abstract: In this paper, an optimal base station placement for a LTE cellular network is provided. The designed system relies on a web server that communicates with pre-trained machine learning models trained using measured data and deployed on MATLAB For training, a fingerprinting database has been created for a target RSSI versus the GPS coordinates as features in an outdoor and indoor environment on a multi floor buildings in the university campus. Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) has been used as a benchmark machine learning algorithm due to its outstanding performance. However, its performance was compared with different machine learning techniques in terms of computational complexity and accuracy. Validation of the system has shown that GPR outperformed the other techniques with mean square error of 4.3% at the expense of the time required for training. Moreover, the application has been provided with an augmented reality interface that shows the placed BS on the map along with the predicted RSSI value and the GPS coordinates. The whole system is designed on unity software and made available to mobile devices.

title: Reference Convolutional Networks for 3D Deep Point Signature Learning
authors: Shuaihang Yuan; Anthony Tzes; Yi Fang
abstract: Learning geometric features directly from point clouds has proven efficient and adaptive in many tasks. Although containing comprehensive information, raw point cloud inputs only provide the geometric information of a 3D object or scene. This paper presents Ref-CNN, a convolutional network with multiple references for point signature learning using point clouds. Ref-CNN learns point signatures without increasing computation, drawing from multiple reference planes for each point cloud. Specifically, this paper defines reference planes for each point set to extract point signatures from multiple perspectives. We then formulate a method to expand the dimension of each point vector, enhancing its spatial location information in multiple reference systems. Additionally, we design a permutation invariant network structure to actively learn local and global features from the expanded data structure of the point cloud. Experiments on popular shape recognition benchmarks demonstrate Ref-CNN's performance.

title: Penetration into atherosclerotic plaque phantoms using helical robots
