authors: Hussein Hatem; Hisham Mattar; Dalia Mahdy; Amna Ramzy; Nagwan Shanan; Anke Klingner; Mohamed E. Mitwally
publication_title: 2020 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Narrowing of arteries by atherosclerotic plaques can lead to serious ischemic vascular diseases. Conventional therapy for flow restoration inside blocked arteries depends on cardiac catheterization. This work presents a less invasive approach for intravascular therapy of atherosclerosis, by the penetration into plaque phantoms using an externally actuated magnetic helical robot. We prepare artificial plaque phantoms with increasing combined concentrations of gelatin, calcium carbonate or hydroxyapatite. Results show the successful penetration of the helical robot into the low gelatin concentration phantoms. The maximum average speed of the robot reached 4.7±0.45 mm/s inside a plaque phantom having 3% gelatin and 50% calcium carbonate.

title: An IoT-Controlled Solar Panel Cleaning Robot: Design and Development Using ESP8266
authors: Raja Fazliza Raja Suleiman; Muhammad Syahmi Amir Mohd. Razuan; Taha Mohamed; Muhamad Fahezal Ismail; Norzanah Md Said
abstract: With the increasing global deployment of solar energy systems, the need for efficient and reliable maintenance solutions has become critical to sustain optimal energy output. A significant factor contributing to the degradation of solar panel performance is the accumulation of dust, dirt, and other environmental particulates, which necessitate regular cleaning. This study presents the design and development of a wireless, remotely controlled robotic system for automated solar panel cleaning, utilizing the ESP8266 microcontroller. The ESP8266 offers low power consumption and integrated Wi-Fi capabilities, enabling real-time remote control of the system, and ensuring adaptability across a wide range of solar installations. The proposed robotic system is designed to reduce manual labour requirements, lower operational maintenance costs, and potentially extend the operational lifespan of photovoltaic panels. Experimental validation confirms the robot’s ability to traverse solar panel surfaces inclined at 30 degrees and effectively remove surface contaminants. These results demonstrate the system’s potential to enhance overall panel efficiency by maintaining cleaner surfaces with minimal human intervention.

title: Numerical Analysis of the Impact of Internal Defects on the Mechanical Properties of Solid Axles under Combined Bending and Torsion
authors: Shang Wang; Chuan Liu; Yichen Sun; Hui Jiang; Jing Ma; Ao Zhang
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: The detection and characterization of internal defects in solid components is crucial for ensuring structural integrity and safety in various engineering applications. This study investigates the influence of internal annular sector-shaped defects on the mechanical behavior of circular solid shafts under combined bending-torsion loading. The research methodology involved developing finite element models with and without internal defects, representing a bending-torsion testing setup. Numerical simulations were performed to analyze the stress distribution, deformation patterns, and reaction forces under various loading conditions. The results revealed that the presence of internal defects significantly alters the stress distribution, leading to localized stress concentrations near the defect location. Furthermore, the maximum Mises stress values were consistently higher in the model with internal defects compared to the defect-free model. The constraint reaction force analysis demonstrated a reduction in mechanical resistance due to internal defects, resulting in lower reaction force values. The main conclusion drawn from this study is that the presence of internal defects has a profound impact on the mechanical behavior of solid shafts under combined bending-torsion loading. The observed variations in stress distribution, maximum Mises stress, and reaction forces offer potential avenues for detecting internal defects based on bending-torsion deformation. These findings contribute to the development of reliable non-destructive testing techniques for ensuring the structural integrity of critical components.

title: Improving Microgrid Efficiency with AI-Based Control of Boost DC/DC Converters
authors: Vlad Muresan; Cristina-Maria Stancioi; Mihail Abrudean; Radu Miron
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive solution for controlling and modeling power delivery in a microgrid powered by photovoltaic panels, with a focus on robust operation both in normal conditions and under faults. The system uses advanced mathematical models to describe key system components, which serve as reference points for a fault detection mechanism. An adaptive control strategy regulates power output and rejects disturbances, ensuring fault tolerance. The DC/DC converter model is based on a transfer function structure with variable coefficients, and a feedforward neural network is employed to dynamically adjust these coefficients based on the duty cycle. The control framework also incorporates a compensator to prevent instability when converter parameters deviate from nominal values, enhancing the system's fault resilience. The integrated control algorithms for the boost DC/DC converter and single-phase inverter are designed for real-time implementation on 32-bit ARM processors, providing an efficient, fault-tolerant solution for microgrid management.

title: Reachability Optimization for an Autonomous Soil Sampling Platform with the Central Opening*
authors: Josip Spudić; Ana Šelek; Ivan Hrabar
abstract: This paper presents a method for optimizing the dimensions of the central opening in the mobile platform, ensuring adequate surface reachability for a 6-DOF robotic arm. The reachability map is extended with the concept of 8 Configuration Reachability to account for the redundancy of the arm, where up to eight possible joint configurations exist for a given pose of the end effector. Additionally, Weighted Reachability is proposed to quantify reachability throughout the workspace, taking into account the varying importance of surfaces, such as the ground and walls. By varying the dimensions of the central opening; width, length, height, and offset, dimension of the platform is determined for optimal reachability. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which achieves high reachability for selected configurations. The findings provide a practical basis for the design of mobile platforms with a robotic arm, particularly those with a central opening for operational tasks.

title: Non-Singular Terminal Sliding Mode Control with Coupling Compensation for High-Speed Maglev Suspension System
authors: Peichen Han; Junqi Xu; Lijun Rong; Xiang Liu; Fei Ni; Yougang Sun
abstract: The interference of the high-speed maglev train is significant at higher operation speeds, bringing challenges to sus-pension control. In this paper, the diverse sources of interference on the electromagnet of the high-speed maglev train are analyzed, and a finite time disturbance observer is constructed for matched and unmatched disturbances. Combined with the observer, a non-singular terminal sliding mode control algorithm is designed to overcome the disturbances. Furthermore, considering the multi-point coupling effect of the suspension electromagnet, a cross-coupling control compensation algorithm was designed to compensate the controller. Compared with traditional terminal sliding mode controllers, the composite method proposed can reduce the fluctuation amplitude of the suspension gap under disturbance conditions by more than 60%, providing a new idea for further improving the suspension reliability and stability of maglev trains under high-speed operating conditions.

title: Equivalence Among PID and Several Robust Control Methods with Application to Motor Control
authors: Zhixiang Chen; Yuguo Hou; Kunyang Huang; Zhenglong Zhao; Ruiqiao Yao; You Cao
abstract: This paper explores the equivalence among proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control and several robust control methods, including an adaptive backstepping control, an improved backstepping control, “P+PI” control and a quasi-sliding mode control, in time domain. It can be concluded that all the discussed robust control methods can be reconstructed in PID form. Experimental results of a servo motor control system verify the equivalence among PID and the discussed robust control methods.

title: An Autonomous Navigation Approach based on Bird’s-Eye View Semantic Maps
authors: Juan Galvis; Dimitrios Pediaditis; Khawla Saif Almazrouei; Nikos Aspragathos
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of the use of mobile robots, providing them with autonomous navigation capabilities for different environments has become a very active research topic. In most cases, navigation systems are built around sensors like LiDAR which are expensive, not only due to the sensor cost but also to the computational power required for the processing of Point-Clouds. To provide an alternative to such systems, we propose a navigation approach that only requires a front-facing RGB Camera. In this system, every image is processed online using a semantic segmentation model to build a Bird’s-Eye view semantic map, from which a local path and the corresponding motion commands can be calculated. Our method is evaluated first in simulation and later on, in a real mobile robot. The results show that our system enables the robot’s successful navigation and collision avoidance through simulated and real indoor and outdoor environments.

title: Finite Element Simulation of Hot Rolled Steel Strip Flying Shear Process at High Speed
authors: Li Ke; Chen Min; Gao Aimin
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: A finite element model was established to simulate the flying shear process of 40Mn strip steel, and the influence of key parameters of the flying shear on the shear was analyzed. Firstly, the kinematic analysis of the flying shear mechanism was carried out to obtain the motion path of the cutting edge in the shearing process. Then, a plane strain finite element model was established on DEFORM software to simulate the flying shear process of 40Mn strip steel. Johnson-Cook plastic constitutive model and damage model considering strain, strain rate hardening and temperature softening were adopted. Through the calculation and analysis of the finite element model, the influence law of the fillet radius of the cutting edge and the relative clearance of the cutting edge on the shearing power and the quality of the cutting section is obtained. Under the given strip size and flying shear conditions, the optimal cutting edge clearance and fillet radius are determined.

title: Advancing Autonomous Vehicle Perception: YOLO Algorithms and Custom Dataset Integration for the UAE Environment
authors: Faris Syed; Mohamed Al Musleh; Nidhal Abdulaziz
abstract: This paper presents a study on the optimization of You Only Look Once (YOLO) object detection algorithms for enhancing autonomous vehicle (AV) perception systems, with a focus on the United Arab Emirates (UAE) driving conditions. Through evaluation of YOLO variants in simulated environments, YOLOv5m proved optimal by balanced detection accuracy and processing efficiency. The research involved creating a UAE-specific dataset to address regional scenarios, integrating real-time data processing in a virtual environment, and assessing algorithm performance across different conditions. Findings demonstrate the importance of varied environmental condition testing for object detection Algorithms, Furthermore the successful application of the custom UAE dataset underscores the necessity for regionally adapted training data in achieving high precision in object detection that is essential for navigation requirements of an AV.

title: Sort Planning of Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hands Using Deep Learning
authors: Xiangyu Dong; Haoyuan He; Peng Du; Xinsheng Tang; Teng Li; Ruijing Yang; Jie Huang; Weiwei Shang
abstract: In real application scenarios, objects are usually in complex unstructured environments, so object sorting operations based on machine vision are essential. To solve it, we propose a sort planning method for multi-fingered dexterous hand to handle multiple target objects by using the two-stage object detection network and the sort order decision algorithm. Firstly, the two-stage object detection network based on RGB images is designed, in which the first-stage network is used to search candidate regions where objects may appear while the second-stage network evaluates each region to detect the positions of all target objects in the RGB image. Secondly, the global depth information of the objects and the relative positions between them are obtained from the depth image. Thirdly, the sorting order of the target objects is determined according to the human sorting behaviors, and the grasp planning method is applied to the segmented depth image which contains the chosen target object. Finally, the above steps are repeated until all sorting operations for all visible target objects are finished, and the performance of the sort planning method is verified on the actual robot platform with multi-fingered dexterous hand and the success rate of sorting is up to 82%.

title: Experimental Study on Semi-active Vibration Absorption Method for Flexible Antenna Structure
authors: Jiale Peng; Peng Liu; Yushu Bian; Yechi Zhang; Qiang Cong; Yizhu Guo
abstract: A semi-active vibration reduction method based on internal resonance is researched to solve nonlinear vibration problems of large flexible antennas. By adjusting the parameters of the vibration absorber, the fourth-order vibration mode of the large-space antenna and the vibration mode of the vibration absorber form 2:1 internal resonance, and the energy channel between them is established. The existence of energy interaction and effectiveness of vibration absorber are verified by experiments.

title: A Biogeography-Based Optimization Algorithm with Heuristics for Distributed Multiproduct Scheduling Problem
authors: Yaya Zhang; Xingsheng Gu
abstract: Multiproduct batch plant scheduling problems arise in various industries, such as fine chemical, pharmaceutical, rubber, food, and daily cosmetics industries. To remain competitive in such a global economy, the modern production mode has shifted from a single factory to a multi-factory production network. Thus, distributed batch scheduling has attracted wide attention. To address the distributed batch scheduling with multiproduct and multi-factory production networks, we consider minimizing the global makespan over all factories and propose a biogeography-based optimization algorithm combined with heuristics to find the optimal production plan and enhance productivity. First, the time key encoding scheme and the First Come First Served rule have been adopted to improve the search efficiency. Then, the power of this heuristic rule has been enhanced by changing the production sequence based on the sequence of other stages instead of only the first stage. Besides, a high-efficient heuristic has been proposed to balance the load of different factories. The proposed algorithm is compared with three algorithms, and simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm on distributed multiproduct batch plant scheduling problems.

title: Flexible Omnidirectional Driving Gear Mechanism with Adaptation over Arbitrary Curvatures
authors: Moses Gladson Selvamuthu; Kazuki Abe; Kenjiro Tadakuma; Riichiro Tadakuma
abstract: A support structure for flexible displays such as OLED or flexible LEDs was developed using the flexible omnidirectional driving gear mechanism. It is a gear mechanism having two degrees of freedom on one surface. This flexible display mechanism is expected to be placed inside a car dashboard as a human interface and for workspace optimization. In this study, we propose a novel flexible omnidirectional driving gear for supporting flexible displays discussing its design, motion range, repeatability, positional accuracy, and adaptability to any guide surface through magnetic coupling. The experiments showed satisfactory results for positional accuracy and repeatability with adaptability over a wide range of curvatures.

title: A UKF-based Loose Coupling Framework for Odometry Fusion
authors: Yangmin Xie; Jinghan Zhang; Wei Qian; Yang Feng; Hang Shi; Yusheng Yang
abstract: Odometry fusion is crucial for mobile robots with various types of sensors. However, traditional odometry fusion approaches often suffer from high complexity and limited robustness, particularly in complex environments with few features. To address these challenges, a loose coupling framework based on the UKF is introduced for odometry fusion. By integrating multiple odometry sources using the UKF, the framework enhances both accuracy and robustness in localization and mapping. The experimental results in indoor and outdoor scenes verified the effectiveness of the proposed method, which can not only improve the accuracy of localization and mapping but also can handle the situation if partial sensors are not functioning.

title: Enhancing Point Cloud Scene Understanding with a Data-Aware PointNet
authors: Kai Xiao; Jialin Gui; Jian Long; Xiang Hu; Yuanxi Peng
abstract: The precision of point cloud scene classification is crucial for applications related to robotic vision. Despite the introduction of numerous sophisticated network models, advancements in model complexity have not consistently translated into proportional improvements in outcomes. Our investigation revisits foundational methodologies, revealing that conventional benchmark techniques often utilize non-data-centric sampling strategies, such as random sampling or farthest point sampling, to incrementally downsample input point cloud. These methods overlook the varying significance of individual points within the classification task. To this end, we design a data-aware PointNet (DAPNet) for enhanced point cloud classification. The DAPNet framework incorporates a novel data-aware sampling algorithm tailored to the 3D spatial characteristics of input point cloud, selectively retaining critical points that encapsulate essential spatial features during downsampling. Coupled with this algorithm, a data-aware PointNet is built as the backbone network, augmenting feature extraction capabilities. The efficacy of the proposed DAPNet is substantiated through evaluations on publicly available datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in performance metrics across classification task. Remarkably, the DAPNet achieves advanced performance on the ModelNet40 and ScanObjectNN dataset.

title: Dynamic Task Sequence Allocation Based on Natural Language Instruction
authors: Yongchang Li; Jianhang Feng; Zhigang Tao; Lumeng Ma; Yanzhi Dong; Xiaohu Yuan
abstract: In recent years, with the development of technology, robots have become more prominent in the public eye. Service robots are now being used in some smart hotels to decrease manual transportation costs. However, these service robots operate according to set instructions, and humans usually apply fixed operating instructions to control the robots. Whether in daily life or at work, humans are more likely to use natural language to communicate and give task instructions. Moreover, in the field of multi-robotics, most of the existing researches on multi-task assignment have been conducted in simulation environments on a list of pre-set tasks, and seldom update the task sequences in real time in conjunction with the real environmental information and time. In this paper, we propose a method for assigning dynamic navigation task sequences based on natural language instruction and verify its effectiveness in a real scenario.

title: Path Planning of Unmanned Underwater Vehicles in Ocean Current Environment based on Safe Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
authors: Yu Wang; Yongli Hu; Zhenzhong Chu
abstract: This article aims to explore path planning for unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) using safety reinforcement learning (SRL) algorithms. Specifically, this article implements an SRL algorithm model that can adapt to ocean currents by setting reasonable state space, action space, reward function, and introducing safety constraints based on a real UUV. UUV path planning experiments were conducted in the Gazebo simulation environment using the ROS communication system. Additionally, a wireless communication module was designed for the real UUV. This article provides valuable experience for the research and practical application of UUV path planning based on SRL algorithms.

title: Design and Development Bionic Flexible Gripper with Embedded Self-Powered Triboelectric Tactile Sensor
authors: Daniyar Dauletiya; Azat Balapan; Alibek Kakimov; Azamat Yeshmukhametov; Gulnur Kalimuldina
abstract: The robotic gripper, a pivotal device in robotics for accomplishing grasping tasks, has revolutionized industrial processes, elevating efficiency and productivity by ensuring secure and precise object handling. However, evolving technological demands have spurred the need for improved grasping capabilities, including precise grasping, force control, shape identification, and adaptability. To meet these challenges, recent developments in composite materials and tactile sensors have led to significant advancements in gripper technology over the past decades. Notably, the integration of an all-printed soft Triboelectric Nanogenerator (TENG) as a tactile sensor has emerged as a cutting-edge solution, offering unique capabilities to perceive physical object shapes and patterns through voltage modulation. In this research, we propose a new approach for the application of a self-powered TENG sensor embedded with a flexible gripper. Moreover, the classification of objects' shapes was conducted by using machine learning.

title: Research on Test Parameters of Ultra High Resolution CMOS Image Sensor Microsystems
authors: Yu Tian; Pei Liu; Erming Rui; Qiang Jiao; Yuanyuan Xiong; Yanlei Dong; Yue Ma; Junlin Li
abstract: With the development of the information society and the rapid rise of new generation information technology industries represented by smart earth, the internet of things, and cloud computing, the data transmission and processing capabilities has faced unprecedented challenges for the existing visual information perception methods, which limits the improvement of imaging system characteristics. The ultra high resolution CMOS image sensor microsystem is a groundbreaking product which leads the future development of the optoelectronic imaging field. This manuscript mainly focuses on the research ideas of Test Parameters for ultra high resolution CMOS image sensor microsystem. Moreover, the optoelectronic/spectral parameter testing and image quality parameter testing are similar with the traditional CMOS image sensor, and the new Test Parameters derived mainly include geometric parameter testing and complex scene multi object recognition testing according to the characteristics of the ultra high resolution CMOS image sensing microsystem. In addition, this manuscript proposes aspects that need to be improved based on new products in terms of testing methods for optoelectronic/spectral parameters and image quality parameters. A preliminary set of Test Parameters for new products has been established. Adopting targeted testing methods is an important part of subsequent performance evaluation of new products.

title: Endoscopic Lesion Detection Based on Improved SSD
authors: Tao Wu; Xiaohui Liu; Lisheng Wei; Ziqiang Shao; Xiaoxue Huang; Shengbo Zhu
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low accuracy and speed of lesion detection by lightweight model, an endoscopic lesion detection algorithm based on improved SSD is proposed. Firstly, the VGG backbone network is replaced with a lighter MobileNetV2 network to reduce the consumption of computing resources. Secondly, the CBAM attention mechanism is proposed to refine the shallow input features, so as to comprehensively capture the key information of the features. Finally, the improved SmoothL1 loss function is used to balance the accuracy and robustness of the model. Experiments show that the average accuracy of the improved model is improved, the parameter amount is 1/6 of the original model, the calculation amount GFLOPS is reduced by 59 G, and the frame rate per second FPS is increased by 96 frames/s. Compared to other algorithms, there is an improvement in average accuracy, the model is more lightweight, and it consumes fewer computing resources, indicating the effectiveness of the improved algorithm in the detection of endoscopic lesions.

title: Multi-Branch Attention-Enhanced Contrastive Framework Based Domain Adaptation Method for Unsupervised Rolling Bearings Fault Diagnosis
authors: Haibo Liu; Junjie Ma; Junfeng Man; Zhiguang Song
abstract: The complexity of work conditions leads to significant challenges for rolling bearing fault diagnosis. Major challenges include feature distribution discrepancies across work conditions, and lack of labeled data in modeling process. Current transfer learning methods face limitations in addressing non-stationary signals. In particular, they struggle to balance robustness and adaptability in domain alignment under unsupervised situations. This paper proposes a novel unsupervised domain adaptation method that combines Multi-Branch Attention-Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network (MBAECNN), Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations (SimCLR), and Conditional Domain Adversarial Network (CDAN) for unsupervised rolling bearings fault diagnosis. MBAECNN facilitates multi-scale feature extraction and fusion, while SimCLR improves feature learning for unlabeled target domain data. Additionally, CDAN effectively minimizes inter-domain distribution discrepancies by jointly aligning marginal and conditional distributions, thus enhancing cross-domain fault diagnosis performance. Experimental results through six cross-condition tasks using the Jiangnan University bearing dataset demonstrate the validation of the performance of the proposed method.

title: K-Medians Clustering-Based Secure State Estimation
authors: Zhiyuan Wang; Cui Zhu
abstract: This study proposes a secure state estimation algorithm for distributed cyber-physical systems (CPSs) under the threat of false data injection attacks (FDIA). The study uses the robustness of medians, employing a clustering algorithm of K-medians to derive detection thresholds in an adaptive manner, thus reducing the incidence of missed detections. Subsequently, an attack compensator is designed to process anomalous data using weighted adjustments, with the objective of minimizing information loss and enhancing resilience. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology, which demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy and precision in state estimation, outperforming conventional approaches in reducing false alarms and missed detections.

title: Beidou Positioning Antenna PCB Board and Software Design
authors: Chengyong Li; Gang Dong
abstract: Short-range wireless transmission has the advantages of strong anti-interference performance, high reliability, good security, limited by geographical conditions, flexible installation, etc., and has a wide application prospect in many fields. Low power consumption and miniaturization are the actual needs of users for current wireless communication products, especially portable products. Short-range wireless communication has gradually attracted wide attention. Common short-range wireless communication has 802.11-based wireless LAN WLAN, blueTooth, HomeRF and HiperLAN (high performance wireless LAN) in Europe, but its hardware design, interface mode, communication protocol and software stack are complex, requiring a special development system, high development cost and long cycle. The end product costs are also high. Therefore, these technologies are not widely used in embedded systems. Common RF products do not have these problems, and short-range wireless data transmission technology is mature, simple function, easy to carry, so that it has been widely used in embedded short-range wireless products.

title: An Electrical Information Based Positioning and Homing Strategy for Intelligence Mobile Robot
authors: Zhe Liu; Yingshuang Cao; Yueqiu Chen
abstract: Compared to traditional wired charging methods, wireless charging is freer and more flexible. When the robot runs to the charging area, it can be charged automatically. However, If the robot is too far away from the charging station, its charging efficiency will decrease greatly, which doesn't meet with the development concept of energy conservation. In order to guarantee the charging safety and efficiency of the mobile robot, a homing strategy based on the electrical information in the robot is proposed. Based on the electrical information variables in the mobile robot, such as output voltage and current, the relative position between the operating robot and the charging station can be judged. Furthermore, the operating robot will move to a more suitable position automatically for next energy supplement process. The detailed theoretical analysis and implementation process are given to verify the feasibility of proposed strategy.

title: A Scenario Encoding Model for Long-Term Lane-Change Prediction Using Self-Organizing Map
authors: Nanbin Zhao; Bohui Wang; Ruikang Luo; Yun Lu; Jialu Zhang; Rong Su
abstract: There is no doubt that in the near future, machines will share roads with human drivers [1] [2]. Therefore, the prediction of human drivers' lane changing behavior is imperative. Lane-change prediction is one of the most important ones. Both human drivers and autonomous vehicles should make sure that no other vehicle switches lanes or moves into the same region of the target lane as the ego vehicle. The existing short-term prediction algorithms can only provide a prediction horizon of 3 ~ 5s, leaving only a limited reaction time for drivers and autonomous path planning modules. Additionally, the majority of previous research analysed less on investigate lane segmentation or merging, simply the inference of lane shift in an expressway context. Most of earlier research only focused on the inference of lane-change in an expressway context, as opposed to the more typical urban environment. There are relatively few of these studies that can handle multi-scenario and scenario switching. In this paper, a Scenario Encoding Model (SEM) is proposed to help solve the problem of long-term lane-change prediction and the scenario switching problem in the existing short-term lane-change prediction. Even in the absence of road history data, the SEM can model the road scenario and encode the real-time road scene by using Self-Organizing Map (SOM) In the mean time, the established initial model has the ability to be further evolved into a historical bias model in the background of a large amount of road historical data. The evaluation test of this SEM has been done through the NGSIM dataset.

title: Multi-Classes Object Detection and Manipulation for Industrial Robots Using Deep Learning
authors: Anawin Pechbooranin; Thanatsorn Chaisirithungnaklang; Suradet Tantrairatn; Kontorn Chamniprasart
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly enhanced the accuracy and efficiency of various industrial sectors by automating tasks and reducing manual labor. Notably, the integration of AI, particularly deep learning, with computer vision has enabled the detection of objects within images. This capability has proven valuable in robotics applications, as demonstrated in this study. The present study utilizes the YOLOv8s model to achieve multi-class object detection and localization from webcam footage. The identified objects are then manipulated by the SCARA robot DobotM1, which picks them up and sorts them into designated piles based on their classification. The model achieved an impressive mean average precision of 99.5 percents on the validation set data. Furthermore, its integration with the robot arm facilitated accurate and reliable object handling.

title: Advanced Waste Detection: Mobilenetv2 SSD and Yolov8 for Waste Bank Mobile Application
authors: Sofviyah Aprillani; Faishal Yusuf Baqir; Ikhwan Nashir Zaini; Sofia Naning Hertiana; Sussi Sussi
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Control & [::Automation::]; Electronics; [::Robotics::]; Internet of Things; and Artificial Intelligence (CERIA)
abstract: The research addressed the challenge of waste management in waste banks using deep learning-based object detection. The study focused on comparing two models, MobileNetV2 SSD and YOLOv8, for identifying and classifying inorganic waste. The research process involved preparing a dataset of waste images, which were then used to train and evaluate models. The research methodology encompassed a systematic approach, commencing with preparation of a dataset comprising waste images. These images were then labeling and subsequently partitioned into distinct training, validation, and test sets, ensuring a robust foundation for model training and evaluation. The training and evaluation phase leveraged key performance metrics, namely mAP (mean Average Precision) and AR (Average Recall), to gauge the efficacy of both models. The results unequivocally demonstrated the consistent superiority of the YOLOv8 model over MobileNetV2 SSD across these evaluation metrics. Notably, YOLOv8 achieved an impressive mAP of 0.834 and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A R$</tex> of 0.791, underscoring its exceptional accuracy and stability in waste detection. The research conclusion is that YOLOv8 stands as the preferred model for seamless integration into waste bank mobile applications, owing to its enhanced detection capabilities. These advancements significantly bolster recycling efforts and promote heightened awareness and participation in waste management practices.

title: Prescribed-Time Formation Tracking Control with Collision Avoidance Under Limited Information
authors: Shun Yang; Qiang Xiao; Zhigang Zeng
abstract: The prescribed-time formation tracking control with collision avoidance under limited information is studied in this paper. A new null-space-based of the prescribed-time behavioral control strategy containing time-varying gains is proposed for followers to form and maintain a formation within the prescribed time by tracking the leader and guaranteeing no collision among them. Before this, the newly designed behavioral velocities, as an important part of the algorithm, complete the tasks within the prescribed time in a distributed manner respectively. According to a Lyapunov candidate function, we prove that the formation tracking errors with behavioral conflicts can convergence within a prescribed-time. Finally, the effectiveness of the strategy is validated by simulation examples with four agents.

title: The Data Visualization of Large Scale AIS Trajectories Data on Hadoop
authors: Bao Lei
abstract: With the establishment of Automatic Identification System(AIS) networks, maritime vessel trajectories are becoming increasingly available. The visualization of AIS trajectories data is an effective way on large scale spatiotemporal data analysis and is critical for real time applications ranging from military surveillance to transportation management. In this paper we uses the real AIS data as experimental data and uses Hadoop as data processing and storage, presents a dynamic visualization of global marine AIS data and local sea area situation. A multi-charts visualization model is presented, where the characteristics of complex ships in port area can be analyzed.

title: Fixed-Time Bearing-Only Formation Tracking and Maneuvering Control for Multi-UAV Systems
authors: Yihao Fu; Ye Zhang; Jingyu Wang
abstract: A fixed-time b earing-only s liding m ode control framework is proposed in this article to achieve formation tracking and maneuvering of multiple unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV) systems, in an obstacle environment. Existing approaches have provided limited solutions to this practical yet challenging problem, typically requiring additional measurements such as relative position information. This paper makes two main contributions: First, we propose a novel bearing-only formation tracking controller that enables multi-UAVs to achieve bearing-constrained formations within finite time. Second, we develop a bearing-angle-based formation deformation strategy, allowing UAV swarms to autonomously reconfigure and split when encountering obstacles. The effectiveness of the proposed control framework is confirmed through simulation results.

title: Homing Control of Parafoil System with Optimal Trajectory Planning
authors: Shangmin Yu; Hao Sun; Junqing Sun
abstract: Parafoil delivery system is widely used in the area of the cargo airdrop and aircraft recovery. Their main function is to deliver the payload to the target position. There are many methods used in homing control of parafoil with trajectory planning. Traditional planning trajectories of parafoil are generally composed of standard circles and straight lines. But it is difficult to plan and track the flexible trajectory during real-time motion as well as consider obstacle avoidance and the fluctuation of control input. In this paper, we use the Gaussian pseudospectral method to plan three degree of freedom model trajectory. Then, we make an eight degree of freedom dynamic model trajectory tracking based on active disturbance rejection controller. Simulation experiments are conducted to evaluate the model and the control method. Results show that the model trajectory can realize optimal trajectory planning and easy to track.

title: A Multi-Agent Path Planning Method based on Improved MADDPG
authors: Cong Ye; Xiaoli Li
abstract: To effectively address the multi-agent path planning problem in complicated environments, this study proposes an improved Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) method for multi-agent path planning, with multi-unmanned aerial vehicles (MUAVs) as the research subject. The proposed method incorporates a directional reward function that considers the dynamic changes in the UAVs' actions over two consecutive steps. This ensures stable flight direction and smooth trajectory adjustments based on the surrounding environment. Additionally, the method includes reward functions related to coverage range and movement cost, aiming to overcome challenges such as path instability and long planning times in multi-agent path planning. Experimental results show that compared to traditional methods, the proposed approach significantly reduces the time required for MUAVs to complete tasks, increases path smoothness by nearly 96%, and improves the cumulative reward value.

title: Research on Singular Avoidance Algorithm for Redundant Manipulators Based on Screw Theory
authors: Hongwu Wang; Yifan Liu; Lei Lv; Yunji Li; Xiangkun Zhang
abstract: The singularity avoidance problem of redundant DOF manipulator is studied in this paper. Firstly, a kinematic model of a 7-DOF manipulator was established based on the screw theory. Then, the singularity of the manipulator was analyzed, and the velocity level inverse kinematics algorithm for singularity avoidance was derived based on the minimum singular value as the singularity optimization index. Finally, a path planning experiment for singularity avoidance was conducted based on the velocity level inverse kinematics algorithm. The experimental results showed that the inverse kinematics algorithm has good accuracy, which verifies the effectiveness of the singularity avoidance algorithm and lays the foundation for the motion planning of redundant manipulators.

title: Parameterized Even-Symmetric Function for Stabilizing and Designing Variable Lowpass Filters
authors: Tian-Bo Deng
abstract: A variable filter (VF) is capable of tuning its frequency-domain response promptly without redesigning a novel filter. Despite the fact that a recursive VF requires less computations as compared with its non-recursive counterpart, it faces a challenging stability issue. The stability issue can be skillfully resolved through replacing the coefficients in the VF's denominator by using some special functions of other parameters. Replacing the denominator coefficients with such special functions enables the stability requirement to be always satisfied without any con-cerns about the values of the new parameters. To perform those parameter replacements, a function (unity-bounded function: UB function) must be used. The UB function needs to meet a special condition. In this paper, such a UB function is presented for carrying out the denominator-parameter replacements, which is an even-symmetric function. Furthermore, this even-symmetric UB function is employed in designing a recursive variable-lowpass-filter, and computer simulations are given for showing the assured stability and achieved high accuracy.

title: A Dual-Graph Learning Framework with Sparse Adaptive Embedding for EEG Emotion Recognition
authors: Wenkang Liu; Fangkun Li; Yang Li
abstract: EEG brain networks capture the complex relationships between multiple brain regions, providing rich information for emotion recognition. However, most existing methods rely on dynamically random initialized adjacent matrix, which limits their ability to effectively model emotional features across different brain regions. Additionally, these methods typically ignore the importance of synchronously modeling both adjacent and long-distance channels, resulting to suboptimal emotion recognition performance. In this paper, we propose a novel dual-graph learning framework with sparse adaptive embedding (DGLF-SAE) for EEG-brain-network emotion recognition, which includes a global hypergraph sparse adaptive embedding (GHG-SAE) module and a local adjacency graph sparse adaptive embedding (LAG-SAE) module. Specifically, the GHG-SAE module is designed to capture global relationships by associating long-distance channels, while the LAG-SAE module focuses on learning local relationships by modeling adjacent channels. We validate the effectiveness of our proposed DGLF-SAE on the SEED and SEED-IV datasets, with experimental results (98.05% and 92.83% on SEED and SEED-IV datasets, respectively) demonstrating that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

title: Quadcopter Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Formation Trajectory Tracking based on Extended State Observer with Model Predictive Control
authors: Linjie Hu; Kun Tian; Chao Bai
abstract: To address the formation trajectory tracking of Quadcopter Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (QUAV) in the complex environment, this paper integrates a Model Predictive Control (MPC) method with an Extended State Observer (ESO), which effectively solves instability of flight coordination resulting from external disturbances and internal uncertainties. The prediction model of the MPC controller is obtained based on Taylor series expansion and Euler transform. ESO estimates external disturbances and internal uncertainties in real-time, adjusts the desired speed via proportional compensation, thereby achieving precise control of formation trajectories. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method efficiently suppress external disturbances and internal uncertainties, thereby enabling precise tracking of the trajectory for the formation.

title: Reducing Emissions through AdBlue Tank Temperature Control in Diesel Engines with SCR System
authors: Jojan Valle-De La Cruz; Luis Crisostomo-Soto; Gonzalo Sulca-Ramos; Kener Velasquez-Colorado; Hector Valcarcel-Castillo; Deyby Huamanchahua
abstract: The AdBlue system consists of inserting the urea-water mixture into the exhaust pipe to reduce the emission of polluting gases. Hence, the liquid and exhaust pipe temperatures are essential factors. This research aims to implement a temperature control and monitoring system for AdBlue deposits when they are affected by environmental temperature and climate change. To carry out the design of the control system, the VDI 2206 methodology was used based on four stages until the modeling and analysis of the model in the LabView software. The design of the controller was obtained before the change in temperature of the environment, which affects the urea deposits, so suitable and selected components are used through a morphological matrix. Finally, this research allows controlling the state of the AdBlue deposits, since to have a good performance of emission reduction, there is a temperature range ranging from -10 to 25 ° C, for this control system is created that allows to increase the temperature or decrease it, to obtain a good performance.

title: Motion Error Analysis of High-speed Parallel Robots
authors: Liangliang Zhu; Sergey S. Gavriushin; Jingzhong Zheng; Guannan Chi
abstract: To enhance the operational speed of robots and minimize energy expenditure, a majority of Delta parallel robots employed in the industry have a lightweight design. At high operating speeds, the lightweight construction of Delta robots often causes elastic deformation and vibration. Traditional analysis and control methods for rigid robots do not ensure positioning accuracy of the Delta robot. To address this problem, in this paper we have chosen the WSC-600DJ Delta robot as the subject of our research. Our focus is on analyzing the robot's rigid-flexible coupling dynamics. Firstly, the active and passive arms of the Delta robot are made flexible using Hypermesh software. And then, the rigid-flexible coupled dynamics model of the Delta robot is established in Adams program. Finally, the end effector trajectory is planned in MATLAB using the modified sinusoidal correcting keystone acceleration curve. The driving angle of each active arm is determined via inverse kinematics solutions, which then is imported into Adams for simulation. By comparing the results of modeling the rigid-flexible coupled dynamics of the Delta robot with the theoretical trajectories of the rigid model, we are able to estimate the positioning errors of the robot's actuators caused by the elastic deformation. The results of this study establish a foundation for designing a high-accuracy control system for this particular robot model.

title: Research on Multi-UAV Track Planning by Improving Grey Wolf Fusion Cuckoo Algorithm
authors: Hengyi Huang
abstract: In this paper, an improved gray Wolf algorithm is proposed to solve the problem of multi-UAV cooperative path planning in multi-peak environment. Based on the original GWO algorithm, this paper innovatively introduces a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism to strengthen the global search capability, improve the local search accuracy, and effectively avoid the risk of premature convergence to the local optimal solution. The paper proposes to improve the integration strategy of gray Wolf algorithm and Cuckoo algorithm, and dynamically adjust the contribution proportion of the two algorithms. The performance of the algorithm is optimized and balanced. Through a series of standardized test functions and real scenario cases of multi-UAV flight path planning, the experimental results strongly show that the fusion algorithm proposed in this paper provides a more efficient, accurate and reliable optimization solution in the field of multi-UAV flight path planning, which has far-reaching academic contributions and broad practical application prospects.

title: 6-DOF Localization in 3D Feature Points Maps for LiDARs of Small FoV
authors: Shenliang Li; Pengfei Qu; Jinyang Zhng; Zhansheng Duan; Kuizhi Mei
abstract: LOAM (lidar odometry and mapping) plays an important role in the field of mobile robot and relocalization based on prior maps is essential for LiDAR-based navigation. In this paper, we propose a system of LOAM and real-time relocalization only based on a low cost Lidar with small FoV (field of view). By taking effort on the matching method, the problem of drift at the sharp turn is settled and the robustness in map-building is improved. To accelerate the matching process in relocalization, our relocalization algorithm is based on the feature points map, not the full map. Finally we demonstrate our system to be accurate and robust by experiments in our school.

title: Design and Fabrication of Power Management Systems for Deep-Sea Environments
authors: Gangda Liang; Dayong Ning; Jiaoyi Hou; Rui Dong; Ziwei Li; Lulin Chai
abstract: Underwater vehicles used in deep-sea exploration require the coordinated operation of multiple sensors and actuators, which depend on a power management system for the distribution of various voltages. However, the extreme water pressure, low temperatures, and high corrosiveness of the deepsea environment present substantial challenges for the development of power management systems. To address these challenges, we have designed and developed a power management system tailored for high-pressure deep-sea environments. The system incorporates multiple voltage outputs, infrared control, and wireless charging capabilities, controlled by an integrated microcontroller. Flexible buoyant materials are employed in the system to achieve zero buoyancy balancing and pressure-resistant encapsulation, minimizing weight and reducing manufacturing costs without the need for rigid protective structures. The system underwent simulated deep-sea high-pressure testing, demonstrating stable output of driving voltages and control signals at a water pressure of 110 MPa. The design's adaptability to deep-sea conditions was further validated by periodic flapping powered by a biomimetic pectoral fin. This design offers an innovative solution for the lightweight and cost-effective development of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), advancing the technology of deep-sea underwater equipment.

title: Design of a Gecko Inspired End Effector for Multi-Terrain Legged Wall Climbing Robots
authors: Shweta Ullala; Yasasvi Challa; Pooja K R; Nithyashree R; T S Chandar
abstract: This work introduces a wall-climbing robot designed in Autodesk Fusion360, featuring a novel gecko-inspired adhesive foot incorporated with passive adhesive technology rather than relying on active adhesive mechanisms. Various simulations conducted in Fusion360 validate structural robustness under heavy loads. The mathematical modeling conducted involves the calculation of DH parameters, forward kinematics, and bond and peel forces. The manual PI-controlled movement system for the end effector demonstrates fine-tuned control, emphasizing the potential of climbing robots in various applications ranging from structural inspection to maintenance. Finally, the successfully constructed hardware model of a single end effector concludes the study, highlighting the functionality of bio-inspired wall climbing robots' pivotal role in multiple relevant industries.

title: Hierarchical Table Tennis Spin Estimation Using Ball Trajectory Data
authors: Xudong Zhou; Yuxin Wang; Haibo Zhang; Zhiyong Sun; Erkang Cheng; Bo Song
abstract: Accurate spin estimation is crucial for assisting table tennis robots in defeating high-level human players. Currently, most researchers use methods based on physical models or identify logos on the flying table tennis ball to estimate spin. We try a new approach, considering the use of a data-driven method to estimate spin. However, directly using such models does not produce satisfactory results, as these methods do not consider that table tennis spin estimation is a coarse-to-fine process. To address this problem, we develop a hierarchical spin estimation network to estimate spin progressively. Furthermore, we introduce a Mix Conv-Attn Block to enhance feature extraction from table tennis trajectories. This block can capture both short-term and long-term features to improve the estimation accuracy. Comparing our approach with physical-based and non-hierarchical neural network methods, experimental results show that our method achieves superior performance.

title: A Robust Sliding Mode Control for Electro-Optical Stabilized Servo Tracking System Based on Extended State Observer and Adaptive Neural Network
authors: Bin Feng; Weihua Fan; Qingwei Chen
abstract: The tracking performance and line-of-sight stabilization of electro-optical stabilized servo tracking systems are often affected by various disturbances and uncertainties. To address the problems, a robust motion control scheme is developed. The control strategy effectively amalgamates sliding mode control (SMC), extended state observer (ESO), and adaptive radial basis function (RBF) neural network. Specifically, an ESO is constructed to estimate unknown disturbances and uncertainties in the system. An RBF neural network is employed to correct the estimation accuracy of ESO for time-varying disturbances. Furthermore, the sliding model control strategy is combined with ESO and RBF neural network to mitigate the impact of multi-source disturbances and uncertainties on control precision. The asymptotic stability of the system is demonstrated through Lyapunov theory and LaSalle invariance principle. Finally, simulations are implemented to illustrate the superiority and effectiveness of the proposed control method compared to the traditional SMC-ESO method.

title: Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process Based Health Evaluation of Business Systems
authors: Dequan Gao; Meng Yang; Wang Luo; Bing Zhang; Bao Feng; Jing Du
abstract: With the development of business application systems of large enterprises to cloud and system architecture to micro services, the system scale and the complexity of call interaction and business coverage are increasing, and the improvement of system complexity brings new challenges to the evaluation of system operation status. O&M personnel need to regularly evaluate the health status of the systems to identify risks and hidden dangers in system operation in a timely mode. The health degree evaluation of information systems that performs comprehensive analysis and assessment of the system to determine whether the operational status and capabilities meet expectations, is a typical multi-objective and multi-level problem. To provide a feasible solution of this problem, this paper proposes a fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP) based health evaluation method. Specifically, a multi-layer indicator system for business system health evaluation is constructed by combining it with the experience of operation and maintenance (O&M) experts. Moreover, an FHAP-based weight calculation method is proposed to obtain the weights of the indicators. The FHAP-based method can reduce the impact of O&M experts' subjective evaluation on the overall health score. Furthermore, a fuzzy comprehensive evaluation (FCE) based health evaluation method is proposed. An empirical analysis is provided to make the proposed method more accurate. This method can simultaneously complete the scoring of system health and the positioning of hidden dangers in the business system.

title: Fault-Tolerant Control for a Class of 1-D Systems with Unknown Input Powers and Measurement Drifts
authors: Chengjun Ma; Qikun Shen
abstract: This article considers a fault-tolerant control problem for a class of 1-D systems with unknown input powers, actuator failure and measurement drifts. Unlike most current systems where the input power is one or known, the unknown input powers is considered in this article. Based on Lyapunov stability theory, two kinds of controllers are designed, which are suitable for the two cases of whether the system has measurement drift or not. Under the control strategy proposed in this article, the closed-loop system is asymptotically bounded, and all the signals in the system converge to a small neighborhood of the origin. Finally, two numerical examples are given to verify the effectiveness of the control strategy.

title: Study on a Novel Snake Arm Robot for Working in a Narrow Space
authors: Wei Sun; Shujian Liu; Yunfei Liu; Weijun Wang; Yangzhou Zhao
abstract: In some narrow environments, it is difficult for ordinary robots to enter them to work. The snake arm robot has a large aspect ratio, can move flexibly, and can shuttle in a narrow and tortuous environment. It has great advantages in working in a narrow space. A novel snake arm robot for working in a narrow space is designed. The robot has the characteristics of large length-to-diameter ratio, large bending angle, and multiple redundant degrees of freedom, and can traverse a relatively narrow space. Its redundant degrees of freedom allow the snake-shaped arm to adapt to the surrounding environment autonomously, and it can better complete a series of tasks.

title: Hopping Control of a Monopod Robot: Reinforcement Learning vs Raibert Heuristic
authors: Zhuochen Yuan; Linqi Ye; Houde Liu; Bin Liang
abstract: As a classic control problem, monopod hopping was traditionally solved using a state machine-based approach known as the Raibert Heuristic. Recently, reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful alternative for robotic control. In this paper, we apply RL to monopod hopping control and compare its performance with the traditional Raibert Heuristic. Simulations demonstrate that RL achieves faster hopping speeds and better robustness than the Raibert method. Both control strategies were implemented on a simulated monopod robot and evaluated based on hopping speed and robustness. The results highlight RL’s superiority in complex environments, while the Raibert approach remains a good solution for simpler scenarios. (The attached video can be found in https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1eTxgeuEjV)

title: Study on Point Cloud Processing Technology in Robotic Welding for Ship Sub-Assembly
authors: Ruixue Zhang; Chenpeng Liang; Yan Huang; Shihao Kang; Naikun Wei; Xuyue Yin
abstract: To address the issue of insufficient automation in robotic welding for ship small assemblies, this study develops a welding technology based on point cloud processing. The research utilizes vision sensors to collect point cloud data of workpieces, and an improved point cloud processing algorithm is employed to extract weld seam information effectively. A novel real-time online calibration method for vision sensors is introduced, which precisely transforms the weld seam position from the vision sensor coordinate system to the robot coordinate system, thereby ensuring accuracy and continuity in the robotic welding process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed technology significantly enhances automation and weld quality in ship small assemblies, showing substantial industrial application potential.

title: Text Input Through Swipe Gestures Based Personalized AI Agent
authors: Xiangyu Qi; Dongdong Weng; Jie Hao; Zihao Li
abstract: Text input based on virtual reality is a common technique in interactive systems, but it may face challenges related to input efficiency and task load when interacting with VR hardware and applications. The development of artificial intelligence interaction technologies offers new approaches to addressing text input challenges. In this paper, we propose a swipe gesture-based text input method under a personalized AI agent framework, combining portable devices (e.g. smartphones) with VR input and incorporating user profile information, input habits, and conversational intent. By integrating the GPT-3.5 model to train a personalized AI agent, we emphasize the importance of understanding and responding to human behavior or capabilities from the agent's perspective, enabling text prediction based on specific contexts. The keyboard layout design is based on a disk divided into 8 equal regions, where the outer circle is subdivided into key areas containing letters, and the inner circle serves as the input buffer area. By resolving word ambiguities based on user input and leveraging the extensive capabilities of large language models in context awareness and text prediction, the system allows complete sentences to be generated from keywords. This reduces the number of manual inputs required by the user, improving text input efficiency and enhancing the overall user experience.

title: An Adaptive Path Planning Method Based on the Frenét Frame
authors: Xinyong Luo; Hui Zhang; Xidong Zhou; Lian Yang
abstract: In the realm of mobile robot path planning, this study integrates local path planning with the Frenét Frame, presenting an adaptive path planning approach. Firstly, the A* algorithm is employed to extract the shortest path from the map. Subsequently, cubic spline interpolation is applied to the path to generate a smooth global reference trajectory. Next, a cost function based on lateral offset distance is introduced to enhance the proximity of the trajectory to the reference trajectory, thereby improving efficiency. Lastly, an adaptive sampling strategy is incorporated to enhance the robot's dynamic obstacle avoidance performance. Experimental results validate the efficacy of the proposed path-planning approach.

title: Hybrid Steganography: Leveraging Chaotic Encryption and CNN for Robust Image Hiding
authors: Xiaoqing Niu; Guohong Yi
abstract: This paper presents a robust image information hiding method integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and image encryption based on the Lorenz three-dimensional chaotic system. We introduce chaotic image encryption technology based on the Lorenz three-dimensional system into the CNN-based image steganography framework. Leveraging the high sensitivity and unpredictability of the Lorenz system, the original secret image is first encrypted to render it visually imperceptible. During the image hiding phase, the encrypted secret image is embedded into the carrier image using an improved CNN-based image information hiding model. This model capitalizes on CNN’s powerful automatic learning and feature extraction capabilities to achieve information hiding, resulting in a steganographic image. In the information extraction phase, the steganographic image serves as the input for the decoder network within the model, where the decoder decrypts it to retrieve both the carrier image and the encrypted secret image. Finally, the secret image is decrypted using the Lorenz chaotic encryption algorithm. Analyses of PSNR/SSIM and visual quality demonstrate that the proposed hybrid image steganography scheme offers high security and robustness, effectively preventing distortion of the secret image.

title: A New Approach to the Design of the Linear Systems with Desired Poles and Zeros
authors: Tadeusz Kaczorek; Łukasz Sajewski
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: A new approach to the design of linear continuous-time systems with desired poles and zeros of their transfer matrices is proposed. The method is based on the solving of the linear matrix equations. The presented procedure are illustrated by simple numerical examples.

title: Dynamic Event-Triggered Control for Discrete-Time Markov Jump Systems
authors: Yueyuan Zhang; Yiyang Chen
abstract: This paper concentrates on the dynamic event trigger based controller design for discrete-time Markov jump systems. The rich data transmission within the network channel may cause the collision and the waste of resources, which leads to some kinds of poor system performance. Firstly, a discrete time domain dynamic event trigger mechanism is proposed for controller design. Secondly, for discrete time Markov jump systems, a mode-dependent Lyapunov function is designed to ensure the system state to be exponentially mean-square ultimately bounded by linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Finally, a numerical simulation example is conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the provided method.

title: New Approach Using Hough Transform in a Visual System for Advanced Control in Flat Glass Industry
authors: Andrei Hossu; Daniela Hossu; Ioana Fagarasan
abstract: The paper presents the implementation aspects of a visual inspection system dedicated as part of the advanced control in Flat Glass Manufacturing Industry. The system has to identify and to provide a measurement of the mechanical no-uniformity of the glass ribbon before the cutting process in order to maximize the output of the manufacturing process. The necessity of developing the presented system is pointed out by being imposed for achieving an advance automation level. The image processing techniques and algorithms used have to provide results with a high reliability even in conditions of a very large variety of the types of image distortions necessary to be identified. The development of the proposed visual inspection system is coming with the approach of modified Hough transform technique for processing the images and is obtaining a high robustness of the results.

title: Energy Saving Oriented Electricity Load Calculation of High-speed Train Group: A Distributed Computation Method
authors: Zhe Zhang; Yani Sun; Muhetabaier Baihetiyaer
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: Electricity load calculation of high-speed train group is one critical step for traction power system design. The energy-saving oriented electricity load calculation of high-speed train group is time-consuming. A distributed computation framework is proposed to improve the computing efficiency of solution algorithm by splitting the train group into single trains and dividing the railway lines into various sections. The experiment results show that the computing efficiency has been improved by 80.9% and becomes more stable under distributed computation environment.

title: Design and Motion Control Strategy of a Bio-Inspired Jumping Robot for Aerial Rod-Hooking
authors: Reno Pangestu; Yu-Cheng Xu; Chi-Ying Lin
abstract: Inspired by the jumping behavior of cassowary animals, this research proposes a ledge-grasping robot that is specifically capable of exploring vertical jumping motion patterns; for example, the robot launches from the ground and then grasps an object on the upper vertical wall. The motion process is divided into four phases: Squat Phase, Launch Phase, Transition Phase, and Landing Phase. The analysis is carried out by investigating the dynamic effects of the various operating parameters and phase switching conditions so that the robot can jump optimally at any target altitude. The motion trajectory planning is integrated with a virtual impedance control algorithm implemented on the BLDC motor as the joint actuator. In addition, the incorporation of Quasi-Direct-Drive (QDD) actuators facilitates smooth transitions between motion phases and improves energy accumulation efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the robot's motion gait effectively mimics the natural movement of a cassowary. The robot achieved a jump height of 0.34 m, a jump agility of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.7 ~\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$</tex>, a cost of transport (COT) of 2.72, and successfully grasped a target rod in mid-air. Furthermore, a comparative analysis with similar existing robots was conducted to study the design performance factors more widely, based on the respective results of vertical jump agility and COT.

title: Deep Learning Based Autonomous Robotic Grasping and Sorting System for Industry 4.0
authors: Muhammad Arsalan; Abid Imran; Syed Salman Shah; Sahar Malaika; Zar Afshan Iqbal
abstract: This paper introduces a deep learning (DL)-based vision system for real-time object detection, grasping, and sorting using a UR5e robotic manipulator, aimed to address the challenges faced in industrial automation while grasping and sorting randomly placed objects in the workspace. The system utilizes a fine-tuned detection model, YOLOv8s, trained on a custom dataset of three distinct objects for testing a real-time grasping and sorting system using DL. Once the objects are detected in the workspace, image processing techniques are applied to each detected object to extract the accurate grasping information like the centroid and the orientation. This information is then converted to the robotic arm-based coordinate system to ensure the accurate manipulation of the objects in the workspace. The system is tested in the cluttered environment of the tabletop workspace to grasp and sort the objects, significantly enhancing both speed and accuracy in real-time industrial tasks. Experimental results show grasping accuracy of 93.33%, demonstrating the system's potential to improve automation efficiency in Industry 4.0 applications.

title: Development of Automatic Detection System for Explosion-Proof Test
authors: Wenqiang Xie
abstract: Explosion-proof electrical equipment can be divided into explosion-proof type, intrinsically safe type, pouring type and so on according to the explosion-proof principle, among which explosion-proof electrical equipment is the most widely used. Explosion test is the basis for judging whether flameproof electrical equipment can meet the standard requirements and can be used in explosive dangerous environment. In order to test the explosion-proof performance of flameproof electrical equipment, a set of flameproof test and detection system is developed, which consists of explosion test tank and control system. The test results show that the system realizes the automatic control of explosion test of flameproof electrical equipment shell, and the detection data is reliable and the detection efficiency is high.

title: Exploration and Navigation in Unknown Environments for Guide Dog Robots
authors: Jiahui Chen; Bin Zhang
abstract: This study presents the development of an autonomous robotic guide dog designed to navigate unknown indoor environments, effectively avoid obstacles, and guide users to specified destinations based on verbal commands. Addressing the growing global shortage of guide dogs, this robotic system offers a safe, flexible, and reliable alternative to traditional guide animals. Upon receiving commands such as “Find the restroom,” the robot systematically explores the environment, detects relevant landmarks, calculates their global coordinates, and safely guides the user toward the targeted location. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed system successfully achieves high accuracy in environment mapping, reliable object recognition, and efficient path planning within previously unknown indoor settings. The findings underscore the potential of this autonomous guide dog robot as a practical alternative to traditional guide dogs, significantly enhancing mobility and independence for impaired individuals.

title: High Misalignment Tolerance Wireless Power Transfer System for Mining Unmanned Vehicle with a Low Cost Semicylinder Magnetic Coupler
authors: Min Guo; Peng Wang; Xuanming Zhao; Jingqi Shao; Yibo Yin; Pengdong Wang; Haibing Wen
abstract: Wireless charging system for mining unmanned vehicle (MUV) requires simplified structure and low cost in the complex and dangerous environment of coal exploitation. To address this issue, this paper proposes a low cost semicylinder magnetic coupler, which the receiving coil is semicylinder in place of the traditional solenoid coil. The cost of magnetic coupler is impressively reduced. The transmitting coil is planar square coil. To further verify the performance of magnetic coupler, the finite element analysis is used to optimize the parameters of semicylinder. A 150W experimental protype is built. Comparing with the traditional solenoid coil, the cost of semicylinder is impressive. The peak value of power transmission is 86.63%. With the tilt angle varies from the 0deg to 360deg, the power transmission efficiency is within 1.2%. At the extreme condition misalignment, the output power there still remains 86.2W. It verifies the semicylinder has excellent performance of cost reeducation and anti misalignment.

title: Gesture Control of a Lightweight Industrial Robot Supported by Augmented Reality
authors: Christian Thormann; Mohammad Ehsan Matour; Alexander Winkler
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to intuitive robot control by gestures made by a human operator supported by augmented reality. Unlike to the concepts of different robot manufactures to guide the robot using the manual control pendant, gesture control would be a universal method to drive the manipulator arm, where no special knowledge is necessary. For this purpose, we develop a set of gestures to move the robot in Cartesian space and to operate the gripper. In order to that, it is possible to program handling tasks, which are very relevant concerning robotic tasks. Furthermore, our scenario may be enhanced towards teleoperation. Augmented reality is then used for verification and modification of the robot program. In contrast to several approaches which use expensive hardware, for example head mounted displays, our concept needs only a monitor or a video projector. We compare the performance of gesture based robot control with conventional methods, such as moving the manipulator with the teach pendant or by hand guidance. For this purpose, a simple handling task is configured and the programming times are analyzed.

title: Learning of the Exploratory Behavior of Mobile Robots for Environmental Segmentation
authors: Manabu Gouko
abstract: A model that can describe the operating environment of robot is necessary for mobile robots to operate effectively in real-world environments. Environmental segmentation, which classifies environments based on their features, is useful for environmental modeling. To realize autonomous environmental segmentation by a robot, the robot must explore through its environment and collect data. In previous studies, the exploratory behavior of a robot for data collection was predesigned by a designer. In addition to the information on environment, those on physical features of robots are essential for design the robot's behavior. Additionally, the exploratory behavior must be redesigned based on the changes in the environment. In this study, an autonomous learning method is proposed for the exploratory behavior of mobile robots using reinforcement learning. Moreover, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified via a simulation experiment. Results revealed that the feature-based environmental segmentation can be performed using the sensor information obtained from the exploratory behavior of robot, realized with the proposed method. By using the proposed method, robots can be expected that automatically explore new environments “collect data” and segment the environment.

title: Sleep Stage Classification Using EEG Signals: A Empirical Wavelet Transform-Based Decomposition Approach
authors: Rajveer Singh Lalawat; Varun Bajaj; Prabin Kumar Padhy
abstract: The objective of signal processing using transformation techniques, is to accurately detect the frequency decomposition and extract small variations within the signals. Previous studies have explored various algorithms aiming to decompose signals and classify sleep stages based on EEG signals, offering valuable insights. However, there is still scope for improvement in handling highly non-stationary signals across all sleep stages. The article proposes employing spectrum partitioning from six sleep phases and the Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT) to properly decompose extremely non-stationary EEG data. This approach uses an adaptive filter bank to control dynamic data in the frequency domain to accurately distinguish sleep stages. Our experiments demonstrate that, the Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifier outperforms Random Forest (RF) and k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classifiers, and it achieves notable classification accuracy for all sleep stages. This method enhances the performance of medical devices and benefits for their use in healthcare.

title: Assistive Helmet for Visually Impaired Human Beings
authors: Ovidiu Ceoca; Eva-Henrietta Dulf
abstract: The presence of visually impaired people around the globe has greatly increased due to many factors that affects the overall health of a person. In such way, this article reviews the current state of technology and aims a new way to help the people in question. It presents an assistive helmet that incorporates three essential features for the blind people to regain their selfconfidence through independent mobility and with all these, maintaining a low cost making it affordable for the majority. The features early mentioned are Obstacle Avoidance which will guide the person without being hurt by any sudden obstacles, Fall Detection which will produce a strident sound and light signals in order the person to be helped and, lastly, Track Monitoring which is responsible to record the path the user took.

title: Evaluation and Optimization Design of Road Traffic Markings Based on Understanding
authors: Mingzhen Zhang; Menglu Chen; Hongfeng Hou
abstract: The proper implementation of traffic marking is crucial for ensuring traffic safety. Insufficient comprehension of marking is a major contributing factor to frequent road traffic accidents. This study aims to clearly define and evaluate the understandability of traffic marking from a design perspective, taking into account both driver characteristics and the design itself. The Q-type clustering method of cluster analysis and SPSS software were employed to obtain clustering analysis results. Through an intra-group homogeneity test, the understanding level of traffic marking was ultimately categorized into three levels: A, B, and C. Additionally, this paper summarizes the relevant indicators, principles, and guidelines for graphic symbol design. By conducting an importance evaluation using factor analysis methodology, three types of design factors (layout rationality, visualization, and appearance style) comprising a total of 12 indicators were identified. The weightage for each factor was calculated in order to determine their relative importance in optimized design factors. Based on these findings regarding the factors influencing the understandability of traffic marking designs, an optimization design approach for traffic markings is proposed herein. Finally, by utilizing examples such as tide lane lines and no-turn markings, optimization designs are implemented with subsequent effect evaluations demonstrating significant improvements in the understanding level of traffic markings after optimization – thus validating the effectiveness of this proposed method.
