title: RBF Neural Network-Based Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control of Electromechanical Servo System with LuGre Friction
authors: Haibo Zhao; Xianghong Zhou
abstract: An adaptive control scheme was put forward for electromechanical servo system with LuGre friction, with a view to mitigating the detrimental effect on the system by friction nonlinearity. Initially, the LuGre friction model was presented for the servo system. Through incorporation of sliding mode function, selection of Lyapunov function and development of adaptive law based on a radial-basis-function (RBF) neural network (RBFNN), we designed an adaptive fault-tolerant controller that used RBFNN for electromechanical servo system for the first time, to the best of our knowledge, and assessed its stability. Simulation results showed that our control scheme outperformed the single RBFNN control in both speed and position tracking.

title: Relative Position Control in 3D Space of Cooperating Multirotor UAVs Using Modular Relative Jacobian
authors: Rodrigo S. Jamisola; Larona P. Ramalepa; Keletso Z. Thebe; Olebogeng Mbedzi
abstract: This paper implements a new approach of controlling cooperative unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) using relative Jacobian. A new Jacobian-based formulation in controlling UAVs is shown, such that they become components of the modular relative Jacobian that is used to coordinate the motion between two UAVs. This new approach affords a holistic control on the two UAVs that is based on the relative motion of one UAV with respect to the other. In this way the two UAVs are now controlled as a single manipulator with an end-effector and posture control. Thus, any control strategy of a single manipulator can now be applied to the control of the two UAVs. Simulations in Gazebo RotorS shows the relative position control between the two UAVs as well as the posture control of the reference UAV.

title: Northern Cthulhu Algorithm Optimized VMD Combined with SVM for Fault Diagnosis
authors: Dengxue Cao; Luyi Liu; Wei Lin
abstract: For a long time, in the face of complex signal processing, such as rolling bearings signals and other complex nonlinear signals, most of them are using traditional signal processing methods to extract signal features. However, it is difficult for general signal processing strategies to extract all the signal features contained in the signal one by one. With mature signal extraction methods like variational mode decomposition (VMD), the number of layers of signal decomposition determines the effect of final fault detection. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a northern goshawk optimization (NGO) algorithm to optimize the VMD and find the optimal decomposition parameter K, which further improve the detection effect. Finally, the experimental data simulated in the MATLAB software platform shows that the detection effect achieved by the optimized VMD of the NGO algorithm is improved by 6.4814%.

title: IrriGaia: IoT-Integrated Robotic System for Comparative Analysis of Mist and Drip Irrigation
authors: Stephanie Rose P. Miranda; Angelo Regis M. Celestino; Fritz Symon D. Blancaflor; Glenda S. Guanzon; Jopearlson Icy Ituriaga; Adha Theza Naputol
publication_title: 2025 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on [::Robotics::] and Technologies for Industrial [::Automation::] (ROBOTHIA)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of IoT-based mist and drip irrigation systems for Thai basil (Ocimum basilicum var. thyrsiflora) cultivation in a controlled indoor environment. We developed a prototype system that integrates ESP32 microcontrollers, capacitive soil moisture sensors, water flow sensors, and energy meters to automate irrigation scheduling and data collection. IoT integration facilitated real-time monitoring, automated control, optimized the irrigation schedules and resource management and enabled the remote visualization in the cloud dashboard. We found that the mist irrigation system demonstrated 33% less water consumption than the drip irrigation system but consumed 55% more energy due to continuous operation. Conversely, the drip irrigation system exhibited superior energy efficiency, making it more suitable for large-scale operations. These findings highlight the potential of IoT-enabled robotic irrigation systems to enhance sustainability and resource efficiency in agriculture. Researchers' future works will explore scalability to diverse crops and environments, as well as the integration of renewable energy sources.

title: Numerical Characterization of Compliance of Thick PDMS Microchannels
authors: Mohammed E. Elgack; Omar Ghannam; Mohamed Abdelgawad
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to characterize the dynamic response of fluid flow inside compliant microchannels such as the ones made of Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). This compliance can affect the accuracy of transient microfluidic experiments. We modeled the main effects of the compliance numerically to obtain the compliance as a function of microchannel dimensions without any fitting parameters as opposed to the ones available in the literature. We also modeled PDMS as a hyperelastic material to include its non-linear stress-strain relation. The model is based on the infinite thickness assumption and was determined to be valid when the PDMS thickness from all sides was higher than 3mm. The relationship obtained for the compliance provides a good fit for data outside of the study range with an error mostly within 4% based on the additional cases we simulated. The compliance was found to be non-linearly dependent on the cross-section with a slightly higher dependence on the height than the width. It also showed a linear dependence on the channel length.

title: A study of obstacle avoidance problem for robots based on basic line-circle combinations
authors: Kang Jiawen
abstract: Aiming at the obstacle avoidance path optimization problem for a robot to reach a specified goal point in an area on the same plane, this paper analyzes different path optimization models, and at the same time divides the obstacles into two categories of vertices and no vertices, and divides them into different exclusion zones, and optimizes them according to the goals. The single-objective point shortest path model is divided into three models: no-goal zone vertex, turning radius, and turning center at the vertex shortest path model, and according to the path turning situation is divided into turning once and many times model, and at the same time, the shortest path time model is established and calculated.

title: Enhanced CBBA with Multi-Condition Evaluation for Multi-Robot Collaborative Exploration
authors: Wei Qian; Yonghang Zheng; Kang Xu; Jiaying Hu; Wenwei Qiu; Yangmin Xie
abstract: In multi-robot collaborative exploration of unstructured environments, redundant exploration often occurs, leading to significant consumption of computational resources and thus reducing exploration efficiency. To address this issue, this paper proposed the EC-MCE algorithm, an enhancement of the Consensus-Based Bundle Algorithm (CBBA) algorithm, which integrates a fully connected neural network to evaluate five key factors: travel cost, information gain, loop closure likelihood, revisit probability, and deviation for local benefit evaluation. This approach ensures the efficient allocation of boundary points, which in turn ensures the efficient completion of exploration tasks. The effectiveness of this method was verified on the Airsim simulation platform, with experimental results showing that compared to traditional methods, this approach reduced the total exploration time by about 10% and decreased the number of repeated area explorations by about 20%. These improvements significantly enhance the exploration efficiency of the system while ensuring the safe navigation of multiple mobile robots in unstructured environments.

title: The Aircraft Assisted Driving Method Based on Machine Vision
authors: Zheyuan Zhang
abstract: This electronic Monitoring the changes in various flight data during aircraft operation is crucial for ensuring safe flight. Currently, most aircraft are equipped with on-board monitoring software that can obtain real-time flight data during operation. When problems occur with the aircraft or the pilot performs abnormal operations, it will trigger warnings of different levels. In addition, the use of satellites, radars, and other equipment allows for the collection and analysis of flight data of aircraft in operation on the ground to predict potential risks. The pilot's operation plays a vital role in flight safety, and there are misoperations caused by human factors when the pilot is operating the aircraft. Aircraft instruments provide a lot of information, and if the pilot needs to perform additional judgment work during the flight based on this information, it will increase the pilot's workload. Therefore, it is essential to correctly and efficiently utilize the aircraft's own information, obtain the status information of the aircraft from the instrument information to predict potential risks, and provide prompts to the pilot. Currently, there are many auxiliary flight devices for aircraft, which mainly help pilots better understand and judge the aircraft's condition in different environments.

title: Research on Motion Simulation for a Rigid-flexible Coupled Manipulator in CoppeliaSim
authors: Bo Hu; Quan Xiao; Congjun Ma; Songyi Dian; Jiaxin Liu; Rui Guo
abstract: For the task of inspecting in complex and narrow space and overcoming shortcomings from rigid manipulator, a type of manipulator with strong adaptability and deformable characteristics is urgently needed. Therefore, a type of rigid-flexible coupled manipulator is analysed from the perspective of mechanical structure and working mechanism in this paper, which are the bases of creating the simulation platform. Then, for the purpose of simplifying tedious motion control processes and analysing its motion state under the data collected, we build the CoppeliaSim model of the manipulator studied in this paper step by step. Finally, a stochastic motion test and an unclosed circle end positioning control task are carried out with detail result analyses, which prove the created CoppeliaSim model of flexible manipulator is well-designed with high accuracy.

title: Spatial modelling of virus transfer and exposure using Bayesian inference with Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation
authors: Andrzej Neścior; Adrian Dudek; Waldemar Bauer; Jerzy Baranowski
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Airborne transmission is a key element in the spread of viral contagion. To prevent this, health organization publish guidelines for every major disease outbreak. However, they are often based on researches carried out without access to modern solutions. In this paper, we propose usage of Bayesian inference as an additional, to computationally-intensive methods such as CFD or FEM, way to analyse short - range virus exposure. We build a spatial model, using INLA package, which allows us to optimize the complicated computational process and deal with conundrums of virus exposure modeling.

title: Neural Sliding Mode Control using Neural Disturbance Observer for Gyroscopes
authors: Luoyu Zhang; Zhiwei Wen; Xinsong Zhang; Yunxiang Guo; Cheng Lu
abstract: In this paper, a neural network sliding mode control based on neural network disturbance observer is proposed for the control of MEMS gyroscopes under external disturbances. In the design process, two sets of RBF neural networks are incorporated in the sliding mode controller design as well as the disturbance design separately to release the dependence of each module on gyroscope system parameters. Meanwhile, the integration of the neural disturbance observer can help to alleviate chattering phenomenon in conventional sliding mode control forces. Simulation studies are implemented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

title: Automated Quantification of Traffic Particulate Emissions via an Image Analysis Pipeline
authors: Kong Yuan Ho; Chin Seng Lim; Mathena A Kattar; Bharathi Boppana; Liya Yu; Chin Chun Ooi
abstract: Traffic emissions are known to contribute significantly to air pollution around the world, especially in heavily urbanized cities such as Singapore. It has been previously shown that the particulate pollution along major roadways exhibit strong correlation with increased traffic during peak hours, and that reductions in traffic emissions can lead to better health outcomes. However, in many instances, obtaining proper counts of vehicular traffic remains manual and extremely laborious. This then restricts one's ability to carry out longitudinal monitoring for extended periods, for example, when trying to understand the efficacy of intervention measures such as new traffic regulations (e.g. car-pooling) or for computational modelling. Hence, in this study, we propose and implement an integrated machine learning pipeline that utilizes traffic images to obtain vehicular counts that can be easily integrated with other measurements to facilitate various studies. We verify the utility and accuracy of this pipeline on an open-source dataset of traffic images obtained for a location in Singapore and compare the obtained vehicular counts with collocated particulate measurement data obtained over a 2-week period in 2022. The roadside particulate emission is observed to correlate well with obtained vehicular counts with a correlation coefficient of 0.93, indicating that this method can indeed serve as a quick and effective correlate of particulate emissions.

title: Static Analysis and Design of Tendon-Driven Universal Joints for Robot Manipulators
authors: Mitsuhiro Yamano; Koki Shimojo; Rai Suzuki
abstract: This paper discusses the effective design of a tendon-driven universal joint. We developed the joint in our previous study. The problem with joint is that differential kinematics and statics are not simple. We present static analysis based on the model of the joint. The route of the tendon strings affects the performance of the joint. The results of the analysis show the significant tendency for the design of the joint. We show some design examples of the joints and an example of a robot finger using the joints.

title: Autonomous Aquatic Laser-Following Robot Through RGB Sensors and Optimized Artificial Neural Networks
authors: Efrain Mendez-Flores; Thomas Kallmann; Joseph Garcia; Brianna Mena; Naji Tarabay; Camilo Velez
abstract: Aquatic Robots have a critical role to enhance oceanography studies, enable search and rescue scenarios, and basically enable performing tasks that without them, would be too dangerous or even impossible for humans alone. Among the different types of Aquatic prototypes, robots with laser-following features offer enhanced precision, adaptability, simplified guidance, object tracking, and research opportunities due to their suitability for multiple applications. Thereby, this paper explores the design and implementation of an Autonomous Aquatic Robot, capable of following a laser beam through an arrange of multiple RGB sensors feeding an embedded Artificial Neural Network (ANN), optimally trained through a metaheuristic algorithm (Earthquake Optimization Algorithm) to create a laser-following robot. Experimental results validate how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be applied to generate a control structure for a laser-following robot, with over 99% of accuracy to generate activation signals by the laser presence detection, to provide a reliable signal for the autonomous prototype.

title: A Novel System for Robot Trajectory Programming based on VR Tracking System
authors: Yiming Ji; Minxiu Kong; Chuancheng Bian; Jiawang Wang
abstract: This paper proposes an efficiently robot trajectory programming system that enables operators to program a robot conveniently. Based on VR tracking devices, a pen-shaped teaching tool is designed to track its position and orientation for demonstration, so the system could reach the advantages of low cost and high precision. A valid experiment is set by adapting UR5 system to assess the efficiency of the proposed system, the maximum deviation between real and demonstration trajectory is 1.13 mm. As proved by the experiments, the proposed robot trajectory programming approach is more efficient than UR kinesthetic teaching system.

title: MIMO Control of a Twin Rotor Aerodynamical System(TRAS)
authors: Chun Cao; Xiandao Huang; Wenjie Cao; Hongwu Wang; Ya Yang; Jinxin Xu
abstract: As a model developed from the helicopter, the twin rotor aerodynamical system has particular interesting dynamic features. The main difficulties in designing controllers for it follow from nonlinearities and couplings. In this paper, A black-box model is developed based on the subspace identification algorithm(N4SID). A mixed-sensitivity H∞ controller is designed to minimize the effect of disturbance and noise. There are several compensations applied to improve the performance. A reasonable experiment result is obtained.

title: Disturbance Observer-Based Nonsingular Finite Time Control Scheme for a Class of Chaotic Systems
authors: Saleh Mobayen; Maryam Jafari; Afef Fekih; Farhad Bayat
abstract: The current article suggests a new non-singular fast terminal sliding controller approach for a class of chaotic systems subject to exterior disturbances and time-varying nonlinear terms. The approach combines the estimation properties of disturbance observers with the robustness features of sliding mode control. The disturbance estimator is designed to ensure the convergence of disturbance approximate error to origin in the finite time, whereas the proposed stabilizing controller guarantees the existence of switching behavior around switching surface in the finite time. The performance of proposed approach was evaluated using a Wang-Chen chaotic system subject to external disturbances and time-varying nonlinearities. Achieving good dynamic behavior with reduced chattering without requiring any information about upper bound of disturbance are among the positive features of the proposed design.

title: 3D gated Imaging Using a Unet Model
authors: Siqing Zhang; Xiaoquan Liu
abstract: Range gated 3D imaging is widely used in space imaging, distance measurement, automatic driving and other application scenarios. A range gated 3D imaging system based on neural network is proposed. The system inputs three range gated images through convolutional neural network, and then outputs a depth map. A single convolutional neural network is proposed to process range gated images, and a multi-scale loss function is used. The test results on the real data set of outdoor driving show that the model trained on the GPU(graphics processing unit) in this paper realizes range gated 3D imaging.

title: Self-reconfiguration Strategy of Modular Robot Based on Topological Graph Comparison Algorithm
authors: Zhengyu Liang; Gang Chen; Junting Fei
abstract: Configuration can be reconstructed is an obvious advantage of modular robot, how to conduct robot to achieve target configuration is the key technology of modular robot. In order to improve the efficiency of reconfiguration algorithm, a chain-type self-reconfiguration strategy of modular robot based on topological graph comparison is proposed. Firstly, the structure characters of modular unit and configuration representation of modular robot are introduced. Secondly, topological graphs of initial and target configuration are deconstructed into single chains by starting from their root/bifurcation nodes and ending each leaf node respectively. Thirdly, chain-similarity index is built for evaluating difference of two single chain, and the most similar deconstruction plan between initial and target configuration is seen as optimal plan. On this basis, comparing the connection features of initial/target sub-chains, reconfiguration sequences can be solved according to “break-before-connect”. Finally, the simulation verifies the validity of reconfiguration strategy.

title: Factor Graph Optimization for Real-Time Positioning in Unmanned Driving
authors: Yihan Huang; Zhiyu Lu; Qinyang Liu; Siqi Bai; Yue Yin; Zhilin Gao
abstract: Global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) have made significant advancements in recent years, allowing for free access and the provision of more dependable services. However, the conventional method produces erroneous positions and has to be modified. This paper proposes a factor graph optimization for real-time positioning in unmanned driving. GNSS/INS provides precise measurements of position data with better accuracy and robustness, and the use of the iSAM algorithm minimizes costs while enhancing the accuracy of the algorithm. Through field tests, compared with the data that had been filtered using the Kalman filtering, the outcomes demonstrated that our real-time localization and algorithmic findings performed better than the Kalman filter fusion results in precision.

title: Observer-Based Fixed-Time Coordinated Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Multi-agent Systems
authors: HaiTao Liu; Xin Huang
abstract: In this article, the fixed-time coordinated control problem is solved in terms of uncertain nonlinear multi-agent systems without leader’s velocity measurements. Firstly, an innovative leader state observer in absence of velocity measurement is created to obtain the estimate value of the leader status information. Secondly, a fixed-time cooperative tracking control method under the directed network topology is developed. Finally, a simulation carried on a set of manipulators illustrates the vaildation of effectiveness of the control strategy we developed.

title: The Automation of Uncrewed Aircraft Systems Traffic Management Calibration Based on Experimental Platform Data
authors: Thomas C. Henderson; David Sacharny; Chad Mello; William Raley
abstract: Many countries are developing an Urban Air Mobility (UAM) capability defining an Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS) Traffic Management (UTM) architecture to allow safe UAS services in urban environments (e.g., delivery, inspection, air taxis, etc.). The main considerations are air worthiness, operator certification, air traffic management, C2 Link, detect and avoid (DAA), safety management, and security. In addition, if thousands of simultaneous UAS flights are to be achieved, it is not possible for them to be controlled individually by human operators. This makes it necessary to have a rigorous and safe automation methodology to handle such a number of flights. A lane-based airspace structure has been proposed which reduces the complexity of strategic deconfliction by providing UAS agents with a set of pre-defined airway corridors called lanes [1], [2]. This yields collateral benefits including UAS information privacy, robust contingency handling exploiting the lane structure, as well as improved observability and control of the air space. A robust set of UTM parameters and policies must be determined based on the performance characteristics of the deployed UAS platforms, and a methodology which constitutes a first step toward this end is proposed and demonstrated here. In order to realize this approach, a set of initial experiments have been performed to determine the constraints imposed by the UTM on UAS platform capabilities and vice versa. Initial implementation parameters and policies are defined. The major contribution here is a methodology to calibrate UTM safety parameters (e.g., headway, platform speed) in terms of specific platform models' operational characteristics. That is, UTM parameters are a function of platform and not some arbitrarily imposed values. Safety uncertainty is then characterized by the calibration method.

title: Integration of Hand Tracking and Process Mining to Improve Knowledge Transfer on the Shoopfloor
authors: Yannick Dassen; Yan Zhao; Oliver Petrovic; Werner Herfs
abstract: For many small and medium-sized companies in Germany, maintaining best practices on the shopfloor is essential for competitiveness. Due to the impending wave of retirements and the changing employment patterns of the younger generations, there is a risk that knowledge will be lost when employees leave. This calls for innovative solutions for the digital capture, storage and provision of knowledge. This article presents a method that uses machine learning to capture hand movements and thus generate event logs for evaluation based on process mining. Using an example from manual assembly, it is shown how this system can be used to record the actions of different employees and analyze them from an efficiency and ergonomic point of view in order to gain an insight into the individual strategies, routines and tricks of the employees during assembly and make them usable for everyone.

title: A Enhanced MPF Method for Terrain Aided Loosely Coupled Navigation
authors: Peng Ding; Shenshen Yang; Lei Wang; Xiufeng Li
abstract: Terrain aided navigation (TAN) is an emerging positioning technology that leverages terrain elevation data acquired from depth sounding equipment mounted on underwater vehicles to align with prior terrain maps, thus enabling absolute position estimation and correction of strapdown inertial navigation system (SINS) errors. This paper integrates marginalization technique into the regularized particle filter to address mixed linear/nonlinear models, achieving terrain aided loosely coupled navigation that simultaneously facilitates position estimation and SINS error correction. Furthermore, a likelihood interval particle initialization method is proposed to constrain the number, position, and weight of initial particles. Field tests evaluate the integrated navigation performance of the proposed method against existing particle initialization techniques, demonstrating its effectiveness in arranging the initial particle set and enhancing the tracking accuracy and robustness of the terrain matching navigation filter. The average terrain tracking positioning errors below one grid and heading angle error less than 10'.

title: Bicycle Stabilization with Safety Guarantees
authors: Maciej Różewicz; Dariusz Cieślar
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: Control and stabilization of autonomous twowheeled, single-track vehicles is challenging due to their inherently unstable dynamics. This paper explores the application of Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) for the stabilization and reference tracking in closed-loop control of such vehicles. The proposed approach relies on a CBF to ensure safe and efficient operation. The nominal case is expanded by the consideration of input and state constraints, model uncertainties and presence of disturbance. The overall method is illustrated through simulations with a CBF operating in a series arrangement with a PID controller. The effectiveness of the approach is confirmed leading to improved stability and responsiveness of the closed-loop setup.

title: On Reductions Among Observation Properties of Discrete Event Systems
authors: Chaohui Gong; Hanran Zhang; Zhong Guo; Zihai Yan; Weilin Wang
abstract: We present a framework for reduction between different observation properties of discrete event systems modeled by automata under language-based dynamic observations defined in [1]. This framework encapsulates the reduction from coobservability to codiagnosability in [1] and from k-codiagnosability to coobservability in [2]. Under this framework, we show a reduction from observability to diagnosability, but a general reduction in the opposite direction does not exist.

title: SOC estimation for lithium-ion batteries based on BiLSTM-AdaBoost with Savitzky-Golay filter
authors: Qinyi Liao; Shidong Li; Xiangjin Yin; Qiaoqiao Xing
abstract: Battery State of Charge is one of the key performance indicators of lithium-ion batteries, and its accurate and stable estimation is crucial to the operation of lithium-ion batteries. Varying environmental temperatures and dynamic working conditions can affect the internal performance stability of the battery, leading to reduced SOC estimation accuracy. In this paper, a BiLSTM-AB-SG model is presented which combine BiLSTM network that integrates the Savitzky-Golay filter and the Adaptive Boost ensemble learning mechanism, to enhance SOC estimation accuracy. The proposed method was experimentally validated using real battery data across various temperature and load conditions, with results demonstrating superior estimation accuracy and robustness compared to traditional single BiLSTM networks under different working conditions and temperatures. Validation through transfer learning indicates that this model is adaptable to other similar lithium-ion battery datasets, showing strong scalability.

title: A Novel Soft Robotic Manipulator Design with Zig-zag Chamber Geometry
authors: Shen Treratanakulchai; Arnau Garriga-Casanovas; Korn Borvorntanajanya; Enrico Franco; Ferdinando Rodriguez y Baena
abstract: The development of soft robots has advanced rapidly in recent years. However, most designs present significant non-linearities and deviate from the desired bending direction in an unpredictable manner. This makes accurate control more difficult. In this paper, we present a novel design of a soft robotic manipulator with zig-zag partition walls, which minimize those deviations. We first outline the design and describe a lost wax manufacturing process for complex geometries. We then report experiments to evaluate the bending characteristics, force, and repeatability of the prototype, and we compare it against an existing design. The results show a significant improvement in bending consistency with minimal deviations.

title: Hybrid Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm for Weighted C-Type Random 2 Satisfiability in Discrete Hopfield Neural Network
authors: Yunjie Chang; Xiaofeng Jiang
abstract: In the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the implementation of propositional satisfiability logic rules in Discrete Hopfield Neural Networks (DHNN) has increasingly attracted attention. However, few studies have focused on expanding the storage capacity of DHNN. To address this gap, we propose the Hybrid Binary Artificial Bee Colony (HBABC) algorithm to optimize the Weighted C-Type Random 2 Satisfiability logic rule. Experimental results demonstrate that HBABC can enhance storage capacity by achieving 100% satisfaction of clauses and more than 8.4 unduplicated solutions. The HBABC algorithm exhibits high efficiency, robustness, and stability, making it a promising candidate for further applications and modifications in logical mining approaches to solve real-world problems requiring random dynamics analysis.

title: Towards Extracting Structured Drug Information from Raw Texts using Deep Learning
authors: Ştefan Cristian Hanţig; Radu Razvan Slavescu; Kinga Cristina Slavescu
abstract: This paper presents a technique that extracts relevant information from a medical prescription. In order to solve this problem we have approached the problem from Name Entity Recognition (NER) perspective, which aims to label each word with a specific tag. The NER problem is solved using Deep Learning (DL) techniques combined with Conditional Random Fields (CRF). The final model is tested using 5-fold cross-validation technique, and it achieves around 91% F1-measure. The training and testing is done on our corpus, which was manually annotated.

title: Human-Robot Teaming and Coordination in Day and Night Environments
authors: Yufeng Yue; Xiangyu Liu; Yuanzhe Wang; Jun Zhang; Danwei Wang
abstract: As robots are sharing work spaces with human, human-robot teamwork is becoming increasingly important. It is foreseeable that the daily work team will be composed of human and robots. The integration of the appropriate decision-making process is an essential part to design and develop the team. If robots can understand the activities and intents of human, it is convenient for a person to cooperate with robots in a natural manner. This paper proposes a system that enables robots to understand human pose and execute given command. The system provides two options for different hardware systems: the first one is suitable for powerful computational units; the second model is compact and efficient on a normal robot platform. In order to enrich application scenarios, we propose a method to extract human pose from thermal images so that our system can be used in all-weather scenario. In addition, we collected extensive training data and trained a MLP neural network to classify several human poses. The experimental results show the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed MLP neural network in day and night environments.

title: Design and Application of Pavement Structure Depth Calibration Device
authors: Yongbo Du; Chao Liu; Linfeng Huang; Jiahao Chen; Shuwen Hou; Yifeng Zou; Junhai Xu
abstract: The depth of pavement structure is an important indicator of pavement detection, which can evaluate the anti-skid performance and drainage performance of the pavement, and plays a decisive role in the safety of pavement traffic. The traditional pavement structure depth measurement method has problems such as poor measurement accuracy and unintuitive measurement results. The laser measurement pavement structure depth measurement method has been widely used. In the process of calibrating the laser structural depth instrument, a calibration device is urgently needed, which can provide a stable rotation speed and drive the rotation of the simulated road surface turntable. The turntable has standard values and different structural depths, thereby completing the verification of the structural depth instrument. A depth calibration device for pavement structure proposed in this paper meets the above requirements. The device prototype is composed of mechanical system and control system. The mechanical system consists of a control box and a turntable rotating base. This paper describes the structure of the turntable rotating base. The main controller of the control system is based on the Mitsubishi FX3U PLC design and controls the speed of the direct drive motor through the analog voltage. During the experiment on the system linearity, due to the poor linearity of the motor driver, it caused greater inconvenience to the speed design, so the program control logic designed the speed feedback loop, and the negative feedback logic was introduced to ensure the stability of the turntable speed and the system speed. The error is within ±15r/min. Through system testing and actual industrial field experiments, the system performance meets the requirements.

title: Optimizing Wind Speed Estimation with Least Squares Generative Adversarial Networks: A Case Study of Pakistan
authors: Iqra Ashfaq; Hasan Zahid; Fajr Naveed; Aaisha Abid; Zaki Uddin
abstract: Wind energy has emerged as a key player in sustainable power generation. Accurate prediction of wind speed is critical for optimizing wind farm operations, energy output forecasting, and reducing dependency on traditional power sources. In this study, we propose a Least-Squares Generative Adversarial Network (LSGAN) for wind speed prediction in a specific region of Pakistan, utilizing data from Tandoghulamali, which includes features like wind speeds at various altitudes and wind direction. The model is designed to predict wind speed at 80 meters, a crucial target variable for wind turbine operations. The LSGAN model effectively leverages adversarial training, achieving high accuracy with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.54 and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 1.77. Through a detailed comparison of actual versus predicted values, the model demonstrates its ability to generalize well across unseen data, with stable performance during the adversarial learning process. This approach opens up new possibilities for applying advanced machine learning techniques in renewable energy forecasting, particularly in regions with sparse historical data.

title: A Method for Minimizing Energy Consumption of Industrial Robots with Cycle Time Considerations
authors: Djamel-Eddine Tahraoui; Nicolas Séguy; Hicham Hadj-Abdelkader; Mokrane Abdiche
abstract: This study presents a novel approach to optimizing energy-efficient path planning for industrial robots, focusing on minimizing energy consumption while adhering to cycle time constraints. Simulations were carried out on a virtual FANUC R-2000iB/250F robot within an industrial scenario. The method begins by analyzing the influence of key variables, such as speed, acceleration, waypoint positioning, and termination types, on both energy consumption and cycle time. A statistical model of these two responses was developed, followed by the application of a genetic algorithm to determine the optimal parameters that minimize energy consumption, either by maintaining the cycle time within a predefined range or by simultaneously minimizing it, resulting in a Pareto front of optimal solutions. Validation tests revealed an average 23% reduction in energy consumption compared to non-optimized settings, while maintaining constant cycle time. These results demonstrate the strong potential of the proposed method for industrial applications.

title: Trajectory Planning Technology for Lunar Launch Window Expansion Based on Improved PSO
authors: Hongyu Han; Yibo Ding; Xiaokui Yue; Haibo Zhang; Wenbo Li; Guangshan Chen
abstract: A guidance method based on particle swarm optimization (PSO), suitable for expanding the launch window of lunar ascent phase, is developed. Firstly, the dynamic model of Lunar lander is constructed. Then, a PSO, whose inertia and acceleration coefficient have been improved, is established to solve the problem of accurate ascent guidance. Finally, the improved algorithm is compared with a traditional one. The results show that the improved PSO can effectively meet the requirement for accuracy: the error of semi major axis is in the order of 10 meters, the error of inclination and right ascension of the ascending node (RAAN) is in the order of 0.01°. For the problem of expanding launch window of lunar ascent phase, RAAN can be transformed from coplanar launch by 10° when using improved method, which is equal to 20 hours of launch delay or advance. Compared with the traditional PSO, improved PSO has significant advantages in solving the problem of accurate lunar liftoff, its convergence is stronger and the accuracy is significantly higher.

title: Automotive OTA Upgrade Scheme Based on Optimal Difference Algorithm
authors: Guihe Qin; Yingbei Wang; Yanhua Liang; Jiaru Song
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency and reliability of the automotive OTA (Over-the-Air) upgrade, and make it more adaptable to the characteristics of the car. In the paper, we propose to use an optimized BSDIFF algorithm to remotely swipe the car. Specifically, the divsufsort algorithm is used in the suffix sequence, and the Zstd algorithm is used in the compression and decompression process to further improve the upgrade speed. Fault-tolerance mechanism and buried point analysis mechanism are also designed to ensure the robustness of the upgrade process. We conducted OTA upgrade simulation experiment on Linux platform. Experiment results show that the proposed combinatorial optimization algorithm can improve the efficiency of ECU remote writing under the bandwidth limitation of vehicle network.

title: Development of a Terrain Adaptive Quadruped-Wheeled Robot
authors: Alen Gigi Joseph; Sreevidya P Menon
abstract: Hybrid quadruped-wheeled robots offer a compelling blend of mobility and adaptability by combining wheeled and legged locomotion. Despite their promise, their structural and control complexities often result in high costs, limiting broader accessibility. This paper presents the development of a novel, low-cost hybrid quadruped-wheeled robot capable of switching between locomotion modes in response to changing terrain. The robot employs a hexapod-inspired configuration, with its middle legs replaced by wheels to simplify mechanics and reduce costs—though this comes at the expense of speed and agility compared to conventional high-performance quadrupeds. The design emphasizes affordability through the use of lowcost actuators and sensors, making it more suitable for prototyping and educational purposes rather than high-speed or dynamic applications. This paper details the kinematic modeling necessary for motion planning, along with gait generation strategies tailored to its legged locomotion. We also present a basic autonomous navigation system and a terrain-adaptive control framework that enables the robot to intelligently transition between wheeled and legged modes.

title: Coaxiality Measurement Method for Micro Components based on Image Processing
authors: JiaJing Yuan; SongYi Dian
abstract: The precise measurement of micro components is of great importance in the field of micro assembly. However, the innate characteristic of micro components poses huge challenges both in the efficiency and accuracy for precise measurement, due to its complex spatial structure. In this work, a HALCON-based coxiality measurement method for micro components is proposed. Firstly, the CCD camera is used to obtain the geometric vision image of micro components. Secondly, the precise positioning and parameter measurement for micro components can be achieved through HALCON with threshold selection, edge detection and feature extraction. Then, the contradiction between high precise measurement and low consumption time in traditional precision measurement is resolved., Finally, the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method are verified by the experiment.

title: Interactive Force Analysis of High-speed Locomotion of Quadruped
authors: Senwei Huang; Xiuli Zhang
abstract: How to continuously improve the locomotion speed is an important research problem in the field of quadruped robots. This paper shows how interactive force can perform useful functions in high-speed galloping of quadrupeds, but few robots make much use of them. Based on the reconstruction of biomechanical data, the change of the direction angle of the ground reaction force of quadrupeds was analyzed. After that, the mechanism model of the cheetah was established by referring to the body shape of a real cheetah. Then the dynamic model of the cheetah's leg was derived according to the Lagrange method, and the joints torques and the other terms of the dynamic equation were analyzed. At the same time, some practical methods for improving the speed of quadruped robots were summarized.

title: Using Cognitive Services within CPS/SCADA Systems Federations - Concepts; Research Areas and Challenges
authors: Andrei Scurtu; Cătălin Dehelean; Szilárd Enyedi; Liviu Miclea
abstract: Artificial intelligence has entered all the underpinnings of modern science to such an extent that any field with a pretense of progress is bound to make room for this chapter. It is a cornerstone of modern applied science. This article will circumscribe a few fundamental aspects which characterize the AI universe, highlighting the important features thereof. The field of applications for CPS/SCADA has been significantly boosted by the integration of AI within its most basic structures. An important feature of the development and integration of AI in the modern world of software is brought about by the providers of AI services which allow for their integration, with ease, in the SCADA application as well as in many other applications. In the last section of the article, we discuss aspects related to the most important suppliers of this type of service, those belonging to the present-day.

title: Model parameters variation in constrained discrete time sliding mode control
authors: Marek Jaskuła; Piotr Leśniewski
publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: In this paper we take into account the variation of the model parameters, during the regulation process, in the discrete time sliding mode control approach. Moreover, the system is affected by unknown, but bounded external disturbances that do not need to satisfy the matching conditions. The controller guarantees the fastest, monotonic and finite time convergence of the representative point to the switching hyperplane, simultaneously ensuring constraints satisfaction on both state and input signal. Sufficient condition that assures all mentioned properties is formally proved and the simulation example demonstrates advantages of the theoretical considerations.

title: Recognition of Loosening Position of Reactor Windings Based on FBG Signal
authors: Hongzhong Ma; Yongteng Sun; Yifeng Qing; Honghua Xu
abstract: The shunt reactor plays a crucial role as a reactive power compensation device, and its operational condition directly affects the safety and stability of the power grid. Among the various mechanical faults that can occur in reactors, loose winding is particularly significant. Currently, the identification of reactor winding looseness primarily relies on methods such as analyzing vibration signals and frequency response. However, these methods are limited by their susceptibility to environmental noise interference and relatively weak online diagnostic capabilities. Strain signal can provide a direct indication of the state of winding looseness; however, there is currently a dearth of research focused on analyzing the winding status using strain analysis. To tackle these challenges, this study takes a 10kV reactor as an experimental platform and gathers data from the winding with Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors. After processing the collected wavelength signals through cleaning and decoupling, this paper introduces a diagnostic method that incorporates an improved SVM based on the Black Hole Optimization algorithm and Principal Component Analysis. Experimental results demonstrate that by utilizing FBG signals and the diagnostic framework proposed in this study, the accuracy of identifying loose winding in the reactor is significantly enhanced. The study holds the promise of offering new insights into the identification of winding looseness.

title: Position Correction and Coordinate System Fusion for Multi-Robot Arm Systems Using Multiple LiDAR Sensors
authors: Ziming Zhang; Kai Li; Shaosheng Xu; Weiguo Wang; Wei Hu
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of improving the accuracy and robustness of multi-robotic arm coordinate system fusion and position correction using multiple LiDAR sensors. We propose an enhanced adaptive Extended Kalman Filter (A-EKF) that dynamically adjusts process and measurement noise covariances based on real-time sensor data and environmental conditions. The theoretical framework encompasses spatial coordinate transformation, sensor data integration, and error mitigation strategies, ensuring precise harmonization of multisensor data. Convergence analysis demonstrates the stability and effectiveness of the proposed A-EKF, and numerical experiments validate its superior performance over traditional EKF methods, particularly in scenarios with varying noise characteristics. The findings highlight the potential of the proposed method for applications requiring high-precision positioning in dynamic and complex environments.

title: Design and Experimental Study of Fiber Bragg Grating Temperature Sensor for Thermal and Vibration Environments
authors: Jicheng Yu; Xin Li; Yijing Huang; Zhaojie Xu
abstract: Aiming to the accurate measurement of aircraft surface temperature in thermal vibration environment, a design and fabrication method of fiber Bragg grating (FBG) temperature sensor based on 304 stainless steel tube package is presented in this paper. Firstly, the simulations were conducted to investigate different materials, tube diameters, and integrated designs of the FBG encapsulation sleeve, and the optimal parameters were selected. Based on the optimal parameters, high-temperature fiber optic connectors and fiber tubing encapsulation were fabricated. The sensor was calibrated and tested within the temperature range from 50 to 900°C, with experimental results showing a sensitivity coefficient of 14.2 pm/°C and the fitness exceeding 0.999, indicating excellent repeatability. Finally, the sensor was tested under high-temperature (700°C) and vibration conditions (10.8g), demonstrating its usability in vibration and high-temperature environments, providing practical value for aircraft surface temperature monitoring.

title: Line Segment Probability Alignment Direct Visual Odometer
authors: Yuhang Wang; Cong Peng
abstract: The direct method is to compare the pixel difference between two frames of images. However, the gray image and photometric error only keep convexity in a small range. Therefore, when there is a large displacement of the camera position, the system may fall into a suboptimal local minimum. Semantic features can solve this problem, but they can only be run in scenarios where semantic features are known. Line features can extract edge information and have good convexity for large camera displacement. In addition, it is easy to adapt to different scenes. In this letter, we propose a line feature probability matching visual odometer. We have built a lighter line feature probability estimation network, which can be deployed on platforms the limited computational power. A joint error function based on gray image and line feature probability is constructed, which has better reliability than photometric error. We experiment the proposed method on public indoor and outdoor datasets, and the results show that the joint feature probability error function is significantly improved than the original method.

title: Decision-level Fusion-based Compressor Blade Crack Detection Method Using Acoustic and Vibration Signals
authors: Jiakang Wen; Feiyun Xu
abstract: Due to the influence of noise, the performance of crack detection methods employing a single signal is not satisfactory. In order to fully utilize both acoustic and vibration signals, a compressor blade crack detection method based on decision-level fusion of acoustic and vibration signals is proposed. Firstly, a crack detection model using SVM is designed, which utilizes the extracted permutation entropy and energy entropy features for classification. Then a convolutional neural network model that fuse multi-source homogeneous signals is designed. Finally, multiple SVM models and convolutional neural network models were trained by taking acoustic and vibration signals as inputs, respectively. The improved BP network approach performs decision-level fusion based on the results of multiple models, and realizes the compressor blade crack detection. The effectiveness of the compressor blade crack detection method is verified through experiments.

title: Automated Ton Bag Handling System Based on Vision and Laser Localization
authors: Jun Tang; Jiacai Liao; Tengjiao Long
abstract: A ton bag is a packaging form used for transporting and storing bulk materials, characterized by its large capacity, strong durability, reusability, and safety in terms of environmental protection. Manually handling ton bags requires overcoming challenges such as heavy weight, difficulty in lifting, poor stability, and slow loading and unloading speeds. The efficiency of using manual forklifts to transfer ton bags in factories is low, with high energy consumption and significant pollution. To address this issue, this paper proposes an automated gantry system for loading and unloading ton bags, which combines laser radar and vision for detection and localization. First, the center of the ton bag is detected using vision, returning the coordinates of the ton bag's center. Next, a PLC controls the gripper to move directly above the ton bag. Finally, the laser scanning method is employed to determine the direction of the lifting straps, find their vertical orientation, and use the gripper to grasp the ton bag. Experimental results show that the automated gantry handling system based on vision and laser localization has significant advantages over traditional manual fork-lift systems.

title: A Sensorless Control Method with LCL Filters for Magnetic Suspension Centrifugal Compressor Drives
authors: Quanyao Yang; Kun Mao; Peng Tan
abstract: In this paper, a sensorless control strategy of magnetic suspension centrifugal compressor (MSCC) based on an LCL filter is proposed, which can effectively suppress the interference of stator current harmonics and high dv/dt common-mode voltage on an active magnetic bearing system. First, the mathematical model of MSCC with LCL filter is established. Based on the new model, a novel terminal sliding mode extended state observer is proposed to estimate the capacitance voltage, and the stability of this method has been strictly proved by second method of Lyapunov. In addition, in order to improve the accuracy of rotor position detection, the same frequency filter compensator is designed in the static coordinate system to eliminate the phase delay and amplitude attenuation caused by the low-pass filter. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation.

title: Modeling; Simulation and Decoupling Control of Resistance Furnace Using MATLAB and Simulink
authors: Qianqian Chen; Yong Wang; Zhao Xu; Xiaojina Chen; Tingting Zhang; Yun Zhang
abstract: The resistance furnace has the characteristics of nonlinear, pure time delay, large inertia, strong coupling, so the decoupling experiment of resistance furnace control system is studied. The mathematical model of resistance furnace was created using the soaring curve method. The system is decoupled by feedforward decoupling method of improved Smith predictive compensation PID using MATLAB. Through the simulation result shows that it can eliminate the coupling between the two temperature ranges well, each temperature can track a given value without difference. Improved Smith predictive compensation PID parameter tuning has better effect than traditional PID tuning, smaller overshoot and faster settling time. When the model mismatches, the stability of the system can be improved. Besides, it has the capacity of resisting disturbance.

title: Design of Bionic Batfish Based on Topology Optimization Method
authors: Yanbo Wang; Runfeng Zhang
abstract: Bionic batfish is a new type of unmanned underwater vehicle. It combines the advantages of low noise and low energy consumption of ocean glider, and low water resistance and high flexibility of bionic robotic fish. It has great significance in pelagic research and observation and deep-sea exploration. This paper first introduces the mechanical structure of bionic batfish, shows how topological structure optimization algorithm is applied to realize the optimal layout of each interior part, demonstrates that the design of hull is based on the form of batfish considering its high mobility, and exemplifies the approach of modularization in designing components; then it shows the analysis of the pressure resistant hull, and MATLAB simulation of different motion states of the bionic batfish, which lays a theoretical foundation for the later practical engineering application.

title: Electrostatic Effect Intelligent Monitoring for Automatic Stirring Process
authors: Yue Feng; Fanye Meng; Xingfeng Shen; Ruiguo Wang
abstract: The stirring with a rotary motion is a highly automatic process in the industrial automation, especially in the chemical, food and pharmaceutical industries. The intense friction and collision between the stirring blade and raw materials (solid granules or liquids) can produce an obviously electrostatic charging effect, especially in dry environment. The unexpected discharging can ignite dust clouds. In this paper, we presented the real-time monitor methods for both charging strength and discharging event. Experiment results showed that the maximum potential of 20.61 kV was obtained at 9 cm from the bottom wall by the designed potential transfer measurement. The discharge leakage current of microseconds was detected across the designed high-speed current circuit while it was connected to the grounded wall of stirring drum. Those proposed sensing methods is capable of early prevention of electrostatic hazards in the field of automatic stirring process.

title: A Spiking Neural Network Model for Object Recognition with Tactile Properties
authors: Fei Wang; Juan Wu; Yanxin Pan
abstract: Tactile properties such as hardness, roughness, and texture are critical information for robots interacting with their surrounding environment, forming the foundation for various tasks including grasping, autonomous navigation, and collaboration. Inspired by human perception mechanisms, this paper presents a tactile property recognition method based on spiking neural network (SNN). We designed a distributed three-dimensional tactile sensor that mimics the structure of human skin, aiming to collect tactile signals through active exploration modes of pressing and sliding over artificially synthesized samples with varying textures and roughness. The collected signals are converted into pulse sequences using Poisson encoding, with object classification determined by the frequency of spike emissions. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method exhibits a straightforward structure and robust predictive performance, achieving an object classification accuracy of 95.56%, effectively simulating human tactile perception capabilities.

title: Multidimensional Spatiotemporal Analysis of Air Quality Based on Big Data
authors: Wei Liu; Jun Ou; Xirong Guo
abstract: It adopts a multidimensional spatiotemporal analysis method to analyze the temporal distribution and spatial distribution characteristics of haze pollution from the dimensions of time and space in Chengdu. Through the analysis of real-time data from six air monitoring points over the past three years in Chengdu, it is concluded that the frequency of haze pollution is higher in December and January, and the air quality is relatively poor inside the city compared to outside the city. In addition, adopting a multi criteria perspective to display the changes of air quality in a certain region or time period can discover potential patterns of spatiotemporal changes in air quality, and provide auxiliary decision-making support for formulating long-term prevention and control strategies under different spatiotemporal conditions.

title: Enhancing Trajectory Tracking of Quadrotor Using Feedback Linearization with MPC-LPV and LQI-LPV under Variable Disturbances
authors: Raian Haider Chowdhury; Ahmed Imtiaz Ferdous; Amreen Hossain; Kazi Arafat Rahman
abstract: The deployment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has markedly improved industrial efficiency. Optimizing control algorithms for precise path tracking is essential for enhancing the reliability and performance of these systems. This paper presents a comparative analysis of Model Predictive Controller (MPC) and Linear Quadratic Integral (LQI) controller, combined with the Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) approach, for quadrotor trajectory tracking under variable disturbances. The quadrotor is modeled using Newton-Euler equations for a six-degrees-of-freedom system. The control architecture includes an outer loop position controller using Feedback Linearization (FL) and an inner loop attitude controller implemented as either MPC-LPV or LQI-LPV. Disturbances are modeled using a custom sinusoidal model. Numerical simulations are done to evaluate controller performance for six different trajectories. The results for the helical trajectory indicate that under variable disturbances, the MPC-LPV+FL outperforms the LQI-LPV+FL. The MPC-LPV+FL achieves a steady-state error of 0.1934 m compared to 0.6611 m for the LQI-LPV+FL. Additionally, the MPC-LPV+FL reaches the minimum error in 3.1 seconds, compared to 3.8 seconds for the LQI-LPV+FL, resulting in a 22.58% faster response. Therefore, MPC-LPV+FL is the superior choice based on accuracy, stability, and speed of response under adverse conditions.

title: Improved A * Algorithm for Autonomous Vehicle Path Planning under Post-disaster Rescue Scene
authors: Zeyu Dong; Hanxu Sun; Gang Chen; Nan Ma; Qingdong Wang; Yuhang Yan
abstract: Mobile robots play a crucial role in various applications, such as explosion prevention, warning systems, and post-disaster rescue missions, owing to their small size and flexible movement capabilities. Traditional mobile robots often employ a single motion mode, which can be insufficient in adapting to the complex and dynamic post-disaster rescue environments. Composite mobile robots, equipped with multiple motion capabilities, have gained popularity in such scenarios. This paper focuses on wheel-legged robots as carriers and proposes a heuristic function that combines distance and energy consumption constraints to improve the A * algorithm. The goal is to achieve effective global path planning in the challenging post-disaster rescue conditions. The environmental features are represented using distance grid maps and energy grid maps. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved algorithm reduces path planning time and successfully balances optimal path selection with energy-efficient planning in typical post-disaster rescue conditions.

title: Manipulation of Cell Cultures by Means of Holographic Visual Feedback
authors: Rahmetullah Varol; Gizem Aydemir; Barkin Gonenc Kamisli; Sevde Omeroglu; Ali Anil Demircali; Zeynep Karavelioglu; Yasemin Baskin; Huseyin Uvet
publication_title: 2020 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: In this study we present a novel untethered micro tool that is able to accomplish minimally invasive micro manipulation tasks in 2D and 3D cell cultures. We demonstrate the proposed system for targeted drug delivery, cell translation and mechanical cell stimulation applications. Due to the ability of the proposed system to control the motion of the micro tool in 6 DOF and obtain depth information through holographic visual feedback, we show that the microtool can be manipulated in a way such that the sample cell culture will go negligible mechanical stress. We show that the proposed system can be used for a variety of micro manipulation tasks without effecting the sample in question.

title: Depth-Changing Motion Control of Under-Actuated Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Based on Prescribed Performance Control
authors: Zhuang Bowen; Yang Botong; Li Zonghao; Gao Guozhang
abstract: To address the depth control accuracy of an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) under unknown disturbances, our study proposes an anti-jamming depth-tracking method based on prescribed performance control. By defining constrained performance functions, we designed a prescribed performance control (PPC) backstepping controller to enhance the tracking control performance for the vertical plane motion of the under-actuated AUV. Additionally, nonlinear disturbance observers (NDOs) are integrated to precisely compensate for unknown disturbances. An adaptive law with “σ-modified leakage terms” is also introduced to estimate the bounds of these disturbances, enabling adaptive backstepping disturbance rejection control and improving both the transient and steady-state depth control performance of the AUV. Simulation results using a MATLAB/Simulink model demonstrate the accuracy of the proposed mathematical model. The adaptive inverse controller, designed with prescribed performance criteria, aligns perpendicularly to the AUV's motion, providing high control performance along with stable and effective transient behavior.

title: Design of PID Anti-Windup System Based on QFT
authors: Xiaoqin Mo; Zhengqing Li; Sanli Fu; Wenfu Sun
abstract: This paper addresses the anti-windup design for PID control systems with significant parametric uncertainty. Actuator saturation, a common nonlinearity in practical systems, can degrade performance and destabilize the closed-loop system, especially when integrators are present. By leveraging Quantitative Feedback Theory (QFT), we propose a robust anti-windup compensator that ensures stability and performance under saturation and parameter variations. The uncertain plant is represented using templates, and the anti-windup structure is analyzed via its Lur'e equivalent system. A detailed example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method, highlighting its advantages.

title: Optimized Global Path Planning with SLAM for Efficient Warehouse Autonomous Mobile Robot
authors: Sharul Amir Abdul Majid; Wan Nurshazwani Wan Zakaria; Mohd Nor Azmi Ab. Patar; Mohd Razali Md Tomari; Mohamad Dzulhelmy Amari; Farah Adilah Mohd Kasran
abstract: Current Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) systems in warehouses often lack flexibility in navigating around obstacles due to limitation of line and marker-based navigation methods. This study presents an intelligent navigation system for an autonomous mobile robot (AMR) designed to improve efficiency of item retrieval in warehouse environment. The proposed system employs a Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithm to enable real-time mapping, obstacle avoidance, and efficient path generation. The global planner is a critical component in the navigation framework, as it determines the optimal and collision-free route through the warehouse, providing an efficient high-level path for the local planner to refine during real time navigation. Extensive evaluations were conducted to determine the optimal combination of global path planners between 1) RRT and Hybrid A* with local planners DWA and 2) TEB for path optimization, based on minimizing path length and travel time to the goal. Experimental results showed that the Hybrid A* with TEB planner achieved the fastest navigation time of 1.25 minutes with a 90% success rate, outperforming the RRT with DWA combination in both speed and reliability. This advancement offers significant potential to enhance warehouse operations by enabling fully autonomous mobile robots capable of performing item retrieval without human intervention.

title: Workspace Analysis of an 8-UPS Parallel Robot
authors: Feng GuoXin; Xu Yong; Chen Yuhao; Li Huizi; Zhang Yuhao; Guo Shuyan; Sun Weijun
abstract: To meet the production requirements of automated tasks in large-scale workspaces, a concept of an industrial robot designed for processing large components (such as wing riveting) and large workspaces is proposed, i.e. the 8-UPS parallel robot. The overall structure and branch configuration of the 8-UPS parallel robot are introduced. Using a three-dimensional search method, the workspace of the parallel mechanism under machining conditions is solved with MATLAB. The impact of rod length on the workspace is analyzed through attitude workspace studies.

title: Quantization-Based Finite-Time Distributed $H_{\infty}$ Filtering for Multi-Sensor Systems under DoS Attacks
authors: Xinran Xu; Zehua Ye; Dan Zhang
abstract: This paper investigates the issue of distributed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> filtering for multi-sensor systems using quantization, in the presence of DoS (denial-of-service) attacks. Firstly, the logarithmic quantizers are introduced in the data transmission channel, where this quantized data is then used for the filter's input. Secondly, a switching analysis model for the filtering error system under cyber-attacks was established, and sufficient conditions are obtained for the allowed attack frequency and duration of DoS attacks. Then, it is deduced that the filtering error system possesses a finite-time bounded (FTB) characteristic and exhibits an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> performance index. Next, the gains of the designed filter are solved using LMI. Finally, a simulation example is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Evaluating Measurement Consistency of Palm Grip Device Through Multi-Phase Clinical Testing
authors: Nurul Atiqah Othman; Nurul Afiqah Rosli; Fatin Izzati Khairul Isham; Noor Ayuni Che Zakaria; Nadia Mohd Mustafah
abstract: Accurate assessment of grip force is essential in rehabilitation, particularly for monitoring motor recovery and spasticity in patients with neurological conditions. This study outlines the iterative development of a palm grip device using rapid field-testing. Over four design phases, the hardware evolved from a basic USB-powered setup to a battery-operated system with improved sensor stability, ergonomic fit, and integrated feedback. Testing involved six patients interacting with various objects (cylindrical, rectangular, cubic, and soft) allowing evaluation across different grip types. Standard deviation and coefficient of variation (CV%) metrics were used to assess measurement consistency. Results indicated lower variability for cubic and soft objects, while cylindrical items exhibited higher fluctuation due to grip instability. Progressive hardware improvements significantly reduced overall variability, demonstrating the impact of patient-informed design. The study emphasizes the value of integrating rapid field-testing into medical device development to ensure both functional reliability and clinical relevance.

title: EAPNet: Enhanced Attention-Guided Network for Fine-Grained Semantic Segmentation
authors: Minyu Huang; Beiping Hou; Feng Pan; Jianwei Dong
abstract: Ground-based cloud observation is essential for meteorological research and climate monitoring. Existing methods for cloud detection and classification in whole-sky images (WSIs) often focus solely on binary segmentation (sky and cloud) or image-level classification, which perform poorly in tasks requiring the classification and segmentation of different cloud types. This paper presents an enhanced attention-guided pyramid network (EAPNet) designed to enhance the accuracy and robustness of fine-grained cloud classification in whole-sky images through deep learning techniques. The key innovations include: 1) the utilization of the pyramid spatial pooling (PSP) module to capture multi-scale contextual information; 2) the introduction of the convolutional block attention module (CBAM), which leverages an attention mechanism to enhance feature representation; and 3) an improved decoder module that enhances localization accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that EAPNet outperforms existing mainstream methods in both cloud classification and segmentation tasks.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Man-Machine Interface of Shield Main Control Room Based on Matching Goodness
authors: Xingyu Jiang; Shengshun Ma; Xiaoying Pang; Haojie Sun; Yisong Jin; Peng Qi
abstract: The shield tunneling efficiency is affected by the man-machine interaction of shield driver and main control room. The comprehensive evaluation index system of man-machine interface of shield main control room is constructed based on the design principle of the man-machine interface of shield main control room. The evaluation indicators of the system are processed by normalization and the comprehensive weight of each evaluation indicator is calculated by order relationship method. On the basis, to evaluate man-machine interface, matching goodness is raised to build the comprehensive evaluation model based on gray matter element analysis. In this paper, shield inclination console is taken as an example to verify the evaluation model. The result shows that the question of comprehensive evaluation is solved efficiently, drivers' ability of quick response to dynamic change of soil layer is increased and the rate of human error is lowered.

title: An Optimized Capture Point Concept Considering the Ankle Stiffness
authors: J. Q. Zhang; M. Cong; D. Liu; Y. Du
abstract: For the load-carrying exoskeletons, balance is a problem that must be solved, which is an important prerequisite for ensuring the safety of wearers. Under external intervention, to enhance the lower extremity exoskeleton's ability to restore balance, the capture point (CP) concept is usually used to perform the push recovery of the lower extremity exoskeleton. However, the traditional CP concept does not consider the impact of ankle stiffness of the lower extremity exoskeleton. This paper proposes the linear inverted torsion spring pendulum model (LITPM) and enhances the CP concept. Push recovery control for the lower extremity exoskeleton is realized based on the LITPM. The experiment results show that the improved CP concept has a smaller step length, under large external interference, which enhances the stability of the lower extremity exoskeleton.

title: Aging Condition Evaluation of Oil Paper Insulation Based on Adaboost Algorithm
authors: Yongqin Ke; Min Li; He Zhuang
abstract: Aging is a critical element influencing the insulation Characteristics of transformers, and is a key link to maintain the balanced work of the power system. To more accurately and comprehensively assess the aging extent of the transformer, this paper deeply analyzed the change mechanism of FDS spectral lines with different aging degrees, and extracted three frequency domain characteristics significantly related to the aging degree of the transformer from the spectral lines for subsequent aging degree evaluation. Then based on adaboost algorithm, the aging degree of transformer was evaluated. The conclusions show that the root mean square error of the proposed model is significantly reduced compared with other models, which fully verifies the accuracy of the model built in this paper.

title: Real-Time Monitoring of Hydraulic Oil Deterioration Using a Hall Effect Sensor Under Operational Conditions
authors: Witsarut Sriratana; Pijaya Chartpolrak; Narin Tammarugwattana
abstract: This paper presents a method for measuring hydraulic oil degradation by detecting metal particle flow using a permanent magnet's magnetic field and monitoring voltage changes in a Hall effect sensor (HES). Degraded hydraulic oil containing increased metal contaminants from component wear exhibits reduced viscosity and higher flow rates. We developed a measurement device incorporating a microcontroller to process data and display contamination levels on an organic light-emitting diode (OLED) screen, enabling real-time monitoring without interrupting machine operations. Experiments measured voltage variations at three system locations with metal contamination levels from 2.5 to 5.0 grams per liter (in 0.5 grams per liter increments). Results showed the HES output voltage varied linearly with particle concentration, demonstrating a maximum deviation of 4.73 millivolts (0.47 %) at 2.5 grams per liter, particularly at the reservoir outlet. This approach helps assess hydraulic oil contamination under operational conditions, offering advantages in real-time monitoring capability, cost-effectiveness, and non-invasive implementation.

title: CAFEs: Cable-Driven Collaborative Floating End-Effectors for Agriculture Applications
authors: Hung Hon Cheng; Josie Hughes
abstract: CAFEs (Collaborative Agricultural Floating Endeffectors) is a new robot design and control approach to automating large-scale agricultural tasks. Based upon a cable driven robot architecture, by sharing the same roller-driven cable set with modular robotic arms, a fast-switching clamping mechanism allows each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$CAFE$</tex> to clamp onto or release from the moving cables, enabling both independent and synchronized movement across the workspace. The methods developed to enable this system include the mechanical design, precise position control and a dynamic model for the spring-mass liked system, ensuring accurate and stable movement of the robotic arms. The system's scalability is further explored by studying the tension and sag in the cables to maintain performance as more robotic arms are deployed. Experimental and simulation results demonstrate the system's effectiveness in tasks including pick-and-place showing its potential to contribute to agricultural automation.

title: Coordinated Control of Precision Conveyor Based on Array Piezoelectric Actuators
authors: Yujuan Tang; Yongquan Zhao
abstract: Due to the problems of the traditional transmission platform device, such as low transmission accuracy and single transmission path, a precision conveyor based on array piezoelectric actuators is present. In order to meet the requirements of the two-DOF drive motion, a structure of double-V orthogonal two-DOF piezoelectric actuator is adopted. The advantages and disadvantages of three different layout methods are discussed, and the layout of four ultrasonic drivers with regular hexagon for conveyor is determined. The working principle of the ultrasonic piezoelectric transmission platform module is classified and discussed according to the regular hexagon layout, and the output speed of each ultrasonic driver under different required motion angles is obtained, so as to achieve the effect of coordinated control. According to the layout and working principle of the GSA-based fuzzy PID controller and piezoelectric precision conveyor, the coordinated control simulation model of the precision conveyor is built on the Simulink. A coordinated control experimental platform is built to validate whether the piezoelectric conveyor can move things translationally and rotationally. The results show that the translation and rotation displacement of the carried objects can be realized.

title: Spatially Nonuniform Filtering and Encoding of Visual Information in a Retinomorphic Hardware System
authors: Tatsuya Yamada; Hiroyuki Yokota; Yuki Hayashida; Shinsuke Yasuakwa
abstract: Efficient information processing in biological early-vision systems is thought to rely on spatially nonuniform computations in the central and peripheral visual fields. Inspired by this functional segregation, we developed a digital hardware vision system that integrates two distinct spatiotemporal filters and spike encoders for the central and peripheral regions on a single image sensor plane. The system employs digital processing techniques to emulate graded potential signals and point-process spike outputs, mimicking the functionality of vertebrate retinas. System-level testing on actual hardware equipment verified region-specific response characteristics for the central and peripheral regions. This proposed approach advances the realization of retinomorphic efficient computations in future robotics and embedded vision systems.

title: Research on Intelligent Command Technology of Navigation Control Reach of Yangtze River
authors: Yong Liu; Sikai Liu
