abstract: In order to effectively solve the problems existing in the current navigable control reach of the Yangtze River, such as the quality of front-end data acquisition needs to be improved, the system command algorithm needs to be optimized, and the active scheduling capability of collaborative command is not yet available, researches on ship dynamic datas acquisition and fusion, signal revealing mode, signal remote control mode and electronic control system are carried out. By means of field investigation, field test and software development, an intelligent command system was developed, and the system was placed in Luzhou Waterway Bureau of the Yangtze River to carry out centralized control and remote command of the three control reaches of the Luzhou section of the Yangtze River: Lianshitan, Shenbeizui and Bingpan Moraine. After more than two years of trial operation, the effect is good, and it has a good prospect of popularization and application.

title: Improvement and Application of a Fire Alarm Method for Building
authors: Ying Xiu
abstract: The current building fire intelligent alarm system relies on single point abnormal signal analysis to generate alarm behavior, which is often affected by signal interference, resulting in low efficiency. This paper proposes an optimized and improved method for building fire alarms. carries out sensor beam collection on the sensing information, and test the connectivity of the sensing information of the building's intelligent fire alarm system; sort the sensing beam signals through spectrum decomposition and feature separation, and extract the accurate feature quantity of the transmission signals of the building intelligent fire alarm system; uses multidimensional wavelet decomposition method for transmission signal identification, in combination with joint tracking and detection of the sensor information to realize fire alarm. The experimental results show that the accuracy of using the improved method for building fire alarms is between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90{\mathrm{\% }}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$98\%$</tex>, and the signal processing capacity is significantly enhanced compared with before the improvement, and the overall has application advantages.

title: Research on Testing Method for Broken Rail Monitoring Equipment Based on Ensemble Learning
authors: Qi Wang; Congcong Liu; Yulong Xing; Yu Zhao
abstract: Broken rail monitoring equipment is essential for ensuring the safety of train operations, and it is necessary to conduct functional and performance testing before the equipment is put into operation. Considering the safety and order of line operations, laboratory testing methods are typically used, employing simulation boards to mimic actual rails. Since the rail is an inductive element, its impedance characteristics are closely related to the frequency of the electrical signal. Accurately simulating the impedance transmission characteristics of the rail under different scenarios and conditions is vital to implementing these testing. To achieve this, we utilize real measured data of rail impedance under different scenarios and frequencies, and establish an equivalent model of rail impedance characteristics using ensemble learning algorithms. This model takes the application conditions of the broken rail monitoring equipment as input and determines the impedance parameters of the signal during rail transmission. Based on this, a rail simulation board can be designed, and a track circuit and broken rail monitoring equipment testing platform can be set up, enabling scientific and efficient testing in the laboratory.

title: Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Model for Wheat Spike Counting
authors: Haiting Wang; Mengbo Jia; Huicheng Yang; Ke Xu; Yaocong Hu; Mengwen Zhang; Jianbin Sang; Wei Chen
abstract: Predicting wheat yield based on wheat spike images is highly significant for breeding, cultivation, and agricultural production. Counting the number accurately of wheat spikes per unit area is a crucial component in monitoring yield. A novel approach utilizing a deep convolutional neural network with multi-scale feature fusion for the automatic localization and regression of wheat spike counting is proposed. Initially, the point labeling-based P2Pnet (Point-to-Point Network) is employed as the backbone to construct the basic counting framework. Furthermore, considering the variation in the size of wheat spikes, multi-scale information is preserved by extracting features from different depth feature layers of the VGG16 network. To tackle the challenge of tiny wheat spikes, a Triplet Attention mechanism is added to the multi-scale feature fusion module, facilitating the interaction of information across the channel, height, and width dimensions to prevent the loss of features from tiny objects during the learning process. Experimental results show that on the public dataset, the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) achieved by the proposed method is 13.827, which is 20.6% lower than that of the basic P2Pnet. Compared with the single-stage object detection algorithm YOLOV5, the MAE is reduced by 9.28%. Compared with the two-stage object detection algorithm Faster R-CNN, the MAE is reduced by 1.24%.

title: Design of an efficient trapping and analysis system for tobacco pests
authors: HAN Shaolong; JIAN Jinling; RAN Baoxin
abstract: The damage of tobacco pests seriously restricts the high quality development of enterprises. The effective pest control is based on accurate and timely monitoring information of the pest, the traditional monitoring process for information of the pest has many problems, such as heavy workload, low efficiency and high error rate. In this paper, an efficient trapping and analysis system is designed, which consists of five modules: tobacco pests trapping, power supply voltage stabilization, image acquisition, wireless communication and image processing, all modules work together to catch tobacco pests automatically, take pictures of the trap board and upload them to the host computer, after image recognition, the number of tobacco pests is calculated, the result can guide us to take effective pest control work. The design of the system has improved the degree of automation and accuracy, reduce the manual workload and work efficiency has also been greatly improved.

title: Reliable Aerial Manipulation: Combining Visual Tracking with Range Sensing for Robust Grasping
authors: Marc Blöchlinger; Yasunori Toshimitsu; Robert K. Katzschmann
abstract: Reliable object localization is a critical challenge in drone-based aerial manipulation, particularly when objects are outside the camera's field of view. This paper presents a new approach to enhance drone reliability in aerial grasping tasks by integrating a 1D time-of-flight range sensor with a vision-based localization system. The range sensor, positioned beneath the drone, generates a detailed point cloud of the ground beneath the drone, allowing for precise object localization even when the drone hovers directly above the target. By combining visual tracking with realtime distance measurements, our system achieves a 96 % grasp success rate across 128 trials with diverse objects, representing a significant improvement over previous approaches. This method enables zero-shot grasping without prior knowledge of the objects, increasing versatility and robustness in complex, unstructured environments. The open-source software and hardware design of the platform provide a foundation for further research and development in the field of autonomous aerial manipulation.

title: Improvement of mobility spectrum algorithm based on Hall measurement
authors: Xin Wang; Ruiqiang Zhou; Ning Yu; Jian He
abstract: Mobility spectrum analysis is a data analysis algorithm based on Hall measurement, which aims to analyze the spectrum of semiconductor carriers. By collecting the semiconductor conductance tensor analysis in the variable magnetic field, the electron and hole transport behavior in the material can be studied. However, the traditional maximum entropy mobility spectrum algorithm has some limitations, such as sensitivity to data noise and uncertainty, and high computational complexity. To solve these problems, this paper proposes two key improvements. Firstly, the entropy information containing probability values is introduced into the change matrix to improve the robustness and accuracy of the algorithm. Secondly, the adaptive step factor is adopted. Through the simulation verification of various situations, the results show that the improved algorithm can not only better deal with noise and uncertainty, but also improve the evaluation indexes such as fitting degree, Gaussian peak parameter and convergence factor under the same number of iterations, which is more meaningful in the material research of semiconductor field.

title: Development of an IoT-Based Robot for Real-Time Customer Satisfaction Monitoring
authors: Lourdes Jullete G. Gumawa; Jeanbe A. Lomugdang; Allen Gem E. Bermejo; Glenda S. Guanzon; Adha Theza Naputol; Jopearlson Icy Ituriaga
publication_title: 2025 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on [::Robotics::] and Technologies for Industrial [::Automation::] (ROBOTHIA)
abstract: This research presents the development of an IoT-based robot for real-time customer satisfaction monitoring. The study aimed to monitor the parameters such as clients' feedback and response time for real-time customer satisfaction analytics. It addresses traditional methods' existing challenges, such as time-consuming data collection, manual tabulation, offline updating, and viewing feedback summary results. Prototyping method was followed to design the circuits, assemble materials, create program codes, conduct testing, and implementation. The materials used are a 7-inch Nextion Screen Display, a microcontroller, a cloud server, fans, servo motors, and a speaker. The testing results showed that the system average response time from user data input of 1000 to cloud web server screen output was 0.39 milliseconds, with the highest of 0.95 milliseconds, and the lowest of 0.21 milliseconds. While the implementation results showed that the overall real-time customer satisfaction rating for each department is 93.27%, and 89.67% for the accounting office, and the registrar office, respectively, which are both exemplary based on the CSAT score. The average response time for accounting is 0.54 milliseconds for 139 clients, while for registrar, the average response time is 0.48 milliseconds for 141 clients. Integrating IoT technology into customer satisfaction monitoring system provides continuous real-time data collection and data analytics, and engaging experience leading to higher feedback data to measure satisfaction levels and quality of services.

title: A Joint Torque Sensor Based on Strain Gauge for Collaborative Robot
authors: Liangjie Tao; Miao Liu; Jin Li; Guangcan Jin
abstract: Collaborative robots require the information of external forces applied to the robot body for collision safety and precise operation. Joint torque sensors mounted between the speed reducer and the link can serve this purpose. The torsional sensitivity of the torque sensor is an important consideration in its design because the low sensitivity of the sensors adversely affects the overall sensitivity of the robot. In this study, torque sensors of various shapes with identical torque sensitivity were designed and the sensor sensitivity was investigated through simulations. Based on the simulations, it is designed to be able to diagnose the sensor state in the signal amplifier through the Whitston bridge output.

title: Basic Study on Improvement of Interior Sound for Ultra-compact EV by Masking Including 1/f Fluctuation
authors: Taro Kato; Takuya Kitamura; Fumiya Maehara; Hiroya Nakayama; Keigo Ikeda; Ayato Endo; Hideaki Kato; Takayoshi Narita
abstract: Ultra-compact electric vehicles (EVs) have advanced characteristics, such as compactness, light body, and low environmental impact. However, interior noise caused by the road and wind is a serious problem. We propose an active noise control (ANC) system for ultra-compact EVs using a giant magnetostrictive actuator. The proposed ANC system has a two-way interior noise control and achieves both noise reduction and masking, depending on the driver. In this study, we investigated the improvement of interior sound by masking considering 1/f fluctuation, which relaxs drivers by providing ride comfort based on their preference. In addition, we proposed a calculation method for 1/f fluctuation, including masking music by a numerical analysis using a Fourier transform. Furthermore, we conducted a real-time analysis of the music including 1/f fluctuation using the short-time Fourier transform and evaluated the relationship between the 1/f fluctuation of the whole music analysis and the appearance rate of 1/f fluctuation.

title: Research on Axle-Hole Assembly Method Based on Improved DDPG Algorithm
authors: Fujun He; Xiaozheng Wang; Kai Liu
abstract: In view of the traditional teaching mode on industrial for assembly tasks involved in the attitude control, poor adaptability of assembly process problem such as open-loop control, designing an Improved Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) reinforcement learning algorithm to realize the axle-hole assembly task. This method obtains multi-dimensional information, including the end-effector's posture parameters and the robot joints, adopts the hierarchical reward mechanism function, to train robot searching, positioning and attitude-controlling skills, then finish the assembly position adjustment task; Finally, an improved DDPG algorithm based on improved hierarchical reward and multi-dimensional information is proposed to realize dynamic posture adjustment during robot assembly. We set up an experimental environment based on the Baxter robot in Gazebo simulation software. The experimental results show that, compared with DQN and DDPG algorithm, the improved DDPG algorithm performs well in the final training steps, rewards and success rate. Results compared with the previous two algorithms, the success rate increased by 21.7% and 15.4%. By comparing the changes of state dimension, the experiment further proves that the improved DDPG algorithm has the advantage of dynamically adjusting the pose in the process of axle-hole assembly task.

title: Fault Diagnosis of an Underwater Remotely Operated Vehicle Through Structural Analysis
authors: George K. Fourlas; George C. Karras
abstract: This paper introduces a model-based approach for diagnosing actuator faults in an underwater remote operated vehicle (ROV). The method employs structural analysis techniques to perform diagnosability analysis and to generate residuals, aiming to detect actuator faults at an early stage and issue timely warnings. To achieve this objective, we construct the mathematical model of the underwater robot, which facilitates the development of the system's structural model. This approach yields parity equations that serve as residual generators. A key advantage of the proposed method is its ability to provide practical solutions for residual generation in nonlinear systems. The CUSUM algorithm is used to detect changes in residual signals. The underwater remote operated vehicle BlueROV2 serves as the robotic platform for experimentation.

title: Alternating Aeration Control And Optimization In Activated Sludge Processes
authors: Ioana Naşcu; Gabriel Harja; Mihai Stanese; Ioan Naşcu
abstract: The optimization and control of wastewater treatment plants is a very important and challenging issue in modern society. Model based control strategies are developed to control the aeration of an intermittently operated municipal wastewater treatment plant. A hierarchical control framework with two layers is implemented where the lower layer ensures the intermittent aeration sequencing by maintaining the aeration fraction coefficient at the value provided by the optimization level and uses a PID controller to control the concentration of the dissolved oxygen. The higher level uses a model predictive control algorithm to determine the optimal value for the aeration fraction of the aeration cycle. Compared to traditional control systems, the new control techniques exhibit good performances for both setpoint tracking and disturbance rejection within the imposed constraints as well as maintaining the aeration fraction within its constraints.

title: Research on Signal Processing Algorithm of Step Excitation Electromagnetic Flowmeter Based on Slurry Noise Analysis
authors: Bin Li; Yue Yan; Jie Chen
abstract: Electromagnetic flowmeter will be interfered by slurry noise during slurry measurement. This paper analyzes the randomness and 1/f characteristics of slurry noise, and studies the influence of flow rate, sand-to-water mass ratio and excitation frequency on slurry noise characteristics. In order to reduce the influence of slurry noise, this paper compares and analyzes several smoothing filtering algorithms of slurry flow signal based on step excitation electromagnetic flowmeter. Through flow measurement experimental device, the comparative experiment of steady-state volatility and dynamic response speed of different algorithms has been carried out. Experiments show that moving average median smoothing algorithm has the best comprehensive filtering performance.

title: Study on a method for detecting and tracking multiple traffic signals at the same time using YOLOv7 and SORT object tracking
authors: Quan Pham Hong; Thien Nguyen Luong; Tung Pham Xuan; Manh Tran Duc; Ngoc Pham Van Bach; Tuan Pham Minh; Tuyen Bui Trong; Hoang Le Huy
abstract: Improving transportation safety and efficiency is currently a top priority worldwide. With the increasing use of autonomous vehicles, it is crucial to develop real-time traffic sign monitoring systems to assist self-driving cars in recognizing and making safe decisions on the road. However, detecting and tracking multiple traffic signs poses challenges due to variations in numbers, sizes, and colors, especially when there are similar warning contents. Therefore, the development of a real-time traffic sign monitoring system using advanced image recognition technology is highly significant. This study introduces the utilization of the YOLOv7 model combined with SORT object tracking to simultaneously track multiple traffic signals. The focus is on a system that provides speed limits for self-driving cars based on different types of signs, such as R.120 and P.127, placed closely together. The YOLOv7 model will be used for sign recognition, while SORT object tracking assigns individual IDs to track the signs. Based on each specific case, the maximum speed for self-driving cars will be determined. This method will greatly benefit self-driving cars in detecting multiple traffic signs in real-time.

title: Artificial Enhanced Image Inpainting for Broadband SMM
authors: Markus F. Wieghaus; Warda Saeed; Muhammad Yasir
publication_title: 2024 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Scanning probe microscopy techniques changed the understanding of micro and nanometer scaled objects. Since the invention of the scanning tunneling microscope and the atomic force microscope, these techniques were further developed and combined with different measurement methodologies such as scanning microwave microscopy. By introducing an electromagnetic signal in the microwave frequency range via the scanning probe microscope tip to the sample, electromagnetic characteristics of the specimen can be acquired. Using a series of frequencies in one scan, even more information like dopant concentration or different layers of material can be captured. The drawback of this method is the long data acquisition time, which cannot be neglected on nanometer scale. To address this issue, we are using reduced raster scan techniques with broadband scanning microwave microscopy and calculate the missing data information by using image inpainting algorithms afterwards. In this work we will present the development of a deep learning algorithm and compare the output of it with different inpainting algorithms, which can even be used in other scanning probe microscope setups.

title: Human-Robot Interaction in Multi-Robotic System Frameworks for Industrial and Other Applications
authors: Balasubramaniyan Chandrasekaran
publication_title: 2025 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on [::Robotics::] and Technologies for Industrial [::Automation::] (ROBOTHIA)
abstract: In this paper, a review of some of the human robot interaction techniques used in multi-robot systems is presented. The knowledge gained from this review will help in understanding and development of an interface for human-robot interaction for the multi-robotic framework for field or environment monitoring. This is research in progress.

title: Development of a 3 DoF Underactuated Robotic Finger
authors: Yau Shin Ru; Jamaludin Jalani; Amirul Syafiq Sadun
abstract: This paper introduces the design and evaluation of a three-degree-of-freedom (3 DoF) underactuated robotic finger, inspired by the 3-Finger Adaptive Robot Gripper by ROBOTIQ. The proposed design utilizes a single DC servo motor to drive multiple joints, simplifying the actuation system while ensuring adaptability in diverse grasping scenarios. Its underactuated mechanism dynamically adjusts to object geometries, enabling versatile and efficient manipulation. The performance of the robotic finger was assessed through experimental testing using MATLAB Simulink. Calibration methods were implemented to align the system's response with desired input, significantly improving precision and reliability. The results demonstrate the system's potential applications in prosthetics, industrial automation, and robotics, offering a cost-effective and robust solution for tasks requiring adaptive manipulation. This work contributes to advancing robotic gripper technology by achieving a balance between simplicity, functionality, and adaptability.

title: Biomimetic Goat Leg Robot Leg Configuration Kinematic Analysis
authors: Zitian Zheng; Qionghua Xia; Zhengyong Feng
abstract: Bipedal robots are inherently poorly self-stabilizing mechanisms. To enhance stability and achieve high-level dynamic control, it is necessary to refine the mechanism design, which often leads to an increase in degrees of freedom, thereby complicating the kinematic and dynamic models. This paper analyzes the dynamic model of a newly designed bipedal robot inspired by the legs of a bionic sheep. Each leg of the robot has 5 degrees of freedom, forming an 8-joint serial-parallel hybrid mechanism. Based on the D-H parameter modeling, taking the right leg as an example, forward and inverse kinematics are solved for the robot, and the model is tested. The results show that the robot exhibits good walking capability in a simulation environment, confirming the feasibility of the overall design.

title: Swin Transformer Encoder and Local Attention Network Via Transfer Learning Strategy for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
authors: Jiacheng Yun; Yang Li
abstract: The effective segmentation of retinal blood vessels is an important means for diagnosis of fundus diseases. However, recent segmentation methods often ignore the global dependence of retinal blood vessels and have poor segmentation capability to small blood vessels. In addition, these methods are trained on limited datasets, resulting in a weak generalization ability. To solve these problems, we propose a new method based on Swin Transformer encoder and local attention network. First, Swin Transformer is used as an encoder to extract the global dependence of retinal blood vessels which can improve the continuity of blood vessels in segmentation results. Then, a local attention network based on edge detection module and coordinate attention module is developed to enhance the segmentation ability of the method to small blood vessels. Finally, a transfer learning strategy is also utilized in this paper. The encoder of our proposed method is pre-trained on ADE20K to enhance the generalization ability. Our proposed method is evaluated on three retinal image datasets: DRIVE, STARE and CHASE_DB1. The results demonstrate that the method proposed in this paper has better performance than others.

title: Offensive Text Detection on Social Media Using Machine Learning
authors: Jesslyn Tanuwijaya; Ivan Sebastian Edbert; Hans Christian Arinardi; Derwin Suhartono
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Control & [::Automation::]; Electronics; [::Robotics::]; Internet of Things; and Artificial Intelligence (CERIA)
abstract: People are social creatures, people of all ages use social media to engage with one another. But not everything that circulates on social media is suitable for all ages; some content, such hate speech, bullying, and cursing, can be harmful to users' mental and physical health. Thus, the necessity for a social media content filtering tool arises. To solve this problem, the researcher proposed a model to classify English tweets by implementing machine learning algorithms specifically Random Forest Classifier, SVM, XGboost, Logistic Regression were used to detect and classify offensive text messages. In this case, dataset were extracted by using countvectorizer algorithm, the researchers also apply data cleaning to remove stop words, punctuation, url and prefix that come from the dataset. Because the imbalance of the dataset the researchers try to fix by using undersampling technique. The best result of the experiments are Random Forest Classifier perform 0.8808 accuracy.

title: Modeling the structure of efficiency indicators in railway station management
authors: Robert Ranosz; Barbara Kowal; Tomasz Moś; Zbigniew Jancewicz
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The authors attempted to build a structure of efficiency indicators for managing railway station assets. The study aims to answer the following research question: how to model the structure of performance indicators for railway station management? This study focuses on the station and the assets of the Premium station. The article proposes a general model for calculating Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), which, when supplied with data, will enable a unified comparative assessment of station asset management at various railway stations.

title: Hierarchical Decomposition and Prescribed Performance Bound based Adaptive Control for Leader-Follower Formation of Uncertain Nonholonomic Mobile Robots
authors: Jiajun Shen; Wei Wang; Jinhu Lü; Chao Deng
abstract: In this paper, the cooperative formation control problem is investigated for multiple two-wheeled mobile robots with unknown parameters. By combining the hierarchical decomposition and prescribed performance bound (PPB) technique, distributed adaptive formation controllers are designed based on dynamic surface control. It is proved in the Lyapunov sense that all the closed-loop signals are semi-globally bounded and the tracking error converges to a compact set, which can be made arbitrarily small by adjusting the design parameters appropriately. Furthermore, formation maintenance, connectivity preservation and collision avoidance can be achieved with the proposed control scheme. Simulations are also given to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Mobile Robot Navigation in Unknown Environments
authors: Benpeng Huang; Jianliang Mao; Chuanlin Zhang
abstract: Efficient and safe autonomous navigation of mobile robots in dynamic and unknown environments remains a central challenge in robotic navigation. Most traditional path-planning methods rely on prior map information and perform poorly in complex, map-less scenarios with multiple moving obstacles and randomized goal positions. Although reinforcement learning can partially address these issues, it still suffers from sparse rewards and low sample efficiency. In this paper, we propose a hybrid navigation framework that integrates velocity obstacles (VO) priors with soft actor-critic (SAC) reinforcement learning to enhance training sample efficiency and convergence speed. At the same time, we leverage the dynamic window approach (DWA) to assist in reward function design, alleviating sparse-reward problems, and employ curriculum learning to guide the agent from simple to complex tasks. We validate our approach in the PyBullet simulation environment, and results show that, compared to both traditional reinforcement learning and classical path-planning algorithms, our method delivers significant improvements in safety, efficiency, and robustness.

title: Target Localization Method for Underwater Robots Based on Synthetic Aperture
authors: Yuzhe Wang; Ming Xu; Chun Li; Guobing Di; Zhun Li; Hao Li
abstract: The article proposes a method for locating sound sources using a single hydrophone on an underwater robot that varies its depth vertically. By equipping the underwater robot with a single hydrophone and changing depth at a constant speed, multiple virtual short-aperture subarrays are synthesized. The direction information of the sound source is obtained using a beamforming algorithm, and then the location of the target is calculated based on the depth of the synthetic array. Simulation experiments were conducted to locate the classic calls of marine mammals, validating the method's feasibility. The simulation results show that this algorithm can accurately locate targets several kilometers away.

title: A Branching Network for Human Parsing Based on Quantifying Background-Part Relationships *
authors: Tao Yang; Juan Du
abstract: Human parsing is a critical computer vision task that involves segmenting and labeling body parts in images. Due to variations in human poses and clothing, designing effective parsing algorithms is challenging. This paper examines how background impacts parsing results and proposes grouping body parts based on mutual information with the background. We introduce an end-to-end replacement-concatenation network to enhance existing methods and a branching network that refines feature sharing to reduce negative interactions and improve feature learning for different body parts. Experimental results show a significant improvement in parsing effectiveness using our approach.

title: Learning to Modulate Action of Deterministic Policy for Autonomous Navigation
authors: Xin Chen; Ke Zhu; Jianming Zhang
abstract: Unmanned mobile robots are widely used in un-known environments, where the exact overall arrangement of environments may not be available. This paper investigates navigation strategy for mobile robots based on reinforcement learning method to allow mobile robots to navigate in such environments. Deterministic policy gradient algorithm has recently been shown to be effective in complex tasks. However, deterministic policy may not be safe to solve navigation problem in unknown environments due to its determinacy. We propose a learning framework composed of dual policy networks, in which one of the policies acts as a tuner for the other. Multiple simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework implicitly learns key navigation ability and is more efficient than baseline method.

title: Research on fire protection system based on deep learning
authors: Tiannian Zhou; Ping Liang; Zhi Zhang; Zhiyong Dai; Guangqi Li; Hongyuan Guo
abstract: Flame detection systems are becoming more and more important in firefighting, and for indoor large space occasions, this paper designs a firefighting system based on computer vision. Combining the knowledge of mass kinematics and fluid dynamics, the trajectory of the firefighting water cannon jet is deduced, and the effect of different parameter conditions on the trajectory is analyzed using MATLAB simulation. The yolov4 flame detection model is trained to achieve accurate detection of the flame, and the coordinate value of the flame center position relative to the upper-left corner of the image is calculated at the same time. Then the horizontal turning angle required for the rotation of the fire gun is calculated according to the coordinate value, and the monocular visual localization technology is used to realize the localization of the fire source in the actual space, and the horizontal distance from the camera to the fire source is calculated. Substituting the horizontal distance into the jet trajectory algorithm can get the pitch angle of the fire cannon under the corresponding range.

title: Development of Switching Power Module Based on SKHI 10/17 Driver
authors: Kai Rao
abstract: In the experimental device of nuclear fusion, DC energy is injected into the secondary heating system by high-voltage power supply to improve the plasma temperature. Because the secondary heating system mostly uses klystron and neutral beam as the load, the output of the power supply should be meet the requirement of the load. The rising and falling edge of the high-voltage pulse power supply is short, the ripple is small and the stray energy storage of the system is small. The high-voltage pulse power supply based on step modulation technology is adopted as the main high-voltage power supply of the secondary heating system by researching the power supply used for the same type of load at home and abroad. This high-voltage power supply is used by several same switching power supplies in series, and high-voltage output can be obtained through by adjusting the delay time and duty cycle modulation, which has a good performance. According to the output parameter of single power supply 100A/850V, the Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) module of 200A/1700V made by SEMIKRON is selected as the switch, and it is driven by the SKHI 10/17 driver. The rising time and falling time of the IGBT and power supply can be adjusted by adjusting the driving resistance.

title: Sampling-with-Path based Planning: Easing Non-Holonomic Mobile Manipulator Motion Planning
authors: Qilong Yuan
abstract: In mobile manipulator motion planning, typical sampling-based methods have difficulty in (1) solving the planning problem fast. (2) finding a path with high quality. (3) maintaining the non-holonomic constraint along the path. This paper firstly proposes to solve the general non-holonomic planning problem based on sampling with various connection paths between the samples with constraint satisfied, which enables typical planners such as RRT, RRT*, RRT-Connect, PRM, etc., to be able to solve mobile manipulation motion planning with differential drive constraints. Meanwhile, with proper sampling and activating alternative paths added to connect state pairs, it is proved that the rate of valid connectable state samples significantly increases and this also contributes in improving the planner efficiency and success rate. Simulation experiments have been conducted through MoveIt! with differential-drive based UR5e robot in environments with obstacles. Results show that the proposed method has the highest success rates against four existing planners. In general, the planner generates faster solutions with better path quality in all five experiment scenarios, useful in achieving responsive real-time mobile manipulation behavior in daily applications.

title: Energy Efficiency Optimization of CCHP Microgrid Energy Hub with Multiple Scenario Model
authors: Ruichun Wu; Lintong Wang; Haiba Xu; Xueyan Wang; Chouwei Ni; Yitian Hong
abstract: This paper investigates energy efficiency optimization of Combined Cooling Heating and Power (CCHP) microgrid energy hub with multiple scenario model. To start with, the interfaces of the energy hub according to the form of energy conversion are studied. Then, according to the established bus-type integration model, this paper proposes the corresponding specific models of the energy hub according to different user requirements. Based on the multiple scenario model with aiming at maximizing the energy efficiency coefficient of the civilian energy hub, energy efficiency optimization of CCHP microgrid is investigated. Finally, the model and algorithm are verified by simulation based on a typical example. It is revealed that due to the multiple energy hubs for CCHP microgrid, the energy complementarity between regions can be realized, reducing the investment cost of a single energy hub and improving the overall energy utilization rate.

title: Revolutionizing Endangered Species Conservation: Employing Synthetic Satellite Data to Monitor and Protect Polar Bears
authors: Justin Q Chen; Benjamin Rhodes-Kropf
abstract: The polar bear (Ursus maritimus), a keystone species of the Arctic, holds immense importance for animal conservation and climate change efforts. Most traditional methods for tracking polar bear populations, which involve direct observation, can be logistically challenging and expensive in distant regions like the Arctic. We propose a novel approach to monitoring the species by generating and using synthetic satellite imagery to train artificial intelligence (AI) to identify polar bears from space. We leverage the 3D computer graphics software Blender to produce synthetic datasets of satellite images that accurately model the characteristics and environments of polar bears. We then train YOLO object detection models on these datasets. By varying the ground sampling distance (GSD) of the synthetic datasets, we determine the satellite image resolution required for polar bear identification. Our results suggest that our approach can accurately identify polar bears on publicly available satellite hardware. Additionally, the YOLO model identified polar bears in real aerial images with backgrounds extremely dissimilar from the training set, demonstrating its ability to generalize polar bear identification beyond the type of satellite images it was trained on. Models trained on synthetic images of lower GSD values generally showed better identification performance, achieving accuracies as high as 96.17%. Our approach can also be easily adapted to monitor other wildlife species and revolutionize many environmental and conservation efforts.

title: Measurement Based on Image Processing on Air Resistance Characteristics of Skiing in Wind Tunnel Experiment
authors: Jin Song; Sheng Xu; Weiguo Zhang; Dong Li; Yu Lan; Bei Liu
abstract: In order to study the characteristics of air resistance experienced by skier, an experimental method has been developed in the wind tunnel. While measuring the air resistance of skier by balance, the windward projected area of skier is obtained by image acquisition and processing, and then the corresponding resistance coefficient is calculated. The skier simulated different postures in the wind tunnel and obtained the data of each posture. The experimental result shows that the air resistance and resistance coefficient decrease as the human body changes from standing to squatting, and the resistance characteristic of the half squatting is the most stable and the resistance coefficient is small. This method can provide reference and basis for guiding training.

title: Roll-motion stabilizer design for a sounding rocket using the ADRC methodology
authors: Natalia Wiśniewska; Andrzej Rafalski; Maciej Marcin Michałek
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: A high roll rate can decrease the chance of the research-oriented rocket mission success. There is scant information about the effective roll-motion stabilizer solutions for sounding rockets. Thus, a roll-motion stabilizer for a sounding rocket using the active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) methodology is proposed. The presented roll-motion stabilizer is designed for a subsonic sounding rocket. An effectiveness of the designed control system was verified by simulations and experiments in a wind tunnel. Results of the verification show that the designed control system enables robust roll-motion stabilization despite large uncertainty of a rocket model. Practical guidelines for designing of the roll-motion stabilizer are provided.

title: High Load-to-Weight Ratio and Large-Deformation Vacuum Pneumatic Actuator
authors: Meiru Ye; Xiang Qian
abstract: The potential of artificial muscles is becoming increasingly evident in a number of fields, including robotics, prosthetics, and wearable devices. However，there is still a need to develop a soft actuator that is lightweight, compact and has a high load-to-weight ratio.We designed, manufactured, modeled and tested modular contracting actuators which achieves remarkable deformations exceeding 80% while supporting loads up to 4 kg. With a load-to-weight ratio of 455 and an energy conversion efficiency of 20.5% under a 1 kg load. The actuator stands out in performance. It is driven by negative pressure, offering significantly higher safety compared to actuators driven by positive pressure or other methods like electrical, thermal, or chemical means. Our fabrication process is both rapid and cost-effective. Additionally, we present a theoretical model to explain and predict the actuator's motion. Benefiting from its unprecedented modularity and high performance, this actuator is poised for practical applications in fields such as healthcare and industrial production.

title: Analysis of the Performance of an Omnidirectional Bionic Leg
authors: Yuze Xu; Jianzhong Shang; Shanjun Chen; Minghai Xia; Yiming Zhu; Zirong Luo
abstract: Inspired by the structure of the human leg, a bionic leg with the constant posture of the endpoint and capable of omnidirectional legged locomotion is proposed. The structural layout of the bionic leg is introduced. The flexibility of the leg mechanism is analyzed using the condition number of the Jacobian matrix as a performance index. The static model of the leg mechanism is developed based on the virtual work principle. The bearing capacity performance index and the force equilibrium performance index are established by the vector extremum method. Furthermore, the static performance of the leg mechanism is analyzed. In order to verify the applied feasibility and the performance of omnidirectional legged locomotion, the motion simulation of the quadruped robot based on the proposed design is carried out as it moves along seven different directions. A prototype is developed to serve as the foundation for the next phase in the improvement and practical implementation of omnidirectional bionic legs.

title: An AMR Mapping Method based on High Efficiency Recursive Filtering Fusion Algorithm
authors: Xudong Liu; Junfei Lu; Yuanze Gui; Yi Yang
abstract: An AMR mapping method is proposed based on a high-efficiency recursive filtering fusion algorithm. Specifically, this method utilizes the extended kalman filter to combine the data of the mileage measurement and the inertial measurement unit with the lidar calibration, which improves the accuracy of the initial attitude value and solves the problem of high computational complexity, poor real-time performance, and inaccurate attitude estimation at subsequent moments. Physical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method, and the comparison results with the original algorithm are given.

title: Analysis of Electric Field on the Surface of Fittings and Main Equipment Inside ± 800kV UHV Converter Valve Hall Based on the Finite Element Analysis
authors: Jing Wang; Guohua Yang; Wei Zhang; Yue Zhao; Ruonan Hu; Wenwei Li; Yanan Wu; Yaoguang Yang; Bo He
abstract: The valve hall in a UHV converter station serves as the hub of a UHV DC transmission project. When operating normally, it adheres to rigorous standards concerning the surface electric field of its internal fittings. Consequently, during the design phase of the valve hall, it is crucial to calculate and validate the electric field strength on the surface of these fittings to guarantee that it remains beneath the corona field strength for each piece of equipment. In this paper, the simulation calculation of the high-end valve hall fittings of a UHV DC transmission project ± 800kV converter station is carried out. The numerical calculation method of the surface electric field of the UHV DC valve hall fittings is studied. The whole model of the valve hall equipment is established to calculate and analyze the electric field. The distribution characteristics of the surface electric field when the valve hall equipment is working are obtained, and the maximum surface field strength of each fitting in the valve hall is found. Analyze whether it is dizzy, study the distribution law of its surface field strength, and check the performance of shielding fittings.

title: Impact of Volume Constraint and Weighting Factors of the Electric Field on Topology Optimization of Electrodes: Application to Dielectrophoresis (DEP)-Based Devices
authors: Abdenbi Mohand-Ousaid; Abdullah Abdelraheem; Abbas Homayouni-Amlashi; Aude Bolopion
publication_title: 2025 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: The shape of electrodes is a key design parameter in dielectrophoresis (DEP)-based devices, directly influencing the DEP forces induced by applied voltage to the electrodes. These forces find application in medical therapy devices, particularly in tasks such as cell manipulation, sorting and separation. In these applications, it is essential to control the direction and the magnitude of the DEP forces. To address this challenge, this paper proposes to use topology optimization to design the shape of the electrodes. Building upon our previous research, we investigate the influence of the volume fraction constraint and the weighting factors of the electric field components along <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> axes on the resulting electrode layouts and their corresponding DEP force performances. To this purpose, a case study has been defined as trapping particles inside a desired convergence zone in a fluid stream inside a microchannel. A series of numerical simulations were conducted to evaluate the influence of the volume constraint and weighting factors. The results show that for each set of parameters the methodology enables the generation of electrode layouts that effectively direct the DEP forces to trap the targeted particles. Beyond this, The results show that, for this type of problem, it is not advantageous to impose a volume constraint. The optimization process implicitly identifies the volume that achieves the best trade-off between material distribution and DEP forces.

title: Adaptive Online-Trained RBFNN-Aided Super-Twisting Slide Mode Control for Servo Systems under Uncertainties
authors: TengDa Zhan; YiFei Wu
abstract: Suppressing disturbances while improving control accuracy in servo motors remains a major challenge, especially under the influence of strong external perturbations and un-certainties. This paper proposes an adaptive gain composite sliding mode control method with a Radial Basis Neural Network (RBFNN) chattering compensator. The proposed approach lever-ages an adaptive gain composite control strategy to effectively counteract external disturbances and enhance the precision of servo control. In addition, an online-trained Radial Basis neural network is employed to mitigate the chattering typically observed in sliding mode control. Comparative experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces control chattering while improving tracking accuracy under external interference, outperforming conventional sliding mode control methods.

title: Acoustic Emission Signal Characteristics Extraction Based on Improved EMD Method for Industrial Robot Body
authors: Shishang Dong; Shuai Qiao; Hao Zhang; Shi Gong; Ming Li; Xuechao Yuan
abstract: In order to explore the transmission characteristics of acoustic emission (AE) signals in industrial robot body, the Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) method is applied to decompose the AE waveform, and the characteristics of AE signals are analyzed by time-frequency domain analysis. The simulative AE signal generated by pencil-lead breaking was initially acquired using the DS5 acoustic emission instrument with a 3 MHz sampling frequency. Furthermore, the AE signal was analyzed by CEEMDAN to obtain various layers of the Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMF) component, followed by calculation of weight, correlation coefficient, and variance contribution ratio of the original signal. The reconstruction was then utilized to reconstruct the aforementioned AE signal waveform, and the FFT analysis was introduced to analyze the frequency domain characteristics of the reconstructed signal. The findings indicate that the AE signal generated by interior and exterior surface of the body ranges from 144 kHz to 170 kHz and 122 kHz to 155 kHz, respectively. Those results suggest that the surface coating of the industrial robot has an un-negligible impact on the transmission of the AE signal.

title: Design and Modeling of an Amphibious Quad-Rotor for in-Pipeline Inspection
authors: Petar Durdevic; Shaobao Li; Daniel Ortiz-Arroyo
publication_title: 2025 29th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This paper presents the modeling and design of Hybrid Unmanned Aerial Float Vehicle (HUAFV), an amphibious quadcopter integrating quadcopter dynamics with a floating platform, controlled by a PI controller for in-pipeline inspections. Experimental validation demonstrates the HUAFV's performance with a translational rise time of 5.13 s, a peak time of 10.14 s, and a settling time of 71.35 s in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex> direction. For rotational motion in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\psi$</tex> angle, the rise time is 0.4452 s, the peak time is 0.6988 s, and the settling time is 5.06 s. Our experimental results confirm the HUAFV's stability and efficiency, establishing its potential for effective in-pipeline inspections.

title: A Simplified Model for the Secular Dynamics of a Parametrically-Excited Magnetic Micro-Particle
authors: S. Aditya; G. R. Jayanth; A. K. Mohanty
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: Magnetic micro-particles find numerous applications as the end-effectors in micro-manipulation technologies. A recent micro-manipulation technology proposed the use of micro-ring actuators and parametric excitation to trap magnetic particles in three-dimensions (3-D). Here, a simplified linear time-invariant system model is proposed to describe the secular dynamics of such particles. First, the exact dynamic equations are obtained for the case of a particle oriented upwards and the procedure to obtain their approximate solution is described. The obtained approximate response is employed to subsequently propose a simple linear time-invariant system model for the secular dynamics of the particle. Next, the same approach is extended for the case of a magnetic particle with arbitrary orientation. In both cases the results of the simplified model are compared with numerical solutions of the exact system equations. The two are found to match with an accuracy of over 99.6%.

title: Controlling and programming a robot using virtual reality
authors: Maksymilian Gorzelak; Tomasz Grzejszczak
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The paper presents software that allows a user to control and program a robot using virtual reality. The user will be equipped with a Virtual Reality kit and will be able to use it to manipulate the robot arm as if they were physically interacting with it. One key feature of the software will be the ability to set the robot in a specific position, allowing the user to create and execute complex movement sequences for the robot to follow. The use of VR technology in this context offers a unique and immersive way for users to interact with and program the robot, making it an exciting and innovative approach to robotic control.

title: A Geometrical Criterion for the Synchronization of Dynamic Networks with Input Saturation
authors: Juncen Ye; Haoyi Que; Longhua Ma; Ming Xu; Hongye Su
abstract: The paper investigated the global synchronization control problem of dynamic networks with discrete-time communications and input saturation. Based on a geometrical criterion of certain non-linear non-autonomous systems, we proposed a sufficient condition for stability of saturating linear control for a linear networked system. The stability could be ensured simply from a range of gains rather than a complex Lyapunov function. A numerical example is offered to show the effectiveness and the relative analysis.

title: Research and Design of an Intelligent Strawberry Picking Robot Based on STM32 and Color Sensor Technology
authors: Xiang Pan; Chun Luo; Yuru Zheng; Zhengyi Hou; Awen Ma
abstract: With the economic boom, strawberry cultivation has flourished in China. However, the repetitive and labor-intensive nature of strawberry harvesting poses challenges. To address this, we designed a strawberry harvesting robot incorporating strawberry recognition, harvesting, transportation, and packaging. The robot utilizes STM32 and color sensors for intelligent recognition of ripe strawberries. Its mechanical arm grasps the strawberries and deposits them into a box. The sensor system adjusts the distance between the robot and the target, enabling precise maneuvering. This robot addresses issues like high labor costs, low efficiency, and complex machine structures, revolutionizing strawberry harvesting.

title: Research on modeling method of Globoidal Cam mechanism
authors: Zhenghao Ge; Qiujie Zhao; Jiawei Li
abstract: Taking the globoidal CAM mechanism as the research object, this paper deduces the calculation equation of globoidal CAM contour surface and pressure Angle, and summarizes the general motion law of globoidal CAM follower. On this basis, the design software of globoid CAM is developed to realize the globoid CAM mechanism, including globoid indexing CAM, globoid deceleration CAM, globoid CAM with oscillating roller follower, as well as the contour data output of ATC multi-head globoid CAM, cutter position processing data output, and the verification of mechanism pressure Angle. Finally, ATC multi-head cambered mechanism is taken as an example to realize the establishment of its model and kinematic simulation, and the rationality of the design is verified.

title: EC-5G: Edge Computing-Aware 5G Heterogeneous Networks
authors: Md. Shamrat Apu Gazi; Mobasshir Mahbub; Mir Md. Saym; Md. Abdur Rouf
abstract: 5G is a cellular network of the advanced generation which aims at dramatically boost service quality, such as better capacity and lower latency. The edge computing infrastructure is emergent and allows 5G to grow by the proximity of cloud resources to end-users (gadgets) so that the underlying issues of current cloud issues such as high latency and lack of security can be solved. This paper offers an overview of the advance edge computing technologies in 5G focused on aims, computational frameworks, features, 5G tasks, performance measures, and responsibilities, and includes taxonomy of 5G edge computing. Other relevant issues are also highlighted, including key criteria for efficient adoption of 5G and edge computing implementations of 5G. The authors then focused on the new advances in edge computing for 5G. This shows the excellent characteristics of numerous 5G edge computing paradigms. Finally, research issues regarding EC-5G are highlighted.

title: MarineSwin-DETR: A Frequency-Adaptive and Dynamic Histogram Attention Fusion Framework for Marine Small Object Detection
authors: Yaoyao Ran; Shijun Sun; Yihong Zhang
abstract: With the rapid development of remote sensing technology, the demand for accurate detection of small targets on the sea surface is increasingly urgent in the field of maritime monitoring. However, complex sea conditions such as strong solar flares, dynamic reflection of waves, and non-uniform illumination lead to three core challenges for traditional detection methods, namely, the lack of small target features, pseudo-target interference, and dynamic deformation. To this end, this study proposes the MarineSwin-DETR innovation framework, which mainly includes the following two innovations. Frequency domain Adaptive Dilated Convolution (FADC) module: By dynamically adjusting the dilation rate and kernel weight, the high-frequency details of multi-scale features are preserved and the low-frequency background is suppressed. Dynamic Range Histogram Self-attention (DHSA) mechanism is used to reconstruct the attention distribution based on the intensity bucketing strategy, which effectively solves the contrast degradation problem under high dynamic illumination. Experiments on the SeaDronesSee dataset show that the proposed model achieves 84.6% mAP@0.5 at a computational cost of 55.0 GFLOPs, which is 2.2 percentage points higher than the baseline model RT-DETR r18, and the detection accuracy of small objects such as life-saving equipment is improved by 9.5%-10.1%. This result provides a solution with both high accuracy and low power consumption for real-time target detection in complex sea conditions.

title: Integrating 3Ds Max with Robot Technology: A Case Study on the Robot Palletizer System
authors: Epiphania Caroline Ponde; Lei Zhang; Binrui Wang; Xiaohua Shi; Fei Chang
abstract: This paper explores the integration of 3Ds Max, a powerful 3D modelling and animation software with robot technology using a robot palletizer system as a reference framework. The main problem addressed is the lack of effective methods to evaluate robotic systems' functionality and enable optimization before robot physical installation. To overcome this challenge, 3D Max simulations are proposed to enable virtual prototyping thus providing comprehensive evaluations of the performance of robotic systems. The research has developed a robot palletizer system simulation that can serve as a training platform for engineers and clients, allowing them to familiarize themselves with the robot's operation in a safe and controlled setting. The paper contributes to the field of robotics by demonstrating the effectiveness of 3Ds Max simulation for enhanced performance, efficiency, and safety in robotic systems. Furthermore, it emphasizes the importance of further research on leveraging simulation and virtual environments within the context of Industry 4.0 and 5.0.

title: Adaptive control for a class of switched nonlinear systems via event-triggered output feedback
authors: Manman Yuan; Junyong Zhai
abstract: This paper studies the problem of dynamic event-triggered (ET) output feedback (OF) control for switched nonlinear systems (SNSs) with uncertain output function. The considered system allows more general growth restriction. Firstly, to deal with the system uncertainties, a homogeneous observer embedded with a dynamic gain is put forward. Then, an adaptive control scheme under arbitrary switching is presented. It is worth emphasizing that the threshold parameters of the used ET mechanism can be dynamically adjusted. Besides, it is proven that all signals of the closed-loop system are bounded. The effectiveness of the presented method is verified by an illustrative example.

title: Wearable Wheel-legged Device for Load Carriage
authors: Shanjin Zhang; Junfei Wang; Jiyuan Wu; Mengqian Tian; Xingsong Wang; Gang Chen
abstract: In military operations, soldiers often need to carry high-quality combat equipment, which inevitably puts greater pressure on the human body. Studies have shown that high loads and high instantaneous impact forces can cause adverse damage to the musculoskeletal system of the human body. In view of this situation, the wheel leg load device (WLD) designed in this research can effectively improve this problem. In this study, the usefulness of WLD was evaluated. Three volunteers performed five different sets of experiments on a treadmill. Data on the subject’s oxygen consumption and plantar strength during the experiment were collected. According to biomechanical analysis, WLD reduced the peak pressure when the subject was carrying a heavy load, and showed high performance when carrying a high-quality load. In a 20 kg load, oxygen consumption increased by 0.8% for every 1 kg of weight added on the WLD (an average increase of 1%/kg for a 70 kg load); Compared to the backpack’s 1.43%, it shows a great advantage. At the same time, WLD can reduce the instantaneous impact force, which has the effect of reducing the risk of overuse injury.

title: A long-distance small target perception optimization algorithm integrating SRGAN and YOLO
authors: Shuchen Liu; Ningning Ren; Lianqin Jia
abstract: In order to improve the image resolution of long-distance small targets in actual traffic scenes, this study utilized an improved SRGAN reconstruction, which is based on the GAN, and uses the global image feature information extracted by the attention module for image reconstruction, and the image size is normalized on the image pixels, which solves the image reconstruction task. The pixel loss function is constructed to improve the quality of the image by using the robust Charbonnier loss function, At the same time, the traditional YOLO algorithm is improved to lightweight, based on the research results, it can be concluded that, SRGAN and lightweight YOLO algorithms are used to improve the resolution and real-time detection long range targets and small targets, and enhance the perception ability long range targets and small targets in actual traffic scenes.

title: Spatial-Temporal Evidence Combination Method for Multi-sensor Target Recognition Based on Prospect Theory
authors: Zihan Zhang; Zhentao Hu; Junwei Li; Yujie Su
abstract: Evidence theory has been widely used in the field of spatial-temporal information fusion, and since target recognition information fusion exhibits obvious dynamic and sequential characteristics. In order to realize the target recognition information fusion, spatial-temporal evidence is combined based on prospect theory and credibility decay model. Firstly, introducing the prospect value function to evaluate and adjust for evidence credibility, after that, an weight for each spatial evidence can be obtained to achieved the spatial information fusion. Finally, evidence combining by evidence discount criterion and Dempster combination rule to achieve sequential combination of temporal evidence. In this way, judgments for updated data of target recognition are data-driven, and makes more reasonable. The numerical simulation indicate that the proposed method fully reflects the dynamic and sequential characteristics of spatial-temporal evidence combination. Moreover, it has a strong capability to handle conflict information.

title: Investigation of Propeller Control Method Focusing on Reverse Force Input for Collision-Free Arrival Motion of Ship
authors: Yoshinori Mizooka; Hideki Toda
abstract: In this paper, a novel controller design focusing on reverse input using propeller thruster such as air plane taxiing and ship for collision-free arrival motion was proposed and evaluated in mock up model. And ultimately, it is necessary to control the position, attitude and speed at the same time. The operation of docking at a port has not yet been automated by machines, and is known as a special skill that requires the concentration of craftsmen. In our study, to aim at automating accurate docking and berthing operations in ship control, we used an airplane-type model with a propeller, which is relatively easy to test, rather than a test environment using water, where the effects appear three-dimensionally, and the reaching motion characteristics on the ground were investigated. In this process, we focused on the reverse motion often employed when the craftsman controls the ship. We developed two types model devices of ground taxiing airplane and ship, and perform the reaching movement experiment by normal P, PD control and human's visual feedback control also performed. As a result, in order to rapid approach without overshoot, the applied thrust for a constant time period gave relatively good results, and it was possible to control stably even though it was necessary to search for parameters. By comparing with a human control by pressing keyboard button method using a reverse force input, it also relatively good result, and by introducing the human reverse force input way to the thrust for a constant time period method, it could realize rapid and stable controlling. As a basic study, we developed a simple ground taxiing airplane model and U-shaped guided model ship to realize a rapid, non-overshoot and stable reaching movement. The difficulty of the reaching movement would be mainly occurred by propeller / screw type thruster control difficulty, however, by using a human control way of using reverse force input, we found some reaching movement performance improvement even though using a constant time period forward / reverse force input controller.

title: Active Control for Segmented Deployable Ultra-thin Piezoelectric Space Telescope
authors: Dalong Tian; Jianguo Guo; Zhenxin Feng
abstract: For segmented space optical telescopes based on microsatellite platforms, ultra-thin piezoelectric deformable mirror technology is applied for precise shape control to compensate for wavefront errors caused by disturbances, thereby improving the resolution of telescopes and reducing emission volume. First, the layout of the piezoelectric segmented ultra-thin telescope is introduced and analyzed. Second, taking typical optical modes and random shape as tracking targets, control strategies under space loads and disturbances are described. Subsequently, numerical simulations on the shape control performance for different tracking targets are carried out by SVD (Singular Value Decomposition) and DLS (Damped Least Squares) controllers. Finally, optimizations based piezoelectric actuator number and system control parameters are investigated respectively to further improve the tracking capabilities, reduce the voltage range. The research results show that, the active control can significantly reduce the RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) of the tracking target, which is further decreased through optimization of the number of actuators. On the premise of meeting the performance indicators, the voltage difference between actuators can be reduced by the optimization of control parameters. This paper provides an effective reference value for the precise shape control of space optical telescopes.

title: Design and realisation of a construction robot applied to concrete vibration for box girders
authors: Shuai Fan; Tao He; Xiangxiang You; Chuang Zeng; Ye Liang; Chao Li
abstract: The growth of industrial intelligence has led to greater automation in numerous sectors. As robots are becoming increasingly prevalent, companies must confront the essential matter of how to employ them to supplant manual labour, ultimately heightening productivity and efficiency. This paper outlines the development of an automated vibration robot comprising a vertical vibration robot cell, a rail-type inclined insertion vibration robot system, and other cells working in collaboration. This paper uses box girder vibration as the foundational framework and conducts field experiments with an automated vibration robot designed for this purpose. The measurements of concrete strength reveal that the automated vibrating robot meets industrial standards, thus verifying its capacity to perform large-scale construction vibration. The potential for substituting human labour with automated robots in large-scale vibration construction is showcased.

title: MLS: A Meta-Learning Based Stackelberg Model for Robot Trajectory Guidance
authors: Jin Guo; Zhiyong Jiang; Yifan Liu; Lili Gong
abstract: The critical role of trajectory guidance in facilitating follower robots to reach target destinations under the supervision of a leader robot is well-established. However, the complexity of coordinating efficient collaboration increases when a leader must guide a diverse set of followers with unknown specific characteristics. To address this challenge, we propose a novel meta-learning-based Stackelberg approach. We model the guided trajectory planning problem as a dynamic Stackelberg game, capturing the intricate interaction dynamics between the leader and followers. Utilizing meta-learning techniques, the leader learns a meta-best-response model from a selected set of followers. When a follower initiates a guidance request, the leader swiftly adapts to the follower's unique characteristics using a few learning data. This follower-specific model is then used for effective trajectory guidance. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate the superior generalization and adaptability of our proposed method over alternative learning methods, and emphasize the practical value and effectiveness of the guidance mechanism. Our findings underscore the potential of our meta-learning-based Stackelberg approach in addressing collaborative trajectory planning challenges in heterogeneous multi-robot systems.

title: Containment problem for a multi-agent system with heterogeneous delays
authors: Branislav Rehák
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The consensus problem for a multi-agent system with linear agents is considered. The agents may exhibit a time delay, this delay is not required to be equal for each agent. It is shown that different values of the delay may prevent the follower agents to settle in the precise convex hull of the leader agents, however, they converge to a larger set that can be determined using the robust control methods. The results are illustrated by examples.

title: Real-Time Detection of Defective Products of a Tortilla Machine Production Line Using TensorFlow Object Detection API and OpenCV
authors: M D Ashfakul Karim Kausik; Ahamed A. H. Sunny; Rahat K. Bhuiyan; M. H. Bappy; Adib Bin Rashid; C. M. A. Rahman
abstract: This work focuses on the real-time detection of defective products on a production line of a Roti (Flatbread) maker machine. In this research work, an object detection model, SSD-MobileNet-v2 has been used and fine-tuned through transfer learning with the help of a custom dataset. The model is trained for 10,000 steps and demonstrated superior performance, achieving mAP and recall values of 0.9278 and 0.9379 respectively. This defect identification in real-time leads to huge cost savings and human interventions. This is not only beneficial for the food production industry but also holds potential for broader applications in large-scale industries including FMCG products. The integration of these models into production lines offers invaluable tools for ensuring high standards of quality and safety across various sectors.

title: A Nonlinear Model Based on Data-Driven Control for Cascading Failure in Power Grids
authors: Beibei Li; Kefan Song; Linfeng Chen; Aohui Jia
abstract: People’s ability to manipulate complex networks depends on the design of efficient control algorithms, as well as the availability of accurate and operable models of network dynamics. Although the design of network system control algorithms has made significant progress in the past few years, most of them are based on static network research, which is difficult to satisfy in practice. Finding the key nodes in the network plays a decisive role in network cascading failure and fault repair. This paper aims to establish a method for controlling cascade failures driven by nonlinear data in complex power grids. The focus is on minimizing the input nodes of the control system. The model is applied to the simulation network ER, SF and the real network topology of the US Powergrid to verify that it achieves the largest cascading failure of the network under the least node control, so as to effectively predict the cascading failure of the reverse protection network, and effectively quickly repair cascading failures before the system completely crashes.

title: A Lidar-Vision Fusion Target Detection Model for Low-Light Environments
authors: Jing Wang; Shuai Duan; Meng Zhou
abstract: In the field of autonomous driving and specific environments, target detection is a critical task module. Currently, the mainstream approach to target detection is to use deep learning to train specific network models, enabling them to recognize targets. Although many effective network models have been proposed by scholars, there are few target detection networks tailored for low-light environments. In practical applications, complex lighting changes can lead to decreased accuracy in target detection. This paper combines a low-light enhancement network with a LiDAR-camera fusion target detection network to achieve target detection in low-light environments and validates the algorithm using the Nuscenes benchmark dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that the improved network exhibits greater robustness in target detection under complex lighting conditions.

title: Intuitive Robot Path Planning through Augmented Reality
authors: Mohammad-Ehsan Matour; Alexander Winkler
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: In this paper, an approach for intuitive path planning of a collaborative robot (cobot) based on augmented reality (AR) is presented. For this purpose, a user interface is developed that offers practical functions to the operator for full motion control over a robot manipulator. A mixed reality head-mounted display (HMD) acts as an interface for the operator by displaying virtual content that allows interaction with the robotic system. Besides providing information about the state of the robot, including joint position, velocity, and the force exerted on the robot flange, the gripping force can be adjusted during gripping operations, and motion commands can also be sent to the robot controller. It includes motion commands in joint and Cartesian space, as well as intuitive path planning of the robot based on waypoints created by the operator. A virtual cursor is incorporated into the virtual robot model, with its position and orientation aligned to that of the tool center point (TCP) of the real robot. The operator can execute linear point-to-point as well as non-linear motion. Regarding the safety aspects of the robot motion, a virtual model of the robot is also overlaid on the working environment, allowing the operator to carry out a preview motion to the given trajectory, showing the current and final position of each joint, before executing the motion on the real system. While the human-robot interface and virtual content are created on top of the Unity3D game engine, the Robot Operating System (ROS) provides reliable data transmission and processing between the HMD and the robot controller. The novelty of this work lies on the one hand, in an extensive interface and, on the other hand, in the robot path planning that takes into account the orientation provided by a virtual pointer.

title: Research and Design of Automatic Posture Adjustment System for Space Deployment Arm Joints
authors: Zhijia Wang; Juntao Liu; Zilan Zhang; Haiyang Guo; Shuqian Feng; Deyong Li
abstract: The space deployment arm is a new type of multi-joints space structure for performing satellite functions. With the increasing number of space missions, the space deployment arm structure is becoming more and more complex. In this paper, the overall architecture is designed according to the overall design principles and technical indicators of the system, and the system is divided into several sub-modules, in which the measurement module acquires the space pose data of the deployment arm joints, the software control module is responsible for the overall scheduling, and the parallel execution module carries out the posture adjustment movement. After completion, the measurement module feeds the information back to the software control module to realize the closed-loop control of posture adjustment. In addition, to ensure that the deployment arm joints are not affected by external forces during the posture adjustment process, a six-dimensional force detection module is designed, and a compensation algorithm is designed for joints gravity errors.

title: TSHC-DTS: A Two Stages Semi-supervised Dialogue Topic Segmentation Based on Siamese Transformers and Hierarchical Clustering
authors: Yuan-Lin Liang
abstract: Dialogue segmentation is one of the fundamental tasks in natural language processing that involves partitioning a dialogue into coherent segments or topics. Previous methods often explore only the surface level of contextual features such as lexical features. The proposed method in this paper is a two-stage approach to dialogue segmentation. The first stage uses a Hierarchical Clustering algorithm to group semantically similar utterances based on the embeddings. The second stage uses a Siamese Transformer to calculate the similarity between the utterance pairs in each group. The proposed method can detect both broad and subtle transitions within the dialogue. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively identifies segment boundaries compared with other methods.

title: Multivariable Dynamic Performance Seeking Control of Civil Turbofan Engine*
authors: Kai Peng; Zhaorong Zhang; Hongxia Wang; Huanshui Zhang
abstract: As regards gas turbine engine control, how to achieve the optimal performance of engine within multiple control and physical constraints in real time is a sticky problem to be solved. A novel multivariable optimal control architecture is proposed to compensate engine into a pseudo-linear system by using the nonlinear dynamic inverse and the constrained optimization, and then linear feedback controller is used for control synthesis. At each sampling instant, a real-time linearized model of engine is applied to reduce computational complexity. The simulation results show the resultant control system of civil turbofan engine has good decoupling and tracking response.

title: Joint Fault Diagnosis of a Hydraulic Hexapod Robot Based on 1D Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Jiangtao Wan; Lanying Yang; Gang Jiang; Xingan Hao; Renqiang Zhang; Chao Li; Hui Liu; Siqi Hou
abstract: Leg joints are important motion actuators for hydraulic hexapod robots.
