publication_title: 2022 26th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: ADCS test stands are used for on-the-ground testing of satellite altitude determination and control systems. Their main purpose is to simulate time-vaying conditions similar to those found in outer space on a geocentric orbit. The paper presents the main component of the ADCS test stand – a Helmholtz cage used to simulate the orbital magnetic field. The design and integration of mechanical, electrical, electronic and software components that led to a highly uniform and precisely controlled magnetic field is described here. The validation process, including 3D scanning of the magnetic field, is presented. Remarks on the employed technology, limitations of the proposed solution, some design recommendations, and plans for future work are provided.

title: Towards Semantic Scene Segmentation for Autonomous Agricultural Vehicles
authors: Esma Mujkic; Dan Hermann; Ole Ravn; Morten L. Bilde; Nils A. Andersen
abstract: The development of autonomous agricultural vehicles depends on accurate visual interpretation of the environment. Semantic pixel-wise segmentation plays an important role in achieving a more detailed description of the scene and understanding of the spatial-relationship between different objects. In this paper, a deep architecture for road scene and indoor scene segmentation, SegNet, is applied in solving the scene recognition problem for the agricultural environment. The network is trained on an agriculture image dataset collected during field operation. The problem focuses on the segmentation of five classes of structures commonly found in the fields: vegetation, grass, ground, crop field and obstacles. We apply frequency balancing to address the challenge of class imbalance and transfer learning technique. The quantitative performance of the network is evaluated using pixel accuracy and intersection over union metrics. Moreover, we present an approach for an infield qualitative validation of the trained network.

title: Design of a Knee-joint Exoskeleton to Reduce Misalignment in Both the Sagittal and Coronal Planes
authors: Shubhranil Sengupta; Jee-Hwan Ryu
abstract: Many individuals experience knee dysfunctions attributed to the natural aging process and degenerative conditions. To aid individuals in regaining knee functionality, supportive exoskeletons were designed to be affixed to both the shin and thigh. However, a common issue encountered in knee exoskeletons involves the misalignment of joints between the exoskeleton and the user, resulting in discomfort and potential injuries. To reduce misalignment with the knee joint, it is essential for the thigh and shin harnesses of the exoskeleton to replicate the natural trajectories of the knee. However, achieving this is a complex task due to the shifting center of rotation of the knee in both the Sagittal and Coronal planes. Previous knee exoskeletons primarily focus on aligning the joint in the Sagittal plane, neglecting alignment in the other dimension due to inherent design constraints. For the first time, this study introduces a knee-joint exoskeleton capable of conforming to the natural movement of the knee in both the Sagittal and Coronal planes, with the aim of minimizing joint misalignment without the use of inherently soft materials. A spherical scissor linkage mechanism (SSLM) was utilized in conjunction with a customized guide rail to adjust the center of rotation of the SSLM. This configuration facilitates knee flexion/extension while accommodating the knee joint’s center of rotation in both the Sagittal and Coronal planes. The experimental outcomes demonstrated a substantial reduction in misalignment with the knee when compared to a commercial knee-support brace with a one-degree-of-freedom revolute joint.

title: Discrete quasi-sliding mode control of a two rotor aerodynamic system
authors: Szymon Król
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: The variable structure system with sliding modes are wide known for their performance, robustness and low computational effort. The development of digital technology over past decades resulted in the discrete variant of sliding mode control, which is more suitable for modern hardware. This paper presents the discrete-quasi sliding mode control of a highly nonlinear, strongly coupled two rotor aerodynamic system, which is a down-scaled stationary model of a helicopter.

title: Development of Pneumatic Circuit with Intraoral Pressure Control on Humanoid Saxophone Playing Robot
authors: Chongyi Liu; Jia-Yeu Lin; Zixi Gu; Cosentino Sarah; Atsuo Takanishi
abstract: To investigate the human mechanisms involved in musical instrument performance, the humanoid saxophone playing robot was developed. However, there are limitations regarding the performance stability and difficulties in controlling dynamics. To address these issues and ensure stable sound production, an improved pneumatic circuit that combines intraoral pressure control with the existing flow control mechanism was developed in this study. The oral cavity was improved by reforming the frame part with hard materials to increase air tightness and facilitate easier maintenance compared to the previous design. Soft material was partly used to enable tongue movement and cross section change while absorbing echoes in oral cavity. A proportional valve was implemented as the air outlet of the oral cavity to mimic the human act of air inhalation, solving the problem of control delay and enabling smoother note transitions. The improved system allows the robot to deliver a consistent and stable performance, enabling a better musical expression.

title: Kinematics of Adjusting Parallel Mechanism for Component Assembly
authors: Xinqi Tao; Miao Yuan; Yang Qi; Dong Liang
abstract: To improve the assembly accuracy of large curved structural components, this paper proposes an adjusting parallel mechanism serving as the end-effector of a robot. It accurately adjusts and assembles within the limited space of the curved surface structure. Firstly, the mechanism's movement is determined based on the expected pose transformation, using finite screw to represent the finite motion of adjusting parallel mechanism's chains and moving platform. Secondly, the kinematic model of adjusting parallel mechanism is established through geometric constraints, and the analytical expressions between the drive angles and the posture angles are obtained. The motion feasibility is verified by combining two types of software simulation. Finally, the workspace is visualized using the Monte Carlo method based on the analytical relationship between the input and the end-effector output angles.

title: Periodic Steady State Analysis of Lower Limb Rehabilitation Robot Based on Max-plus Algebra
authors: Cuifeng Qin; Zuojun Liu; Jie Zhang
abstract: The periodic steady state and the autonomous control of a lower limbs rehabilitation robotic walking training system are studied in this paper. Using the timing event diagrams and the max - plus algebra method, a mathematical model of the lower limb rehabilitation robotic walking training system is built. The system cycle calculation formula, estimation of the range of periodic steady state disturbance and independent control strategy are provided, as well as the robustness analysis of cycle stationary relative to parameter perturbations. The periodic steady state disturbance estimation can be used to improve the accuracy and compliance of lower limb rehabilitation robot. The autonomous control strategy is beneficial to ensure the real-time performance and safety of lower limb rehabilitation robot. The proposed disturbance estimation and autonomous control methods are easy to implement on a lower limb rehabilitation robot.

title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Microsleep Detection Using EEG and Physiological Signals
authors: Norzanah Md Said; Raja Fazliza Raja Suleiman; Safwan Syafiq Bin Suhaimie
abstract: Microsleep episodes (MSEs) represent a critical safety concern in environments requiring sustained attention, such as driving and industrial operations. While EEG is the standard tool for detecting these brief lapses into sleep, relying on EEG alone may not capture the full spectrum of physiological changes associated with MSEs. This study proposes a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates electroencephalography (EEG), electrooculography (EOG), and electromyography (EMG) signals from the Sleep-EDF Expanded dataset to enhance microsleep detection. Spectral features, including absolute and relative power across delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands, were extracted from all three modalities. In this work, Sleep Stage N1 is used to represent the sleep class, enabling binary wake-sleep classification aligned with microsleep detection. The resulting binary wake-sleep classification task was addressed using a deep learning network composed of two fully connected layers and a softmax output layer. Models were trained and evaluated across six modality combinations, with and without the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to address class imbalance. The best performance without SMOTE was achieved by the dual modality, EEG+EOG configuration (97.50% accuracy, 0.975 ROC-AUC), while with SMOTE, the tri-modality, EEG+EMG+EOG model remained robust (94.61% accuracy, 0.972 ROC-AUC). These findings underscore the potential of multimodal signal integration and class balancing techniques for real-time microsleep detection using deep learning.

title: Heart Disease Classification with XAI and Kernel SHAP
authors: Nishat Vasker; Anika Tabassum Nafisa; M D Arifur Rahman; Mahamudul Hasan
abstract: Heart disease is a major worldwide health concern, necessitating advances in precise and cost-effective diagnostics. While machine learning (ML) models have shown promise in this field, their opaque nature frequently impedes clinical use due to a lack of interpretability. This work investigates the effectiveness of Explainable AI (XAI) approaches, specifically Kernel SHAP, to increase the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning models for heart disease categorization. We evaluated the interpretability and performance of a logistic regression model using a well-known heart disease dataset. Our logistic regression model has an accuracy of 85.2%, precision of 82.5%, recall of 84.7%, and F1-score of 83.6%. Kernel SHAP analysis gave useful insights, demonstrating that characteristics like ’ca’ (number of main arteries) and ’thal’ (thalassemia) have the high influence on predictions. These findings suggest that adding XAI approaches might significantly increase the confidence and acceptance of ML models in healthcare contexts, eventually leading to better patient outcomes.

title: Image Processing Based System for Detecting and Unloading Billets from a Hearth Rotary Furnace
authors: Cristina-Maria Stancioi; Vlad Muresan; Mihai Abrudean; Iulia Clitan; Mihaela-Ligia Unguresan; Tiberiu Colosi
abstract: Based on the current location of the billet, this article describes the construction of an application to determine the placement of an unloading machine that collects billets from within the rotary hearth furnace. The picture obtained by the video camera must be processed using image filters to decrease noise and eliminate superfluous information from the raw image to determine the contour of the billet. The computation discussed in this work was designed to improve billet evacuation efficiency from a rotating hearth furnace. The scenario when two billets are positioned one after the other on the same axis was considered in this study. The median filtering approach was chosen for image processing since it is a critical function for attaining strong filtering performance at a low cost in the case of the pictures gathered by the video camera. The edges of the billet were detected with the Active contour method. The created program calculates and generates the unloading arm's location for a correct billet grip.

title: Optimizing Deep Reinforcement Learning Models for Stock Trading with Technical Indicators
authors: Minxi John Wang; Xiaorong Li
abstract: This paper presents the development and optimization of a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agent for stock trading, leveraging different technical indicator strategies to enhance decision-making process. The study tackles the challenges associated with using the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicators and proposes a robust DRL framework that integrates different technical indicators. Through comprehensive data acquisition, feature engineering, and model development processes, our proposed method demonstrates the potential of using DRL in predicting stock performance and executing profitable trades. The ensemble strategy emerged as the top performer, achieving up to 76% cumulative returns with a Sharpe ratio of 1.37 for the stock “AAPL.” These results indicate the effectiveness of the developed DRL models and their improvements over existing approaches in literature. The study concludes that DRL-based trading strategies offer significant advantages in profitability and risk management, paving the way for more advanced and reliable automated trading systems.

title: Design and Research of Bionic Ankle Joint Based on Tensile Structure
authors: Yang Li; Xiangyu Ma; Shuang Liang; Qi Tuo; Tianhong Luo
abstract: Combined with the morphological structure and tensile structure of the human ankle joint, a bionic structure of the ankle joint based on the tensile structure is proposed in this paper, in view of solving the problems of poor adaptability and poor structural flexibility of traditional bionic foot mobile robots in complex environments. Firstly, the bionic design method is used to analyze the mechanism design and configuration, by constructing the equivalent mapping model of the human ankle joint. Then, ANSYS software, Matlab numerical calculation and ADAMS are used to simulate and verify the theoretical numerical calculation results of spring deformation. The results show that the error of the experimental and simulation results is less than 3.7mm, and the designed ankle joint mechanism could realize the movement on a slope of 15 degrees. Furthermore, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed structure are verified, which extend the design method for the legged robot with adaptive walking ability.

title: Barrier Lypanunov Function-based Adaptive Control of an Ankle Exoskeleton
authors: Yapeng Wang; Yunhai Geng
abstract: The application of exoskeleton robots in industrial assembly and other fields plays a significant role in alleviating low back pain caused by work-related musculoskeletal disorders and improving work efficiency. Currently, the ankle joints of lower limb exoskeleton robots used in this field are all treated as passive joints. Ankle is important for weight-bearing joints of human lower limbs in the stability and flexibility of daily activities. To this end, the authors of this paper have designed a cable-driven ankle exoskeleton structure to achieve active dorsiflexion and plantarflexion movements in the sagittal plane. To compensate the modeling error and estimate the perturbation, neural network (NN) and nonlinear disturbance observer (NDO) are used. A time-varying barrier Lyapunov function is used to design an adaptive backtracking controller to constrain the system output error and ensure the tracking performance and safety of the robot. A healthy subject participates in the experiment wearing the cable-driven ankle exoskeleton. the experimental is conducted to validate performance of the proposed controller.

title: Enhancing Robotic Task Parameter Estimation Through Unified User Interaction: Gestures and Verbal Instructions in Collaboration
authors: Shuvo Kumar Paul; Mircea Nicolescu; Monica Nicolescu
abstract: As the presence of robots increases in our daily lives, it becomes crucial to gather task and environmental information through intuitive, meaningful, and user-friendly interaction interfaces. This not only aids users in adapting to and trusting robots in collaborative environments but also enhances core sensory data, enabling robots to make dependable decisions. This paper introduces a framework that incorporates two natural interaction interfaces-gesture and speech-to accurately deduce the object of interest and robotic task parameters. The gesture recognition module utilizes a pre-trained model trained on 21 hand landmarks from 2D images to deduce gestures. Additionally, we trained a model to extract task information from verbal instructions. Combining the extracted task parameters from verbal instructions with inferred gestures, the framework is capable of detecting and/or clarifying object(s) of interest (OO1) in the scene, which is needed to generate the final task configurations. The proposed system showcases how combining these two modules identify and disambiguate relevant robotic task parameters.

title: Online Identification of the Open-Circuit Voltage Characteristic of Lithium-Ion Batteries with a Contractor-Based Procedure
authors: Marit Lahme; Andreas Rauh
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: An accurate estimation of the dynamic behavior of lithium-ion batteries is important for a lot of applications, for example, in battery management systems to efficiently and safely charge and discharge the battery cells. The dynamic behavior of lithium-ion batteries is influenced by aging and temperature effects. In order to precisely estimate the dynamic behavior, these effects have to be considered. This is possible for example with a set-valued online identification approach, combining an interval state estimation with the identification of state-dependent characteristics. A drawback of this approach is that the estimation uncertainty increases over time, so that the identification accuracy is limited. In this paper, we investigate if a contractor-based procedure can be used to reduce the estimation uncertainty. The contractor-based procedure was successfully integrated into the set-valued identification approach and leads to a significant improvement of the identification result. The extended identification approach is evaluated with a numerical simulation.

title: Recognition of Macrofungi by Convolutional Neural Networks with Attention Mechanism
authors: Yonggong Han; Wenbin Liao; Jianxin Wang
abstract: Macrofungi refer to fungi with large fruiting bodies. In terms of systematic classification, the species of macrofungi come from the Discomycetes of Basidiomycota and Ascomycota. As the decomposer of nature, macrofungi play a key role in the carbon cycle of the earth and have strong research significance. However, there are many kinds of macrofungi, with a population of more than 10 000. It requires profound professional knowledge to identify them, which is a waste of manpower and material resources. In this study, we creatively proposed a new method based on convolutional neural network (CNN) to recognize macrofungi images. By combining the attention mechanism with the lightweight backbone model densely connected convolutional network (DenseNet), A-DenseNet model is proposed to complete the efficient classification task of macrofungi. The recognition accuracy of our model on the public macrofungi dataset reached 84.3%, and the recognition accuracy on the local macrofungi dataset reached 82.2%, which illustrates the excellent performance of our network in the macrofungi recognition task. This method is an effective supplement and reference for macrofungi classification task.

title: Aerodynamic Parametric Optimization and Analysis of Joined-wing Configuration
authors: Cheng He; Dongli Ma; Gang Chen; Xing’an Liu
abstract: The joined-wing is considered to be a potential configuration because of its low induced drag, light structure, and direct force control. A configuration optimization design method for a high-altitude joined-wing aircraft is proposed for simultaneous considerations of the features of the joined-wing configuration. The purpose is to provide a more reasonable method for the optimization design of the shape parameters of joined-wing aircraft. The shape optimization design model consists of a shape parameterized model, aerodynamic analysis model, and genetic algorithm optimization process. Through comparative analysis before and after optimization, the lift-to-drag ratio of the whole machine after optimization increased by 14.6%. Moreover, detailed sensitivity analysis was carried out on the unique shape parameters of the joined-wing configuration, such as the rear wing sweep angle, the rear wing dihedral angle, the joint location, and the endplate height ratio.

title: Design and Evaluation of a Non-Adhesive Wearable Electrotactile Haptic Device for the Palmar Hand Region
authors: Karan K C; Sajid Nisar
abstract: This study presents the design and evaluation of a non-adhesive, wearable electrotactile haptic device aimed at delivering tactile feedback to the palmar region of the hand. Unlike traditional adhesive electrode-based devices, the proposed system features a reusable non-adhesive, modular structure with flexible electrode casings and contoured holders to ensure stable electrode-skin contact while preserving finger dexterity. The device employs Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) to activate mechanoreceptors through targeted stimulation of the median and ulnar nerves. Experimental evaluations with six participants revealed that electrotactile sensations were consistently perceived in the thumb but varied between other fingers depending on the size of the hand and the position of the electrode. Users with dimensions of the hand closely matching the reference design reported a uniform sensation across all fingers, while others required electrode modifications for optimal performance. The results underscore the importance of adaptable electrode configurations to accommodate anatomical differences. This study highlights the potential of non-adhesive electrotactile interfaces for practical applications in haptics and human-computer interaction.

title: The Innovative Multi-Cavity Pneumatic Actuator: A Chemical Reaction-Driven Device for Generating Mechanical Crawling Motion
authors: Junqi Mu; Yiyang Wei; Xiaofeng Zong
abstract: The low manufacturing cost and fast response speed of pneumatic actuators have attracted widespread attention from researchers in the field of soft robotics. Biomimetic design, as one of the mainstream design concepts of pneumatic actuators, has provided researchers with a source of inspiration. Most existing actuators are based on biomimetic design. In this paper, a pneumatic soft actuator with a biomimetic worm-like design for crawling robots is proposed. This actuator is composed of multiple mesh-like air chambers, and its main parameters are optimized through finite element analysis, enabling it to perform various complex movements. Moreover, in most existing pneumatic actuators, the air source is supplied by air pumps, while the designed actuator in this paper is powered by chemical reactions. By controlling the types and ratios of raw materials, different chemical reactions occur, leading to periodic inhalation and exhalation, allowing the actuator to perform repetitive movements as intended. This driving method can effectively combine with the mechanical motion of the crawling robot, enhancing the autonomy and environmental adaptability of soft robots.

title: The Comprehensive Evaluation Method for The Visibility Ability of ATCT Based on BP Network
authors: Bo Wang; Xiaofei Peng; Jiaquan Ye; Gang Su; Chenyu Liu
abstract: Airport Traffic Control Tower (ATCT) is one of the most important facilities at civil aviation airports. The location and height of ATCT will directly affect the controller's observation and judgment. In order to evaluate and compare the visibility capability of different tower construction schemes, a comprehensive evaluation method is set up. This method includes building an index system of obligatory and preference indicators, forming calculation methods for each indicator, and establishing a comprehensive evaluation model. In the evaluation model, two networks have been constructed based on Coefficient Strategy (CS) and Level Strategy (LS) respectively. Selecting a certain airport in East China as a case study, CS-BP and LS-BP network models of 5-10-1 in topology have been set up after 12000 typical samples for training respectively. The research results show that LS-BP network has the smaller Mean Squared Error (MSE) and greater regression coefficient compared to CS-BP network. And the results of CS-BP were similar to Traditional Strategy (TS). Therefore, selecting LS-BP network to evaluate calculated indicators of given schemes and considering that scheme 3 was best. The entire method can serve as a reference for decision-making by air traffic control unit.

title: Transient Stability of Grid-Forming Inverters in Microgrids: Nonlinear Analysis
authors: Mohsen Eskandari; Andrey V. Savkin
abstract: A current limiting scheme is employed for Inverter-Interfaced Distributed Generation (IIDG) units, mostly in the control loops, to limit the current within the tolerable range and to facilitate the IIDG units being connected to the grid during the transient. However, current-limiting/saturation of the droop-controlled grid-forming inverters affects their transient stability and may make them unstable, which yet has not been explored in the literature in the context of autonomous microgrids (MGs). It is disclosed in this paper that the sharp phase angle variation and the arbitrary resistive output impedance of grid-forming inverters in the current limiting mode make the autonomous MGs unstable. Time-domain simulations prove the idea.

title: Pedestrian Positioning Algorithm Based on Zero-Velocity Correction
authors: Shiying Huang; Haolin Li; Xueyan Zhang; Hongwei Liu; Tianhua Fu
abstract: Pedestrian positioning technology is a key technology that has emerged in recent years in the field of navigation. It is of great significance in indoor, underground and other navigation fields. In this paper, aiming at the problem of error accumulation in pedestrian positioning systems based on MEMS devices, a pedestrian positioning method based on the inertial navigation scheme is studied, and the zero-velocity correction method is used to suppress the accumulation of velocity errors, thereby improving the positioning accuracy. The effectiveness of the method in this paper is verified by experiments.

title: Give Me a Wrench!: Finding Tools for Human Partners in Human-Robot Collaborative Manufacturing Contexts
authors: Pallavi Tilloo; Weitian Wang
abstract: Manufacturing processes can be optimized by enabling human-robot collaboration. A relevant goal in this area is to create a collaborative solution in which robots can provide assisting actions to humans, thereby, reducing menial labor as well as increasing productivity. The solution is based on implementing efficient hand-over of mechanical tools from robots to humans. Hand-over tasks are inevitable in human-robot collaborative manufacturing contexts. These tasks need three-step mechanism: object identification, object grasping, and the actual hand-over. This paper presents an approach for robots to find tools for human partners in human-robot collaboration via deep learning. This is achieved using the object detection system YOLOv3 for identification of commonly used mechanical tools. By training on a custom dataset of 800 images of mechanical tools created for the study, the tool recognition is implemented in realworld human-robot hand-over tasks. Experimental results show that the proposed approach achieves a high accuracy for identification of tools in real-world human-robot collaboration. Future work of this study is also discussed.

title: Design of linear systems with desired poles and zeros of the transfer matrices
authors: Tadeusz Kaczorek
publication_title: 2024 28th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: A new method for the design of linear systems with desired poles and zeros of their transfer matrices is proposed. Conditions for the existence of the solution to the problem and the procedure for computation of the desired matrices are given. The procedure is illustrated by numerical simple examples.

title: Robot Teleoperation via Virtual Reality: A Unity and ROS Approach
authors: Matheus Nicolás Hernandez; Brenno Henrique Ramos; Roberto Simoni; Doglas Negri; Diego De Souza; Luís Gonzaga Trabasso
abstract: This paper explores the integration of virtual reality (VR) with teleoperation systems to enhance human-robot interaction. With the rise of remote operations, traditional methods often rely on two-dimensional interfaces, making it challenging to control robots in complex three-dimensional environments. This research presents a VR teleoperation system using the Meta Quest 2 headset, enabling immersive control of a climbing robot with six degrees-of-freedom and magnetic adhesion. The system architecture integrates Unity for virtual simulation and the Robot Operating System (ROS) for real-time communication and control. A virtual environment allows the user to control the virtual robot model through the VR headset and controllers, with ROS serving as the communication bridge between the virtual and physical robots, enabling effective operations in various applications, including high-risk environments (A video is available at https://youtu.be/MiZDOV4IfLA).

title: Working-Hour Calculation of Construction Machinery Based on Outlier Analysis
authors: Yunfei Shi; Shubo Cao; Shitao Liu; Gongzheng Chen
abstract: This paper focuses on a class of vibration signals collected near the engine of construction machinery, which is used to propose a working-hour statistical method that conform to labor rights and interests. According to the quartile method to analyze the short-term amplitude distribution of the samples, a method of counting outliers is proposed to classify the idle state and working state of the mechanical equipment to achieve fine-grained state classification of the machinery. Based on the actual scene requirements, time smoothing is adopted to revise the idle state with short duration in the collected samples to the working state, while the continuous idle state with long duration remained unchanged. The experimental analysis shows that the method based on counting outliers is hopefully suitable for the state classification of various construction machinery (manufacturer, date of manufacture, size). The method proposed in this paper is simple in implementation and avoids the work of collecting data on the different running states for different devices and labeling in methods based on supervised learning, which is greatly convenient for practical engineering applications.

title: Comparative Research of Nonlinear Decoupled Tracking Controller Design for an Open-Frame AUV
authors: Halit Ege Ceyhun; Kerim Deniz Kaya; Kubilay Bayramoğlu; Aytaç Gören
publication_title: 2023 27th [::International::] [::Conference::] on Methods and Models in [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] (MMAR)
abstract: This study presents the design and implementation of two different nonlinear controllers for trajectory tracking control of an open-frame observer type Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV). The AUV's dynamics are modeled using the Newton-Euler formalism, and the state-space representation is obtained. The controller comparison consists of two nonlinear controllers for horizontal motion control in planar coordinates(x,y): Backstepping Control (BS) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC), and a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) for controlling the depth and rotational dynamics. Both controller structures are designed to ensure stability using the Lyapunov stability criteria for trajectory tracking while LQR guarantees stability by placing eigenvalues on the left half plane for depth and rotational dynamics. The system states are decoupled to facilitate control design, and Simulink models are developed to validate the controllers' performance in the presence of sinusoidal disturbance. The results show that both BS and SMC provide robust and accurate tracking performance under sinusoidal disturbances, while LQR exhibits good performance in the remaining coordinates.

title: Adaptive Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Systems with Measurement Uncertainty
authors: Song Jiang; Yan Lin; Chen Sun
abstract: In this study, the global adaptive control is considered for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with measurement uncertainty, where the bounds of the measurement uncertainty and system uncertainty are not a priori. A dynamic gain-based control strategy and the feedback domination technique are applied for the controller design, where a set of new dynamic gains is proposed to deal with uncertainties with unknown bounds. It has also been proven that global stability can be achieved under the designed controller. Finally, a simulation example is presented to illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

title: Provably Safe Deep Learning-Based Offset-Free Model Predictive Control and its Application to Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving
authors: Han Wang; Longyan Li; Chao Ning
abstract: Offset-free model predictive control (MPC) provides a useful means for controlling systems with uncertainties and constraints, but suffers from the heavy computational burden of repeatedly solving an optimization problem in real time. Such computational issue precludes the possibility of its application in systems requiring high realtime requirements, such as autonomous driving system. To address this problem, we develop a provably safe deep learning-based offset-free MPC framework. Based on the nominal offset-free MPC, the proposed MPC not only reserves the ability of disturbance rejection, but also leverages deep neural networks for approximating the explicit MPC solution to greatly reduce online computational time. Furthermore, a gauge map is used to guarantee the satisfaction of safe constraints. The proposed MPC is used in trajectory tracking control for smart autonomous driving. The simulation results show that the proposed MPC is an order of magnitude faster than the nominal offset-free MPC in safety-critical systems.

title: High Speed Laser Stripe Extraction Method for Measuring Strip Flatness using Linear Structured Laser
authors: Yibing Fan; Xiaochen Wang; Jianwei Zhao; Shuzong Yan; Kaiyuan Zhu; Quan Yang
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of strip steel flatness calculation, it's hard to overstate the significance of accurately and efficiently extracting the center of laser stripes in strip steel images. It serves as the foundation for accurate calculation of strip steel flatness and adjustment of process parameters. The main intention of this dissertation is to show a solution for efficiently obtaining sub-pixel centerlines of dual line laser stripes, which combines the region of interest (ROI) extraction and the Steger algorithm based on Gaussian operator. The method consists of three steps. Firstly, preprocessing is performed on each laser stripe to remove the background and exclude redundant laser line regions on both sides of the steel plate based on area selection. Secondly, the ROI region is determined using the merging operator, and the processed region is intersected with the pixels of the original image. Finally, according to the pixel width of the stripes, the parameters of the Gaussian operator are calculated, and the center position of the sub-pixel is calculated using Taylor expansion in the normal direction. It has been proven that the processing time for a single dual-line laser image is only 6.779 ms. The most striking conclusion that can be reached when using the indicated method to extract the center position information of laser stripes is quite frankly high precision and efficiency. This method ensures the real-time nature and detection accuracy of industrial steel plate flatness measurement, providing theoretical and data support for process control in industrial settings.

title: Switching Process Analysis and Drive Circuit Simulation of SiC MOSFET in Dynamic Wireless Charging for Electric Vehicles
authors: Zongwen Li; Rong Long; Liyan Zhang; Qihong Chen
abstract: In order to solve the problem of device impact and switching speed in dynamic wireless charging device for electric vehicles (EVs), first, a new SiC MOSFET model was established based on manufacturer's model and datasheet. Combined with this model, the hard-switching and soft-switching processes of SiC MOSFETs are compared and analyzed. Although soft-switching can solve the problems of changing switching speed and reducing device impact, it needs to modify the hardware circuit, which is not practical in the changeable environment of dynamic wireless charging of EV s. Based on this question, a new multi-grade voltage drive circuit is designed to meet the various requirements of the drive circuit in the wireless charging process of EVs. Finally, the drive circuit is simulated in Pspice, and its feasibility is explored according to its waveforms.

title: Static Gains Based Output Feedback Stabilization for a Class of Nonlinear Systems with Sensor Uncertainties
authors: Yanjie Li; Wenjie Chen; Yan Lin
abstract: In this paper, the problem of global output feedback stabilization is addressed for a class of nonlinear systems with sensor uncertainties. To be specific, in the case of sensor sensitivity error and measurement deviation, a linear state observer and an output feedback controller are constructed on the basis of two static gains. It can be proved that all signals of the closed-loop system are globally bounded and that the system can achieve global stabilization. Simulation results are presented to show the effectiveness of proposed strategy.

title: Modeling of Body Pressure Distribution on Alternative Pressure Mattress
authors: Masamichi Kosuge; Masaki Takahashi
abstract: Recently, an alternative pressure mattress has been proposed to prevent pressure ulcers. In this study, we aim to design a control system for body pressure distribution using the mattress. This study focuses on modeling the dynamics between the body pressure distribution and the mattress. As modeling based on first principles is challenging, we identify the model from experimental data. However, when high-dimensional data such as body pressure distribution are directly used for identification, the model accuracy can deteriorate. Therefore, we need to determine the suitable model structure or dataset. Herein, we examined how the prediction accuracy of body pressure distribution varies with the dataset and model structure. We also proposed a method for representing the model as the dynamics of the parameters of the Gaussian Mixture Model to suppress the estimated parameters. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to propose the body pressure model as dynamics of the parameters of the Gaussian Mixture Model.

title: Implementation of a Wireless Mesh Network for Orienteering Monitoring
authors: Hui Yang; Chuan Xu Liu; Zhi Bin Hou; Yan Fei Sun; Guang Xing Wang; Qing Ting Liu
abstract: Characterized by complex organization on crucial terrains for the numerous competitors, Orienteering activities are facing formidable safety challenges during training and competitions sessions. A robust communication network is crucial need for Orienteering organization progress management and control, timely emergency treatment, and comprehensive data analysis. Referring to the Longley-Rice model, theoretical calculations for equipment selection and network coverage capacity of a Wireless Mesh Network were conducted. Feasibility of a two-tiered backbone-access network structure was validated through network design and communication capability test. The safety management level of the Orienteering events was enhanced obviously through Orienteering monitoring on the structure of a self-configuring Wireless Mesh Network. The athletics abilities of Orienteering candidates were improved significantly with the support of the data analysis obtained through Wireless Mesh Network.

title: Adaptive Filters for DC Motor Identification: A Case Study
authors: Simona-Daiana Sim; Attila Medgyesi; Zsófia Lendek; Mircea Susca; Vlad Mihaly; Doina Pisla; Calin Liviu Vaida; Petru Dobra; Anca Elena Pica
abstract: This paper investigates the practical application and evaluation of four adaptive algorithms: Least Mean Square (LMS), Normalized Least Mean Square (NLMS), Recursive Least Square (RLS) and Affine Projection (AP) for the identification of a DC motor. The work focuses on dynamic system identification, where the adaptability and efficiency of numerical filters play an important role. To identify the parameters of a DC motor, these adaptive algorithms are used on measured data. With the aim of having a shorter processing time, the data was downsampled. Satisfactory results were obtained with all algorithms. Finally, the difficulty of implementing the algorithms, the errors obtained and the processing time were analyzed.

title: Thrust Allocation Method for Solid Attitude and Divert Control Engine
authors: Zuohao Hua; Zhuang Fu; Lu Niu; Bang Liu; Jiazheng Zhang
abstract: A thrust allocation method for a solid attitude and divert control engine, using a single combustion chamber shared by 4 divert thrusters and 6 attitude control thrusters, is proposed. Thrust allocation for multi-valve solid rocket engines is typically under-constrained due to multiple degrees of freedom and the need for precise control. To address this, we designed a distribution strategy based on the engine's operational requirements, aiming to maximize total impulse output while prioritizing attitude control thrust synthesis. This comprehensive method optimizes thrust distribution across thrusters, ensuring the engine operates within design constraints for reliable and precise control in spacecraft and missile systems. Our approach demonstrates significant improvements over traditional methods by ensuring effective thrust utilization, minimizing propellant consumption, and maintaining high precision in attitude and divert control. This paper offers a novel solution and algorithm for thrust allocation in solid attitude and divert control engines, contributing valuable advancements to aerospace propulsion systems.

title: Neural Adaptive Control for Robotic Systems With Saturation and Disturbance
authors: Shuai Ding; Jinzhu Peng; Yan Liu; Yage Wu
abstract: This paper proposes a neural adaptive control (NAC) strategy for the robotic systems with saturation and disturbance. The strategy involves using a neural network (NN) to estimate the robot’s dynamic model and constructing a compensator to mitigate the impact of input saturation. To obtain estimated velocities and external disturbances in the robotic systems without prior knowledge of the system model, an NN-based extended state observer (NNBESO) is designed. Based on the designed error compensation term and NNBESO, NAC is proposed to achieve the tracking for the desired trajectory under input saturation and external disturbance. Finally, the proposed NNBESO-based NAC strategy is verified by the simulation experiments on a 2 rigid-link robotic manipulator with input saturation and system disturbances, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed NNBESO-based NAC strategy.

title: Research on Application of Personalized Recommendation Technology in Adaptive Learning System Based on Java Programming
authors: Xiangmei Zhao
abstract: This paper taking the course of Java programming as an example, an adaptive learning question bank system based on personalized recommendation is realized by using collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm. Personalized test exercises that are suitable for students' own curriculum learning status can help students improve their learning efficiency and effectively promote the improvement and progress of students' academic achievements. At the same time, the application of this system can provide a reference basis for other adaptive learning systems based on personalized recommendation.

title: Design and Control of the Prototype Electro-hydraulic Energy Regeneration Actuation System for Electric Construction Machinery
authors: Chen Ji; Jiaqiang Zhang; Lijie Zhang
abstract: The electrification of construction machinery is a key development trend, but challenges such as high energy consumption and difficulty in energy replenishment have hindered its effectiveness in field operations. To improve the energy efficiency of the actuation system in construction machinery, an electro-hydraulic energy regeneration actuation system (EHERAS) and a multi-mode switching control strategy are proposed. The actuation system utilizes a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) and a four-quadrant hydraulic pump with bidirectional driving capability to enable energy regeneration. A Hardware-in-the-Loop experimental platform for the electro-hydraulic energy regeneration actuation system has been developed for a 3-ton electric-powered forklift, and experimental verification has been conducted. The results have revealed that the proposed system achieves a potential energy regeneration efficiency of 40.72%, with an energy-saving rate of 15.35%.

title: Guiding Deep Reinforcement Learning by Modelling Expert’s Planning Behavior
authors: Ruidong Ma; John Oyekan
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithm has shown its strength in solving complex robot control problems. Nevertheless, the existing challenge is that random and unnecessary exploration may lead to slow convergence, which causes difficulty in the training process. In this paper, we propose a novel framework of using a small amount of demonstration to guide the exploration. Unlike previous works, we model the demonstration as a function between direction preferences and goal-state distance using Neural Network. To evaluate our work, we designed several tasks in the robot simulation platform VREP. The results indicate that our algorithm can guide the exploration and hence improve the performance of Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient(DDPG).

title: Maximum Temperature Prediction Based on GPS and Meteorological Data by Using Neural Network
authors: Shenzheng Zuo; Renjie Cai; Yan Wang; Enrui Hu; Lingzhi Liu; Yibo Guo
abstract: Temperature prediction is a task involving agriculture, military, industry and other aspects, and it is related to daily life and production tasks. Therefore, accurate temperature prediction is an important research topic at present. In this paper, a neural network-based maximum temperature prediction method is proposed. Combined with the Precipitable Water Vapor (PWV) data calculated from GPS satellite data, it achieves high precision, high time granularity prediction under the condition of low computing power requirements.

title: Neural Network Based Friction Compensation of Motion Control on A 6-DoF Robot Manipulator
authors: Xiaozhi Zhang; Liangyu Chen
abstract: Friction is the force resisting relative motions between two bodies, it causes cycle oscillations and impairs closedloop tracking performance for robot manipulators. To address this problem, in this paper, we propose a neural network (NN) structure with attention mechanism, which compromises the calculate efficiency and accuracy. In this structure, both instantaneous data and feature abstracted from historical data are utilized as inputs, and the torques needed to compensate for the effects of friction of each joint are the targets. Besides, the proposed NN method are contrasted with XGBoost method and convolutional neural network method to demonstrate that NN can achieve better approximation performance in offline experiment. Training data are collected by traversing through the working velocity of robot joints on the task trajectory, based on which the best model will be produced and is deployed on servo controller of a 6-degree-of-freedom (DoF) robot manipulator. Finally, the NN structure is tested on a real robot manipulator for online validation, the robot manipulator is programmed to run on the same trajectory with random speeds for a period of time. Online experiment results show that the predicted compensating torques applied to robot by adding feedforward control to the current command are always closer to the desired torques, and tracking errors of joints are effectively reduced.

title: RANS Model-based Constant Temperature Anemometry Examination to Validate Negligible Wind Tunnel Blockage Effect on Developed Multi-scale Generated Grid Turbulence
authors: Keita Nakamura; Hiroki Suzuki; Toshinori Kouchi; Kento Tanaka
abstract: The aim of this study is to quantitatively assess the effect of wind tunnel blockage on multi-scale generated turbulence and to analyze the results in comparison with the results of previous studies. In particular, the study focuses on the mainstream weak acceleration phenomena and their turbulence characteristics, and the effects are evaluated using acceleration parameters. The decay exponent calculated by introducing a turbulence time scale was larger than the results in the previous study for square lattice turbulence, indicating a rapidly decaying field. An evaluation of the dependence on flow velocity was also carried out, and the results obtained by varying the set flow velocity confirm that the effect of acceleration on turbulent energy, dissipation rate, length scale and time scale is independent of flow velocity. Compared to the measurement uncertainty, the effect of acceleration was small and no statistically significant differences were found. The results of this study provide important information for the quantitative assessment of the impact of weak acceleration phenomena in the main flow due to blockage effects in the wind tunnel test section on multi-scale generated turbulence.

title: EEG Based Imagined Word Recognition Using CNN-Bi-GRU
authors: Sabitha Rani B S; Elizabeth Sherly
abstract: A notable advancement in brain-computer interface (BCI) for the benefit of the speech-impaired community based on EEG led many insights for imagined speech. This study addresses challenges in translating brain-computer interface (BCI) advancements for speech-impaired individuals using EEG. Existing neural speech decoding methods, despite progress, face classification accuracy issues. The proposed solution combines a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) and a bi-directional gated recurrent unit (Bi-GRU) for improved classification. The systematic approach includes EEG signal preprocessing with bandpass and notch filters, power spectral density analysis, and coherence analysis for cognitive speech task-related EEG topography. The integrated CNN and Bi-GRU enhance memory capacity and classification. Simulation results show the system effectively detects four words with an 88 % recognition rate, surpassing previous performance benchmarks.

title: AI-Driven Resource Allocation Prediction for 6G Open RAN Using I-SFO-Tuned CatBoost Model
authors: Akshat Gaurav; Brij B. Gupta; Varsha Arya; Kwok Tai Chui
abstract: The development of 6G Open RAN systems requires dynamic, effective resource allocation to manage several uses and network conditions. Real-time optimization and complexity are challenges for many traditional approaches of resource management. In this context, we proposed an AI-driven resource allocation prediction model based on the CatBoost algorithm optimized with the Improved Sailfish Optimizer (I-SFO). Comparative study using conventional models shows better performance, attaining the lowest MSE (0.0043) and MAE (0.0255). The results confirm the capacity of our proposed approach for effective, real-time resource management in RAN systems configured for 6G programming.

title: Research on Intelligent Automatic Operating System of Marine Concrete Coating Aided by Computer Technology
authors: Zhangfeng Guo
abstract: Concrete structures are prone to corrosion under marine environmental conditions. The marine environment can usually be divided into atmospheric region, splash region, tidal region and underwater region according to the different regions of its effect on the structure. These regions have different corrosion conditions, corrosion characteristics and corrosion rates. Therefore, coating is required. In order to reduce resource consumption, the operation of marine concrete coating is handed over to the computer intelligent automatic operating system to realize. This paper studies the design of intelligent automatic operating system for marine concrete coating, and proves that the automatic operating system assisted by computer technology will greatly improve its performance. A series of investigation experiments are carried out for this research. First, the important position of marine concrete coating in today's marine engineering and its practicability are fully analyzed, and then the analysis is carried out with computer technology to illustrate its feasibility. Secondly, the PID control algorithm is used to improve the fast response characteristics of the system, enhance the stability of the system, and improve the dynamic characteristics of the system. Final experiments show that intelligent, automated coatings can improve concrete's frost resistance, after using the intelligent automatic operating system, the coating efficiency is significantly improved by more than 20% due to the reduction of manual operations.

title: Kinematic Calibration of a 3DOF Compliant Nanopositioning Stage Based on Visual Measurement
authors: Nuo Xu; Hai Li; Xianmin Zhang; Lei Yuan; Benliang Zhu
publication_title: 2023 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a vision-based kinematic calibration method for a 3DOF compliant nanopositioning stage (CNPS). First, the nanopositioner's simplified linear elastic kinematics model is established based on the pseudo-rigid body model. The vision-based multi-DOF pose measurement scheme that can accurately measure the milliradian rotation angle is given, including the measurement system and principle. To accurately calibrate the kinematic model, the motion transfer Jacobian matrix is split into a translation part and rotation part, and different pose data and direct linear transformation are used to solve them, respectively. Finally, the calibrated kinematic parameters are utilized for CNPS positioning control. The results show that the rotation error of CNPS is reduced from 0.0232° to 0.00380°, and the translation error is reduced from 0.3754μ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> to 0.0612μm.

title: Challenges in Transition of Software Defined Radio Implementation from Bare Metal to Real-Time Operating System
authors: Kashif Shahzad; Muhammad Zeeshan; Muhammad Umar Farooq; Shoab Ahmed Khan
abstract: Real-time embedded implementations like software defined radios (SDR) impose several challenges being priority-driven and mostly sequential. Such critical real time embedded applications require a significant level of intelligence for hardware resource management. This feature is inherently offered by off-the-shelf available real-time operating systems (RTOS). Most of the fragments of support code available are in the form of bare metal implementations and are associated with specific hard-ware. There is no absolute guideline for how to convert a real-time (RT) embedded application into one with the usage of RTOS. Matters become much trickier if one has to port the entire application software from bare metal hardware implementation to an operating system (OS) environment. In this paper, we investigate the implementation details and problems encountered in timer-based scheduler errors, while porting the SDR application to an RTOS. This paper uses customizable RTOS by Micrium (µC/OS-II) for SDR implementation on Motorolla’s Power PC (MPC-565). This paper also discusses the use of timers to strictly control the clock drifts and rollovers for such embedded systems. The discussion uses MPC-565 as an implementation platform, however, the recommendations and analysis apply to all processors in general.

title: Optimization of Design Information Decoupling of Kinematic Machinery Based on Meta-Action Theory
authors: Xin Yang; Yan Ran; Yifan Chen; Genbao Zhang
abstract: In the late stages of concept design of mechanical product is usually based on sequential design, but the interaction among different performances is ignored. Once defects are generated in the design process, it will be difficult to make up in the subsequent design and cause a constant waste of energy during entire production cycle. In view of this defect and combined with the main characteristics of the motion machinery, we firstly propose the framework of soft decoupling technology for motion machinery's design process is proposed. Secondly, coupling characteristics among the meta-action units are analyzed and the coupling constraint model is constructed. Then we reduce iteration and feedback of the design process information through reducing the information interaction among the aggregation sets of the units to reach the purpose of soft decoupling. Finally, the analysis results demonstrate that the meta-action design units decoupling technology is successfully applied to the design of pallet exchange frame motion scheme, which shortens the product development cycle and provides a beneficial reference for the design of motion-dominated mechanical system.

title: Kinematic Tracking Controller Design for Unknown Robot Manipulators Based on Improved Gradient Neural Dynamics
authors: Hainan Yang; Tao Zhao; Peng Qin; Qinyin Su
abstract: Accurate and complete knowledge of the kinematic model is fundamental to achieving high-precision trajectory tracking in robotic control. Nevertheless, in scenarios where motion information is unavailable, model-based methods may prove ineffective in fulfilling the desired objectives. Hence, the kinematic tracking problem for unknown robot manipulators is investigated. To compensate for the lack of model information, an adaptive Jacobian estimation method is proposed, where the Jacobian gradient is computed via an improved GND approach. A low-pass filter estimates the end-effector velocity, while a Kalman filter is integrated to suppress measurement noise and improve robustness. Based on this, a time-varying power-exponent-type recurrent neural network (TVPET-RNN) is designed to implement the tracking control strategy. The proposed method operates without any a priori information of the manipulator's kinematics, relying solely on data-driven representations, and its feasibility and effectiveness are validated through comprehensive simulation studies, demonstrating accurate trajectory tracking and strong robustness.

title: MMCLS: An Efficient Vision Mamba-Based Framework for Martian Image Classification
authors: Yuqi Dai; Zhoujuan Cui
abstract: Gazing upon the cosmos, humanity has never ceased its journey to explore the unknown realms. For Martian data analysis, efficient and stable image classification models are essential. Mamba, a novel variant of State Space Models (SSM), has recently emerged as a breakthrough in sequential data processing, demonstrating exceptional memory efficiency and computational speed. Building upon this advancement, we pioneer MMCLS, a novel method integrating vision Mamba module for Martian image classification. Comparative experiments demonstrate that MMCLS is both succinct and effective, achieving state-of-the-art performance on HiRISE and MSL datasets.

title: Finite Element Simulation Study of Ultrasonic-Assisted Vibration Cutting of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polyetherketoneketone (CF/PEKK)
authors: Ran Tao; Liqiang Zhang; Zeyu Zhou; Yichen Jiang
abstract: In the past few decades, the demand for carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites has significantly increased in aerospace, biomedical, and marine engineering industries due to their outstanding properties. These properties include high strength, high stiffness, low density, and excellent corrosion resistance. However, the high hardness and rigidity of polyetherketoneketone (CF/PEKK) materials result in high cutting forces during machining, which can lead to vibration and tool wear, posing significant challenges for numerical modeling, simulation, and process testing of the machining process. This study develops an ultrasonic vibration cutting force simulation model for carbon fiber reinforced CF/PEKK materials and validates the model’s effectiveness in predicting cutting forces and temperatures, with prediction errors controlled within 15%. The results provide a reliable theoretical basis for simulating the elliptical ultrasonic vibration cutting process of CF/PEKK materials and lay the foundation for future research in machining surface quality optimization and process improvement.

title: Transmissive phase measuring deflectometry system using frequency domain Gamma error elimination algorithm
authors: Xianguang Fan; Yixin Yang; Xin Wang; Yingjie Xu
abstract: Transmissive phase measuring deflectometry plays an increasingly pivotal role in lens wavefront measurement, owing to its uncomplicated system structure, expansive curvature measurement range, and commendable versatility. Nevertheless, the Gamma error, stemming from the nonlinear characteristics of the display screen and the camera, has emerged as a critical factor impeding measurement precision. This limitation significantly hampers the accuracy of lens phase coordinate calculation. In this paper, we propose a frequency domain Gamma error elimination algorithm based on linear regression for the transmissive phase measuring deflectometry system. This algorithm effectively mitigates the Gamma error introduced by the display screen and camera within the system. The method is characterized by its universality, rapid execution, and high accuracy. Experimental results substantiate the algorithm’s viability and effectiveness.

title: Analysis for influences of eccentric distance on grinding performance of eccentric AG mill using DEM simulation
authors: Ziqiang Fang; Songlin Peng
publication_title: 2024 IEEE [::International::] [::Conference::] on Advanced Information; Mechanical Engineering; [::Robotics::] and [::Automation::] (AIMERA)
abstract: Tumbling mill is an industrial equipment for producing fine and uniform granules. In recent decade, the eccentric ball mill is proposed for improving milling efficiency of particles. In this paper, a validated Discrete Element Method (DEM) model is used for simulating charge motion in eccentric AG mill at different eccentric distances ε. The DEM results showed that movement pattern of particles periodically changes as AG mill revolves, when ε is larger than 0·r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>, where r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> is radius of AG mill. Cascading phenomena can be observed in particles in the first half turn of each mill revolution, while most particles roll down from shoulder position in the second half turn. With the increase of ε, the number of high-energy collisions among particles grows dramatically at charge impact point position, while the number of high-energy collisions between particles and lifters is reduced. Based on the DEM results, it can be concluded that the eccentric AG mill can help to improve the grinding efficiency of granular materials while guarantee structural safety of lifters’ boundaries, especially for the large ε.

title: Embedded Marine Target Detection and Positioning Shipboard Terminal Based on Beidou Navigation Satellite System
authors: Mingyong Yuan; Min Wang; Zhenjia Chen; Xiao Zhao
abstract: Improving the maritime information supervision system and establishing a strong maritime nation is one of the important strategies for national defense. Civilian fishing vessels, as the main body of marine economic activities, are important nodes for sensing marine information. In this paper, lightweight neural network is deployed to embedded devices for maritime target recognition. Target ranging is realized by building a maritime monocular visual ranging model. And the high precision real-time ship information of heading and speed is obtained by sensors. The positioning of the observation vessel is obtained based on BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS). And the obtained maritime information is transmitted back to the shore terminal through Regional Short Message Communication (RSMC). The detection of maritime targets and the detection of the surrounding environment are realized through embedded devices using maritime vessel nodes. Monitoring of suspicious targets at sea and data return can be completed. During the simulation experiments, the relative error rate of ranging was below 18.2%.

title: DABI: Evaluation of Data Augmentation Methods Using Downsampling in Bilateral Control-Based Imitation Learning with Images
authors: Masato Kobayashi; Thanpimon Buamanee; Yuki Uranishi
abstract: Autonomous robot manipulation is a complex and continuously evolving robotics field. This paper focuses on data augmentation methods in imitation learning. Imitation learning consists of three stages: data collection from experts, learning model, and execution. However, collecting expert data requires manual effort and is time-consuming. Additionally, as sensors have different data acquisition intervals, preprocessing such as downsampling to match the lowest frequency is necessary. Downsampling enables data augmentation and also contributes to the stabilization of robot operations. In light of this background, this paper proposes the Data Augmentation Method for Bilateral Control-Based Imitation Learning with Images, called “DABI”. DABI collects robot joint angles, velocities, and torques at 1000 Hz, and uses images from gripper and environmental cameras captured at 100 Hz as the basis for data augmentation. This enables a tenfold increase in data. In this paper, we collected just 5 expert demonstration datasets. We trained the bilateral control Bi-ACT model with the unaltered dataset and two augmentation methods for comparative experiments and conducted real-world experiments. The results confirmed a significant improvement in success rates, thereby proving the effectiveness of DABI. For additional material, please check: https://mertcookimg.github.io/dabi

title: Mobile Robot Path Planning Based on Improved Elite Ant Colony Algorithm
authors: Kaiying Yu; Bin Xu
abstract: Aiming at the problems of slow convergence speed and easy to fall into local optimum of ant colony algorithm in solving path planning problem, an improved elite ant colony algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the pseudo-random state transition rule is used to select the path, and a dynamic selection factor is defined to adaptively update the selection ratio to improve the search efficiency and path search ability of the algorithm. Secondly, an elite path selection operator is designed to improve the quality of the search path by retaining the better path. Finally, based on the elite ant model, an improved pheromone incentive strategy is proposed to update the pheromone increment and improve the convergence speed of the algorithm. The comparative experiments of path planning are carried out under different complexity grid maps. The results show that the improved elite ant colony algorithm has faster convergence speed, and has better global search ability while improving search efficiency, which verifies the effectiveness and practicability of the algorithm.

title: Study on Vibration Suppression Trajectory Planning of Axially Moving Cantilever Beam
authors: Jikai Chen; Hao Chen; Xiang Luo
abstract: The push out process of steel bridge can be simplified as an axially moving cantilever beam model under harmonic excitation. Aiming at the lateral vibration control problem of the system, a vibration suppression trajectory planning method based on quintic polynomial function interpolation of genetic algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the assumed mode method and Lagrange equation are used to establish the dynamic model of the system, and the Newmark-β numerical method is used to calculate the dynamic response. Secondly, the polynomial function is used to construct the basic value of the trajectory control point. The displacement offset of the trajectory control point is taken as the optimization variable, and the cumulative vibration energy at the gear is taken as the optimization objective. On the premise of meeting the kinematic constraints of the system, the genetic algorithm is used to optimize the optimal vibration suppression trajectory of the system. The simulation results show that compared with the quintic polynomial trajectory, the cumulative vibration energy of the optimal vibration suppression trajectory is reduced by more than 45%, the stability of the system is improved, and the service life of the gear is extended.

title: Research on target system selection of correlated data based on Bayesian network
authors: Min Zhang; Xin Xu; Qi Ji
abstract: Many related data are involved in the production process of the cigarette industry. These related data exist in multiple production systems, and there is also a requirement to select relevant systems to extract data. It is our goal to select high reliability systems to extract related data. This paper constructs a selection prediction model, selects the key influencing factors of the target system, carries out Bayesian network reasoning, calculates the selection probability of the given associated data from the Bayesian network algorithm, and constructs the model according to the actual joint probability to realize the algorithm, a new discrimination method is realized for the deployment and retrieval of the production decision-making system of tobacco automation system. Compared with the selection of real data, it is concluded that the Bayesian network based acquisition of related data target system is highly effective, and further points out that higher dimensions can be used for deeper research and application.

title: Research on Defect Category Identification Method for Rough Surface Thick Wall Steel Plate Based on Autoencoder-BP Neural Network
authors: Biao Xue; YuHang Wang; Yang Yang; LiJun Dang; SongYi Dian
abstract: For the processing of echo signals in defect detection, wavelet transform and principal component analysis are mostly used to extract features. However, the feature values obtained by these methods often lead to redundancy, resulting in the waste of a lot of resources for defect identification. This paper, in the context of defects in thick-walled steel plates with rough surfaces, proposes a defect category recognition classification method based on an autoencoder-BP neural network. It uses signals from electromagnetic ultrasonic and pulsed eddy current composite detection as the neural network learning signals. Impedance analysis is used to more comprehensively reflect the characteristics of defects, thereby improving the accuracy of defect identification. Autoencoder is selected to extract the geometric features of the composite detection signals, which can effectively extract useful features from the dataset. The feature dataset is then divided into training and testing sets. Simulation experiments show that the trained neural network model has achieved a classification accuracy of 90.8% in the testing.

title: Extended State Observer and Kalman Filter Based Control for DC-DC Buck Converter Subject to Disturbances and Noise
authors: Rui You; Yunjun Chen; Lu Zhang
abstract: Direct current-direct current buck converters are widely used in industrial fields. In practical applications, parameter uncertainty, external disturbances and measurement noise affect the control performance of DC-DC buck converter. To deal with external disturbances and measurement noise in DC-DC buck converter, a control strategy combining extended state observer (ESO) and Kalman filter (KF) is proposed in this paper. The extended state observer is used to estimate the lumped disturbance of the DC-DC buck converter system. However, in order to achieve fast convergence in the control process, the observer chooses a large control gain, which results in severe noise amplification. To this end, the Kalman filter is used to filter the noise. The composite control method proposed in this paper can improve the robustness and voltage tracking performance of DC-DC buck converter. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

title: Neural Network Design for the Restoration of Blurry Images Taken by the Line Inspection Robot
authors: Xin Chen; Bin Zhang; Xuan Jiang
abstract: Transmission line inspection robots have played an important role in transmission line inspection. However, the inspection robot occasionally oscillates when capturing images, resulting in blurry inspection images. This article proposes a neural network model based on the improved SRNdeblur algorithm. Firstly, we use residual dense modules (RDB) instead of residual modules to reduce lost information in the network. Secondly, the multi-loss fusion function is used to focus on the pixel differences, overall structure differences and frequency space differences between image pairs. Finally, a fuzzy image dataset PLID for power inspection robots was created. And the test results show that our proposed algorithm performs better on PSNR and SSIM compared to SRNdeblur.

title: A Fuzzy Inference System-Based Hybrid Assignment Method for Cobot Assignment Problem
authors: Marrisa Kimaporn; Wuttinan Nunkaew
abstract: To address the complexity of a cobot assignment problem in smart manufacturing, this research has pioneered a new hybrid assignment method integrating the fuzzy inference system (FIS) into both multi-objective assignment and linear assignment models. It focuses on the critical tasks of assigning robots, jobs, and workers to create efficient cobot workstations, covering three core activities: robot-to-job, job-to-robot, and worker-to-robot-job assignments. An FIS-based multi-objective assignment model is utilized in the initial step to form effective sets of a single robot and jobs. The model also allows users to adjust the level of negative deviation from the target to enhance the satisfaction of the decision-maker. In the final step, workers are assigned and the cobot workstations are concurrently created using a FIS-based linear assignment model. To illustrate the method's efficacy, we provided a practical example that demonstrates its performance in action for industrial applications.

title: Wide-range Load Sensor Using Vacuum Sealed Quartz Crystal Resonator for Simultaneous Biosignals Measurement on Bed
authors: Yuichi Murozaki; Fumihito Arai
abstract: Monitoring of biosignals on a daily basis plays important roles for the health management of elderly. The monitoring system for the daily life, the system should not require the subjects to take special effort like wearing a sensor. We propose biosignals measurement using wide-range load sensor on the bed. The sensing system can detect the body weight, heartbeat and respiration simultaneously by just lying on the bed. We have developed load sensor using quartz crystal resonator (QCR load sensor) as wide-range load sensor. However, the measurement range was not sufficient for the simultaneous measurement of biosgnals on bed. To realize such sensing system, we propose a QCR load sensor utilizing vacuum sealing technology for expanding the measurement range. We improved the oscillation characteristics of the QCR by the vacuum sealing to stabilize the sensor output. Accordingly, the resolution of the sensor was improved. Moreover, the load capacity of the sensor was increased by improving the bonding strength of sensor structure. The fabricated sensor had a measurement range of 0.27 mN - 1180 N (4.4 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>). This wide enough compared with the conventional force sensor (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> - 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>).Also, we developed mechanically robust jig of QCR load sensor for practical use of QCR load sensor. We succeed in simultaneous measurement of weight, heart rate, and respiration rate using fabricated QCR load sensing system. The accuracy of heart rate and respiration rate measurement are 0.4 bpm (0.6 %) and 1.1 brpm (6.1 %), respectively, in standard deviation of error compared with ECG signal.

title: Acousto-Microfluidic Probe for Fluid and Particle Manipulation
authors: Waqas Waheed; Mohammed A. Qasaimeh
publication_title: 2024 [::International::] [::Conference::] on Manipulation; [::Automation::] and [::Robotics::] at Small Scales (MARSS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Acousto-Microfluidic Probe (AcouMFP) for fluid and particle manipulation within an open microfluidic system, which integrates the interaction of Bulk Acoustic Waves with hydrodynamic flow confinement (HFC) to perform multiple operations within a single device. The probe comprises a single central injection part, two crescent-shaped aspiration ports, and numerous triangular posts protruding on its mesa region. A piezoelectric transducer attached to the probe uses the piezoelectric effect to induce acoustic forces on the fluids and particles within the HFC and achieve the counter-rotating vortices of the fluid and the dynamic trapping of microparticles at relatively high flow rates. A two-dimensional numerical study is also carried out to capture the interaction of the acoustic waves and the HFC, and a close agreement with experiments is observed.

title: Optimization Design of the Toroidal Worm Wheel Hob for Robotic Joint with Worm Gear Pair Transmission
authors: Zhijiang Chen; Chunming Xia; Yingfan Ren; Chao Zhang; Jie Yang
abstract: To improve the transmission efficiency of the toroidal worm gear pairs in robotic joints and to enhance the accuracy of the toroidal worm wheel hob in cutting worm wheels, a method is proposed that involves using cylindrical forming surface milling to create helical grooves on the front face of the toroidal worm wheel hob. Based on the principle of gear meshing, a mathematical model is established for the development of the helical grooves on the front face of the toroidal worm wheel hob using a cylindrical generating surface. The model uses planar second envelopment for the toroidal worm wheel.
